title: Running around Alton Water on the Shotley Peninsula
short_description: If you're into jogging or trail running, a quick circuit around Alton Water reservoir on the Shotley Peninsula is always a sound option. It's also a great walk for those who prefer to keep things more sedate.
long_description:
With nice views, easy parking, and a trail that's easy to navigate, a run around Alton Water is a great way to blow away the cobwebs. Whether you decide to do the whole thing or the shorter version that involves cutting across Lemon's Hill Bridge leading to and from Tattingstone, a meditative time in pleasant surroundings is pretty much ensured.
Conditions along the way vary between patchy woodland and open areas of grass and gorse skirting farmland. There are a couple of very gentle hills and the tracks are free of any undergrowth. The only bit that isn't as nice is the short stretch along the A137 where - this being England - you can expect some roadside litter.
Cycling the route is also an option as far as the bridge (bikes are not permitted beyond this point), or you can just as easily walk the whole thing. The route can also be done in reverse. It's your choice.
Enjoy :D

images.caption: The highest point of the route
Cycling is restricted in some areas

title: Short hiking route Sonthofen
short_description: This short hiking route shows you the old castle of Sonthofen.
long_description: This route leads you around the old castle of Sonthofen. During the route you will find some signs with information about the buildings. The political party of Hitler used this place. Nowadays these buildings are part of the German army.  The view of Sonthofen is also very beautiful.

title: Around Oberstaufen
short_description: On this tour we experience the landscape around Oberstaufen.
long_description: The Staufner Berg is a must due to its position as Oberstaufen's local mountain, although the view is not worth the climb. Back in town, we hike around the Staufener Berg. We hike via Hinterstaufen and Bad Rain to Wei&szlig. Now we climb up to the Kapf, where in good weather we can see as far as the Sentis. Behind it we enjoy the landscape around Sinswang, Bufflings and Kalzhofen.

images.caption: View from the Staufener Berg into the West Allgäu
Oberstaufen with old lift valley station
Residential houses on the outskirts of Oberstaufen

title: Along the Iller past Lake Ortwang
short_description: The tour along the Iller past the Ortwanger See lake is particularly suitable for nature-loving people who like things a little quieter.

images.caption: Weg zwischen Ostrach und Ortswanger See

title: Walking route Naardermeer
short_description: During this walking route, you will discover beautiful nature around Naarden.
long_description: The Naardermeer is one of the natural monuments in the Netherlands. The Naardermeer still exists because people made sure it became a nature monument. Today, the area is home to many species of birds. Also living there are otters, badgers and foxes.

title: Hadassa Trail
short_description: A circular walking track of short-medium length that surrounds the Hadassah Ein Kerem Hospital.
long_description: The Hadassah Trail is a short-medium length hiking trail, the total length of the trail is about 6 kilometers. Parts of the route combine with the Jerusalem Trail, the Israel Trail and the Springs Trail . The trail marking is red-green.

title: Rhine-Nahe Wine Trail - Stage 2
short_description: The second stage of the Rhine-Nahe Wine Trail leads from Bad Sobernheim via Staudernheim, Schlossböckelheim, past a former winegrowing domain to Norheim.
long_description: The second stage of the wine trail is also dedicated to wine and takes us initially to the heights above Staudernheim, where the Nahe and Glan rivers almost completely flow around the Disibodenberg with its monastery ruins. There are wonderful views of the surrounding vineyards and down into the valley to Boos. With the following Heimberg-Höhe, we cross the core area of the Waldböckelheim vineyards. Here it is worth climbing the Heimberg tower, from which we have a deep view down into the Nahe valley and over the entire region. Over field and meadow paths and through forests and vineyards we reach Norheim.

images.caption: Blick auf die Nahe und Oberhausen
Blick vom Heimberg zur Nahe und zum Lemberg

title: Winter hike to the Adlersprung ski jump, Zinswald and Katharinenhöhe
short_description: Easy circular hike with start and finish at the Tourist Information in Schönwald in the Black Forest with unique far-reaching views of the wintry Black Forest.
long_description:
The historic ski jumps of Schönwald are the first stage destination of this approximately 6 km long circular hike. They are among the most famous ski jumps in the Black Forest and were inaugurated as early as 1924. The Hotel Adlerschanze is located directly at the run-out with a view of the ski jumps.
On wintry paths you continue through the mystical Zinswald forest to the Katharinenhöhe with rehabilitation clinic. From here you can enjoy a panoramic view of the snow-covered coniferous forests of the Black Forest before heading back towards Schönwald.
Just before Schönwald you can stop for a break at the café „Zum Kreuz". The last few kilometres take you past the Schönwälder outdoor swimming pool into the town centre, where there are further opportunities to stop for refreshments.

title: Nordic Walking Park Amtzell
short_description: This challenging Nordic walking tour takes us through an impressive landscape.
long_description: From the car park at the gymnastics and festival hall, we follow the red and white Nordic Walking route "3". This takes us past the turnoff to the Lourdes Grotto (1) to Singenberg. Via Steppach and along the Bücheler Weihers (2) we reach Hackbrettler and turn left. Past the old oak tree (3), a natural monument, we finally reach the picturesque Tobel (4). Here we keep to the left and turn left onto a gravel path. Behind Niemandsfreund, we turn right onto a meadow path and continue via Ettenlehen (5) to Haselmühle. There we cross the Eggenbach (6) and walk until shortly before Schlegel. Here we turn right onto a field path. Via Maierhofmühle we walk through the forest to Schirings and on to Tannberg. Here we take a sharp left and return to Amtzell via Winkelmühle.

images.caption: The view of the mountains from Tobel.

title: Stammbach Panorama Trail
short_description: A beautiful circular trail through idyllic villages and the romantic Kosertal valley. Along the route we are repeatedly offered beautiful panoramic views.
long_description: The village of Weickenreuth, which belongs to the municipality of Stammbach, was the state and national winner in the competition "Our village shall become more beautiful" in 1993. The idyllically situated village, close to nature, with its old farmhouses and beautiful farm gardens is well worth a visit. A visit in the summer months is a feast for the eyes because of the diverse flowers. Furthermore, beautiful circular hiking trails invite you to take a walk with a magnificent panoramic view, e.g. the 13 km long circular hiking trail "Panorama". The hiking trail consists mainly of field and forest paths. From Weickenreuth you go to Untersauerhof and from there to Förstenreuth. The restored old flax house is worth seeing here. Via Höhlmühle, the route then leads to Marienweiher, a place of pilgrimage with a beautiful basilica. From there you reach Weickenreuth via Kosermühle, through the romantic Kosertal valley. There are rest and refreshment opportunities in the well-kept restaurants in the villages along the way.

title: From Syke through Barrier Switzerland
short_description: This hike takes us into the picturesque nature between Syke and Barrien, which bears the significant name "Barrier Switzerland".
long_description: Our hike begins at the Kreismuseum Syke and from there we head into Friedeholz. We take the next path on the left and can make a detour to the right at the following crossroads into the "Wolfsschlucht". Various cultural events take place in this gorge-like valley from May to September. The Kastenbeinbuche (box-legged beech) and the Märchenplatz (fairy-tale square) are also in the immediate vicinity. Back on our actual path, we soon reach the edge of the forest. We leave the forest, walk up the Friedeholz ridge and follow the field path over the Geest Ridge towards the gorge. Before we reach the gorge, we turn left and walk through Barrien on the right. Then we cross the Krusenberg and take the Krumme Straße to the left. Continue along the streets Zum Walde and Im Sande until you reach the subway of the B6 federal road. After the underpass, we continue on a straight stretch to the water mill and walk around the mill pond to the left. We meet Glockenstraße, cross the B6 again and turn right into Heinrichstraße at Am Hohen Esch. At Schwarzer Berg we change to the road "Südfeld", which we leave shortly afterwards to the right to follow the B6 for a bit. Then we turn right into the forest and walk back to the Kreismuseum.

images.caption: On our tour we cross the Hache river.

title: Dog walk with "Stöckchen" in the Altstädter Moos
short_description: This easy tour takes us to the Altstädter Moos, where we have a beautiful view of the Oberstdorf mountains.
long_description:
On this easy Nordic walking tour we have a beautiful view of the Allgäu Alps and enjoy the sound of the trees.
There are B&änke along the way where we can rest. We have a magnificent panoramic view.
Dogs also get their money's worth, because they have plenty of room to run around. Dog toilets are available.

title: Marktleuthen 1
short_description: This enjoyable hike takes us from Marktleuthen to Kaiserhammer Forst West and back again via Marktleuthener Allee.
long_description: This enjoyable hike takes us from Marktleuthen to the Kaiserhammer Forest West and back again via Marktleuthener Allee. Pleasant ascents and descents take us across fields and through the forest, with some historical relics along the way.

images.caption: Town hall and Protestant church in Marktleuthen, the starting and finishing point of our tour.

title: Trade route (German section Töddenweg)
short_description: The trade route connects Osnabrück with the Dutch Hanseatic city of Deventer. The German section of the route runs continuously along the Töddenweg, an old trade route used by linen merchants to bring their goods to the Netherlands.
long_description: The hiking trail is called "Töddenweg" in the German part. Tödden were foot-travelling merchants who travelled across Europe to sell linen goods. The trail runs through Heger Holz in Osnabrück, past Rubbenbruchsee, Gut Leye, Sloopsteine, Westerkappeln, Mettingen, Dickenberg, Heiliges Meer nature reserve, Hopsten, through Rheine along the Ems to Bentlage Monastery and to Stovern Estate. On Lower Saxony territory, the trail then runs through Bad Bentheim and Gildehaus.

images.caption: Osnabrück City Hall with Market Square

title: Around Heblos Tour near Lauterbach
short_description:
On meagre grassland and juniper heaths we circle Rimlos.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description:
To the west of the Wiegel holiday farm, we hike up the hill to the edge of the Hölsberg forest. The wonderful view over Rimlos and Lauterbach compensates for the slight incline. With a good distant view, you can make out the crests of the Rhön.
The path continues below the Hälsberg forest, past unspoilt nature with rough grassland and juniper heath. Now the trail goes downhill, part of it is asphalted and leads to the country road towards Wallenrod. Walk a short stretch of road over the bridge. Above the old railway station, turn left in a southerly direction and walk straight on towards Sickendorf. On the left you will see part of the 18-hole golf course, the Sickendorf estate and the castle. A bridge leads us across the Brenderwasser to the country road towards Sickendorf until we reach the stables of a farm on the left. The road uphill leads to the Schmittberg. From here we come to the cycle path, which leads us left down the field path to the talking railway barrier. We follow the path back to the village of Rimlos.

title: Climbing Mount Borus - Shushensky Bor National Park
short_description: Mount Borus – a multi-headed mountain, is located near the Western Sayan, not far from the famous Sayano-Shushenskaya hydroelectric power station. The peaks of the Borus Ridge are the property of the «Shushensky Bor» national park.
long_description:
The Borus range has clearly defined peaks. Malyy Borus, Bolshoy Borus, Koshurnikov, Durak – these are all peaks of the same range. The highest of them is Bolshoi Borus – 2,318 metres. The range is named after the first travellers who reached the top. Their names were Borisov and Rusanov; they put the first letters together and the name Borus came out easily.
Borus
The route is highly recommended to lovers of outdoor activities because of the presence of mountain waterholes, lakes, taiga forests and glacier rocks. The ridge blooms in summer and boasts a mighty whiteness in winter.

images.caption: Top of Mount Borus against the background of the Yenisei at dawn
View of the reserve from Big Borus Peak
Above the clouds, the Borus range
Cross on the Bolshoy Borus in memory of fallen mountaineers

title: Through the Schwarzach Valley - Kinding
short_description: Lots of nature and an impressive ruin await us on this tour.
long_description: The Schwarzach flows into the Altmühl at Kinding. Around this estuary lies the Altmühltal Nature Park. The nature park is characterised by the low mountain range landscapes of the southern Franconian Alps. Typical landscape features such as the dry grassland, juniper heath, wet meadows and quarries can be seen here. Above all, however, the dense forests are the hallmark of the nature park.

title: Climbing the Ostrachtaler Klettersteig (Via Ferrata) by Oberjoch, Allgäu
short_description: Clip in and shimmy up this short via ferrata route by Bad Hindelang in the Allgäu. Great for a bit of evening exercise or in preparation for something more hardcore.
long_description:
Not as well known as the Salewa-Klettersteig on the nearby Iseler, this short B/C (K2/K3) via ferrata route combines the fun of clambering up an 85m cliff face with a short hike around the environs of Oberjoch and some great views across to the Hintersteiner Tal, back towards Sonthofen, and over to the Nagelfluhkette in the far off distance. 
In terms of difficulty, I'd say the route is largely suitable for beginners. There are a couple of steeper sections (no overhangs) that require the use of some artificial placements/pins, but as long as you're reasonably strong, don't have a problem with heights, and know how to use your gear, these should not pose a problem. The duration of the climb also depends on you. It's not a long VF, so I recommend you slow things down and savour the moment.  The only drawback is the noise from the road below you, which motor cyclists sem to love for some reason!
Have fun.

images.caption: The sign by the entrance down to the start of the VF
The noise from the road is the only annoyance

title: Cow & Calf short circular
short_description: A short circular walk starting from the cow & calf car park, counterclockwise and does include a bit of a steeper climb up the western side.

title: Through forest and field near Mulfingen
short_description: This tour takes us into the beautiful nature around Mulfingen. We hike through dense forests, wide fields and pass interesting geological formations, the three sinkholes.
long_description: We start our hike in Eberbach and walk from there into the Rötelbach valley. After about 1.8 km, we continue on a gravel path through the "Streitbergwald" forest until we reach the "Hegenest" forest area. Here we can take a look at the "Wolfsgrube", a restored medieval wolf trap and the former estate "Zerenbergbrunn", which is about 100 m off the trail. We then pass the "Wolfgangsee" and reach the "Kalksklingenberg" via a part of the former trade road "Hohe Straße" to the open field "Taubenhof". Behind the district road we go uphill to the three sinkholes. These are natural, funnel-shaped collapses or hollows in the terrain formed by the erosion of limestone. We walk along the edge of the slope to the "Egelsee" field. From there we return to Eberbach on an asphalted path.

title: Team Tour Trail Hainsburg
short_description: This panoramic Nordic walking tour takes us around the Hainsburg, the "local mountain" of Illschwang.
long_description: The team tour trail takes us around the Hainsburg, the "local mountain" of Illschwang, around. As the name suggests, this circuit is particularly suitable for walking in groups. in groups. Again and again we can enjoy the magnificent view of the picturesque, listed village of Illschwang.

title: Border path Töpen
short_description: On the border trail, the hiker experiences an excursion into recent German history.
long_description: On the border trail, the hiker experiences an excursion into recent German history. The destination of our hike is the village of Modlareuth, which lies partly on Bavarian and partly on Thuringian territory. There we can visit the "German-German Museum Mödlareuth e.V.". The return route is partly on the former "Kolonnenweg", the patrol route of the GDR border troops. GDR border troops. The extensive hike offers not only historical experiences, but also beautiful nature. The most scenic part runs along the Tannbach valley to where the stream flows into the Saale.

images.caption: The border tower in Mödlareuth is a witness to German-German history.

title: Blaibach Walking Tour
short_description: This Nordic walking tour takes us through narrow forest paths and across meadows. Wide views of the landscape reward us for the ascents.
long_description: The start and finish of this Nordic walking tour is at Blaibach Castle. From here we walk uphill along the cobbled street through the village. At the memorial stone of the marksmen, we turn left in the direction of Spielberg. We pass a farmhouse decorated with old agricultural implements on the façade. After a stretch through the forest, we can rest at a rest stop or continue towards Reckendorf. Before reaching the village, a path leads us back to the left into the forest. At the end of the loop, the restaurant of Blaibach Castle offers us the possibility of a stop. Before we finish this tour, we can take a look at the castle courtyard and the parish church of St. Elisabeth opposite.

images.caption: An artful way to decorate the house with old farm implements.
The castle in Blaibach was converted into a restaurant.

title: Bischofsgrüner Heilklima-Runde 6
short_description: A challenging hiking trail through the Fichtelgebirge Nature Park with beautiful views of the forest and meadows and the village of Bischofsgrün.
long_description:
We set out on a medium-length circular trail (9.0 km) with ascents totalling 280 metres in altitude. In the process, we overcome a slight and moderate, in the short term also a steep incline. Our average energy consumption at a weight of 75 kg is approx. 550 kcal.

The demands due to the climate are to be classified as high. Some parts of the route are very strenuous, as they are often sunny and windy and lead across open spaces. However, there are also stretches with subdued, yet stimulating climatic stimuli at the edge of the forest or through loose buildings. In summer, thermal conditions are predominantly comfortable to cool. In winter, cold stimuli are often to be expected.
In the "place of power", one can find the way to inner harmony and physical and mental balance through deep relaxation and tranquillity. The special powers of this place were discovered in May 1996 by the radiation seeker Lothar Meinhardt from Kempten.

images.caption: In Bischofsgrün all paths are well signposted.

title: Lodhi Garden Trail Delhi
short_description: The Lodi Garden Trail is an urban natural trail route located in New Delhi, the capital of India.
long_description:
This is a moderately crowded loop trail about 2 kilometers long that is good for hikers of all skill levels. Accessible year-round, this trail is primarily suitable for walking, nature walks, viewing beautiful wildflowers, and bird watching.
Lodhi Gardens is one of the largest urban parks in the world. Located between Khan Market and Safdarjung in Delhi's Lodhi Road, the garden covers an area of 90 acres (360,000 m²). Many types of birds live in its trees such as black drongo, Indian tree pie, myna, red-vented bulbul, kingfisher, sparrow, eagle, peacock etc. Lodhi Garden is also a playground. Here you will see many people doing jogging, yoga, and exercising.
Being in the middle of a metropolis, it is very popular among outdoor sportsmen and nature lovers.

title: From Berlin to Usedom
short_description: This tour of almost 300 km takes us through scenic areas on the long-distance cycle route from Bernau near Berlin to the Baltic Sea holiday island of Usedom.
long_description:
This tour of almost 300 km takes us along the long-distance cycle route from Bernau near Berlin to the island of Usedom. It is advisable to divide the route into individual stages depending on your physical condition. There is a dense railway network in the region between Berlin and Usedom and the trains run relatively frequently. There is no point along the long-distance cycle route from which a railway station cannot be reached within at least an hour. In the high season it is advisable to book overnight accommodation.
We start at the S-Bahn station in Bernau, Brandenburg. From Ulitzkastraße we turn left into August-Bebel-Straße. At the crossroads we follow Jahnstraße to the west and turn north onto the state road. North of Ladeburg we keep to the right and continue our tour through the Barnimer Land with its extensive forests and rolling hills via Lobetal, Biesenthal as well as Finow to Eberswalde. We continue cycling in a westerly direction to Niederfinow, from where we now head north on the Hebelwerkstraße. We are now in the Schorfheide Chorin Biosphere Reserve. The Schorfheide as a core area is a contiguous forest area of about 200 km², which we can only cross on a very old, but cobblestone road of cultural-historical value. At the lock stairs we keep to the left and leave it after about 2.5 km in a northerly direction. At the first crossroads we keep left and cycle straight ahead until we reach Chorin Monastery. The Cistercian monastery was built around 1270 to 1300 and still has Romanesque and some Byzantine architectural elements, but was then mainly completed in the brick Gothic style. From Chorin, the route continues partly on very sandy paths via Golzower Weg to Senftenhütte. We cycle northwest along the village road until we reach the state road, which we follow to the left and a short distance later turn right to reach Althüttendorf. Along the western shore of Lake Grimnitz, the trail leads us to Joachimsthal. At the northern end of the lake, we turn right into Glambecker Straße, which we stay on for quite a while. In Glambeck we cross the motorway and continue our tour in a westerly direction to Lake Wolletz. Angermünderstraße leads us across the fish ponds to Görlsdorf. Now we continue along the railway tracks on the road Am Peetzigsee. At the fork in the road, we keep to the left. We pass the northern shore of Großer Peetzigsee and head northwest towards the village of Steinhöfel. We keep this direction, cross the motorway again and finally reach Flieth-Stegelitz. There we turn right into Dorfstraße, cross the country road and continue to follow the path parallel to Oberuckersee northwards to Seehausen. From there we continue via Potzlow, Strehlow, Zollchow and Ropersdorf to Prenzlau. From there we ride via Schönwerder, Bandelow and Nechlin through the Uckermark to Rollwitz and on to Pasewalk. Via Viereck we ride through Torgelow and Eggesin to Uckermünde. Now we keep west along the coast to Leopoldshagen. Via Bugewitz we reach Kamp, from where we take a ferry to the island of Usedom. Via Wilhelmsfelde we now continue our cycle tour to the village of Usedom and cycle around Lake Usedom. Our route continues along the Szczecin Lagoon through the villages of Prätenow, Dargen, Bossin and Neverow. Now we head to the other side of the island. We pass Zirchow and Korswandt until we arrive at the Baltic Sea coast in Heringsdorf. The last part of our cycle tour takes us directly along the coastline, where we can enjoy wonderful views of the sea. The destination of our bike tour is the railway station in the village of Zinnowitz.
There we board the Usedom Bäderbahn and start our return journey to Bernau near Berlin, our starting point.

title: Round tour around Ingelfingen
short_description: On this tour we hike from Ingelfingen to the "Lindle" from where we can enjoy a magnificent view.
long_description: We start our hike in Ingelfingen, south of the Kocher at the Kocher bridge. Via Lipfersberger Straße we reach the Steinsteige. We continue straight on past the Kocherstein, uphill through the hillside forest to the Lindle, a lookout hut that invites us to take a break. From here we can look out over Künzelsau and the Kocher. On beautiful forest paths we hike to the village of Lipfersberg and reach the settlement of Galgenäcker via an asphalted road. From there we walk back down to Ingelfingen and back to our starting point at the Kocher bridge. In the state-recognised resort town of Ingelfingen, we can still take a look at the castle of the Count of Hohenlohe after our hike, which has been used as the town hall since 1985. Also worth seeing are the town nobility house "Schwarzer Hof" and the shell limestone museum Hagdorn.

title: The Golan Trail
short_description: A long walking trail in the Golan Heights, about 120 km long. Due to the length of the path, it is made in sections where in each section you pass historical sites. This is a path that is generally considered not particularly difficult but includes several steep climbs.
long_description: The Golan Trail, as its name suggests, is an organized walking trail that crosses the Golan Heights. The route of the trail stretches from Hermon in the north of the plateau to Ein Tawfik (near Hamat Gedar) in the south of the plateau. Due to the geographical conditions of the Golan Heights, the walk on the trail for beginners from the north is mostly downhill, except for a few peaks in its area (the highest among them is 200 meters). Due to the fact that in the Golan Heights there are many minefields and fire areas, the route of the path is limited and it does not reach everywhere on the level.

title: Quick Süd City Hike  - Bottom to Top
short_description: Looking for a quick escape into nature? Start in Marienplatz and take a few steep staircases to a hilltop park with scenic views over Stuttgart Süd.
long_description: Great for a morning dog walk or an evening view of the sunset. Start near Marienplatz and wind your way up some steep staircases to a hilltop park. Take in the views from one of the many benches and lookouts in the park, then work your way back down. Enjoy one of the many cafes and restaurants in Marienplatz or along Tübinger Str. at the start or end of your hike.

title: One-day hike on Via Transilvanica route (from Criș to Mălâncrav)
short_description: An easy stage of the Via Transilvanica route between the villages of Criș and Mălâncrav; crosses a couple of really secluded areas. The route can, of course, be done the other way round.
long_description:
The route starts from the center of Cris village and follows the Via Transilvanica markings. Alternatively, there are the markings made by the Colinele Transilvaniei NGO. The start is rough, with an ascent to the forest above the village. The path enters a thicket of deciduous trees, its coolness being more than welcome on sunny days.
The forest is home to wild animals, some of which may appear unexpectedly. Deer often cross paths with you.
After a few hundred meters, you come out into a meadow that opens wide to the right. From spring to autumn, the bright green grass grows here untouched by other creatures besides the local fauna.
Following the orange T marks, you walk for about one kilometer by large fields. Hardly anybody comes in these parts. Traces of wild animals (including bears) are common. The shepherds in the area graze the sheep on the hills that guard the area.
The exit to the asphalt that leads to the village of Floresti reminds one of civilization. At the end of the village, you reach Stâna de pe Coline, a sheepfold with permanent activity, where the hosts can offer a cup of water and local products.
Continuing towards Mălâncrav, the road is wide, only good for cycling. The path enters yet another forest, without ascending or descending, that soon comes to an end into a large meadow. The view opens here to the surrounding hills. There's a picnic spot, and even a tent spot, for the daring.
The last kilometers are quite steep, again through the forest, this time a brighter one and with more traces of human passage.
Once in the village of Mălâncrav, you can look for accommodation or continue on to the next stage.

title: Trail running around the Råbjerg Mile, North Jutland
short_description: Empty beaches, heather, rolling dunes, and wetlands are all yours to discover on this surprisingly wild stretch of North Jutland's coast.
long_description:
As a runner, I found Denmark's North Jutland region an excellent place to get out on the trails, and though relatively compact, this particular route offers some wonderfully diverse conditions and unique scenery. I also enjoyed the solitude that came with most of the run. You're never all that far from civilisation, but there are moments when you really feel as though you are. 
Starting just off the arterial route 40 road at the quaint Råbjerg Kirke (church), the first section of the run leads you along a clear path through gentle heather and grassland towards the beach. After a brief jog next to the crashing surf, you head back inland to cross the Råbjerg Mile, a bizarre 'micro-desert' of dunes covering around 2 square kilometers and a local tourist attraction. A winding track through sandy scrub and small trees leads towards a more established forest trail. After a few kilometers, you will veer off into the wilds again to traverse a crest of grassy dunes flanked by wetlands. A rather heavy section of soggy heather then follows, where the trail disappears for a while before you finally find yourself meeting up with a grassy bridlepath leading back to the church. 
In all, this is definitely a run I enjoyed and would recommend. It does require a bit of navigation, but the primordial scenery and peaceful surroundings far outweigh the effort.
If you enjoyed this route, why not try this one too: Trail running on the Rubjerg Knude by Lønstrup, North Jutland

title: Around Herbstein
short_description:
The best way to get to know Herbstein - once around.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description:
We start from the Hensler farm guesthouse. We start in the direction of Gallberg, passing above the quarry and reach the former mills (Wei&szligmle and Trappenmle), which are now used as agricultural buildings. The path continues to the volcano cycle path, which we cross. Turn left and follow the meadow path next to the Vulkanradweg to the B 275. Cross the main road and walk past the riding hall (Dachreiter - Bistro) in the direction of the Heidegrab (heath grave), where you have a wonderful view of the Rhön region. Continue on the asphalted path until you reach the „Fourteen Saints“ (wayside shrine). We reach the edge of the forest via a meadow path, which we follow before entering the forest and coming out again at Steimel with a magnificent view of Herbstein. After a few minutes we reach the
Vulkanradweg again, which we now walk along to the Galgen. From there we walk back towards Herbstein. Once again via the B275, past the volcano spa through the spa gardens to the starting point of the Hensler farmhouse guesthouse.

title: Hike from Samoëns to the hamlet of Chantemerle via Les Suets
short_description: Starting from the village of Samoëns, explore the wild, unspoilt beauty of the Savoyard mountains, passing through the hamlet of Chantemerle and Les Suets!
long_description:
The trail begins with a moderate climb through lush green forests, where the fresh air and birdsong accompany your steps. The higher you climb, the more impressive the views of the Samoëns valley and surrounding mountains become. The first part of the route takes you through the pastures of Les Suets, a place where the scenery gradually unfolds, offering grandiose panoramas of the surrounding mountains and valleys.
The Suets are also a charming place, with their traditional chalets and high mountain scenery. You can observe the local wildlife and enjoy moments of tranquillity. It's an ideal place to take a break, take photos or simply admire the view.
The trail continues towards the hamlet of Chantemerle, an authentic place that seems frozen in time. Chantemerle, with its stone houses and tiled roofs, is a haven of peace where you can discover the traditional mountain way of life.

title: Through the Breitachklamm gorge to Oberstdorf
short_description: We experience the wildly romantic Breitachklamm gorge with its bizarre ice formations and then enjoy a very scenic walk via Reute to Oberstdorf.
long_description:
The Breitachklamm gorge was created after the last ice age, when the masses of water from the melting ice carved the rock more than 100 metres deep. At the beginning of the 20th century, the Tiefenbach priest Johannes Schiebel began to develop the gorge. Due to numerous rockfalls and floods, the gorge path was repeatedly badly damaged. However, the Breitachklamm Association spared no expense or effort and ensured that it was restored each time. In places the gorge is only 2 metres wide. This is why the water level rose to over 6 metres during the severe flood in August 2005.
At the lower ticket office is a part of the Oberstdorf mountain show. A special highlight here is a model of the Breitachklamm gorge that can be flooded with water to simulate different water levels. A 15-minute film provides information about the Breitachklamm, the work of the association and the mountain show.

title: A shortcut to the hexagon pool
short_description: A short-to-medium-length hiking route that starts from the village of Katzrin, descends in a southeast direction along Nahal Zytan and ends at the Meshoshen pool
long_description:
A hiking route that leaves from the capital of the Galilee - Katzrin in a southerly direction towards the Meshoshen pool.
The waters of Nahal Meshushis/Zuytan flowing in the basalt bed of the pool create several small waterfalls, over the millions of years this flow created the pool.
The name of the pool was given to it thanks to its walls built of basalt columns in the shape of polygons, which were shaped by nature. The height of the columns reaches about 5 meters and their diameter is 30-40 cm.
The shape of the columns was created naturally following the cooling process of the lava flows after a volcanic eruption. That is, their shape was obtained as the surface of the lava cooled and contracted while the surface of the lava continued to be hot and continued to move. The temperature differences between the outer and inner parts of the lava caused the cracking of the outer mantle, which resulted in the formation of the polygons.
** Since this is a route, the distance lines and the calculated walking times are in one direction.

title: Alsterwanderweg - From Fuhlsbüttel to Poppenbüttel
short_description: Leisurely walk along the Alster, through the beautiful woods of Teetzpark.
long_description: We start our walk in the quiet district of Fuhlsbüttel, which takes us along the Alster to the elegant district of Poppenbüttel. We stroll leisurely through Teetzpark and enjoy beautiful views of the Alster and the surrounding ponds. There are several places to stop along the way, especially when the weather is nice.

title: Donsbach game park tour
short_description: The wildlife park circuit is perfect for an afternoon walk with children. There are plenty of adventure points, animals and a great playground to keep the little ones entertained.
long_description:
Although the route is only just under 2 km long, it is particularly suitable for families with children. Lots of exciting waypoints, animals that you can feed and stroke and a great playground make for an entertaining afternoon.
If you don't want to walk uphill, you should be dropped off in Tiergartenstraße and walk flat into the park. There are only disabled parking spaces here, all others please park at the village community center!
Dogs are allowed (except in the playground) but must be kept on a lead.

title: Bohusleden - Stage 7 - Lysevatten to Hasteröd
short_description: The seventh stage of Bohusleden leads through forest and moorland from Lake Lysevatten to Hasteröd.
long_description: The trail leads through an extensive mixed forest and a lake-rich moorland. Up to Lake Västersjön the terrain is hilly, later we walk on easy paths through a more even forest area. The landscape is unspoilt throughout the stage and has a great variety of native animals and plants

title: The most beautiful railway route in Romania: Oravita - Anina
short_description: The train route between Oravita and Anina is considered today probably the most beautiful train route in Romania. Reservations for a round trip should be made well in advance, especially during the summer holiday season!
long_description:
Romania might not excel when it comes to sustainable tourism, but this route is surely a positive example.
Once called the "coal line" because it used to link the coal mines between Anina and Baziaș, where the goods were loaded on ships, the "Baziaș-Oravița-Anina Railway" site is today a historical monument, It includes the train stations of Anina and Oravița. Only the last leg of the route is fully used for tourist purposes.
The railway was built by the Austrians between 1861 and 1863 and inaugurated at the end of 1863. It measures 33.4 km long and is technically difficult to travel, having a slope gradient of 339 meters.
Since its reopening, the train route has become the main attraction in the Banat Mountains because of the beautiful landscape and the importance of the whole engineering structure. A special attraction is the Jitin Viaduct, with five arches over the Jitin Valley. Another 9 viaducts and 14 tunnels add to the beauty of the route.
The whole one-way journey takes about two hours. The train running on the route is operated by CFR and ticket reservations can be made up to 30 days in advance. The cost of a one-way ticket is 13.9 RON.

title: Canto de Atins to Baixa Grande
short_description: First part of the Travessia dos Lençóis Maranhenses, which goes from Canto de Atins to Baixa Grande, on a route with beautiful scenery of dunes and crystalline lagoons.
long_description:
The first part of the long-distance trail Travessia dos Lençóis Maranhenses starts at Canto de Atins, a little north of Ponta do Mangue. To better enjoy the journey, it is worth getting up very early because it is approximately 25 km to Baixa Grande. For the first few kilometres, much of the trail is flat or over low-lying dunes.
After two or three hours of walking, small and small lakes begin to be noticed, and the dunes gain a few good metres of slope. Remember to make the most of the walking time when the sun is still low and leave the stops for bathing in the lagoons for after 9am, when it is already hot and you are closer to finishing this stretch.
Once you arrive in Baixa Grande, where some families live, look for accommodation in the house of the residents who provide lodging, such as the house of Mrs. Odete. The tip for the late afternoon is to follow the sunset over the dunes, about 15 minutes from the house.

title: Adrasan Sahili - Gelidonya Lighthouse - Mavikent
short_description: This route on the Lycian Way, which is one of the most popular routes of Turkey and offers unique views, starts from Adrasan, stops at Gelidonya Lighthouse and ends in Mavikent.
long_description:
Lycian Way is undoubtedly one of the most important hiking routes in Turkey. How can this historical trail, which brings together nature lovers with stunning views, not be at the top of the list?
This route, which is located on the Lycian Way and includes the famous Gelidonya Lighthouse, starts from the beach of Adrasan Sahili and extends to Mavikent. You start at sea level and gradually climb up. As your height increases, of course, the views you witness are another pleasure. Right on the nose, like every yürüyüyüşçü you can pause at Gelidonya Lighthouse and take a breather in this bölge for your break. After taking a break at the lighthouse, you can take the seafront route again, first to Karaöz and then to Mavikent. The route ends here. 
Those who have done a little research on the Lycaonian Way surely know that, as with every stage, travelling on this route requires being fully equipped and careful.

title: To the Black Sea, by bike (Lehliu-Gară - Vama Veche)
short_description: It is a staged itinerary (2-3 days), entirely on asphalt, partially covering the EuroVelo 6 cycle route.
long_description:
If you want to be adventurous and get to the Black Sea resorts by bike, while also camping, this route is one possibility. (Another one would be from Cernavoda.) Moreover, a segment of this route is officially part of the European cycle tourist route EuroVelo, which connects the Black Sea and the Atlantic.
The route passes through villages in the Bărăgan Plain - places that seem to be dilating under the summer heat, crosses the Danube by ferry from Călărași to Ostrov, and then follows an up-down-up course before finally descending to the sea.
The scenery is beautiful, especially after the ferry crossing. The Danube peacefully joins you a good part of the way, and so are the rapeseed or poppy fields if you ride this route in early summer.

title: German Wine Route
short_description: The German Wine Route is considered one of the most important tourist routes in the Palatinate and has enjoyed growing popularity since its opening in 1935. The tour offers an interesting insight into the home of exquisite varieties such as Riesling and Burgundy.
long_description:
The Palatinate is Germany's second-largest wine-growing region after Rheinhessen and can call more than 300 vineyards its own. Thanks to its enormous soil diversity, wine varieties of the most diverse aromas can be grown here. The local climate also gives visitors the impression of being right on the Mediterranean: The sandstone walls of the vineyards are ideal heat reservoirs and thus ensure pleasant southern temperatures.
The first German vineyards are located in the Mediterranean.
Germany's first wine tourism route begins directly at the House of the German Wine Route in Bockenheim near Worms and leads for a total of about 80 km to the German Wine Gate in Schweigen-Rechtenbach on the border with Alsace. Along the course of the road, colourful orchards line up with idyllic wine-growing areas, but also numerous places steeped in history such as Hambach Castle, Wachtenburg Castle, Neuleiningen Castle and Villa Ludwigshöhe Castle.
.
Wine lovers have the opportunity to get to know typical Palatinate grape varieties such as Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir at close quarters, to learn about classical viticulture and wine pressing and to be enchanted by Palatinate culture and hospitality.

title: Gunthersteig
short_description: The Gunthersteig trail follows the former migration of St. Gunther, a woodsman revered as a popular saint. Starting from the monastery of Nierderaltaich on the Danube, it penetrates deeper and deeper into the wooded mountains of the Bavarian Forest through a varied cultural landscape and finally crosses the border ridge to the Bavarian Dobrá Voda (Gutwasser).
long_description:
1st stage: Niederalteich - Lalling (21 km, approx. 5 hours)
From the Danube plain near Niederalteich and Hengersberg, with numerous interesting church and monastery buildings, the easy and varied hike leads into the gentle hilly landscape of the foothills of the forest and further über Auerbach into the climatically favoured fruit-growing area of the Lallinger Winkel.
2nd stage: Lalling – Rinchnach (19 km, approx. 5 hours)
From Lalling you climb the southern ridge of the Bavarian Forest on steep forest paths with the viewpoint „Guntherstein“. From there the trail leads to Kirchberg. Through the valley of the Haider Bach stream you come to the former monastery town of Rinchnach. Here you will meet the local founder Gunther almost at every turn.
3rd stage: Rinchnach – Lindberg (21 km, approx. 5 hours)
From the parish church, which is particularly worth seeing, the hike runs past the open-air stage in Gehmannsberg, where the historic Gunther Festival takes place, up to the pilgrimage church „Frauenbrünnl“, where Gunther had a hermitage. Through extensive mountain forests and original mountain meadowland with small farming villages, you reach Zwiesel. From the splendid town square it is not far up to Lindberg. <Stage 4: Lindberg – Dobrá Voda (27 km, approx. 8 hours)
Through the mountain forests of the Bavarian Forest National Park, the route crosses the border mountains to Böhmen in the Sumava National Park. In the wildly romantic cultural landscape of the Böhmische Grenzland, the hike leads üvia Prásily (Stubenbach) to Günthersberg near Dobrá Voda (Gutwasser, little church with a glass altar worth seeing). Below the lookout peak, a small forest chapel commemorates this important personage.

title: Hiking route to Lac des Gouilles Rouges
short_description: Take a hike to Lac des Gouilles Rouges: a picturesque route with varied landscapes, majestic panoramas and a serene alpine lake at the end of the road.
long_description:
The hike often starts from the indicated starting village, usually accessible by car or public transport. The trail begins with a gradual climb through coniferous forests, where fresh air and birdsong create a soothing atmosphere. As you advance, you begin to leave the forest behind and enter alpine pastures, offering unobstructed views of the surrounding valleys.
The route traverses different types of terrain, adding to the diversity of the experience. You'll cross streams, climb gentle slopes, and take on wildflower-lined trails during the summer months. Every turn and climb rewards you with ever more spectacular views of the surrounding mountains, craggy ridges and verdant valleys.
The closer you get to Lac des Gouilles Rouges, the more grandiose the scenery becomes. The lake, nestled in a mountain cirque, is surrounded by rocky peaks and alpine vegetation, creating a setting of perfect serenity. Its generally crystal-clear waters reflect the surrounding mountains, adding a magical dimension to your hike.
Once you've arrived at the lake, you can enjoy a picnic while admiring the peaceful surroundings. Lac des Gouilles Rouges is an excellent spot for contemplation, photography or simply enjoying the soothing silence of nature. Depending on the season, you may see icebergs floating on the lake or alpine flowers in the surrounding area.

title: The coastal path near Saint-Raphaël
short_description: From the bay of Saint-Raphaël to the bay of Agay, this hiking route allows you to discover the corniche of the East with a breathtaking view of the Golden Island.
long_description: This 11 km long route takes you on the trail of the old customs officers' path between steep creeks and fine sandy beaches.

title: Yenikonacik - Asmacik - Yenikonacik
short_description: The route starting from Yenikonacık leads to Asmacık Plateau and from there back to Yenikonacık
long_description:
Asmacık Plateau is a location where you can enjoy the beautiful nature of Adana. It is also very popular with nature lovers.
This route, which includes an outbound and an inbound route, starts from Yenikonacık. After leaving the settlement behind, you have a pleasant walk on the Asmacık Plateau. On this route, where you can reach fresh air, the dirt roads, where the trees are staggered, accompany you on the plateau. You are travelling in an exquisite nature.
The route returns to Yenikonacik on the same line and is a long route when travelling back and forth. For this reason, you should be prepared for the route in advance and set off well-equipped.

title: Elfstedentocht stage 1
short_description: First part of the Elfsteden cycle tour.
long_description: The first part of the Elfstedentocht takes you from leeuwarden to Sneek. Sneek is a beautiful historic city from the 15th century. Sneek is known for its water sports and quaint waterside cafés. I would say enjoy a delicious snack and drink in Sneek after the first leg of the Eleven Cities Tour.

title: Hike through the Kempt Forest
short_description: The extensive circular hike through the Kempter Wald forest is the perfect excursion for nature lovers and all those who also want to hike a short distance on the Jacobsweg in general;
long_description: The hike leads on mostly well-surfaced (forest) paths and without major ascents through natural forests and past rare plants and moors. Here and there we discover references to the Jacobsweg.

title: Sentier littoral le long de la plage de Bonne Source
short_description:
Bel itinéraire pour une promenade ou une course à pied sur le sentier côtier longeant la plage de Bonne Source. La façade littorale est agrémentée de villas d'architectures et d'époques variées, certaines datant du XIXème siècle. Le sentier longe la dune de Bonne Source, préservée pour son rôle écologique et protecteur. La pointe de Congrigoux offre un magnifique panorama sur le littoral et les quelques îles qui le compose. Une table d'orientation permet de les identifier facilement. Fréquenté en toutes saisons, le sentier présente de nombreux aménagements de sécurisation et d'accessibilité pour tous.
Translate to English
long_description:
Un itinéraire idéal pour une promenade ou une course à pied vivifiante, entre la façade maritime, la plage de Bonne Source et le long des villas en front de mer. Le parcours se fait principalement sur un platelage en bois bien entretenu, ce qui le rends aussi très facile pour une promenade en famille avec de jeunes enfants. Il permet de profiter d'une très belle vue sur l'océan et de beaux levers ou couchers de soleil, en toutes saisons. Le cordon dunaire de Bonne Source sur lequel se situe le sentier est un espace préservé pour son rôle écologique et protecteur. Au bout de la plage de Bonne Source se trouve la pointe de Congrigoux qui offre un point de vue panoramique sur le littoral et les îles.
Translate to English

Ce circuit de randonnée de 15 km vous emmène au pied du Grand Veymont et offre un superbe point de vue sur le Mont Aiguille.

long_description:
Du parking au Champ de l'Herse, la parcours sillonne la forêt domaniale du Grand Veymont (point culminant du massif du Vercors). Par les sentiers forestiers, la randonnée se poursuit jusqu'au chemin des Collets où le Mont Aiguille se dévoile sous vos yeux.
On passe ensuite par le lieu-dit Chauplane pour rejoindre à nouveau la forêt et le Col de l'Allimas (vue imprenable sur le Mont Aiguille). Le retour s'effectue par la Combe Rouge.

title: धरमकोट-त्रिउंड ट्रैक। मैक्लोडगंज, हिमाचल, भारत
short_description: दो दिवसीय त्रियुंड ट्रेक एक मध्यम कठिनाई वाला हिमालयी ट्रैक है। कांगड ़ा घाटी और बर्फ से ढ़की धौलाधार पर्वत श्र ृंखला दिखाने वाला यह ट्रैक बहुत लोकप्रिय और दर्शनीय है।
long_description:
बिना कठिनाई के हिमालय में ट्रैकिंग करने के लिए त्रिउंड आदर्श स्थान है। त्रिउंड की पगडंडी छोटी लेकिन खड़ी चढ़ाई वाली है। इस मार्ग में मून पर्वतचोटी, आर्थर सीट, और धौलाधार पर्वतमाला जैसे कई प्राकृतिक रोचक बिंदु हैं। हालाँकि इस ट्रेल पर जंगलो का हिस्सा थोड़ा कम है लेकिन बुरांश, चीड़, देवदार और बाँझ के कुछ शानदार पेड़ जरूर मिलेंगे।
सूर्यास्त और सूर्योदय त्रिउंड ट्रैक का मुख्य आकर्षण है और इसी लिए सभी ट्रैकर रातभर रिज शिविर में रहते हैं। सूर्योदय और सूर्यास्त की किरणे बर्फ से लदे पहाड़ों पर ऐसे गिरती हैं मानो किसी ने पिघला हुआ सोना उड़ेल दिया हो।
 त्रिउंड ट्रैक का एक और फायदा है कि अन्य शिखरों की तरह यह एक अंतिम पड़ाव नहीं है। त्रिउंड बेस कैंप कई दुसरे रोमांचों के लिए प्रवेश द्वार का काम करता है। ऊपरी बर्फ रेखा (स्नो लाइन), लाका ग्लेशियर, लहेश गुफाएं और इंद्राहार दर्रे को जाने का विकल्प हमेशा खुला रहता है।

title: Nature trail to Fundătura Ponorului picturesque valley
short_description: This is a moderate route, accessible to anyone, which leads to Fundătura Ponorului - the idyllic place in Romania sought by mountaineers, occasional hikers, or photographers alike.
long_description:
The hiking route is organized as an educational path with 6 information panels, officially known as "Karst Relief from the Șureanu Mountains". It can be completed on foot or by bicycle (on the dirt road).
The Fundatura Ponor or God's Palm, as the place is sometimes called for its surreal beauty, close to the fairy tale, can be considered a unique place in Romania. At the end of the route, travelers discover a wide valley, with the Ponor river cutting its way all along the plateau, with scattered isolated households and with haystacks built by the locals. The area is, in fact, a karst depression located at an altitude of 900 meters. It resulted from the karstic action of Ponor river, which has cut into the Jurassic limestone rocks forming the photogenic ensembles of rocks seen here. The Ponor Valley stretches for 9 kilometers.
In the rainy season, the waters overflow, sometimes flooding the plateau, and in wintertime, they freeze, forming large icy segments, like ice rinks.

title: Stone mushrooms (Altai Mountains)
short_description: Stone mushrooms in the Altai have been growing «ng for millions of years. Earthquakes destroy them, and locals say that as soon as the last hat of the mushroom falls, the world will end. Is this true?
long_description: In the protected Akkurum tract, not far from the Chulyshman valley, where the two rivers Chulyshman and Chulcha merge into one, on the slope of Ak Korum Mountain (White scree in Altai) there are mushroom meadows resembling stone pillars with hats – they are also stone mushrooms. The place is picturesque and unique in its significance. The stalks of mushrooms reach a diameter of 1.5 meters and caps up to 2 meters. The caps are stronger than columns, which is why during earthquakes, mushroom stalks cannot withstand the rocking of the slope and some of them fall down quite hard. Trouble is, but new mushrooms appear, but how they grow again &lquo;raquo; in such a sacred protected area — it is a mystery, a riddle of the nature of the Altai. Does it happen that special rains pour down in the tract? We are yet to find out.

title: Rund um den Åsnen See

Dieser wunderschöne Fernradweg führt uns durch den Nationalpark Åsnen. Viel Waldgebiet und einige Gewässer erwarten uns auf unserer Tour.

long_description:
Eine herrliche Seenlandschaft, alte Laubwälder und Sumpfgebiete begleiten uns auf dieser Radtour um den Åsnen. Einige der Wege sind dabei nicht von Autos befahrbar, weshalb wir unterwegs ungestört in die Natur von Småland eintauchen können.
Zwischendurch können wir einige kulturell und geschichtlich interessante Sehenswürdigkeiten entdecken. Ein Abstecher nach Huseby Bruk, eine Pause beim Nationalpark-Eingang Trollberget oder ein Ausflug zur alten Kirche von Jät lohnen sich auf jeden Fall.
Verschiedene Unterkünfte und Einkehrmöglichkeiten versorgen uns unterwegs mit allem, was wir für unsere Tour brauchen. Unser Start- und Endpunkt in Alvesta ist mit öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln oder mit dem Auto gut zu erreichen.

title: Pacific Crest Trail (Triple Crown of Hiking)
short_description: Pacific Crest Trail is a long-distance hiking trail of more than 4000 km through the western USA. It leads from the Mexican border through California, Oregon and Washington up to the Canadian border.
long_description:
About 150 to 200 km inland of the West Coast rise the mountain chains of the Sierra Nevada and the Cascade Range. This is a trail for long-distance hikers and those who love challenges, for sure: To cross the mentioned mountains and conquer the 4100 km distance from Mexico to Canada. Hikers who take the whole trail at one go usually train months or even years beforehand. The ‘Triple Crown of Hiking’ refers to three major long-distance trails: Pacific Crest Trail, Appalachian Trail and Continental Divide Trail.
Nonetheless, even if you decide to hike only one leg of the PCT, you will be enchanted by the unmistakable beauty of the trail. So much so that most hikers eventually come back.  A major part of the trail leads through nature reserves and national parks, e.g., the well-known Yosemite National Park. Moreover, it covers five different climate zones, including deserts and 4000 m high peaks covered with snow. The Pacific Crest Trail is many things, but most of all, it is spectacular.

title: From Oetz to Oetzerau along the Auerklamm to Ambach
short_description: Through the tranquil village of Oetz, you briefly walk along the Kühtaierstraße before turning onto a forest path that leads over hill and dale towards Oetzerau. Once there, you cross some partly cultivated fields and meadows until you soon enter the mystical Auer Klamm. Here you can listen to and follow the soothing sound of the roaring water in the gorge.
long_description: The hike begins in the picturesque village of Oetz, which boasts an idyllic location. From here, the route continues along the Kühtaierstrasse towards Oetzerau. The first section along the road offers a wonderful opportunity to admire the surrounding mountains and valleys. After a short stretch, you turn onto a shady forest path that leads through dense, quiet forests and finally ends in Oetzerau via mountain villages such as Schlatt and Klingenburg.Oetzerau is a small, charming village that is perfect for a short rest to enjoy the rural atmosphere and the views of the wide fields and surrounding Alpine peaks. From here, a village road leads out onto the fields, where you can quickly continue hiking towards the fascinating Auer Klamm.The Auer Klamm itself is a true natural wonder, characterized by steep rock faces, roaring waterfalls and picturesque bridges. There are a variety of photo opportunities for nature lovers and opportunities to linger and marvel. The path through the gorge is well signposted and varied, but hikers should make sure they have sturdy shoes and sufficient surefootedness, as some sections can be challenging. This hike offers a perfect combination of cozy village paths, quiet forest trails and spectacular gorge passages. Ideal for nature lovers and adventurers alike, it enables an unforgettable experience in the breathtaking Tyrolean mountain landscape. Hikers should bring plenty of water and snacks and be prepared for changes in the weather. The route is family-friendly, but small children should be well supervised in the Auer Gorge.

title: Winter circular hike in Schönwald in the Black Forest via Tiefenbach
short_description: On this winter hike starting from Schönwald in the Black Forest, winter hikers are offered a varied landscape with some leisurely climbs.
long_description: The winter hike, which starts and ends at the town hall in Schönwald, first takes us through the Alpine Garden of Schönwald, which is beautiful to look at in summer, and then  across snow-covered meadows through the magnificent winter landscape of the S dschwarzwald Nature Park.Here we also pass the monument showing the birthplace of the cuckoo clock. In 1735, it was invented by Anton Ketterer in the farmhouse that used to stand here. Continue along the path and through a smaller section of forest to Tiefenbach. Then we walk via Escheck, the highest point of our winter hike, and the Dobel ski lift Schönwald back to the city. If you still have some energy left, you can also work off your energy on the toboggan run at the ski lift.

title: Saar-Rhine Path
short_description: The Saar-Rhine Trail starts in Saarbrücken and leads via Zweibrücken to Wörth am Rhein. On the hilly route through the Pfälzerwald Nature Park, we experience the sights and highlights of the region.
long_description:
The trail can be divided into many different stages according to individual needs. It starts in Saarbrücken and from Hassel follows the long-distance hiking trail "Saar-Rhein-Wanderung". The following is an alternative suggestion from the outdooractive.com editorial team for the Saar-Rhine Trail:
Stage 1: Saarbrücken- Bischmisheim - Kirkel (23 km)
The first hilly stage takes us along the Tiefeltsbach into the forest and then along the Wogbach into the valley of the Würzbach. Through Reichenbrunn and past Hassel we hike through Pirminiusland to the castle in Kirkel.
Stage 2: Kirkel - Zweibrücken (20 km)
From Kirkel, surrounded by seemingly endless forests, we head to Schwarzenacker, where we can visit the Roman museum of the same name as well as the Wörschweiler monastery ruins. After Kirrberg we reach Zweibrücken. The ducal palace of Zweibrücken, the duke's suburb, the largest rose garden in Europe as well as the Alexander and Karl churches are definitely worth a look.
Stage 3: Zweibrücken - Bottenbach (17 km)
Even before we reach Contwig, we see the St. Laurentius Church and the town's maypole. Now we are getting closer and closer to the German-French border. In Walshausen, we cross the Felsalbe and continue hiking through sparsely populated areas, alternating between wide fields and small forests.
Stage 4: Bottenbach - Ludwigswinkel (23 km)
Once again, long stretches of unspoilt nature await us and we continue in the area of the Palatinate-Lorraine border via Kröppen to Eppenbrunn, which is famous for its red sandstone formation. The last stretch to the spa town of Ludwigswinkel then takes us into a magnificent forest with numerous streams and ponds. At the Birkenfeld leisure park, we can treat ourselves to some diversion and relaxation.
Stage 5: Ludwigswinkel - Bobenthal (21 km)
Three castle ruins await us today: in Petersbächel the Wasigenstein, in Schönau the Blumenstein and in Nothweiler the Wegelnburg, the highest castle in the Palatinate. From Nothweiler at the latest, we realise that we are in the middle of the Dahner Felsenland and can take a look at the visitor mine before arriving at the stage's destination in Bobenthal.
Stage 6: Bobenthal - Kapsweyer (16 km)
After Bobenthal we reach Sankt Germanshof and touch the German-French border here. We then take a long curve to Schweigen-Rechtenbach, which is a special highlight of this long-distance hiking trail with its German Wine Gate. We continue through a wide landscape of fields and meadows to Kapsweyer.
Stage 7: Kapsweyer - Wörth am Rhein (25 km)
Today we experience a wonderful conclusion to the tour and walk leisurely through the Haardtrand and Bienwald nature reserves. Slightly downhill, we pass Bienwaldmühle, with a forest inn for refreshments, and then hike through the middle of the Bienwald. We take in the natural beauty of the region one last time and finally reach Wörth am Rhein, the finishing point of the long-distance trail.

title: Hiking in the Luberon via the Mur de la Peste
short_description: Beautiful discovery loop between the Monts de Vaucluse and the Petit Luberon massif, with an emblematic passage along the Mur de la Peste in Lagnes.
long_description:
Sometimes garrigue, sometimes pine forest... This route is a condensed version of Provencal landscapes along narrow paths, wide and sometimes stony paths.
Dry stone will also be present with the presence of sheds and the famous Mur de la Peste. The latter corresponds to the rampart built, in the Monts de Vaucluse, to fight against the spread of the plague, which struck Marseille and its region, during the years 1720-1722.
Bref, a hike made for people who love history and beautiful landscapes!

title: Walking between the Black Sea Coast resorts
short_description: A classic and leisurely walk from one resort to the other on the Romanian coastline. You can complete this walk at any time of the year, in any direction you prefer. It adds a touch of physical activity to a lazy vacation at the seaside, spent mainly at the beach.
long_description:
The walk takes you through all the small resorts near Mangalia - basically, through all the "villages" that are part of Mangalia, from an administrative point of view. You walk mainly on the beach or on so-called promenades. Along the way, you can detour through the resorts themselves, and take breaks for a swim in the sea or a meal.
The Romanian beach resorts at the Black Sea appeared between 1972-1973 in an engineering effort to capitalize on the access to the sea and boost tourism. As a result, their aesthetic appearance is relatively unitary. Until the 80s, the resorts enjoyed international fame, and the hotels here were recognized for their quality services. All resorts offer spa treatments for various ailments, based on the healing effects of mud and salt water.
The beaches do not differ much in terms of quality, but Neptun beach, in the La Steaguri area, is sometimes recommended for its fine sand and gentle entrance to the sea, suitable for families with children. However, these details can also be found on the rest of the beaches.

title: Raigarh Fort Tracking
short_description: Karnala Fort is a hill fort in the Raigad district of Maharashtra. 60 kms from Mumbai and 16 kms from Panvel. Located within the Karnala Bird Sanctuary, the fort is a popular trekking and tourism destination.
long_description:
The two-tiered Karnala Fort, located inside the Karnala Bird Sanctuary, is also called the "Funnel Fort" because of its shape. The fort was built in the 12th century and was occupied at various times by the Gujarati kings, the Mughals, the Maratha Empire, the Portuguese, and the British.
There are two trails for trekking till Karnala Fort-
Karnala Fort Trail :- It is a 2.7 kilometer trek from the bottom of the hill. There are 5 resting places on this route made by the Forest Department. The final climbing steps near the entrance of the fort are made safe by iron railings. The water of a water cistern cut out of the southern rock is potable.
Prakriti Trail - This is a short (1.20 kms) and uphill trek leading to the fort.
Being surrounded by hills and thick green foliage, this place is a very popular trekking spot. The area around it has been made a protected area in the year 1968 by giving the status of bird sanctuary. Apart from the fort, the temple of Bhavani Mata and many beautiful birds like Common Hawk Cuckoo, Jungle Owl, Alpine Swift, Ashi Minivet, Oriental Neelkanth, and Malabar Trogon are also seen here.

title: Trek to the Wei Sawdong Falls
short_description: The trek route to Wei Sawdong Falls is a half-kilometer terraced path that leads to a very beautiful and huge three-tiered waterfall which is situated about 10 kilometres from the beautiful town of Cherrapunji in Meghalaya.
long_description:
वेई सॉडाँग झरने पर पहुँचने पर लगता है की मानो एक जादुई दुनिया में पहुँच गए हों। झरना इतना सुन्दर है की यहाँ आने वाला हर हाइकर इसकी फोटो अपने सोशल मीडिया में साझा ज़रूर करता है।
इस झरने में तीन स्तर है और सभी में एक छोटा नीले साफ़ पानी का तालाब भी है। यहाँ तक आने के लिए देंथलेन रोड से किनारे से सीढ़ियां शुरू होती हैं। सीढ़ियों से उतरने के दौरान एक हिस्सा झरने के व्यूपॉइंट तक ले जाता है जहाँ से आप झरने की शानदार फोटो खींच सकते हैं। सीढ़ियों से उतरकर फिर आप झरने तक पहुँच जाते हैं।
यह ट्रैक मुश्किल से एक किलोमीटर लंबा है। अगर चेरापूंजी से साइकिल चला कर यहाँ आएं तब यह ट्रेक जरूर 10 किलोमीटर लम्बा हो जायेगा। पिकनिक और परिवार के संग एकदिवसीय छुट्टी मनाने ले लिए यह जगह बढ़िया है।

वेई सॉडोंग झरने के ट्रैक मार्ग पर लगा साइनबोर्ड, सोहरा, मेघालय।

The theme trail is also the most traveled part of the pier, with hikes sometimes continuing to the Great Tunnel. After the tunnel, the trail becomes difficult and requires more serious equipment.
On the portion marked as a thematic trail, information boards about the carnivores of the Tișița Nature Reserve have been placed, as well as interactive boxes. On the trail there is also a recreated bear den or artificial animal tracks.
The theme trail is accessible all year round. In rainy weather, however, there may be difficulties walking some sections with chains or ladders.

title: A trip around Lake Vilsalpsee
short_description: A short and circular hiking route that surrounds the wonderful Villasalfeza lake in Tyrol, Austria
long_description:
This hiking route encompasses in about an hour's walk a lake known as Villes-Alpesa, which is surrounded on all sides by a gorgeous panoramic view of the Alps. The route is mostly flat with a very slight uphill slope (10 meters in total). You can of course go in any direction you want and also take a walk only along one of the banks of the lake and come back or alternatively/in addition to rent a rowing boat and sail on the lake's waters. The waters of the lake have a mesmerizing blue hue and in the shallow part are incredibly transparent.
Depending on the conditions prevailing in the place, this trip is suitable and special even in the winter months, during which the lake freezes and the mountains are covered with snow.
The route is not paved but it is possible in principle to walk at least most of it with a stroller.

title: Akita Komagatake, Amida Pond, Mt.
short_description: If you visit in the summer season, you can enjoy alpine flora, walk along wooden paths around Amida Pond, climb Mt.
long_description:
From the 8th station of Akita Komagatake, which can be accessed by car, the route follows the Shindo trail and climbs to the summit of Mt. On the way back, the course returns to the 8th station at the starting point via Yokodake and Yakimori via the Baba no Koji trail, also commonly known as Moomin Valley, and Oyakisuna.　Akita Komagatake is attractive for the variety of alpine plants that delight the eye throughout the seasons, but it is particularly beautiful in the vicinity of Amida Pond and along Baba no Koji, with flower gardens such as Chinguruma and Nikkoukisuge, and in the Komakusa colonies found in Oyakasuna and Yakimori. The view from the Katakura-dake Observatory and the Nyose-dake (Male and Female Mountains) is also an important attraction.
At the 8th station, there is a mountain hut where water and toilets are available and where you can make preparations. The first viewpoint after starting the course is the Katakura-dake Observatory. From here you have a clear view of Mount Moriyoshi and Lake Tazawa, and on a clear day you can also see the Shirakami mountain range and Mount Chokaisan. As you approach Amida Pond, the trail turns into a wooden path. Due to the alpine flora in its native habitat, do not deviate from the wooden path. Amida Pond is surrounded by Mt. Flowers such as Chinese linden, red spider lilies, and day lilies can be enjoyed. On the east side, a refuge hut and toilets have been built, making it ideal for a break. From the top of Akita Komagatake you can enjoy a 360° panoramic view of Otoko-dake, Onna-dake and Lake Tazawa to the west, and on a clear day you can even see Mt Chokaisan in the distance.
Return to Amida Pond and turn left at the fork between Yokodake and Baba no Koji. From here, you will finally reach the Moomin Valley, commonly known as Moomin Valley, with its beautiful flower fields. Enjoy the large colonies of chinguruma and other alpine plants around you. From the Baba no Koji and Oyakidake branches to Yokodake, the ascent continues. Oyakisada, especially in July, when large colonies of komakusa grow. After passing the peak of Yokodake, descend to the goal while passing through Yakimori with a fine cairn on the way.

title: Hiking Iezer Ighiel - Ciumerna Plateau - Frumoasa Cave (unvisitable)
short_description: An easy hike through the forest to the Ciumerna Plateau and on to the Hăldăhaia Meadow. The purpose of the hike was to search for the Frumoasa Cave.
long_description:
The starting point, Lake Ighiel, is particularly picturesque. Situated in a caldera, surrounded by forests, the lake changes colour depending on how the sun's rays reflect in the water.
The forest you have to cross to reach the Ciumerna Plateau is particularly beautiful, with tall, thick-crowned trees. In decoy season, the forest is overgrown with this plant, so crossing on the marked path can have a whiff of... garlic.
The mountain scenery is completed by the appearance of some abandoned huts, probably used by local shepherds when crossing with their flocks of sheep. The wide meadows on the plateau, as well as the abandoned hut in the middle of the plateau, can be used as a place to camp or shelter if needed.
Discarding the official names, found on signposts or maps, the route also passes through Poiana Hăldăhaia, an unofficial name, known only among locals or geographers. Here there is a superb view of the Gorges of Capra. In the warm season, the meadows in this area are covered with wildflowers, which sprout like drops of bright colours - yellow, pink, blue - from place to place.
The Beautiful Cave can be found near the Hăldăhaia Stone, in the area known as Hăldăhaia Mică.
The trail does not officially pass through here, but follows the course of a water and continues up to the top of Dambau through a hilly, wooded relief. From the plateau to the summit takes about 4-5 hours.

title: Around the Brocken
short_description: For those who already know the Brocken and the Hexenstieg, this hike from Ilsenburg via Braunlage and Schierke to Wernigerode is just right. We hike along lesser-known paths through the beautiful Harz mountains - a detour to the Brocken is of course also possible.
long_description:
Stage 1: Ilsenburg - Braunlage (25 km)
The first stage is demanding due to its length, but easy to manage. First we follow the Ilse into the forest from Ilsenburg. In the Ilse valley and along the Tiefenbach stream, we reach the Scharfensteinklippe ranger station - here you can get fresh spring water. We then hike in a south-westerly direction, partly on the Harzer Grenzweg (former column trail of the German-German border) to Eckersprung and past the Dreieckiger Pfahl memorial stone. The route then follows the Bode to Achtermannshöhe and via Königskrug to Braunlage.
Stage 2: Braunlage - Schierke (17 km)
We start our tour in Braunlage and hike in the Harz National Park to the potato monument. Now we continue through the forest and a short stretch parallel to the B242. We then walk through the Harz stream valleys on the Harzer Hexenstieg (Harz Witches' Trail) to Elend and follow the Kalte Bode to Schierke, where we should definitely try the famous herbal liqueur Schierker Feuerstein. From here, we either hike up to the Brocken the next day or head straight for the third and final stage of the tour.
Stage 3: Schierke - Wernigerode (18 km)
From Schierke railway station, which lies in the middle of the forest and exudes the flair of a model railway, we walk past the Erdbeerkopf and the Hohenstein cliffs to Wernigerode. On the way we experience the wonderful natural beauty of the Harz, see old tall trees and how life bustles in the forest. Once in Wernigerode, we can visit the castle and stroll through the small streets with half-timbered houses. In addition, the Brockenbahn goes up the mountain from here.
