title: La Panoramique snowshoe trail - Gourette
short_description: Take this snowshoe hike to discover the area around Gourette resort and Lake Bézou!
long_description:
Leaving the gondola at the Bézou plateau, follow the terrace of the high-altitude restaurant Le Cairn to the totem pole marking the start of the circuit. Walk past the Pitchouns chairlift to reach Lac de Bézou. This body of water is a reserve for the production of artificial snow, generated by spraying micro-droplets of water into the air. For this snow to be produced, temperatures must be negative, without the addition of additives. Continue along the right-hand side of the lake to join the snowshoe trail that climbs towards the forest. You can also walk around the lake to discover effortless snowshoeing.
After a short, slow climb, which is the only difficulty of the route, you enter the forest. The wide, winding trail winds through beech and fir trees, giving you the opportunity to observe the tracks and clues left by animals in the snow. Shortly afterwards, you'll reach an emblematic point, easily identifiable by its large antenna: the relay station. Continue on the trail which, after a few hundred metres, turns sharply to the left to return to the starting point. It rises slightly above the one you followed on the outward journey. After a few bends, you gradually emerge from the forest.
The route still follows the wide track, which this time offers you a view overlooking Lac de Bézou. The trail crosses small cliffs, creating gaps that add a unique touch to the journey. The forest gives way to snowfields. The trail continues to the lake, offering exceptional panoramic views of the Gourette cirque and surrounding mountains. After two downhill hairpin bends, the trail reaches the lake. All that's left to do is return to the start of the Pitchouns chairlift and head back up to the Le Cairn high-altitude restaurant. Don't forget: it's forbidden to use the ski runs with snowshoes, in accordance with a municipal by-law.

images.caption: snowshoeing in Pyrénées-Atlantiques: La Panoramique snowshoe trail

title: Emmerweg
short_description: The Emmerweg follows the Emmer, a tributary of the Weser, from its source to its mouth. Along the way, we experience numerous impressions of the beautiful Weserbergland. All three stages can be comfortably reached by train.
long_description:
Stage 1: Altenbeken - Steinheim (24 km)
On the first stage we hike from the source of the Emmer to Steinheim. The second section in particular is characterised by a wide landscape of fields and meadows. In Steinheim we should not miss the Vinsebeck moated castle, which is considered one of the most beautiful castles in Westphalia.
Stage 2: Steinheim - Bad Pyrmont (24 km)
Today a very scenic section awaits us at the Schiedersee ("Emmerstausee"), which serves both as flood protection and recreation for locals and tourists. Via Lügde we then head to Bad Pyrmont. The medieval town offers the fortress and castle of Pyrmont, the "Hylligen Born" fountain temple and the Evangelical Lutheran town church as well as other impressive sights.
Trip 3: The route continues via Lügde to Bad Pyrmont.
Stage 3: Bad Pyrmont - Emmerthal (19 km)
The alternation between forest, such as the Pyrmont Forest, and fields determines today's character of the tour. On the last stage, we accompany the Emmer to Emmerthal, where it flows into the Weser.

title: Tête du Vuargne hiking trail
short_description: From the Col de Joux Plane, this route invites you to discover the Tête du Vuargne alpine massif, offering superb panoramic views of the surrounding area.
long_description:
Departure is from the Col de Joux Plane, at an altitude of around 1700 m, offering immediate panoramic views of the surrounding peaks and valleys below. This high starting point allows you to plunge straight into the adventure, with a breathtaking view of Mont Blanc on a clear day. The first steps take you along a well-marked trail, winding through an alpine landscape dotted with boulders and verdant meadows.
The ascent to the Tête du Vuargne begins gently, offering unobstructed views of the Lac de Joux Plane. The trail passes through areas of alpine moorland where local flora, including wildflowers and bilberry bushes, add touches of color and vibrancy to the landscape. As you advance, the climb becomes steeper, but the spectacular panoramas revealed at every turn make the effort well worthwhile.
On reaching the Tête du Vuargne, you'll discover a summit offering exceptional panoramic views of Mont Blanc and the Chablais massifs. It's an ideal spot for a well-earned break, where you can soak up the beauty of the landscape and take some memorable photos. The 360-degree view is particularly impressive, offering a fascinating glimpse of Alpine geography and the valleys nearby.
In front of the Ranfolly chairlift station (Les Gets ski area), an orientation table lets you put a name to the peaks around you. Following the edge of the ridge, the path descends gently to the Co road and back to the lake.

title: Countryside walk Sawston, Babraham, Stapleford (Tracked)

long_description: This route starts in the North East of Sawston. Upon leaving Wakelin Avenue you briefly head onto Babraham Road before turning left off road down a public footpath. Here you will be on a public footpath walking through fields until entering Stapleford. There are picturesque views along the way with no roads or housing in sight. At one point you cross a small stream. The route ends at the Rose Pub in Stapleford.

title: Thermal trough from the plains to the volcanic region beyond the Bakony
short_description: Soaking in the warm water after a long roll is always a turn off. This thermal loop connects 15 thermal spas across the country in a multi-day cycling tour.
long_description: On this multi-day cycling tour, you can get to know the Kiskunság countryside, followed by a visit to the thermal baths of the Danube plain. After leaving the river, we will wander through the Mezőföld and pass Lake Venice. Then we will cross the Northern Bakony and leave it for the Marcal Basin. Along the way, we can stop in the country's largest wine region, take a refreshing dip in the Danube or Lake Venice, visit the birthplaces of our famous poets and many other beautiful natural and architectural monuments.

title: Belemedik - Kiralan
short_description: The Belemedik - Kıralan route offers beautiful landscapes for nature lovers as well as history and culture.
long_description:
A special route for those looking for nature routes in Adana is the Belemedik - Kıralan route. 
About 20 kilometres in length, this trail has varying degrees of difficulty and requires some experience. If you are with someone who knows the region or if you are familiar with the region and have knowledge of mountaineering - mountaineering - mountaineering - mountaineering, it is a track that you will enjoy. Otherwise it is a difficult track. To have an idea about the structure and slope of the region, you can take advantage of the 3D ön monitoring feature.
Starting from Belemedik, the route stretches parallel to the Akıt Suyu. After a long walk, you arrive at Kıralan. Due to the line where the route known as the service road is located and the tünel and old ruins you come across during the route, your journey is accompanied by a richness of history and culture. In addition, you are also faced with many rock formations.
Those who do the route usually camp and stay on the route. Otherwise, you will spend too much energy for a day on this long journey. Since it is a long and sloping route, you need to be equipped on the road. In other words, your equipment must be complete and you must have enough food and drinks.

title: Ascent to Leaota Peak from Brătei Cabin
short_description: Leaota Mountains sometimes seem uninteresting in terms of natural scenery, compared to their much more popular neighbors - Bucegi Mountains. And though the routes in the Leaota Mountains have less variety, they can be rewarding for mountain lovers. This ascent to the highest peak, starting from Brătei Cabin, is one of them.
long_description:
This isn't the main route to the peak, but a secondary one, so little sought after. Besides, the ascent is almost continuous to the top, so more than 6 kilometers of non-stop climbing, while the scenery can be desolating at times. Those who venture on such trails are never casual hikers.
The route starts from Brătei Cabin, a place that you can take as a base camp if you want also to spend a few nights away from the city rumble.
For a start, you cross two streams: one on a bridge, the other straight through the water. Then comes a steep climb of about 10 minutes, that gets you to an area devastated by deforestation. The marked route becomes hard to follow at this point.
But, following the exploitation off-road you reach the forest above, and you should find the signs again. The signs are very visible in the forest, so don't get discouraged and look for them.
In about an hour or so, the forest hike takes you to a clearing from where you can see the main ridge, especially Răteiul Peak. Your final destination seems to be getting closer. And still...
After another 10-15 minutes, you leave for the forest, into the main ridge, just above the Răteiul sheepfold (abandoned in the winter). 
From here on, you keep climbing only on the main ridge, while the panoramic views keep opening up. To your right, you have a superb panorama towards the Bucegi Mountains, and to your left, towards the secondary valleys or peaks of Leaota.
When you reach Răteiul Peak, the panorama truly becomes 360 degrees, including the Iezer-Păpușa or Piatra Craiului Mountains. It stays with you all the way to the top, at 2133 meters.
The way back will surely seem easier and shorter unless something unexpected happens; you have already cleared your path and returns always seem shorter.

title: Rhine-Nahe Wine Trail - Stage 3
short_description: The third stage of the Rhine-Nahe Wine Trail leads through the Rotenfels nature reserve and Bad Kreuznach to Bretzenheim.
long_description: The third stage of the Rhine-Nahe Wine Trail takes us through a varied landscape. A wide vineyard landscape, forest, field and meadow paths alternate. The Nahe River is also usually in our field of vision on this stage or we hike directly along it. Highlights of the stage are probably the Rotenfels, the highest continuous steep face north of the Alps, Bad Kreuznach, the largest town along the route, and the Salinental, the largest natural open-air inhalatorium in Europe.

title: चोकरामुडी पीक ट्रैक
short_description: चोकरामुडी मुन्नार की सबसे ऊंची चोटियों में से एक है जो नेचर प्रेमियों क ो एक शानदार और रोमांचक ट्रैकिंग अनुभव देती है।
long_description:
चोकरामुडी पीक का ट्रैक केरल राज्य के कुछ सबसे ज्यादा लोकप्रिय ट्रैक्स में से एक है। यह ट्रैक छोटा लेकिन दमदार है। एकतरफा ट्रैक मार्ग 2 किलोमीटर लंबा और आना जाना मिलाकर कुल 4 किलोमीटर लम्बा है।
यह ट्रेल राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग 85 (कोच्चि-मदुरै-धनुषकोडी रोड) पर गैप बस स्टॉप से शुरू होती है। माना जाता है यह ट्रेल/पगडण्डी प्राचीन काल से हाथियों चलने से बनी हैं।
ट्रेल का कठिनाई स्तर मध्यम है और इसमें थोड़ी चढ़ाई भी है। ट्रेल के दोनों तरफ हरियाली है और लाल मिटटी की यह पगडण्डी साफ़-सुथरी है और पथरीली नहीं है। ट्रेल का अंतिम हिस्सा लगभग पहाड़ चढ़ने जैसा ही है।
यह ट्रेल चोकरामुडी पीक पर जाकर खत्म होती है। पर्वत शिखर से आसपास से शोला जंगलों और नीलगिरी पहाड़ियों का दृश्य देखे देता है। यहाँ का नज़ारा बेहद सुन्दर है। सूर्यास्त का दृश्य भी मनमोहक दिखता है और हरी-नीली पहाड़ियों के झुंड में तैरते सफ़ेद बादल किसी जादुई पेंटिंग जैसे लगते हैं। केरल आने वाले हर हाइकर की लिस्ट में यह ट्रैक ज़रूर मौजूद रहता है।

title: Sjöstigen Seerunde
short_description:
Diese einfache Wanderung führt uns auf Pfaden und Holzstegen einmal um den Bräkentorpasjön.
Translate to English
long_description:
Nicht weit von der Stadt Ljungby entfernt befindet sich das Landschaftsschutzgebiet Bräkentorp. Der gleichnamige See ist nicht nur bei SUP- und Kajakfahrern beliebt. Dank der vielen Rastbänke rund um den Bräkentorpasjön bietet sich dieser auch herrlich für gemütliche Wanderungen an.
Auf unserer Runde um den See wechseln sich verschiedene Wege ab, wobei wir auf sandigen Pfaden ebenso unterwegs sind wie auf schmalen Stegen aus Holzbrettern, die uns sicher über den nassen Waldboden bringen. Unterwegs erhaschen wir immer wieder wunderschöne Blicke auf den See und einige Badestellen laden uns dazu ein, schwimmen zu gehen.
Auf der Westseite der Halbinsel treffen steile, mit Kiefern bewachsene Hänge des Gebirgskammes auf den nährstoffarmen See. Auf der Ostseite geht er in flache Sandfelder und Feuchtwiesen über. An mehreren Stellen finden wir historische Überreste wie Grabstätten, Runensteine und Ruinen von Gebäuden mit Informationstafeln.

title: Shiyundezan Ohama trailhead course
short_description: This route, which was featured in the New York Times in the USA, takes you to the summit of Mount Shiyunode, a mountain with the beauty of the Seto Inland Sea's many islands and the changing nature of the four seasons.
long_description:
This course takes you to the summit of the highest mountain on the Shonai Peninsula, the 352-metre-high Mount Shikunode. It is also part of the Shikoku no Michi. Mount Shikumoide is in the Setonaikai National Park area, and the mountain is beautifully decorated with approximately 1000 cherry trees in spring, hydrangeas in early summer and flowers of all four seasons. A breathtaking view of the many islands of the Seto Inland Sea awaits you as you walk along the nature-rich promenade to the top of the mountain. The mountain has attracted attention as it was the only Japanese mountain to be listed in the New York Times as one of the 52 destinations to visit in 2019.
There is a shuttle bus service from the foot of the mountain during the spring cherry blossom festival, but the view from the summit after walking from the foot of the mountain is exceptional. After passing the erosion control dam, the trail climbs steeply in places, but there are also sections where you can walk on the roadway. To avoid stress on the feet, we recommend shoes with soft soles that are easier to exercise in than mountaineering boots. The path is not easy to see until you reach the road, but from the road you can see the sea and the fishing port through the trees, and you will be in a good mood for the summit. At the top, there are shady spots where you can picnic, and in spring you can enjoy cherry blossom viewing with the best views.

title: From Sarmizegetusa to Ohaba Ponor on Via Transilvanica trail
short_description: This 30km route between Sarmizegetusa Dacian Fortress to the village of Ohaba Ponor is one of the most picturesque (in my opinion) on Via Transilvanica long-distance route. It can easily qualify as THE leg you should take if it's your first time in Romania.
long_description:
Here are a few reasons:
you get to see the nucleus of the Dacian fortresses and of the Dacian people, the ancestors of the Romanian people. Sarmizegetusa was the most important Dacian fortress and the surrounding natural landscape is mesmerizing. No wonder some say they feel a certain powerful energy around it.
you take to the paths in the Grădiștea Muncelului-Cioclovina Natural Park, one of the most mysterious and lush natural parks in the country
you enjoy a beautiful, peaceful natural landscape like you've rarely seen
you reach Fundatura Ponorului, sometimes called "the God's hand", a lush valley shaped like a cavity in between rocks, with the greenest pasture and a river meaning its way only to disappear into the underground
In Fundatura Ponorului you will find a few isolated summer cottages, with a handful of people living there all year long, seeing to their cattle. You can take shelter here, and buy dairy products from the people.
In the official Traveler's Guide onVia Transilvanica, this route is separated into two legs, to be covered in two days so that you can actually enjoy a night here, at Fundatura Ponorului.

title: Climbing the Rohnenspitze in winter (1,990 m), Tannheimer Tal
short_description: A route that is perfect for a morning trip and represents a varied and fun challenge for more experienced winter hikers. Plenty of ozone and fresh air are assured.
long_description:
Although not especially high, the ridgeline up to the Rohnenspitze is quite craggy when approached from the south and in snow, the ascent to the summit from the Bergwacht-Hütte takes on a whole new angle of fun, with some of the smaller sections bordering on the sketchy side. 
However, with some great views across the Tannheimer Tal and back towards the Allgäuer Hochalpen, the trip is definitely a  rewarding one and short enough to ensure you don't have to worry too much about limited winter sunlight.  
Snow conditions on the day will dictate whether you'll want to put on pair of trail spikes, snowshoes, or just your boots, so keep an eye on the weather a few days in advance. In our case, both came in handy, as shaded and less exposed areas came with deeper snow. 
You might like to also check out my other winter route that takes you up the neighbouring B'shießer: Climbing B'shießer in winter (2,000 m) 
Have fun.

title: To the gravel bank on the Iller
short_description: The easy, leisurely tour takes us for an extended rest along the Iller.
long_description: From the station we follow Bahnhofstra&szlig to Marienplatz. We pass the Nikolauskirche (St. Nicholas Church) and cross the roundabout to Salzstra&szlig. Along the railway we walk north to the tunnel at the primary school. We cross under the tracks. Behind the kindergarten lies the school centre, where we turn left. Along the Hochrainebach stream and the hospital we walk to the football pitch and skate park. At the playground we cross the stream. Between it and the Konstanzer Ache it is only a few minutes to its mouth. Behind the bend in the path we walk down to the gravel bank. After the rest, we follow the Iller dam sideways to the Illersteg. Westwards we go back to the school centre. We return to the primary school along the same route. At the gymnasium we keep to the right. Through Grüntenstra;e we reach St. Nikolaus Platz. and further on to Klosterplatz. On the left hand side is Marienplatz. We walk through Bahnhofstrasse back to the station.

title: Hike to Lac des Chambres via the Folly refuge
short_description: From the Pied du Crêt parking lot, follow this itinerary to discover the surprising Lac des Chambres, which is rarely completely filled with water and more often than not evokes a polar landscape.
long_description:
Departure is from the La Chapelle d'Abondance parking lot, a convenient access point to the region's hiking trails. Right from the start, the trail takes you through a dense fir forest, offering a cool, shady atmosphere. The climb is gradual, allowing you to soak up the calm and serenity of the forest landscape before reaching the Folly refuge.
The Folly refuge, at an altitude of around 1560 meters, is a welcome stopover for a break and refreshments. It offers breathtaking views of the surrounding mountains and is an excellent starting point for the rest of the hike. The refuge, with its warm and friendly atmosphere, is an ideal place to rest before continuing on to Lac des Chambres. Take the opportunity to admire the alpine panoramas and prepare for the final ascent.
From the Folly refuge, the trail climbs more steeply towards the Lac des Chambres. This section is a little more demanding, but the spectacular views and scenic beauty are well worth the effort. The trail winds through alpine meadows and rocky areas, offering ever-wider panoramas of the surrounding valleys and peaks. At every turn, the view of the surrounding mountains unfolds further, creating a breathtaking picture of alpine natural beauty.
When you reach Lac des Chambres, you'll discover an enchanting mountain lake surrounded by majestic peaks. This alpine lake, with its crystal-clear waters and peaceful setting, is an ideal place to relax, picnic and enjoy the scenery. The reflections of the mountains in the water add a magical dimension to the environment, creating a fascinating visual experience.
The return journey follows the same path, but with new perspectives on the scenery. The descent allows you to enjoy panoramic views of mountains and valleys once again, while admiring the diversity of the alpine landscapes you've traversed.

title: Fumaça Waterfall Trail
short_description: Incredible trail to one of the most beautiful waterfalls in São Paulo and a natural pool for a refreshing and unforgettable swim.
long_description:
The complete trail that leads to é the fuma ça waterfall has about 6 km round trip. However, although it is not very long, it is full of obstacles and adventures. You can cross mud pools and rivers, and given the diversity of sceneries, it is a very fun trail. Before reaching the end point, one finds a natural pool, perfect for a break and a swim.
The name of the waterfall é because of the névoa that the waterfall does. A little because of the heat, another because of the wind, but part of the áwater that will fall on the rocks is suspended in the air forming néflies. During the course of the trail, we will see many times the railway, the Death Valley, the immense rocky masses common in the route of the Serra do Mar and in some parts, we can see the immense blue sea and even the industries of Cubatilatildeo. On site, between rocks and trees, and with the scorching sun, sunscreen and repellent will be your best friends.

title: Costa da Lagoa Trail in Floripa
short_description: Get to know a little of the history and culture of the small villages of the Lagoa da Conceiço region, in Florianópolis. Enjoy a waterfall bath, taste the typical cuisine and marvel at the rich local biodiversity.
long_description:
A trail é a path from colonial times,  éo time when the region was surrounded by farms and mills. The trail is surrounded by the Atlantic Forest, well signposted, easy and without steep slopes. You will pass through small villages, wooden decks à edge of the lagoon and some historical buildings. The most famous of them is the Sobrado da Dona Loquinha, one of the oldest buildings in Santa Catarina. The house was built around 1780 with slave labour and you can see the sign marking the place where the flour mill and the coffee plant were located.
Another highlight of the trail é the waterfall  of Costa da Lagoa, a perfect place for a refreshing swim. Afterwards, choose one of the various restaurants in the village to enjoy the view and the local cuisine.

title: 5 Lakes Circuit and Pedra do Altar in Itatiaia Park
short_description: Perfect trail for those who wish to do a light hike, even with children, on the Itatiaia plateau and get to know a large part of Brazil's 1st National Park.
long_description:
<The trail is in the high part of Itatiaia National Park, on border between states Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais, municipalities Itataia Itamonte.
Although it is 12 kilometres long, the route is considered easy, as it does not have many climbs and descents. The trail begins at an altitude of approximately 2,400 metres and it is possible to enjoy the landscape and the distinctive vegetation of the Serra da Mantiqueira.
During the way, you é will pass by small lakes of altitude and the Pedra do Altar, with 2,665 meters of altitude. It is the 11th highest mountain in Brazil, so take the opportunity to rest at the top and enjoy the incredible view from the top. Then, the trail goes through the base of Pico das Agulhas Negras (Black Needles Peak), and it is also possible to see the Prateleiras Mountain in the distance, until reaching the Rebouças Shelter. From here it is another 3 kilometres along the road back to Posto Marcenildeo and the car park.

title: Coast at its best: In Sweden's archipelago
short_description: This loop south of the well-known island of Marstrand north of Gothenburg is a dreamlike combination of archipelago coast and nature reserve. It is highly recommended to pack a bathing suit and a picnic.
long_description: This loop near the beautifully situated Lycke golf course leads us through a nature reserve and a long stretch directly along the sea. Especially in the evening, this round is worthwhile; if the weather is good, hikers can expect dreamlike evening atmospheres by the sea. In places, wooden plank paths lead across the damp meadows. Old stone walls covered in moss and lichen line the path. The glaciers have smoothed the rocks by the sea, offering a whole range of wonderful picnic spots. If you are out and about at the right time of year, you can pick mushrooms in the forest for dinner. The hikers share the last stretch along the golf course with the riders from the nearby hotel.

title: Gullholmen - Archipelago round off Sweden's coast
short_description: Gullholmen is the inhabited part of a peninsula of the large island of Orust about 50 km north of Gothenburg. Here you can combine the romance of the archipelago with a leisurely walk across the island and through the nature reserve. Gullholmen is car-free and can only be reached by boat.
long_description: Gullholmen is an island off the west coast of the island of Orust in the middle of the most beautiful archipelago in western Sweden. Like many of the smaller inhabited archipelagos, Gullholmen is car-free and can only be reached by boat. A trip to Gollhulmen is definitely worthwhile. Here, nature and archipelago romance can be wonderfully combined with a picnic and a tour of the islands. The picturesquely situated wooden fishermen's cottages, painted in the typical Falun red, give visitors the impression of a paradisiacal landscape. The island's hinterland impresses with a rocky coastline and small bays, some of which even have sandy micro-beaches. So if you visit Gullholmen in the summer, be sure to pack your swimsuit and a picnic. The car park is about five minutes' walk from the boat landing stage, so it's a good idea to check the boat timetable before you arrive. You should also note the return times if you don't want to spend the night on Gullholmen.

title: Walking loop between Samoëns and Verchaix
short_description: Lovely loop hike to discover Samoëns and Verchaix, notably along the Giffre.
long_description:
The route starts in Samoëns, a charming Alpine village with a rich history and picturesque setting. The route starts in the heart of the village, where you can admire the traditional stone houses and flower-filled alleyways.
Halfway along, you'll arrive at the picturesque village of Verchaix, where you can pause to explore and discover the local charm. Verchaix is an authentic little village with traditional buildings and a tranquil atmosphere. It's an ideal place to relax, enjoy a picnic or simply stroll the streets and appreciate the local architecture.
After crossing the bridge, you can see the blue lake before continuing along the Giffre and crossing back over the R'Biolle footbridge to Samoëns, the starting point for this hike.

title: Rondane Triangle
short_description: The Rondane triangle route is one of the most famous Norwegian multi-day hikes. The five day trek takes you into the heart of Rondane National Park, Norway’s oldest.
long_description:
The route starts with a short first day, hiking from Spranget parking lot to the Rondvassbu cabin. From Rondvassbu, after a boat ride across Rondvatnet Lake, begins three days of fairly long hikes that form a triangle through the national park. The final day is the return leg from Rondvassbu to Spranget.
The stage between Spranget and Rondvassbu takes only about two hours to walk, so it’s possible to do a longer hike on the first or last day and complete the route in three or four days. However, it’s recommended to allocate 5 days in total and use the first and last days to travel to and from Rondane.

title: Dolomites high trail 4
short_description: The Dolomites High-Altitude Trail No. 4 leads from San Candido in the Puster Valley through the eastern Dolomites to Pieve di Cadore in the province of Belluno.
long_description: Trail no. 4 is one of the shorter, but at the same time also one of the more demanding Dolomite high-altitude trails. Numerous sections lead over secured paths and also include free climbing passages up to the II degree of difficulty, which requires alpine experience and climbing skills. The high-altitude trail continuously inspires with breathtaking high-mountain landscapes - with the mighty Three Peaks starting over the craggy Cadini group and the mighty stock of the Sorapiss group up to Monte Antelao, the second highest peak of the Dolomites, this tour can hardly be surpassed in impressive scenery. The high-altitude trail is also called the Grohmann high-altitude trail, as it is dedicated to the Austrian alpinist Paul Grohmann. The trail is marked with the Dolomites High Altitude Trail markings as well as red-white-red markings. In the following, the route is divided into eleven sections, mostly the high-altitude trail is mastered in six to eight daily stages.

title: Short Walk Around Kursunlu Waterfall
short_description: A short walk around Kurşunlu Waterfall in a magnificent nature and accompanied by the peaceful sounds of nature
long_description:
Kurşunlu Waterfall is located in a very favourable area for nature walks. The waterfall is known for the paths around it, the bird sounds you hear while walking on these paths and its wonderful nature. This very popular waterfall is a great address for anyone who wants to meet nature in Antalya.
This route around Kurşunlu Waterfall is a short but very enjoyable route. You can come here together with your family and friends and enjoy the magnificent nature thanks to this short route.
There are paths with green trees and paths evolving with each other, and the göz attractive beauty of the waterfall seems to büyüler you and opens the doors of a different world. Local and foreign tourists who come here can catch the meaning of being quiet and peaceful here, while admiring the natural beauty of this place.
Anyone who wants to relieve the stress of a busy day and have a good time in nature can try this cosy route.

title: South Tyrol Sky Trail - Percorso corto
short_description: This tour is new to the Südtirol Ultra Skyrace event which is held annually at the end of July and it represents a perfect way to access the world of trailrunning.
long_description: The route is the same as the second section of the Südtirol Skyrace and is ideally suited for all athletes who are starting trail running and would like to gain a first experience in mountain running.

title: 17 Mile Drive
short_description: This coastal street alongside the Pacific is a feast for the eyes: Spectacular views of wildlife and bizarre rock formations make this sceneric route a unique experience.
long_description: The 17-Mile Drive is a famous road leading along the Monterey Peninsula from the city of Monterey to Carmel-by-the-sea, passing by the legendary Pebble Beach golf resorts. Alongside the route you will find several stunning viewpoints over the picturesque coastline and its spectacular wildlife. Especially the idyllic cypress forests with their natural beauty offer a unique attraction to the visitor. With all these sights and impressions you surely won’t mind the speed limit, as it gives you the opportunity of taking them all in. From Carmel-by-the-Sea you’ll get back directly to Pacific Grove Gate at Sunset Drive. Please keep in mind that motorcycles are not allowed on 17-Mile Drive.

images.caption: Spanish Bay, one of the viewpoints closest to Monterey
At Bird Rock you might see lots of seagulls and even cormorants.
Fanshell Overlook is a natural spot next to 17-Mile Drive.

Pebble Beach has it all: the dream-like beaches and the breathtaking views.

title: Hike to Col de la Golèse
short_description: North of Samoëns, this hike is ideal for those looking for a challenging climb and magnificent views.
long_description:
The Col de la Golèse hike, starting from the Plan des Arches parking lot, is a rewarding experience for mountain enthusiasts. The route takes around 3 hours round trip, with a vertical drop of around 550 metres, and is suitable for intermediate hikers. The trail begins in a peaceful atmosphere, first passing through a larch forest before opening out onto flower-filled alpine meadows. Along the way, you can spot marmots and enjoy magnificent views over the Giffre valley.
Halfway up, the climb becomes steeper, but the views improve with every step. Once you reach the pass, at an altitude of over 1600 metres, you'll be rewarded with spectacular views of the Dents Blanches and surrounding peaks. This is the perfect spot for a well-deserved break, where you can enjoy a picnic while admiring the alpine scenery. This hike is ideal for those seeking an immersion in nature, combining physical effort with scenic beauty.

title: From Albisheim to the memorial
short_description: This moderately difficult hike takes us through the vineyards and meadows of the Vorderpfalz.
long_description: This moderately difficult hike takes us through the vineyards and meadows of the Vorderpfalz. Along the way we enjoy magnificent views from the Osterberg and pass the memorial and the natural monument "Schwarzer Hergott".

title: Crown Princess Victoria of Sweden Hiking in Skåne
short_description: On 12 June 2018, Swedish Crown Princess Victoria visited Skåne for one of her hikes. The hike started in Stenhuvuds National Park and ended in Brösarp.
long_description:
Crown Princess Victoria of Sweden has set out to walk through all the provinces of Sweden. This has resulted in a number of royal trails that can be followed in the footsteps of the crown princess. These trails are not to be confused with the Kungsled in Lapland, however, which is very demanding.
Stenshuvuds National Park was established in 1986 and covers 200 square kilometres. The hike first went up Stenshuvud Mountain, which is over 90 metres high. From here, with a good view, you can see as far as Bornholm. Crown Princess Victoria took a break in Vitemölla before continuing in the afternoon via Haväng, Skepparp and Kungsmölle to Brösarps Station, where the hike ended.

images.caption: Interaktives 3D Erlebnis: Kronprinzessin Victoria von Schweden Wanderung in Skåne

title: Loop of the Lac de la Raho
short_description: A unique view of the Canigou massif and a place of passage for migratory birds. Herons regularly nest in the protected - but accessible - part of the lake.
long_description:
The Lac de la Raho is a hydraulic reservoir of 18 million m3, located about 6 km south of Perpignan, and straddling 5 communes. It was created by the General Council from an existing basin with a very small catchment area, originally occupied by a pond of about 150 hectares. <It is closed on the north, west and south sides communicates with plain via a channel east side.<The latter connects to the Agouille de la Mer via an underground channel. It is a site for bathing, walking as well hunting and fishing reserve.
It is possible to go to the beach and to the lake.
It is possible to make variations by going out into the vineyards around the lake. Be particularly careful on hunting days.
The lake is a very popular place for swimming, walking and fishing.

title: Hiking at Angolon Point
short_description: The hike to the Pointe d'Angolon offers an exhilarating ascent, with magnificent panoramas of the Alps, varied landscapes and breathtaking views from the summit.
long_description:
The starting point for this hike is the Col de Joux Plane, at around 1700 m altitude. This pass offers easy access to mountain trails and immediately provides panoramic views of the surrounding peaks, including Mont Blanc on a clear day. The trail starts gently from the pass, with a gradual ascent through lush alpine meadows and rocky areas.
Right from the start, you'll be immersed in spectacular alpine scenery, with unobstructed views of the surrounding valleys. The trail winds through fields of wild flowers and areas of alpine moorland, offering a serene and refreshing ambience. Continuous panoramas of the surrounding mountains and alpine lakes add to the beauty of the route.
As you progress, the path becomes steeper, with more sustained uphill sections. The views become increasingly impressive, revealing breathtaking scenery and majestic peaks. The climb also offers opportunities to observe alpine fauna and flora, adding an extra dimension to your hiking experience.
Approaching the Pointe d'Angolon, the terrain becomes more rugged and the trail crosses rocky areas. This final part of the climb is more demanding, but the panoramic views at the summit are an exceptional reward. The Pointe d'Angolon, at around 2090 m altitude, offers breathtaking views of the Geneva Alps, Mont Blanc and the surrounding mountains. The summit is an ideal place to rest, admire the scenery and take memorable photos.
The view from Pointe d'Angolon is spectacular, with a 360-degree panorama of alpine peaks, verdant valleys and crystal-clear lakes. It's a place where you can really soak up the majesty of the mountains and feel the satisfaction of having reached an impressive summit.
The return journey follows the same route, allowing you to relive the highlights of the climb from a different angle. The well-marked and well-maintained trail ensures a safe and pleasant descent. Enjoy panoramic views of the Alpine landscape as you descend to the Col de Joux Plane.

title: Exploring Garliste Gorges - some of the most spectacular gorges in Romania
short_description: The tourist route marked with a red dot between Anina and Gârliște passes through some of the wildest gorges in Romania,  Gârliște Gorges. The only way to see them is to follow this path.
long_description:
The route starts at the end of the Schlucht borough in Anina, as you walk along Teilor street, near the former mine. At first, the route runs parallel to the Anina-Oravița railway, offering the opportunity to observe one of the beautiful bridges built specifically for this railroad.
The path becomes wilder and wilder, traversing various sectors of cliffs or running just at the brim of rocky walls leaving no place for clutching. The Gârliște river flows along the path, with its rapid and cold waters.
The route is also dotted with a series of abandoned water mills. As you get closer to the end, the path becomes more and more adventurous. It passes by the small Gârliște waterfall and next to the Water Cave, the longest in these gorges. Just at the end, you can see the tracks of the narrow-gauge railway route.

images.caption: The path runs below several natural arcades

title: Zugspitze via Stopselzieher from Ehrwald (Hike & Fly)

Since myself could not find recent information about the launch site, I share my pictures from the last weekend.
I had perfect conditions at the launch site (almost laminar 15 km/h of wind from the west with a slight southerly impact). Thus, a controlled reverse launch was easily possible.

short_description: During this 12-kilometre hike, you will walk through a peaceful nature reserve.
long_description:
This nature reserve is fairly new. You will find wet ground and drifting sands. You can also walk along small fens and pieces of forest. It is still nice and quiet here and therefore you can hear many birds.

title: Winter hiking trail Moosfluh-Riederalp
short_description: This easy winter hike from Moosfluh is the ideal option for all hikers who want to admire the Aletsch Glacier, the largest glacier in Europe.
long_description:
From Riederalp, take the glacier cable car to the Moosfluh. From there, you will be rewarded with a breathtaking view: the Aletsch Glacier, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, stretches out between the snow-covered peaks. This impressive panorama accompanies you on most of your winter hike. The well-marked trail takes you along the Härdernagrat to the top station of the Hohfluh chairlift.
You then go down to Riederfurka, where you pass the imposing Villa Cassel. However, this magnificent Victorian building remains closed during the winter months.
Finally, it will take you around 30 minutes to get back to Riederalp, where your winter hike ends.

title: Wendlandweg
short_description: Together with the Elb-Höhenweg and the Wendenstieg, the Wendlandweg forms the great Wendland circular trail. We start in Hitzacker (Elbe), with the former imperial hunting forest of the Göhrde, and hike through the wooded hills of the Drawehn to the regional centre of Clenze.
long_description:
Stage 1: Hitzacker - Tollendorf / Gemeinde Göhrde (21 km)
We start our hike in Hitzacker on the Elbe and follow the river westwards via Tie&szlig to Tiesmesland. Along the way we experience the Lower Saxony Elbe floodplain biosphere reserve, with resting migratory birds, floodplains and the Elbe riverbanks. In Drethem we leave the Elbe and walk in a southerly direction past Bahrendorf and Wietzetze. Now the trail leads through the Grünhagen forest to Tollendorf.
Stage 2: Tollendorf / Gemeinde Göhrde - Spranz (24 km)
The first attraction of the day is the Lilienpfad in Govelin. Through the densely wooded Göhrde, a former imperial hunting forest, we hike on über Riebrau past Zernien to the small cottage settlement of Spranz.
Stage 3: Spranz - Clenze Flecken (23 km)
At the beginning of the last stage, the route climbs up the Hoher Mechtin on winding paths. Behind Gohlau, the forest gradually thins out and alternates with open fields and meadows. We turn towards Dickfeitzen and then walk along the Klosterberg to Reddereitz. Then we cross another beautiful forest and reach the destination of the Wedlandweg in Clenze.

images.caption: The view from High Mechtin over the surrounding flat land.

title: Oberterzen - Murgwald - Unterterzen
short_description: Common hike with views of the Walensee and the Churfirsten. First you walk along a hilly path, then there is an attractive descent through the Mur forest and finally you walk back along Lake Walen.
long_description:
The starting point of the tour in Oberterzen is easily accessible from Unterterzen by cable car. Even from the cable car you have wonderful views of the fjord-like Walensee and the towering Churfirsten peaks behind it. These views accompany you throughout the rest of the hike.
After a short descent, a continuous gentle climb begins in a forest past the village of Quarten until you are above half of Murg. Now the trail descends to Murg, partly through the beautiful Murg forest with the largest chestnut forest north of the Alps. The picturesque Murgbach waterfall is certainly an attraction here, and there is a playground with a fireplace nearby. From Murg you walk back along the shore of the Walensee to Unterterzen.

title: कब्बे हिल्स ट्रैक
short_description: कब्बे हिल्स कूर्ग इलाके में कर्नाटक-केरल राज्यों की सीमा पर स्थित बेहद सुन्दर पहाड़ियां हैं ।
long_description:
कूर्ग ज़िले की कब्बे पहाड़ियों का ट्रैक कर्नाटक का एक लोकप्रिय ट्रैक है। कब्बे पहाड़ियों से एक तरफ केरल के घने जंगलों और नीलगिरि पर्वत श्रृंखला दिखती है और दूसरी तरफ कर्नाटक के कॉफी बागान और चोल जंगलों का दृश्य दिखता है।
करीब 8 किलोमीटर यह ट्रैक बेहद सुन्दर और आसान है। शुरूआती 500 मीटर के अलावा पूरी ट्रेल एक प्राकृतिक पगडण्डी है जो हरेभरे घास में मैदानों से गुजरती है। ट्रेल लाल मिट्टी की बनी है और इसमें बिलकुल भी कंकड़-पत्थर नहीं हैं। पूरे ट्रेल में लगातार हलकी चढ़ाई है और यह सभी नए अनुभवी सभी किस्म के हाइकर्स के लिए उपयुक्त है। ट्रेल में आप अपना कुत्ता भी साथ ले जा सकते हैं।

title: Abraão to Parrot Peak Trail (T13)
short_description: With 959 meters high, Pico do Papagaio in Ilha Grande enchants its visitors with the beautiful view from its summit and also with the challenging trail in the middle of the Atlantic Forest.
long_description:
Leaving the Vila do Abraão, the first 20 minutes of walking happens through the flat road that leads toé Dois Rios Beach.At this point you will see a sign announcing the beginning of trail T13, the official numbering of the Ilha Grande State Park for the Parrot's Peak trail. The trail is well signposted and follows through dense Atlantic Forest for most of its length.It also maintains a constant gradient for most of the way, with almost no flat or downhill sections.
Há four áwater points in the first 25 minutes of walking à from the start of the trail. The último point of the whole trail é a small river, which é a good place to rest and have a snack.After an hour's walk from this last point of water, you reach an important fork, where going left, you follow the trail to the summit, while the right leads to the base of the immense rock that é the peak.

title: धर्मकोट-मैक्लोडगंज टरैक मार्ग
short_description: धर्मकोट से मैक्लोडगंज तक का एक छोटा लेकिन बेहद सुन्दर पैदल यात्रा मार्ग जो धर्मकोट के पॉपुलर मॉर्गन प्लेस से शुरू होकर मैक्लोडगंज के पास स्थित तिब्बती मंदिर तक जाता ह ै।
long_description:
इस पहाड़ी मार्ग का आरंभिक बिंदु, धरमकोट शहर हिमाचल प्रदेश के कांगड़ा जिले का एक छोटा सा पहाड़ी शहर है। धर्मकोट से कांगड़ा घाटी और धौलाधार पर्वतमाला के मनमोहक दृश्य मिलते हैं। यह करेरी झील और त्रिउंड ट्रैक का आधार शिविर (बेस कैंप) भी है।
पास के ही लोकप्रिय धर्मशाला शहर के विपरीत, जो अब पूरी तरह से एक व्यावसायिक टूरिस्ट ट्रैप बन गया है, धर्मकोट अभी भी शहरीकरण से अछूता है, इसलिए प्रकृति प्रेमियों और हिप्पी समुदाय के बीच एक छुपा हुआ राज है। यहां आपको सिर्फ वही प्रकृति प्रेमी मिलेंगे जो धर्मशाला की हलचल से दूर जाना चाहते हैं और असलियत में शांत हिमालय की गोद में शांति से समय बिताना  चाहते हैं।
इस मार्ग का गंतव्य बिंदु मैक्लोडगंज शहर है जो भी धर्मशाला का एक उपनगर (Suburb) है। यह चीन द्वारा तिब्बत पर कब्जे के बाद विस्थापित हुए कई तिब्बती नागरिकों को दिया गया सबसे पहला शरणस्थान है । मैक्लोडगंज में निर्वासित तिब्बती सरकार का मुख्यालय और दलाई लामा का निवास स्थान भी है। यह एक बौद्ध जीवन शैली वाला बेहद सुंदर और शांतिपूर्ण शहर है।
एक तीन किलोमीटर लम्बी नेचर ट्रेल से होते हुए  धर्मकोट से मैक्लोडगंज तक पैदल यात्रा की जा सकती। इस पृष्ठ पर आपको उस छोटी लेकिन सुंदर सैर का विवरण मिलेगा जो आपको एक गुजरे हुए से समय में वापस ले जाती है।

title: Trekking with kids: Breaza - Lizera de Pini
short_description: If you spend a few quiet days with your family in Breaza, this is an easy and scenic hike that children will surely enjoy.
long_description:
More than half of the route is on asphalt, on secondary roads in Breaza or above the town, making this route practicable in any season and in any type of weather.
After slightly ascending the hill, you first reach Liziera de Pini (the Pine Edge) - a historical place shadowing the northern part of the town and offering beautiful views both north and south. The pines were planted in the 19th century by the owners of the Breaza estate, the members of the Bibescu-Brâncoveanu family.
Nearby is the Breaza Gate, sometimes called the Infinity Gate or the Kiss Gate. It is a lookout point sought not only by photographers but also by occasional hikers.
From here, the path continues along the edge of the forest towards Gura Beliei commune, only to return to the starting point in Breaza.
The route is recommended as an easy trekking route for children; if you're looking ffor a slightly bigger challenge, try it by bike.

title: A tour of the Crane Homeland Nature Reserve
short_description: To the north of Moscow, the «Crane homeland» can be visited in the Dubna lowlands. The moorland museum has attracted some attractive birds.
long_description:
The name «Crane Home» for the reserve was invented by the famous writer Mikhail Prishvin. He used to stay on the marshes near Moscow and absorbed material from the natural surroundings. Obviously after having seen a lot of cranes the name Crane's Home Story was born, which later changed into the name of the reserve.
Seeing such a bird in the city limits – good luck! There are many species of birds in the reserve, but the cranes are more favored by the writer that he named his novel after them.

Being so close to Madrid (Puerto de Navacerrada), with the possibility of climbing one of the highest peaks of the Sierra Guadarrama and for being one of the most famous mountain passes of the Tour of Spain, this route is one of the best in Madrid.
long_description:

title: Duisburg Rhine Circuit
short_description: The district of Homberg and Baerl are ideal for a one-hour jog in Duisburg. On both sides of the Rhine you can run mostly on the top of the dike, partly asphalted, but mostly gravel. You cross the Rhine twice and have a nice circuit away from the urban centre.
long_description: On both sides of the Rhine, you can either go for a short hike or a jog on the dike crest. The jogging circuit takes about an hour for averagely fit people. The jog gives you a view of the Lower Rhine, but on the right bank of the Rhine you can see the relics of Duisburg's steel past: the right bank of the Rhine is dominated by ThyssenKrupp, which you can see in Duisburg-Homberg at the old Thyssen power station. If you move along the right bank of the Rhine and look to the left, you can already get an impression of how the landscape is becoming more and more dominant as the river flows further downstream towards the Netherlands. All in all, a very nice regeneration tour after a hard day's work.

title: McCallum Trail
short_description: The McCallum Trail begins on a short section of boardwalk in the Thousand Palms Oasis Preserve, and after approximately half a mile on a well-marked, sandy wash, hikers will come across this pristine desert oasis.  Walk around the Thousand Palms Oasis to learn about the flora, the fauna, the geology and the cultural history of this hidden gem of the desert. This short version (Walk and Talk) of his tour will take about an hour and will cover about a mile. The long version (Walking Tour) is about 2 miles and will take about two hours
long_description: The Simone Pond is surrounded by tall palms and park benches, creating an ideal shaded retreat.

title: Glass grinder route
short_description: In five daily stages, we hike an 80 km loop that takes us through the Upper Palatinate Forest to the German-Czech border. The cultural-historical circular route gives us insights into earlier times and shows us the charming nature of a low mountain range landscape.
long_description:
Stage 1: Gehenhammer - Pleystein (15 km)
We start at the 160-year-old and still functioning Gehenhammer mill, meet the Zott in Georgenberg and follow the small stream via Neuenhammer to Pleystein. The hiking trail takes us to the Pfifferlingsstiel and past mills, grinding mills and small tranquil villages.
Stage 2: Pleystein - Böhmischbrück (18.5 km)
On the second day we also hike through the Upper Palatinate Forest: first along the Zottbach, then along the Pfreimd. The Trutzhofmühle, the Hammermühle and the castle Burgtreswitz (behind Moosbach) await us at the two bubbling rivers. When we reach our destination in Böhmischbruck, we can also visit an old monastery.
Stage 3: Böhmischbrück - Eslarn (23 km)
Today we have to tackle the longest section of the Glasschleifererweg, but we are rewarded with the original beauty of the Upper Palatinate Forest: The Tröbesbach has some waterfalls ready for us, on the Stückberg we climb a lookout tower and fields, forests and meadows alternate constantly. The baroque parish church of the Assumption in Eslarn marks the stage destination from afar.
Stage 4: Eslarn - Waidhaus (13.5 km)
Along the densely wooded German-Czech border area, we hike to the Teufelsstein and the Goldberg. Past the Pfrentschweiher, a medieval reservoir, which today is an important resting place for many animal and plant species, we walk via Ziegelhütte to Waidhaus.
Stage 5: Waidhaus - Gehenhammer (18.5 km)
In a northerly direction we cross Frankenreuth and Reichenau and our path then winds its way through the huge forest area on the Sulzberg to the Czech border. From the small village of Leßlohe to Neukirchen to St. Christoph, fantastic views and wonderful impressions await us again and again. Now we only have to climb the Troidelberg and reach Gehenhammer, the starting point of our beautiful round tour.

images.caption: View of Moosbach with the parish church

title: Through the Jagst Valley to Langenburg Castle
short_description: On this tour, we go both directly to the banks of the Jagst and on a high trail that offers us a beautiful view over the river valley. Our ascent to Langenburg Castle is steep.
long_description:
Our tour starts at the market place in Langenburg. From there we walk down the Kronenbuck to Bächlinger Straße. We change sides of the road, pass the Rumanian house and reach Agnes-Günther-Platz. Here we turn right and take the Weinbergweg, which leads us along the forest to the Gipsgrubenweg junction. Turn left and follow the Gipsgrubenweg down to the Hagsteige. From the slope we have a beautiful view over the Jagst valley. We descend via a ridgeway to the Jagsttalstraße and arrive at the Schimbach rest and camping area. We can now take a short break directly on the banks of the Jagst.
Freshly strengthened, we then head back up into the forest. Our path leads past a sewage treatment plant and joins the Steigenpfad. As we continue, we come across the Schlosssteig and switch to it to the right. The path goes steeply up the slope and can be slippery when wet. Soon we have the walls of the castle in front of us and walk past the Tummelhaus towards the car park of the Automuseum, where we follow the Philosophenweg, which takes us along the city wall to the steps up to the Philosophenkeller. Finally, we walk back along the main road to our starting point.

title: Hjelledalen Old Church Road
short_description: Follow a historic trail though the Hjelldalen Valley
long_description: The old road through Hjelledalen is an easy stroll through the valley with steep mountains either side. From the village of Hjelle the historic tail leads along the Hjelledøla River and through farmland to Bolstad, finishing at Nygård Camping. If you are staying at Nygård Camping or Folven Camping this is a nice route to follow to Hjelle instead of walking along the main road.

images.caption: The start of the trail in Hjelle

title: Hiking to the Poenari Fortress
short_description: 1480 steps to a mysterious tourist location: a little known fortress of Vlad Țepeș (Vlad the Impaler) also called Vlad Țepeș Fortress or Negru Vodă Fortress.
long_description:
The end point of the hike is the Poenari Fortress, located on a rock that dominates the Argeș gorge near the Vidraru dam. The ascent begins in the valley near the Vidraru hydroelectric power station.
The path to the fortress has 1480 steps, but they are not too difficult to walk. The forest we pass through is beautiful, so we are distracted by tiredness.
The path has been closed due to the danger of bears. However, measures have been taken to secure the area by installing an electric fence. Since December 2019 instead of December 2019, tourists are now protected from bears.

title: Lying on your nose... - Bad Sooden-Allendorf
short_description: Lying on your nose... and enjoy the sun and the beautiful view, that's what you can do on this hike.
long_description:
Start at the car park above Asbach. From the altitude diagram you can see that the ascent is good straight away. You need to be a little fit and sure-footed, and in the course of the tour you will also need a head for heights.
This tour is not recommended in wet conditions.
The first magnificent view can be had from the "Dietzenröder Stein", and you should walk to both vantage points.
We walk back the same way. It would also be possible to walk through the forest, but this route is more interesting.
On returning to the turning point, you soon reach the "nose". Here you can lie in the sun directly on the cliff and enjoy the wonderful panorama.
After extensive enjoyment, the trail descends through the forest, along a wide path with a shortcut through the forest. Again on a wide path, you cross the Bossebach stream and climb towards the Altenstein ruins.
You can stay on the wide path and comfortably reach the ruin in 5 min. You will find another beautiful rock formation and then climb up to the Altenstein across a meadow.
The rest of the route can be walked back along the wide path downhill to the left, but we walked the small section directly on the slope and then rejoined the wide path.
Shortly before Asbach, we walk another small loop through the forest and are rewarded with the sight of a beautiful meadow landscape when we exit. A last resting view is offered before we reach the starting point again.

title: Trescovăț volcanic peak and panoramas over the Danube gorges
short_description: Climbing the Trescovăț peak is one of the hiking recommendations in the Almăj Mountains, next to hiking up the Ciucărul Mic and Ciucărul Mare peaks. This is one of the few ways to admire the photogenic Danube watercourse as it enters Romania, but also to see the Serbian shore.
long_description:
The route to the Trescovăț peak, marked with a red triangle, is a moderate to difficult one due to the constant ascent to the top, but also because of its length. However, the beauty of the landscape is worth the effort.
Along the route, there is a spot from where you can observe rare species of flowers and trees - the black pine, species of orchids - or reptiles - turtles or horned vipers.
In some places, the markings might be missing, so pay attention to the correct path. The distinctive shape of the Trescovăț peak can be seen from many points along the route, so take it as a landmark.
Once you reach the top -  a block of solidified lava otherwise called a volcanic neck - you have to turn slightly to the right to reach the actual peak. This is not the only lookout point on the route, but it is certainly the most spectacular. From the top, you can see the Serbian and the Romanian shores and the Danube meandering to Cozla and along the gorges.
If you choose to do a full circuit, you'll exist to the main road some 3 km upstream of your starting point. Alternatively, you can return to the same path.

title: Alatsee
short_description: A hiking trail that surrounds the gorgeous Lake Alat, southeast of the town of Posen and a short walk from the town of Wills in Tyrol
long_description:
An easy and mostly level walking route (including one short ascent with a negligible slope) that surrounds Lake Alat, which is characterized by a faint turquoise hue. Along the way, a number of shop windows await you where you can see figurines showing the animals living there. Those who want to extend the walk can turn along the way, according to the signs in the place, towards a local alpine hut or walk towards the town of Wills in Tyrol (Austria). You can stop on the way and have a family picnic in one of the lawns along the way as well as bathe in the cool lake water.
This is a great trip for the whole family. The crystal clear waters with a mesmerizing turquoise hue that characterize the lake add another layer to the experience of visiting the place. Along the route there are spacious lawns, benches, bathing beaches as well as a hotel with a local restaurant. The trip can be combined with a visit to the famous castles in the town of Posen, which is a short drive from the lake.
The route is not paved but is in principle suitable for walking with prams.

title: From the Devil's Moor to the Wadden Sea
short_description: This 450 km long circular cycle route leads through the typical landscape of the north. Over many lakes, rivers and finally also past the sea, this route takes us once around nature reserves and tourist regions;
long_description: Those who read the name of the tour will not fail to notice that this tour leads through the so-called Devil's Moor, a moorland area of more than 600 square metres. This title, however, only hints at one of the many landscapes we cross on this long-distance cycle route. On mostly asphalted and only in a few places gravel roads we cycle on mostly traffic-free roads and paths. The region between the North Sea and the rivers Elbe and Weser is characterised by moorland, small villages and the large urban centres of the north such as Cuxhaven, Bremerhaven and of course Bremen;

title: Coastal hike at Sauðárkrókur - Ósmann - Hegranesviti
short_description: This is a nice hike along the coast. You can watch birds, enjoy the view of the sea and literally feel the silence. At the lighthouse it goes back through the inland to road 75.
long_description: The hike begins about 5 km east of Sauðárkrókur at the parking lot behind the bridge. First it goes north on small paths along the coast and the steep bank. Sometimes there are fences in the way that you can climb over. At the lighthouse we are at the head of "Landsendi" the end of the world. Then it goes through barren landscape back to the road.

title: Aussichtsreiche Winterwanderung und Rodeltour Elmen- Stablalm
short_description: Die familienfreundliche Winterwanderung von Elmen zur Stablalm bietet eine wunderschöne Aussicht auf die benachbarten 2000er und läd am Ende zur gemütlichen Einkehr ein. Highlight: Rodelabfahrt
long_description:
Vom Parkplatz in Elmen folgen wir dem gut präparierten Forstweg leicht ansteigend für mehrere Kilometer. Je höher wir kommen, umso schöner wird die Aussicht und die Bäume geben die Sicht auf die umgebenden Berge frei. Als großes Ziel wartet die Einkehr in der Stablalm. Auf der Sonnenterrasse mit bombastischer Aussicht lässt sich der Topfenstrudel besonders gut schmecken.
Die Rodelabfahrt stellt ein weiteres Highlight der Tour dar, da sie überwiegend relativ gerade und mit gleichmäßigem Gefälle verläuft.

title: Around Liebhards in the Hessian Rhön
short_description: This beautiful circular walk takes us through a lovely landscape and offers wonderful views of the Rhön mountains in addition to mixed forest passages.
long_description: We walk on the road "Am Felsenkeller" to the left out of the village. Shortly after a crossroads, we turn left towards a stone field cross, which we pass on the right. At the following forks and crossroads, we keep to the right in each case until we walk left on the road towards Obergruben. We follow the white "4" on a black background to the left until we reach the rest area "Kleine Grubenhauck". Now the red triangle leads us to the road to Harbach, onto which we walk to the left. In Harbach we follow the road to the right out of the village and turn left towards the barbecue area. We pass the Harbachstein with a beautiful view. At the next T-junction, we walk to the right and then turn left. We come across a road and walk to the right back to the starting point.

title: Scenic tour through the Croatian villages in Banat
short_description: The Czech villages in the Banat region are already quite famous and touristy both locally and internationally. Yet less is known about the Croatian villages, where more than 80% of the population is of south-Slavic origin and touristic promotion is even lower. A one or two-day tour of the Croatian villages in rural Banat will unravel the unique cultural features of this rather isolated community; the picturesque landscape will fully add to the whole experience.
long_description:
Scattered around Reșița, the seven Croatian villages or towns are relatively easy to access on secondary roads (mostly paved). The first immigrants settled here in the 14th century, in Carașova, which is now the main Croatian settlement. The other localities stand on both sides of the national road 58 connecting Resita with Anina, and so they can be easily included in a circuit.
From the very beginning of the tour, you feel like entering another realm. The official bilingual signs or the foreign accent you hear everywhere around you on the streets also contribute to this. The feeling is similar to the one you have when visiting Szeklerland, in Transylvania.
The route passes briefly through the Cheile Nerei - Beușnița National Park; while on the road between Carașova and Iabalcea, make a detour to see Caraș Gorges or the Turk's Fort.
While on the road, remember that few get to admire the surrounding landscape. And don't hesitate to make a pit stop at a local bar and try to talk to the locals: it's the only way you can enter the universe of the daily lives of the Croats in Romania.

title: From Ingelfingen to the ruins of Zarge Castle
short_description: This hike takes us from Ingelfingen along a beautiful panoramic path to the ruins of Zarge Castle, which may have been the seat of the legendary Mechthild vom Stein around 1090.
long_description: This hike leads us from Ingelfingen along a beautiful panoramic path to the ruins of Zarge Castle, which may have been the seat of the legendary of the legendary Mechthild vom Stein. The castle was built around 1000 and was was already in ruins in the 14th century. Today, only the shield wall of the can still be seen. Back in Ingelfingen, we should take a look at the town hall. town hall, which since 1985 has been housed in the former castle of the Count of of Hohenlohe since 1985. It is also worth visiting the the Schwarzer Hof and the Hagdorn shell limestone museum.

title: Adriatic Cycle Route
short_description: The central element of this cycling route partially conceived by FIAB is the Adriatic Sea surrounding the eastern part of the Bel Paese.
long_description:
The route starts in Trieste and arrives at the southernmost point of Apulia, passing through several Italian regions with one's gaze always turned towards the sea.
.
The route is characterised by relatively little altitude difference and mostly follows flat or sloping roads. This is why it is classified as 'easy'.

title: Easy hike near Red Lake -  peaks Suhardul Mic & Suhadul Mare
short_description: This is one of the few scenic trails that reach over Red Lake; the path is marked to Suhardul Mic, but unmarked to Suhardul Mare.
long_description:
The route to Suhardul Mic is a popular one, frequented by many hikers. Conveniently, it is a very accessible route, including for children, with a little care. It's also the kind of trail suitable for dogs.
We start from the Tourist Hotel and follow the path that leads over the lake. Suharul Mic peak stands on a rock that rises, imposingly, in front of you from the very beginning of the route. Along the way, you will see it almost permanently to your right. After climbing for a bit through the forest, there comes a rocky part, with an insurance railing, just in case. Next, you'll come to a clearing where several paths separate. Your route continues to the right, among old fir trees with spectacularly branched roots.
At the top, you find a plateau perfect for a rest. The information panel here shows you which peaks can be seen in the distance; the view opens to the south to Hășmașul Mare.
To reach Suhardul Mare you have to return a bit on the same route and break off from the main path after the rocky steps. Other curious trekkers have already trodden this trail, so there's a barely visible path that can be followed, at least in the summertime. About 400 meters before the actual peak, the path is lost in the coniferous forest, so you reach the peak somehow intuitively since you don't have any signs. To the left on the way up, the forest thins out, and from here you can see the tail of the lake to the front and the Suhardul Mic peak to the right.

images.caption: Panorama with the Red Lake from Suharul Mic Peak
Climbing Suhardul Mare, view towards Suhardul Mic

title: Nordic Walking at the Black Lake near Schlemmin
short_description: The nature reserve "Schwarzer See", the remains of a Slavic fortress and endless, sparse beech forests are the backdrop for this beautiful tour.
long_description: From the TV tower "Hohe Burg" we follow the path parallel to the road to the Black Lake. Our marker is the "Green crossbar". After crossing the road we are in the nature reserve "Schwarzer See" (1). An information board explains the most important facts. Our path leads straight ahead here to the bridge (2). To the right and left of the path, the moor is close enough to touch. Peat mosses, cotton grass, Christopher's weed, forest fescue and sundew are the most important plants. With luck, rare animal species can also be observed. Grey geese, wood sandpipers, black woodpeckers and cranes occur in this area. The area was severely damaged by drainage measures in the 19th and 20th centuries. Since 1985, attempts have been made to renaturalise the area through damming measures. The success is visible. A little later we come to a crossroads that leads to the remains of the Slavic "High Castle" (3). An information board explains the history of this site. We continue to the right. We come to the actual Black Lake with its small open water area (4). The name comes from the pitch-black lake water. We follow the path in the nature reserve until we reach the large crossroads with an information board (5). Then turn left. The path leads along sunken paths through beautiful beech forests. At the next large crossroads we turn left. We walk straight ahead until we reach a fork in the path. Here we keep to the right. Again we pass a wetland. At the T-junction before the meadow, we turn left. The houses of Jabelitz can already be seen through the trees. In a wide curve, the path leads us back to the main road and the TV tower.

images.caption: The peat bog is often very close.
Especially on overcast days, the peat bog looks threatening.
Dead trees are characteristic of moorland.
The Black Lake has a small open water area.
Fungi in particular feel at home in the humid environment.

title: A trip to the Steigbach stream and waterfalls
short_description: A lovely hiking route that includes a hike along the Steigbach stream that flows from the mountain to the valley. Along the relatively short road you can see several waterfalls and small pools of water.
long_description: A relatively short and easy favorite hiking route that includes going up natural stairs next to the Steigbach stream that flows from the mountain into the valley and into the town of Immenstadt. Water flowing into waterfalls and pools with clear water awaits you along the way. The route is linear and you can go up and down it the same way next to the stream or take one of the directions on the paved road parallel to the natural road. You can of course continue to climb the mountain beyond the route marked on the map.

title: Hiking to Mount Aragats' South Summit  (3,879 m), Armenia
short_description: Experience the wonderful sense of isolation that comes with this hike to Mounts Aragat's South Summit, one of the four peaks that make up this lonely volcano massif located deep in the Armenian Highlands.
long_description:
Despite being the shortest of Aragats' four summits (the Northern peak is Armenia's highest point at 4,090 m), the wild and open countryside that stretches off into the distance on the trip to and from the South Summit makes for a spectacular backdrop to this technically easy- though pretty high- trek.
We didn't have great weather when we visited, but the vistas on a clear day are said to be immense and include sweeping views all the way over to Mount Ararat in Turkey.

title: Pai Zé Trail
short_description: Trail that leads to the famous Pico do Jaragu á from where é possibile have a beautiful panoramic view of the city of São Paulo with its skyscrapers, besides being able to breathe pure forest air.
long_description:
Trail that leads to the summit of Pico do Jaraguá has about 4.2 km (round trip) and takes about 2h30 – 3h to be covered. For beginners in mountain hiking é a good choice,  as  the trail é well  signposted and has low level of technical and physical difficulty. But for those who already have some mountain experience and just want to go for a light walk close to São Paulo, the walk is also a great option.
 At the top the effort &eaccedil;o é rewarded  with a viewpoint where é possible see much of the city. In addition, on the summit are located two towers that are shared by three TV stations, radio transmitters and other private companies. Despite the pollution layer of the initial city, the climb is rewarded with the panoramic view of the city of São Paulo, with its thousands of buildings.

title: Pitcher Mountain Trail
short_description: The Best Berry Picking Hikes in America. Savor summer’s bounty on these four treks to berry havens.
long_description: Our best tip for the Pitcher Mountain Trail? Don’t skimp on container size. Shoulder-high blueberry bushes line the trail up 2,153-foot Pitcher Mountain, and come late July, they’re sagging with ripe fruit. New Hampshire’s cold winters and rocky, acidic soil make for the massive bushes along the Blue Trail, which wends .2 mile through the berry maze to a summit firetower. There, indulge in your harvest and a panorama that includes Mt. Monadnock to the south, Vermont’s Green Mountains to the west, and, on clear days, the White Mountains to the north. After, continue 2.3 miles north to Hubbard Hill, another blueberry hot spot, to replenish before turning around for a 5-mile out-and-back

title: Glæra
short_description: Follow an old farm road through a wild valley near the Gamle Strynefjellsvegen scenic route
long_description:
Glæra is an old farming road between the Skjerdingsdalssætra farm and the old stone-vault bridge called Jøl bru. The trail is surrounded by steep mountains with a rushing river to keep you company. 
This trail works best as a point-to-point hike through the valley, so have someone pick you up at the other end if possible. It can be hiked in both directions, but if you start at Skjerdingsdalssætra the trail is mostly downhill.

images.caption: Jøl bru, at the end of the route.

title: Emigrant’s Trail
short_description:
Auf dem Emigrant's Trail, oder schwedisch Utvandrarleden, wandern wir durch Wälder und Wiesen, an Steinmauern und Seen vorbei auf den Spuren der Emigranten.
Translate to English
long_description:
Vilhelm Moberg ist ein bekannter schwedischer Autor, der unter anderem über die Auswanderer aus Schweden geschrieben hat. Die Orte, die in seinen Werken erwähnt werden, können wir auf dem Emigrant's Trail erkunden. Ljuder, Korpamoen, Moshult und Åkerby sind nur ein paar Beispiele davon.
Die Wanderung ist aber nicht nur geschichtlich und kulturell interessant. Auf Pfaden, Feldwegen, Forststraßen und gelegentlich Landstraßen wandern wir vor allem durch viel Waldgebiet und über grüne Wiesen. Hier können wir die Essenz Smålands erleben: die Düfte der Wälder, die Geräusche der Natur und die malerischen Dörfer. Die Steinmauern, roten Häuser mit weißen Ecken und traditionellen Zäune erinnern uns an die reiche Geschichte der Region.
Übernachtungsmöglichkeiten gibt es in regelmäßigen Abständen auf dem Fernwanderweg. Wir können in Herbergen, Bauernhotels oder auf Campingplätzen übernachten und auch länger verweilen. Für den Trail werden auch Pakete mit Unterkunft und Verpflegung angeboten.

title: From Fichtenberg near Gaildorf to Erlenhof
short_description: On this moderately difficult hike we experience a magnificent panorama from the Viehberg plain.
long_description: The hike starts at the community hall in Erlenhofer Straße in Fichtenberg. Via Schulstraße and Neue Straße we come to Russbergweg, where we follow the right-hand bend. From here we walk up to the "Viehberg Ebene", where we have a sensational view into the Rottal. From the "Viehberg Ebene" we walk to the left to the Erlenhof. Now we follow the signs over the old "Steige" in the direction of Fichtenberg. On the main road we keep to the left, so that after a while we come to "Diebach". We continue on the path to the reservoir, where we can cool off after the hike in summer. Of course, the sunbathing lawns of the open-air swimming pool also invite you to sunbathe. On the Erlenhofer Straße we get back to the community hall in Fichtenberg.

title: मेघालय में लिविंग रुट पुल और डबल डेकर पुल तक हाईकिंग। भारत
short_description: लिविंग रुट पुल भारत के पूर्वोत्तर राज्य मेघालय में स्थानीय जनजाति के लोगों द्वारा जीवित वृक्षों की जड़ों से बनाये गये पुल हैं और इसलिए इन्हे जीवित जड़ सेतु भी कहा जाता है। चेरापूंजी ज़िले के तिरना गाँव और नोंगरियात गाँव में ऐसे 2 प्रसिद्ध पुल ट्रैकिंग के लिए बहुत पसंद किये जाते हैं। इनमे से एक पुल तो डबल डेकर भी है।
long_description:
मेघालय प्राकृतिक सुंदरता के अलावा अपने लिविंग रुट पल के लिए भी जाना जाता है। यह पुल इंसान और प्रकृति की मित्रता का नायाब उदहारण हैं और दर्शाता है की दोनों के समन्वय से कितनी सुन्दर चीज़ें बन सकती हैं। इन पुलों को खासी और जयंतिया लोगों द्वारा बरगद अथवा पेड़ की हवाई जड़ों से बनाया जाता है। इंडोनेशिया में सुमात्रा द्वीप भी ऐसे कुछ पुल देखने को मिलते हैं।
मेघालय के चेरपुंजी ज़िले के नोंगरियात गाँव के पास ऐसे 3 पुल देखने को मिलते हैं जो सैकड़ो साल पुराने हैं। हर साल कई पर्यटक इन्हे देखने आते हैं। इनमे से डबल डेकर ब्रिज सबसे ज्यादा प्रसिद्ध है। यह BBC के Human Planet कार्यक्रम और जापान की Asahi TV की डॉक्यूमेंट्री में भी दिखाया गया था।
यह मार्ग सीढ़ियों, झूलते पुलों, लिविंग रुट पुलों, जलधाराओं और हरियाली से भरी हुई पंगडंडियों के वजह से हाइकर्स और प्रकृति प्रेमियों के बीच बहुत लोकप्रिय है।
