title: Stone graves in Visbek
short_description: This tour takes us past the largest stone tombs in north-west Germany.
long_description: Our tour starts in Visbek-Engelmannsbäke, near the Reinke trout farm. We walk past the largest stone graves in north-west Germany, including the "Visbeker Bräutigam", a 5,000-year-old and 104 m long barrow. After visiting the graves, we follow the main path straight ahead through the forest until we turn right onto the Varnhorner Weg. At the next opportunity, we turn left. The path bends to the right after a while, after which we soon turn right and thus rejoin the Varnhorner Weg. Follow it to the left for a few metres and then turn right at the next junction until you reach a T-junction. Here we turn left and soon cross Varnhorn. Our path now leads us to Siedenbögen and on along Wildeshauser Straße to Visbek. Via Vitusstrasse, "Am Bruch" and the Kreuzweg we soon leave the village again to the north. We walk through fields past Endel before we come back to Engelmannsbäke in a curve and through the forest.

title: Alpe Mitterhaus
short_description: This hike takes us from the mountain station of the Hornbahn around the Imberger Horn over the Strausbergsattel to the Alpe Mitterhaus. We then hike steadily down past the Horncafé to the valley station of the Hornbahn.
long_description:
During this hike, we are repeatedly offered magnificent views of the surrounding mountains of the Allgäu Alps and over the villages in the valleys. We circle the Imberger Horn, cross the Strausbergsattel and can stop for a hearty meal at the Mitterhaus or the Horncafé. The hike is also suitable for families with older children.
If you are looking for a challenge, you can alternatively hike directly over the Imberger Horn. The path is partly secured with wire ropes. However, this somewhat more demanding route is not suitable for children.

title: Bracuí Waterfall Trail
short_description: With an incredible pool of crystal-clear water and a sequence of five waterfalls, the Bracuí Cachoeira do Bracuí offers a spectacular view of the Bocaina Serra da Bocaina and Angra dos Reis.
long_description:
With  large volume of water, a  beautiful pool for bathing  and a sequence of five falls that total 1.100 metres, the last of which is 70 metres high, the Bracuí Cachoeira do Bracuí offers a breathtaking view of the cliffs of the Bocaina Serra da Bocaina and the Islands of Angra dos Reis. You are really spoilt for choice whether you sit with your back to the waterfall, enjoying the landscape, or if you stand with your back to the view, admiring the waterfall.
The trail has about 1,5 km and 2 km (one way) and é flat in its majority. It begins at the door of the Pousada do Rio Mimoso, where an entrance ticket to the waterfall is charged (R$ 10 per person). It takes about 1 hour to get there and the same time to get back. There are some stretches inclined and where you need to pass between paths. Moreover, already arriving at the waterfall, you will have to go through a very steep part, using a rope that exists on site and holding on to branches
.

title: Mt Takao Road 1 (Omotesando Course)
short_description: Main route to the summit of Mt Takao up the approach to Yakuoin Temple. Many of the paths are paved and wide, making it easy for families to walk. A cable car can also be used one way.
long_description:
Road 1 is paved all the way to Yakuoin Temple and is the most popular route for visitors to Mt Takao. Takao has become a very popular mountain since it was awarded three stars in the Michelin Green Guide. The paths are wide and easy to ascend, but be prepared for a long slog uphill to the summit. In spring, flowers such as violets can be seen by the side of the path.
At the start of the climb, you walk along a stone-paved path. There is a river running alongside the path, so even in summer you can walk while keeping cool. The slope gradually gets steeper and steeper, and after passing a zigzag path, you will soon reach a lookout point on the way up. The cable car stop is reached on foot, watched over by Jizo-san. Enjoy the view from the observatory and a smoke at the teahouse.
After passing the Monkey Park, you will see the 450-year-old Takosugi (octopus cedar), which is also a power spot. Next to the octopus cedar, there is also a "pulled octopus", which you can pat on the head and ask for good luck. After crossing the Shoshinmon Gate, it takes about 10 minutes to reach Yakuoin Temple. Beyond this, there is a two-way path, the male and female slopes, with the female slope being the gentler of the two.
Yakuoin is almost reached when you see the Gongen Tea House, famous for its tengu ramen, in front of you. You can get the famous red seal and see a statue of a tengu, the symbol of Takao. After passing the main hall of Yakuoin, there are some ups and downs to the summit.
From the Omiharu Park at the summit of Mt Takao, on a clear day you can see Mt Fuji, so be sure to look out for it.
You can use the cable car to take a short cut to the Monkey Park and the observatory area in the middle of the mountain.

title: Bamberg World Heritage Run
short_description: This tour is less for runners chasing their personal best and more for those who want to see some of Bamberg's beautiful old town while jogging.
long_description: The World Heritage Run has been held in Bamberg every two years since 2003. Its historical predecessors are the relay race "Quer durch Bamberg" and the "Bamberg Stadtlauf". This city-running course is one of the most demanding but also undoubtedly one of the most beautiful in all of Germany. In addition to the wonderful scenic highlights of the World Heritage Run, it is primarily the cultural and historical sights that make the World Heritage Run an unforgettable experience. The starting point of the tour is St. Mark's Square. The St. Mark's House of the same name, the former hospital of the city of Bamberg, is home to a faculty of the University of Bamberg. Besides the monastery of St. Michael, which is situated high above the roofs of the city on the Michaelsberg, the cathedral square with its historic buildings is one of the absolute highlights of this tour. But the Laupassagen along the Regnitz and through the Theresienhain also have their own special charm. The last kilometres of the route take us through the beautiful alleys of the city and across the Maxplatz, the central market and event location of the cathedral city.

title: Hike to Schoimos Castle
short_description: A short hike to Schoimos Castle.
long_description: The hike to the Schoimos Castle takes us to a special vantage point (to the town of Lipova and river  Marosh) marked by history.

title: North Baltic Sea Hiking Trail
short_description: The Nord-Ostsee-Wanderweg (North Baltic Sea Hiking Trail) runs for around 115 km from Meldorf on the North Sea to Kiel on the Baltic Sea. The scenic route runs through the marshes and the Geest, along the Kiel Canal into the eastern hilly country of central Holstein.
long_description:
1st stage: Meldorf - Albersdorf .
We start our hike in Meldorf at the railway station, cross the railway tracks there and continue straight ahead to the main road. We walk along the road towards the end of the village and turn right into Grenzweg. Along field paths we pass the Wolmersdorfer brickyard to Farnewinkel and finally Dellbrück with its impressive megalithic tomb. A short time later we reach the ruins of Marienburg, a former fortress from the Middle Ages. Our path continues through fields and small woods to Trensbüttel. At the memorial, we keep half-right, cross the motorway and follow the path towards Grünental. Here it is worth taking a short detour to the high bridge, which offers a magnificent view of the Kiel Canal and the impressive container ships. Back on the path, we walk north along the railway embankment and west through a small forest in Gieslautal. We then turn north again and follow the path through the Bredenkop enclosure past Neolithic burial sites. For those interested, a visit to the Archaeological-Ecological Centre Albersdorf is recommended. After a short detour to the Kaiserberg and the lookout tower there, we finally reach our first stage destination, Albersdorf.
2nd stage:  Albersdorf - Breiholz
We start our second stage in Albersdorf, where we cross the railway line and reach a car park via Grossers Alle and Danziger Straße. Here we enter the forest and hike to the Ochsenweg (Ox Trail), which already led from the Elbe to Jutland in the Stone Age. We cross the historic path and reach the road to Bunsoh through the Tiefen Grund, which we do not descend into. We follow this road northeast for about 1 km and then turn right onto a field path that leads us to Weiche Fischerhütte on the Kiel Canal. Cross the grass verge at the edge of the canal (caution, danger of slipping in places!) to reach Hinrichshörn. Here we turn left onto a flagstone path and walk to the Gieslau Canal, which we cross at the lock. After a few hundred metres we reach the country road, which we follow back to the canal. On the north bank we hike to Tackesdorf-Nord and continue along the path across fields to our next stage destination, Breiholz.
3rd stage: Breiholz - Rendsburg
We leave Breiholz and follow the road to Hamdorf. In Drof, we turn right and take field paths first to Elsdorfer Gehege and later to Osterhammer Gehege. I, fishermen and boatyard village Nübbel, we cross the Eider on the footbridge and reach the Kiel Canal again at the pilot station. We walk along the shore to our stage destination Rendsburg. Here, sights such as St. Mary's Church, the Parade Square or the old town hall invite you to take an extensive tour of the town.
4th stage: Rendsburg - Westensee
At the beginning of our fourth stage, we walk through the Rendsburg pedestrian tunnel and cross under the Kiel Canal. On the south side, we follow the path to the left to the railway high bridge and floating ferry in Osterrönfeld. Here we walk right along the high bridge, under the access ramp and cross the B202. Then turn left into Aspelweg and reach the foot of the railway embankment. Behind the first farmstead, our path branches off to the right and leads across fields, through the Stadtmoor and the Wilde Moor to Bokelholm. In the village we cross the railway tracks and the main road and follow the path across the Mühlenau, the A7, past Wittenkamp and the Nordmoor to the Rümlandteich. The pond, which is cordoned off by bushes, invites you to take a relaxing rest. South of it, our path continues through wooded areas and past the Emkendorf estate, which is well worth seeing, to Brux. From here it is not far until we reach our stage destination Westensee in the middle of the Westensee Nature Park.
5th stage: Westensee - Kiel
From Westensee we hike east via Eckhöft on the road leading to Wrohe. Behind Whrohe we enter the forest again and follow our path past Kleiner Schierensee to Hohenhude. We cross the Eider and walk in a beautiful avenue to Schönwohld. From here we follow a field path north of the Hansdorfer See lake to the A215. After crossing under the motorway, we turn south to the Ihlkate at the Ihlsee and walk through the wildlife park to the Kuhfurtsau. We walk along the shore to the confluence with the Eider, then turn east and walk along the river to Kiel-Schulensee, where our stage tour ends. In the state capital, numerous sights and Baltic beaches invite you to visit and relax.

title: Kiryat Ata Hiking Trail
short_description: A walking trail of short-medium length connecting the city of Kiryat Ata to the Kiryat Ata forest.
long_description: A 14-kilometer linear walking trail that allows foot access from the city of Kiryat Ata to the city forest. The road passes through the territory of Tsipri forests and exposes the walkers to wooded landscapes and interesting observation points.

title: From Estana to Prat de Cadí
short_description: This easy hike takes us from the mountain village of Estana to a gentle meadow with stunning views right under the impressive north face of the Serra del Cadí mountain range.
long_description: The Cadí-Moixeró Natural Park is home to some of the most rugged mountains in the foothills of the Pyrenees. On this short but rewarding route, hikers get to enjoy the diversity of landscape and flora in one of Catalonia's wildest areas. From the village of Estana, the Serra del Cadí looks almost inacessible, with impressive rock faces towering over the valley. The Prat de Cadí is an almost paradisiacal alpine meadow at an altitude of about 1,830 meters and is rightly considered one of the most spectacular viewpoints in the region. But even the way up, through wild pine forests with occasional views back over the shoulder into the valley of el Segre, is well worth it. Once you reach your destination, all you really have to do is take off your shoes, drop into the grass with a deep sigh and feel very close to heaven.

images.caption: Serra del Cadí north face seen from Prat del Cadí
On the trail up to Prat de Cadí

title: To the Burgbach waterfall near Bad Rippoldsau
short_description: The tour to the Burgbach waterfall is relatively short at just over 6 km, but very varied in terms of technical demands and scenic surroundings.
long_description: Our tour starts at the hikers' car park. From here, we follow the yellow rhombus in the direction of Burgbach. We cross the village of Burgbach and immediately turn right onto a narrow path into the forest. At a fork, we first follow the yellow rhombus to the waterfall about 200 m away, before returning to the fork and taking the steep path up the slope. After the ascent, we reach the Burgbach rock, from where we can enjoy a fantastic view into the valley. Then we follow the signpost with the yellow arrow a short way up the slope and across a meadow. We continue - always following the yellow arrow - along the slope through the forest. After a while there is a short descent and we find ourselves a little above Bad Rippoldsau and enjoy the beautiful view of the town and the monastery. We continue to follow the yellow arrow down into the village across the main road and the river to a miniature golf course. From here we walk always in the valley of the Wolfach back to the hikers' car park.

images.caption: The view of the Burgbach rock.
A view from the bridge over the Woll.
Deep forests accompany us on the route.
At times our tour runs directly along the stream.

title: Bighorn Creek Trail
short_description: We pass through pine and fir forests, as well as pastures and meadows, on this moderate hike. Nature at its best!
long_description: Our tour begins east of Vail at the parking lot of Bighorn Creek Trail. The hike can be classified as moderately difficult, since we have to overcome a steep section in the beginning. Later on, the route is flatter and can be hiked easily. We hike along forest trails, pastures and meadows. In some places the therrain is quite difficult, most of the time rather easy though. Highlights are the beautiful views of Vail and Bighorn and the untouched nature. Furthermore, the hike can be extended by a few kilometers on the Bighorn Creek Trail.

title: Silence Trail
short_description: Short and easy trail, but with a great diversity of fauna and flora within the State Park of Jaraguia. Ideal for children and the whole family.
long_description:
Beautiful trail, having the possibility to see some animals very close. Without doubt one of the best parks in the capital. The Parque Estadual do Jaraguá é an ideal place for short walks, because its trails are easy, short, flat, safe and located less than 1 hour from downtown São Paulo. Furthermore, there is public transport that takes you to the park.
Hope to arrive in the early hours of the morning;, if youê go on a Saturday or Sunday, considering that in the course of the day many people will á have the same idea. For nature lovers, several species of birds, mammals and insects can be seen. There are no major difficulties in parking, there is a good infrastructure of toilets, kiosks and court.

images.caption: Trilha do Silêncio, Parque Estadual do Jaraguá, São Paulo

title: The Dent de Moirans on foot in the Vercors
short_description: This hiking trail takes you along the northern paths of the Vercors massif. Like the prow of a ship, the Dent de Moirans is a great spot for overlooking the Isère valley!
long_description: The itinerary begins amidst meadows and crops and continues through undergrowth to the Dent de Moirans lookout point, a veritable promontory offering sublime panoramic views over the Isère valley and the Chartreuse, Belledonne and Ecrins massifs.

title: To the Mary's Cross and the Lourdes Grotto near Achern
short_description: This route from the Illenau via the saddle to the Marienkreuz is a very beautiful, easy Nordic Walking tour. It takes us to the Waldsee lake and the Lourdes Grotto.
long_description: Our tour first takes us in the direction of the woodland. At the Illenbach we turn right following the signs. After just under 1 km, turn right at the T-junction and left again at the next junction. Here we walk straight ahead into the forest, past the forest lake and the restaurant as well as the sports field. The asphalt path now becomes a wide gravel path. This is where the ascent to the saddle begins. After 1.5 km we come to a fork in the path, we follow the signs straight up the mountain until the path makes a bend. Here we leave the gravel path and go up the mountain on a path for a short time. After about 200 m, the path joins a wider path. After a good 500 m we reach the saddle, turn right and start our descent. At the next crossroads, we turn right and continue down the mountain until we reach the Lourdes Grotto. Following the right-hand bend of the path, we turn right behind the Marian statue, which we reach after 300 m, back to the forest lake. Along the lake we come back to the inn and back to the Maison de France.

images.caption: View of Sasbach and the Rhine plain.
The former Maison de France in Achern.
The educational apiary of the Achern Beekeepers' Association.
The statue of Mary in the Lourdes Grotto in Oberachern.

title: Red Round Schönthal
short_description: This wonderful tour takes us through the forest near the village of Flischbach, which has been awarded a prize for its beauty. Here, mushroom pickers will also find what they are looking for.
long_description: At the car park we walk from the information board to the right onto the road. Our route is the red loop "No. 2". Soon all three signposted routes turn left. We walk very nicely along the edge of the forest. We reach the forest where our route turns right at a fork. After a long climb, we reach two resting benches at a crucifix with a memorial stone. When the path joins another one, we follow it to the right. At the next fork, keep to the right. We pass a hikers' car park. Shortly before the wide forest path leaves the forest, we turn right onto a forest path. At the following crossroads, we go straight ahead and join the outward trail, which we follow to the left back to the starting point.

images.caption: The route runs very beautifully through the forest.
We start from the Vogelbierl hikers' car park.
At a crucifix, two benches invite you to take a rest.
At the starting point, this board informs us about the course of the Nordic Walking routes.
In this area we can find valuable edible mushrooms such as the curly hen when the weather is right.
After a short stretch on the road, all three routes turn left.
We start from the Vogelbierl hikers' car park.

title: Biendorf round
short_description: The majority of our circular tour leads us across fields and through forests. In some places we come across manor houses that still show much of their old splendour.
long_description: After a few metres on the main road, we turn right into the forest. We pass the sports field and enter the mixed forest. Behind the forest reserve, we turn right. The path initially leads us along the forest, but after a short distance we walk into the middle of it. After a few hundred metres we are back at the edge of the forest. We turn right and continue towards Körchow. Before entering the village, there is a covered rest area (1). After a break, we walk into the small village. At the crossroads in Körchow, we turn right into Hofstraße and see the manor house (2) in front of us. We recognise the individual farm buildings that were built around a small pond. The manor house is at the front, giving us a glimpse of the old splendour. In front of the manor house we turn right and stand on the narrow road to Jörnstorf. Here, on the Kirchweg, we follow the white-yellow markings to the left. After about one kilometre, a mixed forest begins again. We emerge from the forest and come to a bridge over the Hellbach. At a rest area before the bridge, we inform ourselves about the nature trail (3) along the Hellbach. Before the bridge, the road turns off to Jörnstorf. Follow the signs into the village. In Hof Jörnstorf (4) we pass the estate and continue on the road towards Biendorf. Now begins a gently ascending, narrow road that leads us to Biendorf. At its highest point is a lookout hut (5), from which we have a magnificent view over the landscape. The early Gothic church (6) of Biendorf awaits us at the entrance to the village. After visiting the 13th century church, we walk back along the main road to the starting point.

images.caption: A rest area at the edge of the forest invites you to take a break.
The honeycombs contain information about life in the river.
From this elevated lookout hut we have a wide view over the country.

title: गुरु शिखर का साइकिल टूर
short_description: यह अरावली की सबसे ऊँची छोटी गुरु शिखर का साइकिल द ौरा है जहाँ से अरावली पर्वतमाला और माउंट आबू का सु न्दर दृश्य दिखाई देते हैं।
long_description:
गुरु शिखर राजस्थान के अर्बुदा पर्वतों की एक चोटी है जो अरावली पर्वतमाला का सबसे ऊँचा स्थान भी है। इसकी अधिकतम ऊंचाई 1722 मीटर है। यह पर्वत शिखर भगवान विष्णु के दत्तात्रेय अवतार से जुड़ा हुआ है और यहाँ पर उनको समर्पित एक गुफा मंदिर भी है। माउंट आबू से 15 किलोमीटर दूर स्थित गुरु शिखर तक साइकिल टूर करना संभव है। माउंट आबू बस डिपो से यह साइकिल दौरा शुरू किया जा सकता है। बस डिपो के पास एक किराये की साइकिल की दुकान भी है। यह साइकिल टूर प्रसिद्ध दिलवाड़ा जैन मदिरों के बिल्कुल करीब से होकर गुजरता है। पूरा रास्ता एक डामर वाली पक्की सड़क है जिस पर दुपहिया और चौपहिया वाहनों की आवाजाही भी रहती है। मार्ग की एक तरफ़ा लंबाई 15 किलोमीटर है जिसे आराम से धीरे धीरे कवर करने में 2 घंटा लगता है। शुरूआती 6 किलोमीटर का रास्ता एकदम समतल है और उसके बाद का बचा हुआ बाकी 8 किलोमीटर रास्ता हलकी चढ़ाई वाला है। फिट या शौकिया साइकिलिस्ट को इसे दौरे को पूरा करने में कुछ ख़ास दिक्कत नहीं आनी चाहिए।
गुरु शिखर के तले पर पहुंचने के बाद आखिरी चरण हाइक करके पूरा करना पड़ता है। यहाँ से शीर्ष पर जाने के लिए करीब 300 सीढ़ियां चढ़नी पड़ती हैं। गुरु शिखर के शीर्ष से अरावली और माउंट आबू शहर का सुन्दर दृश्य दिखाई देता है। माउंटेन टॉप पर भगवान दत्तात्रेय का एक छोटी मंदिर भी है। इस तरह यह दौरा फिटनेस और तीर्थयात्रा दोनों का आनंद एक साथ देता है।

images.caption: माउंट आबू के गुरु शिखर से दिखता अरावली पर्वतमाला का शानदार दृश्य, राजस्थान, भारत।
गुरु शिखर राजस्थान का सबसे ऊँचा पर्वत है, माउंट आबू, भारत।
माउंट आबू राजस्थान में गुरु शिखर की ओर जाने वाली साइकिलिंग सड़क का हिस्सा।

title: गुड़ीबंदे किला ट्रैक
short_description: गुड़ी बंदे किला भारत के कर्नाटक राज्य के चिक्कबल्ला पुर ज़िले में स्थित एक शानदार पहा ड़ी किला है जहाँ तक हाईकिंग करके पहुँचा जा सकता है ।
long_description:
गुड़ीबंदे किला का निर्माण 400 साल पहले करीब 17 वीं शताब्दी में बायरे गौड़ा नामक एक स्थानीय सरदार ने करवाया था। यह किला प्रसिद्ध मधुगिरी किले का छोटा रूप है। गुड़ीबंदे किले के शीर्ष पर एक शिव मंदिर है जिसे "श्री रामेश्वर मंदिर" के नाम से जाना जाता है और ऐसी मान्यता है की इसे ऋषि विश्वामित्र और भगवान राम द्वारा स्थापित किया गया था। किला मजबूत और ठोस बलुआ पत्थर यानी सैंडस्टोन से बनाया गया है। , जिसे 108 ज्योतिर्लिंगों में से एक माना जाता है। किले में मूल रूप से 19 तालाब थे जो की बारिश के पानी की हार्वेस्टिंग के लिए बने थे और हर साल 3 लाख लीटर पानी जमा करते थे।
यह ट्रैक छोटा और आसान स्तर का है जो नए और अनुभवी सभी हाइकर्स के लिए ठीक है। ट्रेल हलकी चढ़ाई वाली है और इसकी दूरी एक घंटे के अंदर तय की जा सकती है। ट्रेल के अंत में एक सूर्योदय बिंदु भी है जहाँ से आसपास और भैरसागर झील का सुन्दर दृश्य दिखाई देता है।

images.caption: चिक्कबल्लापुर जिले के गुड़ीबंद शहर में स्थित भव्य गुड़ीबंद किला, कर्नाटक, भारत।
चिकबल्लापुर जिले के गुड़ीबंदे किले के पास पहाड़ी की चोटी से दिखता हुआ पैनोरैमिक दृश्य, कर्नाटक, भारत।

title: Three countries in two days: cycling around Lake Constance (main lake)
short_description: Lake Constance is one of the most popular holiday destinations in the whole of Germany. The mild climate, the pretty lakeside towns, three countries, the proximity to the mountains and the many cultural attractions attract countless visitors every year to the "Swabian Sea", as the lake is also called.
long_description:
Once, instead of today's Lake Constance, there was a huge ice-age glacier that gouged out the current depth of the lake through its movements. Today, the third largest lake in Central Europe at the foot of the Alps connects three countries: Germany, Austria and Switzerland. We can cycle through these three countries and their three cultures in two days. We enjoy Lake Constance in all its beauty, experience a lot of culture along our route, can always stop for a swim at one of the beaches and, on a clear day, marvel at the snow-covered peaks of the Alps.
The tour starts at the Meersburg ferry (or in Konstanz and we take the ferry) and takes us through Friedrichhafen, Lindau, Bregenz, Rorschach, Romanshorn, Kreuzlingen and Konstanz. The first day will be a little more relaxed with 45 km and plenty of time for sightseeing along the route. The second day with 80 km will be a bit more challenging.
In Constance we should take an extra day off to explore the town, enjoy the flair and possibly do a short hike, e.g. from the Imperia in Constance to the Horn lido (Hörnle).

images.caption: Lion pier at the port of Lindau

title: Circular walk around Grafing
short_description: Lots to see and little effort - that's what awaits you on the Grafinger Spazier-Rundweg.
long_description: We start our hike at Villa Katharina in Schlossstraße. From here, we walk to the right along the forest path into Großer Dobel (1). At the fork in the road, keep left - the Mariensäule (2) is in sight - until you reach Graf-Ernst-Straße. Continue along this road for about 250 m to the right and then turn left onto the forest path to the mirror ponds (3). Behind the third pond, follow the green sign "Spazierweg". Keep left and cross a small stream on stepping stones. The path leads us to a forest road, on which we continue to the right. Soon we turn left to the Schlossgaststätte (4) in Unterelkofen. There we keep to the right and walk below Elkofen Castle (5) until we reach "Neuhäusl". Here we turn left, walk to Schlossstraße and walk right back to our starting point.

images.caption: A view of the Marian Column.

title: Hiking in the Luberon by the Quillot
short_description: A beautiful circuit on the heights of Robion and Maubec to take advantage of magnificent panoramic views of the Luberon and Rhône valleys. A real treat!
long_description:
From the Théâtre de Verdure in Robion, the route starts directly with a steep climb for just over a kilometre, then a succession of false flats or less difficult climbs will take you to the heights.
Don't miss a few stops along the way to appreciate the panoramas that are available to you: the Monts de Vaucluse, the Alpilles, the Mont Ventoux (on a clear day), the Mourre Nègre...
Then, for 1 km, you walk between the Vallon de Peyrot and the Petite Trappe with a dense forest on each side of the path which is not shaded unlike the majority of the route. You then arrive at Le Quillot and turn left to join the Draille de Maubec. A stony descent awaits you, sometimes rough, but always with the Géant de Provence and the pretty village of Maubec below in sight.
The return is behind the Royères du Prieuré campsite and then along a quiet little road before reaching the starting point of the circuit.
A nice loop to discover a pretty corner of Provence!

title: England Coast Path - Newport Bridge to North Gare
short_description: This route is part of the England Coast Path National Trail.
long_description:
The 16 km (10 miles) stretch of the England Coast Path (ECP) from Newport Bridge to North Gare is now open to the public. 
  The England Coast Path is happening because of a completely new right of access that gives everyone the legal right to explore our coast for the very first time. It is much more than just a path, it gives access to beaches, cliff-tops, and most of the wonderful habitats around our coast. You can see the open sections and how they relate to the other National Trails here.
  Coastal sections of existing National Trails will become part of the England Coast Path in time. This will give the Trails better protection when the coast erodes. The Trails won't lose their own identities though, they will still be National Trails in their own right and the signage will be the same, but you may see new signs saying 'part of the England Coast Path'.
  You can find out about the other National trails on the official National Trail website.

title: From Bernshausen to Bad Salzungen - Rhön
short_description: This medium-length hike is the last stage of the Hochrhöner, a multi-day hike through the Rhön.

images.caption: The Bernshäuser Kutte is a beautifully situated natural lake.
On the summit plateau of the Pleß, numerous seating groups invite you to take a break.
The observation tower on the Pleß is open at weekends.
A beautiful view of Bad Salzungen.
The Bad Salzung graduation house - brine to breathe deeply.

title: Rando Lac de Payolle - La Gaoube and les Esclozes
short_description: A beautiful outing, to be done in summer or winter (with shoes or snowshoes depending on the level of snow), which follows the Gaoube stream before rising and returning via the ridges and woods.

title: In the "border triangle" of Franconia, Swabia and Old Bavaria around Monheim
short_description: The small town of Monheim lies in the middle of the Altmühltal Nature Park and forms the centre of the border triangle of Franconia, Swabia and Old Bavaria. Our hike takes us through the gentle hilly landscape east of the town, which was formed in the Jurassic period. Near Ried, we pass a ring wall that dates back to the Middle Ages.
long_description: The small town of Monheim lies in the middle of the Altmühltal Nature Park and forms the centre of the border triangle of Franconia, Swabia and Old Bavaria. Particularly impressive is the renovated market square with the town fountain and the town hall, which is surrounded by town houses in Franconian half-timbering. Our hike takes us through the gentle hilly landscape east of the town, which was formed in the Jura. Near Ried, we pass a ring wall that dates back to the Middle Ages.

title: Horgen - Au Seeguet
short_description: A short walk from Horgen station to the Au along the Zürisee.

title: Circular hike near Dötlingen
short_description: This circular walk takes us first past the Dötlinger Steingrab and then deep into the Wildeshauser Geest Nature Park.
long_description:
Our hike begins at the hikers' car park near the Schützenhof and we follow the Rittrumer Kirchweg in a northerly direction. Then we turn right to the stone grave. This restored but partly destroyed burial place was used by people in the early Bronze Age (2200-1600 BC). Excavations in 1956 and 1958 unearthed extensive grave goods, including an amber necklace and 12 hundredweights of clay shards.
We continue our hike and walk to the right through the residential area to the road "Zum Morgenland", where we turn left into the state forest "Sieben Buchen". In the forest, we walk straight ahead for a short distance and turn left. At a crossroads we cross the Geveshauser Kirchweg, leave the next junction on the right and follow the path diagonally to the right. After a while we pass another junction, but continue straight ahead through the forest. Finally, our path comes to a T-junction, where we continue to the left. To our left, the forest ends and we have a clear view over a field, along the edge of which we walk. Shortly afterwards, after a slight bend to the left, we turn right again into the forest. Behind a small clearing, we follow the path to the right and walk straight ahead towards the Poggenpohlsmoor nature reserve. Paths do not lead through the wetland as it is very wet. Furthermore, we are not allowed to enter the moor as it is an important habitat for rare plants and animals.
With the moor always on our left, we walk from north to south along the moor embankment until it meets the Poggenpohlsweg, which we follow to the left. At the next junction, we continue to the right and a few metres further on we turn right again to join the forest path, which leads us to the left in the direction of Dötlingen. We leave the forest at the natural gas storage tank, where we meet the road "Zum Poggenpohlsand" and continue walking on it to the left. After a short while, the field path "Loh" branches off to the right, which becomes the road "Zur Loh", on which we return to our starting point, the hikers' car park at the Schützenhof Dötlingen.

title: From Bad Kissingen to Stralsbach - Rhön
short_description: With this hike we follow the first stage of the Hochrhöner, a long-distance hiking trail through the Rhön.
long_description:
Elegant villas, floral splendour in parks and prestigious spa buildings: even the first few metres of the Hochrhöner have flair. The starting point of the trail is south of Bad Kissingen: From the hiking portal opposite the railway station, we stroll along Kurhausstraße into town and through the centre of Bad Kissingen, Germany's most famous spa town. We follow the Kurhausstraße to the Ludwigsbrücke bridge. Cross the bridge and follow Theresienstraße to the Salinenpromenade/Gradierbau. Salt extraction at the Gradierbau ensured the town's wealth for centuries. From the Saaleauen along the banks of the Saale, we walk up the shady Kaskadental to the Klaushof with its animal enclosures. Soon we reach the forester's lodge at Hermannsruh. Our destination Stralsbach is already in sight, but the Hochrhöner turns off into the forest once more. Soon we are at the edge of a meadow. From the chapel opposite, it is now only a few steps downhill, past the stations of a Way of the Cross, to the first houses of Stralsbach, overlooked by the mountain church. We have reached our destination.
Your destination, the Gasthof Zum Weißen Rössel, is not far away.

images.caption: In the Klaushof Wildlife Park you can experience the shy forest animals up close.
Bad Kissingen is a health region where exercise is a priority.
The promenade along the Franconian Saale is used by many recreational athletes.
The Klaushof forester's lodge is the starting and finishing point of our hiking tour.

title: From Riezlern in Kleinwalsertal to the Gottesacker
short_description:
The dry regions of the Gottesacker offer a unique flora that is usually only known from a rock garden. The karst plateau can only be found in this form in Germany in the Steinernes Meer in the Berchtesgaden Alps.
On the way, you pass the imposing Hölloch, a cave system with an approx. 77 m deep entrance gorge.
The view to the south is limited by the mighty Ifen wall.

title: Local history trail around St. Georgen
short_description: St. Georgen is the focus of this circular tour. From here, the route goes over the Sternenhöhe and the Kesselberg to the Brigach spring and back over the Sturmbühl and the Sommerauer Höhe.
long_description: Our circular tour starts at the market square in St. Georgen. A good orientation aid for the tour is provided by the 20 information boards that have been set up along the route. If you don't find one of these signs for more than two kilometres, you have almost certainly strayed from the hiking route... The first of these signs is in front of the post office on the market square. From here we walk the first part of the tour always on the "Mittelweg Pforzheim-Waldshut". This section of the trail is marked with a red rhombus with a white bar. We follow the signpost "Heimatpfad" over a short flight of stairs to the Catholic church. Here you will find the second information board and continue in the direction of the signpost "Heimatpfad". At the next corner, follow the sign with the red rhombus in the direction of the monastery pond to the third information board. A paved footpath now leads steeply downhill and under a subway. We reach the fourth information board, continue to follow the red rhombus in the direction of the Way of the Cross and after about 700 m we reach the edge of the forest. Continue along the edge of the forest and past the fifth information board, from where we have a beautiful view back to St. Georgen. We hike, slightly ascending, up into the forest, past majestic old fir trees that stand here to the left and right of the path. A little further on we come to the seventh information board - here we have a magnificent panoramic view of the valley. The path leads us to the eighth information board. From there we follow the signpost with the red rhombus to the left until we reach a road. Now we walk along the path, which runs alternately to the right and left of the road, past the bus stop, to the youth recreation and education centre. From here, take the path to the left in front of the buildings uphill through a fairytale-looking coniferous forest to the tenth information board. From here on, the path is not always easy to find and you have to pay close attention to the signposts and the markings (red rhombus). After we always follow the red rhombus to the eleventh and twelfth information board, we orientate ourselves from the twelfth information board on a new marking: We now hike along the blue rhombus on the access path Kesselberg-Hochwälder Höhe in the direction of St. Georgen. After about 500 m we reach the Hirzwald inn. Then we continue along the road, following the blue rhombus. Cross the road after about 200 m and follow the path to information board 13. From here you can take a short detour to the Brigach spring. Follow the signs downhill and, after visiting the spring, return to information board 13. We continue, still following the blue rhombus, over the Sturmbühl, past the next information boards to the Sommerauer Höhe. Through a varied landscape, with alternating meadows and wooded areas, we reach information board 18. About 100 m further on, we hike left into a forest, where the 19th information board is located. From here we change the path and now follow the signpost of the Heimatpfad, which is marked with a yellow rhombus, through the forest, walk past a small pond and reach the glass yards lying in a meadow. We continue hiking until we reach St. Georgen. In the village we walk along the asphalted road until we reach Westendstraße. We follow this to the right and finally turn left into Sommerauerstraße, which after a short stretch becomes the main road and leads us back to the starting point, the market square.

images.caption: After a good one and a half kilometres of walking, we have this view of St. Georgen.
Again and again, the tour offers impressive views of the region.
We reach the glass courtyards shortly before the end of our tour.
To the west, after 3.6 km, there is this view of Brigach.
The Sturmbühl offers a view of the region.
The St. Georgen heritage trail offers many views.

title: पलक्कड फोर्ट का साइकिल दौरा
short_description: पलक्कड़ फोर्ट साइकिल टूर एक शहरी दौरा है जो आपको पलक्कड़ शह र के अंदर स्थित एक ऐतिहासिक किले तक ले जाता है।
long_description:
पलक्कड़ किला बहुत प्राचीन काल से अस्तित्व में है, लेकिन इसके शुरूआती इतिहास के बारे में बहुत कम जानकारी मिलती है। मध्यकाल में पलक्कड़ रणनीतिक रूप से एक महत्वपूर्ण शहर था। जब यहाँ के तत्कालीन स्थानीय शासक पलक्कड़ अच्चन ने हैदर अली से ज़मोरिन राजवंश के खिलाफ मदद मांगी, तो हैदर अली ने उसकी मदद करने के बदले में पलक्कड़ शहर मांग लिया। उसने ही किले को मजबूत और विस्तारित किया और इसलिए कभी कभी यह समझा जाता है की हैदर अली ने यह किला बनवाया। 
पलक्कड़ किले तक का साइकिल दौरा पलक्कड़ टाउन रेलवे स्टेशन की पार्किंग से शुरू होता है और शहरी सडकों से होता हुआ अंत में किले तक पहुँचता है। रास्ता मुख्यत एक डामर वाली सड़क है। किले पर पहुँचने के बाद रास्ता अच्छी रखरखाव वाली कच्ची सड़क बन जाता है। टूर के दौरान मार्ग का कठिनाई स्तर आसान है।  ज्यादातर रास्ता समतल है लेकिन किले के पास आखिरी चरण में कुछ उतार चढ़ाव आते हैं। किले अपने आप में बहुत सुन्दर है। साइकिल टूर के साथ साथ किले की घुमाई-फिराई दोनों को आराम से 4-5 घंटे में पूरा किया जा सकता है।

images.caption: पलक्कड़ फोर्ट का साइकिल टूर पलक्कड़ टाउन रेलवे स्टेशन से शुरू होता है। केरल, भारत
पलक्कड़ शहर में पलक्कड़ फोर्ट, केरल,भारत।
पलक्कड़ शहर के बीचोबीच पलक्कड़ किले का नज़ारा केरल, भारत

title: Karl May Circuit through Hohenstein-Ernstthal in the Ore Mountains
short_description: We follow in the footsteps of Karl May and his stories.
long_description:
Our walk in the footsteps of Karl May begins at the house where the author was born at Karl-May-Strasse 54 and leads us from here to the church of St. Trinitatis on Neumarkt. Karl May was baptised in this church on 26 February 1842. After visiting the church, we walk from Neumarkt to Badegasse and on to Dresdner Strasse, which we cross to Karlstrasse. We follow the street to the upper part of the Altmarkt and enjoy a wonderful view of the market and the Hotel „Drei Schwanen“. This is where Karl May was arrested in 1861 for allegedly stealing a clock.
Now we follow the path further past the St. Christophori church into the Windmühlengässchen, which we follow up to the Anger Weg. Here we turn right and arrive at a place where the writer Karl May would certainly have felt at home: a ranch like one would find in westerns. From the Pfaffenberg we continue and turn left before the Knüppelbrücke, so that we come to the motorway. We take the hiking trail towards the forest and reach the Karl May cave. It is said that the writer hid here several times from the police when he was wanted for various cases of fraud.
Continue to Goldforstweg and then turn left past the Clausteich pond. At the Schaftreibe we turn left and then right at the next junction. Here we cross the motorway. We now take the sunken path and return to the town centre and our starting point.

title: Hiking route De Meinweg
short_description: De Meinweg is the most southern nature reserve of the Netherlands.
long_description: De Meinweg is 1800 hectares and its terrace landscape makes it a special nature reserve. In the past, the area was mainly woodland, whereas now there is more heathland. This is because many trees have been felled over the years. The area is home to many reptiles, such as lizards, vipers and hookworms;

title: Witness Mountain Tour around Neumarkt
short_description: The Zeugenbergrunde takes us around Neumarkt in der Oberpfalz. Among other things, there are several table mountains and breathtaking views to discover.

title: The Hespenbusch cemetery near Großenkneten
short_description: This tour leads through the beautiful Wildeshauser Geest Nature Park near Großenkneten and to the prehistoric "Hespenbusch cemetery".
long_description:
We start our hike at the town hall in Großenkneten, first walk to the main road and turn left there. Before the railway tracks we turn left and walk along the street "Am Kirchholz". At the end of the road, we turn left onto Grevskamp, which bends to the left after a few metres. Further on, a path branches off to the right and we reach Ahlhorner Straße, which we follow to the right. Soon we come to a transformer station, where the path "Bakenhuser Esche" branches off. We then walk straight ahead for quite a while and then into the forest. We cross a crossroads and leave a junction on the left before we walk diagonally left and follow the right-hand curve of the path. Shortly afterwards, we turn left and walk along the edge of the forest until we come to the Hageler Straße, which we follow only a few metres to the left and then immediately leave again to the right. At the next opportunity, we turn off before the forest and keep straight on along its edge. We stay on a straight stretch, leaving a few junctions to the left and right and follow the natural course of the path to Hellbusch. There we do not turn into Hellbuscher Weg, but into the following path to the right, cross the beech avenue and walk straight ahead on an unnamed road to the end. From here we turn right to the natural monument "Gräberfeld Hespenbusch", which is located on the left of the road. An information board explains what we can see here. The total of 54 mounds of this prehistoric cemetery are clearly visible in untouched heath landscape. When archaeological investigations were carried out in the late 19th century, a single bronze bead helped to date it more precisely. The burial ground was used from the Late Bronze Age to the Pre-Roman Iron Age (from about 1200 BC to the birth of Christ).
At the Buchholz farm, which is located right next to the cemetery, you can stop by by appointment and enjoy fresh bread from the stone oven. At the next junction, we turn left and go straight on. After a while we cross the Moorbeker Straße, pass a racing stable and follow the road "Lehms" to the left at the end. We stay on this road for about 3 km, which then briefly turns into the road "Am Hogenesch" and then becomes Hageler Straße. One last time we turn right into the street "Am Esch", which ends at the market where our starting point, the town hall, is located.

title: From Oberrot through the Schlattwald
short_description: On this short hike, children in particular get their money's worth at the forest playground.
long_description:
We start our tour at the Stiersbach hikers' car park in Oberrot. From here we walk past the Stiersbach forest playground and continue to the next fork in the path. Here we turn right and follow the path up the slight incline through the beautiful Schlattwald forest. We follow the path back to our starting point.
Oberrot is considered one of the oldest communities in the Limpurger Land. It is likely that it was first founded by the Franks as early as 650 AD. Worth seeing testimonies of Oberrot's long history are the old town and the moated castle surrounded by it.

title: Franzbogen Tour - St. Leon-Rot
short_description: On this somewhat shorter tour we hike through the Hardtwald forest in the south of St. Leon-Rot.
long_description:
Most archers will be familiar with the name "Franzbogen". Franzbogen 3-D animals are considered the best and most beautiful in Europe and can be found at every major field bow tournament on the continent.
On this pleasant walk, we experience the birthplace and creation site of the Franzbogen animals (the production hall). We walk past the grounds of the St. Leon-Rot field and compound archers and walk through the shady Hardtwald forest, one of the most beautiful forests in the region, where the famous asparagus tournament is shot every year in May.
With a bit of luck, we may spot an animal here and there - alive or made of foam.

images.caption: The forest of St.Leon-Rot is a paradise for archers.

title: Hinterseerunde (AT)
short_description: Leisurely and family-friendly hike around Salzburg's Hintersee.
long_description: The route runs directly along the water. The lake impresses with its fantastically clear and clean water.

title: Jam Town Bad Schwartau
short_description: This short hike takes us through the jam town of Bad Schwartau.
long_description: Our short hike starts at the spa gardens in Bad Schwartau. From there we walk along Eutiner Straße into the "Töpferberg". At the end of the hill, we cross Pariner Straße and turn left into Schnoorstraße. On the right, we follow Kirchweg, which leads into Lindenstraße. We turn left and come to "Ranzau Allee", which turns right into the street "Alt Rensefeld". Then we turn left into "Strampfershof", follow Faaschweg to the right and walk on the right into "Windberg". Now we reach the green areas of "Möhlenbarg", walk to the end and pass the small and large park lakes. A traffic light brings us safely across the Eutiner Ring, on the other side of which the Markttwiete, a small pedestrian zone, begins. At the Markt, we turn right and then follow Lübecker Straße to the left. Finally, we turn right into Geibelstraße and then left back to the Kurpark where we started our walk.

title: Hiking Route on March 14, 2022
short_description: Crossways Christian Centre

title: To the Hammersee on Juist
short_description: We hike to the natural monument Hammersee, the largest freshwater lake in the North Sea islands.
long_description:
The East Frisian island of Juist on the tidal flats of the North Sea is only 17 km long and in many places only 500 m wide. Motor vehicles are almost exclusively prohibited on the island, so hiking and cycling here can be a particularly relaxing experience.
On our hike we pass the harbour of Juist and can have a look at the island's new landmark, the 17 m high sea mark with beacon. Since 2008, you can also find the newly built marina with over 200 berths here.
Then we walk to Hammersee, the largest freshwater lake on a North Sea island. It was first formed in 1660 by the influx of sea water and is now an important biotope for the island's birds and insects.

images.caption: In the evening along the beach...

title: Virne-Burgweg
short_description: This tour offers a fabulously beautiful mix of forest and open moorland. Exploring the ruins of Virneburg is worthwhile and from Schafberg you have an overwhelming view of the Eifel panorama. The scenic highlight awaits us in the Blumenrather Heide.
long_description:
Highlights:
Nitzbach valley, Virneburg castle ruins (mid-13th century), extensive juniper heaths (Blumenrath and Schafberg), mountain path, Eifel panorama, view of Nürburg Castle.

The dream trail starts at the Virneburg community centre and leads across the Nitzbach up to the small chapel. A narrow meadow path winds its way to the mighty ruin of the Virneburg. The descent leads down into the village to the edge of the forest. Above the Nitzbach stream, the trail continues through the forest. Steadily uphill, the trail leads through a side valley into the high forest and then to the juniper heaths on the Schafberg with a phenomenal Eifel panorama. After another field and forest passage and crossing the B258, the trail reaches Blumenrather Heide. The loosened heath stands out beautifully from the surrounding mixed forest and offers magnificent views as far as Nürburg Castle. Passing the Brauberg, the trail leads to the refuge above Virneburg, where there is a great view. A mountain path leads along the edge of the slope to the descent into the Nitzbach valley. At a stream crossing, tired feet can be cooled before a short ascent through lush meadow slopes follows. A rest area at the edge of the forest with a great view of the Virneburg invites you to take a last rest before continuing to the starting point.

images.caption: A bench along the way invites you to take a short break.
The castle is a great place to romp around.
We are approaching the next historic building.

title: Rheingoldbogen
short_description: Following in the footsteps of the Romans and viticulture, you cycle through varied countryside, past well-tended vines and unspoilt hedgerows onto the Rhine plateau with fantastic views of the Rhine valley and the Rhine loop.
long_description:
The highlights of this tour include:
Fantastic views into the Rhine valley and of the Rhine bend at Osterspai (UNESCO World Heritage: Upper Middle Rhine Valley), of Marksburg Castle, Braubach, historic vineyards of Boppard Hamm, Brey, Rhine plateau, Jakobsberg Monastery, Mother of God Chapel.
From the starting point at Brey cemetery, the path soon leads into the forest. Here, shafts provide a view of old water pipes built by the Romans. At the Brey sports field, a narrow path leads steeply up to a refuge with a great view towards the Rhine valley. Continue on soft forest paths to the Rhine plateau. Inconspicuous elevations in the forest conceal a stately burial mound. The trail curves around this area and reaches the former Jesuit monastery Jakobsberg, today used as a hotel with golf course. The trail descends on forest paths towards Peternach. The path reaches the famous vineyards of Bopparder Hamm, where a panoramic view of the largest bend in the Rhine opens up with views of Boppard, Filsen and Osterspai. Accompanied by dense hedges, the path turns its back on the Rhine valley. The flat plateau offers phenomenal views of Marksburg Castle, which seems within reach. Across open fields, the meadow path reaches the Mother of God Chapel. The path now heads downhill and runs along an idyllic meadow path down to the starting point in Brey.

images.caption: A beautiful half-timbered house with a rose vine.
Aerial view of the Rhine bend near Osterpai.
Along the hiking route, beautiful places invite you to take a rest.
A little wine education right on the spot.

title: Seven Ponds Circuit - Wermsdorf
short_description: On this medium-length hike we experience forests and, in addition to the seven ponds, a bonus pond.
long_description: Our tour starts in the centre of Wermsdorf, at the old hunting lodge, and leads us along Grimmaer Straße, Schumannweg and Sachsendorfer Straße on the Förstersteig trail through the forest for a while. Soon we reach the first pond on our hike, the "Zeißigteich". We walk on to the "Kirchenteich" and after it we come to the "Drei Teiche". Here we can also take a look at the excavation site "Wüstes Dorf Nennewitz", about which we can inform ourselves with the help of display boards. From here we follow the "Three Ponds" further to the "Doctor's Pond", on whose southern shore evidence of Bronze Age settlement can be found. We continue to the north bank and from here to the "Reiherteich". Here we turn left into the forest and turn right again after the fourth crossing. We cross the B6 federal road and continue along the path through the forest. At the next opportunity, we turn right. Once we have crossed the B6 again, we walk at an obtuse angle to the right at the next junction. Now we follow the path straight ahead until we reach the "Häuschenteich". Here we leave the forest and walk through fields towards Wermsdorf. We return via Luppaer Straße directly to the starting point of our tour at the old hunting lodge.

title: Dense forest around Rathenow
short_description: This easy and short tour takes us into the mysterious forest landscape around Rathenow.
long_description: Surrounded by countryside and nature reserves in the area of the lower Havel, the town of Rathenow lies at the centre of the largest nature park in the state of Brandenburg. The district itself has seven nature reserves. On this tour we walk through part of this beautiful nature. To the east of the town, we follow pleasant paths through the dense Rathenow urban forest.

images.caption: We hike through the dense forest near Rathenow.

title: Erlbach Mountain Tour near Markneukirchen
short_description: This extensive hike in the German-Czech border region takes us up five hills in the Vogtland Nature Park.
long_description:
We start our tour at the market place of Erlbach and walk on the Eubabrunner Straße out of the village. On the left of the road is a small pond, behind which we turn left into Waldstraße. Parallel to the Stockrauhbächel brook, our route leads towards a piece of forest and right along the edge of the forest until the last houses of the street "Waldhäuser" can be seen on the right. Here our path enters the forest and
goes straight on until it reaches the German-Czech border, which we follow on the left. Now we first go downhill to the Julius stone, a border stone from 1544 with the coat of arms of the Electorate of Saxony and a Bohemian lion, and then steeply uphill again to the Hinterer Kegelberg, the highest point of our "mountain tour". At the summit, we turn left and descend through the Kegelberg ski area to the former forest restaurant. In serpentines, our path now winds its way back along the border up to the Luchspöhl. We follow the state border until we reach the Drei-Rain stones, which mark the border point between the former dioceses of Naumburg, Regensburg and Meissen. Here we leave the border in a westerly direction and hike downhill into the Landesgemeindetal. Following the Floßbach stream, we pass the Hintere and Vordere Floßteich ponds, both - as the name suggests - witnesses to the former timber rafting in the Vogtland. Near the Vorderen Floßteich is the Tannenmühle, a former paper mill that now houses a children's home. Now we go uphill to the right to the Gopplasgrüner Berghäuser (mountain houses), from where we enjoy a magnificent view of the village of Erlbach and the Schwarzbach valley. Then we descend to the district of Gopplasgrün, turn left there, turn right at the end of the village and reach a stream. Cross the stream and walk parallel to it along the edge of the forest to the right. At the last houses of Gopplasgrün we come to a T-junction, where we turn left and then left again at the next junction. Continue straight ahead on the Mittelweg up to Spornreuth, a former execution site, where a plaque commemorates the last execution in 1823. After we have mastered this last ascent, we walk through the fields down to Erlbach and return to the market square, our starting point, via the street Am Sommerberg and Kirchstraße.

title: From Dermbach to Urnshausen - Rhön
short_description: On this medium hike through the Rhön, we are accompanied by the legendary Rhön Paul.
long_description: The starting point of our tour is on the outskirts of Dermbach in Waldstraße. Shortly before the end of the road, we take a path to the left through the trees across the slope. Fruit trees and hedges accompany us at the start of this short stage along the Gläserberg to Glattbach. The Rhönpaulus lived not far from the village. The notorious robber stands as a wooden figure on the village square. You cross the small river Felda, then the trail climbs steeply. In the Ibengarten nature reserve, the branches of old yew trees form a dark green tunnel through which the hiker passes. You pass the village of Wiesenthal. Past a dishevelled beech tree, the Hochrhöner climbs up the slope of the Horn across meadows. The path climbs steeply in the forest to the top of the mountain, which offers views of Roßdorf. The trail descends through beech forest. A small valley is crossed, then the trail heads towards the houses of the small village of Bernshausen.

images.caption: The Bernshäuser Kutte is a beautifully situated natural lake.
On the last part of the route we enjoy a beautiful view of Bernshausen.

title: From Oberdorf to the Falltobel
short_description: This tour presents the diversity of the Allgäu in an impressive way. Wide lakes, lush pastures, dense forests and deep ravines alternate with picturesque villages and huts.
long_description: On our tour we experience the unique Niedersonthofener See lake with its adjacent wet meadows, walk along the picturesque little village of Niedersonthofen, which boasts many pretty old houses, and soon reach the densely wooded and very varied Falltobel. Shortly before the turning point we reach the waterfall, which is often compared to the veil falls on the Ammer. On the Rückweg über Gopprechts we can let our gaze wander über the lake to the Illertal before the descent. Filled with many beautiful impressions, we enjoy a drink at the Seehof after the long tour.

title: Pankeweg (Berlin)
short_description: We follow the Panke from its official source at the Teufelspfuhl in Bernau to its confluence with the Spree - in the middle of Berlin. The cycle and hiking trail runs almost exclusively along the banks of the river, which is characterised by large parks and wide meadows.
long_description:
Since the Panke flows past numerous public transport stops and is therefore easily accessible throughout, we have not divided the route into stages.     
We start our hike at Bernau railway station and walk in a southerly direction past the district of Lindow. (The official source of the Panke is at the Teufelspfuhl a little further north of our chosen starting point). Between Eichwerder and Zepernick we walk along the railway tracks and cross the Dransebach at some sports grounds. Behind Röntgental we follow the Panke on a meadow path to the Schlossparkteichen Buch and thus enter the Berlin city area. Gradually the river widens a little and we walk past several small ponds in the Karow district. Now the Panke at Blankeburg takes us a few metres along the A114 and to Niederschönhausen Palace Park. The baroque palace of the same name was a well-known object of representation of the SED leadership and today shows an exhibition on German history. Parallel to the Majakowskiring, the former housing estate of top GDR politicians, we reach the Volkspark Schönholzer Heide. Passing the Franzosenbecken, we continue to follow the course of the Panke and are soon in Berlin-Wedding. Now we leave the river for a short distance to go around the Erika-Heis ice stadium. Directly behind the stadium we turn right, pass some tennis courts and reach the confluence of the Panke and the Spree. From our finishing point at Nordhafen, we can watch the passenger ships chugging by in peace and quiet.

images.caption: The Panke in Buch Castle Park

title: Danube Cycle Route: from Passau to Vienna in eight days
short_description: The Danube Cycle Route takes us in eight days from the three-river city of Passau to the Austrian capital Vienna, for which we should take an extra day. Plenty of cultural and geological highlights await us along the way.
long_description:
The Danube Cycle Route is one of the most popular cycle routes in Europe and is one of the absolute "classics" - after all, the Danube is the second longest river on the continent after the Volga. It rises in the Swabian town of Donaueschingen and after 2860 km later flows into the Black Sea, crossing Central and Southern Europe along the way.
This tour describes the route from Passau to Vienna. Historical places, a very varied landscape and highlights such as the Schlögener Donauschlinge, the Benedictine Abbey of Melk and large parts of the Wachau will be passed during our journey. The stages are divided in such a way that we have enough time for all the sights. Finally, we reach Vienna and thus the cultural highlight of this tour.
The Danube Cycle Path is generally well signposted and the paths are pleasant to ride as they are mostly flat and well built.

images.caption: View of Passau on the Inn.
Main Square Linz with Plague Column

title: From Rheinfelden around the Dinkelberg
short_description: Our circular tour leads past old estate walls from Roman times and to typical karst phenomena in the shell limestone and promises insights into the history of the Nollinger Berg.
long_description: We start at the St. Felix and St. Regula Church and follow the road to the left up to the forest. After a short but steep climb along a forest path, we reach a comfortable forest path. On the relatively level path we pass the boundary stone „Gutshofweg“ directly to the Römischen Gutshof (1). The protected cultural monument shows the foundation walls of a Roman estate from the time of the Roman settlement of this area in the 1st-3rd century AD. This is one of the few Roman manor houses that have been excavated. We leave the estate behind us and walk along the Wolfsgrabenweg (Wolf's Ditch Path) to the Salzbrünnele (2), an old, set spring, the name of which is carved legibly on the sandstone surround. A small rest area invites you to linger in this attractive natural landscape. The path through the Wolfsgraben (3) runs along a narrow forest path, which can be slippery, especially in the wet season. A short time later we reach the paved path again, which is part of the Nollingen Trimm-Dich path with forest nature trail. Along the Trimm-Dich-Pfad, which was created in 1980, there are information boards about the forest and especially about forest dieback. At a bend in the path there is an old boundary stone with the date 1563, the so-called Totenkopfstein (4). The carved skull probably refers to the village of Geitlikon (Gelken), which was destroyed by a flood in 1504 and never rebuilt, and whose boundaries extended to this spot. The village was probably located south of today's Gelkenhof in the valley basin. According to an old entry in the parish archives of Herten-Degerfelden, 34 people drowned in the night flood. Shortly after the Totenkopfstein, we reach the car park with rest and play area on the connecting road to Obereichsel. Follow the road to the left for a short distance and turn right at the next opportunity. Immediately afterwards, at the next fork in the road, we decide to take the path to the left, which leads slightly downhill. At the next large crossroads, we go steadily uphill to the right, past the water tank on the left and back towards Nollingen. After the Schützenhaus, a tarred footpath leads us down into the village. From here we have a beautiful view of the Rhine plain and Rheinfelden. On reaching the forest again, we could go straight back to our starting point via the road, but we make a detour through the Bachtelengraben (5). This narrow gorge path, which leads steadily uphill through a ditch, is a special experience. However, it is only suitable for sure-footed hikers with good shoes. We reach a forest path via a small staircase, follow it to the left and shortly afterwards meet a forest path. This leads us directly back to the connecting road to Obereichsel (6). With a clear view of the Rhine plain, we hike downhill to turn right at the next opportunity onto an asphalted footpath that leads us directly to Nollingen. Via Obere Dorfstrasse, the old centre of Nollingen's upper village with houses dating back to the 17th century, we reach our starting point at the church a short time later. Just below the church, on the bridge, is the main source of the Nollinger Dorfbach, marked by a large stone.

images.caption: Gorgeous sunset: it doesn't get more atmospheric than this.
We also pass this little fountain.

title: The Hochrhöner (Western Kuppenrhön variant)
short_description: The Hochrhöner is currently one of four German long-distance hiking trails certified as a premium trail by the German Hiking Institute. This seal of quality promises a particularly natural and varied hiking experience along the entire route. The tour indicated here runs from Bad Kissingen to Bad Salzungen.

title: From Vellberg through the Steinbach Valley
short_description: This circular walk runs through the picturesque nature around Vellberg. At the end of this tour, you can take a walk through the old town of Vellberg.

title: Coastal walk from Xlendi to San Lawrenz
short_description: Third stage of the varied coastal circular walk on Gozo – Malta's neighbouring island
long_description: The third stage of our 11 km long coastal walk on Gozo takes us from Xlendi in the west of the island to the highly situated San Lawrenz. Along the way, in addition to exciting cliffs, the Azure Window awaits us. A rock formation that allows us to look through a picture-book arch into the vastness of the ocean. This impressive view makes us forget all the efforts of the tour. But the mistral, which blows steadily all year round, and the waves can take their toll on the rock formation, which is millions of years old. So it cannot be ruled out that the Azure Window is a natural phenomenon that will not last forever.

images.caption: Der Xlendi Tower am Rand der Xlendi Bay
Der Xlendi Tower am Rand der Xlendi Bay

title: Snowshoe: Esterbergalm and Vorderer Riedberg from Garmisch-Partenkirchen
short_description: The Vordere Riedberg near the Rotenkopf (1685 m) is a rewarding snowshoe tour destination away from the often crowded Wank above Garmisch-Partenkirchen, but somewhat more difficult.
long_description:
Individualists climb the Vorderer Riedberg just below the Rotenkopf (here we take into account a protected area), while the majority of tourers climb the Wank. Both tours start at the same car park and the beginning of the ascent is identical. We part ways at the Esterbergalm, which is also a good place to stop on the way back from the summit of the Rotenkopf. Therefore, we should not overload the rucksack with food.
Since this tour from the Esterbergalm is rather seldom used, it often requires track work from the alp. In addition, it is recommended that the tour is only undertaken when the snow cover is sufficiently high, as some tree corpses otherwise make the ascent and descent difficult. With very little avalanche risk, we mostly move on west-facing slopes. The orientation up to the Esterbergalm is very easy, but from the alp it can be a challenge due to the infrequent access and therefore lack of tracks.

images.caption: Daxkapelle on the ascent to the Esterbergalm.

title: From Eibenstock to the Auersberg
short_description: This tour takes us via the "Dam of Peace" to the Auersberg, from whose lookout tower we can enjoy one of the most comprehensive views in the entire Ore Mountains.
long_description: We hike through dense forests to the Sosa dam. It was built between 1949 and 1952 in the Höllengrund near Eibenstock as a youth facility for the FDJ. In the following years, it was also called the "dam of peace". From the lookout tower on the Auerberg you can not only see the heights of the Erzgebirge and the Vogtland, but on a clear day you can also but also, on a clear day, as far as the Ochsenkopf in the Fichtelgebirge Fichtelgebirge (80 km) or even as far as the Monument to the Battle of the Nations in Leipzig (100 km).

title: From Ebensfeld up to the Veitsberg
short_description: On this tour we experience the mountain ranges of the "God's Garden on the Obermain". We hike from Ebensfeld up to the Veitsberg and enjoy the panoramic view and a rest there before returning to Ebensfeld through the Kelbach valley.
long_description:
Our route starts in Ebensfeld, a town with 3,000 inhabitants, which lies at the southern entrance to the "Gottesgarten am Obermain". We start at the car park on the main road and immediately take the footpath and cycle path to the left of the road in a northerly direction until we reach the roundabout. There we take the path to the east and immediately find ourselves on a small land consolidation road up to the Veitsberg - always keeping our destination in mind. Our route is initially flat until we reach the motorway subway. Directly behind the subway we have the opportunity to take a short break at the "Brünnla", an enclosed spring. Now we face the first ascent to the hikers' car park at the Veitsberg, where we again have the opportunity to take a rest on one of the benches with a magnificent view. Now we hike uphill into the forest, soon leaving the asphalt path and reaching a path that leads steeply up to the Veitsberg. The ascent is extremely steep by Franconian standards, so we have well earned a rest on the Veitsberg plateau (don't forget to bring a snack!). Here, too, we find numerous benches with a wonderful view up to the Staffelberg and into the Main valley. We can also peek through a viewing window into the interior of the Veitsberg Chapel - the little church is very popular especially for weddings.
Now we walk in a south-easterly direction downhill to Dittersbrunn, which we reach after passing the hikers' car park. In the village, we turn steeply left downhill into a small road that leads us almost directly to the Veitsberg inn, where we have the opportunity to stop for a break in a typical Franconian inn. After our rest, we follow the Flurbereinigungsweg downhill to Prächting, where we follow the Dittersbrunner Straße to the Prächtinger Hauptstraße. At the crossroads we walk 300 m to the right and have the opportunity to stop at the Landgasthof Hummel with a beautiful beer garden. Through a narrow path at the inn we get down to the Kelbach, where we keep to the right and always follow the course of the stream until we get back to the outskirts of Ebensfeld under the motorway bridge. Here we have the opportunity to take a detour to the left up to the Engelhardtskeller, a very idyllic beer garden, and continue straight ahead along the course of the stream to the main road, where we can take a detour to the left to Gasthof Neuner with its beer garden, continue straight ahead to the parish church Maria Verkündigung, which is well worth seeing, or turn right and walk 200 m back to the starting point.

title: Hike to Shiria Fortress
short_description: An easy hike to the Șiria Fortress.
long_description: The tour takes you from the village of Șiria through a beautiful landscape to the Șiria Fortress;

title: Two peaks from Bodenmais
short_description: This demanding tour leads to two "local mountains" of the spa town Bodenmais. Wonderful views await us.
long_description: First follow the signs for the "Haas Trail" ("Nordic Walking Tour 2"), which takes you to Harlachberger Spitz. On the descent, before reaching the district of Glashütten, take the inconspicuous branch on the right up to the Kuh-Alm. Approx. 300 m after the Kuh-Alm, our route branches off to the right, now marked with the "9", to Böhmhof. In Böhmhof, turn right at the chapel and walk around the hotel up to the Silberberg. The last few metres to the summit are very rocky. We go back along the same path until we reach the path we already know and turn right there. We pass a former tunnel next to the chairlift. Behind the car park we come across a huge mountain man statue, 100 m behind it a path leads us back to Bodenmais.

images.caption: The Kuh-Alm offers a stop for refreshments in the first third of our tour.
Our ascent to the Harlachberg leads through forest.

title: The Thieving Magpie" circular trail near Spiegelau
short_description: A shady circular trail leads us on soft paths through the national park forest and to the forest play area with nature discovery trail.
long_description: We walk to the spa park, which starts at the "Waldbahn Kiosk". At the stream bridge, a board provides information on Nordic walking exercises. We walk between the stream and the lakes to a covered rest area. To the left we have the opportunity to make a detour to the Kneipp facility, but we turn right to the road. From here we follow the red Nordic Walking signs "2" with the name "Die diebische Elster". We follow the markings "Elster" first along a forest path, then along soft paths through the National Park forest. We pass the Jägerfleck settlement. From the "Martinswiese" we follow the forest path, which takes us past babbling brooks to the forest playground. The "Elster" finally points us straight ahead, but we turn left and return to the car park.

images.caption: Large, colourful mushrooms live on the deadwood along the path.
The path leads through sparse beech forest.
Bright green horsetails grow along the streams.
We walk past the lakes of the spa park.

title: Via Aurelia - a sense of Roman culture
short_description: This historic trade route takes you along the Italian coastline with an irresistible charm: Discover one of the most important roads of the former Roman Empire, spanning from central Italy to Southern France.
long_description:
Via Aurelia was constructed back in 100 BC in order to connect Rome, the city of the vast Roman Empire, with Pisa in Tuscany.
With a widespread network of paths and streets, Via Aurelia was also connected with other important trade routes such as Via Appia and Via Aemilia Scaura. Nowadays, it leads from the heart of the Roman Empire to Southern France alongside a picturesque coastal route.
This tour is packed with lots of different impressions: Starting from the busy city center of Rome, we get to the sunny coast of Latium heading for North Italy. Stopping by the National Park Cinque Terre and the stunning port cities of Genoa and Sanremo you can get a sense of what living at the Italian coast feels like. Quite different, though, is the small town of Noli. It’s on the official list of Italy’s ”borghi più belli” (Italy’s most beautiful small towns), but abroad it’s still among Italy’s inside tips.
The route leads to the French city of Arles, one of the countrie’s oldest cities. As Friedrich Barbarossa’s former seat of government, Arles has a lot of cultural spots to offer. However, if you feel like making a field trip, you can go for a stroll through the Camargue, a regional park with picturesque lagoons.

images.caption: "Gigante", a stunning sculpture at  Monterosso al Mare.
Noli, a precious spot on the Italian coastline
