title: Wiesn Tour in Munich
short_description: During the Oktoberfest season, this is the most important tour of all for many people. We experience the marquees, the Bavaria and can make up to six million new friends or even the love of our lives.
long_description:
This cheerful tour takes us around the Oktoberfest. We walk past the impressive festival tents and should decide early on for one or the other. The "Einkehr" becomes problematic on weekends as early as 11 am. We should also not try to move from one tent to the next and drink a beer everywhere. Firstly, no one can tolerate one Maß per tent, and secondly, this is no way to develop a cosy society. That is important. You realise this at the latest when, after the fourth Maß, you are lying in the arms of the gentleman/lady to your left and making eternal vows of friendship or a marriage vow.
Rides are dangerous. For some, however, they unfortunately only become interesting after a few beers. But that can end badly - literally. It's best to ride a few rounds of the carousel before visiting a beer tent and then we can concentrate on the really important things in life: Beer, atmosphere, chicken. The latter is the bone of contention every year, because on the one hand, half a chicken in the tents is usually immensely expensive, on the other hand, there is probably nowhere else you can get such a perfect fried chicken as at the Wiesn. The same goes for the beer. No matter which brewery we choose - the festival beer is good everywhere. Incidentally, it's a little stronger than the beer usually available, something that many newcomers and even more Italians have had to bitterly atone for.
Festival acquaintances are quickly made and even more quickly forgotten. Sometimes they end up on the slopes of the Theresienhöhe in front of the Bavaria and sometimes with being thrown out of the festival tent. This usually happens when you assume that the waitress has given you "clear signals" and that she "looks really great". Never, really never, should the waitress be taken for more than she is: the bringer of beer. Everything else leads nowhere. She is not the marquee management, not the security, not the cigarette machine and definitely not a flirting opportunity.
>

images.caption: Brass band in the Augustiner Festhalle, Oktoberfest Munich
Beer kegs in the Spatenbräu festival hall, Oktoberfest Munich

title: Easy hike near Sighisoara: Aurel Vlaicu -  Trei Drumuri
short_description: An easy hike -or rather a longer walk - part of the Via Transilvanica hiking route. This is recommended for anyone visiting Sighisoara and willing to see some different sights than those advertised in travel books.
long_description:
The route starts from St. Dimitrie Monastery (Aurel Vlaicu). This is where the asphalt ends and a wide forest road begins. The paths are well marked, being on the Via Translvanica route. The Colinele Transilvaniei Association also marked the route with a red stripe.
The road crosses the picturesque and quiet village, heading gently towards the forest. Access to the forest is relatively easy, and the path is easily accessible.
The hiker has the opportunity to admire picturesque hills, pierced from place to place by access roads. The orchards and cultivated or uncultivated fields of the locals extend to the forest.
Apart from the barking of dogs and the occasional roar of cars - until leaving the village - a deep silence dominates the landscape.
At one point, in the forest, the route meets another marking - red cross. Also here on beautiful days, a lovely view opens to the village of Vulcan. Depending on your preferences, you can return or continue to the village of Șapartoc.

title: "The Tree Trail" an experiential trail for children near Borgberg
short_description: A great, fun and educational hiking trail for children in the forest near the town of Burgberg in the upper Allegoi region
long_description:
The "Tree Path" (Holzer Pfad) is a charming hiking route that includes 10 stations with various and experiential activities on the subject of trees and forests near the town of Borgberg in the upper Allegoy region. Along the way, various activities await the children, such as the simulation of sawing a log, the simulation of wooden axes, omega, a small ropes park with three tracks and more.
The itinerary is relatively easy but still includes one ascent with a reasonable gradient. Due to the nature of the trail, it is not fully accessible to strollers, but children can navigate it relatively easily. A great itinerary to combine with a visit to the nearby mine .

title: Through the vineyards of Hammelburg
short_description: A panoramic tour over the vineyards of Hammelburg awaits us.
long_description: From the market square we head east and then north via Ofenthaler Weg. The "Rhönwanderweg 1" accompanies our tour. In front of the hospital we turn left into Karl-Kaiser-Straße and right into Urbanweg. We climb the steps and walk uphill to a resting place under a paraplui (1). The path leads us over the Heroldsberg to Rheinhold-Schmidt-Platz. Here the path branches off, leading us downhill through wonderful mixed forest to a forest path. The "1" leads us to a steep edge. A bench near a sculpture of a woman (2) invites you to take a rest. At the edge of the field, we keep left and pass the hang-gliding field (3). Passing between vines (4), we now descend again to Hammelburg.

images.caption: The figure by an unknown artist from Hammelburg.
The town hall and the market fountain date back to the Renaissance.
A beautiful lookout bench at the side of the path.
The vines thrive excellently on the sunny, sloping walls.
The old wine town of Hammelburg.

title: Lahn Valley Cycle Route from Marburg to Lollar
short_description: On this short bike tour we cycle along the picturesque Lahn from historic Marburg to Lollar.
long_description: Marburg is quite charming, has a beautiful old town centre and the oldest Protestant university. Here we have a beautiful view from the mighty landgrave's castle into the Lahn valley. The cycle tour begins on the lakeside path, which leads along the Lahn valley cycle path the whole way. It is only a few kilometres to the first refreshment: At the Weimarer See recreational area, you can take a break and swim a lap. Then we pass through Niederweimar, a small village with a half-timbered mill. And if it gets a bit chilly, we can warm up in Lollar in the small Central Heating Museum and marvel at the exhibits. In the district of Odenhausen, it's worth climbing up to the heights of Altenburg: from there, the view stretches all the way to Marburg and Gießen.

images.caption: We follow the course of the Lahn on our bike tour.

title: Around Donaueschingen
short_description: The circular walk around Donaueschingen takes you through the beauty of the regional natural and cultural landscape.
long_description: Our tour starts at the railway station in Donaueschingen. We walk in a north-westerly direction, past the bus station and the P+R facility. Via Bahnhofstraße, our path leads to Schellenbergbrücke and over this bridge across the railway tracks. Here we come across the trail markings for the first time, which will accompany us for the next few kilometres: a white line on a blue background. We continue straight ahead, up a first ascent and out of Donaueschingen. We follow the white-blue markings, reach an agricultural path and a first vantage point with a view over the Sonnhalde. 500 m further on, we reach a signposted fork in the path and continue straight on towards Bräunlingen (white-blue marking). As soon as the Donaueschingen sanatorium becomes visible, we take the next fork to the left, walk across a meadow to the edge of the forest and finally reach the Schellenberg viewpoint and the Amalienhütte, which invites you to take a break. After the hut, first turn left and then immediately right downhill. Follow the white-blue markings until you reach the first houses of Bräunlingen. Shortly before the first house, turn right and walk downhill on a small path across a meadow. After 50 m you will again see a white-blue marker. Follow this three times to the right, enter the forest and orientate yourself according to the local sign "Urlaub in Bräunlingen" (holiday in Bräunlingen) in the direction of Bruggen. From then on, we stay on the wide forest path until it forks and leads us left downhill to Bruggen. At the next fork, we turn left again. From here we can already see the Breg. We cross the small river and go right to Bruggen. Before we reach the church, we turn left and after 50 m we meet the cycle path to Wolterdingen. Here we walk straight on (approx. 2 km) until we turn right onto the road to Wolterdingen. In the centre of the village, we again follow the white-blue markings straight ahead across the Breg. We pass the bridge and turn right along the main road onto the cross-country trail - Schwarzwald-Kaiserstuhl-Rhein (red rhombus on yellow background). After leaving the village of Wolterdingen, we hike through open terrain. Soon we leave the road (L180, Donaueschinger Straße) and go straight ahead on a path to the edge of the forest. At the fork, we follow the path to the left to the Eichbuckhütte. Continue left through the forest. Finally we come to a crossroads. Here we follow the path marked with a black fir tree on a blue circle straight ahead until a path branches off to the left (red rhombus on a yellow background). We walk along this path downhill, meet a wide path and continue straight ahead to Aufen. Pass the church on the right, then turn left again and follow the main road. After 200 m, leave the road and follow the signs to the left in the direction of Aufen railway station. Here we reach the Brigach. Cross the river and follow the signs to Donaueschingen on the right through a mixed deciduous forest. Soon we leave the forest on a footpath that leads across a meadow. After reaching the main road (Hindenburgring), we walk to the right along the signs to the railway station. Now we continue along the Brigach river. Finally, we leave the course of the Brigach and follow the signs to Donaueschingen main station. In Donaueschingen we can stop for a bite to eat at the end of the tour.

images.caption: The view from the Amalienhütte is impressive in good weather.

Gems can be found along our tour.

title: Isar Cycle Path to Freising
short_description: We cycle from the cosmopolitan city of Munich along the river to the cathedral city of Freising. The route is absolutely flat and leads through dense floodplain forest outside the cities.
long_description: From the Isartor in Munich, our bike tour leads along the Isar to Freising.

images.caption: Freising's picturesque old town around Marienplatz is worth a detour.
At the cable footbridge, the view falls on the neo-Gothic Mariannenkirche on the other bank.
As you drive towards Freising, you capture the whole backdrop of the monastery buildings on the Domberg.
The tour along the Isar is well-known and popular among cyclists.

title: Cultural hike to Româneşti Cave
short_description: An easy hike to the Romanești Cave in Timiș County, where every year, in October, a symphony concert takes place organised by the Speotimiș Association with the participation of the Banat Philharmonic Orchestra.
long_description: The hike starts in the village of Romanești, next to the cemetery (in the east of the village). Follow the sign "yellow cross", which leads you through a gentle hilly landscape. The hut can be reached after about 80 minutes.

images.caption: The Way to the Cave Romanești
The Way to the Cave Romanești

title: My Lawford to Dedham trail running circuit, River Stour and Dedham Vale AONB
short_description: A short circular run - or walk - in Constable Country that takes in a section of the River Stour and a corner of Dedham Vale to deliver some classic East Anglian vibes.
long_description:
Despite its proximity to some busy roads, the train track, and the creeping sprawl of Manningtree, this run takes in some very pretty and timeless countryside. Perfect for a few hours of exercise at the weekend and with the option of some nice stops along the way, the route can just as easily be walked. The only thing you should be mindful of is the possibility of mud and flooding in some sections along the river, especially in the winter. 
The route itself starts at St Mary's Church in Lawford and after a quick drop to Manningtree station, then leads along the Stour in the direction of Flatford. Once you hit Dedham, you will start the return leg across fields and lanes until you arrive back at the car park. 
Enjoy :D

images.caption: St Mary's at the start and end of the run
Reeds and rushes next to the Stour
Signage on the return leg from Dedham

title: Walk around the Lake of Pavin
short_description: One of the must-do hikes in the Puy de Dôme to discover Lake Pavin from all angles! This circuit is a variant of a more accessible itinerary which passes by the Puy de Montchal culminating at 1407 m of altitude.
long_description:
This 1.5 hour hike begins on a wide path with tall trees. After 600m, you start to gain height in a heavily wooded environment and on a path that is narrower than before.
You then continue on the most difficult part of the route, the ascent to the summit of Puy Montchal, the youngest volcano in France! In September and October, you may have the opportunity to meet some locals as it is a good time to pick mushrooms. Beech and spruce trees surround you all the way to the summit. From there, you will have a view of the Super Besse resort, magnificent! Enjoy the panorama before taking more or less wide paths again.
.
After 1.5 km, at the RIS sign "Parc des Volcans d'Auvergne", you will enjoy the plunging view on the turquoise waters of Lake Pavin. The hike ends quietly by joining the restoration point located at the edge of the lake.

images.caption: First steps on the edge of Lake Pavin
View of Super-Besse from the summit of Puy Montchal
randonnée - Puy-de-Dôme: Randonnée autour du Lac de Pavin

title: Belemedik - Kuschular
short_description: Those looking for a hiking route in Adana can try this route starting from Belemedik and ending in Kuşçular
long_description:
One of the only routes that can be done within the borders of Adana province is the Belemedik - Kuşçular route. 
This route follows the Belemedik - Hacıkırı line, which adds historical and cultural information to your hiking pleasure and is known by many hikers. You start from Belemedik and set off on a line running parallel to the Akıt Water. Before reaching Hacıkırı, the route leaves the Çakıt Suyu line and curves towards Kuşçular. When you reach Kuşçular, you have reached your destination point. You are accompanied by landscapes where you can explore the geography of the region.
The route can be challenging for someone who does not know the structure of the region. Therefore, you need to be careful.

title: Glauchau and surroundings
short_description: On this long hike we experience Glauchau, its reservoir and its surroundings.
long_description: We start our tour at the hiking board at Glauchau railway station, where we can get information about the route. From here we walk along the green markings into the upper town and on past the historic post office building and the market square. We now arrive at Glauchau's castle complex with the two castles Vorderglauchau and Hinterglauchau. Behind the two castles, we walk down the Mühlberg to the Gründelpark, past the Gründelteich pond and on until we cross Albertsthaler Straße and reach the Glauchau reservoir. We walk around the lake on its western side and through a small forest to the Wernsdorf sports field, from where we cross the village and continue towards Scheibenbusch. On our way we come to Rümpfwald and turn left at the "Thumer Kreuz" hut onto the Forsthausweg, which leads us to the Glauchau forester's lodge. We first continue to the right in the direction of St.Egidien, but after a few metres turn left onto the Elise-Schmid-Weg, which leads us to Niederlungwitz. We now walk along the edge of the forest until we reach the Erzgebirgsweg, where we first keep to the right. After a while we turn left to the animal enclosure in the Carolapark. We then continue to Lungwitzer Straße and up to Schlachthofstraße, which leads us back to the station on the right.

title: Near Gemünden am Main in the picturesque Sinntal valley
short_description: The easy hike leads through the idyllic river landscape of the Sinn and beautiful forests.
long_description: At the open-air swimming pool (1) we cross the Saale and walk straight ahead under the railway line to the health centre. Our tour is marked with the "Eichhorn". A forest path begins at the left end of the car park. First parallel to the Sinn, the path leads us to a crossroads after 2 km. We turn left, go under the ICE line and cross the old railway line. Cross the stone bridge (2) to reach Schaippach and turn left at the Landschulheim (3) towards the sports field. At the end of the sports field, the path turns into the forest. We turn left to the railway line, walk under it and reach the Anglersee (4). In front of it, a path leads to the salmon fishing pier (5). Walk right along the shore to the "Sauruh" (6). A trail runs across the meadow, which finally takes us along the river bank to the starting point.

images.caption: The view from the cycle path along the Sinntalauen.
We walk through the hilly landscape on comfortable paths.
The bridge saint on the historic sandstone bridge of Schaippach.
Our path runs past fruit trees and fields.
An old steam locomotive is the attraction at the tourist office.

title: Snowshoe: Wank from Garmisch-Partenkirchen
short_description: After the pistes were closed some time ago, the Wank is once again a touring mountain and is also suitable for late risers who are happy to have a place to stop for refreshments.
long_description:
The Wank is one of the most popular excursion mountains in Garmisch-Partenkirchen in summer. On its summit, we experience an outstanding panorama that lets us look at the entire Wetterstein Mountains on one side and far into the foothills of the Alps on the other.
Since the ski lift operation was discontinued, the Wank can once again be enjoyed as a proper touring peak. In addition, the Wankhaus and Esterbergalm huts, which are open all year round, offer the opportunity to leave your rucksack lighter and have a snack there.

images.caption: Daxkapelle on the ascent to Wank.
The Esterbergalm with chapel, in the background the Krottenkopf.

title: From Roggenbach to Schlüchtsee
short_description: The tour impresses with the ruins of Steinegg and Roggenbach, from where the trail leads along the Erlenbach valley to the idyllic Schlüchtsee lake and the "Hüsli".
long_description: At our starting point, we cross the road and meet the valley path between Roggenbacher Hof and the mini-golf course and hike up the valley along the Erlenbach stream towards Schlüchtsee. The Erlenbachweg (built in 1845), runs through the forest and leads slightly uphill past interesting rock formations. Via the Fohrenhölzle (1) we reach the Kreuzplatzhütte. The beautifully landscaped barbecue area with fountain and shelter invites you to take a short break. From here, the Wasserraintalweg leads us further uphill to the Schlüchtsee lake. At the next but one signpost, we follow the left fork and immediately change to a narrow forest path. After a short ascent through the forest, we continue our tour on a level forest path. This leads us to the right to the next junction. There we choose the left path and shortly afterwards we reach the campsite at Schlüchtsee (2) on our right. A few metres further on, the large car park directly at the lake with its beautifully laid-out barbecue area is a good place to take a break. From here we have a charming view of the village of Grafenhausen. The Schlüchtsee with its nature reserve is a real gem and invites you to swim on nice days with its sunbathing lawn and kiosk. To get to Rothaus, we follow the southern loop around the lake, walk the asphalt road down the valley for a short distance, past the sports field, and turn right at the next opportunity onto the Schlüchtseeweg. Back at the lake, we pass the Schlüchtseehof (3), a mare's milk farm. Following the road further, after a short walk we reach the district of Rothaus, three kilometres northwest of Grafenhausen. Here you will find a small local museum, the "Hüsli" (4). Anyone who has followed the series Schwarzwaldklinik on television knows it: Dr. Brinkmann, the television doctor, lived there. The "Hüsli" was destined for nobility from the very beginning. It was built in 1911 for the concert singer Helene Siegfried. She herself lovingly collected many treasures in this house: pretty furniture, beautiful stoves, reverse glass paintings and sign clocks. Today, the interior shows the rural living culture of the old Black Forest tradition. Past the museum, a path leads down to the lake. From here we follow the newly laid out nature trail with numerous panels and sculptures until a small, narrow forest path leads up into the forest to the left. Via this we reach a forest path that leads us directly back to the Schlüchtsee campsite. From here we hike back to the Roggenbacher Schlösser car park along the same route as on the way there. If we still feel like it, we can take a wonderful detour to the two ruins: We follow the route marked with a yellow rhombus via the Schlosshaldenweg along the Steina. At the next, larger signpost, our ascent begins on a narrow forest path up to the Roggenbach ruins. One of the two towers of the ruin can be climbed via an outside staircase. From there you have a beautiful all-round view over the surrounding woods and meadows. After enjoying the view, we walk back along the same path to follow the signpost to the Steinegg ruins (blue rhombus with a vertical white line). To do this, we hike a short distance on the Tunzauweg (middle path) to immediately turn left over an embankment up to a small forest path. This leads us through varied woodland to the tower of the Steinegg ruins, which we unfortunately cannot climb. We walk back along the path to our starting point.

title: Walk to the Breite Reserve near Sighisoara
short_description: An easy walk in the woods, part of a segment on the Via Transilvanica hiking route, leading to the Breite oak tree reserve. From some spots, beautiful panoramas open up toward the city and the surroundings.
long_description:
The hike starts on Ana Ipătescu Street, following a path between two houses. You'll see two official markings: one is made by the Transylvanian Highlands Association (red band) and another by NGO Via Transilvanica. The latter - part of the VT national network - comes from the city center.
From the starting point, follow the path that will quickly start to climb quite steeply. After a few hundred meters you reach a turning point from where you have a beautiful view over Sighisoara. The path then enters the forest. The rest of the climbing parts are easy and they will lead you to the plateau area where you'll see the old oak trees. Mind that the area has been invaded by the European hornbeam (Carpinus betulus) lately.
Explore the entire plateau at ease. The most picturesque oak has a swing attached. In rainy weather, the soil may be very muddy. Also, the path - especially the clearer parts of the forest - becomes slippery. Don't ignore the wild animals warning, especially after dusk.

title: Walking from station to station between Bois-le-Roi and Fontainebleau-Avon
short_description: Starting from the Bois-le-Roi station, this hike allows you to explore the northern part of the Fontainebleau forest, with the Fontainebleau-Avon station as the final destination.
long_description:
<From Bois-le-Roi station, you head towards the Fontainebleau forest along Chemin des Coureurs (GR1). For 6 km, will discover made of oak and pine trees as well characteristic rocks this place before arriving at Tour Denecourt.
It is here that you can climb to the top (you are 136m above sea level) and enjoy a 360° view of the forest. Magnificent ! The édifice was built by Claude-François Denecourt (who landscaped the forêt of Fontainebleau) in 1851, and then restored à several times.
While no river crosses the Fontainebleau forest, you will pass respectively:
La Fontaine du Touring Club de France, created in 1901;
La Fontaine Désirée, discovered in 1837 then improved by Denecute;nagacute;e in 1852;
La Fontaine Dorly, also created in 1852 by Denecourt;
The Isabelle Fountain, created by Denecourt in 1866 and restored by Colinet in 1893.
The details of these 4 fountains are however very variable.
Finally, take a break at the Roche Eponge, a curiosity in the Fontainebleau forest, which owes its name to an aspect resulting from the erosion.

images.caption: View from the Denecourt Tower over the Fontainebleau forest

title: Hermannstein and Jewish Church
short_description: This circular trail leads along mostly lonely paths, trails and roads through the picturesque landscape between Fischen Tiefenbach and Langenwang.
long_description: From Fischen we walk past the open-air swimming pool through the meadows. We climb up to the Hermannstein. Via Jägersberg and Kreben we reach Tiefenbach. A path takes us up to the Judenkirche. Back in Jägersberg we follow the road down to Langenwang. Through the meadows we return to Fischen.

images.caption: View over Fischen to the Grünten

title: Mindelheim via ferrata above the Kleinwalsertal valley
short_description: The moderately difficult to difficult Mindelheim via ferrata offers us interesting climbing passages alternating with quieter stretches and impressive views of the Allgäu ridge.
long_description: The Mindelheimer via ferrata, built as early as 1975, connects the Fiderepasshütte with the Mindelheimer Hütte (both managed) and can be climbed in both directions. You cross the three Schafalpenköpfle and the smaller Kemptner Köpfle, mostly on the ridge. The highlight and landmark of the moderately difficult to difficult climb is an iron ladder that serves as a bridge, on which you cross a 3-4 m wide saddle. The constant alternation of interesting climbing passages and quieter stretches as well as the impressive views of the Allgäu ridge make the entire trail an alpine pleasure.

images.caption: View of the Kleinwalsertal valley with Hohem Ifen and Gottesacker plateau.
View towards the north with the course of the ridge.

title: Coastal walk from San Lawrenz to Marsalforn
short_description: Fourth and final stage of the varied coastal circular walk on Gozo – Malta's neighbouring island.
long_description: The last stage of our circular walk on Gozo takes us steadily downhill from San Lawrenz to Marsalforn. On the way we discover the north coast of the island, which has a lot to offer. We walk past the Wied il Ghasri gorge. It is particularly remote and invites you to linger because of its tranquillity and beauty. The gorge is particularly popular with divers, as it is home to many different species of animals. Another place of interest on the route are the salt pans of Xwejni Bay. Salt has been mined here for hundreds of years, mainly to be sold on the island of Gozo. The salt pans, arranged like a chessboard, stretch for several kilometres along the coast.

short_description: This tour leads to the 814-metre-high Mweelrea, the highest mountain in the western Irish province of Connacht.

title: Following the Water - Skiathos Trail ST9
short_description: Wild creeks, pristine beaches, remote monasteries, and mysterious ruins in the forest - one of the most varied hikes on the island.
long_description:
On this moderately difficult, well-marked hike we cross the island from south to north and experience the whole diversity of the landscape: from the densely populated south coast along wild creeks and past the ruins of old water and oil mills to two lonely, paradisiacal beaches on the north coast and past the monastery Kechria over hilly country with many views back to the starting point. Especially in the off-season an equally solitary and rewarding undertaking.
This is Trail 9 of the official Skiathos Trail Network.

images.caption: View from a high plateau on Skiathos island
Cyclamen blooming by the trail near Kechria Monastery.

title: Hiking to Marjash - in company with 89 years old man
short_description: On windy October day we went with offroad cars to Stanet e Prilepit village to start the hike from there. In our company was Joussuf an 89 year's old man who could run up the mountain and back. Beside that ambitious positive man the way up the peak is incredible.
long_description: Marijash or Bogdaš Albanian: Bogdash is a mountain in Kosovo in the Prokletije range. At 2,533 m high, it is the highest peak of the Bogićevica area and one of the highest peaks in Prokletije in Kosovo. We started from village called Stanet e Prilepit which can be reach by motorized transportation of the off-road type.

title: To the Inca Fortress of Quitoloma
short_description: Explore the ruins of Quitoloma, likely the Inca's most important fortress in the conquest of northern Ecuador, on this easy panoramic hike.
long_description: This unassuming hilltop next to the mightier Pambamarca volcano harbors an ancient secret: Thze ruins of a large pukara, a hilltop fortress built by the Incas in their conquest of northern Ecuador in the 15th century. As the name "Quitoloma" - "Hill of Quito" - already suggests, this fortress was most likely one of the largest and most strategic forts in the northern Sierra during the Inca Empire. Around a terraced platform called "ushnu", used for religious ceremonies, more than 100 buildings serving as living quarters, storehouses, and administrative buildings formed a fortified city on 3,780 m. Quitoloma is part of a complex of 14 pukaras scattered across Pambamarca volcanoe, most of them built on top of previous fortresses errected by the Cayambe culture. During their conquest of northern Ecuador, it took the Incas 17 years before the Cayambe people surrendered. And it was only after Pambamarca fell, that the Incas were able to finally take control over the wider region.

title: Bear Lake nature trail, Sovata
short_description: The Bear Lake (Ursu) eco-didactic trail in Sovata adds to the educational route of the Salt nature trail and takes you over the main salt lakes in the resort and to a few viewpoints. It's a great opportunity to get moving, and admire the nature and richness of the place.
long_description:
The route is easy to follow, takes little effort, and can be done even by children, even if it has a few short climbing sections.
Along the way, there are rest areas, viewpoints (at Salt Mountain and above Lake Paraschiva), as well as information panels, a toilet, and even a wi-fi point.
The distance of the route is short, but the walking time can vary between an hour and even half a day, if you make frequent stops or if you choose to combine this trail with the alt trail or even with a climb to Tivoli (at the end).

title: From Levanto to Monterosso (Cinque Terre)
short_description: The coastal hike from Levanto to Monterosso, the northernmost of the Cinque Terre villages, is a wonderful walk away from the busy villages. The path is mostly in pleasant shade and the deep views to the sea are impressive.
long_description:
This wonderful coastal hike takes us from Levanto to the northernmost village of the Cinque Terre - Monterosso. The path always leads along the often steep coastline and you can enjoy wonderful views of the sea. Liguria is known as Italy's vegetable garden and a visit to the market in Levanto is definitely worthwhile. Here we can also stock up on fresh fruit and vegetables for a snack. The path described is not yet part of the National Park area and can therefore be walked free of charge. However, if you want, you can easily extend it and visit all the Cinque Terre towns afterwards (but then you have to pay, as it is a National Park area).
Each section can be covered comfortably and cheaply by train, which stops in each of the villages. The described route leads along partly stony paths high above the sea, past lonely farmhouses, olive and fig trees, cacti and typically Mediterranean vegetation. It is highly recommended to take enough drinks with you. There are plenty of places to eat and drink in both Levanto and Monterosso.

images.caption: Levanto lies to the north of the Cinque Terre and is the starting point for many hikes.

title: Pambamarca - Legendary Mountain of Inca Fortresses
short_description: Panoramic hike through beatuiful Páramo to the top of Pambamarca, the legendary mountain of Cayambe and Inca fortresses. Ancient history, incredible views, and Andean hospitality.
long_description:
When Inca emperor Topa Inca Yupanqui began the conquest of Ecuador in the late 1460s, his army was met with fierce resistance by the Cañari and Cayambe cultures of the northern sierra. The stronghold of the Cayambe was Pambamarca, a 4,062 m high stratovolcano, scattered with fortresses. Even after conquering Quito, iYupanqui and his son Huayna Capac had to lay siege on this mythical mountain for 17 long years before they were able to defeat the Cayambes. As a result, Pambamarca became a strategic control post for the entire northern Inca empire and the Incas errected no less than 14 hilltop fortresses ("pukaras") of their own on the volcano - most notably, Quitoloma.
Today, Pambamarca makes for a fantastic hiking destination that lets visitors explore both the ancient history and the contemporary culture of the high Andes. The hike to the summit is not very difficult, but strong winds and the high altitude should not be underestimated.

title: Hansjakobweg
short_description: This eventful circular walk through the beautiful Black Forest takes us on the trail of the folk poet Heinrich Hansjakob. In five day-long stages we cross many a valley, hike along bubbling brooks and see several castles, old farmhouses and historic towns.
long_description:
Stage 1: Haslach - Wolfach (16.5 km)
We start on the forecourt of Haslach's Capuchin monastery, i.e. in the middle of Hansjakob's birthplace. Passing the Freihof, the poet's retirement home, we leave his hometown and set off on several idyllic valley crossings. Along the way, we also experience the Gutach and Wolfach valleys as well as several castle ruins.
Stage 2: Wolfach - Brandenkopf   (14 km)
Just behind Wolfach, a mountain with beautiful views of the surrounding area awaits us. We will steadily gain altitude throughout the entire stage and finally reach the Brandenkopf, the highest point of the Hansjakob Trail (945 m above sea level).
Stage 3: Brandenkopf - Zell am Harmersbach (21 km)
From the tower on the Brandenkopf we have a magnificent view üover the Black Forest. We hike down to Oberharmersbach and then in the beautiful Harmersbach valley. Back in the dense forest, the trail goes uphill every now and then to Zell am Harmersbach.
Stage 4: Zell am Harmersbach - Höhenhäuser (29 km)
Today we have the longest stage of the Hansjakob Trail ahead of us at 29 km. Past the pilgrimage church of Maria zu den Ketten, we pass only a few small footpaths and do not reach a larger town until we reach Steinach. After leaving this behind us, we are once again completely surrounded by nature and hike through the forest to Höhenhäuser.  
Stage 5: Höhenhäuser - Haslach (20 km)
On the last day's hike we hike leisurely and without any major ascents through the central Black Forest. We cross beautiful valleys on forest and field paths, the village of Oberbiederbach and a high plateau and reach the Biereck, which is often found in Hansjakob's texts. Past the ruins of the Heidburg, we continue via Flachenberg to Mühlenbach. Now we hike relaxed up the Gährenberg and then down to Haslach, where we had started our circular walk.

images.caption: The heated outdoor pool offers fun for young and old alike
The local history museum in Steinach provides information on the history and customs of the village.

title: Coastal walk from Marsalforn to Mgarr
short_description: First stage of the varied coastal circular walk on Gozo – Malta's neighbouring island
long_description: On the first leg of our four-day tour on Gozo, we can expect some highlights right at the beginning. In Dahlet Qorrot Bay we will discover the small huts cut into the rock, which the local fishermen use as shelters for their colourful boats in case of a storm. We will also be able to enjoy the beautiful view of the neighbouring islands of Comino and Malta at the most elevated point of the island. Another bay we pass is Ramla Bay. It is no less inviting than Dahlet Qorrot Bay.

images.caption: Bootshütten in der Bucht Dahlet Qorrot

title: Windheim Nature Trail
short_description: A nature trail over 3 km long through the Franconian Forest Nature Park.
long_description: The nature trail provides information about interesting things along the way. It can be reached from the Ölschnitzsee via the district road KC18. There it begins with an overview map and leads over 3 km with 25 information boards (pictures and text) always on the same path to Kehlbacher Straße. There it turns right and follows the forest road to the Rennsteig. On the Rennsteig, the nature trail turns right to the road to Windheim. This road takes you back to the starting point.

images.caption: The Windheim Natrulehrpfad leads us through dense forest.

title: Crossing the Seven Falls - Section 2
short_description: Second leg of the Seven Falls Walk through the Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park, where we find beautiful waterfalls in the middle of the Brazilian savannah.
long_description:
Trekking located in the National Park of Chapada dos Veadeiros, where the goal é reach à Sete Quedas waterfall, waterfalls of small size, but with good extension of width. There are several natural pools, which provide unforgettable moments of diving, contemplation and relaxation.
The second section of the Travessia das 7 Quedas can be done in less than a day, starting from the áarea of camping which is 150 meters from the falls and ends on the GO-239 Highway, where it is recommended to hire someone to pick you up in advance.Opened in 2013, the Travessia das 7 Quedas is perfect for lovers of hiking amidst nature, as well as being a true invitation to immerse yourself in the Cerrado and a chance to see what is most beautiful in this biome.

title: Iseler - Kühgundkopf - Kühgundspitz
short_description: On this beautiful alpine hike we pass three imposing peaks - the Iseler, the Kühgundkopf and the Kühgundspitz.
long_description: We can safely spare ourselves the ascent to the Iseler and take the Iselerbahn up, because three more summit ascents and a few metres of altitude await us in the course of the hike. On the ridge we hike along the German-Austrian border from the Iseler over the Kügundkopf and the Kühgundspitz - three peaks with a magnificent mountain panorama. Via Wiedhagalpe and Gundalpe we finally descend almost 800 metres in altitude to Oberjoch. Attention: This is an alpine tour that requires a head for heights and surefootedness. The Kühgund crossing should not be undertaken in wet conditions.

images.caption: Hike in the Allgäu: Iseler - Kühgundkopf - Kühgundspitz
Blick vom Iseler Gipfel über die Zipfelsalpe

title: From Obermaiselstein to the Riedberger Horn
short_description: The Riedberger Horn (1787 m) is also easy to climb from the east side. The ascent is through the Bolgental valley. From the summit you have a fantastic panorama.
long_description: The ascent to the Riedberger Horn on this snowshoe tour is from the east from the Bolgental. The ascent and descent route runs mainly on east and north-east facing slopes with a moderate to steep incline. For the most part, orientation is easy. The German Alpine Association has already marked this ascent option to the Riedberger Horn as part of its "Ski mountaineering environmentally friendly" initiative. Please follow the signs of the Alpine Club.

title: The Baïse valley by bike (V82)
short_description: Cycle the canalised course of the Baïse, from the Canal des 2 Mers to the foothills of the Pyrenees, over a distance of 170km, from Buzet-sur-Baïse to Lannemezan.
long_description:
Dive into the heart of the gentle hills of Gascony, exploring the history of France with Henri IV and following in the footsteps of the Musketeers.
Once a major trade route for the transport of flour, ore, coal and the famous Armagnac, the Baïse Valley by bike invites you to discover an area of exceptional scenery and picturesque charm.
Gems such as Buzet-sur-Baïse, Vianne, Barbaste, Nérac, Moncrabeau, Condom, Valence-sur-Baïse, Castéra-Verduzan, Auch, l'Isle-Noé, Mirande, Trie-sur-Baïse and Galan will provide you with ineffable experiences.
Crossing part of the Lot-et-Garonne, most of the Gers and ending in the Hautes-Pyrénées, this cycle route requires excellent physical condition due to its rugged terrain, making it suitable for experienced cyclists. The panoramic views of the snow-covered Pyrenean peaks, particularly after Trie-sur-Baïse, are well worth the effort.

title: Tali Taal Lake Trek in Auli
short_description: This Himalayan hike leads to the beautiful serene lake "Tali Taal" in the Auli town of Garhwal Himalayas in Uttarakhand India.
long_description:
Tali Tal trek takes you to a picturesque lake situated in the beautiful "Gorsan Bugyal" alpine pasture in the Chamoli district of Uttranchal state of India. "Bugyal" is a Pahari language term for high-altitude Himalayan grassland. Tali Tal trek is a part of "Kuari Pass" which is a much longer and difficult multiday hike suitable for experienced hikers. But this smaller segment until the lake is also an enjoyable and serene trek in its own right. It is very suitable for hikers of all ages and experience levels.
The trek starts from the town of Auli and follows a gradually climbing uphill trail that passes through a small stretch of pine and cedar forest before entering the green velvety Gorsan Bugyal and then finally arriving at the lake.
Tali Lake offers an open view of the Garhwal Himalayan ranges and the Kuari Pass. This lake location is also suitable for a campsite and hence this is a popular hiking tour for newbies. Amateur hikers and new trekkers generally spend a night here and return back to Auli the next day. If you are an experienced hiker then you can further continue the hike to the Kuari Pass and Pangarchulla peak. 
Covered with beautiful flowers in summer and sheets of snow in winter, this trek is a must-do when you are holidaying in Garhwal.

The path can be walked all year round and is also suitable for prams. It is marked with a yellow church symbol on a white background.

long_description: Run on the paths of local shepherds and on old mule tracks overlooking the cliffs and discover one of the very few wilderness left in Europe.

title: From Beerheide through the forest park
short_description: This hike takes us from Beerheide through the forest park. Particularly noteworthy are the "Hochmoor Grünheide" and the Röthelstein rock, from which we can enjoy a beautiful view.
long_description: Our hike begins at the Kulturhaus in Beerheide. From Rempesgrüner Straße, we turn right into the settlement and immediately turn right again at the first junction. Through fields we reach Klingenthaler Straße, which we follow briefly to the left, passing the Altes Kaffeehaus restaurant. We then turn right onto the Frankenweg, which takes us past the Frankenhaus into the forest park. After a while we meet the district road, walk a short distance to the right and then continue straight ahead where the road bends to the left. We walk through the wonderfully dense forest park until we reach the Rautenkranzer Straße, which we follow briefly to the right and take the next turn-off also to the right. We leave the Grünheide forest or holiday park on our left. The 15-hectare area of a former pioneer camp is now home to the Grünheide holiday park with many overnight accommodation facilities. After a few minutes, we reach the "Hochmoor Grünheide" landscape conservation area through the forest. We come to a fork in the path. Here we take the path to the right, cross a junction and turn right again at the next fork. In front of us, fields appear on the left in the middle of the forest, along which we walk and pass the state road behind it. Then we continue straight ahead through the forest. We ignore three crossroads before we leave the path to the right. We walk through a forest area called Großer Riss. Down the valley we head towards Röthelstein. This rock soon rises to our right and over a bridge at its foot we reach the ascent by which we can climb the 35 m high viewing platform of the Röthelstein. After an extensive view of the surroundings, we walk back to Beerheide, where we take the Röthelsteinweg and the Birkenweg to the Obere Straße and finally to our starting point, the Kulturhaus.

title: The trail of the huts
short_description: A lovely hike for an immersion in the past to meet the way of life of the shepherds of yesteryear and their stone huts, the ORRIS.
long_description:
<Because of the altitude, environment this circuit is different from that lower Fenouill.<Here there are no vines, but meadows where cows graze. This explains the presence of numerous stone huts, or orris, which line this route. These temporary shelters were used by shepherds to protect themselves from bad weather and to store some tools.
This route was realised with the support of the European cross-border cooperation programme POCTEFA
.

title: Spessartweg 1: Of princes, carters and pilgrims
short_description: The Spessart Trail is divided into Spessart Trail 1 and Spessart Trail 2. The Spessart Trail 1 described here takes us from Aschaffenburg to Gmünden, past many wonderful cultural and scenic sights.

title: Fairy Falls (Fairy Falls) via the Grand Prismatic Spring lookout
short_description: A short-to-medium hiking trail leading to the impressive Fairy Falls via the stunning viewpoint of the Grand Prismatic Thermal Spring in the west of the Yellowstone Nature Reserve
long_description:
A beautiful and interesting hiking trail all the way leading to Fairy Falls with a short detour (including a short ascent) but definitely worth it through a unique view point on the impressive Grand Prismatic Spring, considered the largest of its kind in the United States! In fact, this is the best and most accessible view point on this huge and colorful spring, so it is very worthwhile to do this section (on the route that passes by the lake, you cannot see all its beauty). Its colors as well as the smoke that rises from it create a surrealistic and fictional spectacle! You can pass by the view point on the way out or on the way back from the falls or both on the way out and on the way back.
Fairy Falls, which is the destination of this route , is considered one of the most impressive waterfalls among the Yellowstone Falls, their height reaches about 60 meters. Already at the beginning of the route near the parking lot you will see two impressive colorful hot thermal pools. If you don't want to go through the lookout, you can skip the route directly to the falls.
In principle, it is possible to walk part of the route with strollers, but it is not particularly adapted for this, the visit to the observation deck involves a short ascent with a relatively negligible gradient.
Since this is a one-way route, the estimated walking times as well as the distance shown on this page are for one direction only.

title: From Diepolz to the Hauchenberg
short_description: We enjoy a beautiful hike across partly untouched meadows. A magnificent panoramic view awaits us on the Hauchenberg from the Alps to far into the Alpine foothills.
long_description: The Hauchenberg mountain stretches from Missen-Wilhams in the west into the area of Immenstadt, on the municipal border with Waltenhofen, to Freundpolz. In autumn 2007, a wooden lookout point (Alpkönigblick) was built on the ridge at an altitude of 1237 m, not far from Klings Hütte. From there you can enjoy a fantastic panoramic view, from the Zugspitze, over the Allgäu Alps to the Säntis and from the western Allgäu over the Kugel, the Isny basin, the Adelegg, the Weitnau valley with Sonneck, Blender and the Illertal.

images.caption: View from the observation tower towards the Allgäu Alps

title: Circular walk in Karka Park
short_description: An experiential trip in the Kraka National Park in Croatia starting with an experiential cruise departing from the village of Skradin. An experience that includes transparent water with a mesmerizing turquoise hue, views, viewpoints, bathing in the water of the reserve and other surprises.
long_description: A relatively easy circular tour in the Karka Waterfalls Reserve, which is rich in water and unique views, the tour includes, as mentioned, a cruise to the park and a magical walk next to water and waterfalls. After the end of the walk on the route you can bathe in the central pool of the park. A respectable part of the route is on wooden bridges passing through the center of the park's ponds, with the largest bridge crossing the central pond and connecting the walkers on the route to the beginning of the circular route.

title: The Innsbruck via ferrata in the Karwendel mountains
short_description: The Innsbruck via ferrata is a wonderful ridge climb high above Innsbruck. The views of the Inn Valley and the Stubai peaks on one side and the Karwendel on the other are wonderful.
long_description:
The Innsbruck via ferrata (since 2003 officially named "Panorama Klettersteig Hannes Gasser") leads over a total of seven peaks always following the ridge of the Innsbruck Nordkette. The Nordkette cable car ensures a quick and comfortable ascent, and at the Seegrube station there is a restaurant with a sun terrace from which you can enjoy a magnificent panorama. The views of the Inntal valley with Innsbruck, the Stubai Alps and the Karwendel mountains along the entire trail are really something to behold. The protection of the trail is excellent, more than 2 km of steel rope and numerous step bars and pins guarantee a firm hold. The partly exposed route is exposed in all directions, but mainly on the east side. As the route is mainly on the ridge, stable weather conditions are an urgent prerequisite for an ascent.
The first part leads from the mountain station to Kemacher (2480 m) and on to Langer Sattel (2258). Here you can break off the ascent and descend or continue - now much more difficult - to the Frau Hitt saddle. The via ferrata is usually climbed from east to west, but the reverse is also possible. The difficult entry point (C) at the beginning of the first part can be bypassed in an easier variant (A) on the right. The second part after the "Frau Hitt" begins with the key section of the entire climb in an overhanging wall section (C/D).

title: Via the Randkluft via ferrata (normal route) on the Dachstein
short_description: The normal route up the Hohe Dachstein is also known as the "Randkluftsteig". It is considered the oldest via ferrata in the world. The view from the summit of the High Dachstein is magnificent.
long_description: The normal route up the Hoher Dachstein (2995 m), also called Randkluftsteig, is considered the oldest via ferrata in the world. This route was already established during the first half of the 19th century. It is relatively easy to reach with the help of the cable car, but you should by no means underestimate this climb. The ascent leads across glaciated terrain, where you should watch out for crevasses. Especially in poor visibility, orientation on the Schladminger and Hallstätter glaciers can quickly become a challenge. The route is exposed on the northeast side. The route can be icy in places during the low season, so it may be necessary to bring crampons and an ice axe. Climbing the Randkluft can also be a challenge in bad conditions.

title: The Amalfitana
short_description: Sorrent‘s steep coast offers spectacular views over the Mediterranean and the coast trip until Salerno.
long_description:
This coast street nestles on the cliff coast of Sorrent in Campania, stretching from the small town of Piano di Sorrento for about 50 km to the commune of Vietri sul Mare, just a few kilometers from the coastal city of Salerno.
Amalfitana is bordered by picturesque vineyards, with the delicate scent of lemon in the air. This is where you can also find several sight spots such as the Bay of Sorrent, the coastal villages of Positano and Ravello as well as the stunning Grotta dello Smeraldo.
But beware: You should only go on this tour if you are an experienced driver. There are several hairpin bends and narrow serpentine roads, so you might need to give way to oncoming traffic. You shouldn’t be afraid of heights either. The ledges might be impressive and nice to look at, but you might feel giddy when passing them by.

title: Over hill and dale around Hammelburg
short_description: A hike with magnificent views, through picturesque river valleys and romantic villages awaits us.
long_description: Our hike begins at Hammelburg's market square. The old Franconian wine town was first mentioned in a document in 716. The beautiful town hall and the Renaissance-style market fountain date back to the 16th century. If you are interested in the history of Hammelburg, you should buy the "Little Guide" at the tourist information on the market square. We walk along Bahnhofstraße, pass the Bürgerspitalkirche and reach a roundabout. The first turn-off leads us to the right into Seeshofer Straße, which passes under the railway tracks and merges into Kobelstraße. The marking "Rhönclub hiking trail no. 3" accompanies us. At the end of the street, we turn left into Pfaffstraße and immediately right again into Weberstraße. Follow the second road on the left, Faulstiegstraße, for about 1.5 km. The path leads gently uphill in a right-hand bend. We walk along the edge of the forest with a view of the Ganstal (1) below the Buchberg. At a hill we come to a fork in the path, which we follow to the left. From here, a gravel path leads through sparse pine forest until you reach another clearing. Our view opens up here over the vineyards to Saaleck Castle and the valley of the Franconian Saale. Saaleck Castle" was built in the 12th century to protect Hammelburg. The shady path leads us in a loop back southwards and soon becomes a narrow forest path leading down towards the Thulba valley. We can take a break at a rest area (2) with a beautiful view. Our route continues steeply downhill through flowering meadows and comes across a cross path, which we follow to the right. Straight ahead, this path takes us leisurely downhill to Herbertsmühle in Untererthal. If you want to take a break in the village at the historic inn "Zum Goldenen Kreuz" (3), turn left at the mill, cross the river Thulba and follow the view of the church tower. Back at the bridge, follow the signpost "1.4 kilometres to Obererthal". Like the Thulba, the asphalt footpath and cycle path meanders past willows and alders to Obererthal. We meet the Kapellenweg, which leads to the left into the village, follow the Obererthal road to the right and reach the Gasthof "Zum Stern" with its own schnapps distillery. Hiking along the Kapellenweg to the right, we reach a crossroads. Walk straight ahead up the steep forest path. At the next crossroads, turn right. At the next two forks, we keep left and then follow the path sharply to the left until we reach the highest point and a chapel (4). Continue straight downhill on the wide gravel path until you reach a valley again, where you turn left onto the road. In front of us we see the houses of Seeshof. In the village you can admire a well house with a fire bell (5). Walk through the romantic village uphill to the right. At the edge of the forest, a field path begins on the right. With a wonderful view over the valley, to the Erthaler Berg and Buchberg, the path leads us back towards Hammelburg. First, the path slowly descends to the Rechbach stream. We enjoy a rest under an old lime tree (6) with a seating area. On the left bank of the stream and parallel to the road, we walk across the fields and reach Hammelburg. We follow the road "An der Leite" straight downhill. Then we walk under the railway tracks again and reach the roundabout. Here we find the Herrenmühle town museum, which vividly conveys the history of the region. The building with the baroque façade informs about the 1200-year history of wine in Hammelburg and bread making. We turn left into Bahnhofstraße and reach the market square again with its cafés and restaurants.

title: From the Predigtstuhl near St. Englmar to the Hirschenstein
short_description: The Hirschenstein is one of the most interesting lookout mountains in the Bavarian Forest. On clear days, the view can even reach as far as the Zugspitze.
long_description: We start at the car park in the direction of Markbuchen, until after about 100 m we turn right uphill along Hirschensteinweg. At the signpost "Rundweg Predigtstuhl" we go left on the path at the edge of the forest to the last house. There we keep to the right and walk on the slightly ascending path to the valley station of the chairlift. There we leave the path and climb up the mountain via the western ski slope to the Predigtstuhl. With good visibility, we enjoy a wider and wider view with every metre of the ascent. Between the two chair lifts there is a strip of trees, to the right of this stand of trees our path leads up to the summit cross of the Predigtstuhl. From now on, we follow the signs "Hirschenstein" and a green arrow. At a refuge, we meet a wide path that takes us straight ahead on the high plateau of the Predigtstuhl without strong ups and downs for several kilometres to Oedwies. A clearing stretches around the abandoned Oedwies forester's lodge. The Bavarian Ministry of Forestry operates a forest climate station here, which regularly takes extensive measurements of climate values and also records, among other things, the input of pollutants and nutrients. It is one of 22 state measuring stations whose data are intended to contribute to a better understanding of the forest ecosystem. Oedwies is said to have been cleared for the first time as early as 1559, as attested by an old Viechtach document. However, the wasteland was mainly used as grassland. The rural estate was replaced in the mid-19th century by a state forestry house, which also ran a small inn for the forestry workers. The living quarters of the forester's family were only on the upper floor because of the often high snow cover. We continue to follow the signposting "Hirschenstein". Our path leads slightly uphill to Hirschenstein, 1 km away. Here we can take a rest at the tables and benches. Of course, we pay attention to the small lookout tower. On a clear day, it allows us a wide view of the Bavarian Forest landscape. The view stretches from the Großer Arber to the Dreisessel in the east, the region from Deggendorf to Straubing in the south and as far as the Gallner in the west. On a few days a year, the view is said to reach as far as the Alps - even the Zugspitze can be made out then. The lookout tower was built in 1921 by the Bavarian Forest Section Munich and renovated in 1995. We descend on the south side of the Hirschenstein on a path towards Schuhfleck. At this hiking trail junction, eight trails from all directions meet. Here we follow the signs "Rettenbach". After a while, we pay attention to the marking "8", which accompanies us to Loderwinkl. There the path becomes an asphalted road and we continue downhill to Rettenbach. We cross the resort until we reach the town exit sign and here we turn right into the Hans-Sachs-Weg, slightly ascending towards the forest. From this road there are beautiful views northwards into the valley of the Englmarbach and of Sankt Englmar. We follow the signs "5" through the forest to Glashütt. Here we pay attention to the turnaround loop of the bus stop at the Schullandheim and walk uphill on the right along the access road. After about 300 m we meet the "Waldcafé" and continue uphill along the slope until we meet new signposts. We orient ourselves in the direction of "Markbuchen" for the last few metres and walk above Sankt Englmar along wide hiking trails to an information board on an asphalt path. Downhill we reach our starting point.

title: नैना पीक ट्रैक
short_description: 2615 मीटर ऊँची नैना पीक नैनीताल शहर की सबसे ऊंची चोटी और एक प्रसिद्ध पर्यटन स्थल है। गर्मियों में हरियाली और जाड़ों में बर्फ से ढका इसका ट्रेल मार्ग नैनीताल शहर, झील और हिमालय का विहंगम दृश्य दिखाता है।
long_description:
अपनी दर्शनीय ट्रेल और ऊंचाई के कारण नैना पीक, पर्यटकों और हाइकर्स दोनों को समान रूप से पसंद आती है। वृद्ध और कमजोर लोग हैंडलर के साथ किराये पर मिलने वाले टट्टू या घोड़े पर भी यहां पहुंच सकते हैं।
ट्रैक को आपके आरंभ बिंदु के हिसाब से 1 से 3 घंटे के भीतर पूरा किया जा सकता है। तल्लीताल बस स्टेशन से यह ट्रैक लगभग 8 किलोमीटर लम्बा है। यह से आने पर मॉल रोड और नैनीताल शहर से होकर गुजरना पड़ता है। वैकल्पिक रूप से ट्रैक को मल्लीताल रिक्शा स्टेशन या 5 स्टार होटल "द मनु महारानी" से भी शुरू किया जा सकता है जहाँ से ट्रैक की कुल दूरी क्रमशः 5 और 4 किमी है।
किलबरी रोड पर स्थित ट्रेल के प्रवेश बिंदु पर सरकारी साइन पोस्ट लगा है जो ट्रेल के आरंभ होने का संकेत देता है। नैना पीक ट्रैक मध्यम चढ़ाई वाला और ठंडा मार्ग है। यह ट्रेल घने देवदार, बाँझ, चीड़ और बुरांश के जंगलो से गुजरती है। ट्रेल में कुछ ख़ास बिंदुओं से नैनी झील और नैनीताल शहर का एक विहंगम दृश्य मिलता है। नैना पर्वत चोटी जो इस ट्रैक के आखिरी गंतव्य है, बर्फ से लदे हिमालय का भव्य दृश्य प्रदान करती है।

title: Müstair - Piz Chavalatsch
short_description: The border between Switzerland and Italy runs along Piz Chavalatsch, which is also the easternmost point in Switzerland.
long_description: In addition, the summit offers magnificent views of Ortler, Vinschgau, the mountains around Stilfser Joch and Münstertal. Next to the summit cross, on the summit there is an old Italian Zöllner hut and radio antenna. The most important waypoints on the route: Val Pisch car park - Val Torta - Val Plazzöl - Plaun Radond - La Scharta - Piz Chavalatsch - P. 2582 on the NE ridge - Rifairscharte - Rifairalm - Val Plazzöl - Val Pisch car park.

title: Biesbosch walking route
short_description: During this route you can enjoy the beautiful nature in the Biesbosch. You will walk past a watchtower and a museum.
long_description: De Biesbosch is one of the largest freshwater tidal areas in Europe. The national park is connected to the sea and therefore there is a tidal difference of 70-80 centimetres. Because of the tidal difference, special plants live in the Biesbosch, for example the Spindotter. The beaver is a common animal in the Biesbosch, probably not seen very often, because they are mainly active at dusk.

title: पंतवाड़ी- नाग टिब्बा ट्रैक
short_description: समुद्र तल से 9915 फीट की ऊंचाई पर स्थित 'नाग टिब्बा' गढ़वाल हिमालय की सबसे ऊँची चोटियों में से एक ह ै और इसका ट्रैकिंग मार्ग उत्तरांचल के सबसे प्रसिद्ध ट्र ैकिंग मार्गों में से एक है।
long_description: नागटिब्बा दो शब्दों 'नाग' (साँप) और 'टिब्बा' (पहाड़) से मिलकर बना है और इसका मतलब होता है साँप की पहाड़ी। उत्तराखंड के देहरादून ज़िले में घने जंगलों से घिरी और प्राकृतिक सौन्दर्य से भरपूर नाग टिब्बा की पहाड़िया, ट्रैकिंग और एडवेंचर पसंद करने वालों को बेहतरीन अवसर प्रदान करती हैं। नाग टिब्बा से सभी मुख्य हिमालय पर्वत मालाओं जैसे की स्वर्गारोहिणी, बंदरपूंछ, कालानाग, और गंगोत्री का 100 डिग्री का नजारा दिखाई देता है। इसके अलावा केदारनाथ की चोटी, दून घाटी और चांगबांग की बर्फीली चोटियां भी दिखाई देती हैं। यहाँ एक छोटा सा मंदिर भी है | सर्दियों में यहाँ की पहाड़ियां बर्फ से घिरी रहती हैं तथा गर्मियों में यहाँ का मौसम बहुत सुखद रहता है। नागटिब्बा का ट्रैकिंग मार्ग देहरादून ज़िले में मसूरी शहर के करीब पंतवारी नाम से एक छोटे से गाँव से शुरू होता है। पंतवारी तक कार या बस से आना संभव है। पंतवारी-नागटिब्बा ट्रैक जंगलों और घास के मैदानों के बीच से होते हुए जाता है। रास्ते में सुंदर पेड़ पौंधे, चिड़ियाँ, हरे भरे पहाड़, और घने जंगल दिखते हैं।

title: From Oberstdorf to Birgsau
short_description:
Easy, beautiful hike along the Stillach into the valley and back again
.
long_description: The tour mostly leads along the cool Stillach river. There are always benches to rest on in between.

images.caption: Kapelle St. Wendelin in Birgsau im Stillachtal.

title: Cantal lead
short_description: Set off to conquer the Plomb du Cantal, an emblematic summit at an altitude of 1855 m!
long_description:
In the heart of Europe's largest volcano, this hike takes you to an exceptional panorama.
An orientation table at the summit invites you to recognize the surrounding peaks and better understand the richness of these landscapes. With a bit of luck, a curious marmot may well cross your path, adding a wild touch to the experience.
A must for mountain lovers and those who love the great outdoors!

title: Coastal walk from Mgarr to Xlendi
short_description: Second stage of the varied coastal circular walk on Gozo – Malta's neighbouring island
long_description: The scenic second leg of our circular walk takes us from the port of Mgarr to Xlendi Bay. There is much to discover on the route, which takes us along the coast of the island of Gozo. Besides the most important harbour of the island with its colourfully painted fishing boats and the big ferry boats, the Mgarr xi-Xini Gorge with its crystal clear water and the steep cliff face is waiting for us. From the rock on which the Xlendi Tower stands, we enjoy the view over the sea and the bay of the village of Xlendi.

title: Baixa Grande to Queimada dos Britos
short_description: The second and smallest stretch of the Crossing of Lençydes Maranhenses reserve incredible and unforgettable sceneries, connecting two locations considered true "o&aacute'sis" of Lençydes.
long_description:
The second leg of the Crossing of Lençóis Maranhenses has 11 km and goes to Queimadas, the second and largest "oásis" of LençQueimadas is the second and largest "oásis" of Lenccedil; and for this reason we do not need to wake up so early as in the previous stretch and it is possible to enjoy the lagoons for longer. On this day the scenery of dunes and lagoons é surreal and there are several stops for bathing.
Arriving at Queimadas, é at lunchtime, which gives á plenty of time to enjoy the day. The restinga vegetation becomes more abundant on the way that leads to a riverbank clearing, the village of Queimada dos Britos. The village is formed by about 200 people, mostly fishermen. Unlike Baixa Grande, there the aridness gives way to a warm sensation, with the sound of running water, green bushes and cashew trees with fruit. D á to rest in hammocks, dive into the river and cross it with a raft to see the sunset from the top of a dune.

title: From Bøur to Gásadalur on the Faroe Islands
short_description: Scenic, partly exposed hike on the old post path to Gásadalur, once known as the most remote village in Europe, which has also been accessible by car via a tunnel for some years. Fantastic views of the Schären islands Tindhólmur and Gáshólmur, scary views of the Atlantic Ocean and spectacular views of the waterfall in front of Gásadalur are guaranteed - if visibility is good and the weather is fine. Gásadalur
long_description: Gásadalur was considered one of the most remote villages in Europe until the construction of a car tunnel. However, you can still get to the remote village on foot by following the old post road along steep cliffs. The tour offers unbelievably wild nature and views of rugged cliffs, deserted islands and a magnificent waterfall. Gásadalur has just over a dozen inhabitants, and if you take the old post road, you can imagine how lonely they must have felt until the tunnel was built. The view of the offshore islands of Sørvágsfjørður, Tindhólmur, Gáshólmur and Mykines is unique.

title: Climbing the Hoher Riffler (3,168 m) in the Verwall Alps
short_description: Limber up and enjoy this challenging hike to the North Summit of the tallest mountain in Tyrol's Verwall Alps
long_description:
With an elevation gain that's just shy of 2,000 m and a route that took us nearly 11 hours to complete, getting to the top and back down in one day proved pretty demanding. Many will choose to split up the journey by overnighting in the Edmund-Graf-Hütte and tackling the summit climb the following morning.  Whichever option you take, the journey, sense of achievement, and fantastic views from the top of the Hoher Riffler are worth the effort.  We visited in late October and had to contend with quite a bit of snow. I'm sure that the trip is much easier during the warmer summer months!
You might like to also check out my other route that's just down the road in Sankt Anton - should you be interested in conquering another 3,000m peak: Climbing the Saumspitze (3,039 m) via the Kartellsee in the Verwall Alps

title: Crossing the Seven Falls - Section 1
short_description: First leg of the Seven Falls Crossing in the middle of the Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park, where we have a unique experience in the Brazilian Cerrado biome.
long_description:
Trekking located in the National Park of Chapada dos Veadeiros, where the goal é reach à Sete Quedas waterfall, waterfalls of small size, but with good extension of width. There are several natural pools, which provide unforgettable moments of diving, contemplation and relaxation. Before that and throughout the route, there are other swimming and water catchment points, such as the famous Cânion 1 and the passage of the Rio Preto.
This first stretch of the 7 Falls Crossing can be done in one day, departing from the Visitor Centre of the Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park and finishing at the campsite that is 150 metres from the falls.Opened in 2013, the Travessia das 7 Quedas is perfect for lovers of hiking amidst nature, besides being a real invitation to immerse yourself in the Cerrado and a chance to see what is most beautiful in this biome.

title: Myra Falls
short_description: A charming and short hiking route that passes through a forest, rich in water and waterfalls near the village of Moggendorf, southwest of the city of Vienna
long_description:
The circular trip to the Mira Falls is a relatively short drive from the city of Vienna and is a great destination for travelers who want to experience nature in addition to visiting the city.
Travelers can enjoy an experiential route that includes crossing several wooden bridges that pass over water channels and watch the waterfalls on the spot. The hiking route passes through a wooded area, which makes walking in it comfortable and pleasant even on hot days. Walking the route is not particularly difficult, but it still includes climbing stairs and walking uphill with a moderate and negligible slope.
Since the route includes climbing stairs, it is not accessible to strollers and wheelchairs.

title: Overview circular route to the Maly Aktru Glacier
short_description:
The Aktru Valley is one of the most accessible and popular places in the Altai Mountains.
The route runs through the Aktru Gorge along Sukhanov Ring.
long_description:
Aktru Valley Research Tomsk State University together with the Federation of Mountaineering and Climbing of Tomsk region implemented the project "Aktru Mountaineering Camp" on the territory of Aktru research station.
Alpinist camp is situated in a wide part of the river valley at an altitude of 2150m in a picturesque area of the North-Chuysky mountain range in the Altai Republic. There are plenty of routes of varying difficulty. Near the alpine camp there is a local attraction – the cabin of famous scientist Tronov, who studied the glaciers of Altai Mountains. There is also a monument to the mountain climber Galina Afanasyeva. There is a lake Sachki with the tourist base on the shore. Further along the route there is an exit to a waterfall. At the bottom of the waterfall, behind the stream there is an observation deck. From here, there are views of the picturesque places and peaks of the Aktru Range.

title: From Bodenmais to the treasure of the Silver Mountain
short_description: The Silberberg is not only the local mountain of Bodenmais, but was also a source of income for the town with its ores for a long time. We can visit an old mine during our tour.
long_description: From the tourist information office, we walk uphill across the railway tracks and the Rieslochweg towards Scherau. Behind this part of town, the mixed forest with fir, beech, lime and rowan trees begins. In the undergrowth we see ferns and raspberry bushes. At a covered rest area, we continue up the slope. At a fork, we follow the sign with the white ten on a red circle. Here our path becomes a stony path. We cross the Schönebenenstraße and continue into the forest. The signs to the Silberberg summit show us the way. When we stop, we hear nothing but the sounds of nature. Finally we come out of the forest and stand on the Gottesgab plateau. From here we can already see the chairlift. There is a playground here for children, while we can rest a bit at the rest area. We finally walk a few minutes further and stand on the summit of the Silberberg. From the summit cross we look down on the village lying deep below us. The Silver Mountain got its name from the mineral galena, which was found here. The inhabitants of the region knew that they could extract silver from this ore. The ore was first mined by what is known as "firesetting". In this technique, the miners first heated the rock by fire and then cooled it by cold water. The rapid temperature change cracked the rock. Later, people drilled into the rock and split it with explosives. The silver obtained was used as a polishing agent and as an additive for dyes. The entire tunnel system in the mountain has a length of more than 20 km. In 1313, mining in Bodenmais was mentioned in a document for the first time, but it ceased in 1953. On the summit we can still see the traces of past mining. There are no longer any trees on the summit, they were felled a long time ago. The miners needed the wood to build tunnels and for firewood. We walk downhill again from the mountain summit and past the chairlift. At the edge of the forest, we follow the signs to Bodenmais and turn left. After a few 100 m we come to a fir tree with a stainless steel box. Here we can stamp the region's stamp in our hiking book. We pass the entrance to the summer toboggan run and shortly afterwards stand in front of the Bodenmais Mining Museum with the Barbara gallery. This historic mining facility is the tourist highlight of the community. We visit the exhibition rooms and the 500 m long gallery. We learn that more than 60 ores were mined in the Silberberg. In addition to galena, sulphur, chalcopyrite, zinc blende and bismuth could be mined. Even gold and platinum were mined. After visiting the museum, we stop at the miners' tavern and enjoy the view from the terrace. We walk downhill on Barbarastraße. This path is so wide that we can walk on the gravel next to the asphalt. On the right side, the summer toboggan run and the ski slope accompany us down into the valley. We come to the valley station of the chairlift. From here we walk downhill along the tarred road until we turn right into the forest after the bridge over the state road. We hike along narrow paths, cross two wooden bridges over the Zellbach stream and come to a Kneipp basin for treading water. After this break, we continue hiking and come out of the forest at the entrance to Bodenmais. The high residential street offers us another wide view over the town and the valley. Finally, we return via the rake path and cross the railway tracks to reach the starting point.

title: Mars-1 (Kyzyl-Chin tract)
short_description: Would anyone like to feel like a Martian? Then come here, this is the place for you! Kyzyl-Chin Nature Reserve in the Altai Mountains is open for active tourism.
long_description: An amazing land gives you and me Mars on our Earth. Yes, indeed, there is a piece of colourful patch of land on earth that reminds us of the celestial Mars. And this piece of Mars is located nowhere else than in Altai, in the Russian Altai Mountains. To be more exact, the natural Martian wonder is located near Chagan-Uzun village in Kosh-Agachsky region. It appeared more than 300 million years as a result of friendship of specific red shades of polymetallic ores, clay and life-giving winds.
