title: Altamira Route
short_description: A leisurely walk leading from the centre of the small town of Santillana del Mar to the area where the ALtamira cave and its museum are located.
long_description:
The walk is on pavements, on the pavement at the exit of the town, then on footpaths for pedestrians or cyclists. As it is uphill, closer to the museum, the route also offers beautiful views of the village and the surrounding hills.
This is a walk that children can also do. Towards the end, there are some benches for resting.

images.caption: Part of the path to the Altamira Museum
Santillana del Mar seen from the route

title: From Dietmannsried to Bad Grönenbach
short_description: A varied tour through villages and forests between Dietmannsried and Bad Grönbach.
long_description: The first section of the trail to Gemeinderied is more of a must. It is not much fun, as we have to walk partly on the edge of busy roads. In addition, we cross under the motorway. The industrial settlement does not smell like the classic Allgäu. Behind the village it quickly becomes more and more rural. At Bärenwies we enter the forest. Via Ehwiesmühle and Hintergsäng we walk to Ittelsburg. After a final climb up to Falken, we reach Bad Grönenbach station via Streifen and Unterthal.

images.caption: Cottage at the edge of the forest

title: Around Magdeburg
short_description: On the flat and 130 km long circular hiking trail around Magdeburg, we will explore the worth seeing state capital as well as the neighbouring towns and communities. The river landscape of the Elbe, the herb-covered heath and the fertile Bördeland landscape will accompany us and bring us closer to the wonderful natural beauty of the region.
long_description:
Stage 1: Magdeburg / Herrenkrug - Schönebeck (26 km)
After an extensive exploration tour of Magdeburg - with St. Mauritius & Katharina Cathedral, St. John's Church, the Convent of Our Lady and the city park - we start our hike in Herrenkrug Park and walk to the Alte Elbe. Passing the waterfall in the Kleine Cracauer Anger, we follow the course of the river until shortly before the Prester See lake and continue walking in an easterly direction. Behind Pechau we reach Wahlitzer Wald, cross the Ehle at Vogelsang and walk via Elbenau to Grünewalde. On the opposite side of the Elbe, we reach Schönebeck, the finishing point of today's stage.
Stage 2: Schönebeck - Olvenstedt (28 km)
Over the Frohser Berg we hike to Beyendorf and Ottersleben, where we pass the Knochenpark and the Amtsgarten. Wide meadows and fields take us to Diesdorf and Olvenstedt.
Stage 3: Olvenstedt - Groß Ammensleben (19 km)
Today we head from Olvenstedt to several small ponds on the Galgenberg and around the Felsenberg to Gersdorf. We finally climb the 121 m high Teufelsberg and hike over the Florenne to Klein Ammensleben. From here it is only a stone's throw to Groß Ammensleben.
Stage 4: Groß Ammensleben - Mose-Farsleben (railway station) (20 km)
The Mittelland Canal is the longest artificial waterway in Germany. We cross it and the Ohre to reach a wooded section of trail behind Samswegen. Now we go through Lindhorst and to the northernmost point of our circular tour in Colbitz. A wide curve then takes us to Mose-Farsleben station.
Stage 5: Mose-Farsleben (railway station) - Möser (22 km)
At the very beginning of the day, numerous sights await us in Wolmirstedt: Wolmirstedt Castle and the historic castle church from the brick Gothic period, a portico house, the Old Town Hall and a pretty old town with half-timbered houses. Along the Mittelland Canal, we cross the Elbe at Hohenwarthe and then hike through the forest to Möser.
Stage 6: Möser - Magdeburg / Herrenkrug (17 km)
A few kilometres after Möser, the forest thins out and opens up an unobstructed view of the beautiful Elbe meadows. The trail continues through Gerwisch and Biederitz to Magdeburg / Herrenkrug.

title: Santillana del Mar - Playa Santa Justa (Cantabrian Coast)
short_description: An unmissable tour for those who want to see the sea near the small tourist town of Santillana del Mar, which, despite its name, is not by the water. For a short stretch at the end, the route covers several kilometres of the Camino del Norte.
long_description:
While you're heading out to sea, the walk takes you up and down at all times. You pass through several picturesque towns with very little traffic, walk a long way along the spectacular coastline, admire the evergreen hilly countryside, sometimes breathe in the air that heralds the approach of cow farms. And, in general, you get a lot of peace and quiet, even in more touristy times.
As soon as you leave Santillana del Mar, look back for a view of the whole county, far away towards the mountain ranges of Asturias.
On the way, there are some superb panoramic views. Don't hesitate to make a longer stop at Santa Justa Beach, where there are picnic tables. The small, seemingly înguished beach here offers an idyllic view.
The coastal path is much travelled by locals, even on their weekend walks.
This segment is the most beautiful, and the gentlest for the feet, thanks to the sandy terrain. Otherwise, you get plenty of asphalt.

The GR99 is a very beautiful route. <A beautiful viewpoint will offer you one of the most panoramic views region!

title: The Cathar Trail GR®367
short_description: Created in 1985, the Cathar Trail links Port la Nouvelle (Aude) and Foix (Ariège) at the foot of the Pyrenees. This route is one of the most emblematic of the Pyrenees.
long_description:
Loaded with history, this 250-kilometre trail between the Mediterranean and Foix offers a wide variety of landscapes: coastal lagoons, wine-growing hillsides, Mediterranean scrub, canigou, forests, gorges and views of the Pyrenees.
The so-called Cathar castles of Aguilar, Padelun, Queribas, Perepertuse, Puilorren, Puyvers, Montségur... mark out the route. Built on imposing cliffs, these vertiginous citadels recall the pages of medieval history, the Cathars of Languedoc.
.

title: Queimada dos Britos to Santo Amaro do Maranhão
short_description: It is the last part of the Crossing of Lençydes Maranhenses, which goes from Queimada dos Britos to Santo Amaro do Maranhatildeo, on a route with beautiful scenery of dunes and lagoons of crystal clear water.
long_description:
The último day of the Travessia dos Lençóis Maranhense é the most physically challenging, because the  ideal time limit recommended for the departure é 3 am;. The effort é rewarded by the sunrise from the top of the dunes. Some of the most beautiful landscapes are seen during this route, one of them just after sunrise.
At around 10am, you reach à two of the most visited lagoons in Lençóis: the Lagoa da Gaivota and the Lagoa das Andorinhas, further north. Enjoy a refreshing swim in crystal-clear waters to refresh your energy. The next two hours continue through the dunes and with the sun highest in this final stretch, the tip é refresh yourself in the passage of the last lagoons. At the exit of the Park, there is a sand road of about 2 kilometres that leads to the centre of Santo Amaro. The town é small and does not have much infrastructure, but if you have time, it can be a good stop here to rest and go to São Luís the next day.

title: Bjørnskinntinden
short_description: Enjoy a panoramic view of Andøya
long_description:
Bjørnskinntinden is the first mountain that greets you as travel on to Andøya Island from Hinnøya. With the flat landscape at its base it can look quite daunting, but a clear albeit steep trail leads to the top 635 meters above the sea.
From the top of Bjørnskinntinden are views around the southern part of Andøya. The vista back towards Risøyhamn is particularly beautiful on a clear summer’s day.
As the trail nears the summit it follows an exposed ridge. Keep some distance from the edge, especially if the terrain is wet and slippery.

title: Andhauet
short_description: Catch an easy view of northern Andøya
long_description:
Andhauet, also known as Andhue, is the closest peak to Andenes at the northern tip of Andøya Island. The peak is quick to reach and sits just 288-meters high, but towers above the flat terrain below.
With a clear and easy-going trail, Andhauet is a great hike to stretch your legs and discover views of Andenes, Senja and the vast ocean. If you’re after a longer trek, this trip can easily be extended to a triangular route taking in one or both of the nearby peaks, Røyken and Ramnan.

title: Waldsee
short_description: An easy, short, flat and pleasant hiking route around the reddish Waldsee, near the town of Lindenberg in the Allgäu region
long_description:
An easy hiking route suitable for the whole family that surrounds Lake Wald (translated into Hebrew: "Lake of the Forest"), part of the route runs very close to the water while the other part runs through a shady forest. The waters of the lake have a red hue and bathing in them is considered healthy for the skin, you can bathe at an organized bathing beach for a fee or enter the water for free from one of the organized points along the way (without lifeguard services).
Near the lake there is a hotel where you can dine in a local restaurant where you can enjoy, for example, a varied and tasty breakfast buffet at a decent price. From noon you can enjoy a lunch and dinner menu.
The route is not paved but is in principle suitable for walking with prams.

title: Kust till Kustleden - from Hårsjö to Lärkesholm
short_description: The tenth stage of the Kust till Kustleden leads from Hårsjö along narrow paths through dense forests and smaller moors to the Lärkesholm rest area.
long_description: In the region through which our hiking trail passes, there are many small farmhouses, cottages and industrial buildings, some of which have long since fallen into disrepair. However, some of them are still inhabited or are maintained by the local heritage society and can be visited. The numerous lakes are rich in fish.

title: Marfino Manor: beautiful, and unknown!
short_description: The Marfino Estate, built with Italian taste, has provided its chic «walls» for the filming of many famous films.
long_description:
The history of the Marfino Estate is vast. And since it was home to noblemen, the history of the estate is likely to be quite confusing and mysterious. Most of its history the estate was owned by the Golitsyns. The Saltykovs also played a major role.
The name of the village changed, and so did the name of the estate. It is not clear how the name Marfino appeared. It can be either in honour of Golitsyn's daughter, who allegedly drowned in the Volga, or because of his wife, whose name used to be Marfa. There is a variant of the name of the village in honor of Saint Martha. It is noticeable that the manor house was a valuable dwelling with an interesting history, in which the women are closely entangled. The manor now serves as a sanatorium for the Ministry of Defence. With all this being said, the manor house is open to the public. It is written, however, that without a permit it would not be comfortable to walk through the park areas. They write that you can get a pass at the watchtower. And they also write that the manor is in the top of Moscow region sights. So, the manor house with Italian flavour is open to tourist curiosity and it is possible to visit where Golitsyn used to be.

title: Ekkerøya
short_description: Experience the rich birdlife and coastal nature trail on Ekkerøya Island
long_description:
The island of Ekkerøya is well worth a short detour for its cliffs, sandy beach, and rich birdlife. You can walk around the island in an hour or two, exploring the small trails and, in late summer, hunting for cloudberries. A shorter, 1.5 kilometer trail is also available.
Over 50 different species of birds have been recorded on Ekkerøya

title: Guvåghytta
short_description: Relax at one of Norway's most beautiful coastal cabins
long_description:
Spend a night or a few at this idyllic DNT cabin on the shores of the Eidsfjord. In 2014, it was voted Norway’s most beautiful coastal cabin according to Ut.no. With Hellfjord in the west and the start of Jørnfjord in the east, you’ll get spectacular views of the water while adventuring in this area. 
Your days may be filled with soaking up the sun or exploring the sea while using the free rowboats and canoes in the fjord. Take a refreshing dip into the sea or explore the climbing walls located behind the cottage. In the wintertime, warm up in the sauna. 
The cabin was built in 1999, but documentation shows that this area has been inhabited for over 5,000 years. 
There are two accommodations on the Guvåghytta (Guvåg Cabin) grounds. Guvåghytta, the main cabin has 13 beds as well as 4 places to sleep in the loft. Mathiasnaustet (Mathias Boathouse) has 6 beds. For a grand total of 19 beds and 4 sleeping places in the loft. There is also space near the BBQ area to pitch a tent. 
How to access the cabin 
Guvåghytta is part of the DNT cabin network. To get access to the key for opening the cabins you can visit: 
Sport1 Sortland
Esso Havna Sortland
Circle K Sortland
XY Straume in Bø

title: Kvasstinden
short_description: Conquer Andøya’s highest point
long_description:
Kvasstinden is Andøya Island’s highest peak, reaching 705 meters above sea level. The summit has tremendous views of the island and broader Vesterålen.
Neither the trail nor summit is terribly exposed, but some careful steps are required as you near the top. The early part of the trail runs through a marsh, so waterproof footwear is highly recommended.
The trailhead is a little more difficult to access than other hikes on Andøya. The last section of the road to the parking area is a poor-quality gravel road and is slow going.

title: Gavltinden
short_description: Hike up Andøya’s second-highest peak
long_description:
Gavltinden is the second-highest peak on Andøya Island. The top delivers panoramic views over the southern part of the island, as well as the surrounding fjords and other islands of the Vesterålen archipelago.  
The entire trek to Gavltinden is uphill, but a gradual ascent ensures the trail is not too demanding. The ridge from Grønnlitinden to the summit is quite exposed with a steep drop, so keep a good distance from the edge along that section of the trail.
Early in the hiking season you may encounter some snow and the path can get slippery. Walk with care and check with locals if you want to avoid hiking across any snow.

title: Cartierheide hiking trail
short_description: This short walking route is perfect for a quick break to get some fresh air and enjoy nature.
long_description: During this route you will walk across the Cartierheide. This heathland is part of the Kempen nature reserve. As you walk across the heathland, this route is different in every season. In summer the heath will be a beautiful purple while in winter it will look rather grey, but that too is a beautiful sight.

images.caption: The Cartier heath in early autumn

title: Holandsmælen
short_description: Easy hike to beautiful panoramic views
long_description:
Although the summit is only 434 meters above sea level, you'll get 360-degree views overlooking the water and mountains. In the east and south is the Buksnesfjord, in the west the Norwegian Sea, and in the north are the Himmeltindan mountains. You'll also see the Leknes plateau and the gorgeous Haukland Beach. 
This hike is perfect for the entire family!

title: Måtinden
short_description: Stroll to the top of Andøya’s most popular peak
long_description:
Considered by many “the must-see view” on Andøya, the hike to Måtinden surely is a rewarding one. The plateau at the top reveals a view of the island’s western coastline towards Bleik and Stave. Explore the many viewpoints and admire Høyvika beach and the rocky peninsula that extends from the peak.
The hike is not demanding and is suitable for a family outing. In the beginning, the trail travels through a marshy area and then through rocky terrain. Wear waterproof and sturdy footwear. Sometimes the summit can be covered in fog, so check the weather forecast first.
Måtinden can be hiked out-and-back from the roadside trailhead, out-and-back from Bleik, or one-way from the roadside and finishing in Bleik.
The gentle terrain means it’s a nice spot to camp under the midnight sun.
Camp by the summit.

images.caption: View of Måtinden and Bleiksøya Island.

title: Bleikmorenen Nature Reserve
short_description: Explore the oldest moraines in Norway
long_description:
Bleikmorenen Nature Reserve attracts both geologists and nature lovers. Situated right beside Bleik village and its beautiful beach on Andøya Island, the reserve is an easy and interesting place to explore.
The trail through the reserve is a pleasant walk on even terrain. The reserve is made up of small lakes and grassy fields that are surrounded by the moraines.
Moraines are created by a moving glacier leaving behind rock and soil. These deposits build up over time and form mounds of various sizes. The process can last for thousands of years and this is why moraines are often very old.
The highest moraines in the reserve reach up to 40 metres in height. The moraines along the shore of Bleiksvatnet Lake are smaller and reach about 10 metres. The northern border of the reserve that runs along the coast features a 2.5 kilometer-long moraine averaging between 15 and 25 meters high.
The area around the lakes is often damp, so wear waterproof shoes.
It is prohibited to camp in the reserve. In Bleik, Midnattsol Camping offers reasonably priced campgrounds and cabins.

images.caption: Bleikmorenen Nature Reserve, with Bleik village above.

title: Dronningruta
short_description: Hike like royalty on The Queen's Route
long_description:
Embark on this truly stunning journey in either direction during this round trip hike from the historic fishing villages, Stø and Nyksund. The hike along this coast and in the mountains can be challenging at points, especially due to the variety of rugged terrain, but it is easily rewarded with views over the northern Vesterålen archipelago, the sandy beach of Skipssanden, as well as the lighthouse in Stø.
The highest point during the hike is Mount Finngamheia, located at 448 meters above seal level. If you prefer only hiking in one direction, take advantage of the local ferry. 
Dronningruta translates to “The Queen’s Route”, and it is named after Queen Sonja of Norway, who hiked the route in 1994. In 2015, Dronningruta was on Visit Norway’s list of the top 10 most spectacular hikes.
Although both villages are small, Nyksund is quite bigger than Stø and it has a lively art and brewery scene. Only a few minutes walking distance from the harbor at Stø is the pristine beach Skipssanden beach. Nyksund and Stø are where most hikers stay, but there are accommodation options in Myre as well.
Stø
Gunnartangen Rorbuferie offers a variety of cabins on the water with picturesque views. 
Stø Caravan Camp has full-service campsites to pitch a tent as well as areas for caravans. There's also a restaurant on the premises that serves locally caught seafood. 
Nyksund
Holmvik Brygge Nyksund is the ideal place to stay in Nyksund. It has guests houses and apartments located on the water as well as a restaurant and organizes outdoor adventures. 
Ekspedisjonen has whimsical rooms, a restaurant, and cafe. 
Located on a tiny island off the mainland, Nyksund Spa & Hiking Club is a boutique hotel that has 5 rooms. 
The newly renovated, The House on Skåltofta, is located on the outskirts of Nyksund and has great views of the open sea.

title: Lynghaugtinden and Vetten
short_description: Relaxing hike with views of islands and Lofotveggen
long_description:
Mount Lynghaugtinden and Vetten are located in Bø in Vesterålen and can be accessed from the towns, Fjærvoll, Staume, or Steine. The peaks provide nice views of Lofotveggen, Skårvågen village, Gaukværøya Island, Hadseløya Island and many other islands and skerries. 
The trip is not too demanding nor long, which enables you to do other hikes the same day or explore the other trails in the greater network.

title: Trolltinden
short_description: Discover 360-degree views of Andøya Island
long_description:
Trolltinden sits atop the mountain ridge that runs from north to south in the northern part of Andøya Island. The summit reaches 436 meters above sea level and offers views of both the western and eastern coasts. Just a short drive from Bleik on Andøya Island, the trail is pleasant and easy-going with a gradual ascent to the top.
The peak is home to a weather radar station, which serves as an easy reference point during the hike. It can be cold and windy at the top, so take warm clothes and windbreakers.

title: Komagdalen Bird Trail
short_description: Go bird watching on a specially built trail into Varangerhalvøya National Park
long_description:
The Varanger Peninsula is a wonderful destination for bird watchers. To further increase accessibility for birders, the national park has created the Komagdalen Bird Trail. The clear trail is also an easy way to get a taste of Varangerhalvøya National Park, starting at the park’s eastern edge and leading in towards the Komagelva River.
The area is home to a mix of species common elsewhere and those more common to Finnmark. There are 5 signs along the path highlighting birds you are likely to spot.
A brochure from the national park has more information about the local birdlife.

title: Nattfjelldalen
short_description: Hike into Varangerhalvøya National Park along Nattfjelldalen valley
long_description:
The Nattfjell valley sits inside the southern border of Varangerhalvøya National Park, not far from Vadsø. The trek to the end of the valley is long, but not too demanding, and at the end you are rewarded with a tall waterfall.
This area is a popular place for locals to escape to and on a clear day from the valley’s edge you can see over the Varangerfjorden and into Russia.

title: On the Rangiswanger Horn
short_description: The Rangiswanger Horn offers a beautiful panoramic view of the Illertal valley and the Allgäu mountains.
long_description:
On beautiful paths we hike to the Rangiswanger Horn. The 1616 m high grassy mountain is part of the Hörnerkette, which runs from north to south on the western side of the Illertal. The Rangiswanger Horn is a popular destination for ski tourers in winter, but during the rest of the year it belongs entirely to hikers. When the alpine roses blossom in early summer, the slopes of the Rangiswanger Horn are covered in pink flowers.
On the Hörnerpanoramaweg we hike past the Ofterschwanger Horn on the right and the Sigiswanger Horn on the left. Between the two mountains lies the Fahnengehrenalpe, which is managed in the summer months. Then it is only a short but steep climb to the round head of the Rangiswanger Horn. From up there we have a wide view üover the Illertal valley to the forested Sonnenköpfe, the Daumengruppe and the Allgäuer Hauptkamm. We descend via the unmanaged Rangiswanger Alpe and return to the starting point through the picturesque Ostertal.

title: Preikestolen – Pulpit Rock
short_description: Hike the famous Pulpit Rock high above the Lysefjord
long_description:
Easily one of Norway’s most famous hikes, Preikestolen is a steep cliff rising over 600 meters above the Lysefjord below. On top is a large plateau, perfect for a picnic and enjoying the views. The hike to the top consists of slightly hilly terrain with an elevation gain of 350 meters.
Always check the weather report before hiking. Bring sturdy footwear, warm clothing, food, and water. Good physical fitness is recommended and you should start early to make sure you can get up and back in plenty of daylight (and possibly avoid the crowds).
Hiking to Preikestolen when there is snow in the mountains is not recommended without a guide.
There is a base camp at the parking lot for Preikestolen with three accommodation options. All accommodation options have awesome views of Lake Refsvatnet and include breakfast.
Preikestolen Fjellstue (Preikestolen Mountain Lodge) is known for its sleek and environmentally friendly design.
Preikestolhytta is a hostel which offers rooms with 2 and 4 beds that have a shared bathroom.
Vatnegården is the oldest building on the premises and has dorms.

title: Vardø Lighthouse
short_description: Explore the landscape from Norway’s easternmost town
long_description:
The town of Vardø is Norway’s easternmost town and actually lies further east than Istanbul. Situated on Vardøya Island, the town is a key point along Norwegian Scenic Route Varanger and also the departure point for boat trips to Hornøya.
The northern part of the island is not populated, and the road to the lighthouse at the point makes for a relaxed walk. Along the way, you can visit “Drakkar”, an interesting outdoor art piece, as well as some ruins from World War II.

title: A trip to the Hagenbachklamm
short_description: A one-way itinerary, light and rich in water, trees and vegetation northwest of the city of Vienna
long_description:
A charming and romantic hiking route that passes through the territory of the Eichenhain Nature Park, which belongs to the Vienna Forest. The route goes through a forest next to the Hagan stream and includes crossing several wooden bridges that pass over the water of the stream. Due to the fact that the route passes through a wooded area, it is shaded and therefore walking along it is comfortable and pleasant even on hot days.
Due to the fact that the route is linear, the walking time as well as the distance shown on this page are for one direction only, but at any point on the route you can retrace the steps to the beginning of the route.

title: Visgueiro Trail in Maragogi
short_description: The Visgueio Trail is a perfect option for those who wish to discover other natural beauties of Maragogi besides the paradisiacal beaches of the region.
long_description:
The trail is located in the community of Gua Fria, in the rural area of the municipality of Maragogi, and begins at the Association Women of Fibre. This é a place where artisans meet to produce handicrafts created from the raw material of the banana tree trunk. The trail has rich biodiversity and is  inserted in the middle of the Atlantic Forest. 
During the way, you will come across numerous mistletoes of varying sizes. The main attraction of the trail is the impressive Gran Visgueiro, a tree over 500 years old and about 22m high.At the end of the trail there is a natural spring where you can take a dip to refresh yourself after the walk and regain energy for the return journey. 
To do the trail, é need to book in advance and hire a local guide, which will á enrich this walk with  legends and stories about the forest and information about the species of plants, exotic fruits and animals of the region &/p>

title: Wendenstieg
short_description: Together with the Elb-Höhenweg (Elbe Heights Trail) and the Wendlandweg (Wendland Trail), the almost completely flat Wendenstieg forms the large Wendland circular trail. We hike through the Nemitz heathland and see numerous Rundling villages in the Hanoverian Wendland.
long_description:
Stage 1: Clenze Flecken - Lüchow (Wendland) (24 km)
We start our hike in Clenze and solve the riddle of the Rundling villages already in Groß Sachau. For here we can clearly see that all the houses of the village are arranged in a circle around a central square, which can only be reached via a single dead-end road. We will still encounter this special building arrangement very often today. So we also experience this special feature of the cultural landscape of the Wendland in Püggen, Schreyahn, Satemin and Lübeln. At the end of the day and the stage, we arrive in the half-timbered town of Lüchow, with the impressive Ratskeller on the market square.
Stage 2: Lüchow (Wendland) - Trebel (18 km)
Today we leave Lüchow, through which the Jeetzel flows leisurely, and hike via Woltersdorf , Thurau and Groß Freese to Trebel. The stage is quite short, but this way we have enough time to enjoy the beautiful landscape and prepare for tomorrow's (longer) section of the trail.
Stage 3: Trebel - Schnackenburg (27 km)
Directly behind Trebel begins the young Nemitzer Heidelandschaft, which offers a wonderful nature experience especially during the heath blossom from August to September. We hike through the Gartower Tannen, a large enclosed forest area, to the climatic health resort of Gartow. If today's stage is too long for you, you can simply relax here for the rest of the day: The Wendlandtherme spa and the Gartower See lake (with camping site) offer plenty of opportunity for this. Another special feature of the village is the Hagelstein organ in St. George's Church. It is the only instrument built by Hagelstein and has a rather peculiar sound. Via Nienwalde and Bömenzin we finally reach Schnackenburg on the Elbe, where we can take a look at the Grenzlandmuseum.

images.caption: The market square in Lüchow with the Ratskeller (town hall cellar)

title: The Pidinger via ferrata on the Hochstaufen above Bad Reichenhall
short_description: The Pidinger via ferrata is certainly the most strenuous and eventful way to climb Bad Reichenhall's local mountain Hochstaufen: A difficult via ferrata leads through its northern flank.
long_description:
The Pidinger via ferrata leads through the northern flank of Bad Reichenhall's local mountain Hochstaufen (1771 m). Established in 2003 by Sepp Reichenberger and financed by the municipality of Piding, it is one of the most difficult via ferratas in Germany. The choice of routes can be described as successful throughout. During the ascent we experience impressive views and the really strenuous ascent is rewarded by a refreshment stop almost directly at the exit. The Reichenhaller Haus (also called Staufenhaus) is located a little below the highest point of the Hochstaufen. It is open from mid-May to mid-October. The demands on our physical condition are quite high, as there is no possibility of replenishing our drinking reserves during the entire ascent. Except for a few passages, the Pidinger via ferrata is equipped with safety ropes and iron clamps throughout. It is advisable to bring a mountain bike, as most of the ascent is on a forest road. The via ferrata itself is strenuous and requires physical endurance and an absolute head for heights.

title: Poço Preto (Black Well) Trail
short_description: Trail that leads to the place in the river where is the Poço Preto and where can be found a great diversity of fauna and flora of the region around the Iguaçu Falls.
long_description:
A Trilha do Poço Preto é an alternative tour that can be done by any visitor who wishes to go beyond the traditional experience of visiting the Iguaçu Falls. The trail is 9,7km long and its name is due to a fault in a part of the river where an explosion of a gas bubble caused by the collision of tectocircuitic plates occurred 135 million years ago. Currently this well that was formed is 22 metres deep and has a diameter of 400 metres.
The trail can be done on foot, by bike or by electric vehicle, where you can see several species of exotic plants and wild animals. At the end of the trail, a pine bridge leads to a 500 metre trail, at the end of which there is a 10 metre high bunker, from where you can enjoy a panoramic view of the forest, especially the Jacaré Lagoa do Jacar;, which is home to a great diversity of aquatic animals.

title: Storfjellet
short_description: Combine a visit to the Mortensnes cultural heritage site with a trip to this peak
long_description: Stop for a visit at the cultural heritage site in Mortensnes and take this short hike to Storfjellet for coastal views. Storfjellet rises steeply above the tiny village below, but with a height of just 125 meters above sea level it is accessible to most hikers.

title: Vadsø Kjærlighetsstien
short_description: Follow “the love path” along the Varangerfjord coast by Vadsø
long_description: Discover the local flora with an easy stroll along Vadsø’s “love path”. The trail is easily accessible from Vadsø center and leads along the shore of the Varangerfjord. It’s a great place to stretch your legs and you only need to walk as far as you feel like.

title: Syltevika
short_description: Trek to hidden bays near Hamningberg
long_description:
Discover the small hidden bays of Indre and Ytre Syltevika along the Syltefjord on a half-day hike near Hamningberg.
The trail to the coast runs through a pretty valley alongside Syltevikvatnet Lake. At Indre Syltevika sits a simple cabin where you can spend the night. There are also good options for camping in the area.
There is a small no-service DNT cabin at Indre Syktevika.

title: Blanc-Martel Trail - Gorges du Verdon
short_description: A beautiful hike up the Verdon by its bed.
long_description: <The Blanc-Martel trail is the best-known in Verdon Gorges and one of must-do routes for any hiker venturing into region.

images.caption: The stunning view from "Balcons de la Mescla"

title: Aldontoppen
short_description: Take an easy-going trail for views along the Varanger coastline
long_description:
Aldontoppen is a family-friendly and easy-going trail on the Varanger Peninsula. The peak reaches just 171 meters above sea level, but as it is somewhat isolated and right along the water’s edge, there are lovely views of the coastline.
There is a picnic bench at the peak, so this is a great hike to stretch your legs and enjoy your lunch with a view.

title: Hardbaken
short_description: Hike up above Hamningberg for views of the abandoned village
long_description:
Hamningberg is a remote, abandoned fishing village. The village is of particular significance due to the collection of intact buildings from the 1800s.
The relatively easy trail to Hardbaken takes you up above the village for views and exploring. If you’re lucky you may even spot a herd of reindeer.

title: Nubben
short_description: Take a short hike up above Ramberg
long_description:
Nubben is a 240 meter peak above Ramberg village. The trail is steep, but short, and rewards with beautiful views.
From the viewpoint you can look over Ramberg Beach and the village below, as well as other peaks including Volandstind and Ryten.
From Nubben, it’s possible to continue along the trail further east up to Moltinden.

title: Von der Auenhütte zur Melköde
short_description:
Eine traumhafte Tour durchs Winterwonderland am Fuße des hohen Ifen im Kleinwalsertal.
Translate to English
long_description:
Von der Auenhütte startend geht es zur Alpe Melköde vorbei am zugefrorenen Herzsee. Eine wunderschöne leichte Tour mit atemberaubenden Ausblicken.
Translate to English

title: Vågakallen
short_description: One of Lofoten’s most famous peaks
long_description:
It’s important to note that this is a very demanding hike and is not suitable for most people. It is recommended to hike this mountain with a guide or someone familiar with the trek.
Vågakallen, is one of Lofoten’s tallest mountains, towering in the sky at 943 meters above sea level. It’s an exciting and challenging hike to the top, where you’ll get a phenomenal view of the fjord and coastline as well as the two mountains it’s located between, Kabelvåg and Henningsvær.
Depending on how clear the sky is, you can see for kilometers from the top. Not only is it a great mountain to hike, but you can also climb it on the side facing Kabelvåg.

title: Loop from Oberstdorf via  Söllereckbahn and Breitachklamm
short_description: This summer hike will take you through mountain paths near Söllereckbahn and to Breitachklamm. You will get really beautiful scenic views of the mountains. The hike will continue with the gorgeous views of Breitachklamm and continuing the walk along the river and through the forest will take you back to Oberstdorf.
long_description: This round trip takes you through forest, mountain and gorge from river Breitach of Oberstdorf.

title: Offersøykammen
short_description: Get a majestic sunrise or sunset view over Vestvågøy and the sea.
long_description: Offersøykammen is located at 436 meters above sea level and provides magnificent views in all directions including the island of Vestvågøya, the turquoise sea, fjords, other islands, and peaks. The hike starts at the parking just in front of the tunnel entrance on the E10. Park your car here and follow a gravel trail for about 50 meters until a track turns to the right, up the phase of the mountain. Follow the well maintianed track up, passing a lake and a little forest until to you reach the upper part. Here you have to scramble a bit as parts of the trail are sandy. The trail is well maintianed the whole way.

title: Winter trek to Buta Cabin (starting from Cheile Butii Complex)
short_description: The forest road leading from the Cheile Butii Complex to Buta Cabin is a route often avoided due to its length and lack of landscape diversity, although it is suitable for beginners (with partial or total cover). In winter, the same route becomes a real challenge due to the heavy snow and can replace any route you might have in mind while keeping you safe from avalanches.
long_description:
From the Cheile Butii Complex, the path climbs slightly through a deciduous forest. Numerous signs, including one for a cycle route, indicate the multiple possibilities of exploring this area. The spectacular rocky walls of the Butii Gorges can be seen on the right, but the route does not pass through the canyon.
After crossing a very wide meadow, with seasonal shelters located here and there on the hill, you enter the forest road (which starts, in fact, from the national road, and is accessible by car, in dry weather).
If you're lucky and an off-road car has been on this road before, at least it leaves some traces and your progress is easier. Somewhere at mid-distance however, the road is blocked by trees and one must continue either on foot or on skis.
Heavy snow and lack of tourists in winter mean you'll be spending a lot of time opening your own path. The landscape is typical of forest roads - you are surrounded by forest, and the road stretches as far as the eye can see back and forth. Every now and then, the ridge of Retezatul Mic can be seen, to your right. The Buta Valley descends dangerously to your right, and as you reach altitude, the stream reaches the same level as the path and you cross it on two bridges.
After leaving the forest road and enjoying the stillness of the fir and spruce forest, Buta Cabin awaits you at the end of a steep ascent, which you probably finish with your last efforts. It is recommended to make sure that someone is at the cabin so that you can stay warm.
In fine weather, the climb to Scorota Saddle and then to Piule Peak takes just over an hour. In winter, almost no one tries this route.
The descent is easier, since the tracks have already been made, but the forest road will be even more exhausting if you return the same day.

images.caption: Signs in the first part of the route
A clearing before entering the forest road

title: Glomtinden
short_description: Popular and accessible hike with fantastic views of Lofoten
long_description:
Glomtinden is located at 419 metes above sea level, and the views on this trip are simply magnificent. Despite some scrambling, it's a relaxing afternoon hike. 
From a small rocky plateau just before the summit, you can get perhaps the best views of the entire trip. The lookout point includes views of Rørvikvatnet lake, Hopsvatnet lake, the city of Svolvaer, and Mount Vågakallen. At the summit, you'll get more of a panoramic view. 
There are a number of accommodation options in Svolvær.

title: Djevelporten and Fløya
short_description: Pose on the “devil’s gate”
long_description:
The trailhead for this spectacular hike is just minutes from downtown Svolvær in Lofoten. In only two hours, you'll conquer more than a 600-meter altitude increase. 
The first destination, Djevelporten (Devil's gate), is a rock that's wedged between Frosken and Fløya. The rock looks somewhat like a bridge, and you can even stand on it, but be careful! Here you can see the famous Svolværgeita mountain from a different angle, as well as Svolvær, Austnesfjorden, Oddvær, and Storemolla.
From Fløya, located at 590 meters above sea level, you have a slightly better view of what can be seen from Djevelporten.

images.caption: Hiking Fløya on a cloudy day.
View over Svolvær, with Svolværgeita in the foreground.

title: हिडिंबा माता मंदिर ट्रैक
short_description: यह छोटा लेकिन सुन्दर ट्रैक पुराने मनाली शहर के बस स्टेशन से शुरू होकर हिडिम्बा माता के मंदिर तक जाता है । यह नेचर ट्रेल, सीढ़ियों, और शहरी सडकों के मिश्रण वाला मार्ग है ।
long_description:
मनाली का हिडिंबा देवी मंदिर महाभारत की विरासत समेटे हुआ एक प्राचीन पगोडानुमा मंदिर है। एक गुफा के ऊपर स्थित, महाभारत के बाहुबली योद्धा भीम की पत्नी हिडिंबा देवी को समर्पित यह मंदिर 15वी शताब्दी में बनाया गया था। यह खूबसूरत मंदिर गहरे रंग की लकड़ी से बना है जिसमें बारीक नक्काशी की गई है। यह मंदिर मनाली शहर के बीच में घने देवदार और बुराँश के जंगल में स्थित है।
इस मंदिर का ट्रैक नए और अनुभवी सभी किस्म के हाइकर्स के लिए आसान और उपयुक्त है। यह ट्रेल हलकी चढ़ाई वाली है लेकिन कठिन नहीं है। ट्रेल शहर की गलियों, जंगल और सीढ़ियों से होते हुए एक छोटे से प्रवेश बिंदु, बैठने की जगह और हिडिंबा मंदिर की पत्थर वाली पगडण्डी तक जाती है।
मंदिर के आस-पास कोई रेस्त्रां या पार्किंग स्थल नहीं हैं। इस मार्ग पर ट्रैकिंग करते समय हाइकर्स को स्नैक्स और पानी साथ लाने चाहिए। फोटोग्राफी करने के लिए भी यह ट्रैक मार्ग बढ़िया है।

images.caption: हिमाचल प्रदेश में पदयात्रा मार्ग: हिडिंबा माता मंदिर ट्रैक
मनाली शहर के हिडिंबा देवी मंदिर में भक्तों की भीड़, हिमाचल प्रदेश, भारत।
मनाली शहर में हिडिंबा देवी मंदिर को जाने वाली जंगल की ट्रेल, हिमाचल प्रदेश, भारत।
मनाली शहर का भव्य पैगोडा आकार का हिडिंबा मंदिर, मनाली, हिमाचल प्रदेश, भारत।
हिडिंबा देवी मंदिर को जाता हुई पत्थर की पगडण्डी, मनाली हिलस्टेशन, हिमाचल प्रदेश, भारत।

title: Festvågtind
short_description: Hike one of Lofoten’s most popular trails for views of Henningsvær
long_description:
Festvågtind is a stunning hike that rises directly from the sea near Henningsvær on Austvågøy Island. It is easily one of the most popular hikes in Lofoten.
Although it seems like a very steep hike, the trail wraps around the backside of the mountain, providing a gradual ascent the entire way up. From the summit there are breathtaking views to the south over the town of Henningsvær and the surrounding islands.

title: Circling Gurga Hill (Breaza) - Heroes' Cross and sandstone rocks
short_description: The Heroes' Cross and the curious sandstone rocks above Breaza are among the few tourist attractions here, beyond the actual charm of the place. And this hike is the ideal opportunity to see both, especially since the routes are marked.
long_description:
Before admiring the two attractions, you have to climb a few paths with clammy soil that take you to the highest points above the town.
First, there are the rock formations- curious sandstone boulders with circular or oval shapes, whose original is still a mystery to the people (the same goes for similar rocks in Costești or Buzău). The rocks from Breaza also have symbolic names.
The Heroes' Cross dates back to 1929 and was erected in honor of the soldiers who dies in wars. The cross resembles the one on Caraiman, Bucegi, hence the symbolic name of "Little Caraiman". It is lit at night.
To return to the city, you can change the marking to follow the yellow band or you can continue on the yellow dot followed so far.
The route can also be done by bike, provided that the terrain is dry. The children will surely enjoy the scenery and, of course, the rocks, and hiking is not too much of an effort for them.

title: Volandstind
short_description: Hike up to the top of the world
long_description:
Volandstind peaks at 457 meters above sea level, with views of Ramberg and Fredvang to the north and the Skjelfjord to the south. While the mountain looks intimidating from the roadside, an easy trail leads to the back of the mountain and up along a ridge to the summit.
The trail is not very exposed and is suitable for most people.

title: From Hofen to Sonthofener Hof and back
short_description: A short after-work tour. The Sonthofener Hof is catered for. So you can replenish your energy after the climb to Sonthofener Hof with a hearty snack.
long_description: This tour is perfect to do some sport after work and to get a good view. Once you reach the top of Sonthofener Hof, you can relax with a hearty snack and enjoy the view.

title: Vancouver Island Cowichan River Provincial Park Hike
short_description: This spectacular provincial park protects significant stretches of the Cowichan River that encompasses an impressive balance of nature, human heritage and recreational values.
long_description:
The Cowichan River Footpath is an historic 20-km trail that winds its way along the scenic Cowichan River from Glenora to Skutz Falls. The Cowichan Fish and Game Association built the footpath during the 1960’s, and although the trail was primarily for anglers, it is now a popular spot for hikers and naturalists. The banks of the river support an interesting diversity of wildlife. 
Skutz Falls offers magnificent views of river rapids and a man-made fish ladder, and is a prime location from which to watch spawning salmon ascend the fish ladder in the fall, or for a picnic at the end of a day’s hike. The Cowichan River is home to seven species of game fish; coho, chinook and chum salmon, and steelhead, rainbow, brown and trout. The cowichan is one of only two rivers in British Columbia known to contain Brown Trout.

images.caption: hiking trail in British Columbia: Vancouver Island Cowichan River Provincial Park Hike

title: Helvetestind
short_description: Get a peek of the world from Hell’s peak
long_description:
Helvetestind (Hell’s peak) rises up as a pinnacle between Bunes Beach and Horseidstranda providing great views of the two beaches as well as larger parts of Lofoten.
The trail begins in Vindstad, a ferry ride from Reine, and follows the start of the trail to the popular Bunes Beach but quickly finds its own trail up to the top. You can easily do both of these adventures on the same day. If you’re not camping overnight, make sure to double check the ferry schedule so you don’t miss the return journey.
Avoid this hike in bad weather as it makes it very difficult to safely traverse the ridge to the top.
Reine is the closest town with accommodation available in traditional “rorbuer”, the trademark red fisherman’s cottages.

title: Across the Weinberg in Burgberg
short_description: A short hike with great views over the vineyard near Burgberg im Allgäu.
long_description:
The general term stands for many things, but not for viticulture. History, however, teaches us something different. In the sunny Burgberg im Allgäu, wine was apparently cultivated until 1855. As the name of the hillside north of the Knapp village makes clear. Unfortunately, nothing is known today about the quality of the wine produced. The wine no longer exists, but the name Weinberg has remained.
Today, a very beautiful, short, sunny hike leads over this mountain, where you can enjoy wonderful views of the Illertal and the surrounding Allgäu mountains.

images.caption: Stairs to the top of the vineyard in Burgberg
At the top of the vineyard in Burgberg
Resting bench on the Burgberg vineyard
Sculpture on the market square of the miners' village Burgberg

title: Reinebringen
short_description: Climb high above Reine on Lofoten’s most popular hike
long_description:
Reinebringen is arguably the most popular hike in the Lofoten Islands. A short, but steep trail leads up the mountainside to a ridge high above Reine village. Instagram has been flooded with pictures of the spectacular views over the village and the surrounding coast.
Due to the incredible popularity of the trail, erosion has caused some serious damage to the landscape. A project was started in 2016 with Sherpas laying stone steps up the mountainside. By early summer 2019 steps were laid almost to the top, but the summit is still to be secured. While the steps make the trail more sustainable and safer than before, good footwear is required, so be prepared and take care.
For an excellent, albeit longer alternative to Reinebringen, consider Tindstinden. The trailhead is in Sørvågen, a short drive south of Reine. The trail to Munken departs from the same parking lot. Similar hikes to Reinebringen in other parts of Lofoten are Festvågtind near Henningsvær and Fløya near Svolvær.
If you choose to hike Reinebringen, aim for a clear sunny day. A wet trail is slippery and dangerous while clouds and fog ensure there are no views. Parts of the trail are often muddy and slippery so good hiking boots or shoes are highly recommended.
Before you head off, check the Reinebringen Facebook page which has frequent posts with the latest parking and trail information. 
Reine features some of Lofoten’s traditional “rorbuer”, the trademark red fisherman’s cottages.

title: Justadtinden
short_description: Climb the highest peak on the eastern side of Vestvågøy
long_description: Explore this majestic mountain and the highest peak on the eastern side of Vestvågøy: Justadtind. From the top at 738 meters above sea level, you’ll get a 360-degree view over western Lofoten, and the beautiful Norwegian shoreline as well as an excellent perspective of Landegode island.

title: Horseid Beach
short_description: Trek to one of Lofoten’s most remote beaches
long_description:
Horseid Beach (Horseidstranda) is one of the many beautiful white sandy beaches in Lofoten. Horseid Beach is similar to the more famous Bunes Beach, but a bit more remote and usually less visited. If you are hiking with kids, the hike to Bunes Beach is shorter and a better choice.
This hike is quite easy and can be done even when the weather is not perfect. It begins with a ferry ride to the start of the trail in the very northern end of the Reinefjord. The boat ride itself is amazing on a clear day with views of the many mountains surrounding the fjord.
Camp by the beach.
Alternatively, Reine is the closest town with accommodation available in traditional “rorbuer”, the trademark red fisherman’s cottages.

images.caption: The grassy meadow leading out to the beach.

title: Flakstadtind
short_description: Admire the white beaches of Flakstad from above
long_description: The climb up to Flakstadtind offers beautiful views of all the beaches in the Flakstad area. The hike is fairly short, but also quite steep. Make sure you pay a visit to the beaches before or after your hike – they are a must see.

images.caption: Bare hvite strender og blått hav å se.
Utsikt over Bøpollen og bak fjellene kan en skimte Vestfjorden
Mulstøa til venstre, fjellene over Vikten og noen topper i Vestvågøy.

title: Icicle Gorge Trail
short_description: A great trail for those that want to experience the magic of the Icicle Valley without having to grunt up and down significant elevation gains
long_description: A gentle loop trail that traverses both banks of the Icicle River. . One side of the river is dry and sparsely vegetated while the other is a canopied forest. Guess which one is south facing and getting the most sun? Mid-way through the hike you will cross a bridge over roaring waters. Take a minute to relax here and enjoy the cool breeze generated by this roaring, surprisingly powerful creek. The native name for Icicle Creek was Nasikelt. As pronounced this name sounds very similar to Icicle. Legend has it that early pioneers mistook the proper native name and interpreted it as Icicle. The name Icicle was established by USGS maps in the early 1900s.

images.caption: Trail marker on Icicle Gorge Trail
Typical trail terrain on Icicle Gorge Trail
Fallen tree on Icicle Gorge Trail

title: Kvalvika Beach
short_description: Visit Lofoten’s most famous beach, on Moskenesøy Island
long_description:
The trek to Kvalvika Beach is one of the most popular in all of Lofoten. The beautiful beach can only be reached on foot and the sight of the beach nestled between the mountains is a sight to behold.
Kvalvika Beach is also a popular spot to camp, providing extra time to enjoy the magic of the location once the day hikers have left.
Combine the trip to Kvalvika with a hike up to Ryten for more famous views of the sandy beach below.
This is one possible route to Kvalvika. Another popular and slightly shorter route is from the east. That trailhead is 2.5 kilometers south of Fredvang, where there is a small parking lot.
Kvalvika Beach is a great spot to camp. There is a big grassy area around the beach perfect for pitching a tent. Find water from the stream on the right-hand side of the beach, where the trail is.
It’s also possible to stay at Fredvanghytta.

title: Überschreitung Grießlspitze und Grießlkopf
short_description:
Überschreitung der wenig besuchten Gipfel Grießlspitze und Grießlkopf im Herzen der Lechtaler Alpen.
Translate to English
long_description:
Grießlspitze und Grießlkopf liegen etwas abseits der bekannten Wege wie z.B. Lechtaler Höhenweg oder Augsburger Höhenweg, werden daher eher selten besucht und noch seltener überschritten. Aber für die Aussicht auf viele bekannte Lechtaler Größen wie z.B. Parseierspitze, Freispitze etc. lohnen sich die Mühen.

Verbindungspunkt zwischen Memminger und Ansbacher Hütte
Vorne Grießlkopf, hinten: Rotspitze, Rote Platte, Freispitze

title: Bike tour around the Sea of Galilee
short_description: A cycling route that allows riders to circle the Sea of Galilee and actually experience it from all directions. This is a cycling route that provides a powerful and unique experience in particular and in Israel in general.
long_description: The Sea of Galilee Viewing Trail, as its name implies, is a cycling route that surrounds the Sea of Galilee from all directions and allows riders to experience the Sea of Galilee up close and from afar, with parts of the route passing close to the water and parts of it viewing it from above. It is a long circular cycling route with a total length of about 140 kilometers and it is therefore customary to do it in several sections depending on the ability and fitness of the riders. During the ride on the trail you pass springs, beaches, towns and other points of interest that give the ride added value.

title: Ämtlerwäg
short_description: A hike through nature, landscape and history of the Säuliamt. The ¨mtlerwäg is marked with blue signposts and yellow lettering.

images.caption: Wanderung in Zürich und Umgebung: Ämtlerwäg

title: Tjeldbergtind
short_description: The hike with spectacular views of Svolvær, Vestfjord, and surrounding mountains
long_description:
You'll be rewarded for all your hard work of hiking Tjeldbergtind, with truly spectacular views of not only Svolvær, Kabelvåg, and Vågan, but also the vibrant blue-green Vestfjord, and the mountains Svolværgeitathe and Fløyen. 
The trail is easy to navigate and is very accessible. It's suitable for everyone, young children to active seniors. 
There are a number of accommodation options in Svolvær.

title: Brunssummerheide walking route
short_description: The Brussummerheide is a beautiful nature reserve in the south of Limburg;
long_description: Logically, you will find heathland on the Brussummerheide. This heathland is maintained by a herd of Mergelland sheep. There are only 4 herds of Mergelland sheep in the Netherlands, which is quite a lot compared to previous years. The Roode beek runs through the area. This brook gets its name from the large amount of iron that can be found in the soil; the iron makes the water rust-coloured.

title: Lammerklamm gorge
short_description: Lammerklamm gorge is located in the Salzburg region, southeast of the city of Salzburg and offers a relatively short and shady walking tour over rushing water
long_description: The length of the hiking route in Lammerklamm Gorge is about 1.3 kilometers (one way) and mostly includes walking on roads that pass next to the giant rocks in the place. Flowing waters with a mesmerizing and wonderful turquoise shade await travelers in the place. There are steps along the route, so it is not accessible for strollers. Guided kayaking can be organized on site (by prior arrangement). Please note that the gorge is open to visitors between the months of April and October only, click here for information on the full opening hours and admission prices.

title: From Immenstadt to the "Zum Lustigen Hirsch" inn
short_description: It starts in Immenstadt, straight out of town into the mountain meadows, past Allgäu cows, up to Akams, off to the inn.
long_description: Start at the Outdooractive head office in Immenstadt, from where you walk out of the town directly into the mountain meadow, past happy Allgäu cows, to Akams, to the inn "Zum Lustigen Hirsch".

images.caption: View of the Allgäu Alps from Akams

title: Reine to Bunes Beach
short_description: Dip your toes into the ocean at a beautiful Lofoten beach
long_description:
Bunes Beach (Bunesstranda) is perhaps the most beautiful beach in all of Lofoten. The beach is situated in a bowl among the mountains with Helvetestind on one side and Storskiva on the other.
This adventure is quite easy and can be done even when the weather is not perfect. It begins with a ferry ride to the start of the trail in Vindstad, which is a great way of seeing more of the many mountains around the nearby Kjerkfjorden. If you do get a beautiful day, consider hiking Helvetestind as well.
Bunes Beach is similar to Horseid beach (Horseidstranda), but Bunes Beach is a bit easier to get to and has more spectacular surroundings.
Camp on the beach.
Alternatively, Reine is the closest town with accommodation available in traditional “rorbuer”, the trademark red fisherman’s cottages.

images.caption: Along the road looking back towards Vindstad.
Bunes Beach, with the Bunesfjord in the foreground.
Bunes Beach with Helvetestind in the background.

title: Hoven
short_description: Take a scenic hike to Gimsøya’s lone peak
long_description:
Hoven is a stand-alone mountain located on Gimsøya, the island located between Vestvågøya and Austvågøya. This island, aside for Hoven, is very flat and full of wetland area but the coastline is exquisite with snow-white sand beaches.
The trailhead for Hoven is located right beside the infamous Lofoten Links, one of the world's most northern golf courses, and climbs up the northeastern ridge of the mountain to the 368-meter tall peak. The hike provides incredible views of the surrounding ocean and landscape, and at the top provides 360 degree views. You will be able to see Vestvågøya to the south and Austvågøya to the northeast and in the distance to the north, you can catch a glimpse of Vesterålen on mainland Norway. 
Lofoten Links Lodge has individual rooms and entire cabins available to book. 
Hov Camping provides an idyllic location to pitch a tent located next to a peaceful beach.

title: Munken
short_description: Spend a night in Munkebu cabin in the wild Lofoten mountains
long_description:
Hike Munken to see the beautiful Lofoten mountains from above. Add on a stay a night at the Munkebu cabin close to the peak for the full experience.
This adventure is a relatively easy hike up to Munken in Lofoten. The trail starts very close to the ocean and goes all the way up to 769 meters above sea level. On the way up you will pass by Munkebu which is a cabin operated by the Norwegian Trekking Association. An overnight stay at the cabin gives you the possibility to experience the Lofoten mountains by night while staying cozy and warm inside the cabin. 
Stay in the cabin.
Alternatively, in Reine there is accommodation available in traditional “rorbuer”, the trademark red fisherman’s cottages.

title: Mannen
short_description: Challenge yourself with this handsome peak
long_description:
Mannen overlooks three gorgeous beaches on Lofoten: Haukland Beach, Uttakleiv Beach, and all of Yttersia. Haukeland is the starting point of the trip and is known to have the whitest beach of all the islands. 
Although the peak itself is rather small, 400 meters above sea level, Mannen provides some incredible views of not only the beaches but also the surrounding ocean and islands.
Camp down by Uttakleiv Beach, which has some basic facilities.

images.caption: View of Haukland beach from Mannen.

title: Stornappstinden
short_description: Flakstadøya's Towering Eastern Peak
long_description:
Flakstadøya is the island in the heart of Lofoten archipelago and Stornappstinden is a very accessible peak providing an incredible view of surrounding ocean, beaches and landscape. Located just minutes from Leknes, Stornappstinden is a steep hike worth every step. 
This hike is vertically demanding in the middle section of the trek. The trail is very well-tracked so you will have solid footing all the way to the top. The hike starts at 60 moh and climbs to a towering 740 moh. From about 350 meters until the 600-meter mark, you gain the most elevation in the least about of distance, so this is presenting a pretty steep grade.
Stornappstinden is the fourth tallest peak on Flakstadøya but the closest one to Leknes, the second largest city in Lofoten, home to one of the major airports on the archipelago. The first 300 meters of the hike will be climbing up a small winter ski hill. Stornappstinden is also an extremely popular ski touring location in the winter and spring. A quick hike up with your skis will provide you a gorgeous view as well as an exciting trip down. 
Stornappstinden is only 15 minutes away from Leknes which can provide many hotels.
Nusfjord, the highly regarded fishing cabins, is only 20 minutes south of Stornappstinden. Nusfjord has many beautiful hikes and adventures to experience or guides to book.
If you continue another 30 minutes south of Stornappstinden you will reach another small town of Ramberg which has a few other accommodation offerings.

images.caption: View of Stornappstinden from Storvatnet and the main road along Lofoten.

title: Flånebba
short_description: Magnificent viewpoint at Nordmøre
long_description: Flånebba in Ålvundeid is one of the most beautiful hikes in Sunndal. The hike itself isn't a very steep hike compared with many of the hikes in the area. The steep parts are done in the beginning and the last few meters in the end. The hike goes through a lovely landscape all the way and when you are done with the first meters and get above the treeline, you can already see Ålvundeid and Innerdalen in the distance. It is an easy path to follow all the way from the Rødset farm all the way to the top.

title: Vettafjellet
short_description: Get some great views of Sunndalsøra
long_description: With its 969 meters above sea level, you get some great views of Sunndalsøra, the Tingvollfjord and the 360 degrees views of the mountains surrounding you. The trail is quite steep but easy to follow.

title: Ekkertinden
short_description: Preikestolen's twin
long_description:
Ekkertinden is one of those places that you definitely want to visit. Almost everyone knows the famous Preikestolen, but this is Nordmøre's own top with a drop.
The hike is really steep and takes around two hours to get to the top, which stands at 1,189 meters. But the view in the end is stunning and well worth the trip! 
Your easiest option is to stay in Oppdal. Oppdal is a ski destination so you will find lots of options for hotels, cabins and even Airbnbs.

title: Svøufallet
short_description: Short hike to a beautiful water fall
long_description:
Svøufossen (Svøufallet) is a tall and beautiful waterfall near Åmotan in the region Møre og Romsdal. The waterfall plunges 156 meters down and creates the total height of about 313 meters with the vertical river before the main fall. 
Your easiest option is to stay in Oppdal. Oppdal is a ski destination so you will find lots of options for hotels, cabins and even Airbnbs.

title: Heybeliada Walk
short_description: If you want to get in touch with nature and enjoy your daily walking sports, this easy route is just for you.
long_description:
Heybeliada offers a very easy but easy, as well as a beautiful and peaceful route to anyone who wants to travel in Istanbul. We think that those who are looking for a place to enjoy nature in Istanbul will definitely come to Heybeliada. Especially the ease of the route and the fact that it can be done daily makes this route appeal to everyone who is used to it and makes it even more valuable. 
We start this 7-kilometre route, which is approximately 2 hours in total, excluding the resting time, from Heybeliada Ferry Pier. The route offers us a track with a unique view of nature where blue and green blend together. Heybeliada is such a beautiful place that when you complete this route, you are not only satisfied in terms of sports. The route also brings you many points of interest that you can visit. 
If you're looking for something more than just a walk, try this easy route.

title: The rolling hills of Mavrovo: Medenica peak from Galichnik
short_description: Scenic hike from the charming mountain village of Galichnik to one of the best panoramic viewpoints of Mavrovo National Park: Medenica Peak.
long_description: This rewarding hike brings us face to face with all the rich variety of Mavrovo National Park: Starting among the picturesque stone houses of Galichnik, the path leads us up the slopes below the impressive rock face of Govedarnik Peak to the extensive high plateau of the Bistra mountains between Mavrovo and Galichnik. Among these rolling hilltops we ascend to the summit of Medenica, the highest peak of the Bistra plateau and a stunning viewpoint offering a 360° panorama of Mavrovo National Park and the wild Korab Mountains. The descent via the broad east ridge turns the summit tour into a circular route across the sheep pastures on the high plateau. On the descent, keep an eye open for wild herbs and flowers along the way - there's plenty to discover here. Surely one of the most beautiful day hikes in the National Park and a safe bet if you want to make sure that you experience the unique beauty of this region.

images.caption: View towards the Korab mountains from Medenica
The impressive rock face of Govedarnik

title: Elfstedentocht stage 4
short_description: This stage takes you from Sloten to Stavoren.
long_description: You cycle along the beautiful Zuiderzee. Cycling along the Zuiderzee gives you wonderful views throughout the route. Stavoren is also called the Copenhagen of Friesland. This is because Stavoren is surrounded by water and there are colourful houses along the shore.

title: Gotthard Tunnel Trail 2. Stage Bristen-Sedrun
short_description: On foot über the longest tunnel in the world!
long_description:
Tracking the world's longest tunnel
57 kilometres and around 20 minutes separate train travellers from the North and South of Switzerland thanks to the Gotthard Base Tunnel, the world's longest tunnel. But it is more interesting to experience the trail from Erstfeld to Bodio, which lies above it, at walking pace.

Stage 2 Bristen - Sedrun

In order to shorten the second stage a little, you can choose to book a taxi to take you into Etzli Valley from Bristen. From there, the trail winds across two terrain levels to a small plateau which is best viewed from the Etzli cabin. There, a lovely coffee with a slice of cake awaits you, or even a hearty soup for lunch, enhanced by stunning all-round views of the surrounding granite mountains. In order to relax completely, you can also stay the night here and enjoy the starry sky while tucking into a hotpot. Stopping over makes sense because from now on it all gets a bit more Alpine. On the mountain trail to Chrüzlipass at an altitude of 2347 metres, you again cross the tunnel trajectory. It's worth lingering at the pass. The mighty Oberalpstock rises up in the East. Time to say goodbye to the Alpine world of Uri. Because you are now entering Surselva in Graubünden.
Attention: due to a mountainslide the route further down is closed. Take route D via Alp Caschlé down to Sedrun with its healthful spa and swimming pool Bogn Sedrun and wealth of accommodation options.

Note(s)
Attention: due to a mountainslide the route over the Chrüzlipass via Val Strem is closed. Take route C: via Mittelplatten and Val Mila. (T3) only after mid July because of snow!
route D: via Chrüzlipass and Alp Caschlé +1 hour.
Attention: In winter from midd october till midd june this trail is covered with snow. In Summer it is also possible to pass through snowfields. Inform yourself before you start your tour.

Notes
You will cross the Gotthard Base Tunnel trajectory twice.
Public transport is available in Bristen and Sedrun.

title: Bispevatnet Lake
short_description: Escape the crowds at Trollstigen and visit a mountain lake
long_description:
The blue-green Bispevatnet lake sits calmly under the shadow of Bispen mountain, constantly replenished with icy-cold water from a small waterfall.
The hike to Bispevatnet is quite quick but very rewarding. Just a short distance from the crowds at the Trollstigen Viewpoint below, it feels as though you’re being let in on a secret piece of Norwegian nature.
Make sure to fill your bottle with the cold, fresh water from the lake.
There are several hotels, lodges, and campgrounds in and around Åndalsnes.
Hotel Aak is a cozy boutique hotel with wonderful food, located about 5 kilometers from Åndalsnes
Hotel Bellevue is the largest hotel in town and has an in-house restaurant
Trollveggen Camping has modern cabins and campgrounds, right alongside Trollveggen

images.caption: Hiking up to Bispevatnet lake, with Bispen mountain in the background.

title: The rocks of Castelviel - Gorges de l'Ardèche
short_description: A magnificent, relatively easy hike with superb views of the Ardèche gorges and the village of Aiguèze. A must.
long_description:
The route starts from the free car park overlooking Aiguèze. From there, a fairly long and stony, but easy, climb takes you quietly to the heights. Turn around to admire the shadow of Mont Ventoux, the giant of Provence, in the distance.
Once at the top, a loop allows you to reach the rocks of Castelviel. The view on the mountains of the Ardèche is simply magical!
<After this small loop, you go back down towards the village. Headlands allow to admire gorges. The view of village is also magnificent.
Finally, take a tour of the village, labelled as the most beautiful village in France ». Enjoy the castle overlooking the Ardèche and the cafe terraces under the plane trees.
Finally, take a walk around the village, which has been labelled the most beautiful village in France.

title: Stabbeskaret
short_description: Trek to the edge of Trollveggen
long_description:
The hike to Stabbeskaret takes you from Trollstigen Viewpoint right to the edge of Trollveggen. Stabbeskaret is the gorge between the peaks of Semletind and Stabben.
The trek is not for the faint of heart, taking you up close to the sharp Trolltindene peaks with their vertical drop down into the Romsdalen Valley.
There are several hotels, lodges, and campgrounds in and around Åndalsnes.
Hotel Aak is a cozy boutique hotel with wonderful food, located about 5 kilometers from Åndalsnes
Hotel Bellevue is the largest hotel in town and has an in-house restaurant
Trollveggen Camping has modern cabins and campgrounds, right alongside Trollveggen

title: Gotthard Tunnel Trail 1. Stage Erstfeld-Bristen
short_description: On foot über the longest tunnel in the world.
long_description:
Gotthard Tunnel Trail - Tracking the world's longest tunnel
57 kilometres and around 20 minutes separate train travellers from the North and South of Switzerland thanks to the Gotthard Base Tunnel, the world's longest tunnel. But it is more interesting to experience the trail from Erstfeld to Bodio, which lies above it, at walking pace. Because, rising to 2448 metres and extending for around 100 kilometres, you enter a mountain environment of exceptional allure. Enjoy the varied mountain scenery and immerse yourself in the culture of hospitality of Uri, Graubünden and Ticino. Again and again, you will be standing exactly above the tunnel, albeit up to 2000 m higher

Stage 1 Erstfeld - Bristen

You can start directly from the North portal on a forest path to the main tunnel crossing. However, it's really lovely to sway the 650 m from Erstfeld to Alp Schwandi in a little, red four-person cable car. That does require starting on a Saturday or Sunday, because on other days - or when the Föhn is blowing too strongly - the Schwandibahn doesn't run, or only if there are at least eight people. The pace of this short journey might seem exceptionally slow if you have previously been reading up on the Gotthard Base Tunnel: 57 kilometres at up to 250 km an hour, 20 minutes to traverse 190,000 concrete sleepers, 65 passenger trains per day carrying up to 15,000 travellers. From Schwandi, you walk along the varied, panoramic Gotthard Tunnel Trail more or less following the contours southwards. It is a pleasant introduction, embellished with a hanging bridge and, shortly before Waldiberg, a viewing point that lies directly above the tunnel. And once again you are in a cable car, this time in the open air and firmly attached by a traction cable so that it tips forwards or backwards, depending on the direction of travel. You can stay in Bristen or on the picturesque Golzernsee, which is reached from Waldiberg via a varied and partly exposed mountain trail.

Note(s)
You will cross the Gotthard Base Tunnel trajectory once.

Public transport is available in Erstfeld and Bristen.

Parking: Infocenter Erstfeld, Einstieg Bärenboden, Bahnhof Erstfeld.

Option 3: With the Waldibergseilbahn down to Bristen.

Attention: In winter from midd october till midd june this trail is full of snow. In Summer it is also possible to pass through snowfields. Inform yourself before you start your tour.

Attention: the start from Infocenter Erstfeld first goes over the street and then up via a non marked forrestroad.

title: Kløvstien
short_description: Hike up Trollstigen on the old road between Romsdal and Sunnmøre
long_description:
The Kløvstien trail climbs up the steep mountainside, past Stigfossen Waterfall, to the Trollstigen Viewpoint. The trail is the old road between the regions of Romsdal and Sunnmøre, and weaves up alongside Trollstigen Road.
Until Trollstigen Road opened in 1936, Kløvstien was the only route up and down the mountainside. It was a dramatic and dangerous journey, only navigable on foot.
Today, tough sections of the trail feature chains and stone steps for increased accessibility.
There are several hotels, lodges, and campgrounds in and around Åndalsnes.
Hotel Aak is a cozy boutique hotel with wonderful food, located about 5 kilometers from Åndalsnes
Hotel Bellevue is the largest hotel in town and has an in-house restaurant

title: Litlefjellet
short_description: Don’t miss this quick hike with knockout views
long_description:
Litlefjellet is a short, easy hike and one of the most accessible natural viewpoints in the area. It is an excellent vantage point from which to admire Trollveggen (the Troll Wall). With a sheer one kilometer precipice and its collection of jagged peaks, the wall is one of the most famous sights in Norway.
Reaching 780 metres above sea level, Litlefjellet (Little Mountain) sits directly across the valley from the wall. Litlefjellet also gets you up close to Romsdalshornet, a distinctive peak popular with mountain climbers.
There are several hotels, lodges, and campgrounds in and around Åndalsnes.
Hotel Aak is a cozy boutique hotel with wonderful food, located about 5 kilometers from Åndalsnes

short_description: This demanding mountain tour leads to a 3000-metre peak directly on the French-Spanish border. From its summit you can see the central Pyrenees and, if you are lucky, you might even spot one of the vultures that live here.

title: A versatile trip near the town of Fischen
short_description: A varied, interesting and accessible hiking route that passes through the open areas near the town of Fischen in the upper Allgäu region. Panoramic views of the Alps, a river, a lake, a squirrel forest and other surprises await you on this route
long_description: An easy itinerary that is ideal and interesting for travelers of all ages as you can enjoy exposure to a wide variety of landscapes as well as fun attractions. The route starts at the end of the town of Fischen, passes over and beside the river Iller, surrounds a lake with turquoise water called Auwaldsee. On the way back you pass through a squirrel forest and the town's park where you can enjoy a small botanical garden and a variety of fun activities for the whole family - experiential mini golf, a large playground, a rope climbing facility and more. This hiking route is flat and accessible to strollers and wheelchairs.

title: Gotthard Tunnel Trail 5. Stage Cari-Bodio
short_description: On foot über the longest tunnel in the world.
long_description:
Tracking the world's longest tunnel
57 kilometres and around 20 minutes separate train travellers from the North and South of Switzerland thanks to the Gotthard Base Tunnel, the world's longest tunnel. But it is more interesting to experience the trail from Erstfeld to Bodio, which lies above it, at walking pace.

Stage 5 Carì - Bodio

The final stage of the Gotthard Tunnel Trail essentially follows the Strada Alta Leventina, one of Switzerland's oldest mountain passes. For a long time, it was somewhat forgotten. However, it has gained new significance because its course fairly closely follows the tunnel's trajectory. And it has lost none of its charm: tightly-packed mountain villages consisting of rustic houses alternate with resin-scented forests; elegant little churches are planted on top of the most beautiful hilltops with breathtaking views. Those walking in autumn will find sweet chestnuts. In every season, you are accompanied by gorgeous views deep into the Leventina Valley from Airolo to Biasca. Shortly before Biasca, the Strada Alta descends along romantic paths to reach the valley floor almost immediately beside the southern portal of the Gotthard Base Tunnel. There, trains shoot out of the tunnel tubes, completing their journey from North to South in less than half an hour. For the hikers, it has been a very different experience: they have spent five days drinking in the light, hiking nearly 100 km through gorgeous mountain scenery, climbing 5600 m and rediscovering the Gotthard region.

Note(s)
You will cross the Gotthard Base Tunnel trajectory twice.
