title: Fløya
short_description: Climb to the best lookout over Tromsø
long_description:
There is no better way to get acquainted with Tromsø than to head up to Fløya for a bird's eye view of the city. Fløya, the eastern mountain rising 671 meters above the ocean, is a popular location for both a great adventure and to gain a better perspective of Norway's Arctic city. From the top of Fløya, you are witnessing the panoramic view above Tromsø, the surrounding ocean, and the hundreds of small and large Norwegian islands scattered throughout the area. 
There are many paths up to Fløya but the one we propose takes you through the beautiful forest on a friendly incline and winds its way up to the first lookout point at Storsteinen, where the historic cable car arrives, and then takes you further up the hill past Steinbøhytta to the peak. 
Enjoy a meal at Fjellstua, take the cable car ride back down the mountain, or enjoy a casual hike down an alternate route which goes through the neighborhood situated below. 
Choose from one of the many hotels or apartments in the city.

images.caption: View of Tromsø city during the polar night.
View from the upper cable car station.
View by the upper cable car station.

title: Veluwe walking route
short_description: During this route, you will discover a small part of the Veluwezoom national park. This part of the Veluwe lies just above Arnhem.
long_description: The Veluwe is a protected nature reserve with no clear boundaries. Many animals such as: red deer and wild boar have chosen the Veluwe as their habitat. The Veluwe is also an area where many Hanseatic towns and castles can be found. Middachten Castle is near this route, so you could walk past it.

title: From Siusi to the Sciliar
short_description: The mountain tour on the Sciliar is very interesting from a scenic and geological point of view. From the summit we enjoy a magnificent view of the near and far summit regions of the Dolomites.
long_description: With 56 hectares, the Alpe di Siusi is the largest alpine pasture area in Europe. It is accessible by several cable cars and lifts. The Alpe di Siusi cable car takes about 10 minutes to reach the plateau, but we only touch the southern edge of the Alpe di Siusi. On the ascent we soon reach a station on the Oswald von Wolkenstein Trail. This Oswald was an important knight in the late Middle Ages. The next stage takes us to the Schlernbödelehütte, a hut built in 1961 by the Bolzano section of the German and Austrian Alpine Club. It was built to replace the Schlernhaus, which had passed to an Italian association. From the summit of the Schlern, the Petz, you have a wonderful view. The following peaks and mountain groups, among others, come into view: Rosengarten, Puez, Geisler, Piz Boe. On the way back, we take the Geologensteig trail via the Possliner Schwaige. At 10 different stations we can look at the prevailing rock strata.

title: Cheakamus Lake
short_description: Great views with little effort
long_description:
This is one of the easiest hikes in Garibaldi Provincial Park. The hike to Cheakamus Lake will offer you beautiful views of this turquoise lake situated in between towering mountains. The lake is fed by multiple glaciers and this is why it gets it's very special color. 
The hike to just the lake takes about an hour one way and you can choose if you want to continue all the way to Singing Creek Campground or if you want to just take a look at the lake and return to the parking lot. 
You can camp at Cheakamus Campground with 10 tent spots. Or you can camp further in at Singing Creek Campground with 6 tent spots. You need to pre-book overnight stays at these campgrounds.
There are food hang facilities at the campgrounds, but they may fill up so prepare to bring your own equipment as well

title: Black Tusk from Garibaldi Lake
short_description: Get up close with Black Tusk from Garibaldi Lake Campground
long_description:
Black Tusk Mountain is one of the most spectacular mountains in Garibaldi Provincial Park. Its jagged edges and deep black color is visible from far away and from several points along the Sea to Sky highway.
There are three main routes for hiking to Black Tusk. All three options are very long day hikes so consider staying a night at one of the nearby campsites before you do the final section up to the mountain.
This hike starts from Garibaldi Lake.

title: Store Blåmannen
short_description: Hike Kvaløya’s tallest and most demanding peak
long_description:
Store Blåmannen demands your focus and effort the entire trek, but at the top, there will never be a more exquisite experience. Not only will you have worked hard (therefore clearly earning that "kanelbolle" you were eyeing at the cafe this morning) but you will be overlooking some of the most magnificent scenery you can imagine.
Store Blåmannen is the highest peak on the island of Kvaløya, reaching 1044 moh and located in the middle of the island overlooking Kaldfjorden. This is one of the better-known hikes on Kvaløya and therefore well-marked and well-maintained. Keep in mind this is a more physically demanding hike but well worth the accomplishment at the top.
Kvaløya, “whale island”, just minutes from Tromsø, is located within the arctic circle and is the 5th largest island off of Norway’s mainland. This island boasts several fjords and 10 peaks higher than 700 moh, three of which are over 1,000 moh. The west coast of Kvaløya, Sommerøya, faces the open ocean and is the warmest area of the Tromsø municipality. It is hard to choose what stands out more on Kvaløya: the magnificent mountain peaks or the raw coastal beauty. 
Tromsø and Kvaløya both provide a variety of available hotels and airbnb’s. If you are looking for a special norwegian summer accommodation we recommend checking out Sommerøy Arctic Hotel, located on the western coast of Kvaløya.

title: Trail to the Fumaça Waterfall in the Chapada Diamantina
short_description: The Fuma waterfall, surrounded by majestic cânions and the exuberant nature of the Chapada Diamantina, is an impressive 340 metres high and is one of the most famous post cards of the region;
long_description:
If you want to get to know the Chapada Diamantina, this is a trail that cannot be missing from your itinerary. Stay in the bucolic village of Caeté-Açu, in the Vale do Capão, a perfect destination for those who want tranquillity and direct contact with the beauties of the region. From here, it is about 10 kilometres through valleys and rivers for an incredible experience at one of the most spectacular viewpoints of the Chapada.
The trail begins at the headquarters of the Associacao o de Conductores de Visitantes do Vale do Capão, a non-profit association that supports sustainable tourism and protects the environment of the Capão Valley. They also offer reception and guiding of tourists, a variety of information about the region, monitoring and assistance for visitors passing through this trail. You will be invited to enter your details in a control book and hire a guide if you wish. 
Read carefully the safety recommendations on the access à trail. Só é possible to start the tour between 8: 00 and 13:00 hours.

title: The Imbut trail
short_description: In the opinion of many, the Imbut trail is a must for hikers who walk the Gorges du Verdon...
long_description:
The "Wow" effect is coming! This hike requires a certain experience but what a pleasure for the eyes!
You will walk through the Styx du Verdon, a place where the gorges narrow to form a tortuous thread in the middle of the Verdon Canyon, before the waters of the Verdon River flow into the valley;of the Verdon disappear under a huge chaos of boulders overhung by 400 m peaks at the place called "l'Imbut" (the funnel in Provencal).
Some of the passages on the cliff face and through the boulders can be difficult. Although suitable for all seasons, some passages can be technical when it rains or in winter.
The route is not suitable for all seasons.

title: Kyffhäuser Mountain Run - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description: The International Kyffhäuser Mountain Run has been based in Frankenhausen since 1979 and has attracted numerous runners ever since.
long_description: The range of courses includes various distances: The so-called Kyffhäuser Mountain Marathon is the main race. In addition, distances of 6 km, 14.9 km and the half-marathon distance have to be mastered, whereby everything from running to walking/nordic walking to hiking is permitted. The Salomon Trail Running Cup takes place on the 14.9 km mountain run.

title: गौरीकुंड-केदारनाथ टरैक मार्ग
short_description: 18 किलोमीटर लंबा गौरीकुंड केदारनाथ ट्रैक एक तीर्थयात्रा मार्ग है जिसने हालिया समय म ें एक चुनौती पूर्ण हिमालयी नेचर ट्रेल के तौर पर युवा हाइकर्स के ब ीच  लोकप्रियता हासिल की है।
long_description:
भारत के उत्तराखंड राज्य में स्थित केदारनाथ चार धाम तीर्थों में से एक है। केदारनाथ शहर और मंदिर गर्मियों में मई से अक्टूबर तक खुले रहते हैं। हालाँकि यहाँ जाड़ों में भी आया जा सकता है लेकिन तब भारी बर्फबारी के लिए तैयार रहने की जरूरत है।
साल 2013 की विनाशकारी बाढ़ के दौरान गौरीकुंड-केदारनाथ मार्ग का अधिकांश भाग बह गया था। राज्य सरकार ने रामबाड़ा तक पुराने वाले ट्रैक की मरम्मत करी है और रामबाड़ा के बाद नया ट्रैकिंग रूट बनाया है।
गौरीकुंड से पहले पड़ने वाले सोनप्रयाग शहर में एक सरकारी चिकित्सा केंद्र उपलब्ध है। सभी तीर्थयात्रियों और पैदल यात्रियों को यहां से मेडिकल फिटनेस सर्टिफिकेट लेना होता है। सोनप्रयाग से घोड़े और पालकी भी बुक कर सकते हैं।
आपके सामान को केदारनाथ तक ले जाने के लिए पोर्टर्स (जिन्हे स्थानीय भाषा में पिट्ठू कहा जाता है) भी उपलब्ध हैं।वो आपके सामान की डिलीवरी सीधे आपके होटल में कर सकते हैं या आपके साथ साथ भी चल सकते हैं।
केदरनाथ मार्ग बहुत ही सुन्दर है। शहर शांत और अध्यात्म से भरा हुआ है। मंदिर अपने आप में पत्थर के काम का एक उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है और 6000 मीटर से ज्यादा ऊँची चोटियों के बीच स्थित है।

title: Remstecken Koblenz
short_description: This beautiful jogging route, which is not particularly demanding, is suitable for anyone with a little fitness and jogging experience. The route is a five-minute drive from Koblenz city centre.
long_description: The tour leads almost exclusively through woodland and at the beginning even a short stretch on the Rheinburger-Höhenweg. There is a magnificent view of the Moselle valley at one point.

title: Rennesøyhodnet
short_description: A great hike with beautiful views of the islands surrounding Stavanger
long_description: Enjoy an easy hike to Rennesøyhodnet on Rennesøy island in the Ryfylke Islands. Just a 30-minute drive from Stavanger, this hike is easy to access and child-friendly. Walk through the farmlands and small forest out to the vista, providing incredible views of the surrounding ocean and islands.

title: Hovlandsnuten
short_description: Hike the stone steps to a cabin with a view over the Saudafjord
long_description: Hovlandsnuten is a very popular peak to climb near Sauda, with lovely views out over the Saudafjord. Stone steps laid by Nepalese Sherpas help ease the steep trail to the top. On the peak there’s a small cabin where you can shelter from the elements and admire the view.

title: Vinddalen to Skåpet
short_description: Enjoy an easy hike up the valley to the incredible modern cabins at Skåpet
long_description:
A nice, family-friendly hike up Vinddalen valley to the modern cabins at Skåpet. Make it an overnight stay at the new cabins or enjoy a day-trip up the beautiful valley.
Skåpet cabins - The DNT cabins located at the end of the hike. Visit the website to book the cabin or call +47 51 84 02 00.

title: Kvænan
short_description: Visit Senja's third highest peak
long_description:
Kvænan is a characteristic mountain with three pinnacle peaks on the southwest side of Senja island. It is Senja’s third highest peak and is situated on the Atlantic Ocean, so you will surely get some great views from the top. 
Flakstadvåg Camping is your closest accommodation option to this adventure. You can also choose to stay in Finnsnes which is about hour drive from the trailhead.

title: Trekking up Mount Kachkanar: Shad Tchup Ling Monastery
short_description: Mount Kachkanar – is one of the easily accessible mountains in the Middle Urals. The mountain – is picturesque and in addition there is the only Buddhist monastery in the region, Shad Tchup Ling (Shedrub Ling).
long_description:
The itinerary begins from the village of Kosya.
Tourists are interested in Mount Kachkanar because of its bizarre figures. The various stone figures - rocks, aka residuals, have remained at the top of Kachkanar since ancient times unbroken. One of such rocks resembles an exact likeness of a camel's head. This rock is called – a camel's head. There are many places on the mountain with rocks that are scattered all over the surface. On one of these rocks there is a monument in the shape of a rocket to a man of the last century – Yuri Gagarin. Tourists write their names on the rocket, thus dreaming of going into space sooner, or at least being there too someday.
But the main attraction at the summit is the Buddhist temple of Shedrub Ling. The temple was liable to be destroyed on the occasion of the expansion of an iron ore quarry nearby. But the Buddhists have managed to keep their peak intact, the temple will continue its validity and tourists can still climb the sacred mountain of Kachkanar.
The Buddhist temple is the main attraction.

images.caption: View of Kachkanar village from Kachkanar Mountain
Gates to the Shedrub Ling Buddhist Monastery

title: Kjerag
short_description: Get the photo of a lifetime
long_description:
Kjerag mountain sits on the southern shore of the Lysefjord, near the tiny village of Lysebotn at the eastern end of the fjord. The cliff-face along the fjord is practically a vertical drop, plunging over 980 meters down into the water. The hike up to the top is one of the most popular in Norway, along with the nearby Preikestolen.
For many, the main reason to take this hike is the Kjeragbolten boulder, which sits precariously between two mountains. There are often lines as hikers wait to carefully step out on to the boulder for a photo. Note that there is a 240 meter drop from the boulder and no safety fences. Even if you don’t dare to step out on to the boulder, the hike is beautiful and well worth doing for the views.
The hike can be demanding with some steep sections at the start and middle of the trail with chains. Depending on the weather the smooth rock can be quite slippery. As always when hiking in Norway, be prepared for all weather and use footwear with good grip.

images.caption: Looking over the edge down at the fjord.
Relaxing with a view of the Lysefjord.

title: From Jocketa around the sunken village of Pöhl
short_description: Through meadows and fields we circle the Pöhler dam, which is not only a paradise for water sports enthusiasts.
long_description:
Our starting point is the railway station of the state-recognised resort town of Jocketa, whose charming townscape is characterised by 19th century villas. From here we walk along the tracks to Bergstraße and down to the left to Barthmühle. With the imposing Elster Valley Bridge in view, we cross a footbridge along the railway line into the Trieb Valley, the core area of "Vogtland Switzerland". Upstream, we now follow the course of the Trieb and after about two kilometres we reach the dam wall of the Pöhl dam.
The dam bears its name in memory of the former village of Pöhl, which had to give way to the waters when the dam was built in the 1960s. The foundation walls of some of the houses are still partly preserved today, but are mostly far below the water surface. At low tide, however, they can occasionally be seen jutting out of the water. With the reform of the municipalities in Saxony, the name Pöhl was given a new lease of life: the formerly independent districts around the northern part of the Pöhl dam are now grouped together under this name. The dam, once built as a service water reservoir for central German industry, today fulfils the function of flood protection and recreation centre.
From here, our path always leads along the dam wall, past the boat landing stage and the natural outdoor pool to the tourist information office at the Gunzenberg campsite. We walk past the lake ponds, cross a path and come across the road to Möschwitz, which we follow a little way to the left. The beach path to Voigtsgrüner Bucht branches off to our left and takes us closer to the shore again. On the beach path we pass the bungalow settlement Voigtsgrün and come to the edge of Altensalz. We walk through the village of Altensalz on the village road and cross under the A72 motorway. Immediately behind the motorway, we turn left onto a small path and then right over the two barriers of Neuensalz and Thoßfell to the north bank of the dam. If you want to fortify yourself for the way back, the Küpfers Restauration on the main road of Thoßfell is just the right place. Our path goes past the left edge of Thoßfell, under the A72 and along the village road to Gansgrün. We walk through Gansgrün and straight on, passing a rest area on the western slope of the Rollhübel, until we meet the shoreline of the reservoir again. To get to the next village, Helmsgrün, we turn right here, turn left twice and go right again at the second opportunity. In Helmsgrün, a forest village on the Bellwitzbach stream, we keep to the left and follow the course of the bank for a while. Then, passing the sailors' campsite and the youth hostel, we cross the castle peninsula and reach Rodlera on the Aubach. The name Schlosshalbinsel (castle peninsula) is a reminder of the former Pöhl Castle, which had to be blown up during the construction of the dam. Our path leads, always following the shoreline, past the bungalow settlements of Rodlera and Neudörfel and a caravan settlement, until we reach the dam centre with a drive-in cinema, sports garden and restaurant. From the main road we are currently on, Pöhler Straße branches off to the right shortly before the dam wall. Follow it through Alt Jocketa to Jocketa and return to our starting point at the station via Dorfstraße and along the railway tracks.

images.caption: The Elster Valley Bridge near Jocketa.
Magnificent view of the Pöhl dam.
View of Altensalz and the Pöhler dam.

title: Sukkertoppen
short_description: Find coastal views just a short hike from Hamn
long_description:
Sukkertoppen is a great starter hike on Senja. From the top there are views of Hamn resort and the surrounding coastline. In the summertime, a hike up to Sukkertoppen is a fantastic way to take in the midnight sun.
There are some steep parts and some exposure towards the top including a section with a chain. The peak is quite small so hike in the morning to avoid a crowd.
The trailhead is easy to access, about 850 meters from Hamn resort with plenty of parking at the resort and by the trailhead.
The last part of the trail can be slippery and difficult in wet conditions, so avoid this hike in poor weather. There is a viewpoint about one kilometer along the trail which is perfect for a shorter hike.
Hamn i Senja, Skagi Senja and Mefjord Brygge all offer hotel rooms as well as apartments with self-catering possibilities. Each has a restaurant serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and a bar.

images.caption: Descending, with views of Hamn resort and across to Skaland.

title: Ritland Crater
short_description: Visit a 500 million year-old crater
long_description: Ritland Crater is an impact crater created by a meteorite approximately 500 million years ago. This trail leads to a viewpoint of the crater where there is a small shelter known as a “gapahuk”. The shelter features information about the crater and is a nice spot to rest and enjoy a picnic. The return trail leads down into the crater itself before returning looping back around to the beginning.

title: Bandåsen
short_description: Hike to the tallest peak of the Ryfylke islands
long_description: The steady uphill climb to Bandåsen, the highest peak on the Ryfylke Islands, provides beautiful views of the ocean, islands, and surrounding mountains.

title: Rennsteiglauf - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description: A real highlight is the GutsMuths-Rennsteiglauf, a cross-country run along the Rennsteig in memory of GutsMuths, the co-founder of gymnastics from the Goethe era. This is the largest and possibly also the most beautiful landscape run in Central Europe.
long_description:
The GutsMuths Rennsteig Run leads along the "Rennsteig" high trail in the Thuringian Forest, a romantic German low mountain range. The run is correspondingly popular: every year around 15,000 runners, Nordic walkers and hikers find their way to the starting point.
Especially in East Germany, the event, which has been taking place since the 1970s, has cult status: when the GDR still existed, the run was the largest mass sports event ever. Anyone who could claim to have taken part successfully was highly respected in sporting circles. It is no different today. Possible distances include the super marathon (72.7 km), the marathon (43.5 km), half marathon (21.1 km) and various walking and Nordic walking routes (17, 35, 50 km).

title: Flørli Staircase
short_description: Hike from the sea to the sky in Lysefjord
long_description:
4,444 - the number of stairs you will climb from the quaint village of Flørli straight up the mountain. The staircase follows the two water pipelines and the rails which used to transport a trolley full of materials and workers up and down the mountain. 
Hike a section of the staircase or challenge yourself to the entire trip. Either way, you will be in awe of the spectacular views along the entire adventure. Flørli is located in the beautiful Lysefjord and only accessible by boat.

title: Skomakarnibbå
short_description: Tackle a local favorite near Hjelmeland for 360 degree fjord and mountain views
long_description:
Skomakarnibbå is a mountain outcrop around 700 meters above the Jøsenfjord, near Hjelmeland. While it’s not possible to hike out to the outcrop itself, the trail to the plateau above is a popular hike, with 360 degree views from a nearby peak.
Skomakarnibbå and the surrounding mountain can be seen rising steeply across the fjord from the Ryfylke scenic route as you drive Road 13 east of Nesvik.
Parts of the trail are quite wet and marshy so waterproof footwear is recommended.

title: Hellandsnuten
short_description: Visit the highest mountain over Sand for panoramic views
long_description: Hellandsnuten is the highest mountain around the village of Sand, standing 747 meters above sea level. The trail to the peak is very steep in parts, so you need to best prepared for a tough ascent. From the peak there are far-reaching views of the Vindafjord and the Sandsfjord, along with a branch of the Ryfylke scenic route that winds along the coast.

title: Winter hike from Leysin to Les Fers
short_description: This easily accessible winter hike is perfect for exploring the surroundings of Leysin - whether alone, as a couple, with family or with friends.
long_description:
Fancy swapping your skis for winter boots? Leysin invites you to discover a different side to its magical winter landscape - with a hike to Les Fers (or Crête du Fer), which is particularly popular with families. This accessible and well-marked route offers a wonderful break in the midst of an enchanting natural setting.
The gentle ascent leads through a peaceful forest up to the Fers. Once you reach the top, a well-deserved reward awaits you: a breathtaking panorama of the majestic Vaud and Valais Alps. The crowning glory is a stop at the "Chalet des Fers" restaurant, where a well-earned refreshment awaits you.
After this relaxing moment, take the same relaxed route back to Leysin. An easy, sociable and unforgettable winter experience to enjoy with family or friends!

images.caption: Aerial view of the snow-covered Alpine landscape in Leysin

title: Gryteknuten
short_description: A short hike to Preikestolen’s neighbor
long_description: Enjoy this alternate hike from Preikestolhytta, Preikestolen's mountain lodge, up to Gryteknuten.

title: Places of interest around Neubulach
short_description: This family-friendly, short hike takes you to the Hella-Glück visitor mine and a great place to rest with a barbecue and large children's playground.
long_description: Our hike starts at the car park in Calwer Straße on the edge of the centre of Neubulach. The town was a mining town in the Middle Ages and has developed into a health resort in recent years. We keep to the right and come to the Silbertor, through which we reach the market square with the Vogtei, which houses a mineral exhibition. From here, the yellow rhombus as a trail marker leads us first in the direction of the visitor mine. Arriving at the mini-golf course with beer garden, we walk downhill to the right along the road to the mine. We turn left and walk along the mine's educational trail to reach the mine. Now we walk back in the direction of the minigolf course. We leave the village and head towards the forest. On meadow paths we walk to the left, always following the edge of the forest, until we finally come to the rest area with a hut, barbecue area and large children's playground. Now we walk through woods and meadows back to Neubulach, our starting point.

images.caption: Time for a rest? This mini hut invites you to do so.
There is plenty of play equipment here for the little ones.
Hella-Glück-Stollen visitor mine with asthma therapy station.
There is also a barbecue facility at this rest area.

title: Giant’s Cauldrons in Åbødalen
short_description: Giant’s Cauldrons in Åbødalen
long_description:
The Giant’s Cauldrons, known as “Jettegrytene” in Norwegian, are a family-friendly attraction in Åbødalen Valley. Over centuries the rushing water has carved holes in the rock, creating small “cauldrons”. There’s also a small waterfall to see.
The valley is a popular destination for locals on a warm summers day and at Storemyr, by the trailhead, there is a swimming and picnic area. The terrain can be wet and marshy so waterproof footwear is recommended.

title: Himakånå
short_description: Experience ‘Little Trolltunga’
long_description:
Himakånå is known by locals as "Little Trolltunga". It's more family-friendly, easier and faster to hike than its bigger brother but has similar incredible views at the top! 
Standing at only 357 meters above sea level, it's still impressive the panoramic views that the summit provides. Views include of the Nedstrandsfjord, Lysevatnet lake, country farms, pine forests, and beyond!

title: Reinaknuten
short_description: Tackle a challenging climb to this peak near Stavanger
long_description: Challenge yourself with a hike to Reinaknuten, the towering peak across the bay from Stavanger. The 5-hour round-trip hike provides incredible views of the surrounding peaks, lakes, and ocean.

title: Circuit walk in the Reci Birch Tree Reserve
short_description: Those looking for a relaxing outing just outside Brasov, while avoiding the crowds, might try Mestecănișul Reci - Reci Birch Tree Reserve. This is a place for picnicking, walking (including with the dog), exploring the flora, or cycling.
long_description:
The Reci reserve displays several routes marked with different colors depending on your preferred activity: walking, mountain-biking, or horse rding. One of the widest walking routes is called the Fairies Path. It is about 7 kilometers long, and takes you through birch and pine forests, through swampy areas, and among barley and oat crops.
Of course, one does not have to do the full circuit; and since other routes conveniently intertwine along the way, one can alternate.
Depending on the season, the route can offer some surprises if you have the patience to observe the flora and fauna. Birch trees are truly a paradise for many species of birds, and deer can be seen at the edge of the forest. There is even a rather old observatory along the way, though unmarked and harder to find. In spring, most species of plants and flowers bloom.

title: Circular tour around the Trimouns talc quarry
short_description: Moderately difficult hike around the Trimouns talc quarry with exciting views and insights!

title: Rampestreken Viewpoint
short_description: Climb to a spectacular viewpoint over Åndalsnes and Romsdalen Valley
long_description:
Rampestreken viewpoint provides a fantastic view over the valley and Åndalsnes. The locals love this hike, and they often do this for exercising to be rewarded with a magnificent, breathtaking view. It’s classified as a moderate hike, however the last part is quite steep – but manageable. 
There are several good hotels and lodges in Åndalsnes and in close proximity.
Hotel Aak is cozy accommodation located outside the city of Åndalsnes
Hotel Bellevue is found in the city center of Åndalsnes

title: Mannen
short_description: Trek from Trollstigen to Mannen for views of Romsdalen Valley
long_description:
The trail to the summit of Mannen Mountain rewards with wonderful views of the Romsdalen Valley. Mannen sits at the southern end of Trollveggen. The trailhead is located nearby the famous Trollstigen Viewpoint.
Mannen has become quite famous in Norway due to a lot of movement in the mountain and the risk of landslide. Take the trip while it’s still possible!
The hike is demanding, but could be considered relatively mild for a Norwegian mountain hike. The last section of the trail up to the summit is the steepest and toughest part.
There are several hotels, lodges, and campgrounds in and around Åndalsnes.
Hotel Aak is a cozy boutique hotel with wonderful food, located about 5 kilometers from Åndalsnes
Hotel Bellevue is the largest hotel in town and has an in-house restaurant
Trollveggen Camping has modern cabins and campgrounds, right alongside Trollveggen

images.caption: Alnesvatnet Lake. The trail leads up into the valley on the right-hand side.

title: Giglachsee Round
short_description: Easy loop around the larger of the Giglachseen lakes from the hut of the same name and with a detour to the Ignaz-Mattis-Hütte.

title: Parrot's Beak Trail in Tijuca Forest
short_description: This is one of the most famous trails of the Tijuca National Park. Bico do Papagaio is 989 meters high and has one of the most fantastic views of Rio de Janeiro.
long_description:
The Tijuca Forest é the largest urban forest in the world and is á located in the heart of the city of Rio de Janeiro. Its reforestation process began in the second half of the 19th century, by order of Dom Pedro I.
The trail to Bico do Papagaio é one of the most visited trails in the Tijuca National Park. Besides being relatively easy, it is well signposted and surrounded by beautiful forest. The trail can be considered moderate for those who are not used to steeper climbs added to the difficulty of the terrain at the end of the course. Even so, every effort is worth it. Bico do Papagaio is 989 metres high and has one of the most fantastic views of Rio de Janeiro.

images.caption: Largo do Bom Retiro no Parque Nacional da Tijuca, Rio de Janeiro - Brasil
Vista do Bico do Papagaio no Parque Nacional da Tijuca, Rio de Janeiro - Brasil
Vista do Bico do Papagaio no Parque Nacional da Tijuca, Rio de Janeiro - Brasil
Bico do Papagaio visto da Pedra do Urubu no Parque Nacional da Tijuca, Rio de Janeiro - Brasil

title: Romsdalseggen Ridge
short_description: Tackle one of Norway’s most famous ridge hikes
long_description:
Romsdalseggen Ridge is a 10.3 kilometer point-to-point hike over a famous Norwegian mountain ridge. The trail ends in the coastal town of Åndalsnes.
Romsdalseggen Ridge is consistently listed as one of the most popular hikes in Norway. The trail is a demanding, full day hike. Along the journey there are spectacular views of the Romsdalen Valley, Trollveggen, Romsdalshorn, Åndalsnes, and the fjords.
With a total elevation gain of 960 meters over rocky terrain, plus a long descent, you need to be in pretty good shape to attempt this hike. Since the trail follows a ridge, there are some exposed sections. Chains for extra grip are bolted to the rocks in the steepest parts. If you have a strong fear of heights, consider a different hike.
The hike is suitable for families, but only for older children that have hiking experience.
Weather forecast
This hike is best on a clear, sunny day. But since the clouds can move fast in the mountains, even an overcast day can offer spectacular views. With some patience, the clouds may part and reveal the beautiful surroundings.
The hike should not be attempted in bad or very windy weather. Thick fog, low clouds and rain will not only be dangerous but will ruin the views (and your day).
The Norwegian national weather service provides detailed weather reports and forecasts for Romsdalseggen in English.
Alternative hikes
There are several alternative hikes that are much easier and still have incredible views.
Litlefjellet offers great reward for effort. It is a short hike accessed from the same valley as Romsdalseggen with fantastic view across to Trollveggen, as well as Romsdalshorn and the Romsdalen Valley.
Rampestreken is a viewpoint towards the ends of the Romsdalseggen trail that can be hiked directly from Åndalsnes. It’s a steep hike up, but the metal ramp over the trees is an iconic spot for selfies.
Via ferrata
If the hike whets your appetite for more mountain fun, or if climbing is more your thing, check out the via ferrata routes on offer from Norsk Tindesenter. They have both an intro wall and a tougher wall on the western side of the mountain, near Åndalsnes.
There are several hotels, lodges, and campgrounds in and around Åndalsnes.
Hotel Aak is a cozy boutique hotel with wonderful food, located about 5 kilometers from Åndalsnes
Hotel Bellevue is the largest hotel in town and has an in-house restaurant
Trollveggen Camping has modern cabins and campgrounds, right alongside Trollveggen

images.caption: View down the valley towards Åndalsnes.
A trail section with light scrambling.

title: Fern and Water Trail
short_description: The Ácleo Águas Claras of the Cantareira State Park é a haven for those who want to escape the big city and enjoy a day in touch with nature.
long_description:
Friendly and beautiful trail to do with the whole family! The Samambaiaçu Trail is located in a beautiful stretch of preserved forest and passes through a beautiful corridor of Samambaiaçus, native species of the Atlantic Forest. Along the way, you can also observe bromeliads and orchids. The trail is well signposted and self-guided.  
The trail of the Áwaters is part of the Samambaia çu trail and this part of the route é composed of a beautiful preserved forest and several small falls of crystal clear water. Walk in silence and you may be lucky enough to spot squirrels, toucans and other species of fauna and flora.
The Ácleo Águas Claras was opened for visitation in 2000 and helps to protect an important springs area in the region. The Cantareira State Park é divided into four núcleos and was inaugurated in 1963. In 1994, it was declared part of the Green Belt Biosphere Reserve of the city of São Paulo by UNESCO.

images.caption: Trail in the Águas Claras Nucleus in the Cantareira State Park, São Paulo - Brazil
Trail in the Águas Claras Nucleus in the Cantareira State Park, São Paulo - Brazil
Trail in the Águas Claras Nucleus in the Cantareira State Park, São Paulo - Brazil

title: Around the island of Ummanz
short_description: A little away from the Baltic Sea resorts, in the west of the island of Rügen, lies the small island of Ummanz. We hike around Ummanz, along the coast and through the countryside.
long_description: We start our circular walk around the island of Ummanz at the car park behind the campsite in Suhrendorf. At the car park, we go left on a path into the forest and follow the signs "Deich-Rad-Wanderweg". At the coast at the Suhrendorf campsite, we walk left on the paved dyke path. Our hike takes us straight ahead for a long stretch on the dyke path directly along the coast. From here we have a very beautiful view of the island of Hiddensee (1). At the end of the paved dike path, we turn right onto a path and head inland back onto the road. On the road, we walk left along the road, straight ahead past the International Youth Village Ummanz. At a crossroads, we turn left towards Tankow and follow the cycle path "Rund um Ummanz". We now walk straight ahead through the forest area Wokenitzer Busch, keep to the right at the end of the forest and walk straight ahead - parallel to the coast. In Tankow we turn left into the Vorpommersche Boddenlandschaft National Park to the crane observation point (2). At the exit of the national park, we walk left on the cycle path "Around the island of Ummanz" in the direction of Waase. We walk straight ahead for a long time, past Böschow to Waase. At the large crossroads we turn left and walk along Neue Straße through Waase. We pass the National Park Office (3) and the church on the right. On our right is St. Mary's Church (4), further straight ahead we find a fish restaurant on our left. We follow the road "Am Focker Strom" straight ahead and have many beautiful views of the nearby mainland along the Bodden. We now walk through the village of Wusse and continue towards Suhrendorf. In Suhrendorf we walk straight on past the campsite (5) back to the car park.

images.caption: Across the flat island of Ummanz, the mainland can be seen in many places.
Small groups of islands lie in the Bodden waters to the east of Ummanz.
The National Park Authority in Waase provides information about the National Park Vorpommersche Boddenlandschaft with exhibitions and lectures.
From the viewing platform we can observe the fascinating natural spectacle of cranes resting.
In St. Mary's Church in Waase there is a precious carved altar from Antwerp dating from 1520.
From the dyke we have a very beautiful view of the island of Hiddensee.

title: Sonntagsspaziergang in Oberstdorf
short_description:
Eine kleine Runde am Sonntag. Tolles Wetter und genau das Richtige für alle die nicht so weit laufen möchten.
Translate to English
long_description:
Start ist an der Dummelsmoosbrücke in Oberstdorf. Parken kann man an der Straßenseite. 
Direkter Wanderweg Richtung Rubi. Du kommst am Käshüs vorbei und gehst dann weiter. Entweder du läufst komplett nach Rubi und dann am Illerdamm zurück oder du biegst bei der Hälfte ab und dann nach Oberstdorf zurück. Nach dem Campingplatz gehts dann links am Richtung Oberstdorf zurück. Ein aktuell schöner verschneiter Weg und für einen Sonntagsspaziergang genau das Richtige.
Translate to English

title: Riven
short_description: Hike an easily accessible peak, suitable as an evening hike
long_description:
With its manageable ascent, Riven might not be the tallest peak, but the view is still priceless. The elevation gain is tackled right from trailhead, and the trail will soon flatten for an easy and enjoyable hike.
Since Riven resides comfortably surrounded by taller peaks, it is sheltered from harsh winds and makes it accessible in less ideal conditions. The hike is suitable for the whole family, but youngsters should be under supervision on the exposed sections of the hike. Hiking boots or shoes with good grip are highly recommended.
Hamn i Senja and Mefjord Brygge both offer hotel rooms as well as apartments with self-catering possibilities. Each has a restaurant serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and a bar.

images.caption: Riven, the peak to the left of center.

title: Randonnée par Pic de Bertagne depuis Plan-d'Aups-Sainte-Baume
short_description:
Ce parcours vous fait prendre de la hauteur jusqu'au Pic de Bertagne, point culminant des Bouches-du-Rhône. Les panoramas sur les Alpes et la mer Méditerranée valent l'ascension !
Translate to English
long_description:
Du village Plan d'Aups-Sainte-Baume, cette randonnée en boucle emprunte les sentiers de la Sainte-Baume côté ubac en passant par le vallon de Betton par des montées successives avant de rejoindre les crêtes (GR®98).
En passant le col du Fauge, le Pic de Bertagne n'est désormais plus très loin pour profiter de magnifiques vues sur les alentours.
Le retour se fait par le GRP 2013 Marseille-Provence-Métropole au coeur de la forêt départementale de la Brasque.
Translate to English

title: Breidtinden
short_description: Hike Senja’s highest mountain peak
long_description:
Trek to the top of Breidtinden and stand on top of Senja’s highest mountain, 1,001 meters above sea level. Find 360 degree views of Senja including Barden and Segla.
Due to the difficulty of this trail, which includes some climbing and exposure along the ridge towards the top, avoid this adventure unless you’re an experienced hiker and do not have a fear of heights.
With Breidtinden’s altitude, the top can often be clouded over, so check the weather forecast before setting out. Do not hike the trail in bad weather.
The area around Breitindvatnet lake is well suited for camping, perfect for an early morning attack on the peak.
Hamn i Senja, Skagi Senja and Mefjord Brygge all offer hotel rooms as well as apartments with self-catering possibilities. Each has a restaurant serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and a bar.

title: Russehula
short_description: Hike in the footsteps of history near Mefjordvær
long_description:
This easy hike will introduce you to Senja’s exciting landscape as well as its dramatic history. Starting off from the picturesque fishing village Mefjordvær, you follow a well-laid trail to the historic Russehula, named after Russian explorers who invaded parts of the Norwegian coast in the 1300s.
Rest at Russehula and take advantage of the bonfire spot to prepare your food, or explore the giant’s kettles in the area carved into the mountain by the melting ice during the last ice age. From Russehula you can continue your hike further out to Skøytneset or the legendary site of Senja’s last witch burning, Knutskjærringa.
Weather conditions can swiftly change on the island so be prepared for wet, foggy and cold weather as well as dry. It might also be wise to invest in a map of the area you’ll be hiking in and a compass
The area around the trailhead is a great place to camp. There is not a lot of water available though, so bring plenty. Be aware that there are certain restrictions for the right to roam.
There are several accommodation options on the island of Senja, but the closest hotel to this trail is Mefjord Brygge.

title: Lonketind
short_description: A path up to heaven
long_description:
There are a lot of impressive peaks on Senja which are hard to hike but provide views that are worth the effort. Lonketind is a little different: it is not a very difficult climb, but it still gives you the amazing views of Senja and the surrounding Atlantic Ocean.
Lonketind, 848 m.a.s.l, is situated on the very southwest end of the Senja island, close to Stonglandseidet. The hike up to the top is easy with a well-defined trail and never very steep. 
Skrolsvik Kystferie is your closest accommodation option for this adventure. Alternatively, you can stay at Tranøybotn Camping which is about a 30-minute drive away. You can also choose to stay in Finnsnes which is about hour drive from the trailhead.

title: From the Hündlebahn mountain station to the Buchenegg waterfalls
short_description: Buchenegg waterfalls from the top station of the Hündleb cable car and back again.
long_description: The Buchenegg waterfalls start from the Hündlebahn mountain station. You can also start from the valley station. It is family-friendly but less suitable as a bicycle tour or with a pram. Optionally, you can walk to Steibis instead of back to the Hündle mountain station.

title: Ultratrack Supramonte Seaside - TSS
short_description: Medium route of the Ultratrack Supramonte Seaside, an outdoor event in the breathtaking landscape of the Supramonte of Baunei on the beautiful island of Sardinia.
long_description: Run on the paths of local shepherds and on old mule tracks overlooking the cliffs and discover one of the very few wilderness left in Europe.

title: Flatneset
short_description: Take in the dramatic beauty of Senja on a family-friendly coastal trail
long_description:
The island of Senja is an island of contrasts from the flat seashore to the steep, jagged mountain sides shooting up from the ocean. The family-friendly trail from Straumsnes to Flatneset takes you on an easy hike along the water’s edge and offers amazing views without demanding an exhausting climb first.
Parts of the landscape you’ll see on the way are protected under Norwegian law because of their cultural and biological significance. The nature on Senja is quite varied and described by some as a “cross-section” of Norwegian nature containing fjords, mountains, and forest, all in one place.
Weather conditions can swiftly change on the island so be prepared for wet, foggy and cold weather as well as dry. It might also be wise to invest in a map of the area you’ll be hiking in and a compass. 
There are several accommodation options on the island of Senja, but the two closest to this trail would be Hamn in Senja and Skagi Senja hotel & lodge. You can also chose to camp outdoors, just be aware that there are certain restrictions to the right to roam.
For a complete overview of accommodation possibilities and additional information for tourists on Senja, please visit Senja’s official travel guide online.

title: Tryvann
short_description: Hike up Oslo's steepest slope
long_description:
Challenge yourself on Oslo’s steepest slope climbing 407 meters over 2.7 km from the bottom of the Tryvann Ski Resort all the way to the top. This well-known course is a perfect way to benchmark your fitness, and of course, brag to your friends and family that you’ve taken on this steep and demanding route. The best in the world finish in less than 15 minutes! But don’t be discouraged; the average person does it in around 45 minutes.
Every year Oslo’s Bratteste is held here. Learn more about the race and other running races in Norway here.

title: On foot to the Alpe Bärenfalle
short_description:
An hour and a half hike uphill to the bear trap
.
long_description: From the car park at the Gschwenden waterfalls, the tour leads past the Gschwenderberg Alpe for just under four kilometres up to the Alpe Bärenfalle. The Alpsee Coaster then takes you downhill again.

title: Hiking around the Cirque de Navacelles
short_description: Superb hiking circuit to discover the cirque of Navacelles, an exceptional site in the Hérault, labelled "Grand Site de France".
long_description:
The route starts from the belvedere of the Baume d'Auriol. In the centre of this immense abyss, a promontory stands "lou puech du cayla", which has withstood the powerful erosion of the sieges. The aspacutes that gradually encompass it give it the appearance of a gigantic oyster shell.
The path of the postman allows him
The Chemin du facteur (postman's path) allows you to wind down to the hamlet of Navacelles situated at the bottom of this natural cirque formed by a meander cut by the Vis.
<Then, the path along right bank of Vis leads to Foux rise. On last few metres, a botanical old mills once powered by which gushes out cliff at this point.
The Vis is one of the last wild rivers to be labelled to better protect and preserve their biodiversity.
The return journey along the vineyard path, lined with several masets (vineyard huts), shows that not so long ago mixed farming was a necessity for living in this area.

title: Grefsenkollen
short_description: Enjoy a stunning sunset over Oslo
long_description:
Situated north of the city, Grefsenkollen provides great views of the city, fjord, Holmenkollen, and surrounding forest. At the top, you will find one of Oslo's finest restaurants, serving food and drinks, with a café terrace open during nice weather (11a.m.-11p.m.) A grassy slope is located at the front of the restaurant where you can rest and take in the view. The top of Grefsenkollen can also be your starting point for longer trips into the forest.
There are many ways to get to the top, so this route is just a suggestion.

title: Mellomkollen
short_description: Go deep into the forest for a true Nordmarka adventure
long_description:
This hike through lush Nordmarka takes you past the Øyungen lake and up to the viewpoint on top of Mellomkollen. From there you'll have great views of Oslo and the surrounding area. If you're looking for a proper adventure that's not too difficult, this one has some lovely highlights. It's the kind of hike that can keep you coming back to explore more of the forest.
Allow at least half a day for this hike. You can easily make it a full-day activity by spending some more time at the lake. Pack food and water as there are no cafés or kiosks in this area. Hiking shoes or boots are recommended as the ground can be wet and rocky.
You can also do the trail in reverse, enjoying the view before relaxing by the lake, but the climb is a little tougher.

title: Tour over the Marburg Ridge
short_description: Challenging circular tour over the Marburg Ridge with varied terrain with numerous views of the Lahn Valley and surroundings.

images.caption: View from the Friday Temple of the Landgrave's Palace in Marburg

title: Akerselva River Walk
short_description: Enjoy beautiful nature in the heart of Oslo
long_description: Akerselva, Oslo’s beautiful river, is a slice of wilderness right in the heart of the city. The river trail travels with the flowing water from Maridalen lake, just north of the city, down to the city center, through many eclectic and charming neighborhoods. This trail is popular for walking and running and is enjoyed by both locals and tourists. Start from the city center and head uphill to Maridalen, or start at the top and work your way down with the river.

title: Mørkgonga
short_description: Hike to one of the best viewpoints in Nordmarka
long_description: The hike through Mørkgonga and up to Gyrihaugen is a fun and challenging adventure located less than an hour's drive from Oslo. Capture a truly spectacular photo of the gorge before continuing to Gyrihaugen for more views.

images.caption: The viewpoint at the top of Mørkgonga.

title: Ingierstrand
short_description: Hike the rugged forest trails on the shores of the Oslofjord
long_description:
Ingierstrand is first and foremost a popular beach located on the southeast side of the Oslofjord. But what makes this location stand out, even more, is the spectacular hike located only a hundred meters from the coastline.
This hike is rugged due to lots of roots and rocks, yet is still enjoyable for a hike or run. Upon reaching the road, there are awesome views of the fjord. The hike ends at Ingierstrand Beach, so make sure to bring your swimming and picnic gear too!

images.caption: Breathtaking views of the Oslo fjord during the walk back to the beach.
The trail takes you through a thick pine forest.
Take a sharp U-turn to your right when you come to this fork, heading towards Ingierstrandveien and Strandkollen.

title: Lysaker River
short_description: Hike along the river - from start to finish
long_description:
Take a hike through history as you hike along the entire Lysaker River. Begin the trip at the river's source, Bogstadvannet, situated at 145 m.a.s.l. and end the adventure at the mouth of theLysakerfjorden, which is part of Oslofjord. The Lysaker River has been used by several mills and manufacturing facilities, since the 12th century. In modern times, the river divides Oslo and Bærum municipalities.
There are several waterfalls and small rapids, but Granfossen is the most notable waterfall, situated near downtown Lysaker.

images.caption: A local gem, a gapahuk. These are structures intended for temporary residence or for socializing.

title: Ekebergparken
short_description: Get great views of the city and sea
long_description:
Ekebergparken is a 255-acre sculpture and national heritage park that’s perfect for hiking, running or even throwing a frisbee and playing football in the open green spaces.
In short, with its excellent views of the sea and proximity to downtown, it’s the perfect place to escape into nature. There are ample viewpoints on the hike and multiple trails amongst the dense old pine forest. It’s easy to forget you’re in a city! The artwork throughout the park is found in a variety of mediums from international artists.
This hike leads you to the Ekeberg stairs, which overlooks the Langøyene, Hovedøya and Gressholmen islands of the Oslofjord. Watching the sunset here is highly recommended (in the autumn).

title: Sognsvann Lake
short_description: Wander around the lake or start an adventure deep into the forest
long_description: Located on the end of the T-bane line 5 (Sognsvann) at the northern edge of the city, Sognsvann lake is perfect for a quick dose of nature. It is a popular place all year for outdoor activities. Bring a picnic to enjoy next to the lake or splash out on a waffle and coffee from the kiosk. Play volleyball on the sand court and then jump in the water to cool off. Sognsvann is also a great spot for an easy run or to begin exploring the surrounding forest, on foot or skis.

images.caption: Sognsvann is a great starting point for runners with a large trail network.
Trails for both summer and winter.

title: Coastal cycle route: Sanary-sur-Mer -Nice
short_description: In future, a 460 km-long cycle route will pass through a variety of landscapes, from La Camargue to the Côte Bleue, via the Var coast, the Préalpes d'Azur and the Côte d'Azur. This new cycle route, which is currently taking shape, will meet up several times with its well-known counterpart, the Mediterranean by bike.
long_description:
Its ultimate goal is to link Aigues-Mortes in the Gard to Nice, crossing three major metropolitan areas: Aix-Marseille-Provence, Toulon-Provence-Méditerranée and Nice-Côte d'Azur. It will also allow you to explore the rich natural diversity of the Mediterranean hinterland.
To discover part of this future treasure, it is already possible to follow a section between Sanary-sur-Mer and Nice, known as the Parcours Cyclable du Littoral Varois in the Var and the Route des Balcons d'Azur in the Alpes-Maritimes.

title: Nøklevann
short_description: Enjoy the wide trail and picnic areas around Nøklevann lake in Østmarka
long_description:
The loop around Nøklevann lake at the edge of Østmarka is a popular route for cyclists, runners, and walkers. It’s a perfect example of how tightly Oslo is connected to nature, with many locals enjoying an evening by the lake.
The wide trail is mostly gravel and is suited to strollers. Nøklevann has several nice picnic and swimming spots. 
If this is not your first time to Nøklevann, there are many trails leading off the main path so you can easily create your own unique route as you explore.

images.caption: View of Nøklevann lake from the southern shore.
View of Nøklevann lake from Sarabråten.
Path along the eastern edge of Nøklevann lake.

title: Hochrhein High Altitude Trail
short_description: We start in the Swiss city of Basel and hike along the southernmost tip of Germany on the Höhenweg to Schaffhausen.
long_description:
Stage 1: Basel - Rheinfelden (24 km)
In Switzerland we buy some chocolate for the road and then hike above the Rhine into the forest. After Rührberg, a first steep climb awaits us, for which we are rewarded with the view at the Eigenturm. Past Degerfelden we reach Rheinfelden, which impresses with its water tower, Beuggen Castle, St. Joseph's Church and the town garden directly on the banks of the Rhine.
Stage 2: Rheinfelden - Rickenbach / Egg (19 km)
Today's stage starts off quite hilly and we should keep our strength up to withstand the steep climb to Egg. Until then, we cross a beautiful forest area and hike through an open field and meadow landscape before Wehr.
Stage 3: Rickenbach / Egg - Dogern (25.5 km)
Although there are more kilometres to cover today than yesterday, we can hope for some relaxation: Tranquil valleys and pleasant river crossings await us. At the end of the day's stage, the route runs parallel to the Alp river down to Albbruck and the Rhine.
Stage 4: Dogern - Bechtersbohl (18.5 km)
The first section of the tour is rather urban with Liedermatte, Waldshut-Tiengen and Bergstadt, but offers the opportunity to admire the meanders of the Rhine. By the time we have crossed the Wutach at the latest, we are back in the woods and meadows and only have to cross a few small hills before reaching Bechtersbohl.
Stage 5: Bechtersbohl - Lottstetten (21 km)
We continue the climb up the Schloßberg, which had already begun before Bechtersbohl, and climb the Hasle and the Wannenberg. Now it's all downhill again and past the Swiss town of Rafz. We end the short detour into Switzerland in Lottstetten.
Stage 6: Lottstetten - Schaffhausen (16 km)
We finish the Hochrhein Hiking Trail with a leisurely hike down to the Rhine, whose course we will follow on the German side to Dachsen. This is where the Hiking Trail ends, but from the station it is only a few stops to Schaffhausen, a historic town in Switzerland with many places of interest.

title: Waalweg Juval - Castelbello
short_description: Hiking from castle to castle along the picturesque Waalweg, hikers can experience the Vinschgau Valley from its most beautiful side.
long_description: This easy hike takes us along the northern slopes of the South Tyrolean apple paradise Vinschgau from Reinhold Messner's residence to the tranquil Kastelbell Castle and promises not only scenic but also cultural highlights. It begins at Juval Castle, the residence of mountaineering legend Reinhold Messner. Messner's unique art collection can be visited daily in spring (April to June) and autumn (September to November). The tour continues on an easy path past the irrigation channels of the Val Venosta fruit growers called "Waale". The tour ends at Castelbello Castle, which is well worth seeing and can also be visited on guided tours.

images.caption: Juval Castle - residence of the extreme mountaineer Reinhold Messner

title: Bogstadgård
short_description: Hike around an historic estate next to Bogstadvannet
long_description:
Bogstadgård, the historic estate and farm located alongside the lake, Bogstadvannet, was built in the late 1700s and has been home to many notable Norwegians, including merchants, councilmen, and even a former Prime Minister of Norway. Bogstadgård is now owned by the municipality of Oslo and is in cooperation with the Norwegian Museum of Culture and History. 
The beautiful grounds around the estate are popular for outdoor activities. The trails take you down to the lake and into the forest above the estate. Bring hiking boots and a picnic and enjoy a day around Bogstadgård and if the weather is nice, take a dip in the lake.

title: Hauktjern
short_description: Oslo’s eastern adventure haven
long_description:
Hauktjern is a nice small lake in Østmarka with a ridge running along the side that has some unusual rock formations.
Getting to Hauktjern is a nice hike from Ulsrud metro station and into Østmarka. Most of the hike is along a gravel road, so it is not very hard to do.
In the summertime you can expect to see lots of climbers along Hauktjern as the place has numerous options for climbing.

title: Store Åklungen
short_description: Trek into the woods north of Sognsvann lake
long_description:
This route is a quick loop into the woods north of Sognsvann lake past Lille and Store Åklungen lakes. It is a mix of wide easy paths and windy forest trails. The forest trails are well marked with blue signs. There is a good chance of seeing local wildlife including squirrels, rabbits, ducks, and birds. Both lakes have clearings by the shore for picnics and camping.
If you’re visiting Oslo, choose from one of the many hotels or apartments in the city.

images.caption: Store Åklungen lake in early May.
Path above the eastern shore of Sognsvann.
Trail between Lille and Store Åklungen in early May.

title: Traversare Azuga-Predeal prin Clăbucetul Azugii
short_description:
Parcurs ca un semicerc, traseul poate fi o variantă de circuit pentru a marca vârful Clăbucetul Azugii, aflat pe un colț al munților Baiului.
Translate to English
long_description:
Datorită înălțimii mai mult decât moderate a vârfului Clăbucetul Azugii - puțin pet 1500 de metri, cărările care duc spre el oferă mai degrabă un prilej de plimbare de dezmorțire. Vara, traseul oferă multă răcoare, iarna poate pune câteva mici piedici în funcție de câtă zăpadă a căzut și de cât de rece a fost ca să se formeze gheață.
Prima parte a traseului, dinspre Azuga, e des frecventată de drumeții amatori. A doua parte, cel puțin pe segmentul vârf - Susai, e relativ neumblată, mai ales iarna. Deși ninsese doar puțin, noi a trebuit să facem cărare prin zăpada care ajungea pe alocuri aproape de genunchi.
Translate to English

images.caption: Ultimele sute de metri, spre Predeal

title: Østmarksetra to Mariholtet
short_description: Enjoy the view of Nøklevann lake
long_description:
The hike to Mariholtet Sportsstue takes you through a lush forest and alongside several lakes. These lakes provide many opportunities to swim or to relax on a beach. While on the trail, hike past the remains of Sarabråten, a house built by businessman and philanthropist Thomas Heftye, and demolished in 1922. Some claim the Norwegian Trekking Association was even founded in the area. Either way, it’s an excellent spot to take a break and enjoy the view of Nøklevann Lake or even picnic in the large open area.
Upon reaching Mariholtet, enjoy sandwiches, pastries, and hot/cold beverages. There are toilets, running water, and outlets as well. About 300 meters towards the dam, you’ll find a gapahuk, a man-made structure made of pine branches a rope. It’s a perfect spot for a campfire or to just lounge in the shade. After the day is over where better to enjoy a hearty dinner than at the picturesque Østmarkseteren Restaurant, located at the parking lot. The trail is particularly beautiful in the winter time.

title: Embankment and Peace Boulevard with the exquisite delights of Yaroslavl
short_description: They say whoever hasn't seen the waterfront hasn't seen the real Yaroslavl. Is this true?
long_description:
Yaroslavl – the oldest city of Russia, which was laid out back in 1010 by the hand of Prince Yaroslav the Wise of Kiev. Now the original Russian city of Yaroslavl is one of the pearls of architectural, cultural heritage of Russian people.
This walking route is designed for anyone and everyone who cares so much about beauty, purity, love and order of mind. The route runs along the embankment of the Volga, one of the most beautiful rivers in the Russian landscape. The route flows from Red Square along the embankment to Strelka and then turns onto a street or streets near the same embankment to visit historic buildings, museums, educational and just plain interesting places which in modern times are on serious UNESCO lists.

title: Discover Bucharest's urban delta!
short_description: At least three routes await the curious explorer in the Văcărești Natural Park - or the Văcărești Delta. Accessible almost in any season, you can cover them either individually or by planning various combos. This walking route suggestion includes a little of each of the official routes designed by the NGO that lobbies for the park.
long_description:
The walk follows, at the beginning, the so-called "Urban Biodiversity Path". It passes through the main areas of the natural park, through different forms of vegetation, and past an area with very photogenic lakes and reeds. At least two gazebos or observatories can be climbed along the way to admire the scenery from above.
The route then goes up the concrete dyke, all the way to the Asmita Gardens residential complex. This path is often used for trail running training or by cyclists.
Next to the blocks, you descend again into the swampy area, on some wooden stairs, to enter the route called "On the valley". Many photographs stop at the gazebos you'll see along the way, to take snapshots of the sunset, with the Asmita blocks in the background.
Before ending the walk at the same point where it started, you come across an area that used to display, until a few years ago, small vegetable gardens owned by the nearby locals. The path is now safe and enjoyable, but lots of rubbish was thrown here in the past.

title: Wildcat Glades - Bluff Trail - Old Redings Mill to Castle Drive
short_description: To enjoy a picnic with the best view in Joplin, be prepared to take a short hike through the woods
long_description:
There are two picnic tables just off Wildcat Park’s Bluff Trail (see  southernmost trails on the map here), which runs along the bluff above the west side of Shoal Creek and offers breathtaking views. While hiking up from creek level is an option (a strenuous one), so is parking your car on Castle Drive and walking down to the tables (much easier).
  However, the easier option is also the trickier one, as the trail from Castle Drive to the tables is not marked. In fact, after looking around for 15 minutes by myself, I had Travis come help me (he found it right away, of course, which was a bit infuriating). So, we decided to drive from each direction and record the distance, so that we (okay, I) could find it easily next time.

images.caption: hiking trail in the United States of America: Wildcat Glades - Bluff Trail - ...

title: Barlindåsen Ridge
short_description: Get great views of Oslo and Nordmarka
long_description: A perfect hike for a clear day, Barlindåsen Ridge is a relatively easy hike with a huge reward as you look down on Oslo from the northeastern side. Whether you are walking off your weekend indulgences or trying to get in some fresh air after work, this hike is for you.

images.caption: Many great spots to eat lunch or have a snack.
View down to the Oslo Fjord from Barlindåsen Ridge.
View down to the Oslo Fjord from Barlindåsen Ridge.

title: Camping trip from Rotnes to Mellomkollen
short_description: A hiking and camping adventure just outside Oslo
long_description:
The perfect camping and hiking combination close to Oslo and easy to do in one and a half days.
Most of the trails are popular routes with plenty of picturesque hideaways. You can choose where you want to camp along the route as there are many beautiful places to pitch a tent. We recommend finding a nice lake to spend the night.

title: Water and Nature Experience Tour in the Haldertobel (audio guide)
short_description: Take an audio guide through the Haldertobel and get closer to the special features of nature and landscape.
long_description:
A guided tour on your own in the Haldertobel, the exciting biotope at the foot of the Nagelfluh chain: With the Outdooractive app and headphones, nature park ranger Florian will introduce you to the nature and geology along the mountain stream. A detour to the Derb alpine dairy gives you the opportunity to make a worthwhile stop for refreshments.
This is how the audio guide works: (Currently not yet available)
  Start point of the tour: Gunzesried
Arrival time for pilot trip 1 of the Gunzesried adventure bus: 09:01 hrs & 11:17 hrs
Tour end point: Blaichach (Bosch)
Departure time for pilot trip 1 of the adventure bus Blaichach (Bosch): 13:06 & 15:53
  Note: This tour was developed for the pilot test within the project "Flexible Adventure Bus for Sustainable Leisure Transport (FEB-NAFV)". It is therefore tailored to the timetable and stopping points of the adventure bus, which is currently not yet öffentlich betrieben. If you are interested in participating in a future pilot project in the Allgäu, please contact us at research@outdooractive.com.

images.caption: Unterwegs mit dem Audioguide-Feature von Outdooractive
Bridge over the Haldertobel near Gunzesried

title: Øyungen Lake
short_description: Camp on the shore of this beautiful lake in Nordmarka
long_description:
Øyungen lake, located on the northern side of Maridalen, is the perfect hike for adventurers of all ages. Although you’re on a well-maintained, gravel trail, you are completely immersed in nature, walking side by side the Skarselva River, which runs down to Maridalsvannet, Oslo’s main drinking water source.
Bring your canoe, kayak or paddleboard up to Øyungen Lake. There really is no limit to how far you and go and how many lakes you can explore in this region. Bring a tent and you can even paddle all the way to Hadeland.

images.caption: Øyungen Lake on a beautiful fall day.
Campground and BBQ pits at the edge of the lake.
Variety of well marked trails in the area.

title: Gjersjøen
short_description: Relaxing hike and outdoor adventure area in southern Oslo
long_description:
Enjoy a peaceful and easy hike around Lake Gjersjøen, which has a depth of more than 60 meters, and is located in the southern part of Greater Oslo Area. You’ll be surrounded by lush nature as well as an abundance of birds that flock to the area. There are ample fishing opportunities, especially for perch and pike. Many locals claim that the lake has the best tasting freshwater fish in the country! Unlike most waterways in Norway, a fishing license is not needed to fish in Lake Gjersjøen.
The lake is very clean, and it is used for supplying drinking water to around 40,000 people in the local municipalities and eventually flows into the Bunnefjorden. Recreational swimming is permitted. In the autumn, take advantage of Norway’s ‘Right to Roam’ law and go mushroom hunting around the lake. During the winter, ski on and around the northern side of the lake. If you plan to head south, make sure you bring your headlamp. If the lake is still frozen during Easter, soak up the sun while ice fishing.
This is a historic area, as there are several Stone Age settlements that were found to have lived near the water. Additionally, in 2005 a 5-meter long boat was discovered that dates back to the 1100s or 1200s.

title: Brandywine Meadows
short_description: Tough hike up to a beautiful alpine meadow
long_description:
The hike up to Brandywine Meadows is fairly short, but a very tough hike. As the hike is not the most popular hike in the area there is a chance you can get to these beautiful meadows without meeting too many other hikers. 
During summer the meadows can be covered with colorful flowers. 
It is possible to camp up there too, but there are no facilities so bring all the gear you need for an overnight stay. 
Wild camping at Brandywine Meadows is permitted

title: Easy walk on the Călimănești-Căciulata spa trail
short_description: This walking trail is ideal for children and adults alike, to be walked at any time of day, any season. You can also take your bike with you;
long_description:
Whether you're checking in at Călimănești-Căciulata or just passing through and making a stop, a relaxing walk between the two resorts will help you recharge your batteries. Rest benches placed from place to place encourage everyone to try this walk.
The route runs parallel to the national road, through the forest, and is asphalted.
Moreover, on the trail of about 2.3km you have several opportunities to catch beautiful views of the Olt Valley and Mount Cozia.
The route takes about 40 minutes one way and connects the 7th Spring in Călimănești with Hotel Traian in Căciulata. You can return on the same road. Of course, the walk is the same in the opposite direction.
The path is also known as Aleea Muncitorilor or Aleea Geniștilor/Geniului, after the unit of workers who walked the original path between 1910 and 1911 during the construction of the Hotel Traian.

images.caption: Muntele Cozia văzut de pe traseu

title: Taylor Meadows Campground
short_description: Camp on a grassy meadow with great views of Black Tusk
long_description:
This campsite not far from Garibaldi Lake is very popular during the summer. And for good reasons. These meadows are a wonderful sight with views of Black Tusk and Garibaldi Lake nearby. At the end of July and the start of August, the entire area is covered by wildflowers. 
The campground is, although not as popular at the one at Garibaldi Lake, a very well visited campground. So if you plan to tent, then make sure you book your overnight stay well in advance.

title: Three Buckets Trail, Cozla Mountain
short_description: The "Three Cauldrons" route comes in addition to the cable car ride that almost everyone tries when in Piatra Neamt. If for the locals, the route is the siesta or Sunday ride, for tourists, it can bring some pleasant surprises. Among the great advantages of this route is its year-round accessibility, including for children.
long_description:
The path to follow goes îin a straight line on the ridge of the Cozla Mountain, through a particularly beautiful deciduous forest în în în memorable images în different times of the year. The official marker shows a blue stripe, but it appears only sporadically. So it's up to you to guess the path.
&From the very beginning of the walk, you will enjoy extraordinary views of Piatra Neamt and its surroundings, and a little further on you will have the opportunity to see the Bâtca Doamnei or Ceahlăul lakes in all their splendour.
About halfway through the walk, you pass a small lake that looks more like a pond, but is nevertheless part of the ecosystem of Mount Cozla.
Stânca Trei Căldări, the final point of the walk, belongs to the protected area of the Geological Reserve of Aeolian Marshes. As there is nothing to mark this, the pond has been robbed. Its name comes from the three generous hollows whose origin is still debated. Thus, they could be the result of a karstic phenomenon, a glaciation, or the wind.
It is also interesting that excavations in the ridge area have brought to light fish fossils, on display in the city's Museum of Natural Sciences.

images.caption: End gondola station, the place to start the ride
Pig Lake or Cozla Fossil Lake

title: Mountain walk in Hakuba Valley
short_description: This route goes up the mountains in the ski fields of Hakuba Valley and provides beautiful views over the valley.
long_description: This walk goes along a small paved road up the mountain. I did the walk in autumn and it was a bit rainy. There was a very nice autumn atmosphere that you could smell and the colours of the trees were beautiful.

title: Black Tusk from Taylor Meadows
short_description: Get up close with Black Tusk from Taylor Meadows Campground
long_description:
Black Tusk Mountain is one of the most spectacular mountains in Garibaldi Provincial Park. Its jagged edges and deep black color is visible from far away and from several points along the Sea to Sky highway.
There are three main routes for hiking to Black Tusk. All three options are very long day hikes so consider staying a night at one of the nearby campsites before you do the final section up to the mountain.
This hike starts from Taylor Meadows Campground.

title: Black Tusk from Helm Creek
short_description: Get up close with Black Tusk from Helm Creek Campground
long_description:
Black Tusk Mountain is one of the most spectacular mountains in Garibaldi Provincial Park. Its jagged edges and deep black color is visible from far away and from several points along the Sea to Sky highway.
There are three main routes for hiking to Black Tusk. All three options are very long day hikes so consider staying a night at one of the nearby campsites before you do the final section up to the mountain.
This hike starts from Helm Creek Campground.

title: Helm Creek Campground
short_description: Incredible scenery of Black Tusk and the meadows around the campsite
long_description:
Enter Garibaldi Provincial Park from Cheakamus Lake to experience the northern end of this beautiful park. This campground is less used than the more known campgrounds around Garibaldi Lake and offers great views of Black Tusk and the surrounding mountains and meadows. 
Just hiking to the Helm Creek Campground is a great option, but many hikers choose to stay at the campground to hike further on to Black Tusk or Panorama Ridge.

title: Brandywine Falls
short_description: Short walk to a beautiful waterfall
long_description: Brandywine Falls can be found in Brandywine Falls Provincial Park just a few hundred meters off the Sea to Sky Highway between Squamish and Whistler. It is a very short walk from the highway to a spectacular waterfall and it is definitely a place to stop if you are driving by.

title: Wedgemount Lake
short_description: Spectacular alpine scenery
long_description:
The hike up to Wedgemount Lake in Garibaldi Provincial Park is by no means easy. It is a brutal hike ascending more than 1200 meters in only 5.5 kilometers. However, the view when you get up will make it all worth it. 
This turquoise lake is a beautiful place surrounded by an spectacular alpine scenery. In the western end of the lake you can stop at the Wedge hut. If the weather is good sit outside and enjoy the views of the lake and Wedge Mountain. If the weather is turning bad head inside to warm up a bit before you continue your hike.   
Head over to the eastern end of the lake to get some great views of Wedg Glacier.

title: From Gramais to the Kogelsee peak
short_description: Crossing the Kogelseespitze (2647m) from Gramais, the smallest municipality in Austria.
long_description: The trail leads above us first to the Kogelsee and then in easy climbing (UIAA I) over the east ridge to the Kogelseespitze. On the descent we follow the normal trail to Gufelseejöchl and Gufelsee. Then we descend on a steep path to Branntweinboden and follow the Otterbach valley back to Gramais.
