title: Stemshesten
short_description: Get a birds-eye view of the Atlantic Ocean Road
long_description:
Stemshesten and its neighboring peaks dominate the landscape near Farstad, rising steeply above the coastline. A trek up here provides a whole new perspective of the area with a natural aerial view of the Atlantic Ocean Road. The hike provides a steady climb, gaining about 500 meters in elevation over less than 3 kilometers.
For a longer and more challenging hike from the same trailhead, consider Melen.
There are varied lodging options along the Atlantic Ocean Road, with some stunning locations available.
Håholmen Havstuer is a hotel, restaurant, and pub occupying the former fishing village of Håholmen. Situated on a tiny island, the hotel is accessed by boat from Geitøya Island on the Atlantic Ocean Road.
Not far from Farstad Beach is Hustadvika Guesthouse where every room comes with a sea view.
The Atlantic Road Cabins (Atlanterhavsveien Sjøstuer) in Kårvåg offer fully self-contained cabins and camping.
Alternatively you can stay in the bigger centers, Kristiansund or Molde.

images.caption: Stemshesten in the background, with the mast, is hard to miss along the Atlantic Ocean Road.

title: From Hauzenberg to the heights of Staffelberg
short_description: The Staffelberg accompanies us throughout the hike. The heights around Hauzenberg promise us many wonderful views.
long_description: From the starting point we walk downhill through the village in the direction of the secondary school. Behind the school, we turn right into the street "Eckmühle". After a few metres, we walk into the nature trail on the left side. Information boards inform us about various topics of the forest ecosystem. At a fork we turn left and walk to the Staffelbach. The hiking trail to Lake Freudensee is well signposted. We walk between the two streams and after a short stretch through the forest we pass some fish ponds. These were mentioned in a document as the prince-bishop's ponds in 1450 and are now privately owned. We cross the through road on a small bridge and walk to the shore of the Freudensee. The centuries-old reservoir is about eight hectares in size. It was dammed to supply a hammer mill with energy by water power. Today it is used for power generation and recreation. A natural open-air swimming pool invites you to swim in summer. A 2.5 km long circular path runs around the lake directly on the shore. After visiting the lake, we might treat ourselves to a break at the Hotel-Restaurant Seehof, while the children can still stay in the playground. Finally, we continue to the right behind the hotel on a small asphalt road. Behind the subway, we hike up the slope. In front of the Staffenöd estate, we turn left onto the tarred path and hike to the edge of the forest. Here we turn right and walk steeply up the slope. From here we already have a fantastic view across a meadow orchard to the town of Hauzenberg. A few metres later, the forest that covers the Staffelberg begins. First we hike on a well-maintained path through the mixed forest. After a good 1 km, we turn right onto a path. This ascent is clearly signposted with a signpost. The waymarking on the trees consists of two horizontal bars in black and white. After a steep climb, we are on the summit ridge of the Staffelberg. After a picnic at the rest area, we climb the wooden lookout tower and enjoy the expansive view of the region. On a metal sign we read that on a clear day we can even see as far as the Großer Arber, the highest peak in the Bavarian Forest. Behind the lookout tower we go downhill again. The path is not easy to see, especially at the beginning, and we carefully walk down the slope. Soon the path widens again, the marking now consists of two white bars and the white "9". We cross a wide forest road and walk along the path until we reach the foothills of Hauzenberg. Now we hike to the right on the narrow asphalt road and turn left behind the village of Schröck. Here we continue along the road until we reach the Eckmühle. The former water mill is now a residential building. We leave the asphalt road and enter the forest on the left. We follow the Staffelbach stream to a road and turn right up to the Hauzenberg sports stadium. The Staffelstraße leads us further uphill until we reach the well-kept town centre. At the highest point we find the town's parish church, which we have already seen from Staffelberg. The church, designed as a central building, was completed in 1975. Parts of the old neo-Gothic church are still standing right next to the new building. We go inside and see a large interior, which was calmly designed with a lot of wood, bricks and exposed concrete. After the visit, we walk on the church forecourt downhill to the right through the village back to the starting point.

title: Brudesløret
short_description: Visit Brudesløret waterfall at the edge of Rondane NP
long_description:
The river Ula runs from Rondvatnet inside Rondane National Park and southwards down to Otta and the Gudbrandsdal valley. On the way, it plummets down some great waterfalls like Ulafossen and Brudesløret. 
Brudesløret is particularly beautiful, not because the waterfall is very large, but because as a backdrop to the waterfall you have the Rondane mountains.

title: Gamle Grimsa Bru
short_description: Admire the Grimsa river just a short hop from Norwegian Scenic Route Rondane
long_description:
Stretch your legs with an easy walk to Gamle Grimsa Bru (“the Old Grimsa Bridge”) near Folldal, a nice stop while travelling along Norwegian Scenic Route Rondane. You can also start a longer hike by following the river west to Fallfossen Waterfall.
The bridge was initially constructed in 1870 but demolished in 2004 due to damage by rot. The bridge you see today opened in 2005.

title: To Falkenstein Castle
short_description: We hike through the Selke valley to one of the most beautiful castles in the Harz, Falkenstein Castle.

title: Vom Parkplatz Gunzesried über den Stuiben auf den Steineberg
short_description: Eine Aussichtsreiche Tour entlang der Nagelfluhkette über den Stuiben zum Steineberg.
long_description: Anspruchsvolle Sonntagswanderung entlang der Nagelfluhkette beginnend in Gunzesried. Von hier aus geht es zuerst auf den Stuiben (1749 m), welcher seinen Namen von der Schneefahne hat, welche bei starkem Westwind vom Berg geweht wird und weithin sichtbar ist. Danach geht es abwärts auf den Steineberg (1683 m). Hier gelangt man über eine hohe Leiter auf den Gipfel. Anschließend laufen wir den Wanderweg zurück zum Parkplatz.

title: Climbing the Hohes Licht (2,651 m), Allgäu
short_description: Stand on the second-highest point in the stunning Allgäu Alps with this invigorating hike up the Hohes Licht.
long_description:
At 2,651 m, the Hohes Licht is the second-tallest mountain in the Allgäu Alps after the Grosser Krottenkopf and its ascent using this route makes for a fun and full day of hiking.
The route begins in the lush surroundings of the Rappental before bringing you up to open, grassy slopes around the Rappensee (a small lake). From there, you work your way through ever-decreasing vegetation before making your final ascent up the rocky slopes to the summit.  
Granted, things can get busy up there, as the Hohes Licht is the first peak (depending on which direction you come from) of the now rather over-subscribed Heilbronner Weg, so if you prefer fewer people on the trail,  you might want to give some extra thought to when best to go.  You just have to keep in mind that the huts start spitting out their occupants pretty early in the morning, especially during the summer. 
However and whenever you choose to visit, fantastic views are assured throughout the day (weather permitting) and plenty of calories will be burned along the way. Encounters with cheeky marmots are also pretty much guaranteed on the grassy slopes surrounding the Rappensee.

title: A trip to the Pillars of Solomon through the Temple of Hathor
short_description: A short and easy circular tour, but packed with the stunning desert landscapes that characterize Timna Park
long_description:
A beautiful hiking route that starts in front of the Pillars of Solomon through the Temple of Hathor, passes through a stunning view point on the desert and descends back through the Pillars of Solomon. One of the special routes in Timna Park, a short drive from the park's lake.
The route is not accessible to strollers for the most part because it includes stairs, the flat section is also not very comfortable for walking especially with strollers due to the nature of the terrain.

title: Ring of Kerry
short_description: It is said to be Irland’s most famous road, combining breathtaking viewpoints with a wide-ranging cultural offer: the Ring of Kerry. Going there, you can explore a charming coastline.
long_description: The Ring of Kerry – or simply “The Ring” – that’s the name of what is supposed to be Ireland’s famous tourist trail around the Iveragh Peninsula in County Kerry, South Western Ireland. On approximately 170 km you can admire romantic bays and a rugged coastline. The scenic route takes you from the small town of Killarney into the pristine and nearly unspoilt southwest of Ireland. Be it the stunning scenery of Killarney National Park or the picturesque views of the Irish hinterland from the terrific viewpoint Ladie‘s View: the Ring will leave you speechless. But there are also numerous historic sites such as Druid’s Circle, several funeral sites of the Milesians, as well as ancient fortresses along the route.

title: The Path of Sculptures (Wasp Forest / President's Forest)
short_description: A magical road through the wasp forest at the foot of the Jerusalem mountains for a length of about 8 kilometers. Scattered along the road are sculptures that were carved in the rocks by artists according to the spirit of the place and blend harmoniously with the local landscapes.
long_description:
The Sculpture Road in the Wasp Forest crosses it along its entire length, as the name of the road suggests, dozens of environmental rock sculptures designed by various artists can be found all along the road. The way can be done on foot (or also by car). This is a linear route and therefore the calculated distance and walking times are one way.
** Since this is a route, the distance lines and the calculated walking times are in one direction.

title: Hesten
short_description: Get that famous shot of Segla
long_description:
Hesten is Segla’s neighboring mountain and where most of the popular photos of Segla found on Instagram are taken.
Much like Segla, Hesten has a sharp drop into the fjord below, but doesn’t reach quite as tall, at 556 meters above the sea. Apart from Segla, Hesten delivers wonderful views over Mefjorden to the west, and Inste Kongen Mountain and Korkedalen Valley to the north.
The trail is very popular and you can expect to hike in a queue and meet many people at the top, regardless of the season. If you have a fear of heights, consider stopping on the ridge between Hesten and Stavelitippen, about 100 meters below Hesten’s peak, which still provides a great view of Segla and Korkedalen.
Hamn i Senja, Skagi Senja and Mefjord Brygge all offer hotel rooms as well as apartments with self-catering possibilities. Each has a restaurant serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and a bar.

title: Lower Gaisalpsee
short_description: The hiking tour from Reichenbach to the lower Gaisalpsee is perfect for nature lovers and those who like to cool off after a hiking tour.
long_description: You start directly at the car park in Reichenbach. And directly there you start the tour to the lower Gaisalpsee. It is easy to walk, but sturdy shoes are required. Once you reach the top, you can cool off in the lake before walking back. You could also start from there to the nearby Obere Gaisalpsee or for a larger tour directly to the Rubihorn.

title: Around the Mafate Valley (GR R3) - Stage 2
short_description: Stage 2: From Aurère to Cayenne
long_description: On the second stage of the circumnavigation of the Mafate basin on the GR R3 route, we explore the north of the basin. From Aurère we go through the valley of Bras d´Oussy with its steep, forested slopes. At the ridge of Bord Bazar and on the flanks of Piton Tortue we can enjoy wide views over the mountains, valleys and hills of the Mafate basin.

title: England Coast Path - Whitehaven to Silecroft
short_description: This route is part of the England Coast Path National Trail.
long_description:
The 51.9 km (32.2 miles) stretch of the England Coast Path (ECP) from Whitehaven and Silecroft is now open to the public. 
  The England Coast Path is happening because of a completely new right of access that gives everyone the legal right to explore our coast for the very first time. It is much more than just a path, it gives access to beaches, cliff-tops, and most of the wonderful habitats around our coast. You can see the open sections and how they relate to the other National Trails here.
  Coastal sections of existing National Trails will become part of the England Coast Path in time. This will give the Trails better protection when the coast erodes. The Trails won't lose their own identities though, they will still be National Trails in their own right and the signage will be the same, but you may see new signs saying 'part of the England Coast Path'.
  You can find out about the other National trails on the official National Trail website.

title: The Lower and Upper Stoeven Falls
short_description: A short hiking route that will take you to the foot of the lower Steuben Falls in the Tyrol region as well as the upper Steuben Falls
long_description:
The first part of this itinerary is relatively simple, short and easy, and it will take you to the foot of the chain of the stunning Stoeven Falls, also a few more meters of walking (slight uphill) will lead you to a path for observing the falls from above, as well as to other waterfalls that cannot be seen from the foot of the path.
Later, the path becomes less organized and it goes up a relatively short climb (but a little challenging for those who are not in good shape) towards a great observation deck on the upper Steiben waterfall. From here you can choose between three options: 1. Return the same way back. 2. Continue with the road a little longer and make the road circular via "Ministersteig" from which there is a great view of the valley and it includes walking on a fantastic suspension bridge. 3. Continue walking up to the bridge connecting Lake Plen and Lake Heiterwanger and then back through the suspension bridge specified in option number 2.
Click here to view the route that groups all the segments of the trip .
Only the first part of this route is accessible for walking even with strollers (at the foot of the waterfalls and the observation path).

title: Keipen
short_description: A panoramic view and great opportunity to see the midnight sun
long_description:
From the top of Keipen, one can enjoy a great view over Ørnfjorden, Husøy, Segla, Barden, Grytetippen and Breidtinden. From the top of the peak, it is also a great place to see the evening and midnight sun. Keipen is located near Grytetippen so it is possible to conquer both of the peaks in one day.
The trip is not especially open before you reach the top. It is quite a steep climb the entire trip, so one should be in decent shape before taking on this adventure.

short_description: हैदराबाद के शहरी वातावरण के बीच में मौजूद यह मार्ग एक सुन्दर और अन छुई नेचर ट्रेल है जो की हरेभरे यापाल रिज़र्व फारेस्ट से हो कर गुजरता है।
long_description: यापाल रिज़र्व फारेस्ट एक संरक्षित जंगल है जो की रंगा रेड्डी जिले के मुख्य शहर हैदराबाद में स्थित है। पेड़ों और हरियाली से भरे हुए इस जंगल में हाईकिंग करना एक अच्छा अनुभव है। यह ट्रैक 14 किलोमीटर लम्बा और आसान/मध्यम कठिनाई स्तर वाला है। ट्रेल मार्ग में कुछ उतार चढाव हैं लेकिन फिट और अनुभवी हाइकर्स को कोई खास दिक्कत नहीं होनी चाहिए। कुछ पक्षी और जानवर दिखने की संभावना भी है। यह ट्रेल की जानकारी अभी ज्यादा हाइकर्स को नहीं है, इसलिए इस अनछुआ मार्ग के प्राकृतिक परिवेश की खोज करने का अपना एक अलग मजा है।

title: Grytetippen
short_description: One of the best places to see the midnight sun on Senja
long_description:
To many, Grytetippen is a favorite hike on Senja and it is not difficult to understand why! At the top, you can enjoy an impressive view over Ørnfjorden, Husøy, Segla, Barden, Keipen and Breidtinden.
Grytetippen is an incredible place to check out the evening and midnight sun.
The the hike isn’t particularly dangerous before you reach the top, but be aware of the steep cliffs on the along ridge line at the top. It is quite a steep climb along the entire hike so it is recommended to be in decent physical shape to climb Grytetippen. 
Hamn i Senja, Skagi Senja and Mefjord Brygge all offer hotel rooms as well as apartments with self-catering possibilities. Each has a restaurant serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and a bar.

images.caption: Views from Grytetippen with Segla peaking up to the right

title: Inste Kongen
short_description: Bring home an amazing shot of the King’s bridge
long_description:
There is no shortage of great photo opportunities on Senja and Kongeporten (The King’s bridge) on the way up to Inste Kongen is easily one of the most instagrammable spots on the island. Throughout the hike up to Inste Kongen, you will be surrounded by the spectacular scenery of the mountains and fjords which continue all the way north of Senja.
Be aware that this is a very demanding hike with lots of loose stones, unstable footing, and steep cliffs. The hike does not follow a marked trail, so study the map carefully and know exactly where you are going before embarking on this adventure.
Hamn i Senja, Skagi Senja and Mefjord Brygge all offer hotel rooms as well as apartments with self-catering possibilities. Each has a restaurant serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and a bar.

title: Igniș Peak through the Chiuzbăii Caves
short_description: One of the hiking trails close to Baia Mare, preferred both by locals and tourists, the climb to Igniș rewards the hiker with superb views of the Gutâi plateau and Baia Mare.
long_description:
The Igniș relay is easily seen from the city and you can reach it in any season. There are several trails up the Ignis peak. It passes through the Chiuzbaia Fossiliferous Reservation and the place called Groapele Chiuzbăii. An easier route, some say, would be the climb from the Izvoare resort.
The route starts from the Tău Roșu quarry and follows a wide forest road to Groapele Chiuzbăii.
A trail junction marks the change of markings, and the route continues on the blue dot (the alternative is also a red triangle, but it bypasses).
Bourbon lovers have the opportunity to refill a bottle from the întâlnit spring shortly after the change of marker. From here, the path also becomes steep and leads to a stable area. Cross the lonely and imposing rock known as Piatra Dracului and, after a little effort, emerge into the alpine hollow.

title: Cuqueron's vineyards
short_description:
This loop from the heights of Cuqueron, passes over sunny hills, covered with steep vineyards, and dotted with large imposing farms.
In the heart of the Jurançon vineyard, it will allow you to cross the prestigious estates and closures.

title: Around the Mafate Valley (GR R3) - Stage 4
short_description: Stage 4: From Roche Plate to Marla
long_description: The fourth stage of the circular hike around the Mafate basin has some impressive natural features to offer. We reach the higher altitudes of the valley basin, which allows us to enjoy impressive distant views in many places. For long stretches we walk along the river Rivière de Galets, which has carved a narrow gorge into the rock. Finally, we arrive at Marla, the highest village in Mafate, through wide fields of scaffolding.

images.caption: The village of Marla in the south of Mafate, on the left the peak of the Grand Bénare

title: Around the Mafate Valley (GR R3) - Stage 3
short_description: Stage 3: From Cayenne to Roche Plate
long_description: The third stage of the Mafate circuit leads us along the western edge of the basin from north to south. The steep rock face that marks the edge of the basin always towers above us. In the course of this stage, the terrain rises sharply in places and we hike more and more towards the higher, southern reaches of Mafate. The small settlements of Îlet des Lataniers and Îlet des Orangers, which nestle against the mountain on their small plateaus below the rocky walls, are also a highlight on this section.

images.caption: View of the Mafate valley basin

title: From Plauen to the Pöhler Dam
short_description: In the unspoilt nature of Vogtland Switzerland we hike past Jößnitz Castle through the Lohbach Gorge to the dam in Pöhl.
long_description: Our hike begins in the street "Am Stadtwald" in the north of Plauen. We cross the tracks and turn left into the street "Am Essigsteig". Instead of following the road to the right, we choose a small shortcut diagonally right through the forest. This brings us to the road "Nach dem Stadion", which runs between the Haselbrunn open-air swimming pool and the Vogtland Stadium. Behind the sports facilities, our path leads to the left, following route "J6", through the beautiful Plauen city forest with nature trail. We pass a refuge and arrive in Jößnitz. There we first turn right into Beethovenstraße and then via Musikantenweg into Gluckstraße, which we follow to the right into Richard-Wagner-Straße. Here we turn left into Wilhelm-Külz-Straße, which takes us to Rohrweg. There we have a great view of our next destination, Jößnitz Castle, which is perched on a rocky spur high above the town. The ascent via Bahnhofstraße and Schloßstraße is rewarded with a magnificent view. From here we can overlook large parts of the Vogtland. Our path now changes to the route marked "J8" and leads along Fabrikstraße and Röttiser Straße in the direction of Lohbachschlucht. Shortly before the first houses of Dobra, we turn left and walk along above the Lohbach stream until we meet the Döhlaubach stream, which we follow down to the Barthmühle mill. With our next destination - the imposing Elstertal bridge - already in sight, we cross the river Weiße Elster here. Over a footbridge along the railway line we come into the Triebtal, the core area of "Vogtland Switzerland". We follow the course of the Trieb against the direction of flow and after about two kilometres we reach the dam wall of the Pöhl dam. If you like, you can make a detour to the "Mosenturm" (mosque tower) on the Eisenberg and take another look over the dam to the Oberland. However, we always follow the route "J8" to the boat landing stage and further along the dam. At the edge of the forest, we turn right and then left again, moving away from the shore of the reservoir. Near the sewage treatment plant we meet the road to Möschwitz, but immediately leave it again to the right in the direction of Lochhaus. Along a meadow path with resting places we come to the "Lochbauer", an old Vogtland three-sided farmstead. This historical monument is now an inn where we can fortify ourselves for the way back. A service road leads us from there to the "Vogtländisches Umwelt- und Naturschutzzentrum Pfaffengut" (Vogtland Environment and Nature Conservation Centre Pfaffengut) and along Pfaffengutstraße, past an industrial estate, towards our starting point. At the end of Pfaffengutstraße, we turn left into Seumestraße and return to our starting point in the street "Am Stadtwald" via the street "Althaselbrunn" on the right.

images.caption: The Elster meanders through the Vogtland.

title: Mt Ogatsura Yuzuka Ridge Course
short_description: The large cliffs and sheer rocky peaks formed by granite make Mt Ogatsu a favourite destination for climbers from all over the country. This course is one of the most common of the many trails, but it is for advanced climbers with many ladders, ropes and crossings. Even so, the views from the top of the huge rocks and near the summit are spectacular. The sense of achievement after overcoming a number of difficult sections and reaching the summit is immeasurable.
long_description:
Ogurazan is a mountain located in the Grandmother Incline National Park in northern Miyazaki Prefecture. Formed by granite intrusions during the Miocene Tertiary period, it is dotted with many rocky peaks and rock walls that have been subjected to severe erosion and is said to be Kyushu's last unexplored region. It is a popular mountain, visited not only by locals but also by climbers from all over Japan, and this course is one of the most common trails in the Ogatsu Mountains. Even though it is the most popular course for climbers, the fact is that there are many difficult sections in exchange for the real pleasure of the powerful rocky peaks and rock faces of Aizureyama. You have to use ladders and ropes many times to reach the summit. Also, the section where the Shukuko River is crossed becomes impassable when the water level rises, so check the weather report before climbing the mountain. This is definitely an advanced mountaineering course, so if you are unsure, it is safe to aim for the summit with an experienced climber.
At the Sode Daki viewpoint on the way up, you can see the Kozumi Daki rock face, Boju Ridge and the rocky peak of Yukuzuka. At the branch before Shimowaku-zuka, there is a short-cut path to the summit that takes you through Shimowaku-zuka and Naka-waku-zuka, so choose according to your fitness and time. Each of the viewing spots has a good view, but there are steep cliffs at the foot of the mountain. Avoid slipping and falling off the cliffs while you are too engrossed in the scenery or taking photos.
From the stone mound in front of the summit, you can see Mt Kuju, Mt Aso, Mt Grandmother, Mt Kakizan, Mt Yufudake and Mt Kirishima. Also, near the summit, akebono azaleas are at their best during the fresh green season, with their pretty pink flowers.

title: Ås til Åsleden - Krika Skog to Klåveröd
short_description: The third stage of the s til Åsledens goes from Krika Skog to Klåveröd.
long_description: On this stage, too, the trail leads mainly through the forest. We walk along narrow paths past eerie-sounding places such as Vargadalen (Valley of the Wolves), Snuvestuan (Siren's Cave) and Skorstensdalen (Valley of the Chimneys). Finally, a gravel path leads to the highest point in Schonen, at 212 m, between Gålarp and Magleröd, and on to the Klåveröd recreation area, where small lakes and streams invite you to linger. Our destination is on the shore of the small lake Svartesjön.

title: Trip to Gaishöll-Wasserfälle
short_description: A short and easy hiking route leading to Gaishöll Wasserfälle, the highest in the Black Forest.
long_description:
A hiking route in the northeast of the Black Forest leading to Gaishöll Falls which descend from a height of 150 meters and are considered to be the highest waterfalls in the Black Forest ! The total length of the falls is 600 meters and they flow in the heart of a magical green forest.
** The distance and walking time shown are for one direction.

title: Hiking near Baia Mare - Piatra Bulzului
short_description: One of the most popular hikes near Baia Mare is the climb to the rock known as Piatra Bulzului. Not an easy hike, but at the finish point you'll be rewarded with stunning views.
long_description:
The path climbs mostly through the forest, where beeches alternate with wild cherries and maples. At first, the ascent is permissive, but it gets steeper and steeper in the second half; huge boulders spring up here and there along the route.
The blue stripe marking is visible and alternates with the orange stripes that denote a private property.
After about 2 hours from the start, you reach Poiana Bulzului; Piatra Bulzului - the massive rock - is somewhere to the right. In good weather, generous panoramas open towards the artificial Friza lake, the town of Blidari, and the peaks of the Igniș massif. This detail encourages some to consider Piatra Bulzului as one of the most beautiful places in Maramureș.
To descent, you can take the same route; alternatively, return to the path, cross Poiana Bulzului to the groups of rocks stretched along the ridge, and look for a forest road on your right. This variant is not marked and emerges about 1 km upstream of the starting point.

title: International long-distance hiking trail Donnersberg/Palatinate - Donon/Alsace (German section)
short_description: In the middle of the Pfälzerwald Nature Park, the largest contiguous forest area in Germany, we hike from the Donnersberg to the border with France.
long_description:
We start our multi-day tour at the Forsthaus/Pfalz and hike through shady forests up to the Donnersberg. The 27-metre high Ludwig Tower on the Donnersberg affords one of the most magnificent views over the Palatinate mountains, the Alzey hills and the Rhine plain.

We leave the Donnersberg and walk down to Falkenstein, which also holds the title of "Most Beautiful Village in the Palatinate". The picturesque village leaning against a high cliff is overlooked by the ruins of "Falkenstein" Castle. The trail continues through the Falkenstein valley to Winnweiler in the Alsenz valley. Those interested in mining should make a detour here to the Palatinate Mining Museum in Insbach and the "Weiße Grube" visitor mine.

Our next stage destination is Kaiserslautern, which should not only be worth a trip for football fans. A stroll through the old town takes you past buildings such as the imperial palace of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, the collegiate church, the largest late Gothic hall church in south-western Germany, or Casimir Castle, the former Renaissance castle of the hunter from the Electoral Palatinate.

Our hike continues past the Fritz Walter Stadium back into the Palatinate Forest to Trippstadt. Behind Merzalbern we hike into the beautiful Lautertal valley, which leads us into the Dahner Felsenland, the largest red sandstone rock landscape in Europe. Behind Nothweiler we reach the border to France. If you want to hike even further, the trail takes you up to the Donon in Alsace, which is over 1000 metres high.
Text: Landesamt für Vermessung und Geobasisinforamtion Rheinland-Pfalz

title: Fall Creek Falls State Park
short_description: Fall Creek Falls State Park is the largest and most visited park in Tennessee. Its appeal is largely centered on the 256-foot waterfall, Fall Creek Falls, but a few small waterfalls, streams, gorges and greenery in the park make this hike a paradise for nature lovers.
long_description:
Fall Creek Falls State Park is one of Tennessee’s largest and most visited state parks. The park encompasses more than 26,000 acres sprawled across the eastern top of the rugged Cumberland Plateau. Laced with cascades, gorges, waterfalls, streams and lush stands of virgin hardwood timber, the park beckons those who enjoy nature at her finest. Fall Creek Falls, at 256 feet, is one of the highest waterfalls in the eastern United States. Other waterfalls within the park include Piney Falls, Cane Creek Falls and Cane Creek Cascades.
At 256 feet, Fall Creek Falls is the highest free-fall waterfall east of the Mississippi River. The falls are located near Spencer, Tennessee in Fall Creek Falls State Park. A short trail leads from the parking lot atop the plateau down to the base of the gorge, giving access to the waterfall's plungepool. When water flow is sufficient, Coon Creek Falls shares a plungepool.

title: Madonnastien
short_description: Family-friendly hike to the Madonna statue in Trillemarka
long_description:
The Madonnestien trail is different than any other trail in Norway. The trail is really easy to hike thanks to the stones laid out by Nepalese sherpas in 2016 and at the end of the trail you will find a statue of Madonna. 
The statue is a gift from a local forest owner that passed away in 1995. The statue symbolizing peace was created in Vietnam and raised in Trillemarka in 2009. 
Mandonnastien has become one of Norway's most popular trails and can easily be hiked by the entire family.

title: Ysperklamm
short_description: A one-way trip, rich in water, in the stunning Isper Gorge in Lower Austria.
long_description:
A great hiking route that passes through the Isper Gorge, which is considered the largest of its kind among the gorges in this region. Many points of interest await you along the route, such as wooden bridges, waterfalls, animals and more.
The length of the route is about 2 km (one way) and walking it includes a cumulative ascent of about 280 meters which also includes climbing several stairs (therefore the route is not accessible to strollers or wheelchairs). Due to the fact that the route is linear, the walking time and the distance shown on this page are for one direction only, but at any point on the route you can retrace the steps back to the beginning of the route.

title: Deventer city route
short_description: During this city route you will not only discover Deventer's city centre. You will also walk through the Douwelerkolk. This is a beautiful nature area close to the city centre.
long_description:
Deventer is one of the oldest cities in the Netherlands. In the ninth century, the city was already named in found paperwork. Later, Deventer became an important trading city for trade with Germany. This is of course due to its location on the river IJssel. 
On the market square, you will find many monumental buildings that were built when Deventer was a real trading city. These include the weighing house and the town hall.
In Deventer, religion was also very important. Consequently, several churches can be found in the city. During this route you will walk past the Lebuïnuskerk and the Broerderenkerk. 
During this route you will also walk through the Douwelerkolk nature reserve. This nature reserve is a remnant of the IJssel arm. Due to the many groundwater you will find beautiful plants. 
.

title: Ascent to Puy Mary from the Pas de Peyrol
short_description: The ascent of Puy Mary is an itinerary accessible to a relatively large public, which allows you to enjoy a splendid panoramic view of the Auvergne Volcanoes Park from the summit!
long_description:
The ascent is via stairs and a very well-maintained path.
The 2nd part from the small platform is on a significantly steeper slope.
At the summit (1783 m), you will enjoy a 360° view of the Auvergne Volcanoes Regional Natural Park and its glacial valleys. An orientation table will allow you to locate the surrounding peaks.
For the less athletic <For the less athletic, there is possibility of going back down same path. For more experienced walkers, continue on ridge and then turn left to return a pretty path side mountain.

title: Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve
short_description: Great hiking near downtown San Diego
long_description:
Just north of San Diego, you'll find the small Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve. The reserve is situated along the coast and it is a perfect place for some family-friendly hiking. The great views of the ocean coupled with spending some time at the beach itself make this a great afternoon adventure. 
The reserve features high broken cliffs and deep ravines on headlands overlooking the ocean. There are multiple trails in the area, so you can easily add other trails to this adventure to make it longer.

title: England Coast Path - Maldon to Salcott
short_description: This route is part of the England Coast Path National Trail.
long_description:
The 42.7 km (26.5 miles) stretch of the England Coast Path (ECP) from Maldon to Salcott is now open to the public. 
  The England Coast Path is happening because of a completely new right of access that gives everyone the legal right to explore our coast for the very first time. It is much more than just a path, it gives access to beaches, cliff-tops, and most of the wonderful habitats around our coast. You can see the open sections and how they relate to the other National Trails here.
  Coastal sections of existing National Trails will become part of the England Coast Path in time. This will give the Trails better protection when the coast erodes. The Trails won't lose their own identities though, they will still be National Trails in their own right and the signage will be the same, but you may see new signs saying 'part of the England Coast Path'.
  You can find out about the other National trails on the official National Trail website.

title: Trail of Pedra da Marcela
short_description: With a spectacular view of the coast and all the wonders of the region, the Pedra da Marcela Trail challenges its visitors because it is steep and requires a good physical preparation.
long_description:
Parking the car in a grassy area near the Furnas gate, which is always closed, and walking for about 2km. It may seem like a short trail, especially because the road is paved, but the trail is very steep and tiring. It is climbed for about 35 minutes, stopping to rest a few times. There is no infrastructure on site, nor bathrooms. Therefore, take water, repellent, coat, and other equipment you find necessary.
On reaching the summit of Pedra da Marcela one can contemplate an incredible view of the coastline and the entire surrounding region, where on clear days you can see Angra dos Reis, Paraty, Ilha Grande and the ocean.Some people go up in the late afternoon with all the necessary equipment to camp up there and enjoy the sunrise over the sea, a true spectacle of nature and an unforgettable experience.

title: Wallenstein-Tilly-Weg
short_description: The Wallenstein-Tilly Trail is maintained by the Oberpfälzer Waldverein and connects seamlessly with the Albquerweg (Fränkischer Albverein) from Nürnberg. We hike in the footsteps of Johann t’Serclaes von Tilly through the valleys of the Vils and Naab to the Upper Palatinate Forest and to the Czech border crossing at Tillyschanz.
long_description: The Wallenstein-Tilly Trail begins in Pruihausen and leads first to Boden and Oberweißenbach. It continues on a hill path and then descends into the valley of the Vils, which we ücross to reach Vilseck, with Dagestein Castle. We leave the town and after a short while hike on sandy paths through a large forest area to Seugast in the Vils valley. In the varied landscape, past Massenricht and über Tannhof, we reach the village of Kohlberg. After a small southern turn, the route climbs up the Schwarzberg and continues on the densely wooded slope üheber den Bergel. We pass Neudorf bei Luhe on our right and then reach Luhe-Wildenau in the Naab valley. Now we follow the meandering river meadows of the Luhe to Leuchtenberg and see the castle ruins of the same name. Via Steinach and Obernankau we hike to the Kaltenbaumbächlein and meet the Pfreimd, which we follow upstream. We change banks twice and pass Böhmischbruck. At Grünhammer überqueren we cross the Pfreimd again and then leave it to reach the Tröbesbach to the east via Ödpielmannsberg. Passing several small settlements, we now orient ourselves along the stream and reach Tröbes. At the natural open-air swimming pool, shortly after the village, we finally turn our backs on this stream and hike through a large forest area via the Katzenbühl to Eslarn - the economic and tourist gateway to Böhmen. From here it is only a stone's throw to the border hamlet of Tillyschanz, the destination of the Wallenstein-Tilly Trail. In the 17th century, fortifications were built here to protect against Böhmen, but only a few ruins remain.

title: Tverråsen
short_description: Magnificent hike in the woods around Drammen
long_description: Tverråsen will show you the best parts of Drammensmarka. You will find some beautiful trails and forest areas. And you get to enjoy a magnificent view of Drammensmarka and the areas further east. You will also be able to spot Knabben from here.

images.caption: Tverråsen sett fra andre siden av Tverråstjernet
Bekk på vei fra Nerdammen til Tverråsen

title: Picturesque road trip through the Maramureș of yore
short_description: This road trip takes you through one of the most idyllic landscapes in Maramureș, and also in Romania. You will ride through what's known as Ţara Chioarului, passing through Cavnic mountain resort, heading towards Valea Cosăului and, further on, to Valea Izei.
long_description:
While in this area of Maramureș, take your time to notice a few exemplary preserved traditional elements. From village to village, from wooden church to wooden church, you have the opportunity to admire not only some of the most beautiful examples of craftsmanship but also take a glimpse of local life. And if you happen to do this road trip on a Sunday or on a religious holiday, you will surely see a parade of folk costumes on the streets of the communes, because Maramureș is one of the few areas in Romania where the traditional costume is still worn with holiness.
The route passes through several picturesque localities such as Săliștea, Bârsana, Strâmtura, but also through former dull mining towns, such as Cavnic. Along the way, you'll find little parking spots to stop for enticing panoramas over the valleys. You can also deviate from the road to other popular villages such as Breb or Poienile Izei.
This route will probably feel like food for the soul, an opportunity to admire the Maramures landscape, and the way in which these places, seemingly frozen in time, have nevertheless adapted to the current times.

title: Reykjadalur
short_description: Swim in a hot river
long_description: Hiking to the Reykjadalur Hot Springs is one of the best hikes near Reykjavik. It is certainly not a hidden gem anymore but despite lots of other tourists here, you should not skip this hike to the Reykjadalur Hot Springs, which is more of a river! You can decide how warm you want the water as more and colder water blends in and gives you the option to go from anywhere from 40°C and down to 10-15°C.

images.caption: Great views of Drammensfjorden and Oslofjorden.
The forest is pretty much perfect along the top.

title: Hiking Route from Lecco train station to mountain hut Rocca Locatelli
short_description: This hiking route goes from Lecco train station to the mountain hut Rocca Locatelli at the Grigna Mountain

title: Schlösser und Seen Runde von Füssen nach Schwangau
short_description:
Diese beschauliche Rundtour führt von Füssen übern Schwanensee nach Schwangau zu den Königsschlössern. Die Tour bietet atemberaubende Ausblicke auf Seenlandschaften und Schlösser.
Translate to English
long_description:
Der Weg beginnt in der Nähe von Füssen auf einem Parkplatz nahe der Straße. Nachdem man dem Rad und Fußweg gefolgt ist biegt man in den Wald ab wo man Richtung Schwanensee wandert. Hier hat man schöne Ausblicke auf den schön gelegenen Schwanense mit seiner diversen Flora und Fauna. Von hier aus geht es weiter zum nächsten See, den kleinen Alpsee. Dieser bietet wunderschöne Ausblicke auf die Königsschlösser. Auch die Wasserqualität lässt nichts zu wünschen ürbig. Hier empfiehlt sich an heißen Tagen die Badehose oder den Bikini auszupacken. Der Weg führt entlang des Seeufers bis man nach ein paar hundert Meter links abbiegt und sich einem Waldpfad folgend stetig bergauf begiebt. Dort oben wird man mit einem einzigartigen Ausblick auf den Schwanensee und dem Schloss Hohenschwangau mit dahinter liegenden Forggensee belohnt. Danach geht es in Richtung Schloss Neuschwanstein und schlussendlich bergab auf den Hauptweg der zum Schloss Neuschwanstein führt. Bei den Hauptbesucherparkplätzen vobei geht es weider zurück zum Ausgangspunkt, dem Parkplatz bei Füssen.

title: Tverken
short_description: Hike to Drammen's most famous forest cafe
long_description:
Tverken is the perfect stop for a Norwegian waffle or a bolle(sweet bun) when adventuring in Drammensmarka.
Tverken offers bakeries and other things to buy when you have been hiking to Tverråsen or skiing the many ski trails around this area.
Opening hours
Tverken is usually open from 10-15 every Saturday and Sunday except for July.

title: Around the Mafate Valley (GR R3) - Stage 5
short_description: Stage 5: From Marla to the car park at Col de Bœufs
long_description: On the last stage of the GR R3 around the Cirque de Mafate, the natural beauty of the valley basin is presented to us one last time as if on a silver platter – a primeval forest of tamarind trees;a steep climb up a mountain ridge and a last panoramic view of the craggy basin of Mafate, before we set off for home again with numerous new impressions and experiences in our luggage.

title: Walking around Bauduen
short_description: Very nice hike along the lake of Sainte-Croix and then allowing you to get some height on the hill of Défens. This is a must if you are visiting the Verdon Regional Natural Park!
long_description:
From the pretty village of Bauduen, the trail drops down to the GR99B and rather pleasant along the turquoise waters of the Sainte-Croix lake. A few technical passages are also worth noting to challenge yourself.
After the intersection of the two long-distance trails, the second part of the route is in the forest. At the highest point of the hike, there is a beautiful view of the lake of Sainte-Croix and the typical landscapes of the Haut-Var.
For the last part of the hike, you will be able to see the lake of Sainte-Croix. <To finish, we quietly reach the village of Deacute;part by walking about 7 km.

images.caption: View from the village of Bauduen

title: Hike to La Bourgeoise from Col de Joux Plane
short_description: Discover this short hiking route with spectacular views of the Alps, from alpine meadows to rocky ridges!
long_description:
The hike to La Bourgeoise from the Col de Joux Plane combines natural beauty with moderate challenges. It starts from the Col de Joux Plane, at around 1700 m altitude, an ideal starting point with panoramic views of the surrounding valleys. The pass is accessible by car and parking spaces are available.
The trail begins gently through lush green meadows. This section is perfect for warming up and enjoying the colorful wildflowers and mountain panoramas. You may spot marmots and chamois in this area, adding a touch of wildlife to your hike.
As you progress, the trail becomes steeper, leading you through rocky terrain. The climb becomes more sustained, but the exceptional panoramas of the surrounding peaks and valleys below are a source of motivation. You pass through sparse forests offering moments of cool shade before reaching the open ridges.
The final section before reaching the summit of La Bourgeoise is more demanding, with rocky terrain requiring good stability. However, the breathtaking views of the Alps and the peaks of the Giffre massif are a great reward. Once you've reached La Croix de Mapellet, it's the perfect place for a break, a picnic or simply to admire the majesty of the mountains (orientation table). The descent largely follows the same path as the ascent.

title: Itaguaré Trail
short_description: The beauty of the rocky formations of Itaguar Peak, as well as the fact that it is considered a mountaineering icon, has made this trail one of the most sought after by adventurers in Brazil.
long_description:
It is one of the highest points in the state of SP, Pico do Itaguaré has 2,308 m altitude and é considered a ícone of Brazilian mountaineering which is located between Minas Gerais and São Paulo, in the Serra da Mantiqueira.The impressive 360º view from its summit, overlooking the Serra Fina, Vale do Paraíba, Serra da Bocaina, mountains of southern Minas Gerais, and the Pico dos Marins. Some factors make this activity a perfect training for those who wish to reach higher mountains, such as Pedra da Mina or Pico dos Marins.
Most of the route é done inside the forest, when arriving at the camp at the base of Itaguar é we have a ápotable water mine. It is not necessary to walk under the burning sun all the time, nor carry a lot of water up the mountain. Although the elevation is 785 meters, the trail is of medium/high level. If you are a beginner in this sport or without physical fitness, I recommend not choosing this trail at first, or hire a guide to help you on the ascent.

title: Hiking route dunes near Bergen
short_description: During this 12-kilometre route, you will walk through the dunes in North Holland. You can get a nice breath of fresh air.
long_description: You walk through the Schoorl Dunes. These are the highest dunes in the Netherlands. Because you walk through the dunes, it's quite a tough walk, but the view is worth it. You can often get a good view of the sea, and you'll also walk past the beautiful heather found in the Schoorl Dunes.

title: Saxon Wine Trail
short_description: The wine hiking trail runs along the slopes and through the forests of the Elbe valley in the greater Dresden area. From Pirna via Pillnitz we hike in two day stages to the capital of Saxony. Then four more stages await us, most of which run close to the banks of the Elbe and take us all the way to Seußlitz.
long_description:
Stage 1: From Pirna to Pillnitz (16 km)
After a city walk in Pirna, we cross the Elbe by ferry and initially turn our backs on the river. We hike leisurely through Copitz, Hinterjessen as well as Oberpoyritz and meet the Elbe again in Pillnitz, where Pillnitz Castle with its water palace offers a magnificent panorama.
Stage 2: From Pillnitz to Dresden (22 km)
Vineyard walls lead us parallel to the Elbe into the state capital Dresden. Along the way we see the three Elbe castles of Schloss Eckberg, Schloss Albrechtsberg and Villa Stockhausen. In Dresden, we decide for ourselves which of the many sights we would like to visit.
Stage 3: From Dresden to Zitzschewig (15 km)
With the Wilder Mann district, we leave Dresden and set off on a woodland exploration tour. In Boxdorf and near Radebeul we let our eyes wander far into the distance from beautiful vantage points. Half-timbered houses, small churches, vineyards, imposing manor houses and inns line the idyllic path.
Stage 4: From Zitzschewig to Niederau (16 km)
To Weinböhla via Coswig, where the Spitzberg offers a beautiful view of the Elbe valley. Behind Weinböhla begins the Friedewald, a protected forest and pond area that was created in the 16th century. We then pass Lauben Castle and can climb up to the viewing platforms of the Friedensturm (Peace Tower) and the König-Albert-Turm (King Albert Tower). Niederau railway station is Germany's oldest railway station still in operation.
Stage 5: From Niederau to Meißen (13 km)
Today we return to the Elbe, whose course we will follow throughout the day. Along the south-eastern side of the Spaargebirge, an elevation only 3 km long, we pass old vineyards. On the Elbe cycle path we finally reach Meißen.
Stage 6: From Meißen to Seußlitz (16.5 km)
Before we set off on the last stage of the Saxon Wine Trail, we explore the old town of the porcelain city of Meißen, with Meißen Cathedral, the market square and the Benno Church. On the right side of the Elbe, we pass the Proschwitz estate to the Elbe breakthrough and Zadel, where we can taste the region's wine at the Vierseithof farm. Wonderful mixed forests line our route to Seußlitz, offering views of the Elbe Valley again and again.

title: Rugova Canyon - Via Ferrata Ari
short_description: Gripping Via Ferrata over the raging Lumbhardi River - Via Ferrata Ari joins Via Ferrata Mat and leads up past two caves to the top of Rugova Gorge.
long_description:
The Via Ferrata connects to the Via Ferrat Mat. While Via Ferrata Mat is largely horizontal, Via Ferrata Ari takes you high up. You climb higher and higher, while listening to the raging river Lumbhardi. The routes were built and developed in 2016 by Italian experts and certified for safety. In terms of difficulty the trail is ranked in system B (Moderately Difficult).
The Via Ferrata Ari ends up on the Rugova Canyon. There you can take a rest on a bench and follow the marked path down to the main road of Rugova Canyon. The end point is approx. 300 meters in front of the frist bridge in the Rugova Canyon 10 minutes by walk from the starting point.

title: Solbergvarden
short_description: Possibly Finnemarka's best hiking trail
long_description:
This is possibly Finnemarka's best hiking trail. It goes through a beautiful area not even know by many people living around Drammen. The loop takes you through a forested area and up to the Solbergvarden peak with views of Drammen in the east, and Kongsberg and Hokksund in the east. 
The climb on this hike is pretty strenuous, but the views at the top are going to make you forget all your struggles.

title: Mulde Valley Hiking Trail - Freiberger Mulde
short_description: On the Mulde Valley Hiking Trail through the Freiberg Mulde from Nossen to Bad Düben, nature and cultural-historical sights, narrowness and expanse, typical floodplain landscapes and wetlands as well as flora and fauna constantly alternate on nine stages.
long_description:
1st stage: Nossen - Rosswein
We start our first stage in Nossen in Bismarckstraße/corner of Schützenstraße  and immediately hike to the Atzella monastery ruins. The last part of today's stage takes us through the Gersdorf Forest to Rosswein.
2nd stage: Rosswein - Döbeln
From Rosswein we march along the left bank of the Mulden, first via Hohenlauft and then via Niederstriegis and Schweizerhaus to Döbeln.
Third stage: Döbeln - Westewitz
.
The entire route of this stage is identical to the Mulde Valley Cycle Path, on which we march past Technitz to Westewitz.
Stage 4: Westewitz - Leisnig
After Westewitz, we walk along the nature trail to the Maylust lookout point and on to Leisnig. Leisnig is home to Mildenstein Castle, which is well worth a visit
.
5th stage: Leisnig - Colwitz
We start at the market square in Leisnig and hike successively via Altleisnig, Marschwitz, Tanndorf, Podelwitz and Collmen to Colwitz, where the castle of the same name is also located.
6th stage: Colwitz - Grimma
.
At the market in Colwitz we stock up on provisions again before marching back via Sermuth, where the Zwickauer and Freiberger Mulde rivers join. We hike past Leisenau, Kleinbothen, Schaddel and Nimbschen and arrive at Grimma via a suspension bridge and past Gattersburg Castle.
7th stage: Grimma - Wurzen
.
We cross the Mulde and walk in an easterly direction over the Galgenberg to Döben. Now we continue to Trebsen, where we cross the Mulde again and turn right along the Mulde in a northerly direction to Wurzen
.
 Stage 8: Wurzen - Eilenburg
We first march on a paved field path to the flood protection dam and finally reach Eilenburg via Nischwitz and Canitz.
9th stage: Eilenburg - Bad Düben
Our last stage starts at the market square in Eilenburg and takes us along the hiking trail to Hainichen. We then pass Zschepplin and hike via Hohenprießnitz, Ober-Glaucha and Nieder-Glaucha to the destination of the Mulden Valley Hiking Trail, Bad Düben.

title: Zschopautal hiking trail
short_description: We follow the Zschopau river from its source on the Fichtelberg (1200 m) to its mouth in the Freiberg Mulde. Rugged rocky slopes await us as well as romantic valley meadows and flowering meadows.
long_description:
Stage 1: Oberwiesenthal - Tannenberg (23 km)
Up on the Fichtelberg, the Zschopau is still a small inconspicuous stream, but soon the water turns into a white water as it is written in the book. Passing Crottendorf, we leave the Fichtelberg and reach the finish of the day's stage in Tannenberg.
Stage 2: Tannenberg - Wiesenbad (8 km)
The shortest stage of the tour takes us in a right-hand bend above the Zschopau through Wiesa and then to the thermal spa of Wiesenbad, where we can do our feet some good before the next strenuous stretches of trail.
Stage 3: Wiesenbad - Zschopau (21 km)
We turn north again and cross the town of Wolkenstein. Here you can visit Wolkenstein Castle and St. Bartholomew's Church with its impressive gallery. At the market square, we take our bearings from the Heidelbachtal marker. Through the wooded Wolkensteiner Schweiz we reach Zschopau.
Stage 4: Zschopau - Augustusburg (12 km)
Today we can take it easy again, as the day's stage is short and relatively flat. In Witzschdorf we cross the Zschopau and leave the river in Hennersdorf at the Kunnerstein junction to get to Augustusburg.
Stage 5: Augustusburg - Frankenberg ( 17 km)
After Augustusburg, we return via the Lilienstein to "our" river, which we cross. Now we hike leisurely on the opposite side through a large forest area towards the north. After leaving Niederwiesa behind us, we cross the Zschopau again and then head to Frankenberg.
Stage 6: Frankenberg - Mittweida (11.5 km)
For the whole day we walk directly along the river. Only in the forest do we sometimes lose sight of it briefly - but it always remains within earshot. Arriving in Mittweida, we are offered a wide range of cultural and tourist sights.
Stage 7: Mittweida - Waldheim (16 km)
When we get back to the Zschopau today, we will hardly recognise the river: A dam makes it swell to considerable width. Past Kriebstein Castle we reach Waldheim.
Stage 8: Waldheim - Döbeln (13 km)
On the last day of the tour, we cross the Zschopau behind Waldheim   at an old viaduct and hike past the Nixkluft to Limmritz. The river makes another beautiful loop and then flows into the Freiberg Mulde behind Schweta. On the opposite side is Technitz, where our hiking trail ends.

title: Solstien
short_description: The “Sun Trail” from Rjukan to Hardangervidda
long_description: The family-friendly adventure from Rjukan to Hardangervidda. Soak in the incredible views of Gaustatoppen, the tallest mountain in southern Norway, and the surrounding beautiful plateau.

title: Roman Canal Hiking Trail
short_description: We walk along the Eifel water pipeline built in the 1st century AD through the North Eifel and Rhineland Nature Parks. Numerous information boards inform us about the most important Roman building north of the Alps and the region.
long_description:
Stage 1: Nettersheim - Kall-Dottel (15 km)
We start our tour in Nettersheim and hike into the valley of the Urft, from where the Römer laid a water pipeline to Köln, almost 100 km away, to supply the Rhine metropolis with the vital element. Past the former moated castle of Dalbenden and the castle ruins on the Stolzenberg, we hike across fields and meadows to Dottel.
Stage 2:   Kall-Dottel - Mechernich (16 km)
Today we experience some of the most beautiful preserved testimonies of the canal on the forest- and meadow-rich path from Dottel to Mechernich: the Roman well house „Klausbrunnen“, the collecting basin in Eiserfey and the large aqueduct on the outskirts of Vussem.
Stage 3:   Mechernich - Kreuzweingarten (13 km)
This rather short stage leads from Mechernich via Lessenich and Antweiler to Kreuzweingarten. The Mechernich forest awaits us, where the traces of the old canal are still clearly visible between the gnarled oaks. However, the water conduit itself was removed in the High Middle Ages in order to use the stones as building material for castles and churches. So it is likely that parts of the Römerkanal can also be found in the monastery of Maria Rast, which we will pass at the end of the day.
Stage 4:   Kreuzweingarten - Rheinbach (16 km)
After a challenging climb up the Alter Burgberg, we walk past the ruins of the Hardtburg, a moated castle. Over a wide landscape of fields and meadows, we leave Flamersheim, with the former moated castle of Ringsheim, behind us and reach the finish of the stage in Rheinbach.
The route is a little more challenging.
Stage 5:   Rheinbach - Bornheim-Brenig (22 km)
In Reinbach we can take a look at several fragments of the Römerkanal, the Witches' Tower, the Glass Museum and the Himmeroder Hof Nature Park Centre. Afterwards, an equally eventful route awaits us: tranquil villages, St. Peter's Church (tomb of St. Lüfthildis), Lüftelberg Castle, the Kottenforst, the „Iron Man“ and the „Kamelleboom“ can all be seen.
Stage 6:   Bornheim-Brenig - Brühl (water tower) (15 km)
We start our hike in Brenig and first walk through several small villages. After Walbernberg we enjoy the route through a vast forest area with beautiful lakes, which we owe to a renaturalised open-cast mining area.
Stage 7:   Brühl (water tower) - Köln-Sülz (19 km)
On the last stage we pass the Heider Bergsee through a large deciduous forest and then ürth via Hürth with the Kendenich moated castle to Köln. From the Hürtherberg recreation area, we have an impressive view of the city's world-famous cathedral.

title: Elfstedentocht stage 6
short_description: The sixth stage of the Elfstedentocht
long_description: Today you will cycle from Workum to Bolshard. This stage is not very long, so you will have plenty of time to look around the towns. Bolsward is an undiscovered town. This town has a bit of everything: nice terraces, monumental buildings and beautiful nature.

title: Gjende Lake
short_description: Walk along the lakeshore path to escape the hustle and bustle at the dock
long_description:
An easy walk from the dock at Gjende along the quiet lakeshore, this trail leads under the shadow of the mighty Besseggen Ridge. The family-friendly hike leads to a perfect place to relax and enjoy a picnic along the water’s edge. 
Gjendesheim Lodge is a full-service DNT cabin and great place to stay in this area. It is located at the start of the trail.

title: Ridderspranget
short_description: A gorge known from old Norwegian tales
long_description:
Ridderspranget or The Knight’s leap is a small gorge in the river Sjoa by the outskirts of Jotunheimen National Park. Old Norwegian tales describes the story of a knight who escaped his followers by jumping across Ridderspranget together with the girl he loved. You will find more information about this story at site. 
The canyon is about 2 meters wide and you should definitely not try to jump across. But the canyon is definitely an interesting place to visit with the Sjoa river running through the gorge.

title: Helgedalsnosi
short_description: Enjoy panoramic views of the Hurrungane Massif
long_description:
Upon reaching the top of Helgedalsnosi (1,418 meters above sea level), incredible views of the Hurrungane mountain range await. This set of mountains have many of the wildest peaks in Norway, with 23 peaks over 2,000 meters.
The trail runs through open mountain terrain, starting above the treeline (at 1,250 m.a.s.l), offering far-reaching views the entire way. There are multiple access points from Helgedalsnosi into Jotunheimen National Park, so a tip is to pack a tent if a multiday hike sounds tempting.
The geologist Baltazar Mathias Keilhau (1797-1858), was the first to depict the Hurrungane massif. Many used Keilhau's sketches and watercolors as models for their work. Appearing in the painter Johannes Flintoe's Hurrungene, they are among the oldest Norwegian book illustrations. 
Turtagrø Hotel dates back to the 1880s, but was recently renovated and is the closest accommodation to Helgedalsnosi. They serve breakfast, lunch, and three-course dinners. Campsite rental is also available, which includes access to showers, toilets, and a common area. The Lodge is open between Easter and mid-September.
Another option is Sognefjellethytta Mountain Lodge, located about a 20-minute drive northeast of Helgedalsnosi. Here you can enjoy a three-course dinner and far-reaching mountain views in a newly renovated common room. The Lodge is open between Easter and mid-September.

title: Easy circuit around the Tampa Mountain
short_description: An easy hike that surrounds the Tâmpa Mountain, without reaching the top. It follows various easy-to-spot tourist markings, it also meets the most touristic climbing route.
long_description:
Surrounding Mount Tâmpa is an alternative to the classic climb to the top. It can be done in any season since it's not very demanding. This is not a route to do for the views, but rather a relaxing long walk. It can be covered even with your dog, by bike, and with older children - given the length.
It starts with the blue triangle marking which will change along the way, depending on the direction. The path on this segment is popular among locals. Since the width of the path is wide enough, cyclists often cross your way.
In the northern part, you'll reach the rather touristic routes that go to the Tâmpa Peak. Also here, the panorama opens toward the city. Moving onward toward Șchei, the path climbs to Saua Tâmpei. Before the climb and higher, there are benches to catch your breath.
To descend back to the city, follow the yellow triangle marking that will take you to the place called La Iepure. The paths that deviate from the route and descend into the city are practicable in dry weather.

title: The wine road through Dobrogea
short_description: The wine road through Dobrogea is a winding one, with ups and downs on the sunburnt hills of Dobrogea, taking you through places steeped in history and where you can witness the peaceful coexistence of many cultures.
long_description:
Your route through the vineyards of Dobrogea can în start in Măcin, i.e. în Mountains of Măcin Natural Park. If you have the time to spare, in addition to a wine tasting, try an equestrian walk or even a hike on one of the lowest mountain trails in Romania.
On this wine trail, you have the opportunity to taste varieties produced in the Sarica-Niculițel and Murfatlar vineyards, the latter being famous for its sweet or semi-sweet wines - the result of generous year-round sun-drying.
Because you're in a territory where traces of Greek and Roman colonisation before or since our era are still visible, you could include stops at some of Dobrgogea's most famous ancient fortresses.
Turkish culture is also felt everywhere here, from the place names of some of the towns to the cuisine and sights. So, to get a feel for the atmosphere, we suggest you check if the Babadag buoy is open for visits.
For the adventurous, the Dobrogean wine road can also be done with confidence by bicycle or car, especially in the warm season.

title: Reinsvangen to Gjendeosen
short_description: Hike to the Gjende dock for a taste of the Norwegian mountains
long_description:
When visiting the Gjende area it’s often best to park at Reinsvangen, the long-term parking lot 1.7 kilometers from the dock. There’s no time limits and you can explore without any worries! This trail connects the long-term parking lot with the dock, traveling through typical Norwegian mountain terrain. There are great views of Gjende Lake along the way, making the hike a good alternative to the shuttle on a nice day.
Gjendesheim Lodge is a full-service DNT cabin and great place to stay in this area. It is located at the end of the trail.

title: Route to Petria and half way through the valley observation point
short_description: An easy and short hiking route leading to an impressive point of interest known as Petria and half way through wonderful panoramic desert views in the Timna Reserve near Eilat
long_description:
This hiking route leads to a point of interest known as a mushroom and a half, this is through the impressive Bekaa lookout overlooking the mountains of Timna. It is possible to climb to an observation point of the area from this route as marked on the trip map on this page, although it may appear steep and a little difficult, it is a relatively easy and simple climb that is worth reaching.
Please note that the route is not shaded and is not accessible to strollers or wheelchairs.

images.caption: A view of the mushroom and a half from a vantage point

title: Mefjellstien
short_description: Admire the grand Smørstabb Peaks
long_description:
Built like a natural gallery, Mefjellet rest stop is worth a visit. The rest stop is designed like a terrace with natural stone walls, reinforcing the panoramic views and the feeling of loftiness on the Sognefjellet mountain plateau. Here you’ll find a quadrangular stone sculpture made by the Norwegian artist Knut Wold through which you can admire the magnificent Smørstabb Peaks.
From the rest stop, it’s possible to follow the marked roundtrip trail Mefjellstien if wishing to discover the surrounding mountain scenery even further. A section of the trail follows the historic Vardestien (“the Cairn Track”). For hundreds of years, people have traveled across the mountain pass, and this old track features cairns dating back to the mid-nineteenth century.
Being only 3 kilometers long and running through smooth mountain terrain, Mefjellstien is a family-friendly hike. However, in spring and early summer, you’re likely to come across wet and snowy sections. 
Sognefjellshytta Mountain Lodge offers hotel accommodation and serves communal meals. The new, modern common room linking the two traditional buildings is worth a visit. The combination of wood and glass disperses the light through the room and imparts the changing moods of weather and light at this high altitude. The lodge is open between Easter and mid-September.

title: Memurubu
short_description: Take the boat to Memurubu for a short hike in the heart of Jotunheimen
long_description:
A boat ride across the beautiful Gjende Lake is a highlight for many visitors to Jotunheimen. Traveling from Gjendesheim, a scheduled boat stops at Memurubu, where a mountain lodge welcomes both day and overnight visitors.
Memurubu is a starting point for several hikes, including Besseggen Ridge and the trail to Gjendebu. But with its stunning location at the end of the valley in the heart of Jotunheimen it is itself a worthy destination.
Gjendesheim Lodge is a full-service DNT cabin and great place to stay in this area. It is located at the start of the trail.
Memurubu Lodge is a full-service private cabin and a perfect place to overnight before hiking Besseggen Ridge or to Gjendebu.

Traseul de la cabana Brusturet spre vârful La Om e unul din cele clasice din Munții Piatra Craiului.

title: Spiral Hill
short_description: A short easy trip with lovely and panoramic desert views in the Timna Reserve near Eilat
long_description:
This hiking route is the most significant point of interest closest to the entrance of Timna Park. The route leads to Givat Borg where later you can climb it a little and then go around it. Givat Borg itself is very impressive in its shape and structure and offers a great panoramic view of the desert environment that surrounds it.
Please note that the route is not shaded and is not accessible to strollers or wheelchairs.

title: Munken
short_description: Impressive peak in Jotunheimen National Park
long_description:
Munken is one of the seven summits that offshoots from the mountain Kalvehøgde, and is located on the northeastern part of the 10km long glacier situated in the southern part of Jotunheimen.
While hiking to Munken you will pass through the lush Leirungsdalen valley, with 2,000-meter peaks towering on both sides of you. The valley here becomes narrower and the hillsides become steeper the closer you get to Kalvehøgde. You will see Munken standing out more than the others with glaciers on either side.
There are a total of 30 surrounding peaks, as you gain altitude, each peak is nicer than the last. During the trip, you’ll not only reach the summit of Munken, but also of Mugna and Rasletinden. Be prepared to do quite a lot of scrambling.
The National Map Institute chose the name for Munken, which means “The Munk” in English.
Bygdin Mountain Hotel is a charming bed and breakfast located about 11 kilometers south of the trailhead for Munken.
Another option is Besseggen Fjellpark Maurvangen located 8 kilometers north of the trailhead for Munken. Book a cabin, or stay in your tent or RV with access to toilets and showers.

images.caption: Bukkehåmaren har mykje spannande å vise fram.

title: Vardestien
short_description: Step back in history
long_description:
For hundreds of years, cairns have been used to guide people and horses safely over the Sognefjellet mountain pass. This historic trail features cairns dating back to the mid-nineteenth century, allowing you to wander in the footsteps of travelers past. 
Krossbu Mountain Lodge offers hotel accommodation as well as camping facilities. They serve communal three-course dinners. There’s also a café where you can buy hot food throughout the day. The lodge is open between mid-April and mid-September.
Sognefjellshytta Mountain Lodge offers hotel accommodation and serves communal meals. The new, modern common room linking the two traditional buildings is worth a visit. The combination of wood and glass disperses the light through the room and imparts the changing moods of weather and light at this high altitude. The lodge is open between Easter and mid-September.

title: Comic Hut
short_description: A highly recommended hike in the Val Gardena Dolomites from Selva Gardena to the Comici Hut.
long_description: Through the almost untouched Ampeza Valley this circular hike leads along the Sassolungo and up to the famous Comici Hut. The hut, named after the South Tyrolean mountaineer Emilio Comici, is located at 2154 m and attracts hikers and mountaineers with its blue shutters from afar. The steep climb to the hut is rewarded not only by the magnificent view from the top, but also by the first-class refreshments.

Langkofel von der Seiser Alm aus gesehen

title: Gjende Viewpoint
short_description: Take a quick hike from the dock for views across Gjende Lake
long_description:
This short hike provides easy access to a photo-worthy viewpoint above Gjende Lake. Here, at the very eastern end of the lake, you can look deep into the heart of Jotunheimen with the famous Besseggen Ridge alongside you.
Gjendesheim Lodge is a full-service DNT cabin and great place to stay in this area. It is located at the start of the trail.

title: Gjendetunga
short_description: Pleasant hike overlooking Gjende Lake and the Jotunheimen mountain range
long_description:
Gjendetunga is located at 1,516 meters above sea level, in the heart of Jotunheimen National Park. It's an easily accessible hike from Gjendebu Mountain Lodge, with numerous access trails. 
At the top, you will be rewarded with incredible views of the glistening Gjende Lake, the abundance of mountains in Jotunheimen such as Gjendealpene, Storådalen, and Semeltinden as well as nearby glaciers.
Gjendebu Mountain Lodge is located at 995 meters above sea level, on the southern end of Lake Gjende. It's a full-service cabin that was established in 1871, but it's been renovated several times, and currently has 119 beds. It's considered the oldest cabins owned by DNT.
The Right to Roam law enables you to camp anywhere for free as long as you follow some basic guidelines.

title: Besseggen Ridge
short_description: Check this famous ridge off your bucket list
long_description:
Besseggen Ridge has a special status among Norwegians and hiking the ridge is considered a rite of passage, no matter your age. The iconic view is characterized by the colourful Gjende and Bessvatnet lakes. Gjende is a stunning emerald color and very long and narrow. Bessvatnet is a deep blue and among Norway’s clearest lakes.
Hiking the Besseggen Ridge is very demanding. It takes anywhere between 6 to 9 hours to complete the hike. Despite the challenging route, during the short hiking season from the end of June to mid-September, more than 60,000 hikers complete the trip. This makes Besseggen one of the most trafficked hiking routes in Norway. For a quieter hike, go early in the season or on a weekday in September.
The trail becomes extremely difficult in rainy weather, so make sure to look at the forecast and talk with locals and fellow hikers before embarking on the trek.
Gjendesheim Lodge is a full-service DNT cabin and great place to stay in this area. It is located at the eastern end of the trail.
Memurubu Lodge is a full-service private cabin at the western end of the trail. Camping is also available.
Hindsæter Hotel is located 10 minutes north of Gjendesheim by car towards Vågå.

images.caption: The iconic view of the Gjende and Bessvatnet lakes.

title: Glittertind
short_description: Norway's second highest mountain: 2,465 meters above sea level
long_description:
It's easy to understand why the hike up the second highest mountain in Norway is so popular. On the way up and on the peak, there are magnificent views over Jotunheimen.
Glitterheim Tourist Lodge is a full-service DNT cabin located at the base of this incredible mountain.

images.caption: Glittertind er ein fin skitopp om våren og en flott fjelltur om sommeren. På Toppen ligger det snø hele året.

title: Falketind
short_description: Popular hike with beautiful views of the Morka-Koldedalen Valley
long_description:
Falketind is located at 2,067 meters above sea level and it is one of the popular hikes in Jotunheimen. After passing Andrevatnet you'll get beautiful views Morka-Koldedalen Valley, and from the top, you can see both Stølsnostinden and Stølsnosbree. When the weather is nice, there are often many people hiking. 
Tyinholmen Mountain Lodge is located on the northern shores of Tyin Lake, at 1,100 meters above sea level. From the lodge, you can view the beautiful nearby mountains and glaciers. 
The Right to Roam law enables you to camp anywhere for free as long as you follow some basic guidelines. Read more.

title: Great Ocean Road
short_description: With its large sandy beaches and impressive cliffs, Australia’s southern coast offers a great diversity of landscapes. Among all the panoramic routes of the continent, the Great Ocean Road is one of the most spectacular ones. Hardly any other road is better suited for exploring the huge coastline.
long_description:
The Great Ocean Road is a panoramic street between Torquay and Allansford in the state of Victoria at Australia’s southern coast. In 2001 this street was officially listed as Australian National Heritage.  There are millions of visitors every year enjoying the stunning views of the seascapes.
Great Ocean Road starts in Torquay which is also labelled the “Surfing Capital of Australia“. This is where surfers from all over the world are coming together to enjoy the huge waves and the stunning scenery of this picturesque spot. Lovers of the nature as well as hobby photographer are gathering in Torquay to capture the charm and magic of one of Australia’s most impressive locations.
The landscape of Great Ocean Road is as diverse as it is stunning. You can find here cliffs alongside sandy beaches and spectacular viewpoints next to the road. In between you can see beautiful spots of wildlife, a stunning setting for souvenir photos. Another rewarding stop are porth Campbell and Great Otway National Park. This is where you can observe koalas and other exotic animals at close range as well as explore picturesque waterfalls.
You can go snorkelling or rafting, do a canoa tour or go for a ride in order to grasp the beauty of the Australian coastline.
At the end of the road you’ll find one of the most impressive spots along Great Ocean Road: the famous Twelve Apostles. These distinctive rock formations rise above the water and will take your breath away.
If you want to go for a walk along the route, you shouldn’t miss the chance to take a look at Great Ocean Walk. If you’re lucky you’ll even spot whales and dolphins near the coast.
