Situated at the southern tip of Ilhabela, the Bonete Trail begins at the end of the asphalt road, in Borrifos. Visitors can follow a dirt road for another two kilometres until they reach the State Park gate, at the Sepituba Point. The landscape of the whole walk é ssima ssima e, besides being époss vel vel  observe  espeacute;cies of fauna and flora of the region &eatilde;O, there are small rivers where é poss´possível tomar banho em piscinas naturais de áágua crystallinas e observar ainda quedas d’áágua incrincrêndis.
The longest of all the trails in the Ilhabela State Park, the Bonete Trail is approximately 12 kilometres long just going. The trail takes from three to six hours, depending on the walking pace. As it is long, the visitors who take this path should leave early. Arriving at Bonete Beach, the return can be arranged with the boats of the "boneteiros", which take the visitor back to Borrifos.

title: Picturesque Ohe Valley
short_description: A pleasure tour with only one small climb through the floodplain of the Mitternacher Ohe and with a view of the picturesquely situated Schönberg.
long_description: We walk past the information board in the direction of Kirchberg on Nordic Walking Trail 3 "Ohetal". On an ascending field path we reach Mitternach and the inn. The magnificent view accompanies us behind Schönberg to the turn-off at the Jägerstand. Follow the meadow path along the Ohe through an atmospheric valley to the bridge. Cross the bridge and head uphill through the spruce forest. Walking route "3" leads us to the hamlet of Panhof and down the road back to the Ohe. Directly after the bridge, we follow the course of the stream to a fireplace. We do not turn onto the forest path, but walk along the river to another forest path that takes us back to the car park on the left.

title: From Bratwurst Country to the Linth Valley
short_description: The Tanzboden alpine inn is halfway between Toggenburg and the Linth region. It is therefore the ideal resting place on a hike from one valley to the other.
long_description:
The alpine restaurant Tanzboden lies halfway between the Toggenburg and the Linth valley. It is thus the ideal stopping point on a hike from one valley to the other.
You begin this hike at the Ebnat-Kappel railway station and wander upriver along the Thur riverbank for a few minutes. At Thurau you will cross a bridge and start upward, putting behind you the first of the 800 meters difference in altitude that separate you from the Tanzboden. More than half the dis-tance to Tanzboden traverses narrow, sometimes scarcely visible paths through blooming meadows. Of interest are the differences in vegetation as one climbs: in May the meadow grasses bloom up to an altitude of 850 meters, whereas at a height of between 850 and 1200 meters the grass is still re-covering from the long winter, and there are no blossoms to be seen. Further up, however, thousands of gentians and soldanels spring up between the brown winter grasses. Especially impressive is the Alp Ober-Abschlagen. The brutal name is quite in opposition to the charm of the place. On three sides the climb up to this alp is very steep, so it is the more surprising to find at the top a small, nearly flat pre-alpine paradise. From the northern part of this Alp you are rewarded with a magnificent view of the central Toggenburg. Ebnat-Kappel and Wattwil lie below you; to the east you see the Säntis and the Churfirsten. And now it is only a half hour from Ober-Abschlagen to the Tanzboden, the highest point of our trip. Finally, our hike continues over the Gubelspitz to Breitenau and Wielesch, where there is another alpine restaurant with a marvelous view. From the Wielesch, you'll climb steeply down into the Giegentobel and continue on to the Giegental. Finally, board the post bus in the village center of Gommiswald and ride to the Uznach railway station.

title: The Choice between Scree and Karst
short_description: Steep and technical hike with beautiful views of the Schwyz and Glarus Alps.
long_description:
From the Glattalp you have two choices of trails to Braunwald. The first is technically very difficult, because it takes you on a steep path across the large scree fields of the Furggele. The Bärentritt is also a challenge. This very steep trail snakes through rocks that appear from below to be impossible to climb. If you decide on this route you should have no fear of heights, be steady on your feet and very fit. The reward for your efforts are great views of the Schwyz and Glarus Alps. Fun also are the up to 500-meter long snowfields, on which you can slide, sitting on a plastic bag. From the Furggele (2395 meters) you can climb up to the Ortstock (2717) in 45 minutes, and have a view of more than 400 Alpine peaks.

If you are less interested in climbing challenges and like karst landscapes, start from the mountain terminus of the Glattalpbahn and hike to the north. A short climb will bring you to the Charetalp, where you'll be rewarded with spectacular views of karst fields around the Pfannenstock and the Bös Fulen. The Erigsmatt is your next goal, reached on very good paths without any ascents to speak of. Thereaf-ter, however, you will need firm footing on this route as well, for the rocky sections of the Nösseli and Bützi area hide crevices. Stop at the Gumen mountain restaurant, where you can sit on the terrace and fill your hungry stomach before you take the aerial tramway down to Braunwald.

title: Schönbielhütte
short_description: Hike with views of imposing glaciers to the Schönbielhütte.
long_description:
The Matterhorn surrounded by glaciers

If you want to see glaciers, you'll get your money's worth at the 2694-metre Schönbielhütte: just below the hut, the ice stream of the Zmutt glacier flows past. With a 15-minute walk, you can catch a glimpse of a hanging glacier rolling down from Dent Blanche. Close to the hut, Lake Howang with its turquoise water beckons you to splash around. If it's too cold, you'll be amazed at the frogs that jump into the cold water without hesitation.

Thanks to the mountain railways, the trail is also easy for smaller children who like to hike. The cable car takes you to the Schwarzsee, which is already at the foot of the Matterhorn. From here you hike about 400 metres downhill to cross the valley floor at Stafel. The trail continues on the opposite slope. Small lakes make the ascent entertaining, so that the 500 metres of ascent can almost be done on the side. The descent takes about 3.5 hours and first follows the ascent route, but then continues in Stafel straight along the sunny slope to Zermatt.

title: Alabama's Coastal Connection
short_description: Get a sense of the unique southern flair and enjoy Alabama’s stunning coastline on Coastal Connection
long_description:
The state of Alabama is best known as the “heart of Whisky and Dixie“, but there’s so much more to it. At its southern tip you can explore a spectacular coastline, marvellous wildlife preserves and taste the delicious local seafood. All this makes it especially attractive for outdoor enthusiasts and nature lovers alike.
The route leads you to the traditional fishing village of Bayou La Batre, two massive coast defense fortifications as well as two of the most picturesque landscape spots, Bellingrath Gardens and Gulf State Park.
On its nearly 110 miles, Alabama’s Coastal Connection offers you plenty of stopovers where you can have a break and take in the stunning scenery.

title: West Iceland
short_description: The first stage begins on the west coast of Iceland and stretches for almost 420 km to the fishing village of Hellissandur.
long_description: The route heads north from Iceland's largest airport in Keflavík and offers panoramic views of the Atlantic coast. About 180 km further north is Deildartunguhver, Iceland's largest and most abundant hot spring. Here the mighty forces of nature become clear: the rising water vapour is visible from afar. Only a few kilometres further inland we can marvel at the so-called Hraunfossar, a multitude of small waterfalls that pour into the riverbed of the Hvítá in an impressive play of colours. Towards the end of the day we pass the legendary Rauðfeldsgjá gorge, which still amazes its many visitors. The day's tour leads straight to the campsite of the tranquil fishing village of Hellissandur.

title: River Landscape Reuss Tour
long_description:
The tour leads from Cham railway station along beautiful field paths to the Wart excursion site. It continues downhill towards Zollbrücke. The following section is very exciting. It leads us along the Reuss and we can observe a typical river landscape. With a bit of luck, we may spot rare birds such as a kingfisher or a bright yellow oriole, or we may enjoy the colourful Siberian iris. Various information pillars provide information on fauna and flora. We then cross the Reuss plain and reach Frauental Monastery. It invites us to stay for a while. After a short ascent we enjoy the view back to the monastery before we reach the village of Rumentikon. We then hike back on field paths via Friesencham to Cham.

Note(s)
The tour can also be walked in the opposite direction.

title: Ridge walk to the Uetliberg
short_description: With its 870-metre-high summit, the Uetliberg is the ideal option for an excursion near Zurich, especially for enjoying the sun on foggy days.
long_description:
From Adliswil, take the cable car up to Felsenegg and then follow the signs for Uetliberg. After 300 metres you reach the first sight: the broadcasting tower, built in 1959 and visible from afar. The next attraction is the planet trail: between Buechegg and the Uetliberg station, all the planets of the solar system have been reproduced to scale. Information boards provide details about their size, position and orbit. This trail is the ideal option for families.
At some points, you can see almost all of Lake Zurich on the right, while on the left you can see the landscapes of the cantons of Aargau and Lucerne. The descent from this symbolic mountain of Zurich continues northwards before descending into the city on the Hohensteinweg and reaching the Triemli S-Bahn station. From there, the S10 takes you back to Zurich main station in less than 10 minutes.

title: My King's Forest trail running circuit 2, Bury St Edmunds, Suffolk
short_description: If you're into jogging and in need of something other than fields or coastline, King's Forest near Bury St Edmunds offers a lot of potential routes for trail running. Here is just one of them!
long_description:
Like its larger neighbour (I'm looking at you, Thetford), the great thing about King's Forest is the extensive network of paths and trails that runs through it, which means that you can walk or jog distances that suit your personal fitness level and plans.  The woods are also very peaceful and the further you get from the car parking areas, the fewer people you're likely to encounter. 
If you want to mix things up, this route is equally doable in reverse. It's also suitable throughout the year and can be hiked if running is not your thing.

title: Dam Busters - Derwent Dam and Ladybower reservoir
short_description: A woodland trail climb up to Derwent Dam from Fairholmes Visitor Centre.
long_description:
The River Derwent is Derbyshire’s and the Peak District’s major river.
The RAF’s celebrated 617 squadron flew practice sorties here with their ‘bouncing bombs’, in preparation their epic 1943 raid on the dams of the German Ruhr.
The twin-towered dam is at its most impressive when the water cascades over it.
  The River Derwent flows first through Howden Reservoir, then Derwent Reservoir and finally through Ladybower Reservoir. Between them they provide practically all of Derbyshire's water, as well as to a large part of South Yorkshire.
  Find more at wikipedia.

title: The Butte de Vauquois
short_description:
The battle of Vauquois spanned most of the First World War, taking place in the eponymous village perched on a strategic hillock.
This short loop walk takes you there effortlessly.
long_description:
The site became extremely important due to its intensive use in mine warfare. This tactic involved the creation of deep tunnels to conceal large quantities of explosives, causing substantial damage to the surface before the assault.
The deep craters that remain today bear witness to the extreme violence of the confrontations, making Vauquois an emblematic site of this trench warfare.

title: Winter hike from Benken to Kaltbrunn
short_description: This winter hike from Benken to Kaltbrunn puts you in the Christmas spirit with a visit to the Magnus Kirche in Rieden and a giant nativity scene.
long_description:
The hike begins at Benken railroad station and follows the partly renaturalized Steinenbach stream to Steinenbrücke. The 300-metre ascent to Rieden takes you across meadows, gravel paths and small roads before a steep little road leads directly to the Magnus Church. This neo-baroque parish church, built by Adolf Gaudy (1912-1914), is a landmark of the village of 700 souls and is characterized by its onion dome.
To the west of Rieden, you cross the Giegenbach stream and continue the hike to Gommiswald. From there, the trail descends across meadows into the Linth plain. In Rüteli, above Kaltbrunn railroad station, you will find Elisabeth and Toni Müller's Christmas crib, which is lovingly decorated every year in a former cowshed. The Müllers offer warm drinks and snacks before you walk the rest of the way to Kaltbrunn station.

title: Tour of Lake Liez
short_description: This trail takes you through unspoilt countryside to explore the Lac de la Liez.
long_description:
Lac de la Liez, the oldest of the lakes in the Langres region, created in 1888 and the largest at 290 hectares, offers an enchanting view from the ramparts of the fortified town. Its deep blue waters invite you to enjoy a romantic getaway, where the town blends harmoniously with the surrounding countryside. In summer, its lively beach and wide range of water sports make it a favourite destination for families in search of relaxation. However, for a more authentic experience, the hiking trails along the wooded banks offer total immersion in a preserved ecosystem, where fish and birds peacefully cohabit.
Whether you're looking for a romantic getaway, family relaxation or nature exploration, Lac de la Liez promises unforgettable memories and moments of serenity in the heart of an enchanting landscape.

title: Via Appia
short_description: The “Queen among the streets“ was one of the most important trade routes of the Roman Empire and since then it luckily hasn’t lost any of its charm. Alongside the route you can find picturesque parks, idyllic sea landscapes, ancient Christian graves and several cities with historic flair.
long_description:
Via Appia is considered one of the most significant historical routes of Italy. Its beginning dates back to the third century AD when traders from all over the continent roamed Southern Europe to sell their goods.
The road was originally built as a connection road between Rome in central-western Italy and the Apulian port city of Brindisi on the coast of the Adriatic Sea in Eastern Italy.
During the Middle Ages it was used by pilgrims who came to Rome to visit the grave of Saint Peter. Back then, Via Appia was labelled “Queen among the streets”, but nowadays it isn’t preserved completely. Nonetheless, you can visit a few well-preserved road fractions at  Lazio, Campania, Basilicata and Apulia.

images.caption: Track of Via Appia near Casal Rotondo
A few tracks of the original route called "Via Appia Antica" are still preserved.
The catacombs of San Sebastiano are located underneath the basilica "San Sebastiano Fuori Le Mura“.
Still among Italy's hidden gems: Lago Albano.
Rocca di Papa is located near Parco Regionale dei Castelli Romani.
An attractive destination for hikers: Lago di Conza

title: Over Fields of Limestone and Scree
short_description: The paths up the Silberen are just as unusual as the views that can be seen on the large karst field between Muotathal and Klöntal.
long_description:
The trails up to the Silberen are as unusual as the sights offered by the large karst field between Muo-tathal and Klöntal. The film "Treasure of Silver Lake" comes to mind when one glimpses the many white cliffs shortly after reaching the top of the Pragelpass. One sees Winnetou, in the saddle on his horse Iltschi, searching for a place to do good works. The shepherds coming along the path and the jingling of the cowbells reminds one that one is not in Croatia (where the Winnetou films were made) or in Arizona (actual home of the Apaches), but at the east end of the down-to-earth Muotathal.
After an hour's hike, you'll get an idea of what awaits you further up. You'll traverse limestone cut into by furrows gouged out by water and with sharp edges, such as are usually found on the ocean shores and you'll need good shoes and steady footing for walking here. The gigantic fields of karst offer al-pine hikers unusual views. From the mountaintop you'll start down to the Hintere Silberenalp, where there are numerous little lakes and ponds on this plateau, all in the most varied colors. Next comes the Dräckloch, surrounded by high cliffs. From the Rossmatt you'll see how the melted water from the Glärnisch firn falls over the cliffs, and on the Chäseren you'll go by a group of little wooden houses that resemble a gold-prospecting village. No one looked for gold here, however, rather this is a popu-lar base camp for mountain climbers who want to climb the Glärnisch or other nearby peaks. When you've been underway a good five hours, you'll reach the gravel beach of the Vorauen. The water of the Klöntalersee is surprisingly warm, ca. 19 degrees, and swimming along, dazzled by reflected light, you can look up to the summit of the Silberen.

Note(s)
altitude difference downwards: 1576 hm

title: Greifensee Skate: The classic around the lake
long_description:
The 19-kilometre loop around Lake Greifensee is extremely popular with skaters, cyclists and runners. No wonder: the narrow and flat asphalt strip leads through beautiful lakeside landscapes and to original Besenbeizen.
You start the skate tour in Niederuster at the lido and go clockwise around the lake. If you want to do the loop around the lake at the weekend, you should get up early. From ten o'clock in the morning at the latest, there are so many cyclists and skaters on the road that you often have to put on the brakes. It's especially dicey when you're passing through a town. But if you don't want to keep your heart rate permanently in the upper range and want to take breaks, Lake Greifensee is the place to be. There are plenty of bathing places and establishments. Numerous garden and broom pubs lie directly along the way. It is also worth taking a break in Greifensee with its historic centre and lakeside.

Note(s)
A few words about the asphalt quality: On more than half of the route, our blades roll perfectly. At the village crossings and on a longer section in Niederuster, the surface leaves something to be desired.

title: Climbing the Mittag
short_description: We experience a diverse route at the eastern end of the Nagelfluhkette. This is a perfect entry point to the nature park Nagelfluhkette as well.
long_description: From the Marienplatz in the centre of Immenstadt we walk up to the station at the bottom of the cable car Mittagbahn. We climb up until we reach the alpine hut Alpe Hochried. Passing the middle station of the cable car and the alpine huts Mittag-Alpe and Schwand-Alpe we finally reach the summit. After a well deserved break we climb down towards east until we reach the chapel Bildkapelle. Hiking alongside Ettensberg we reach Schwanden. Later we pass the alpine hut Rieder-Alpe and return to the bottom station of the cable car Mittagbahn. We walk back to the centre of Immenstadt on the same route that we took before.

title: Sentiero Italia
short_description:
PLEASE NOTE: This version of Sentiero Italia is updated to 2022, go here to check out the latest version: Sentiero Italia CAI - Official Map.
The longest long-distance hiking trail in the world is getting a revival – on the Sentiero Italia, Italy shows itself in all its diversity. With stamina and a lot of wanderlust, you will get to the most beautiful places in the country!
long_description:
It starts with alpine scenery and ends with salty air by the azure sea. You can hardly dive deeper into the Italian landscape:
7,850 km
350,000 m elevation gain
20 regions
364 stages
The long-distance hiking trail runs through the whole of Italy. It runs from the Alps across the Apennines to Sardinia and Sicily, connecting not only many picturesque villages but also six UNESCO World Natural Heritage sites.
CAI President Vincenzo Torti on Sentiero Italia: "We have a dream to unite all of Italy in one big embrace, walking through the extraordinary places our country has to offer once you leave the paved roads."
You can find the individual stages at the Va' Sentiero project, which is dedicated to digitising the route. You can also support them directly on-site and accompany them on their way through Italy.

title: Lake Zurich circular route: 7th stage Rapperswil - Stäfa
short_description: One of the most beautiful corners of Lake Zürich with many fantastic viewpoints.
long_description:
The landscape around Lake Zürich is not only one of the most sought-after residential regions in the world, but also a hiking country that offers much pleasure and üsurprising contrasts.

12,000 years ago, the Linth glacier shaped the basin of Lake Zürich into the landscape. The picturesque legacy of the ice was protected by the Römers, Alemanni and Habsburgs alike and has since become Switzerland's most privileged residential address.

The Zürichsee Trail shows the multifaceted region at its best. Along the way, there are historic towns and villages, castle parks and villa quarters, but also intact lakeside landscapes, extensive forests and wild ravines to discover. On its ten stages, the Zürichsee-Weg offers further enjoyment: several restaurants, from simple country pubs to gourmet restaurants, as well as first-class wineries are literally along the way. In addition, there are many sports and leisure facilities, museums, cinemas and B&Bs.

Thus, on the lake circuit, hiking purists, nature, culture and history lovers, gourmets and sports enthusiasts all get their money's worth in equal measure. The starting points of the hike can be freely chosen from the ten stage locations. For once, it is not certain places that are the goal, but the path and its pearls.

7th stage: Rapperswil - Stäfa

You hike through landscapes as once described by Gottfried Keller. Several times you run up into the sky and enjoy the best views of the lake and its surroundings. The Glarus and Central Swiss Alps provide a spectacular backdrop.

title: Lake Zurich circular route: 6th stage Schmerikon - Rapperswil
short_description: Leisurely hike along the Strandweg to Rapperswil.
long_description:
The landscape around Lake Zurich is not only one of the most sought-after residential regions in the world, but also a hiking country that offers plenty of enjoyment and surprising contrasts.

12,000 years ago, the Linth glacier shaped the basin of Lake Zurich into the landscape. The picturesque legacy of the ice was appreciated by the Romans, Alemanni and Habsburgs alike and has since become Switzerland's most privileged residential address.

The Lake Zurich Trail shows the multifaceted region at its best. Along the way there are historic towns and villages, castle parks and villa quarters, but also intact lakeside landscapes, extensive forests and wild ravines to discover. On its ten stages, the Lake Zurich Trail offers further enjoyment: several restaurants, from simple country pubs to gourmet restaurants, as well as first-class wineries are literally along the way. In addition, there are many sports and leisure facilities, museums, cinemas and stages.

Thus, on the lake circuit, hiking purists, nature, culture and history lovers, gourmets and sports enthusiasts all get their money's worth in equal measure. The starting points of the hike can be freely chosen from among the ten stage locations. For once, the goal is not specific places, but the path and its pearls.

6th stage: Schmerikon - Rapperswil

The Strandweg leads through the most intact lakeside landscapes in eastern Switzerland. Water birds can be observed in the nature reserves at Wurmsbach and Busskirch. Several bathing establishments and sports facilities are located directly along the route.

Sights:

Island of Ufenau
The two islands of Ufenau and Lützelau are located in the upper part of Lake Zurich. The larger island of Ufenau (correct name Ufnau, common name Ufenau), together with the area of the Frauenwinkel, was placed under nature conservation in 1927.

Island of Lützelau
On the island of Lützelau (3.38 hectares) has a camping site, a fireplace and a small restaurant, which is looked after by the island's caretaker.

Rapperswil Castle and Old Town
Rapperswil, the Riviera on the upper part of Lake Zurich, awaits visitors with its southern charm. The small alleyways in the medieval old town invite you to go shopping.

Knies Kinderzoo
For over 40 years, Knie has offered the special, unique zoo for young and old.

Holzsteg Rapperswil-Hurden
The region was already known to many travellers from the north in the Middle Ages. Lake Zurich lies on the route of the St. James pilgrims, who centuries ago also visited Rapperswil on their way to Santiago de Compostela.

Culture construction kit Rapperswil-Jona
On the hike to 36 cultural stations. Rapperswil and Jona united in 2007 to form the town of Rapperswil-Jona. The Rapperswil-Jona cultural construction kit brings together old and new shared culture.

The Kunstzeughaus Rapperswil-Jona
The art centre welcomes you with ever-changing exhibitions and an exciting overview of the Peter and Elisabeth Bosshard collection.

Alte Fabrik Rapperswil-Jona
A cultural centre has been created at the old Geberit AG site.

title: Triberger Wasserfälle
short_description: A short and relatively easy circular trip to Triberg Falls in the south-central Black Forest
long_description:
A relatively easy hiking route (but uphill) that leads to the Triberg Falls while walking on suspension bridges, a gorgeous view and lots of water. A great hiking route for families and children, mostly also suitable for walking with strollers. The height of the chain of Triberg waterfalls is 163 meters and they are considered the most impressive and the highest in Germany (other than in the Alps).
The Triberg Falls network is divided into two main parts:
* Upper waterfalls that include three main rock steps and lead the water down a steep slope from a height of 872 meters up to a height of 856 meters above sea level.
* Lower waterfalls that include seven rock steps and descend from a height of 805 meters up to a height of 713 meters above sea level.
Walking the route, that is, the entrance to the waterfalls park is paid, while the entry prices in the winter are slightly cheaper than those in the summer. The site can be visited all year round, while in the winter season the frozen and snowy landscapes are an attraction of their own.

title: Walk in the heart of the Cedar forest of the Luberon
short_description: This easy loop takes you to the heart of the Cedar Forest, a must-see place in the region for all nature lovers... and beautiful panoramas!
long_description:
The route starts on the central path leading to the large cedars before taking the Portalas path (marked in yellow) a few metres further on. You proceed downhill on a more or less wide path punctuated by information panels on the flora. At km 1.1, the route takes a winding path. Don't hesitate to take a few breaks on the way up to admire the Cedar forest from above!
You then continue between boxwoods and oak groves until you reach the panoramic viewpoint over the South Luberon and the Durance. Here too, a small natural curiosity awaits you: the Portalas Arch. The way back is through the undergrowth. It is not uncommon to see huts built from branches (fun for children).
After these beautiful discoveries, you will be able to see the "Arche du Portalas".
After these beautiful discoveries, you arrive again on the forest track to reach the car park.

title: Senda Sursilvana A: Oberalp Pass - Disentis
long_description:
The Senda Sursilvana - star of the high-altitude trails - is a multi-day hike from the Oberalp Pass to Chur. It is signposted throughout.

Good footwear is recommended, as the different terrain with mountain paths, corridor and forest paths, stream crossings and steep slopes is very varied. Some sections have to be covered on hard surface. Magnificent views, nature experiences and cultural sights characterise the hiking trail. The area is well served by public transport, so that the long-distance hike can be interrupted at will.

The selected tour covers the Oberalp Pass-Disentis section. Special features of this stage are the scattered former Walser settlements and - in contrast - today's development for winter tourism. The numerous chapels along the way and the Disentis Monastery bear witness to the cultural wealth of this ecclesiastical centre. In early summer, the hiker descends through alpine rose bushes from the pass landscape to flowering alpine pastures and mountain meadows. The villages are protected from avalanches by afforestation and barriers. In Sedrun there is an access tunnel to the New Alpine Transversal through the Gotthard.

From the station of the Matterhorn-Gotthard Railway on the Oberalp Pass, the path leads in a north-easterly direction up to the Tiarms Pass (2148 m.a.s.l.). From here it is worth making a detour to Calmut (2309 m.a.s.l.), an excellent vantage point. We continue along the path over alpine pastures, cross Val Val and climb again to Cuolm Val (2180 m), from where we overlook most of the Vorderrhein valley. Descending eastwards, we reach the summer village of Milez and cross the Val Giuv above Mulinatsch. A little below the Maiensässe of Liets, the trail branches off in an easterly direction into Val Milà, continues above Rueras into Val Strem and from there down to Sedrun. East of Sedrun railway station, the route runs along the railway line, over the viaduct at Bugnei and on through the picturesque villages of Mompé Tujetsch, Segnas and Acletta to the monastery village of Disentis.

Note(s)
The route can also be hiked in reverse.

The Zürichsee Trail shows the multifaceted region at its best. Along the way, there are historic towns and villages, castle parks and villa quarters, but also intact lakeside landscapes, extensive forests and wild ravines to discover. On its ten stages, the Zürichsee-Weg offers further enjoyment: several restaurants, from simple country pubs to gourmet restaurants, as well as first-class wineries are literally along the way. In addition, there are many sports and leisure facilities, museums, cinemas and B&Bs.

Thus, on the lake circuit, hiking purists, nature, culture and history lovers, gourmets and sports enthusiasts all get their money's worth in equal measure. The starting points of the hike can be freely chosen from the ten stage locations. For once, the goal is not specific places, but the path and its pearls.

10th stage: Küsnacht - Zürich Burgwies

From Küsnachter Tobel, the path leads to Schübelweiher and Rumensee, where there are picturesquely situated resting places. What a surprise: the lower part of the Werenbach Tobel lies in the middle of Zürich, but is far away from the hustle and bustle of the city.

title: Royal stage Lag Brit
short_description: High above the Surselva, and below the craggy cliffs of Piz Cavardiras and Piz Run, the sunny path with its great views leads past the small lakes Lag Serein and Lag Crest Ault to Lag Brit.

title: Järnleden - the Iron Trail in Värmland north of Kristinehamn
short_description: Järnleden means "iron trail". The Järnleden runs on old winding paths that were partly used in the 17th century. On it, the first iron transports went from the Bergslagen mining area down to Lake Vänern.
long_description:
Järnleden - the Iron Trail is one of Sweden's 10 most beautiful hiking trails, according to the Swedish daily newspaper Expressen.The explanation is found in the versatility of this trail. It starts in the dense forest. Then it continous across meadows and fields passes lakes and tiny red swedish houses "stuga", over the moor and forest roads, until you reach the end on the archipelago of the largest Swedish lake - the Vänern.
On this trail you will experience all of Sweden at 30km.

title: सुखना झील ट्रैक
short_description: यह ट्रेल सुखना झील के किनारे की सड़क है जिसमे साइकिलिस्ट, हाइकर्स, और टूरिस्ट सैर का आनंद लेते है।
long_description:
ट्रेल मार्ग एक डामर की पक्की सड़क है जो सुखना झील के किनारे होकर जाती है। रास्ता एकदम समतल और बढ़िया है। पूरा रास्ते के दौरान झील और उसके हरियाले किनारे दिखाई देते हैं। प्रवासी पक्षी भी झील में तैरते हुए दिख सकते हैं। झील में बोटिंग भी होती है और ज्यादातर नावें हंस के आकर वाली हैं।
ट्रेल बेहद आसान है और बच्चे, बूढ़े, जवान सभी इसका आनंद ले सकते हैं। ट्रेल पार्किंग से शुरू होकर सुखना लेक व्यू पॉइंट तक जाती है जहाँ से सुखना का सुन्दर दृश्य दिखाई देता है। बसंत या फिर मानसून के बाद के महीने यहाँ आने का सबसे बढ़िया समय हैं।

सुखना झील में नौकायन का अभ्यास करते हुए पेशेवर खिलाड़ी, चंडीगढ़, भारत।

title: Krimmler Wasserfälle
short_description: The Krimmler Falls are considered to be the highest waterfalls in Europe and are located on the territory of the Hohe Tauern National Park in the Salzburg region near the border of the Tyrol and Carinthia regions.
long_description:
The itinerary includes impressive views of the chain of impressive Krimmler Wasserfälle. The network of waterfalls that rises to a total height of 385 meters gives them the title of the highest waterfalls in Europe. The lower waterfall flows from a height of 140 meters, the middle waterfall flows from a height of 100 meters and the upper waterfall flows from a height of 145 meters. The route is about 4 kilometers in one direction and it goes up next to the falls (of course you can also do only part of it).
Due to the fact that the route is linear, the walking time as well as the distance shown are in one direction only, but at any point on the route you can retrace your steps to the beginning of the route. It is also possible to travel by local shuttles in order to reach the higher parts of the falls. Impressive and terrifying nature awaits travelers there.

title: सोनालियम रेलवे स्टेशन से दूधसागर झरने तक हाईक
short_description: भारत के गोवा राज्य में स्थित दूधसागर जलप्रपात एक शानदार चार स्तरीय झरना ह ै। इस तक आने के लिए हाइकिंग करना टूरिस्टों की सबसे पसंदीदा गतिविधियों म ें है।
long_description:
भारत के गोवा राज्य में स्थित दूधसागर जलप्रपात का देखने से छलकते हुए दूध सा आभास होता है, इसलिए इसका नाम दूधसागर पड़ा जिसका अर्थ है दूध का समुद्र। गोवा में भगवान महावीर अभयारण्य और मोल्लेम राष्ट्रीय उद्यान के अंदर स्थित यह झरना मांडवी नदी समुद्र में मिलने से पहले बनता है। 1017 फीट की ऊंचाई और 100 फीट की औसत चौड़ाई के साथ यह भारत का तीसरा सबसे ऊंचा झरना है।
गर्मियों में यह झरना उतना प्रभावशाली नहीं लगता है क्योंकि तब मांडवी नदी में पानी काफी कम हो जाता है, लेकिन मानसून में लगातार होती बारिश से नदी का जलस्तर बहुत बढ़ जाता है और झरना अपने पूरे जोश में आ जाता है। मानसून और उसके तुरंत बाद झरने की सुंदरता देखते ही बनती है।
यहाँ तक आने के लिए कई अच्छे नेचर ट्रेल, पगडंडियां, और हाइकिंग मार्ग मौजूद हैं।
सोनालियम रेलवे स्टेशन से एक बहुत ही सुन्दर ट्रैकिंग मार्ग सीधे झरने तक आता है। यह मार्ग अच्छी तरह से साइन-पोस्टेड है और इसका रखरखाव भी अच्छा है इसलिए टूरिस्ट इस में ट्रैक करना पसंद करते हैं।
संरक्षित इलाके में होने की वजह से झरने के आसपास का क्षेत्र जैव विविधता वाले हरभरे जंगलों से घिरा हुआ है। यह जंगल कई किस्म के वनस्पति और पशुओं का घर है। झरने के तल पर नीले-हरे पानी का एक सुंदर स्वच्छ तालाब है। पर्यटक इस तालाब में जल क्रीड़ाएं और तैरने के लिए आते हैं। झरने के पास में ही कुछ छोटे घरेलू रेस्त्रां भी हैं जो घर का बना हुआ स्वादिष्ट स्थानीय भोजन गरमागरम उपलब्ध करते हैं।

title: From the lower and upper Steuben Falls to the Heiterwanger and Plen lakes and back via Maale Minster
short_description: A comprehensive hiking route in the west of the Tyrol region with stunning views that passes through a network of beautiful waterfalls, continues towards two beautiful and impressive lakes and returns via a mountain road with a panoramic view of a valley and a suspension bridge
long_description:
This hiking route is comprehensive and it starts at the foot of the lower Steuben Falls, goes up to the upper falls and continues to the Heiterwagner See and Plansee lakes and returns via the Ministersteig.
The first part of this itinerary is relatively simple, short and easy, and it will take you to the foot of the chain of the stunning Stoeven Falls, also a few more meters of walking (slight uphill) will lead you to a path for observing the falls from above, as well as to other waterfalls that cannot be seen from the foot of the path. Later on, the path becomes less organized and it goes up a relatively short ascent towards a great observation deck on the upper Steiben waterfall. Walking a few hundred more meters will lead you to a fork in the path, where you must continue straight and cross the road carefully to the other side. From this point the road to the impressive wooden bridge over the lakes is always straight. From this section you return the same way back, cross the small road again and then go over the bridge to complete the circular route. This bridge will actually lead you to a beautiful panoramic road known as "Ministersteig". This road leads mainly downhill back towards the beginning of the route, but still includes one relatively easy ascent along the way, as well as a fun crossing of a suspension bridge and a view that cannot be seen from any other part of the route.
Click here to view the route that groups all the segments of the trip .
Only the first part of this route is accessible for walking even with strollers (at the foot of the waterfalls and the observation path).

title: Rapperswil-Hurden wooden walkway
short_description: On historical paths from Rapperswil to Hurden. This lake crossing has existed for centuries;
long_description:
This walk starts at the Rapperswil railway station. Go through the railway underpass and a few minutes later you'll already be at the beginning of the attractive wooden walkway. The filigree wooden construction is perfect for observing the rich flora and fauna in this protected natural area. The late Gothic chapel of Unsere Liebe Frau is the terminus of this half-hour walk.

This region was not unknown to the many travelers from the north who knew Lake Zurich and Rapperswil as a stop on their way to Santiago de Compostela, on the route of St. James. A rickety, torturous wooden bridge with loose boards helped them across the lake. Since the 19th century a dam with a road has allowed the traveler to cross at the narrowest point between Rapperswil and Hurden. But the wooden bridge has not been forgotten, and in April 2001 a 841 meter long modern wooden walkway was opened on the site of the old footbridge. Walking across it is an adventure, as one finds oneself in the middle of the lake and at the same time feels solidly connected with both shores. On the Rappeerswil shore the little pilgrims' park is an inviting place to stop and picnic.

title: Egg - Schönboden - Stöcklichrüz - Lachen
short_description: The character of this hike is typically pre-Alpine.
long_description:
(Egg - Schönboden - Stöcklichrüz - Bräggerhof - Vorderegg - Steinegg - Lachen)
This hike is of typical pre-alpine character. It is about 12 km in length, and you will climb 464 meters and descend 892 meters. This hike begins in Egg at an altitude of 855 m. It starts out on a good back road to Oberegg and then proceeds to the Naturfreundehaus (friends of nature) Schönboden, at 1087 m, taking a bit more than an hour. One continues on trails over alpine meadows in the Müligassegg direction to Stöcklichrüz, altitude 1248 m., the highest point of this hike. Then down to Diebishütte, Waldeggli toward the Bräggerhof Restaurant, Schweigrüti, Steinegg and then the Lachen railway station.

title: Todtnauer Wasserfall
short_description: An easy and short route at the foot of the Todtnau Falls near the town of Todtnau in the south of the Black Forest.
long_description:
A short and great hiking route that leads within a few minutes' walk to the foot of the Todtnau waterfall. The waterfall whose height rises to almost 100 meters! Considered one of the highest waterfalls in Germany. The first part of the route, which is a walking distance of only 500 meters, leads to the foot of the waterfall and is paved and specially made accessible for walking with strollers and wheelchairs . The second part of the route goes up to the side of the waterfall and is a walking distance of 200 meters (on it) and is only accessible by foot as it has stairs. In this section, comfortable reclining benches are waiting for you that will allow you a beautiful and fun panoramic view towards the waterfall.
A great place to spend time all year round: in the summer the site is a refreshing pastime, while in the winter months you can marvel at snowy and frozen landscapes.

title: Alp Egg - Oberbächen - Tanzboden - Alp Egg
short_description: Leisurely circular hike from Alp Egg through meadows, woods on alpine and mountain paths.
long_description:
The slowly ascending hiking path from the Alp Egg parking lot runs eastward, at first through meadows on up to the Regelstein, altitude 1315 meters. From now on the path itself is the border dividing the Linth area from the Toggenburg. Sometimes through meadows, sometimes in the woods, up and down but without much difference in altitude, one reaches in approx. 40 minutes the signpost pointing to Alp Wielesch (shortcut 1) as well as straight on to Alp Oberbächen. From the latter one hikes through the woods in the Stotzweid direction, and then on a meadow path that becomes gradually steeper via «Tschochen» and soon reaches Tanzboden (1443m). After a rest one returns on the same path to the «Tschochen» signpost. From here one hikes southwest via Alp Stock to the Bergstrasse, which leads to the Cholwald alpine restaurant at 950m. A few meters beyond the Cholwald, the paved road branches off to the right. At the end of this road lies the Wielesch summer restaurant (1167m). From here one crosses a meadow in a northerly direction, and then, after approx. 100 meters, turns onto a path through the woods. One soon crosses the first forest road and shortly thereafter comes to the second forest road, on which one continues, going northwest. At the end of this gravel road one arrives at the hiking trail created in 1988 by the Gommiswald men's sports club, leading to the Chlosterberg alpine restaurant (1025m). Now comes the last stretch, namely the approx. 20 minutes climb back to our starting point at Alp Egg.

Note(s)
Ideal pre-summer, summer and autumn hike at an altitude varying between 1200 and 1444 meters. An early winter storm in late autumn can make this hike impossible.

title: Erlenbach - Erlenbacher Tobel - Chüelemorgen - Egg
short_description: Hike from Erlenbach über den Tobel zur Egg.
long_description:
The route from the Erlenbach railway station and that from the boat station meet on the Wallenthalstrasse. The hiking path toward Pfluegstein soon branches off. The hike continues up through the Erlenbach Tobel to Höhschutzfall. The path, well cared for by the local tourist office, takes us through a mostly natural area beside a brook. While the path to Kittenmüli continues straight on, we keep to the left. A short detour takes one to the shooting practice site (take the Forchstrasse during shooting practice) and the marked Küsnacht-Egg path to the Tüfi, point 663. An attractive sandstone fountain at the Holzkorporation Erlenbach's forest house was erected in the jubilee year 1991. Passing through the sunny Ruchweid area, one arrives at Hohrüti and the clearing in Chüelenmorgen, where several hiking paths meet. Continuing on toward Egg, take the path through the meadows. To the left is the Waldhof restaurant. The view opens out near the houses in Vorder Guldenen, and here is the start of the descent through the Hinteregger Berg. Coming out of the woods, the village of Egg, parts of the Greifensee and the county seat, Uster, lie before us. The Catholic Church in Egg is worth a visit, with its relic of St. Anthony of Padua. And then it is just a few minutes to the Forchbahn railway station.

Note(s)
Attention: take a detour around the shooting practice site when it is in use!

title: Kühkopf-Knoblochsaue
short_description: The European reserve in the old Rhine bend is home to very beautiful floodplain landscapes left to their own devices.
long_description: In the Kühkopf-Knoblochsaue, the visitor walks through vast riparian forests left to their own devices. In between are vast steppe-like meadows. Countless mistletoes grow on gnarled old trees. At the turning point of the hike, the straightened Rhine is reached. The separation of this bend of the Rhine in 1828 made navigation much easier. Those who wish can get more information on flora and fauna at the information centre.

title: Kuroiwa-Sensui mountain Makinodo Pass - Kuroiwa mountain - Sensui mountain - Chojabaru course
short_description: This course traverses Mt Kuroiwa, Mt Kamiizumizu and Mt Shimoizumizu from Makinotoge Pass and returns to Chojabaru and then to Makinotoge Pass. There are no particularly dangerous parts of the route, and the magnificent Kujyu mountain range and beautiful flowers and trees, such as Miyama-kirishima and Bansoreki, can be admired on this circular route.
long_description:
From the main trailhead, Makinoto Pass, head towards Mt Kuroiwa, opposite Mt Kutsukakeyama (沓掛山). After passing the pavilion, the trail climbs steeply. In June, the Reverdin's Blue flowers, rooted in the little soil between the lava rocks, bloom and provide a spectacular view. On the rocky summit of Mt Kuroiwa, many colourful rhododendrons also bloom. The summit is made of black lava rock, hence the name Kuroiwa-zan (Mt Kuroiwa). From the summit, you can see Mannenyama, the mountains of Yabakei and Kujyu.
The ridge walk from Mt Kuroiwa to Mt Sensuizan with the Kujyu mountain range on your right. Io-zan and Mt Hosho-zan (Mt Hosho), and further on, the majestic Mt Minamata comes into view. Hiijidake, a famous spot for Miyama-kirishima, and the Kujyu mountain range changes its appearance little by little as you walk along the ridge line, allowing you to enjoy magnificent views. From Kami-sensui-mountain, walk through the meadows while admiring the hot spring village of Chojabaru spreading out beneath your feet, and after a steep descent, you will reach the summit of Mt Shimo-sensui-mountain. After a steep descent, the summit of Mt Shimo-Sensui is reached. This is a grassland slope maintained by wildfire, and the walk follows the firebreak from the spring wildfire. This is a viewpoint from which the Iida Plateau can be seen at a glance. After descending through the grassland, you arrive at Chojabaru. From here, we walk along the pleasant Kyushu Nature Trail, a mixture of road and nature trails, back to the Makinodo Pass.

title: Hiking up Sedererstuiben and Stuiben in winter  (1,749 m)
short_description: Wrap up warm, lace up your boots, and have a crack at this solid winter hike up to the central portion of the Nagefluhkette ridge.
long_description:
Starting from the car park in Gunzesried Säge, this circular route will see you head up the sunny, south-facing flanks to the main ridge, traverse between the summits, and then make the journey back down again along a separate trail. Experience winter serenity at its best as well as some excellent views across the Allgäuer Hohchalpen and beyond, stretching even as far as Lake Constance.
Snow conditions on the day will dictate whether you'll want to put on pair of trail spikes, snowshoes, or just your boots, so keep an eye on the weather a few days in advance.

short_description: We went on a scenic and adrenaline-packed joyride through the hinterland of Lake Constance with the road-legal electric sports cars E-Rods;
long_description: The start of our tour was the driving safety centre Fahren Erleben in Steißlingen. Afterwards, we drove a round through the hinterland of Lake Constance, where there are a number of sights and places to stop for refreshments that deserve a stop;

title: Delicious Trail Dolomites 38 km
short_description: Long route of the Delicious Trail Dolomiti, a foot race along the trails of the World Heritage Dolomites, of approximately 38 km and 2,350 metres of positive altitude difference.
long_description: This is a non-competitive race that takes place at the end of September in one of Cortina d'Ampezzo's most naturalistically beautiful and historically rich locations.

title: Running route in the Bay of La Baule
short_description:
At the centre of a 9km bay of fine sand, La Baule beach offers a superb playground for running enthusiasts. The beach is very well maintained, allowing you to run directly on the fine sand at low tide or along the embankment, which is wide enough to accommodate walkers and runners. There is plenty of free parking available at the start or finish of the course, along the embankment or in the surrounding streets.
The course is very easy to set up and run.
long_description:
La Baule beach is one of the longest in Europe. From Pornichet to Le Pouliguen, it stretches for 9km in a circular arc facing océan. Pleasant to run on with your feet in the water, on the fine sand at low tide or on the embankment running along the entire beach, it offers runners or active walkers a great route in any season.

title: Traditional costume and marksmen parade Wiesn
short_description: If you have a festive, complete costume from head to toe, this is the place to be!
long_description: In honour of the silver wedding anniversary of King Ludwig I and Therese of Bavaria, a traditional costume parade was held in Munich for the first time in 1835. This has been held annually since 1950 and is now one of the highlights of the Munich Oktoberfest. On the first Sunday of the Oktoberfest, several thousand participants from various traditional costume and shooting clubs parade in their traditional festive costumes from the Maximilianeum along a seven-kilometre route through Munich city centre to the festival grounds on the Theresienwiese. The procession is led by the Münchner Kindl, Munich's heraldic figure, and accompanied by brass bands and flag-wavers. The associations and groups come mostly from Bavaria, but also from Austria, Switzerland and northern Italy.

title: Fuyoshidake, Himemon Course.
short_description: The highest of the 'three peaks of Kunimi', this is a direct ascent of Mt Fuyoshi. The ascent is a bit strenuous, but the round trip takes about one and a half hours.
long_description: This is a direct route to the summit of Mt Hoyoshidake in Kimotsuki Town in the south-eastern part of the Oosumi Peninsula. There are no particular hazards and the trail is well trodden. However, there are sections where you have to climb along ropes, and you may find the ascent too steep. There is abundant vegetation, including camellias and azaleas. The summit offers a 360° panoramic view of the city of Kanoya, the Takakuma Mountains, Kinko Bay, the Satsuma Peninsula, Yaku Island and Tanegashima Island. The elevation is 967 m and from the summit it is possible to traverse to Mt Kunimi (886.5 m) and Mt Kurozondake (908.5 m), also in the Kunimi mountain range.

title: H.v.B. Etappe 1: Von Elbigenalp zur Hermann von Barth Hütte
short_description:
Die Wanderung von Elbigenalp zur Hermann-von-Barth-Hütte startet im wunderschöne Lechtal, geht vorbei an Almwiesen und durch felsiges Gelände hinauf in die hochalpine Landschaft.
Translate to English
long_description:
Die Tour beginnt im malerischen Dorf Elbigenalp im Tiroler Lechtal. Elbigenalp ist der Heimatort von Anna Stainer-Knittel, deren Leben im Roman "Geierwally" beschrieben wurde und die auch Hauptfigur der Oper "La Wally" von Alfredo Catalani ist. Die ersten hunder Meter gehen an der Freilichtbühne vorbei, wo die Oper aufgeführt wird. Kurz danach führt der Weg durch sanfte Almwiesen und folgt dann einem steileren Pfad in Richtung des Modertalbachs. Die Aussicht auf die umliegenden Gipfel, wie die Freispitze, begleitet dich auf dem gesamten Aufstieg. Nach etwa 3-4 Stunden erreicht man die Hermann-von-Barth-Hütte, benannt nach dem berühmten Alpinisten. Hier bietet sich eine Rast an, um die alpine Umgebung zu genießen. Die Hütte ist ein idealer Ausgangspunkt für weitere Bergtouren, darunter die Besteigung des Hermannskopfes oder die Freispitze. Diese Tour erfordert Trittsicherheit und eine gute Kondition, ist jedoch ein absolutes Highlight für Bergliebhaber, die die Lechtaler Alpen hautnah erleben möchten.

title: Crossing the Seven Falls
short_description: The Traverse of the Seven Falls in the middle of the Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park is a unique and unforgettable experience to get to know the wonders of the Brazilian highlands.
long_description:
Trekking located in the Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park, where the aim is to reach the Sete Quedas Waterfall, small waterfalls, but of considerable width. There you will find several natural pools, which provide unforgettable moments of bathing and relaxation. Before that and all along the route, there are other bathing and water catchment points, such as the famous Cânion 1 and the Rio Preto pass.
The trail is carried out in two stages. The first leg of the 7 Falls Crossing can be done in one day, starting from the Visitor Centre of the Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park and finishing at the campsite 150 metres from the falls. The second stretch can be done in less than a day, departing from the camping area and ending at the GO-239 road, where it is recommended to hire someone to pick you up beforehand. Opened in 2013, the Travessia das 7 Quedas is perfect for lovers of hiking in the midst of nature, as well as being a true invitation to immerse yourself in the cerrado.

title: Trekking up to the Kudremukh peak in Chikmagalur district of Karnataka. India
short_description: Kudremukh is the highest peak in Chikmagalur district of Karnataka and the third highest peak in the state of Karnataka. Located in the Western Ghats (Sahyadri Range), this 1894 meter high peak comes under the Kudremukh National Park.
long_description:
This trail-route is located within the Kudremukh National Park which derives its name from the Kudremukh peak. Kudremukh means 'horse's face' in Kannada language and this mountain peak resembles the face of a horse. The height of this peak is 1892 meters and it is the highest peak in Chikmagalur district.
Part of the Kudremukh National Park is spread over the plains and dense hill forests of the Western Ghats and covers parts of 3 districts (Chikmagalur, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada).
Trekking to Kudremukh Peak is done through medium high hills and valleys. Due to the strong monsoon winds, the growth of trees on the hills here is negligible, as a result of which the muslin green grass gets a chance to grow. Evergreen forests are found in the valleys between these lush green and rounded hills. A unique microclimate is found in these valleys which is helpful in the growth of many species of fungi, mosses, orchids, flowers. Patches of forests interspersed with vast grasslands provide a spectacular sight to the hikers. The fresh air of this region invigorates the body. During trekking, one can also spot many wild species of flora, birds, reptiles, amphibians, butterflies, and insects etc.

title: Hike to the Scheibum and the Fatima Chapel Ammergau Alps
short_description:
Beautiful hike from Saulgrub station to the Ammer breakthrough Scheibum. Then via the Höhenwanderweg and the Fatima Chapel back to the station.
The Saulgrub railway station can be reached from Munich main station and Pasing within 90 minutes. Change trains in Murnau.
The hike is a leisurely low-mountain hike with a stop at the Achelschwaig inn, which has a cosy parlour, a sunny beer garden and good cuisine.
long_description:
This hiking trail is easy to walk, even if it sometimes drags on a bit. For northern Germans it is a good introduction to hiking in the Ammergau Alps, for southern Germans a nice walk. There are only really steep passages on the section from the Acheleschwaig inn down to the Ammer. On the way back, you can then stop there as a reward.
The tour starts and ends at Saulgrub station, which can be reached from Munich main station within 90 minutes, change in Murnau to the train waiting there to Oberamergau.
The highlights on the way are the Ammer breakthrough Scheibum with the Kammerl power station next to it, the high trail above Saulgrub with fantastic views over the Ammer valley and the Fatima chapel idyllically situated on a mountain ridge.

title: Walk through the Bouconne forest
short_description: This beautiful loop takes you to the heart of the Bouconne forest, a place much appreciated by walkers, near Toulouse. A route of almost 10 km for a walk in the middle of nature, passing by the Bordette lake and the old telegraph station.
long_description: With a surface area of 2,700 ha, the Bouconne forest, managed by the Office National des Forêts, offers many shady paths and tracks.

title: über den Mirador Kaqasiiwaan zur Nariz del Indio
short_description:
schöne Tour mit knackigen Anstiegen von San Juan La Laguna über den Mirador Kaqasiiwaan zur Nariz del Indio
Translate to English
long_description:
Die Tour startet in San Juan La Laguna am Aufstieg zum Mirador Kaqasiiwaan (Eintritt ca. 4€). Man folgt zunächst den Treppen zum Aussichtspunkt. Oben angelangt hält man sich links (vorbei an den Toiletten) und folgt einem Trampelpfad der allmählich ansteigt und relativ steil wird. Nach einiger Zeit kommt eine kleine Aussichtsplattform. Wenig später teilt sich der Weg: hier folgen wir dem Pfad nach unten (linke Abzweigung, blauer Pfeil im Bild). Dies ist der Weg, dem wir bis nach oben folgen. Wir klettern eine morsche Treppe hoch und erreichen etwa eine halbe Stunde später den Gipfel, wo wir mit einer schönen Aussicht belohnt werden. Für den Rückweg gibt es nun 3 Wege: denselben Weg zurück, nach Santa Clara (und von dort aus mit dem Bus zurück) oder über den Mirador La Mano (auch hier muss man Eintritt zahlen, ca. 6€). Wir haben uns für letzteres entschieden und sind dann (nach Absprache mit der Eigentümerin) über ein Privatgrundstück abgestiegen bis wir wieder an der Kreuzung waren, an der wir anfangs nach links unten abgebogen sind. Von hier aus folgt man wieder dem Weg zum Mirador Kaqasiiwaan und den Treppen ins Dorf. Obwohl die Tour sehr steil und anstrengend ist, lohnt es sich absolut!
Translate to English

title: Büyükada Walking Route
short_description: This day trip route in Büyükada is one of the alternative routes that can be done with pleasure
long_description:
The pleasure of living in Büyükada is different. Travelling on the island not only allows you to enjoy the nature, but also takes you on a unique journey of history and culture. 
This easy Büyükada walking route is just one of the routes you can add to your Büyükada sightseeing routes and make it a reality. This route, which is ideal for those looking for a route that includes history and culture as well as natural landscapes for the weekend, starts right from the pier. On the route, which is accompanied by some special historical spots and island streets in the island, you can catch beautiful views where you can take beautiful photos. From one end of the island to the other end of the island, you end the route again near the pier.
You can try this route, which is a fun route for those who are never bored of travelling in Büyükada and who are looking for routes that blend nature, history and culture together.

title: A thermal trough through the Hortobágy and the Tisza
short_description: Soaking in warm water after a long roll is always a turn-off. This thermal torrent connects the 18 thermal baths of the Hortobágy and the Tisza in a cycle tour lasting several days.
long_description: On this series of tours, we'll tackle the country's first National Park and the Szőke Tisza on thermal water and two wheels. Starting from Hajdúszoboszló, one of the country's most visited health resorts, we cross the Hortobágy National Park. Then we will make several turns along the streets and embankments of small villages, and visit the main canal of Nagykunság for a short stretch. The main watercourse of the tour is the Tisza, whose embankments we will walk along from the right and left, from Nagykörüta through Lake Tisza to Tiszalök. On the last stages of the tour, we will dive again in the Hortobágy wilderness and then return to the Szoboszló spa resort. As well as exploring the thermal baths, we will have plenty of opportunity to admire the wonders of the puszta and the water world in this beautiful corner of the Alföld.

title: Tour through the Todenbach and Katzenbach Valleys
short_description: A challenging jogging route on field and forest paths
long_description: The jogging route leads largely through a stretch of forest between Schwalmstadt and Gilserberg in the Schwalm-Eder district. The circular route starts in Allendorf at the Landsburg. First it goes through the Schwalmaue and then through the Todenbachtal up the path to Teufelsberg s peak. After reaching the highest point of the tour at 365 m, we go down into the Katzbach valley and from there to Rommershausen. From here we walk back on the cycle path via Dittershausen to Allendorf.

title: Vorderthal-Pfäffikon panoramic trail
short_description: Hike with great views über dem Zürichsee.
long_description:
After crossing the Aa, we proceed to the right along the road in the direction of Schrot, Gfall and then to Stalden at an altitude of 673 m. A beautiful view of Lake Zurich, the Linth valley, the March and Höfe accompanies us to Pfäffikon. We continue through Ob. Brätten, Mutzenrüti, and Eggli at 646 m, where a short time later we cross the Spreitenbachtobel. A short climb up to Zug at 750 m takes us then across meadows and forest trails via Schweigrüti and Rietsch in the direction of Autis at 661 m, to Bilsten. Crossing Schwändi at 684 m and Talweid, we arrive in Pfäffikon at 412 m.

This hike is especially to be recommended when the fruit trees are in blossom.

One can make this hike in the reverse direction as well.

title: Breezes
short_description: The unmistakable pyramid of Brisen, which dominates the entire area, is one of the most popular touring destinations in Central Switzerland in all seasons.

The distinctive "pyramid" of Brisen is the area's focal point as well as one of central Switzerland's most popular hiking destinations. Its appeal lies in the panoramic view, the peace and quiet as well as the magnificent surrounding landscapes. The tour leads over alpine pastures to Risetenstock and then over the Glattigrat ridge up to the majestic Brisen. In the area between Risetenstock and Glattigrat you can often spot ibex.

title: A fast river tour on a paved road
long_description:
On the best surface and always a bit downhill, along the picturesque Töss: The skating and biking trail between Bauma and Kollbrunn is one of the best and most attractive in the country.

The picturesque route along the Töss is always slightly downhill. It can be traveled a shorter or longer distance, as there is always a railway station where one can catch the S26.
We start at the Bauma railway station and skate carefully along the sidewalk of the main road to Sennhüttenstrasse. There one turns right and then crosses the Töss. After 500 meters of skating along the river, one goes uphill for a short distance, the last real climb on this route to Kollbrunn. Following the red route signs, one passes through a residential area and then arrives at a small road that takes one back to the banks of the Töss. A bit later, one goes through Saland and by the Au pond. After the bridge comes the best part of the route. On the very best asphalt one glides along the Töss in a wooded area. If you'd like to rest a bit after this short stretch, you'll find lovely gravel banks and places to swim.
Then it's on to Wila, where you cross the river and pass under the railway and the Tösstalstrasse. You'll then arrive in Turbenthal. Finding your way is simple: just follow the red route signs. The last part of the route also runs directly along the Töss. Because it is always slightly downhill, one can easily get up to speeds of 30 mph. Now it is only an hour to the Kollbrunn railway station and on to the local train back to Bauma.

title: Aydos Pond - Aydos Castle
short_description: Nature walking route between the magnificent Aydos Gölü and Aydos Castle
long_description:
Aydos is a marvellous place to walk, with its woodland, gölü and castle, which make this area even more unique. 
The oxygen-rich and green Aydos forest is one of the rare areas where you can enjoy nature in a crowded city like Istanbul. Located in an area surrounded by Kartal, Pendik and Sultanbeyli, this natural wonder is extremely good for both your body and soul. 
There are many routes that you can walk between the castle and the castle in the forest. This route between Göl and the castle is just one of them. We start from the Göl stage and walk through the forest until the castle and return back the same way. Our walk lasts approximately 8.5 kilometres in total and this activity meets our daily sports needs and helps us to stay fit. 
The route offers the opportunity to visit the castle at the beginning and end points. If you want to discover the natural beauties of Istanbul with your friends, you can try this route.

title: Mule Track
long_description:
For some 600 years (1230 till 1830) Horgen was considered a significant goods trade center on the North-South axis.
The «Sust» harbor of Horgen was where costly goods were loaded on mules and later on pack animals. Today, the mule track leading from the Sust and over the Hirzel to Sihlbrugg is indicated as a cultural path by means of brown signs.

title: Mörbylångaleden - Signature route Öland from the bridge to the southern cape of Öland
short_description: STF Signature Trail - From Färjestaden, the 85 km long Mörbylångaleden hike passes through herbaceous lakes, sand dunes, pebble beaches and villages of ancient origin.
long_description:
The Mörbylångaleden, STF's signature trail on Öland, runs through the rugged and beautiful landscape. The Öland Signature Trail offers fantastic experiences for both new and experienced hikers and is a typical signature trail.
The hiking trail "Signaturled på Öland" is divided into five stages. It is marked with red wooden arrows.
There are picnic areas with shelters, fireplaces, basic toilets and information boards about Öland's culture, history and nature
To hike the signature trail you need 5 hiking days, 4-8 hours per day
Day 1: Öland Tourist Office - Linné Station, Skogsby. Time: 6-7 hours hiking, distance: 18 km
Departure 2: Station Linné, Skogsby - Mörbylånga torg. Time: 4-5 hours hiking, distance: 12 km
Stage 3: Mörbylånga square - Kastlösa. Time: 7-8 hours hiking, distance:20 km
Stage 4: Kastlösa - Gammalsby. Time: 7-8 hours hiking, distance: 22 km
Stage 5: Gammalsby - Ottenby (hostel) Time: 4-5 hours hiking, distance: 12 km

title: The Caravelle loop
short_description: The Caravelle trail takes you all the way around the reserve. Along the way, you'll enjoy breathtaking panoramic views.
long_description:
Over 10 million years old, the Presqu'île de la Caravelle is the oldest part of Martinique, alongside Sainte-Anne. Nestling on the Atlantic coast, it extends some ten kilometres into the ocean.
Its tip is currently designated as a protected nature reserve, part of the Martinique Regional Nature Park.

title: Hiking route Holterberg viewpoint
short_description: During this route you will hike from Holten to the Holterberg viewpoint.
long_description: This route runs right across the Salland Ridge. The national park gets its name from the 26 hills found in the area. A small river also runs through the area and you will find beautiful forests and heathland. Furthermore, the Salland Ridge is the habitat for many different plants and animals. For example, you will find last population of grouse.

title: धनकर झील ट्रैक
short_description: धनकर झील एक हिमालयी अल्पाइन झील है जिस तक धनकर गा ँव से एक घंटे की हाईक के बाद पंहुचा जा सकती है। यह हाईकर की श ारीरिक सहनशक्ति को चुनौती देने वाली एक खड़ी चढ़ाई वाली क ठिन ट्रेल है।
long_description:
धनकर झील ट्रैक हिमाचल प्रदेश की स्पीति घाटी के धनकर गाँव से शुरू होता है और एक बंजर, कच्ची पगडण्डी से होकर 5 किलोमीटर दूर धनकर झील तक जाता है। झील तक पहुंचने की यही अकेली ट्रेल है। इतना छोटा रास्ता के बावजूद यह निश्चित तौर पर एक बहुत कठिन ट्रैक है। ट्रैक के शुरुआती और गंतव्य बिंदु में 1600 फ़ीट (500 मीटर) से भी ज्यादा का अंतर है। धनकर गाँव के तापमान के मुकाबले झील इलाके का तापमान कमशकम 5 डिग्री सेल्सियस कम रहता है और झील के आसपास ज्यादातर समय ठंडी बर्फीली हवाएँ चलती रहती हैं।
वैसे समुद्र तल से 4300 मीटर की ऊंचाई पर स्थित झील बेहद सुन्दर है और आठ महीने जमी रहती है। इसे हिमालय की बर्फ़ से ढकी हुई चोटियां घेरे हुए हैं और ग्लेशियर का पानी इसके जलस्तर को रिचार्ज करता रहता है। इस झील की एक और खासियत यह भी है की यह अलग अलग कोणों से कभी हरी तो कभी नीली और कभी गहरी नीली दिखाई देती है।
इस ट्रैक को करने का सबसे अच्छा समय केवल मई के मध्य से सितंबर तक ही है क्यूंकि उसके बाद सर्दियों में यहाँ का मौसम बेहद कठिन और ना सहने वाला हो जाता है। कई बार तो यहाँ पहुंचने वाला मार्ग भी ब्लॉक हो जाता है।

short_description: Beautiful tour around the picturesque Wägitalersee.
long_description:
This simple hiking path takes you from Innerthal to the idyllically situated Wägitalersee lake. During the 20's, this artificial lake was created in the midst of beautiful mountain surroundings.

The Bockmattli is a very well known mountain for climbing. Special mention should be made of the 200 somewhat unknown caves in the Wägital valley as well as the 22 cultivated alps. In addition to fishing, jogging, skating, biking, hiking, climbing and swimming, boats can also be rented and horse and buggy rides taken around the lake.

title: Mittlerwengi - Chüemettler - Bogmen - Mittlerwengi
short_description: Steep but rewarding hike from and to Mittlerwengi.
long_description:
From Mittlerwengi one climbs up to Alp Hinterwengi (1321 m), from there with very little difference in altitude into the Wengital toward Chüemettler. The narrow mountain trail, which now climbs rapidly, takes one in approx. half an hour to Chüemettler-Furggen (1603 m). In order to reach the peak of Chüemettler one must hike along the Chüemettler ridge. Now we come to the steep, but well-made mountain path along the west flank. From the Chüemettler peak, approx. 100 meters to the south, a yellow sign shows the start of the trail down to Alp Obere Bogmen. Although this path is steep, there are metal railings or strong ropes for the safety of the hiker along the most difficult sections. And once you have the first hundred meters of this descent behind you, you can be proud to have accomplished the most difficult phase of this hike. Soon you will reach the next stopping point, the Alp Obere Bogmen (1383 m). From there it is only 20 minutes down through the «Striggital» to your starting point.

Note(s)
You need good equipment!

title: Crossing Petrópolis - Teresópolis
short_description: The crossing between the two mountain cities of Petrópolis and Teresópolis, in the state of Rio de Janeiro, is one of the most famous in Brazil and is also considered one of the most beautiful.
long_description:
Included in the National Park of Serra dos Órgãos - PARNASO - the recommended duration of the Traverse é of 3 days, so that you can take greater advantage of its stunning landscapes. There is a total distance of 30 kilometres between the two locations and you reach an altitude of 2,275 metres. The best time to walk is during the drier months, normally from May to September.
The first day begins at the Park's headquarters in Petrópolis and goes on to the Açu Shelter, place for the first overnight stay. The walk is relatively short, approximately 8km, but due to the high altitude variation (1,145) it is the most demanding part of the route. The 2nd day connects the two shelters of this route: the Açu Shelter and Shelter 4, in Pedra do Sino. But before starting the walk, the day begins with a spectacular sunrise on the Serra dos Órgãos, which can be contemplated from the Pedra do Açu or the Portals of Hércules.The 3rd day consists only of the descent from Pedra do Sino to the Teresó Polis Headquarters of the Park. There are approximately 11 kilometers of descent with beautiful views of the city of Teresópolis and the Parque Estadual dos Tresós Picos.

short_description: A circular hiking route in the Schwartz-Bach gorge, south of the city of Nuremberg in southern Germany
long_description:
A circular hiking trail of short-medium length, mainly flat (ascent with a minimal gradient) that runs along the side of a stream surrounded by a huge rock canyon in the Schwartz-Bach gorge. A great hiking route for those who love water. The length of the route described in this summary is about 4.5 kilometers, but halfway through it can be shortened.
The nature of the path makes it inaccessible to strollers and wheelchairs.

title: Oberricken - Chrüzegg - Oberricken
short_description: Hike from Oberricken to the Chrüzegg viewpoint
long_description:
Starting at the Oberricken parking lot, one climbs for 5 minutes up the road toward Ricken, arriving at the «Bodenwis« and continuing on the paved road in the direction of Hinter Laad and Heid. The road to Hint. Laad is paved, and then a gravel road runs to the little hamlet of Heid (1008m). After passing this farm, one climbs up to Laad (913m), where one makes a 180-degree turn. From now on it is uphill in the Chrüzegg direction via Höch-Laad - Eggli - Hint. Eggli - Unt. Tweralp - Ob. Tweralp. 15 minutes more to the Chrüzegg lookout. At first one descends a bit, passing the Gr. Rotstein, the Hint. Rotstein and the Vord. Rotstein. Now the path gets steeper and one hikes up over the Hüttenberg to the starting point in Oberricken.

title: Schänis - Federihüttli - Federispitz - Schänis
short_description: Once you are in this host village with its 3,500 inhabitants, the main direction of the hiking route is already clear, because from the village with its 3,500 inhabitants, the Federi massif is simply impossible to miss and the final destination is already clearly recognisable.
long_description:
As soon as one arrives in this village with its 3500 residents, the direction of the hiking route becomes obvious. One cannot miss the Federimassiv - the goal of the hike.

Starting at the Schänis railway station, one walks along the main road toward the village center, leaving this road after approx. 150 meters, at the Rathausplatz. At the Rathaus fountain the route wends its way between rows of houses, crosses through a new group of buildings and is already through the most heavily populated part of the village. Now all one has to do is follow the yellow hiking signposts to Ledi (520m) - Wasserhüttli - Federi-Seilbahnstation - Federiwald - Federihüttli - Federigrat - Federispitz.

From Federispitz you'll descend the east side of the mountain by taking the path down to Alp Obernäten - Schwanten at the Federigrat (1701m) signpost, instead of returning to the Federihüttli. You'll reach the Schänis Bergstrasse and follow it into Schänis village.

Note(s)
The Federihüttli is open every weekend from Whitsuntide to the end of October, under the auspices of the «Federiclub», and even every day during the summer school vacation. The view of the Linth area is superb!
You can also stay overnight. Tel: +41 (0)55 615 14 41 or, when no one is there, President Kurt Schoch, +41 (0)55 615 27 48.

title: Wädenswil - Schlieregg - Hirzel - Au
short_description: Scenic hike from Wädenswil
long_description:
Leaving the Wädenswil railway station, we stroll through the attractive village center, and then go gradually uphill and then more steeply to Rötibodenholz, where we cross under the limited-access highway. After passing through the Waggital, Aahalden and Mugeren, we find the Schlieregg picnic area just the place to relax and enjoy the view. From there the charming village of Hirzel is not far. Key words for Hirzel: Johanna Spyri, Meta Heusser and the Doktorhaus. One can learn more about the author of «Heidi» in the town museum, the former schoolhouse. And now comes the highest point of the hike, at 755 m, shortly after Vorderen Höhe. We make a sharp turn in Hirzel-Höhi and pass around the Chruzelenmoss nature preserve, cross (careful!) the heavily traveled highway over the Hirzel and start down to the Aamüli. The hiking trail leading through Fuchsenbüel is only a few years old, and soon we see the many buildings of Au-Wädenswil. Our hike ends at the Au railway station.

The path goes to the right up to the Neuhof industrial area and through the beautiful hamlet of Fägswil to the Pilgersteg, from where it follows part of the Route of St. James and finally leads via Breitenmatt on attractive hiking paths to Hasenstrick. From Breitenmatt your destination, the Bachtel (1115 m altitude), is marked by signs. You can choose the return trip either to Girenbad, Wernetshausen, Hadlikon, Oberdürnten or to Wald, in all of which public transportation is available.

title: मायोंग ट्रेल
short_description: यह ट्रैक असम के मायोंग शहर के पास में घने पाबिटोरा वन्यजीव अभयारण्य के अंदर जाता है।

मायोंग ट्रेल 6 किलोमीटर लम्बी लूप ट्रेल है जो मायोंग शहर की कजली मायोंग रोड (राज्य राजमार्ग 38) के पास वाली वन रेंज ऑफिस रोड से शुरू होकर पोबिटोरा वन्यजीव अभयारण्य के अंदर जाती है। यह एक आसान और सरल नेचर ट्रेल है जो हरियाली, पक्षियों, और जंगली पेड़ पौधों का आनंद उठाने के लिए एकदम फिट है।
यह ट्रैक जंगलों, चट्टानों, और हरियाली से भरी नेचर ट्रेल से होते हुए पोबिटोरा अभयारण्य में करीब 3 किलोमीटर तक अंदर जाता है। ट्रेल की शुरुआत में वन विभाग के ऑफिस से अनुमति लेना जरूरी है। दिन में कुछ सीमित संख्या में ही हाइकर्स को अनुमति दी जाती है और प्रवेश शुल्क लागू हो सकता है।
