title: Zurich's 5-Lake Hike
short_description: Beautiful hike from Bäch to Schönenberg past lakes.
long_description:
This hike starts at the Bäch railway station, going in the Richterswil direction. Before the underpass one must turn right to the Richterswil lake path (1st lake). Continue past the Schönenwerd island and the beach to the Richterswil railway station. Through the underpass and then left along the warehouse to the first fork to the right. Then cross the ring road and take the Gartenstrasse to the traffic circle at Wachthausplatz. Between Zugerstrasse and Schwyzerstrasse there is a footpath running south up the hill; follow this to the first cross street. Then turn right and follow the side street to the sign «Fussweg Mülitobel». And now through the romantic Mülibachtobel to the Sternen pond (2nd lake). Go around the pond on its east and south sides (dam) and hike on the Samstagern road to the underpass under the Südostbahn railway. Immediately after the underpass turn left and then after approx. 100 m left again on the new path. At the next junction turn right, and go south to the Jtlimoos pond (3rd lake). Before reaching the pond turn right to the Neumühle and then on to the Hüttner pond (4th lake). Proceed along the pond to the west. Short climb via Laubegg to the Sägel. Cross the Hütten-Schönenberg road and walk along toward Hütten for 75 m. Turn right after the first farmhouse in the Gschwänd direction to the Tüfenbach pond (5th lake).

title: A walk around Sochi Park
short_description: Just one step before a fairy tale. And that step can start at Sochi Park. The Fairytale Park in Sochi makes entertaining dreams come true, not just for the child, but for the adult as well.
long_description:
A fascinating stroll through Sochi Park can be broken up into an entire happy day. The park has grown to encompass a large area and includes many entertaining rides from which you will not be bored. On the territory of the park & ëquo;sits» a great and very fairy castle-hotel «bogatyr». At night it is illuminated and offers views of genuine, unimaginable beauty, and it's probably more beautiful even outside than inside. The lake near the castle gives it a natural heritage spirit, as if it was born at the bottom of the Black Sea and surfaced on the Sochi Park site.
In addition to the fairytale castle there is a Dolphinarium in the park. The shows with dolphins start from 7th July. <As of 27 July, the park will also host co-op in Baba Yaga's Residence, and petting zoo «Lapushki» Eco Village.
There are also many different playgrounds and attractions for children, as well as for those who are able to pay for their own entertainment on a grand scale. In short, the park offers everything not only to keep you entertained but also to make you feel at home in your own unique way.

title: Snowshoe Trail Gotthard
short_description:
Meditative but sporty snowshoe trail in incredibly peaceful nature
.
Important: Walk on the signposted snowshoe trails at your own risk. Please pay attention to the current avalanche situation and wildlife rest zones
.
long_description: The snowshoe trail starts at the roundabout in Hospental. The round tour is sporty and meditative at the same time. Absolute peace and nature characterise the trail towards the Gotthard Pass. A mysterious silence fills the snow-covered mountain world. First on the Gotthard Pass road to Gamsboden. Then the valley opens up and the gigantic mountain world lies before you. You are now on the Gamsboden, where, especially in spring, chamois flock to get hold of the first grasses after the long winter. The way back on the Gotthard pass road is then a return to civilisation.

title: Southern Iceland (Golden Circle 2)
short_description: A varied day trip with guaranteed views: In addition to spectacular geysers, an impressive crater lake and a mysterious cave await you.
long_description: The eighth stage of the route stretches over about 170 km and leads from the interior over impressive fjord landscapes to the southwest coast of Iceland. The day's stage includes the crater lake Kerið, the mysterious Arnarker Pit and the two geysers "Great Geyser" and Strokkur. Some of these sights are classic stops on the so-called "Golden Circle," a popular tourist route that runs through southwestern Iceland near the capital city of Reykjavík. A historical site is also on the program: the village of Þingvellir, site of the oldest existing parliament in the world, is one of many sights along the route.

title: South Iceland (Golden Circle 1)
short_description: The darkest stage of the multi-day tour through Iceland leads to legendary natural sites whose legends have been spread and kept alive for centuries.
long_description: The spectacular Cape Dyrhólaey, with its mystical cliff, inspires visitors with its interesting rock formations and sends shivers down the spine. The equally impressive waterfall Skógafoss also has a story to tell that goes back centuries. The Secret Lagoon geothermal baths, on the other hand, are much more relaxing; probably the country's oldest swimming pool, they offer spectacular views and a very special kind of bathing pleasure. Another highlight for nature enthusiasts is the Lava Centre, a modern information centre that offers a playful and visual insight into thousands of years of geological history. Some of these attractions are classic stops on the so-called Golden Circle, a popular tourist route that runs through the southwest of Iceland near the capital Reykjavik.

title: The lower and upper Stoeven Falls and up Minster
short_description: A circular hiking route from the foot of the lower Steuben Falls through the upper Steuben Falls in the Tyrol and back via the Ministersteig
long_description:
This itinerary is beautiful and includes several special points of interest throughout. The first part of this itinerary is relatively simple, short and easy, and it will take you to the foot of the chain of the stunning Stoeven Falls, also a few more meters of walking (slight uphill) will lead you to a path for observing the falls from above, as well as to other waterfalls that cannot be seen from the foot of the path.
Later on, the path becomes less organized and it goes up a relatively short (but slightly steep) ascent towards a wonderful observation deck on the upper Stoeven waterfall. Walking a few more meters uphill will lead you to the bridge you turn to in order to complete the circular route, this bridge will lead you to a beautiful panoramic road known as "Ministersteig". This road leads mainly downhill back towards the beginning of the route, but still includes one relatively easy ascent along the way, as well as a fun crossing of a suspension bridge and a view that cannot be seen from any other part of the route.
Click here to view the route that groups all the segments of the trip .
Only the first part of this route is accessible for walking even with strollers (at the foot of the waterfalls and the observation path).

title: Rund um den Goldbergsee
short_description: Eine ca. einstündige Wanderung, die hauptsächlich auf Schotterwegen verläuft und schöne Ausblicke auf die umliegenden Sehenswürdigkeiten sowie auf Tier- und Pflanzenarten bietet.
long_description: Auf dem größtenteils aus Schotter bestehenden Weg kann man gemütlich ohne nennenswerte Steigungen den Goldbergsee umrunden. Große Wiesenflächen sowie zahlreiche Bänke laden zum Verweilen in der abwechslungsreich bepflanzten Landschaft ein. So sind sowohl verschiedene Landschaftsbäume als auch Hecken und Obstbäume zu finden. Das Naturschutzgebiet "Vogelfreistätte Glender Wiesen" bietet zudem Lebensräume für Watt- und Wasservögel und ergänzt damit die Lebensraumvielfalt. Neben der großen Tier- und Pflanzenwelt bietet der Weg auch immer wieder schöne Aussichtspunkte mit Blick auf Schloss Callenberg und die Veste Coburg.

title: Hopfensee Panorama Rundwanderung
short_description:
Traumhafte Bergpanoramen gespiegelt im Wasser entlang des ebenen Hopfenseeuferwegs.
Translate to English
long_description:
Die an jeder Stelle des Hopfenseeuferwegs startbare ebene Rundwanderung bietet am West-Süd-Ost-Ufer traumhafte Ausblicke auf das Ammergebirge, die Spitzen der Nord-Tiroler Berge und der Pfrontner Berge. Am Nord- und Ostufer finden sich zahlreiche Stege, Ruhe- und Badeplätze sowie diverse Einkehrmöglichkeiten. Während der Weg am Westufer durch Feuchtwiesen und Schilf führt, führt er im Süden durch ein schattiges Waldstück.

title: H.v.B. Etappe 2: von Hermann von Barth Hütte zum Waltenbergerhaus
short_description:
Die alpine Etappe von der Hermann-von-Barth-Hütte zum Waltenbergerhaus führt durch hochalpines Gelände und bietet fantastische Ausblicke auf die Lechtaler Alpen und die Mädelegabel.
Translate to English
long_description:
Von der Hermann-von-Barth-Hütte aus beginnt der Weg mit einem steilen Anstieg in hochalpines Gelände. Der Weg ist teils ausgesetzt und verlangt Trittsicherheit und Schwindelfreiheit. Die Tour führt über Geröllfelder und steinige Abschnitte, bis du schließlich die Einsattelung zwischen den Lechtaler Alpen und der Allgäuer Hauptkette erreichst. Hier bieten sich einmalige Ausblicke auf die umliegenden Gipfel, darunter die imposante Mädelegabel. Diese anspruchsvolle Tour ist für erfahrene Wanderer gedacht und führt über steile Pfade und teils ausgesetzte Stellen.
Von der Mädelegabel weiter (hier auch Abzweigung zur Kemptner Hütte) führt der Weg zum Waltenbergerhaus durch karge, felsige Landschaften und ist nur für geübte Wanderer geeignet. Nach etwa 4-5 Stunden erreichst du das Waltenbergerhaus auf 2.085 m Höhe. Die Hütte liegt malerisch im Herzen der Allgäuer Alpen und ist ein idealer Ausgangspunkt für Besteigungen der Mädelegabel oder für den Heilbronner Weg, einer der bekanntesten Höhenwege der Region.

title: Kidstour Disentis - Cumpadials
short_description: Family hike from Disentis to Cumpadials
long_description:
This tour is ideal for hot days when you like to be near the water to cool off. Along the Rhine you will always find nice places to take a foot bath or even a full bath for the brave ones.

Whether you start the tour in Disentis or at the Fontanivas campsite, the first highlight is certainly a visit to the Ustria Fravia in Disla, which you will find right next to the unusual chapel. As the name Fravia suggests, there used to be a blacksmith's shop here, which has been lovingly converted into a restaurant. Various objects on the walls still tell of the old days. The village itself is also a picturesque place.

In a leisurely up and down, the path leads via Madernal and Pardomat to Cumpadials. At the river there is a nice playground with a fireplace and a small swimming lake. The children will be thrilled. From the Sumvitg train stop, the Rhätische Bahn will take you back to Disentis.

title: Keflavík
short_description: A worthy conclusion to the panoramic round trip: The final stage takes you to a picturesque thermal bath and Iceland's largest lighthouse.
long_description: The final stage of the route is also the shortest: on just under 80 km we drive the Reykjanes peninsula and visit some interesting sights: The route first leads to the Blue Lagoon, a pleasantly warm thermal bath with sparkling blue water and a great backdrop. We then pass the bridge between two continents that connects Eurasia and America. At Gareth;ur we can marvel at an impressive lighthouse with its own museum and take a last look at Iceland's picturesque coastline before we reach the final stop on the route, Keflavík Airport.

title: स्कंदगिरी हिल ट्रैक
short_description: स्कंदगिरी हिल ट्रैक जिसे कलावारा बेट्टा ट्रैक भी कहा जाता है जो एक पहाड़ी ने चर ट्रेल से होते हुए पर्वत शिखर तक जाता है।
long_description:
स्कंदगिरी हिल भारतीय राज्य कर्नाटक में मौजूद एक पर्वत शिखर है जिसमें कलावारा दुर्ग नामक एक प्राचीन किले के खंडहर हैं। यह बैंगलोर शहर से लगभग 70 किमी और चिकबल्लापुर से 3 किमी दूर स्थित है। स्कंदगिरी पर्वत शिखर लगभग 1350 मीटर की ऊंचाई पर है और बैंगलोर के पास का एक बढ़िया वीकेंड गंतव्य है। यह प्रकृति प्रेमियों और हाइकर्स के बीच एक लोकप्रिय स्थान है।
इस ट्रैक का बेस कैंप कलावारा गांव है। एक तरफा ट्रेल लगभग 3 किलोमीटर लम्बी है और सभी किस्म के हाइकर्स चाहे नए हों या अनुभवी के लिए उपयुक्त है। ट्रेल में पूरे समय हलकी चढ़ाई है लेकिन यह मुश्किल नहीं है। ट्रेल गाँव से होकर हरे भरे इलाकों और मंदिरों से होकर गुजरती है और अंततः पहाड़ी की चोटी पर कलवारा किलें तक पहुँचती है।
पगडंडी की शुरुआत में एक वन विभाग का कार्यालय स्थित है और इस ट्रैक पर जाने के लिए उनकी अनुमति आवश्यक है।

images.caption: कलावारा गाँव के पास स्कंदगिरी पहाड़ी की चोटी से दिखता हुआ विहंगम दृश्य, चिक्कबल्लापुर, कर्नाटक, भारत।
चिक्कबल्लापुर जिले के कलावारा गाँव के पास स्कंदगिरी हिल्स, कर्नाटक, भारत।

title: बैली'ज वॉक ट्रैक
short_description: बैली'ज वॉक माउंट आबू के जंगलों की सबसे प्रसिद्ध और सुन्दर हा इकिंग ट्रेल है जो नक्की झील से होते हुए सनसेट पॉइंट तक जाती है  और हाइकर्स को प्रकृति की अनछुई नज़ारे पेश करती ह ै।
long_description:
करीब 2.5 किलोमीटर लंबी यह नेचर ट्रेल राजस्थान के सिरोही जिले में स्थित है जहाँ राजस्थान की कई सबसे ऊँची पर्वत शिखर भी हैं।
यह ट्रेल नक्की झील से शुरू होती है और इसमें अच्छी तरह से साइन बोर्ड लगाए गए हैं। ट्रेल के शुरुआती हिस्सों में 54 सीढ़ियों की चढ़ाई शामिल है जो एक छोटे मंदिर पर जाकर खत्म होती है। यहां से ट्रेल धीरे-धीरे घने और हरे भरे जंगल में प्रवेश करते हैं। रास्ते के अलग अलग हिस्सों से जंगलों, नक्की झील और माउंट आबू के शानदार दृश्य देखने को मिलते हैं। ढाई किलोमीटर के बाद ट्रेल अपने अंत बिंदु तक पहुंचती है। यहाँ से थोड़ा आगे जाने पर पहाड़ की चोटियों में सूर्यास्त बिंदु है जहाँ से सूर्यास्त का सुन्दर व्यू और इलाके का विहंगम दृश्य देखने को मिलता है।
ट्रेल का कठिनाई स्तर आसान से मध्यम है और फिट हाइकर्स के अलावा कैजुअल टूरिस्टों को भी इसे पूरा कवर करने में कोई कठिनाई नहीं आती है। ट्रेल पर दोतरफ़ा आना-जाना आराम से 3 घंटे में पूरा किया जा सकता है।

title: Mount Ouaman Climbing course
short_description: Ouakan is the only trail on the mountain. The slope is a little steep up to the halfway point, but from the summit there are spectacular views towards Penketo and Panketo.
long_description:
Mt Ouakan is a 1,370 m high mountain located on the east side of Lake Akan and is known as Pinneshiri (mountain of men) in the Ainu language. It is surrounded by lakes and marshes, including Lake Akan, Panketo and Penketo, and the summit is dotted with the remains of three old explosive craters. The trailhead is a 5-minute drive from Lake Akanko Onsen, and is currently the only trail on Mt Ouakan. Due to the longer distances and steeper slopes throughout, it is more suitable for advanced climbers than Mt Female Akan.
From the trailhead, the trail passes through a mixed needle-and-spade forest with Abies sachalinensis, Ezo spruce, etc. up to around the fourth station through the west side of "Lake Taroko" and "Lake Jiro". From the trailhead, the first lake you see on your right is Lake Taro, where water from Lake Akan flows into the lake and freshwater fish such as carp inhabit. Jiro Lake, which comes into view on the left 700 m from Lake Taro, is surrounded by dense trees, so when you stand by the lakeside you are surrounded by the tranquillity of nature. From the mouth of the waterfall to the vicinity of Jiro Lake, in early summer, flowers such as Gozentachibana, Ezo-ohsakura-so, Tsubame-omoto, Oobananoenreiso and Miyamahanshoduru can be seen, and the autumn leaves are also beautiful.
The section just below the fifth station is the steepest part of the climb, but once you reach the fifth station, the area opens up and the alpine landscape unfolds. Alpine flora such as the Chinese prickly ash, the turmeric azalea and the Ezo azalea are also blooming with pretty flowers. From here to the summit, you can catch glimpses of Lake Akan and Mt. The summit is just below the summit. The summit is a great place to see Mt Female Akan, Lake Akan, Penketo and Panketo spread out below and Lake Kussharo can be seen briefly in the forest surrounding them. In the distance, there are great views of Mt Shari, Mt Mokoto and the Shiretoko mountain range. The area around the summit is rocky and narrow, so be mindful of your surroundings while taking a break.

title: Bird Park Trail around Ortenburg
short_description: This easy hike to Irgenöd Bird Park takes us through the impressive landscape around Ortenburg.
long_description: We start our hike at Ortenburg's historic town hall and walk north from here to Passauer Straße. Turn left into this street and follow the red and white sign "4" through the linden avenue (1) and then along the forest nature trail (2). However, we then keep to the left and walk via "Luisenthal" up to the Hinterschloß inn (3). From here we walk on via Hasling to the bird park Irgenöd (4). Our path then leads us first back to the Hinterschloß inn. There we first keep to the left and then turn right onto the asphalted road, following the red and white marking "4a". This finally takes us up to Ortenburg Castle (5). From here we walk on the "Schlossrundweg - 1", past the game park (6) and via Hinterhainberg, back to Ortenburg.

title: Sedrun (Route 916, 917, 918, 919, 921)
long_description:
Sedrun offers a suitable route for all Nordic walkers. There are 5 marked Nordic Walking tours divided into three levels of difficulty!

Route 916 (length: 4.9km / altitude: 505hm / level of difficulty: difficult)
Uphill through meadows and forest to the Tgom viewpoint. The cable car brings you comfortably back down to the valley. Another slight ascent to Sedrun. Partly asphalted. Only accessible in summer.

Route 917 (Length: 11.9/ Height: 295hm / Difficulty: medium)
From Bugnei on a natural path along the railway line to Mompé Tujetsch, down to the Rhine and through a shady forest back to Sedrun. Partly asphalted. Only accessible in summer.

Route 918 (Length: 31.1km / Altitude: 395hm / Difficulty: medium)
Up to Planatsch with beautiful views of the valley and back via Selva through shady forest along the Rhine. Partly asphalted. Only accessible in summer.

Route 919 (length: 5.2km / altitude: 100hm / difficulty: easy)
Nice loop to get to know the villages of Sedrun and Rueras, along the young Rhine and past the Neat construction site. Partly asphalted. Partly accessible in winter.

Route 921 (Length: 8.6km / Height: 375hm / Difficulty: difficult)
Through the rustic Val Strem and along mountain slopes, with beautiful views of the Val Tujetsch. Partly asphalted. Only accessible in the summer.

title: Senda Sursilvana (Route 920)
long_description: On the gently sloping Senda Sursilvana along the railway line via the picturesque Mompé Tujetsch to Segnas. The Ustria Cresta invites you for refreshment. From Disentis, the Matterhorn Gotthard Railway takes you back to the starting point.

title: Reykjavík
short_description: This stage is a successful combination of city trip and sightseeing in untouched nature.
long_description: The penultimate stage of the round trip covers approx. 115 km and leads from the south coast first to the capital Reykjavík, before the route returns to the coast via the Kleifarvatn mountain lake and the Krýsuvík volcanic system. From the vibrant metropolis, which is also a melting pot of different art styles, we reach important geological sites that take us back to times long past, when huge lava flows poured over large parts of the country. Another stop at Iceland's peaceful mountain lake Kleifarvatn offers no less impressive scenery and invites you to linger for a while.

title: Into the primeval hearts of Switzerland
Hiking from Brașov to Stâna turistică (Poiana Brașov)
short_description: An easy hike from Brașov to Stâna turistică restaurant in Poiana Brașov, which is actually an alternative to the more popular old road. This one takes you through Valea Sticlăriei, on a much quieter and wilder path.
long_description:
Choose this route for the sake of a little variety. It's as easy as the old road (or Red Route), but not as wide or smooth. The path leads through the forest, crossing areas with rich carpets of dead leaves, and many roots popping out from the ground.
The path reaches Poiana Mică (where you enter Poiana Brasov resort); from here, you can continue towards Stâna Turistică Sergiana restaurant and possibly towards Râșnov.
The road is also suitable for children or for walking the dog (although at the exit to the main road there may be some dogs from the neighboring property).

title: Weißenbacher Höhe circuit via Schönwald
short_description: The tour above Schönwald is a beautiful Nordic walking route around the Weißenbach valley and to Schönwald.
long_description: Our path runs to the right through coniferous forest in the direction of Schönwald. After a few metres, we turn right onto a forest path, here we follow the markings of the Schönwald Nordic walking trails. Soon the path leads above the Weißenbach valley to a crossroads with a bench for resting; we follow the path and the Nordic walking route to Schönwald. From here there is a magnificent view of the valley. We descend into the valley and walk up to Schönwald on the other side. Along the edge of the forest and past the cemetery, we keep to the right at the next junction. Continue on the Zinswald circular path, which branches off to the right in the forest, back to the Weißenbacher Höhe. The tour continues along the road for a short distance. Those interested in winter sports should make a detour to the Schönwald ski jump and the biathlon facility.

images.caption: The ski jump in Schönwald is worth a detour.
Local markers show us the way on our round.

title: Circuit pe versantul drept al Defileului Crișului Repede
short_description:
Un traseu ușor, pentru întreaga familie, ideal de descoperit minunile naturale modelate de peisajul carstic al Munților Pădurea Craiului în zona Șuncuiuș.
Translate to English
long_description:
Traseul se face în circuit și e accesibil aproape tot timpul anului. Începi domol, chiar lin, cu o plimbare pe lângă calea ferată, continui în urcuș (că doar ești la munte) și ajungi în coama dealului (la puțin peste 500 de metri altitudine) unde te poți bucura de splendoarea peisajului, apoi revii abrupt la locul de pornire.
Pe parcurs, ai ocazia să intri în două mici grote - Peștera Roșie și Peștera Fugarilor - ambele cu nume sugestive pentru peisajul interior sau pentru presupusa istorie a evenimentelor petrecute aici. Înainte de urcare, ajungi la Pestera Podireului II - o galerie îngustă a carei început poate fi confundat cu un simplu izvor. De fapt, dacă te încumeți să intri, se înaintează câteva zeci de metri și ajungi la un mic lac format de apa subterană mai ales în sezon ploios, Peștera continuă dincolo de acesta printr-un sifon, însă adâncurile se rezervă doar speologilor.
Pe parcurs, te vei opri cu siguranță des pentru poze din acelea care-ți taie respirația, în cel puțin două puncte de belvedere. Te vei minuna la fiecare pas de sălbăticia (controlată) a acestui loc.
Toamna, circuitul e și mai spectaculos, când se colorează copacii.

title: Weekend walk to Pushchino Falls
short_description: A slim but inviting waterfall in Pushchino near Moscow
long_description:
Pushchino Falls are little known and that's a good thing! For weekend hikers, the sparseness of the waterfall will make for a great time out in the huddle. There should be no city pandemonium on the forest trails.
 .
The waterfall in Pushchino is not big (3m), but it is noisy and attractive in its own way. You can take pictures with it and go for a swim under it, for example, as some of the girls - bored travelers of Moscow do.
You can also take pictures with it.

title: To the Grünewald Madonna in Stuppach
short_description: Through the Bürgerwald and the fields around Mergentheim we hike to Stuppach to the well-known Grünewald-Madonna.
long_description:
The starting point of our hike is the car park in Max-Planck-Stra;e at the municipal works. We follow the nearby B19 road for a short distance to the right in the direction of the south, but as soon as we see a wood on the left, we turn off and walk towards it. Walk left along the edge of the forest until you reach a path. This path leads us to the right, above the camping site in the Willinger Tal, through the Bürgerwald to Wachbach. At the entrance to the village, we can make a detour to the fruit tree nature trail along the cycle path on the other side of the road.
From the village street in Wachbach, we turn right into the Lillstadter Steige and turn left at the last houses until we come to another path. Turn left and walk uphill through the fields to Stuppach. From the hill we have a beautiful view of the village with its parish church, which we will visit in a moment. In Stuppach we come along Lindenstrasse and a small path to the parish church of St. Mary with its famous image of the Madonna. The painting by Matthias Grünewald, which hangs in a side altar of the church, is well worth seeing. Behind the Gothic church, which was built by the Teutonic Order in 1607, there is also a military cemetery. We walk back along Lindenstrasse, continue to the end of the village and leave Stuppach. Parallel to the B19, we now walk steadily downhill back to our starting point.

title: Seven Beaches Trail
short_description: Coastal trail in one of the most incredible areas of the São Paulo coast with preserved Atlantic Forest and where seven beautiful beaches are revealed, with clear sand and great for diving.
long_description:
Located in a áarea of preserved Atlantic Forest, the Seven Beaches Trail reveals wonderful beaches, besides belvederes, springs and intense contact with the exuberant nature.The first stretch of the trail to Bonete Beach passes by the West Beach and Perez Beach, with some kiosks and water points at Bonete, and at the end of this beach, the trail continues to Praia Grande do Bonete.
The Praia Grande do Bonete Beach é extensive, with clear sands and very fluffy. At the end of it we go ahead in the trail to the beaches of Deserto and Cedro ending also in Praia da Fortaleza. To continue to the Desert and Cedar Beaches, we cross a creek, and following a wall, we have a sign indicating the continuation of the trail that already begins in a very strong climb, and then a very steep descent with several points of erosion.The Desert and Cedar beaches are separated only by a rocky formation, and in the left corner of the Cedar follows the trail to Praia da Fortaleza.

title: Véu da Noiva and Andorinhas Waterfalls Trail
short_description: Easy trail to reach two beautiful waterfalls of the Serra dos Órgãos National Park, in Petrópolis: the V éu da Noiva waterfall and the Andorinhas waterfall.
long_description:
The V éu da Noiva waterfall is approximately 3 kilometers from the headquarters. With an impressive 30 meters high and icy cold waters, the waterfall is one of the main highlights of the Park. With only 5 minutes walking, you will arrive at the Andorinhas waterfall. There are 15 meters of waterfall in a deep pool perfect for bathing. The place is surrounded by 2 walls, which gives the place a mystic air.
The trail is well marked and there is no way to get lost. However, the path crosses the river a few times, so take care with slippery stones.

title: Weser-Harz-Heide long-distance cycle route (Bokel-Ebstorf-Lüneburg)
short_description: The almost 76 km long section of the Weser-Harz-Heide long-distance cycle route leads through the Lüneburg Heath on minor roads with little traffic in places and on gravel paths in others. ei
long_description: On this route we cycle through the peaceful landscape of Südheide. We pass special features such as the Hösseringen museum village and cultural highlights such as the Ebstorf monastery and the Hundertwasser railway station on paths that climb moderately from time to time but are mostly asphalted until we reach Lüneburg.

images.caption: Cyclists on the Weser-Harz-Heide Cycle Path

title: Martinique Le Prêcheur-Mont Pelée-Grand'Rivière
short_description: The green flow of the northwestern slope of the Montagne Pelée massif offersa set of landscapes that make up a lush forest.
long_description: The highest peak in Martinique at 1397m, Mount Pelee offers a breathtaking view of the northern part of Martinique. Located between the municipalities of Saint-Pierre, Le Morne Rouge, Ajoupa-Bouillon and Grand Rivière, it has a view of both the extreme north and both coasts, if the weather is so favourable of course. It is an easy walk overall and offers several routes.

images.caption: hiking trail in Martinique: Martinique Le Prêcheur-Mont Pelée-Grand'Rivière

title: Scheidegg
short_description: We set off on a wonderful panoramic walking tour with many views of the mountains.
long_description: At the Kurhaus, we follow the Nordic Walking signs "9". We walk slightly uphill until we reach the first exercise board (1). On a small forest path we pass the children's sanatorium. Again and again we pass sections of forest. Soon we have a wonderful view (2) of the surrounding mountains. In Oberstein we follow a meadow path on the right downhill to the next exercise board (3). We follow the signs for a longer time. Via a path we finally reach the Roderbühl lookout and rest area at the end of Buflingsried (4). Here, on a clear day, a magnificent panoramic view awaits us. We reach Scheidegg through a residential area and after a few minutes arrive at Café Fünfländerblick (5). At the Gallus Chapel, we cross the road and follow it back to the Kurhaus.

images.caption: A view of the surrounding mountains.

title: Hainleiteweg
short_description: This beautiful hiking trail opens up the area around Sondershausen in the Kyffhäuser district. Only rarely do we leave the large mixed forests of the Hainleite, a mountain range of shell limestone north of the Thuringian Basin.
long_description:
Stage 1: Friedrichsrode - Straußberg (22 km)
After visiting the nationally renowned Kunsthof, we leave Friedrichsrode in an easterly direction. Immediately, the landscape conservation area Dün-Helbetal at Feuerkopf awaits us. We then pass Lohra Castle and climb the Steckenberg behind Hainrode, where we can cool off in the forest swimming pool if necessary. The castle ruins in Straußberg are only open for tours on special monument days. On the other hand, the Feuerkuppe holiday park and the Affenwald monkey forest with summer toboggan run are open at all times.
Stage 2: Straußberg - Sondershausen (17 km)
Past Großfurra - a detour is worthwhile because of the castle and the old half-timbered houses - we hike up the Frauenberg today. Behind Jechaburg we cross the church valley, hike to the Babraer Teiche swimming pool and into the forest above Sondershausen. Between the Spatenberg and the Fürstenberg we descend into the town. A visit to the castle with its castle museum and regular concerts is a fitting end to a lovely day.

Stage 3: Sondershausen - Seega (18 km)
Today we first walk along the edge of the forest to Hachelbich and then, following the Hachelbach stream, walk directly into it. A forest swimming pool again offers the opportunity for a pleasant refreshment break. Shortly before Seega, we pass the Arensburg ruins, which are well worth seeing.  
Stage 4: Seega - Sachsenburg   (14 km)
We leave Seega along the orchid-rich Wipperdurchbruch and hike in the Raben valley to the Eichelkamm desert, a large field area near the small housing settlement of Düppel. At Wächterberg, you pass the Sachsenburg ruins and the Hakenburg ruins. From here it is not far across the Unstrut to Sachsenburg, the destination of our tour. Before returning, we should definitely take a look at the impressive moated castle in Heldrungen.

title: Hexental circular trail near Freiburg
short_description: This circular trail leads through the Hexental valley to Bollschweil. Along the edge of the forest, fantastic views open up again and again over the open landscape with orchards, pastures and farms.
long_description:
We start in  Merzhausen at the indoor swimming pool and walk along Friedhofweg until we reach Dorfstraße, where we turn left. At the next intersection, we turn right and follow Hexentalstraße until Mühleweg branches off to the left. Now we hike up the hill on this small road. At the top, we follow the signpost in the direction of Stöckenhöfen (Hexental-Rundweg, signposted by a red eagle on a yellow background) to the right and continue our hike on the cycle path and footpath to the entrance to the village of Au. At the through road, we keep left and follow the village road to the end of the village. We pass the Auen town hall (1). After the turnaround loop of the bus, turn left into Selzenstraße and turn right immediately after the bridge over the Selzenbächle (Schützenhausweg). This path leads us past the Au Schützenhaus and through a small piece of woodland. Behind the forest we reach the grounds of the Stöckenhöfen spa clinic (2). We cross the facility and hike up the road to the left behind the car park to immediately turn right again onto the Hexental circular path in the direction of Bollschweil.
The farm track leads below the forest to a crossroads. Here we leave the path and follow the sign "Sägeloch" uphill. In the forest, we follow the signs "Adler und gelbe Raute" (eagle and yellow rhombus) and reach - after crossing a small stream - a wide gravel path. Walk down this path to the right for about 200 m until you follow the sign towards Bollschweil to the left. Now we reach a nice barbecue area with a playground.
Passing the Wittnauer Schützenhaus (3), we continue walking in the direction of Bollschweil until we are above the entrance to Sölden. Here we follow the signs to the right downhill to the edge of the village and then sharply left up the Mühleweg. On the Saalenbergweg we finally reach the idyllically situated, small Saalenberg chapel (4). We cross a meadow and follow the path markings of the "yellow rhombus" into the forest. Now we walk on wide paths for about 2 km through the forest until we reach a district road. We walk up along the road and after about 200 m keep to the right to continue our hike along the edge of the forest.
The path leads us to the outskirts of Bollschweil, where we follow the Leimbachweg downhill to the centre of the village. At the through road (Hexentalstraße), we turn right. At the next crossroads on the left, we follow this (General-von-Holzing-Straße), pass the cemetery and keep to the right at the sign pointing to the sports facilities in the direction of "Bettlerpfad". We go slightly uphill, past a playground, until we reach a driveway.
Now we are on the "Bettlerpfad" (5), which leads along the Schönberg slope and whose signposts accompany us to Merzhausen. The historic hiking trail leads a total of 27 km from Merzhausen to Badenweiler in the Markgräflerland:
Passing the sports field and a Marian grotto (6), we then reach the outskirts of Sölden. Continue along the Schönberg footpath to the outskirts of Wittnau. Shortly after the town hall in Wittnau, a signpost directs us to the right in the direction of Merzhausen (Schönbergstraße). We go down the hill a little and at the crossroads follow the signpost to the left into Heimbachweg. Between meadows and fields, we now head downhill towards Au.
In Au, our path leads downhill to the left just after the "Adlerburg" inn, where it is worth taking a break. At the second crossroads on the left, we finally follow the Mainrain road. At the entrance to Merzhausen, keep left at the fork and right at the next crossroads. We now follow Weberstraße until we reach Friedhofsweg on the left again and thus return to the starting point of our hike at the Merzhausen indoor swimming pool.

images.caption: Along the way: Flock of sheep shortly before our destination in Merzhausen.
The beggar's path brings us back to the starting point.

title: Randonnée autour de Civray -boucle 1 balisage rose
short_description:
Au cœur de la vallée de la Charente, Civray et ses alentours offrent un terrain de jeu idéal pour les amoureux de la nature et de la randonnée. Entre rivières paisibles, forêts ombragées et villages au charme authentique, les sentiers de la région promettent des escapades mêlant détente, découverte et émerveillement.
Translate to English
long_description:
Suivre le balisage rose, longer la Charente, passer à côté du terrain multisports puis sous la rocade et emprunter une première passerelle.
Après une cinquantaine de mètres, prendre à droite pour passer une deuxième passerelle.
Poursuivre par le parcours santé pour rejoindre l'aire de jeu située avant le camping.
Emprunter la passerelle à votre gauche et prendre à droite par la route en contournant le camping.
Dans la montée avant Cap Motoculture, tourner à droite et rejoidnre Savigné par la route de Loing.
A la départementale 148, rester à droite et rejoindre l village de La Grenatière en passant à l'église puis sur le po,nt de la Charente (un panneau donne des informations sur sa construction).
A la Grenatière, prendre à droite la routedes Âges, passer au village Les Âges (à droit, il y a un moulin)
Ensuite, suivre le balisage rose pour rejoindre Acadie en contournant par la droite l'Orégon.
Poursuivre en prenant à gauche pour retrouver le début du parcours santé.
Rejoindre l'Espace François MITERRAND en empruntant les passerelles en sens inverse de l'aller.
Translate to English

title: Walk to the Blue Groto near Lubenice
short_description: Walk from Lubenice to the beautiful beach around the Blue Groto. Extensive views included.
long_description: This scenic walk starts in a small mountain village called Lubenice with spectacular views upon the mediterranean sea. The first section of the path is the same as the one going to Sveti Ivan beach which you can already see from the top. The path winds through a light pine forest most of the time which is really nice when the sun is shining. Along the way there are several stunning vista points. Having reached the wonderful beach the adventurous amongst you can explore the Blue Groto on the left hand side of the bay. There might be some bats around as well... The most spectacular colours you will see during the afternoon hours. That's the busiest time therefore. Most of the visitors get to the bay by boat.

images.caption: Wanderweg zur Blauen Grotte bei Lubenice. Cres, Kroatien
Strand bei der blauen Grotte, Lubenice

title: Black ridge near Bolsternang
short_description: A Nordic walking tour for those seeking peace and quiet, with a fantastic panoramic view from the Black Ridge and beautiful vegetation.
long_description: We start our loop at the Nordic Sports Park car park and follow the Nordic Walking signs to the Black Ridge. At an information board (1) we keep to the right and walk slightly uphill from here. At the clearing we reach the first information board for strengthening and coordination (2). A little later we change from the wide forest road to a forest path and reach Wuerttemberg's highest elevation, the Black Ridge (1118 m), via a network of roots (3). Climbing the lookout tower is "compulsory", as the effort is rewarded with an impressive view from the Alpine chain to Lake Constance. Back on the forest path, we walk down the valley until we reach another signpost (4). Here we keep to the left and return to the starting point.

images.caption: The observation tower on the Black Ridge.
Panoramic view from the Black Ridge.
Flora and fauna on the Black Ridge

title: "Cross Youth" Competition
short_description: Parcul Tineretului din Capitală va găzdui miercuri, 7 mai, „Crosul Tineretului“, un eveniment destinat iubitorilor de sport. Cei care vor lua parte la competiţie vor putea pleca acasă cu numeroase premii.
long_description:
„Crosul Tineretului” se va desfăşura în Parcul Tineretului şi se adresează persoanelor iubitoare de sport. Pentru a participa la competiţie concurenţii trebuie să se înscrie la unul din punctele situate pe platoul de la intrarea în parcul Tineretului - B-dul Şincai, pe mai multe categorii de vârstă.
Ministerul Tineretului şi Sportului invită bucureştenii să participe la eveniment în număr cât mai mare pentru a încuraja sportul de masă. „Voi participa cu toată bucuria la Crosul Tineretului. Vreau să fiu alături de tineri, vreau să alergăm împreună pentru sănătate, pentru energie şi aş vrea să fie alături de noi cât mai mulţi bucureşteni. De aceea, îi invit pe toţi la „Crosul Tineretului” să alerge şi să se bucure.”, Gabriela SZABO, Ministrul Tineretului şi Sportului.
Înscrierea concurenţilor se va face în ziua evenimentului, 7 mai 2014, în zona special amenajată din Intrarea Parcul Tineretului - B-dul Şincai, între orele 8:00-10:00, la punctele special amenajate pentru fiecare categorie de participanţi. Concurenţii trebuie să fie apţi fizic pentru a alerga la „Crosul Tineretului”, pe o distanţă de aproximativ 3 kilometri.
”Crosul Tineretului” este un eveniment ce face parte din proiectul ”Zilele Tineretului”, desfăşurate între 2-9 mai 2014.

title: Circuito dei Castelli
short_description:
Il Circuito dei Castelli è un percorso ad anello di circa 30 km e collega tra loro otto comuni della Valtellina: Tirano, Sernio, Lovero, Vervio, Tovo di S. Agata, Mazzo di Valtellina, Grosotto, Grosio.
Translate to English
long_description:
Grazie a questo itinerario, da fare in 2 o 3 giorni, è possibile scoprire molti luoghi del patrimonio storico-culturale della Valtellina, soprattutto castelli ma anche chiese, torri e rocche. Il percorso costeggia le montagne e conduce tra meleti, boschi, vigneti e terrazzamenti ormai in disuso ma molto importanti per la storia della zona.
Translate to English

title: North Iceland (Whale Watching)
short_description: The third stage of the motorised tour through Iceland is all about whale watching. There are more insider tips to discover along the North Sea coast.
long_description: The third section of the ten-day exploration tour in Iceland runs along the largely uninhabited north coast and, in addition to the picturesque coastal town of Sauðárkrókur, also leads to Lake Stífluvatn. The secluded fishing village of Davlik also offers a similarly idyllic atmosphere. Nature lovers will particularly enjoy the mighty backdrop of the legendary waterfall Goðafoss. After a stopover in the harbour town of Akureyri, we visit the impressive metropolis of Húsavík on the magnificent Skjálfandi Bay.  Here you have the opportunity to catch rare glimpses of minke whales, bottlenose whales, humpback whales and sperm whales on a whale-watching tour.

images.caption: Inmitten von unberührter Natur: der See Stífluvatn
Die idyllische Gemeinde Dalvik inmitten der Natur

title: Prince Luitpold House
short_description: This delightful, longer hike takes us to the Prinz Luitpold Haus (DAV hut).
long_description: The destination of this tour is the Prinz-Luitpold-Haus. We start at the Giebelhaus, which can be reached by bus from Hinterstein. From there a wide forest road leads into the Bärgündeletal. Behind the imposing Täschlefall, a narrow path leads up to the Untere Bärgündelealpe, where we take a break and enjoy the view from the sun terrace. Finally, we hike through willows and mountain pines up to the Prinz-Luitpold-Haus, the highest point of this hike. After a rest in the shelter, we descend back into the valley via the Point Hut.

images.caption: Blick vom Giebelhaus auf den Giebel

title: H.v.B. Etappe 3: vom Waltenbergerhaus nach Holzgau
short_description:
Die Etappe vom Waltenbergerhaus über die Rossgumpen-Alm ins Tal nach Holzgau führt über den berühmten Heilbronner Weg und ist eine der spektakulärsten Wanderrouten in den Allgäuer Alpen.
Translate to English
long_description:
Die Tour startet am Waltenbergerhaus und geht anfangs steil bergauf Richtung Socktalscharte. Oben angekommen verläuft der Weg zunächst auf dem Heilbronner Weg, einem der bekanntesten Höhenwege der Allgäuer Alpen. Der Weg führt durch schroffes Felsgelände und bietet atemberaubende Ausblicke auf die umliegenden Gipfel. Die Route ist anspruchsvoll und erfordert Schwindelfreiheit und Trittsicherheit, besonders an den ausgesetzten Stellen, die mit Drahtseilen gesichert sind.
Kurz vor der Abzweigung zur Rappenseehütte, biegst du links ab Richtung kleiner Steinscharte. Achtung, Weg ist nicht gut erkennbar und man muss das ein oder andere Mal klettern um voranzukommen. Hat man diesen technisch anspruchsvollen Teil des Heilbronner Weg hinter sich gebracht, beginnt der lange Abstieg ins Tal. Zunächst erreichst du die Rossgumpen-Alm, wo du eine wohlverdiente Rast einlegen kannst. Von dort führt der Weg weiter hinab nach Holzgau im Lechtal, einem malerischen Dorf, das für seine traditionellen Holzbauten und die beeindruckende Hängebrücke bekannt ist. Holzgau ist ein idealer Ort, um die Tour zu beenden und die Allgäuer Bergwelt Revue passieren zu lassen.
Translate to English

title: Hike to the sources of the Huveaune from Nans-les-Pins
short_description: A beautiful hiking trail through the Sainte-Baume Regional Natural Park to discover the sources of the Huveaune and the Castelette cave.

images.caption: The Huveaune, near its source, Sainte-Baume national forest

title: Mountain houses - Pass: Betelberg
short_description: These easy to moderately difficult hikes show you the most beautiful paths and the most pleasant mountain huts in the whole Simmental;
long_description:
Leave everyday life behind and experience the space and time that the mountains offer you.

Let yourself be spoilt by the hospitality in the mountain häusern. Enjoy the food from mostly local production, the cheese from the nearby Alps or taste one of the homemade cakes.

A hike takes you across the gentle meadows of the Lenk family mountain Betelberg, where you can discover the world of marmots in a playful way and admire the diversity of alpine flowers. Another path leads past the Lenkerseeli, the imposing Iffigfall and up to the idyllically situated Iffigenalp. Accompanied by the unique panorama of the Wildstrubel, Lenk's local mountain and pride, a trail leads from the Bühlberg to the Hahnenmoospass and Metschberg to Metschmaad. In the picturesque Fermeltal valley near Matten at St. Stephan, a unique hike and 4km of scooter downhill fun await you. Other excursion destinations include the lovely Jaunpass and the trail from cosy Oberwil to the Morgeten Alps, where old customs are still practised. The Stockhorn with its incomparable panorama of 200 Alpine peaks as well as the Jura, Emmental and Lake Thun is another unforgettable experience.

Summarising the hikes and the mountain häuser on the Simmental Mountain Häuser Pass. Anyone who does not yet have the mountain pass in their rucksack should request it in advance from the Tourist Centres in Lenk, St. Stephan or Boltigen. The card can be presented to the staff for validation every time you eat in a mountain restaurant or ride on a mountain railway. If you visit 7 of the 14 mountain huts by the end of the summer season, you will receive an attractive gift at the Tourist Centres in Lenk, St. Stephan or Boltigen. With an additional ride on each of the three mountain railways, you will also be entered into the big prize draw at the end. The first prize is a Lenk cable car season pass.

1. Berghaus Leiterli: The cable car on the Betelberg in Lenk takes you up to the Leiterli. When buying your ticket, please show your Berghäuserpass so that it can be validated. At the top station of the cable car you will find the Berghaus Leiterli. The Kappeler family will be happy to serve you in the cosy restaurant or on the sun terrace and will validate your mountain pass.
2. Alpine Flower Trail: On this adventure trail you can admire the variety of alpine flowers on the Betelberg in Lenk.
3. Murmeli Trail: From the Leiterli mountain hut, the clever Murmeli Trail on the Lenk Betelberg takes you through the world of the marmots in a playful way. The easy-to-follow trail goes over balance bridges, by cable car over the Tuft-Seeli, cleverly over the sound stairs or high up on the climbing marmot made of Lothar wood.
4. Berghaus Betelberg: The Murmeli Trail passes Berghaus Betelberg, where you can enjoy another stop with Samuel Kappeler's team (not included in the Berghäuser Pass).
5. Berghaus Stoss: The Murmeli Trail ends at Berghaus Stoss. Here you can enjoy the sun terrace with the Imdorf family and discuss what you have experienced. Please do not forget to validate your Berghäuser pass. From here, the last rather steep stretch back to the village of Lenk can be done on foot or by gondola lift.

title: Leiterli - Iffigenalp
short_description: Far away from the hustle and bustle of everyday life, this is one of the most beautiful high-altitude hikes in Lenk.
long_description: The starting point of this beautiful day hike is the mountain station of the Betelberg gondola lift. The first section leads along the AlpRundweg and the Rundweg Gryden to the Stübleni. The crater-like bizarre rock landscape is a sight to see in the Lenk Alps. From the Stübleni, the route continues via the Stübleni Pass to the Tungel Pass. Also called Stigellegi, it is a historic crossing between Lenk and Saanenland and was once used by muleteers. From the Tungelpass there is a steep ascent (for the first few metres you need to be free from vertigo and sure-footed) to the Stigelschafberg. And soon you catch a glimpse of the turquoise-blue Iffigsee, a breathtaking sight every time, even for locals. After a few metres of descent towards the Iffigsee, you can turn right and make a detour via the Wildhornhütte (allow approx. 1 ½ hours more). From the Iffigsee, the hike leads via Iffigtal to Iffigenalp. Refreshments are available at the friendly Berghaus Iffigenalp. The return to the valley station of the Betelberg cable car is by bus or on foot.

title: Upper Valley
short_description: The bus takes us from Hinterstein to the Giebelhaus, from here we hike into the beautiful Obertal.
long_description: From the Giebelhaus in the Hintersteiner Tal (1060 m) we hike on a tarred alpine path up to the Engeratsgundalpe (1156 m) and to the alpine dairy Laufbichl (1200 m), from there on to our „day's destination“, the alpine dairy Plättele (1350 m). All the alps are managed in the high season. From here we hike back along the same path to the Giebelhaus. This is a pleasant tour also for hikers without too much alpine experience. The total distance of just under 8 km is also easy for children.

title: To the witnesses of industrial history
short_description: On a hike from Rüti to Rapperswil, you can visit some extraordinary witnesses of industrial history.
long_description:
For centuries, the water of the Jona in Rapperswil powered machines. From the railway station in Rapperswil, walk southwards and leave the village at the sewage works. Following the Jona, you reach the Jonaknie at Chüeweid: gravel bars and mossy stones make this corner of the Jonerwald a true idyll. Two hundred metres away, you come across the first industrial-historical witness of this hike. It is the weir at Hackennest, which diverts part of the Jonawater into a canal. The Braendlin brothers built this waterworks in 1838, because their growing spinning mill needed more energy.

You follow the canal for three hundred metres in a westerly direction, where you see it enter a tunnel. In the Aspwald you cross a small pass that takes you to Tägnernau. There, the water that disappeared into the mountain on the other side comes to light again and backs up to the Brändliweiher. From this pond, the water of the Jona reaches the historic spinning mill on Holzwiesstrasse via a canal. No spinning machines have been running in the building for decades - but the water energy is still used by a small power station (it stands directly on the hiking trail). In the 19th century, there was still a large water wheel on this canal, which drove the machines via a shaft. A special feature of this Braendl waterworks can be seen a hundred metres away from the small power station. There, the water flows in a bridge across the Jona. As early as the 14th century, the first millers were turning in the small town of Rapperswil. The water for this was drawn from the Jona at Gaisrain. You can reach this place by following the Jona on a path 200 metres north of the spinning mill, where the railway line and hiking trail cross the Jona.

To finish the hike, follow the partly underground Stadtbach stream into the centre of Rapperswil. Above the Tüchelweiherwiese üit crosses the railway line. At Stadthofplatz it used to enter the old town, flowed through Halsgasse and Schmiedgasse and flowed into Lake Zurich where the university now stands. Today, the city stream flows underground to the Giessi and flows into the Kempratner Bucht.

title: Hike to Sea Eye and Beușnitei Waterfalls starting from Potoc Village
short_description: Easy hike through a dreamlike karst landscape, one of the most beautiful in Banat.
long_description: We take a dirt road directly to the Nera gorge then uphill to the sea eye (Ochiul Bei) and further to the Beușnitei waterfalls.

title: Wetland Tour from the Gold Coast to Oberland
short_description: A hike from Stäfa to Bubikon leads through several marshes and other intact natural landscapes.
long_description:
A hike from Stäfa to Bubikon leads through several marshes and other intact natural landscapes. The tour starts above Stäfa near the Lindenbänkli bus stop. Between Risi and Bueschstutz it proceeds through forests and meadows. At Seeweid the view will open over the Ütziker Ried marsh with its numerous ponds. Then you will wander through the orchards of Buen and Lutikon above Hombrecktikon. In Hasel on the shores of the Lützelsee a wine tavern with a sunny terrace is the perfect place for a break. In spring and summer the Lützelsee storks can be seen frolicking in the water. You will come to Reipenhof after traversing Weiler Adlesthusen. After going through the Altrüte forest you will see the fourth marsh of the day, the Reitbacher Riet. Between Landsacher and the final destination in Bubikon you can enjoy the view as you walk through the Bergli Riet. This greenbelt between Stäfa and Bubikon is the perfect place to leave your worries behind. Those who want to see a bit more have ten nature preserves a short distance from the hiking path. Most of them are marshes and ponds. The largest include the Lützelsee and the Lutiker Riet.

title: At your feet lies the petrol blue lake
short_description: Hike from Amden to Quiten.
long_description:
Quinten is Mediterranean, Quinten has a warm climate, figs grow in Quinten: You have probably read and heard this a hundred times. That this is more than just a cliché becomes clear just two kilometres from the little village on Lake Walen: on the Steinlaui clearing, which has been extended by a few acres for the benefit of snakes and lizards, the climate is like that of a stony Tuscan field in high summer. In the first gardens you see on Quintner soil are fig trees and stately palms with bushy crowns.
In turn: The slightly modified classic Amden-Quinten begins at the Amden Post station. A few metres below the community centre, the new path branches off and leads over a bridge that offers views of the Fallenbachschlucht gorge. Between Gadmen and Hinterbetlis you follow the old mule track, which was the connection between Amden and the rest of the world until 1882. Because people came to the village from the east at that time (and not from the west as they do today), Amden is a topsy-turvy world when it comes to field names: everything that is called «front» is back. What is called «hinten» is in front.
On the way to Quinten, the light green of the beech leaves in front of the petrol-blue lake in the depths is a constant companion. Above, a steel-blue sky and in the southeast the sun, scattering tinsel over the wind-swept lake. Soon you can hear the murmur of the Seerenbachfälle and the Rinquelle, which you can visit with a short detour from nearby. At 585 metres, the Seerebachfälle is one of the highest waterfalls in Switzerland. They look really spectacular in spring when the snow melts. The Rin spring, a large underground river system, emerges from the rock a few metres next to the Seerenbach falls. After rainfalls or during snowmelt, up to 10,000 litres of water shoot out of the hole every second.
Half an hour later you are above the quarry, which may soon become the site of a huge solar plant. The terrain is very steep, but the hiking trail is well developed and secured on both sides with ropes or chains at the critical points. If you suffer from severe vertigo, it is better to do the hike in the opposite direction. This way, they walk uphill in the most difficult passages and don't have to look down as much.
A few metres öst of the village centre of Quinten there is a beautiful pebble beach. On the terrace of the «Schifflände» you can enjoy Walensee-Felchen, Quintner Federweisser and many other specialities. The MS Churfirsten finally brings you back to the north side of the Alps, to Weesen.

title: Knausen
short_description: Hike up from Fossestien for lake views
long_description:
Knausen is an easily accessible mountain in Gaularfjellet, with a trail leading through a landscape of summer farms and lakes. The peak offers views of the Gaularfjellet scenic route, the Gaular River and its many lakes, as well as the surrounding mountains. 
This trail begins from the Likholefossen Waterfall and can be easily combined with a longer walk along the Fossestien Waterfall Trail.
Hov Hyttegrend offers cabins and facilities for tents, as well as shuttle services to Fossestien every morning in the high season.
Flatheim Farm is a traditional B&B. They offer comfortable beds and facilities for camping, as well as guided trips and a summer café with local refreshments.
In Balestrand you can find a choice of hotels, B&Bs and self-catering apartments. Historical Kviknes Hotel was the favourite of famous painters in the 1800s.
Near Sande on the the Sunnfjord side of Gaularfjellet, Villa Åmot offers a unique cultural experience. In Jølster and Førde you will find both self-catering apartments and hotels.

title: From the Goldingerbach to the Aabachmündung
short_description: Between St. Gallenkappel and Schmerikon you hike through the Neuhüslertobel and to the Aabachm
long_description:
Between St. Gallenkappel and Schmerikon, you walk through Neuhüslertobel and to the mouth of the Aabach. In the course of this walk, you follow a body of water, which is first called Goldingerbach and then Aabach.

The Goldingerbach (Goldinger stream) originates at the southern slope of Chrüzegg and winds its way through Goldingertal (Goldinger valley), against the Obersee. Its name comes from the gold seekers who made their discoveries in its headwater region. The gold seekers probably also dug at its lower course in Neuhüslertobel and at the foot of the Uznaberg. It is also possible that they no longer made any discoveries there. Perhaps this is the reason why the stream loses its glamorous name in this area and from this point on is modestly called "Aabach". In Neuhüslertobel, between Neuhaus and St. Gallenkappel, flora and fauna are the only living organisms that you encounter on a fall Sunday morning. No wonder, because from the northeast you can gain access to the ravine by taking a long detour and by climbing up several meters of altitude. A few steps away from the moraine landscape in Rappengrund, you begin the descent to Neuhüslertobel. The first inhabitants of the ravine that you can see are a few trouts. Information signs explain who else lives in this mossy crevice. Woodpeckers, kingfishers, various raptors and songbirds, badgers, deer, bats, lizards and grass snakes are a few of these. After the underpass of Rickenstrasse, the trail no longer follows the Aabach, but instead makes a detour through Matten to Bauwil. Only at the junction of Ranzachtobel does the road pass directly by the water again. Apart from a short detour at the Schmerikon highway exit, you follow the Aabach until it flows into the Obersee. This detour is worth it since the pebble beaches in this area are one of the most beautiful lake shores of the region. The best way to conclude the hike is to have a meal on the terrace of the "Strandhotel" in Schmerikon. The food and the service are at least as good as the exclusive location of the restaurant.

title: Fossestien Waterfall Trail
short_description: Wander down the Gaula River’s waterfall trail

The Waterfall Trail (“Fossestien”) leads along the Gaula River and follows old trade routes between Gaularfjellet in Balestrand and Viksdalen in Gaular. The complete trail is 21 kilometers long and includes 14 waterfalls and 7 mountain lakes. The route is easy to access from four different parking lots, and you can adjust the length and difficulty by breaking the trail down in shorter legs.
Fossestien follows the Eldalen Valley. It takes you from wild mountain landscape, past old mountain farms and mountain lakes, and into forest covered valleys. Sheep and cows graze along the trail in the summer, and around 80 milking goats reside at the traditional mountain farm Langestølen.
Hov Hyttegrend offers cabins and facilities for tents, as well as shuttle services to Fossestien every morning in the high season.

title: GPS hiking tour from the moorland to Rossberg
short_description: On a hike from the Third Altmatt to Schindellegi we enter three magically beautiful landscapes: a colourful moor, a splendid clearing and a mountain that is actually an outcrop.
long_description:
When we hike from the Dritte Altmatt (Third Altmatt) to Schindellegi, we find ourselves in three magically beautiful landscapes: a colorful moorland, a magnificent glade and a mountain that is actually an offshoot. In the 1980's, towards the end of the Cold War, the Swiss army wanted to establish a military training ground in the moor of Rothenthurm. However, in 1987 the Swiss people adopted the Rothenthurm Initiative. Since then, the largest moorland and all the other upland moors of Switzerland have been under protection. That is a good thing since it is especially in the fall when a wonderful colorful landscape unfolds up here, which people prefer to enjoy without shooting noise and diesel smell. It is primarily in the mornings when the Bibäränäfel (fog named after the Biber river) offers special effects that are worth seeing. Starting from the Dritte Altmatt (previously Altun Matta, Latin for high-altitude meadow), you pass through the moor in a western direction. After crossing the Biber and the Canton boundary, the trail ascends in the direction of St. Jost. The glade that is approximately the size of five soccer fields and is 1150 meters above sea level is magnificent: it slopes down in a southern direction and provides an unobstructed view freely of the Alps. A small tavern and a chapel offer the opportunity to take a rest. On the remainder of the trail in the direction of Raten and Gottschalkenberg, you are in the company of countless hikers and walkers for just about one hour. Only on the wooded ridge of Höhronen you find yourself alone again. Where the forest is sparse, you get a view of the Lake Zurich and the Alps. At the Dreiländerstein Schwyz, Zug and Zurich, the trail steeply descends to another magically beautiful place. It is Rossberg, which is actually not a mountain but rather a saddle-shaped northern offshoot of the Höhronen. At the Rossberg Inn, you can sit down on the terrace that has a view to Lake Zurich and Säntis. From there, it descends again in the direction of Schindellegi, where you can take the train.

title: Hike Tour around Rapperswil and Schmerikon
short_description: In December, the Weid forest reserve was inaugurated in the Chlosterwald forest between Bollingen and Schmerikon. This is a good occasion to hike the route from Rapperswil-Jona to Schmerikon via Bollgner Seerücken.
long_description:
Commercial use of the Swiss woods should be decreased. An accord between the federal government and the cantonal forestry officials aims to keep ten percent of the forest area as nature reserve. In December, the Weid forest reserve in the Klosterwald between Bollingen and Schmerikon will be inaugurated. This presents a good opportunity to hike along the stretch from Rapperswil-Jona to Schmerikon via the Bollgner Seerücken.

You take the train to Blumenau, and then hike along the shore to Wurmsbach. At the monastery you go north. At the southwest end of the Buch industrial zone you'll see that nature produced by man can also be very beautiful. This is the outdoor workshop of the landscape architect and star gardener Enzo Enea. We can recommend a visit to his magnificent, 75,000 square meter site (admission CHF 15.00, closed Sundays).

You'll cross a field to the Oberwald, victim of two severe storms in the last twelve years. At the Risi rest area you won't take the official hiking trail but rather a path in the westerly direction. After a few steps you'll find yourself standing beside a hole of 10 meters depth, created by the wearing away of sandstone. On the Moos, crossed by the hiking trail of the Bollingen-Wagen pass route, you arrive at the western end of the Weid forest reserve. In March the two long moors between Moos and Katzenriet are still colorless. In just a few weeks, however, butterflies will flit over brilliant green grass and colorful blossoms. The reserve is not yet finished, for the closely spaced trees need to be thinned out so that oaks, beeches and firs can receive more light for optimal growth. In several places wood is being cut for the last time. It will be several decades before the Klosterwald will look the way it did during the Stone Age, when the first settlers arrived in the upper lake region. It's worth visiting right now though! The hike between Blumenau and Schmerikon is very varied and at the end the Seehof in Schmerikon beckons two more reasons for a visit now.

Le sentier, balisé en partie, alterne entre passerelles sur pilotis et chemins de terre. title: From Bad Hindelang to Wertacher Hörnle
short_description: This hike takes us from Bad Hindelang past the Café Polite through the Hirschbachtobel up to the Hirsch-Alpe. From there it goes via the Spieser, the Wertacher Hörnle and the Buchel-Alpe to Unterjoch.
long_description:
This is a tough hike. Over 1000 metres of altitude have to be conquered. In the course of the tour, which leads through the wild Hirschbachtobel, we climb the 1651 m high Spieser and the 1684 m high Wertacher Hörnle. This requires stamina. We are rewarded with magnificent views of the surrounding mountains and the idyllically situated Hörnlesee.
There are three places to stop along the way, the Caf é Polite, the managed Hirschalpe and the managed Buchel-Alpe.
From Unterjoch, the bus takes us back to Bad Hindelang.

title: The beautiful vale of Batzberg
short_description: A large and beautiful pool, in which water collects and thus also a great diversity of species settles, can be found on the southern slope of the Batzberg, west of the hamlet of Mettlen.
long_description:
A large, beautiful dell, filled with water and enjoying great biodiversity, is found on the south slope of the Batzberg, west of the hamlet of Mettlen.

The large pond features unique flora and fauna, including a number of orchid species, grass snakes, dragonflies and butterflies. The main attraction of the large pond is, however, the frogs. More about them later in our excursion tip.

One leaves the S5 in Rüti and hikes in an easterly direction along the official hiking path. This traverses residential areas at first and then the extensive woods on the Batzberg. Although these hiking trails and gravel paths are only a few steps from the towns of the agglomeration, one seldom meets another person. The quiet appears to attract above all the batrachians, which can be fairly noticeable both optically and acoustically! The year begins for the grass frogs and common toads with the awakening of spring. They creep at the start of the season out of the undergrowth in the woods and make their way to the shallow water, where they lay their eggs. Local residents speak of a mass movement, an invasion, that always takes place at this time. Sometimes one can hardly set foot on the path without stepping on one of the slimy animals.

Especially valuable for visitors to the large pond is the fact that frogs communicate with other species. They react, for example, to the noise of road and air traffic as well as to the human voice. The frog pond is thus just the right place for a song or a poem. For the frogs, it is the rhythm in the repertoire that is important, and on a good evening you'll be able to conduct a sizable choir.

One can have fun and still obey the rules of the nature reserve. Stay on the path, don't pick the flowers and carry out the remains of your picnic when you leave.

At the end of your hike you'll leave the large pond and come to the picturesque little ponds, the Mettlen and the Güntisberg. Now enjoy a beer in the Sonnengarten and then follow the path to the Wald railway station.

title: Skageflå Mountain Farm
short_description: Visit a picturesque mountain farm overlooking Geirangerfjord
long_description:
Skageflå is a remote mountain farm overlooking The Seven Sisters Waterfall in the UNESCO-listed Geirangerfjord. It is quite possibly one of the most scenic places you will ever visit.
The easiest way to reach Skageflå is to take the sightseeing boat from Geiranger. The boat stops at a dock called Skagehola. From there you can hike up to the farm and enjoy the views.
You can either return to the dock and get picked up by the next ferry, or hike back to Geiranger via Homlongsætra, which takes several hours. The trail described here leads back towards Geiranger, but can be used for shorter trips up to the farm.
Note that the distance and duration measurements used here are to the end of the trail at Homlong. If you walk all the way back along the road to Geiranger, add another 2.4 kilometers or around 30 minutes.
This trail is part of our guide hiking in Geirangerfjord.

title: Main Loop Trail
short_description: Tackle Bandelier National Monument’s most popular trail
long_description:
The Main Loop Trail is one of Bandelier National Monument’s most popular hikes. In a relatively short distance—just over a mile—you can see the ruins and recreations of five different types of homes and buildings that once made this area a thriving village.
The hike winds through Frijoles [free-HOH-lace] Canyon, which was formed by volcanic ash—tuff—from a Valles Caldera eruption over a million years ago. Tuff is easy to carve, and the Ancestral Pueblo people who lived here used tools to enlarge small bubbles in the rock, carving out homes called cavates over time. Little is known about their predecessors except that evidence of human activity in the canyon dates back at least 10,000 years.
In every direction you look, there’s history as well as beauty. The trail passes by the ruins of a kiva, a ceremonial gathering place built underground, an old village that was once 400 stone rooms built in a circle at least two stories tall, and several cavates. You can climb wooden ladders to explore some of the cavates in the canyon, if you wish.
The views of Frijoles Canyon from inside the cavates is unmatched. The canyon walls are steep, flat rock faces in many places, and you can get a sense for what life may have once been like here as you climb wooden ladders to crawl inside them. You can imagine climbing down to the canyon floor for water from Frijoles Creek or to hunt or gather food. You can imagine climbing back up with precious resources and making a home out of these hand-carved caves. From inside the cavates, especially those higher up on the canyon walls, you can stare straight across the canyon, into the woods, where you can spy on wildlife. If you look to the left and to the right, you can see jagged, rust-colored rock formations jutting out from the walls.
About halfway around the loop, you can turn onto the Alcove House Trail. In half a mile (.8 km), you’ll climb quite a few stone steps and four wooden ladders, and it’s well worth the effort. Much of the path is worn into the tuff knee- and thigh-high in places, and these parts of the path are so narrow it’s nearly impossible to pass oncoming hikers. From Alcove House, 140 feet (43 meters) up from the trail, you can see a reconstructed kiva and stare out beyond the curves of Frijoles Canyon.
There are many places in the American Southwest where you can find ancient ruins from Native American societies. Few, however, are as developed, protected, accessible, and uncrowded as Bandelier National Monument. Mesa Verde National Park, in southwestern Colorado, had more than half a million visitors in 2018. Bandelier had fewer than 200,000. Many of the most popular hikes at Mesa Verde are accessible only if you go with a guided ranger tour, for which you need to reserve tickets ahead of time in the Visitor Center. Bandelier has fewer restrictions and feels like a more genuine exploratory experience rather than a tourist hot spot. The visitor center has a small museum where you can learn more about the Ancestral Pueblo people who lived in Frijoles Canyon and beyond and rangers there are eager to answer questions.
The Main Loop Trail is a great way to start your introduction to Bandelier even if you also plan to hike other parts of the monument. The 21 numbered spots along the trail correspond to descriptions in a trail guide you can purchase in the Visitor Center for $2. Each one explains a bit about ruins, petroglyphs, geology and wildlife in the park, or what the Ancestral Pueblo people’s culture was like.
If you’re looking for a trail that will pique your curiosity, offer stunning views for relatively little effort, and show you quite a few ancient ruins, the Main Loop is exactly what you’re looking for.

title: Storseterfossen Waterfall
short_description: Walk behind an impressive Geiranger gem
long_description:
Storseterfossen Waterfall is one of the most popular hiking destinations in the Geiranger area. The enjoyable trek combined with the experience of walking behind the waterfall makes for a memorable trip. The hike is fairly short, about an hour each way, but has a steady climb.
This trail is part of our guide hiking in Geirangerfjord.
There are several hotels, lodges, and campgrounds in and around Geiranger.
Grande Fjord Hotel is a popular and cozy hotel, with fjord views 2.5 kilometers from Geiranger.
Hotel Union Geiranger is a large hotel set back in the valley and facing the fjord, with an indoor swimming pool.
Hotell Geiranger is in the heart of Geiranger, right by the fjord.
Geiranger Camping is a simple campground located right at the end of the fjord, on the waterfront.
Vinje Camping has cabins and campgrounds, 1.5 kilometers up the valley from Geiranger.

images.caption: Along the trail towards Storseterfossen Waterfall.

title: Shelburn escape line: the Freedom Trail
short_description: The Shelburn escape line allows you to follow the path of the English airmen and resistance fighters to the "Bonaparte Beach".
long_description:
The paths of Plouha are full of history. They played an important role at the time of resistance and they were one of the most important sites in France. It is a duty never to forget the courage of those who have fought and resisted through their courageous deeds, generosity and commitment to freedom. Plouha was liberated on August 5, 1944.
The Shelburne escape line follows the footsteps of the English airmen and resistance fighters to the Bonaparte Beach. The historical path takes us past the Saint-Samson chapel and the Alphonse House. Then the path winds through the forest and across fields, bevore we reach the sea. Finally we arrive at the edge of the 100 m high cliffs where we have a wonderful view at the sea. From the cliffs we can see the Pointe de la Tour, which children call "the crocodile" because of its shapes.

title: Løsta
short_description: Hike off the beaten track in Geiranger
long_description:
Head off the beaten track and away from all the crowds in Geiranger village. From Løsta there are magnificent views of the Geirangerfjord and Ørnesvingen.
Take a drink in the sun on the patio at Westerås Farm once you’ve finished the hike and enjoy the views.
This trail is part of our guide hiking in Geirangerfjord.
There are several hotels, lodges, and campgrounds in and around Geiranger.
Grande Fjord Hotel is a popular and cozy hotel, with fjord views 2.5 kilometers from Geiranger.
Hotel Union Geiranger is a large hotel set back in the valley and facing the fjord, with an indoor swimming pool.
Hotell Geiranger is in the heart of Geiranger, right by the fjord.
Geiranger Camping is a simple campground located right at the end of the fjord, on the waterfront.
Vinje Camping has cabins and campgrounds, 1.5 kilometers up the valley from Geiranger.

title: Schwarzenberg Hut
short_description: This hike takes us up the summer trail to the Schwarzenberg hut (1396 m). At the highest point of the hike we pass the Käser-Alpe at 1401 m and then return via the Engeratsgund-Alpe, which is open in summer, to the Giebelhaus, which is open all year round.
long_description:
The Schwarzenberg hut once served as a military base for high mountain operations. Today it is used as an accommodation house where you can stay overnight by arrangement. The Engeratsgundhof is managed in the summer months. In the Giebelhaus we can stop in all year round.
The Hintersteiner Tal is closed to cars - so we use the bus, which runs regularly from Hinterstein to the Giebelhaus, making several stops along the way.
This hike is particularly recommended for families with children!

title: On the trail of the old and new nature mountain freaks
