title: From Alfdorf around the full forest to the hollow stone
short_description: On this exciting hike we experience two caves and an idyllic forest.
long_description: We start our hike in Alfdorf at the market square and walk via the "Untere Schloss" in the direction of Haselbach. At the end of Alfdorf, we orientate ourselves towards Schölleshof and soon come to the "Hohlen Stein", a grotto-like weathering in the lower Stubensandstein. From here we continue directly to the next cave, the Schillergrotte. We follow the path further to the Kaiserlinde and Gelbfritz until we turn right before Brech and return to Alfdorf along the Winterhalde. Here you have the opportunity to stop at the Hirsch restaurant.

title: Easy hike around Lac des Confins
short_description: This hiking loop is accessible to a wide range of people, especially families with children who want to take a stroll around La Clusaz.
long_description: This hike circles Lac des Confins, offering picturesque scenery and magnificent views of the surrounding mountains. The trail is flat and well-maintained, making it ideal for families, beginners and walks with children. The lake itself is an Alpine gem, with crystal-clear waters and flowering meadows in summer.

title: From the Skywalk to the Holzweg
short_description: The ridge walk between Sattel and Rothenthurm offers a bridge, wooden blocks in the swamp, a sea of flowers, a tree graveyard and curious birds.
long_description:
A hanging bridge, wooden blocks across a marsh, an ocean of flowers, a tree cemetery and curious cows - all this on the ridge hike between Sattel and Rothenthurm. The hike begins with the Skywalk on the Mostelberg. To be sure, the longest hanging bridge for pedestrians in Europe is built of steel, but it sways to a surprising degree. Additional adrenaline is produced by the mesh floor, through which the Lauitobel can be seen between your feet. Crossing the Skywalk is free.

One reaches Bannegg, at an altitude of 1440 meters, by way of Bärenfang. At this point one connects with the trail that will take one seven kilometers further to Nüsellstock. Below Hochstuckli it continues on large wooden blocks through a marshy landscape. Now comes the area with the lovely name of «Beyond the Meadows». Here you can see the Rigi, the Lauerzersee and a corner of Lake Lucerne. Once one has taken a few photos, one crosses a pre-alpine landscape taken from a picture book: marshy meadows, scattered gnarled trees and above all, innumerable flowers.

A further «attraction» on this excursion was caused by a natural catastrophe, the stubborn owner of a forest and millions of insects. Hardly any other area was as strongly hit by the Lothar storm as the range of hills between Sattel and the Alpthal. Winds of more than 240 kilometers an hour hit its west side and cut broad swaths through the woods. Because fallen firs are the favorite food of the bark beetles, the fallen wood was quickly cleared away . Not so on the Näbikenfirst: the owner of this woods said that if no one paid him to cart off the wood he would simply leave the trees lying. Of course he thus created perfect conditions for the bark beetle. Once the pests had feasted on the fallen trees, they attacked the living firs and made of them tree skeletons.

Via Chli and Höch Tändli one reaches the Nüsellstock, which offers a good view of the Rothenthurm high moor. Then comes the descent via Nüsell (where there is a restaurant with a terrace) to Rothenthurm.

title: Climbing the Saumspitze (3,039 m) via the Kartellsee in the Verwall Alps
short_description: Lace your boots up and get stuck into a full-on day of beautiful vistas, azure lakes, tallis fields, glaciers, and copious quantities of fresh air. It's a long one that'll leave you knackered, but well worth it.

images.caption: Leaving the asphalt on my bike.
The Saumspitze on the left and the Seeköpfe on the right.

title: The Sphinx reveals the treasure!
short_description: A varied round trip and discovery tour above the Silvrettahütte
long_description:
Start and finish directly at the hut. Passweg, glacier trail and a small sheep trail combine to create an interesting loop with magnificent views in the midst of an alpine natural landscape. No particular difficulties for accompanied children. Nevertheless, you need open eyes not to lose your way and to find all the way points! The sphinx will reveal towards the end where the silver treasure is to be found...

Hiking trail to the hut:
The trail to the hut leads from Klosters üvia Monbiel to Alp Novai. The path then becomes somewhat steeper and leads through the very beautiful Val Sardasca. (Length: 14.5 km; Time there: 5h; Time back: 4.5h)

title: Lämmeren Hut SAC
short_description: The fact that the Romans already built the path over the Gemmi Pass seems almost impossible to the observer in Leukerbad. So steep and impregnable does the rock face rise into the sky.
long_description:
The pass leads into the Bernese Oberland. You don't have to do the strenuous uphill metres. There is a cable car, thank goodness.

Access:
At the top of the pass (2314 metres above sea level), a high valley widens out. The path to the hut first leads to a smaller lake. Let a flat pebble über the Lämmernsee, then hike around it to reach an alluvial plain through which new streams and rivulets keep flowing. The water constantly seeks new paths across the alluvial plain. Once they have all been jumped over and forded, the path leads up the last steep metres. If you are lucky, you will see an ibex peeking out from behind a rock on the ascent. At the hut, 2501 metres above sea level, a fine drink is certainly not out of place. (Time required: 1.75h)

Then the fresh energy might tempt you to take a trip to the glacier tongue of the Wildstrubel glacier. Half an hour there, half an hour back.

Descent:
The descent then takes you along the mountain flank down to Lake Dauben. You follow the left bank of the lake and reach the Berghotel Schwarenbach. You reach Sunnbüel via a wide alpine pasture. From here you can take the cable car, which takes you easily down to the valley floor. From Eggeschwand, the local bus finally takes you to Kandersteg railway station.

title: From Tauberbischofsheim to Dittwar
short_description: This medium tour takes us through the varied landscape around Tauberbischofsheim to the wine village of Dittwar. There we can visit the beautiful baroque church of St. Laurentius.
long_description: The starting point for this hike is the railway station in Tauberbischofsheim. We cross the tracks and walk south through the Glockengraben and Dittigheimer Straße parallel to the tracks until we meet the B27 federal road. On the opposite side of the road, we now turn right. First parallel to the main road, later to Dittwarer Straße, we walk sometimes along the edge of the forest, sometimes in the pine forest, until we reach the beautiful district of Dittwar, which we cross on Talstraße and Gissigheimer Straße. The baroque church of St. Laurentius is worth a look. At the last houses of Dittwar, we change to a field path to our right, which we follow for a while. We pass vineyards, of which the "Dittwarer Oelkuchen" vineyard enjoys a particularly good reputation. At a fork in the road near a group of trees, we take the right-hand path, then turn left and right again at the next four-way intersection and walk along the edge of the forest for a while. Follow the second forest path on the right through the "Bischofsheimer Gründle". Again we come across the B27, cross it and after a few metres enter the forest again on the left. Cross the Stammberg and continue through fields and meadows to Tauberbischofsheim. The Stammbergweg, which we are now on, joins Königheimer Straße shortly before a roundabout. Straight ahead at the roundabout, we reach the Glockengraben again via the main road, which takes us back to our starting point at the station. In the beer garden "Hexenkessel" or in the restaurant "Zum alten Türmle" we can comfortably end the hike.

title: Lake Spilau
short_description: From the Lidernenhütte, the hiking trail leads past the Spilauhütten to Spilauer See, where you can take a refreshing dip.
long_description:
The highest point is reached here and the route continues leisurely over «Ober Hüttli» back to the Lidernenhütte. The surroundings and landscape around the hut invite you to linger. The website of the Lidernenhütte provides information about current events in and around the hut and about other tours.

Descent and ascent:
The hiking trail to the Lidernenhütte starts at the very back of the Riemenstaldnertal in Chäppeliberg. The ascent leads up a pleasant incline to the hut. (Length: 2.0 km; Time: 1.25h)

title: Hike in the Seleger Moor park
short_description: This hike through the Seleger Moor park is the ideal option for a peaceful break close to the city of Zurich. Fascinating plants await you along the way.
long_description:
The Seleger Moor Park in Rifferswil is an idyllic natural landscape that extends over 120,000 m² and attracts more than 40,000 visitors every year. The park is particularly famous for its colorful rhododendrons and azaleas, which are in full bloom in spring and offer a spectacular play of colors. But the park has much more to offer: Ponds and streams run through the grounds and create habitats for water lilies and other aquatic plants, giving the park a tranquil, almost meditative atmosphere.
The park was founded in 1953 by the passionate gardener Robert Seleger, who collected plants on his travels that could withstand the harsh Swiss winters. Today, the park with its winding paths invites you to discover the diversity of plant life from all over the world and lose yourself in unspoiled nature. The Seleger Moor Park is a living heritage that is maintained and preserved by a foundation.

title: Niagara Falls Boardwalk (Canada)
short_description: An easy and flat route that passes over the nearest boardwalk overlooking Niagara Falls from the Canadian side
long_description:
A one-way and fun itinerary ideal for those who want to get closer and observe Niagara Falls as closely as possible and from as many angles as possible on foot. Along the route you can enjoy view points that offer different viewing angles of the impressive waterfalls. From a distant and relatively frontal view of the falls to the point where the falls begin to pour out of the river. The route is paved and therefore comfortable for walking with strollers as well as wheelchairs.
Due to the fact that the route is linear, i.e. one-way, the walking time as well as the distance shown on this page are for one direction only, but at any point on the route you can retrace the steps to the beginning of the route.

title: Geltenhütte - Rottal - Geltenhütte
short_description: Enjoy the round tour Furggentäli-Rottal-Geltenhütte. The tour takes you past the hydroelectric power station to the waterfall.
long_description:
When climbing into the Rottal, you have a beautiful view of the waterfall. In the Rottal you can also admire a large erratic boulder. On the Rückweg you have the opportunity to build a stone mandli yourself.

Hiking trail to the Geltenhütte: The hike begins at the idyllic Lauenensee lake and leads üvia Büel quite steeply upwards along the Geltenbach stream. Soon we find ourselves in alpine terrain and reach the Geltenhütte. (Length: 3.9 km; time required: 2h)

title: Circular hike Bad Berneck
short_description: This hike takes us through the beautiful cultural landscape around Himmelkron to the famous Baille-Maille.
long_description: We walk from Himmelkron along forest and field paths via Gössenreuth to the famous Lindenallee (Baille-Maille). It was laid out in the 17th century by Margrave Christian Ernst of Brandenburg-Bayreuth and served the nobles as a playing field for the croquet-like mail game. Similar avenues existed at many castles at that time, but this one was considered the longest and most beautiful in Europe.

images.caption: The linden avenue Baille-Maille was once one of the longest and most beautiful in Europe.

title: Hike to the Cabane des Diablerets
short_description: Varied hike to the Cabane des Diablerets
long_description:
Access:
From Reusch the trail climbs steadily upwards ürts over various mats and varied landscapes to the Oldenegg mountain station. Of course, this can be reached comfortably by cable car (note: operating times). Now it gets really exciting: The «Entre la Reille» is very rich in wildlife; and some people play the game «Who will spot a marmot first?». So the path becomes very interesting and almost imperceptibly the Cabane des Diablerets appears before our eyes.

Descent:
The descent can be done the same way as the ascent. However, you can also choose the leisurely way of descending with a few metres of effort. The nearby mountain station of the cable car, the Tête aux Chamois, is quickly reached. We reach the Col du Pillon in no time. So we only have to take the post bus to Reusch, our starting point.

title: Start at the highest dam wall in Europe
Almagellerhütte SAC

title: West Iceland / North Iceland
short_description: The second stage of the day takes you along the west coast of Iceland to the north of the island. The route includes an impressive mountain massif and an interesting open-air museum.
long_description: The route stretches a good 300 km along the west and north coasts of the volcanic island and leads to some interesting sights, first and foremost Mount Kirkjufell, a popular photo motif for the many nature lovers from abroad. Those who want to immerse themselves in the island's history will find an opportunity to do so in the open-air museum of the Viking ruins of Eiríksstaðir. To enjoy the picturesque coastal landscape on this stage, the idyllic and original harbour of the settlement of Hvammstangi is particularly suitable. At the end of this scenic day trip, a secluded campsite awaits us in a quiet location near the village of Skagaströnd.

title: From the Niederurn Valley to the Linth Plain
short_description: The Hirzli is the northernmost mountain in Glarus. It offers great views and unique ridge walks.
long_description: The Hirzli is probably also the only place from which you can see the ends of Lake Zürich and Lake Walen, which are 65 kilometres apart (as the crow flies). The Hirzli is best reached from the Niederurner Valley, which can be reached by cable car from Niederurnen. The hiking trails in this region are uniquely beautiful. The Hirzli and Planggenstock mountains in particular offer almost everything that makes mountain hiking attractive. You change sides of the mountain several times, squeeze through rocky gaps, climb over boulders of Nagelfluh and admire gnarled fir trees that cling to the rocks with their roots like birds of prey. Despite all the exhilaration, however, you don't forget that a misstep can have dire consequences. Anyone who walks along this ridge path must be sure-footed and not afraid of heights. If you want to descend to Bilten, branch off to the north 200 metres west of the Planggenstock. From Büels, head towards Wasserboden, then steeply down through the Niderenwald forest to the Biltnerbach stream. The sound of the stream accompanies you through the damp and humid northern slope. Imitators should be warned of the slippery stones - and also of the many ghosts who, according to legend, inhabit this slope. If you want to hike the entire length of the beautiful Chämmli (west of the Planggenstock), take the path to Säden above the Muesalp. If you hike back to the Niederurn valley along this route, you will be rewarded by crossing the rustic river forest. There are large ferns, old firs and lots of moss to admire. If you are early and have good legs, you can continue to follow the ridge after the Chämmli and hike via Lauihöchi and Stockberg to Siebnen.

title: Glattalphütte SAC
short_description: From Schwyz on a varied hike to Glattalphütte SAC
long_description:
Access:
From Schwyz, first a large, then a very small post bus takes us to Sali, where we board an aerial cable car. So we arrive well rested at Glattalp, but there is no sign of a lake! So we set off on a hiking trail towards the east, where we finally discover our lake after a good quarter of an hour. To make sure we don't miss anything, we walk around it (time: 1.5h). We discover that it has an inflow, but no outflow. But don't worry, underground wells make sure that it doesn't overflow!

When we start to get hungry, we return almost to the starting point. Here, two huts invite you to rest: the Glattalphütte SAC and the Berggasthaus Glattalp.

Descent:
For the descent, we follow the path that takes us steeply but without difficulty via Mütschen down to Sali; 1 ½ h. Of course, we can also choose the cable car.

title: Tiefenbach corner
short_description: This hike with great views takes us from Bad Hindelang to Gailenberg and from there via the Bildstöckle to the summit of the Tiefenbacher Eck. There we are rewarded with a magnificent view of the surrounding mountain peaks before descending back down into the valley via the Baoleskopf.

title: Carschina Hut SAC
short_description: Hike from St.Antönien to the Carschinahütte SAC
long_description:
Access:
The post bus takes us from Küblis to St. Antönien Platz. A wide hiking trail climbs up to Alp Bärgli below the Chüenihorn. On its eastern side we traverse high above the valley, past the small Carschina lake, and after 2 hours we reach the Carschinafurgga. There the hospitable hut (2236 m) awaits us with a well-deserved drink (or a meal), which we have well earned.

Descent:
After this reinforcement we turn to the east and follow the path leading to Tilisunafurggli almost without any loss of height under the mighty walls of the Sulzfluh. After half an hour über alweiden und kleine Geröllhalden we come across the path coming from Partnun. We follow it, descending a little steeper, and soon arrive at the romantic Partnun Lake. Then the descent continues leisurely to Partnun (time required: 1 ½ hours). In another ¾ hours we can gain St. Antönien on foot. But we also have the possibility to order an alpine taxi at the Restaurant Alpenrösli (Tel. +41 (0)81 332 12 18) in Partnun.

title: Chamanna Lischana SAC
short_description: This hike requires stamina, but rewards you with fantastic views.

title: Chamanna da Grialetsch SAC
short_description: In the immediate vicinity of the hut, small lakes invite you to play and drink.
long_description:
Here, at about 2700 metres üater sea level, you can safely take a few steps on the mostly snow-covered glacier.

Ascent:
You can get to Dürrboden in the Dischma valley by bus or your car. On a good mountain path, past Lake Furgga, you reach the Fuorcla da Grialetsch, a wide-open pass, and a little later the Grialetschhütte (2542 metres über Meer), which is actually called Chamanna da Grialetsch. Romansh is spoken on the Engadine side of the pass. 1.75 hours are enough for this ascent.

Descent:
From the hut you can hike as a Rückweg üvia the Fuorcla Radönt to the Flüelapass. There the post bus will take you back to Davos. As an easy alternative, you can also walk back the same way you came. (Time required: 3h)

title: Through the Weißbach Valley
short_description: In the Wei;bachtal valley we come across mighty waterfalls, historic salt production sites, a glacier garden and a playground that is just made for little explorers. On the barefoot path you can test your senses and feel with your feet.
long_description:
Our tour starts at the Mauth car park. A field path leads to the edge of the forest, from where a path branches off to the left into the Wei&szligbachschlucht. This is only for walkers, but we still dare to take a short look into the narrow gorge. We go back and follow the forest path from which we turned off before. Along the Weißbach we now walk, mostly under shady Bäumen, to the village of the same name. Just before you meet the main road, turn left. After 200 m you come to a T-junction, turn left and cross the Wei&szligbach stream. Can you already see the playground? Now it's time for a bit of a romp before we move on to the next adventure station, a bar footpath. What can you find with your feet? We cross the stream again and walk to the left, very close to the bank. Can you spot the wooden figures at the side of the path? After another 700 m, we finally cross the Reiterweg and meet the Inzeller Stra&szlig. Along the country road you pass the small village of Nagling. Behind it, turn left and walk along a narrow footpath for a while. You pass the Trift Monument, which provides interesting information about the transport of wood on the water in earlier times. Large quantities of timber were once transported into the valley here. Can you hear the loud roar in the distance? These are the white water streams, which rush down a steep slope and impress us not only with their sight but also with their loud roar when the water level is high. When the water level is low, the brave can get really close to the waterfalls over the slippery rocks. Who wants to risk a little shower on a hot summer day?
We carefully cross the main road and on the other side we come across the remains of a historic brine pipeline, one of the oldest of its kind. Passing the pipeline, we hike uphill along the path and shortly afterwards encounter the Glacier Garden. Here the traces of the Saalach glacier, which dominated large parts of the region during the Ice Age, are still clearly visible. Particularly interesting are the traces of the so-called glacier mounds, a geological peculiarity. You can see cylindrical holes in the rock, sometimes up to 1 m in diameter, which were formed by swirling masses of water during glacial melting.
Now follow the signs to Weißbach to the right. On this path you will come across the remains of the old brine pipeline and finally the "Himmelsleiter" (ladder to heaven), whose 420 steps lead you back down into the valley. Back at the main road, we then hike back along the familiar path to Mauthäusl.

title: TransSemenic Road
short_description: The road between Slatina-Timiș and Reșița is more recently known as TransSemenic or the Banat Mountain Road. The route and the scenery can rank it among the most beautiful mountain roads in Romania.
long_description:
TransSemenicul passes through the foothills of the Semenic Mountains and through tourist spots such as Văliug or Gărâna. The asphalt is in decent condition, but riders may be surprised to find potholes, rutted or sandy sections along the route. The stretch between Slatina-Timiș and Brebu Nou is the best in this respect.
The moderate altitude of the road also makes it ideal for an endurance mountain bike ride. In the Prislop Pass you reach the maximum altitude (1000m). The landscape is one of deciduous forests that are beautifully coloured in the autumn months.
Probably the most spectacular area in terms of scenery is the one between Brebu Nou and Reșița, which passes at the foot of the Semenic Mountains. In addition to the domed peaks, the eye is delighted by the picture formed by the two reservoirs - Văliug (Gozna) and Trei Ape. Thus, the mountain trail can be combined with a swim or even a boat ride. The areas around the resorts offer possibilities for cycling routes.

title: East Iceland (Glacier Lagoons)
short_description: The southeast of Iceland is characterised by the vast Vatnajökull National Park. There are also two glacier lagoons, waterfalls and former lava fields to marvel at.
long_description: On the route through the southeast of the volcanic island we get to know Vatnajökull, Europe's second largest national park. Here we can marvel at the country's largest glacier and discover another legacy of the Ice Age: the fascinating glacier lagoons. One of them, the so-called Jökulsárlón, is even considered the deepest lake in Iceland and has served as a backdrop for several classic films. The sandy plateau of Skeiðarársandur makes it particularly clear that Iceland is also a land of contrasts. The wide expanses of sand contrast sharply with the island's fjord landscape. A real insider tip, on the other hand, is the idyllic Svartifoss waterfall, which can be reached via a short hiking trail.

long_description: Of course, you also walk a large part through the dunes and along the sea. Couldn't be otherwise, of course, if you walk from Burgh-Haamstede to Westenschouwen. You will also walk a stretch through Zeeland's largest forest.

title: From Jungholz to the Gundalpe in Oberjoch
short_description: Hike with great views from Jungholz to Oberjoch/ Hindelang.
long_description: Enjoyable hike from Jungholz via Unterjoch to Oberjoch. There are many highlights in terms of nature and landscape. The tour always runs along signposted, developed and top modern hiking trails. On the way to the destination (Gundalpe) there are many opportunities to enjoy the view of the Allgäu landscape. There are also smaller rest stops (Vordere Sorgalpe) and small but nice towns and places to visit.

images.caption: On the way on snowshoes to Gendusas

title: Sedrun - Disentis
long_description:
After the railway station in Sedrun, you reach Bugnei on the level of the railway line in the direction of the indoor swimming pool and through various little-travelled neighbourhood streets. Now you are on the most beautiful section of the hike. On a sunny, wind-protected slope along the railway line, the path now leads to the picturesque village of Mompé Tujetsch. Here you have a beautiful view of Disentis with its impressive monastery.

After an easy descent, you reach Segnas, where you can make a short stop at the Ustria Crestas. Now you can decide whether you want to take the shorter route via Cuoz to Disentis or whether you want to extend the hike a little further via Peisel and Acletta (option A). After about 20 minutes, you will finally reach the railway station in Disentis, from where the Matterhorn Gotthard Railway will take you back to your starting point.

Note:
The valley hike is also well suited for families with smaller children who do not want to walk such long distances. Let your little ones ride along on a sledge: The gentle gradient makes it easy for you to pull the sledge and there is even a little downhill run every now and then.

Note(s)
The trail can be shortened as desired, see the MGB timetable, and can also be done well in the opposite direction.

title: GRP® Tour de l'Audomarois
short_description: The GR® de Pays Tour de l'Audomarois trail, located in the Caps et Marais d'Opale Regional Nature Park, is a 6-7 day walk starting from Saint-Omer.
long_description:
This itinerary is divided into several stages, crossing the Audomarois marshland, the only marshland in France to be both inhabited and cultivated, as well as various forests, notably the Tournehem forest.
The Tour de l'Audomarois hike, an approved GR de Pays, offers an opportunity to discover the region, and in particular the marsh of the same name, on a 123km loop. The route, which crosses the departments of Pas-de-Calais and Nord, immerses you in the beauty of the Caps et Marais d'Opale Regional Nature Park.
You can explore the former peat wetlands, which were transformed into market gardens in the 19th century. The modest dwellings of the cauliflower and chicory growers, along with the networks of canals used to drain the marshes, make for an exotic experience.
Walking through this natural region, walkers can also appreciate the biological diversity that unfolds along the way.

title: Teos Ancient City - Sığacık Teos Marina - Çamcaz Beach
short_description: We start from Teos Ancient City and walk to Sığacık Teos Marina, and from there we go to Çamcaz Beach, which is an example of the müthiş bays of Sığacık
long_description:
Routes that bring us together with nature and reveal the historical and cultural values of the region are always very valuable. If there is information that can be learnt on the route, if there are eye-catching intermediate points and if those routes bring us together with nature, greenery and blue at some point, you can enjoy it.
Starting from the Ancient City of Theos, this short route takes yürüyüy enthusiasts to one of Sığacık's beautiful deep blue bays, Çamcaz Beach. Of course, although the route itself is short, you need a little time for stops at intermediate points, visiting touristic spots, photographs. After the tour of the ancient city, we connect to Sığacık Teos Marina by travelling through a köy-like area where there are single settlements. After taking the air of Teos Marina and visiting the historical castle, we take a short, blue and green nature route to Çamcaz Beach.

title: Fenestrettes walk
short_description: A surprising walk in the Infernet cirque, then via the Fenestrettes: this astonishing path, built by the monks of Saint-Guilhem, corbelled above the void.
long_description:
In the heart of the Infernet cirque, a mineral setting with vertiginous cliffs, winds the caladé (paved) path of the Fenestrettes.
These masonry corbels were built in the 18th century to allow muleteers to pass through and gain access to the mounts of Saint-Guilhem-le-Désert and the Larzac causse.
Voted "Most beautiful path in the Hérault", it's the ideal complement to a visit to the village of Saint-Guilhem-le-Désert and offers breathtaking views.

title: Raven Run Nature Sanctuary Trail
short_description: Raven Run is a unique, 734-acre nature sanctuary dedicated to preserving the natural beauty of the Kentucky River Palisades and early Kentucky history
long_description: Over 10 miles of hiking trails provide access to streams, meadows and woodlands characteristic of the area.  Numerous 19th century remnants of early settlers, as well as over 600 species of plants, allow visitors to become acquainted with and appreciate the natural world.  Raven Run also accommodates over 200 species of birds throughout the year.

images.caption: hiking trail in the United States of America: Raven Run Nature Sanctuary Trail

title: East Iceland
short_description: The tour goes from the interior to the east coast of Iceland and introduces some interesting sights, especially Egilsstaðir, the largest town in the area. The coastal region offers some secluded lookout points with panoramic views.
long_description: Over a total of 430 km, the fifth day's stage runs along the eastern coast of the volcanic island and first leads to Egilsstaðir, one of the country's largest cities and an important cultural and economic centre of Iceland. The stage then leads to the much quieter town of Seyðisfjörður on the idyllic fjord of the same name, before a short hike to the Hengifoss waterfall offers the opportunity for picturesque scenery. The Vatnajökull National Park also offers a splendid backdrop for souvenir photos. Some tips are available at the Snæfellsstofa Visitor Centre. The day's journey is rounded off with a stop at the coastal village of Teigarhorn, followed by a visit to the beach at Fauskasandur.

title: Stavel snowshoe trail and Misés winter walking trail
Untersee - Alteinsee - Alteiner Fürggli - Wiesen
short_description: From Arosa through the rugged nature of the Welschtobel, high up to the Alteiner Fürggli, out to Wiesen.
long_description:
The starting point for this beautiful mountain hike is the Unterseeplatz. Due to the orientation board and various signposts, this is a good starting point with detailed information.

The first short section leads us on the tarred road down to the sewage treatment plant. From there we follow the Welschtobelbach stream and cross it after about 1 km. The trail now begins relatively steeply, but evenly and leads through a beautiful mixed forest with leghorns, chestnuts, birches and gnarled stone pines. The high plateau «Uf Altein» lies at around 2,000 metres and invites you to take a first short rest before we cross the Alteinbach stream and continue to gain altitude until we reach the Alteinsee lake. We follow the narrow path, which is now relatively flat, walk across wonderful alpine meadows and finally climb another 250 metres to Alteiner Fürggli, the highest point of the hike.

We now have various options for descending the 1,100 metres of altitude to Wiesen. The most direct route leads via the Heinisch Alp and on to the Wiesener Alp to Wiesen. There are various places to stop for a well-deserved rest. The return journey to Arosa is by post bus via Lenzerheide to Chur, and then on to Arosa by Rhätische Bahn.

title: Prätschli Arosa - Ochsenalp - Tschiertschen
short_description: The starting point of this hike is the Hotel Prätschli (bus terminus). First we walk on a slightly ascending alpine road with wonderful views of the opposite side of the valley.

title: The Sass Rigais traverse (Geislerspitzen)
short_description: The traverse of the main peak of the Geislerspitzen, the Sass Rigais, is a demanding but extremely rewarding undertaking in the dreamlike scenery of the Dolomites combined with the adventure of a not too difficult via ferrata over a real three-thousand-metre peak.
long_description: The Sass Rigais is the main peak of the Geisler Group. It impressively separates the Villnößtal valley in the north from the Grödner valley in the south. The neighbouring peaks of the Puez Group, the Rasciesa and the Sassolungo are always impressively in view. The traverse of the three-thousand-metre peak - the Sass Rigais is, after all, an impressive 3025 m high - from the Wasserrinnental to the Mittagsscharte, i.e. from east to west, is an alpine undertaking, but the panorama during the entire tour is overwhelming. First the Sassolungo appears at our back, then the Geisler with Fermeda, Sass Rigais and Furchetta rise in front of us. To the right is the mighty Montischella. The panorama from the summit surpasses all previous impressions. The Marmolada and the mighty Sella massif are within reach. The view of the Villnöß valley to the north and the Raschötz is fantastic. The via ferrata is initially moderately difficult if you cross the Sass Rigais from the east (i.e. from the Wasserrinnental). A vertical and somewhat exposed passage awaits you right at the beginning, but it is well secured. Absolute surefootedness and a head for heights are a prerequisite for the entire undertaking. On both the east and west sides, there are some passages in easy climbing terrain (I, UIAA). There is also a risk of falling rocks in some places, so it is highly recommended to bring a helmet. Orientation is easy in good visibility, in poor visibility the ascent into the Wasserrinnental can be a bit more challenging to find. The Regensburger Hütte is an excellent place to stop and spend the night along the way. If you want, you can shorten the ascent with the Col Raiser cable car. It is a good idea to spend at least an entire weekend at the Regensburgerhütte. The touring possibilities are almost inexhaustible and worth the longest journey.

title: Easy climb to Florei refuge
short_description: Since its renovation, Florei refuge has become an increasingly "targeted" destination, especially since the route that climbs here is accessible to almost anyone. For a day out in the mountains with children, the refuge is the perfect destination.
long_description:
There are several trails that climb up from behind the Posada Hunting Museum, but only one is marked with a red band. This sign is an indication of a ridge route and yes, in reality, this easy route represents only a leg of the complete ridge route that crosses the Baiului Mountains.
And for the less trained, for children, or even for those who don't feel like covering a complicated route, but still want to feel a little taste of nature, the path that goes up to Florei offers enough.
In Poiana Florei, next to the refuge, there is a picnic area; on a clear day, you can hardly get enough of admiring the panoramas. You can confidently spend the night at the refuge if you feel like it.

title: The Skywalk via ferrata on the Hunerkogel (Dachstein)
short_description: The Skywalk via ferrata, which leads up to the mountain station on the Hunerkogel in the Dachstein region, is certainly one of the most daring via ferrata installations in the Eastern Alps. It leads almost in the fall line of the Sky Walk - a viewing platform next to the Hunerkogel mountain station - extremely exposed and spectacular directly up to the mountain station.
long_description: Opened in 2006 on the initiative of Karl Höflehner, the Skywalk via ferrata is certainly one of the most spectacular climbs in the Eastern Alps. Both for visitors to the Sky Walk platform next to the mountain station of the Dachstein glacier lift on the Hunerkogel and for the more extreme via ferrata climbers. Because anyone standing on the Sky Walk platform can see almost the entire upper part of the via ferrata through the window in the floor. The extremely exposed and difficult via ferrata leads upwards almost in the fall line of the Sky Walk platform. A total of 270 m of steel rope and about 60 step and grip bolts were used by the builders Prugger/Seebacher to create this bold via ferrata. The route itself runs along the south and south-east exposed wall of the Hunerkogel. Orientation is very easy, as for the greater part of the ascent you are literally tied to the path. The demands on strength and psyche are quite high, and there is no opportunity to take a break on the Skywalk via ferrata. It is therefore advisable to take a short webbing sling with a via ferrata carabiner with you to take some of the strain off your arms.

short_description:
Schöne, abwechslungsreiche Tour durch Alpweiden auf das Oberlaubhorn.

long_description:
Beautiful, varied tour through alpine meadows to the Oberlaubhorn. Passing Sennhütten, the pleasant hiking trail climbs to 1999 metres above sea level, from where you have a magnificent view of the Wildstrubel massif.
Back you go to the Siebenbrunnen and down along the course of the Simme. On the last stretch of the trail, you can still gaze at the rushing Simmen Falls! Afterwards you can enjoy a well-deserved drink in the Simmenfälle restaurant.

title: Berghäuser - Pass: Hahnenmoospass
short_description:
Diese leicht bis mittelschweren Wanderungen zeigen Ihnen die schönsten Wege und die gemütlichsten Berghäuser im ganzen Simmental. Lassen Sie den Alltag hinter sich und erleben Sie den Raum und die Zeit, die die Berge Ihnen bieten.
Translate to English
long_description:
These easy to moderately difficult hikes show you the most beautiful paths and the cosiest mountain houses in the entire Simmental. Leave your everyday life behind and experience the space and time that the mountains offer you.

Let yourself be spoiled by the hospitality in the mountain houses. Enjoy the food, mostly locally produced, the cheese from the nearby Alps or taste one of the homemade cakes.

One hike leads across the gentle meadows of the Lenk family mountain Betelberg, where you can discover the world of marmots in a playful way as well as admire the diversity of alpine flowers. Another path leads past the Lenkerseeli, the imposing Iffigfall to the idyllically situated Iffigenalp. Accompanied by the unique panorama of the Wildstrubel, Lenk's local mountain and pride, a trail leads from the Bühlberg to the Hahnenmoospass and Metschberg to Metschmad. In the picturesque Fermeltal valley near Matten at St. Stephan, a unique hike and a 4km-long scooter downhill fun trail await you. Other excursion destinations include the lovely Jaun Pass and the trail from cosy Oberwil to the Morgeten Alps, where old customs are still practised. The Stockhorn with its incomparable panorama of 200 Alpine peaks as well as the Jura, the Emmental and Lake Thun is another unforgettable experience.

Summarising the hikes and the mountain houses on the Simmental Mountain Houses Pass. Anyone who does not yet have the Berghäuser Pass in their rucksack should request it in advance from the Tourist Centres in Lenk, St. Stephan or Boltigen or pick it up. The card can be presented to the staff for validation every time you eat in a mountain lodge or ride on a mountain railway. If you visit 7 of the 14 mountain lodges by the end of the summer season, you will receive an attractive gift at the Tourist Centres in Lenk, St. Stephan or Boltigen. With an additional ride on each of the three mountain railways, you will also be entered into the big prize draw at the end. The first prize is a Lenk mountain railway season pass.

1. Bühlberg mountain restaurant: The local bus will take you from Lenk to the Bühlberg mountain restaurant, where you can enjoy another meal with the Rytz family before the real fun begins. Please do not forget to validate your Berghäuser pass. In summer, you can watch cheese being made on the Bühlberg Alp.
2. Berghotel Hahnenmoos: After the first ascent, you can safely take a rest in the quietly located Berghotel Hahnenmoos. Valuing the Berghäuser pass is again the order of the day with the Spori family team.
3. Standhütte Metsch: The highest point of this hike has been reached, which is certainly a good reason to stop for a bite to eat.
4. Metsch: The Metsch cable car takes you back to the Lenk valley floor. The staff will again validate your Berghäuser Pass. From the valley station of the Metsch cable car, the local bus will take you back to Lenk village in 5 minutes.

title: Höhenweg-Steinwaldweg
short_description: We climb the highest mountain peaks of the Fichtelgebirge and see impressive rocky outcrops. Then we hike on the Steinwaldweg through the forest of the same name in the southern Fichtelgebirge.
long_description:
We start our hike in Schwarzenbach an der Saale and walk behind Hallerstein directly into the Fichtelgebirge. Over the Gro&szlig Waldstein we descend to Wei&szligstadt, which lies idyllically by the lake. The Rudolfstein is just the prelude to the Schneeberg, the highest peak in the Fichtelgebirge. But we will also hike the Nußhardt, the Hintere Messer, the Platte and the Hohe Matze on the Kammweg and enjoy the most magnificent views. On the way, we will experience the different types of rock - from granite and marble to slate and soapstone - as well as the large forest areas, which are partly interrupted by open plateaus. Near Wurmloh, at the Grosse Kösseine, the path changes its name to Steinwaldweg and leads north from Neusorg to the Steinwald. We cross the Kösseine, hike through Schurbach and past Pullenreuth. We continue through the forest to the Dreifaltigkeitskappe, the Wei&szligstein ruin and up to the Steinknock. We continue along the edge of the forest above the valley of the Wondreb, see Mitterteich and only need to cross Pleu&szlig to arrive at our destination in Waldsassen.

title: Northern Iceland (Gravelroads)
short_description: The fourth day's stage runs along the north-east coast of Ireland and offers a number of scenic highlights: Besides steaming craters, there is also a spectacular waterfall to marvel at.
long_description: On this day trip we explore the north-east of the volcanic island of Iceland. We first circle the picturesque lake Mývatn, stop at an impressive viewpoint and then visit a cave that leads to an underground lake. Another insider tip is the Námaskarðpass, a sea of steaming vents and craters that make an impressive sight. The Krafla geothermal power plant, located on volcanic ground, is similarly impressive. The tour is rounded off with a visit to the Dettifoss waterfall and the spectacular Ásbyrgi gorge.

title: Westfalenwanderweg
short_description: The Westphalia Hiking Trail, managed by the Sauerland Mountain Association, takes us from the Ruhr region over the ridges of the Adrey and Haar strands, to the valleys of the Möhne and Alme, and into the Egge Mountains on the southern edge of the Münsterland Bay. We hike along hilly paths and trails that allow us to steadily gain altitude.
long_description:
We start our hike in Hattingen and cross the Ruhr near Witten, which we follow to Lake Harkort and Lake Hengstey. Now we continue to orientate ourselves along the course of the Ruhr to leave the Ruhr area in an easterly direction. However, we do not walk directly along its banks. Rather, between Dortmund and Schwerte, we head towards Lichtendorf and then south of Unna towards the northern outskirts of Wickede. At Günne we meet the Möhne and cross the Möhne dam on the dam wall. Except for a short detour to the Bismarck Tower (near Möhnesee), we walk steadily close to the shore and cross the dam again at Stockum. This takes us to the northern edge of the Arnsberg Forest and we follow the Möhne via Völlinghausen, Allagen and Belecke to Rüthen, with its well-preserved historic town centre. Now we take a north-easterly route to cross Büren and then enter a dense forest area to reach Wewelsburg. Again we go through a forest and then in the valley of the Altenau to Henglarn and Atteln. On a high path we come to Ebbinghausen and, surrounded by narrow strips of forest, via Grundsteinheim to Iggenhausen. In Herbram, the Egge Mountains tower up before us. We boldly step into it and hike in a northerly direction over the Ochsenberg, the Hausheide and the Dübelsnacken to Altenbeken, the finishing point of our beautiful and eventful hiking tour.

title: Piatra Craiului Mountains with kids: Casa Folea - Joaca Pass
short_description: Casa Folea (Folea Mountain Lodge) is an important landmark for those who want to try hiking towards the southern ridge of the Piatra Craiului Mountains or towards the traditional mountain villages at the foot of the mountain, above Bran. A hike up to Joaca Pass (Șaua Joaca) with the kids makes up for an excellent introduction to the secrets of this wonderful mountain.
long_description:
The ascent is mostly on a forest road wide enough to accommodate even two bicycles. It advances smoothly, past a few households, past more or less shabby fences, then through the forest. Closer to the pass, you come out into a generous clearing, where you can see the traces of some sheepfolds.
The effort seems easier with the beautiful natural scenery around you. In addition, ahead on the path, the ridge of Piatra Craiului begins to unfold. As you keep getting closer to the pass, the image of the ridge keeps widening. Only in the end you get to see the mountain in all its splendor. Of course, the mountain ridge is not visible in foggy or gloomy weather.
The route can be covered with children even in winter, with the right equipment and a little more care.

title: On the European Long Distance Trail E3 through Luxembourg
short_description: On the Luxembourg stage of the European Long Distance Trail E3, you hike from Perl/Schengen via Remichen, Grevenmacher, Echternach, Vianden, Clervaux and Wiltz to Esch-sur-Sûre and along the Sûre to Martelange on the Belgian border.
long_description:
The European Long Distance Trail E3 runs for several thousand kilometres from the Black Sea through Central and Western Europe to the Iberian Peninsula. Not all parts of the trail have already been completed and marked. The route is planned to start in Turkey and run through Bulgaria, Serbia, Romania, Hungary, Slovakia, Poland, the Czech Republic, Germany, Luxembourg, Belgium, France and Spain to Portugal.
This section starts at the border crossing from Germany to Luxembourg, more precisely in Schengen.
This section starts at the border crossing from Germany to Luxembourg, more precisely in Schengen. From there, you hike the first few days mainly on little-travelled asphalt roads and through shady forests. Highlights of this section are, on the one hand, the picturesque vineyards that stretch out on both sides of the Moselle and the Wolfsschlucht (Wolf Gorge) between Echternach and Berdorf.
.
The signage is a white or yellow rectangle on a blue background, usually with arrow directions. In forests, you will often only find the yellow rectangle on trees. The paths on the first section consist of asphalt for 90% of the time, then it becomes increasingly more wooded.

title: Berghäuser Pass: Iffigenalp
short_description:
Diese leicht bis mittelschweren Wanderungen zeigen Ihnen die schönsten Wege und die gemütlichsten Berghäuser im ganzen Simmental. Lassen Sie den Alltag hinter sich und erleben Sie den Raum und die Zeit, die die Berge Ihnen bieten.
Translate to English
long_description:
These easy to moderately difficult hikes show you the most beautiful paths and the cosiest mountain houses in the entire Simmental. Leave your everyday life behind and experience the space and time that the mountains offer you.

Let yourself be spoiled by the hospitality in the mountain houses. Enjoy the food, mostly locally produced, the cheese from the nearby Alps or taste one of the homemade cakes.

One hike leads across the gentle meadows of the Lenk family mountain Betelberg, where you can discover the world of marmots in a playful way as well as admire the diversity of alpine flowers. Another path leads past the Lenkerseeli, the imposing Iffigfall to the idyllically situated Iffigenalp. Accompanied by the unique panorama of the Wildstrubel, Lenk's local mountain and pride, a trail leads from the Bühlberg to the Hahnenmoospass and Metschberg to Metschmaad. In the picturesque Fermeltal valley near Matten at St. Stephan, a unique hike and 4km of scooter downhill fun await you. Other excursion destinations include the lovely Jaunpass and the trail from cosy Oberwil to the Morgeten Alps, where old customs are still practised. The Stockhorn with its incomparable panorama of 200 Alpine peaks as well as the Jura, the Emmental and Lake Thun is another unforgettable experience.

Summarising the hikes and the mountain houses on the Simmental Mountain Houses Pass. Anyone who does not yet have the Berghäuser Pass in their rucksack should request it in advance from the Tourist Centres in Lenk, St. Stephan or Boltigen or pick it up. The card can be presented to the staff for validation every time you eat in a mountain lodge or ride on a mountain railway. If you visit 7 of the 14 mountain lodges by the end of the summer season, you will receive an attractive gift at the Tourist Centres in Lenk, St. Stephan or Boltigen. With an additional ride on each of the three mountain railways, you will also be entered into the big prize draw at the end. The first prize is a Lenk cable car season pass.

1. Lenkerseeli: From Lenk, the hike leads past the idyllic Lenkerseeli, which invites you to feed the ducks. This is a frequently visited attraction, but can be described as a valuable reserve. It serves as a spawning and breeding ground for amphibians and various bird species or as a resting place for migratory birds.
2. Iffig Falls: The hiking trail along the Iffigbach leads to the imposing Iffig Falls, which plunge over 100 m into the depths. A sight of a special kind.
3. Berghaus Iffigenalp: Continue up to Iffigenalp, where the Berghaus Iffigenalp is quietly and idyllically situated in the high valley of the Gelten-Iffigen nature reserve at 1584 metres above sea level. Here you must treat yourself to refreshment or taste one of the delicious homemade cakes or wähen. Again, have your Berghäuser pass validated and the Gfeller family will be happy to take care of your physical well-being. The dairy products and cheese (as far as possible) are delivered to the Berghaus directly from the mountain huts. The meat is also bought from local production in the Obersimmental. It is worthwhile to linger a while before the local bus takes you back to the village of Lenk in 30 minutes.

title: Hiking Route around Sorgun Pond, Ankara
short_description: You should add Sorgun Göleti and its stage to your list of places to visit in Ankara
long_description:
Sorgun Göleti is one of the most important values of tourism in Ankara with its densely forested forest area and natural landscape. Sorgun Nature Park and Sorgun Göleti, which are under protection in Ankara's Güdül province, have a very favourable area and nature for activities such as sports and recreation. 
While agriculture, animal husbandry and industry are important sources of income in the region, nature tourism has gained importance in recent years with the investments made in the region.
This approximately 7 km, two-hour hike route in the nature-inspired gölet phase is an ideal route to get away from the city life for a while. This area, which is rich in flora and fauna and home to many species, becomes an indispensable location for many people and photographers. 
Sorgun Göleti Nature Park also offers visitors many special opportunities such as picnics, camping and accommodation in bungalow structures.

title: Haldertobel
short_description: A special and hidden hiking route that includes a lake with mesmerizing hues, lots of flowing water, waterfalls and magical views that together make the hiking experience in the place one of the most magical in the upper Allgäu region
long_description:
A hiking trail hidden in a forest with idyllic landscapes and nature where you can find a lake with a gorgeous turquoise hue, a flowing stream that has shades of light blue-turquoise-green, waterfalls, whirlpools, rich vegetation, bridges and other surprises in nature. A great itinerary for those who love water and nature. One of the most beautiful and special routes in the region. Due to the fact that the route is less known, it is naturally less touristy, which makes walking it less busy and more relaxed.
The walking paths are often covered with stones as well as protruding tree roots and therefore you must pay attention to the road conditions when walking along the route, most of the walking is on the plain but occasionally includes uphill climbs which are mostly negligible. In addition to this and considering that the walk on the route is steep and occasionally includes several steps and climbing on small rocks, it is not accessible to wheelchairs or strollers.
The route is linear (one-way) but it is possible at any point to turn around and retrace the steps, but it is recommended to complete the route and only then come back as there are points of interest worth seeing all along it. You can start the route from both sides, if you are traveling with more than one vehicle, you can leave a collection vehicle on one side of the route, but walking the round trip route is recommended as it extends your stay in this wonderful place and gives a different and interesting angle on this lovely route.

title: Netzbachtalweg at the gates of Saarbrücken
short_description: The primeval forest outside the city gates - that probably only exists in the Steinbachtal/Netzbachtal nature reserve. Here, nature is allowed to do or not do what it wants and we can observe it doing so.
long_description:
This hike takes us through the "primeval forest at the gates of the city". The Steinbachtal/Netzbachtal area has been under nature conservation since 1997 and during this time has been transformed into the "green heart" of the Saar coal forest. In order to allow flora and fauna to develop undisturbed, economic use of the raw material wood is avoided there.
At the very beginning of the hike we pass the Jungfleischhütte, which originally belonged to the former hunting lodge "Philippsborn". After crossing the historic Wolfgarten, the idyllic Waldbach awaits us, along the banks of which we hike past the former Netzbach shaft. Shortly before the Netzbach flows into the Fischbach, we come to two still waters, the Rosenweiher and the Netzbachweiher. In the upper of the two, the Rosenweiher, conservationists have settled a beaver family. The Netzbachweiher is a popular place for excursions, especially in summer.
Through shady forest paths, we finally reach the starting point again, passing the Forsthaus Wolfsgarten.

images.caption: View over the Appenzell hilly landscape

title: Through Rhineland and Westphalia - Velbert
short_description: Our hike takes us across the Deilbach, which forms the border between the Rhineland and Westphalia.
long_description: The starting point of our hike is the old town of Langenberg. From there we walk south into Donnerstraße, which we follow for a short distance. We turn left into a park, which we cross towards Hordtstraße and now follow this past tennis courts into Panner Straße. Shortly after the sports field of the grammar school, we turn left at a swimming pool and now walk along the main path and Hüserstraße towards Rommel. Shortly before reaching the village, we see the Langenberg transmission mast on the left, which we pass along the edge of the forest and now walk in the direction of Hordtberg. At the end of the fields we turn left into the forest and soon reach the Bismarck Tower, from which we have an excellent view of the Rhineland and Westphalia, both separated by the Deilbach. At the Bismarck Tower we also have the opportunity to fortify ourselves in the associated restaurant. Via the cliff we return to the old town of Langenberg, the starting point of our hike.

title: Heilklimaweg 4: Bärenfelsweg Weiskirchen
short_description: A long trail with flat and moderate climbs.
long_description: From the Parkhotel, we walk to the left to the end of the spa pond. Via Burgstraße and Kirchenweg we reach the entrance to the Holzbach valley and follow it straight ahead. We cross the 4th bridge, where the water measuring station is also located. Continue straight ahead to the open-air swimming pool, which you walk almost completely around. Above the car park at the open-air swimming pool, the path leads us to the left again into the forest. We now pass a Kneipp facility on the left until we reach the Hermeswiese meadow. There we cross the Holzbach stream and follow a steeply ascending path that turns into a wide forest path. Follow this path for about 50 m and turn right up the "Eulenberg". In a sharp bend to the left, you will see a showcase. At the showcase, turn right onto a path that winds down the slope. Once in the valley, we turn left along a wide forest path. After about 400 m you can see natural monuments on both sides - the Polecat Rock on the right and the High Rock on the left. Continue straight ahead until the path bends to the right at an acute angle. Following this wide path, we reach the bus turning area of the Hochwald clinics. Here we walk along the footpath that runs parallel to the road, past the clinics, to the open-air swimming pool. From here we take the initial feeder route back in the opposite direction to the Parkhotel.

title: Transfagarasan Highway
short_description: The Romanian hinterland is full of stunning mountainscapes and hidden scenic gems. Discover picturesque lakes and spectacular views of a nearly untouched natural beauty on the second largest road of the country.
long_description: Far from its touristic hotspots, Romania has to offer several original and natural areas. The sparsely populated area of Siebenbürgen or the mighty mountain ranges of the Carpathians, to name but a few, are largely unspoilt and pristine. Among the highlights is Transfagarasan Highway, a breathtaking scenic road within the mountains of Muntenia and Transylvania. Part of this route follows the national road DN 7C and was built back in the 70s. It is said to be the second highest road of Romania. Since Jeremy Clarkson praised it as “the best road in the world” in the BBC TV series “Top Gear” in 2009, there have been arriving countless tourists to visit the scenic road. With its great views of the stunning surroundings from lofty heights of up to 2042 meters. However, it takes some effort to get there: You need to overcome a few hairpin bends and steep roads.

title: Drafted on June 20, 2008
short_description: This medium-length and relaxing hike takes us through an idyllic nature reserve.
long_description: Our hike starts at the Hotel Henriette Davidis in Wengern. From there we walk along the Henriette-Davidis-Weg until it meets the Trienendorfer Straße, which we follow to the right. At the next but one junction, turn left into Pastoratweg, then immediately left again up Pastoratberg. The Pastoratberg leads into the Pastoratbusch, onto which we turn right. We now stay on this path for quite a while, taking care not to turn onto Elbschestraße, which runs partly parallel to our path. At the next opportunity, we walk left along the edge of a small wood and continue in a right-hand bend through the wood. We stay on the path until we meet our main path again. We walk on "In der Ratelbecke", in a sharp right bend we leave the path and choose the narrow path that leads straight ahead. Via it we reach "Auf der Egge", where we turn left at a sharp angle into the forest and stay on this path until we meet the Mühlenweg. It leads us to the Wengener Mühle (mill), which we pass and reach the Trienendorfer Straße again through the "Pastoratbusch". We follow this road back to our starting point in Wengern.

title: Transcarioca Trail: Barra de Guaratiba - Grumari (Part 1)
short_description: The Transcarioca Trail crosses the city of Rio de Janeiro from end to end along a route of approximately 180 km, from Barra de Guaratiba to Morro da Urca.
long_description:
The first stretch of the Transcarioca Trail begins in Barra da Guaratiba and is inserted in the conservation unit of the Municipal Natural Park of Grumari. This park is known for its beautiful and famous wild beaches, which are only accessible by trails or by sea, and for its beautiful natural viewpoints. The largest sandbank area in the city of Rio de Janeiro is inserted in this Natural Park.
It is about 11 kilometres of unique natural beauty. Walk through the Atlantic Forest and dive into the beautiful wild beaches of Perigoso, do Meio, Funda and Inferno. From the top of Pedra do Telégrafo and Pedra da Tartaruga, the panoramic views are spectacular.

title: Around Gaildorf over the Kirgel
short_description: Beautiful views, forests and a hill accompany us on this tour.
long_description:
We start our tour at the market square in Gaildorf and first walk north along Schlossstraße. Before the Kocher bridge at the Old Castle, we turn right onto Grabenstraße and walk along the Old Castle through Eschenau until we meet the cycle path and footpath that runs parallel to the B19 federal road. We walk on this road until we reach the wooden bridge on the right over the B19. Now we continue on field paths to Unterrot, where we turn left after the railway tracks and then turn right into Oskar-Bamberg-Straße, on which we walk until we reach the B298 federal road. We cross the road, first turn right and after a short while turn left again onto the footpath until we reach the traffic lights, where we cross the country road and continue straight ahead into the Arwa settlement. Here we turn into Gerhart-Hauptmann-Straße and follow this until we reach Einsiedelweg, where we walk into the forest.
From here we follow the signs "schwarze Zahl 3" (black number 3) until we reach the television converter. Over the ridge of the Kirgel we walk until we reach a gravel road. At the following fork, we turn right to the Kerner tower, from where we can enjoy a wonderful panorama of Gaildorf and Schwäbisch Hall. Via a forest path we pass a playground and descend back into the town. We cross the railway tracks and return via Kernerstraße and Graf-Pückler-Straße to the starting point of our tour, the market square in the town centre of Gaildorf.

title: Through Wiesenthal Switzerland
short_description: We explore Wiesenthal Switzerland, where a nature conservation project is trying to preserve the unique character of the landscape with the help of sheep grazing.
long_description: We walk down Gartenstraße, turn left and then walk right towards the sports field at Köpfel. At the first fork we go right, at the second left. Behind the Köpfel we turn left with a view at the pasture fence. Along the nature reserve Wiesenthaler Berg we reach the trout farm. We take the forest path to the left and reach an idyllic rest hut with a nature monument. Follow the signs to Roßdorf. At the entrance to the village, we take a sharp turn to the left and hike along the edge of the forest to the Nebelgefecht memorial stone with a magnificent view. At the foot of the mountain, we circle Friedrichshof on the left in a wide arc and return to Wiesenthal.

The landscape around Wiesenthal is captivating in its loveliness.

title: Round from Kaltensundheim over the elbow
short_description: From Kaltensundheim we hike to the highest mountain in the Thuringian Rhön. We return via Kaltenwestheim and along the stream.
long_description: From the main road we turn right into Mittersdorfer Straße. Soon we follow Friedensstraße to the left to a car park. This is where our path begins, which runs straight ahead until we reach a T-junction. We turn right and now follow the signs to Eisenacher Haus. Passing an area nature monument, we reach a viewpoint shortly before the turnoff to Eisenacher Haus. Now we start a short ascent to the Ellenbogen to finally continue our way to the Thüringer Haus. On the way, we learn something about the history at the information board "Urbarmachung des Ellenbogens" (Reclamation of the Ellenbogen), and about the nature of the region in the animal enclosure. We follow the signs over the Weidberg to Kaltenwestheim and past the Stedtenmühle mill back to Kaltensundheim.

title: घनगड किला ट्रैक
short_description: घनगड किले का हाइकिंग मार्ग महाराष्ट्र के सह्याद्रि पर्वतश्रेणी में स्थित ह ै और यह मार्ग एकोल गांव से शुरू होकर 300 साल पुराने घनगड किले तक जाता है।
long_description:
घनगड किला महाराष्ट्र के पुणे जिले में ताम्हिनी घाट में स्थित है। यह लोनावला से लगभग 30 किलोमीटर और पुणे से 100 किलोमीटर की दूरी पर स्थित है। यह पुणे इलाके के किला-समूह एक महत्वपूर्ण सदस्य है जिसमें निकटवर्ती तैलबैला, कोरीगढ़, सारसगढ़ और सुधागढ़ भी शामिल हैं। घनगड किले का मुख्य उद्देश्य कैदियों को हिरासत में लेना और लाभदायक पुणे-कोंकण व्यापार मार्ग पर नजर रखना था। साल 1818 तक घनगड किला महान मराठा साम्राज्य के अधीन था। 17 मार्च, 1818 को पास स्थित कोरीगढ़ किले पर अंग्रेज़ों के कब्ज़े के बाद घनगड किले को भी अंततः ब्रिटिश सेना के हवाले कर दिया गया।
एकोल गाँव के बेस कैंप से घनगड किले तक का रास्ता आसान और सुन्दर है। एकोल गांव से नवरा-नवरी पहाड़ों का शानदार नजारा दिखता है। किले की ओर जाने वाली ट्रेल का रखरखाव अच्छा है। किले की तलहटी पर पॅहुचने पर ट्रेल थोड़ी बोल्डर वाली हो जाती है। किले में घुसने से पहले एक चट्टानी गुफा को पार करना पड़ता है।
छत्रपति शिवाजी महाराज ट्रेल संगठन ने किले के मुख्य द्वार पर 15 फ़ीट ऊँची लोहे की सीढ़ियां लगाई हैं जिससे किले पर जाना बहुत आसान हो गया है। किले की असली पत्थर की सीढ़ियां ब्रिटिश ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी ने 1818 में घानागढ़ किले पर कब्जा करने के बाद ध्वस्त कर दी थी था। किले के दुसरे प्रवेश द्वार पर रॉककट बावड़ी (तालाब) है जिसका पानी पीने योग्य है।
किले के शीर्ष पर पहुँचने पर मुलशी झील, तैलबैला किले, सारसगढ़ किले, पिंपरी झील, और तमहिनी घाट के सुन्दर व्यू दीखते हैं। किले में रात्रि आवास भी किया सकता है। इसके लिये किले के प्रवेशद्वार पर स्थित गरजइ देवी मंदिर के करीब ही तम्बू लगा सकते हैं।

title: Scenic hike above the right bank of the Elbe near Děčín
short_description: In 2010, the Elbe Valley, which reaches a depth of up to 300 metres in places, was declared a national nature reserve in the Czech Republic. It is the deepest sandstone canyon in Europe and an exceptional natural area.
long_description:
Our hike first takes us from the banks of the Elbe through the Dürrkamnitz Gorge (Suchá Kamenice), a 7 km long stream that rises near Bynovec. The cool stream valley is very popular, especially on hot summer days. However, the stream only has enough water in spring or after extensive rainfall - then you can also see waterfalls and rapids there. The path is surrounded by high rock walls, the rocks and fallen trees in the semi-darkness of the canyon are overgrown with mosses and lichens.
Soon afterwards we reach the hamlet of Labská Stráň. This is already at an altitude of 350 m and is partly surrounded by rocks. On one side of the village there is a magnificent view of the rock formations above Hřensko, on the other side the mountains Großer and Kleiner Zschirnstein and the 385 m high Zirkelstein, which are already in Saxon Switzerland, dominate the landscape.
.
Near Labská Stráň is the Belvedere viewpoint, a rock terrace with a beautiful view of the Elbe valley, located about 130 m above the river. A world record in traverse climbing was set here in 1998 above the Elbe Valley at 953.63 m - from the "Belvedere" lookout point near Labská Stráň to a rock formation in Dolní Žleb. Zdeněk Kadlec from Děčín climbed the Elbe Valley in July 1998 in a time of 59 minutes and 6 seconds at a height of 180 m. This type of climbing is called the Tyrolean Traverse - climbing a rope across a river or canyon.
Past other beautiful viewpoints such as the Rosskamm (Růžová vyhlídka) hike on with beautiful views of the Elbe Valley, the Elbe Sandstone Mountains and the Bohemian Central Uplands. Passing between fields and meadows into the rocks, we reach a turnoff to the Sun Gate, a real rock gate. Finally we ll reach Arnoltice (Arnsdorf). The village was first mentioned in the 14th  century. The landmark of the village is the late Baroque Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary from 1756-1758, which had to be almost completely rebuilt after a devastating fire in 1906. 
About the Arnsdorf Walls (Arnoltické stěny) it s not far to the Dürrkamnitz Gorge and back to our starting point.

title: Kneipp Hiking Amden
long_description:
A significant component of the old health teachings of Kneipp are water applications on legs and arms which are intended to stimulate circulation.

Starting at the mountain station's chair lift at Mattstock, the tour leads you to the Durschlegi vista point and into the center of town. The stations along the way have information panels and invite visitors to test the Kneipp methods in Steinbrunnen and in easily accessible streams.

title: Through the Vogtland near Klingenthal
short_description: This circular walk takes us along the German-Czech border to Aschberg and via Sachsenberg-Georgenthal back to Klingenthal.
long_description:
Our hike starts at the Tourist Information in Klingenthal. From there we walk from Schlossstraße into Kirchstraße, turn right and reach Untere Marktstraße via the market square. We follow Auerbachstraße to the right for a short distance before leaving it to the left via Dietrich-Bonhoeffer-Straße. We walk along this road for quite a while until we cross Bergstraße and turn diagonally left onto Zur Alm. We walk out of the town into the forest and turn left not at the first junction, but at the first crossroads. On this path we reach the street Körnerberg and turn right onto the Kamerunweg, on which we stay for some time before we follow the Waldhäuserweg to the left. We cross the Waldgutstraße and go straight on the Höhenweg, which we soon leave to the left via the Kammweg. Now we walk parallel to the German-Czech border, which is why the Kammweg also becomes the border road. After a bend to the right, we continue on the border path until we reach the road Am Aschberg. This leads us into the forest, where we meet the Aschbergstraße and follow it to the left. We meet the border road again, follow it to the left and take the third turn to the left. Via the "Himmelsleiter" (ladder to heaven) we reach the Zollstraße in Sachsenberg-Georgenthal and cross the municipality by changing from the Zollstraße a short distance to the right onto the Auerbachstraße and then continue immediately to the right on the Pestalozzistraße. This takes us out of the village. We go through a short stretch of forest and meet the forest road, which we follow to the left. Soon we meet the state road Falkensteiner Straße, take it to the right and then turn left into Fuchslochweg. We keep left and then turn sharp right onto Schulstraße. We turn diagonally left across Schulstraße and Siedlerstraße into the forest. In the forest, our path bends to the left both at the first junction and shortly afterwards at a T-junction. After a while, our path runs parallel to the Alte Kottenheider Straße for a short distance, but then leads us further through the forest to the right. After a right-hand bend, our path again comes to a T-junction, where we continue to the left. A little later we leave the forest and reach the street Amtsberg. This is also the location of the Klingenthal Zoo, which we can visit after our hike. Via Kirchstraße and Schlossstraße we return to our starting point, the Tourist Information.
Directly next to the Tourist Information is the Music and Winter Sports Museum, which is well worth a visit. It is also worth taking a detour to the round church "Zum Friedefürsten" or to the Schaumanufaktur for accordion and harmonica making.

title: Viewing tour near Langenburg
short_description: On this hike we can enjoy wonderful views over the Jagst valley again and again. A detour to Bächlingen is a good idea to visit the village church and the Ark Bridge.
long_description: We start our tour at the Roseneck holiday village on the outskirts of Langenburg. From there we walk to the left on the Breberweg in the direction of Gerabronn. This high trail offers beautiful views over the Jagst valley and of Langenburg Castle. As we continue, we pass the "Fischer" sheep cheese dairies and turn right at the "Im Heftle" junction. We walk slightly downhill through the forest to the covered rest area, which is close to the former Katzenstein Castle, of which, however, nothing remains. With the Jagst river on our left, we walk along the Katzensteinsteige and the Mühlbergweg along the slope towards Bächlingen. We can make a detour to Bächlingen and look at the village church with frescoes from the 14th century and the Ark Bridge. A state road leads back to Langenburg, but we turn right onto the Totensteige and return to our starting point via this bumpy forest path.

title: Industrial Heritage Trail Limmat-Wasserschloss
short_description: Thanks to its large rivers, the northern part of Aargau grew into an industrial landscape of rare density in the 19th and 20th centuries.
long_description:
Many of these factories and power plant buildings are still standing and bear witness to a culture that left a lasting mark on the people of the region, but is now disappearing.

In the first half of the 19th century, large textile factories were built and with them the first workers' settlements. The rivers were the starting point for the construction of power stations to drive the machines and later for electricity generation. In the second half of the 19th century, the metal and machine industry settled. With industrialisation, the railway age arrived. Striking evidence of all these developments has been preserved.

The Limmat-Wasserschloss Industrial Heritage Trail is a hiking trail that leads past buildings steeped in industrial history. At the objects there are boards containing information on the history, significance and current use of the site. The starting points of the trail sections are railway stations. The trail is part of the network of hiking trails and is signposted with yellow signs.

title: Outdooractive Winter Event 2024 - Variant 2 - Renksteg to Birgsau
short_description: The winter hike from the Renksteg parking lot in southern Oberstdorf to Birgsau offers a varied and idyllic tour through the snow-covered landscape of the Allgäu Alps.
long_description:
The well-prepared trail first leads to the impressive Heini-Klopfer ski jump, one of the largest ski jumps in the world, which is particularly impressive in winter.
After a short break, the trail continues through the Stillachtal valley, where you hike along the gently flowing Stillach river towards Birgsau. The snow-covered forests and peaceful atmosphere make this route a special experience.
After around 1.5 hours, we reach the small village of Birgsau, where inns with warm drinks and regional specialties invite us to stop for a bite to eat.

title: GM Ringway 12 - Norden to Bury via Knowle Hill
short_description: Stage 12 of the GM Ringway - Greater Manchester's long-distance trail - connects Norden (buses from Rochdale & Bury) with Bury town centre.

title: Along the Battertfelsen around Baden-Baden
short_description: On the small Baden-Baden panorama loop, you will experience some highlights around Baden-Baden: Engelskanzel and Teufelskanzel, Strohhütte and the ruins of Hohenbaden offer magnificent views.
long_description: From the starting point at the Caracalla-Therme, we follow the signposting with stylised Nordic walker on a yellow background and with a black square on the entire tour. We walk through the extensive Rotenbach spa gardens and cross the Rotenbachtalstraße to follow the Rotenbächle for 2 km to the Teufelskanzel. Now we walk steadily uphill through deciduous forests on wide forest paths. Again and again, windthrow areas offer interesting views of the Battert rocks still ahead. After about 3 km, we reach the Teufelskanzel (Devil's Pulpit Rock) and enjoy the magnificent view there. We cross the Rotenbachtalstraße and come to the Engelskanzel via a narrow forest path. We continue walking through the forest to the Untere Batterhütte, a small shelter on the edge of the Battert rocks. At this point we have reached the highest point (500 m above sea level) of our Nordic walking tour. From here, we slowly descend on the very well signposted route, past the Hohenbaden ruins and the St. Bernhardus Chapel to the Strohhütte and back to the starting point.

The view of Baden-Baden to the left of the Unterer Felsenweg.

title: Bayrischzell Nordic Trail
short_description: A challenging Nordic walking tour that starts in the Bayrischzell spa gardens. The steep ascent at the beginning is rewarded with beautiful valley and panoramic views.
long_description: We start at the information board for the „Nordic-Aktiv-Zentrum Bayrischzell“ in the spa gardens. First we turn left and cross the Larchbach stream. From now on we follow the black and white signs. We pass a chapel of grace (1) and an old sycamore maple, which is one of the oldest of its kind in the district. There is also a Kneipp facility (2) on the right side of the path. We leave the village in a steep ascent. Our path leads over the Zeller-Alm (3). Finally, we pass the Bergcafé Sigel with a wonderful view into the valley. From Osterhofen we walk parallel to the railway tracks back to Bayrischzell. There the path takes us across the waterfall (4). Past the swimming pool (5), tennis court and children's playground, we return to the spa gardens.

images.caption: The Bergcafé Sigl offers a rest and refreshment stop as well as a fantastic view.
On the outskirts of Bayrischzell, the Legerwaldgraben plunges down to the valley in waterfalls.
The Kurpark Bayrischzell is the starting and ending point of our tour.
From the Zeller-Alm you can see the other side of the valley to the Seeberg and the Kitzlahner.

title: Baden - Wettingen - Neuenhof Cultural Trail
short_description: Sculpture Trail along the Limmat - A walk past the works of contemporary artists such as Beat Zoderer, Roman Signer or Theodor Huser;
long_description: An art exhibition in a beautiful landscape. The foundation stone for this cultural trail was laid by the municipalities of Baden, Wettingen and Neuenhof in 1991, when they organised an open-air sculpture exhibition to mark the 700th anniversary of the Swiss Confederation. Twenty-one site-specific works were selected in a competition.
