title: From Langenleiten to the Kissinger Hut
short_description: This hike takes us mainly through woodland to the Kissinger Hütte on the Feuerberg and back to Langenleiten via the basalt works.
long_description: At the entrance to Langenleiten, follow the signpost to Kissinger Hütte. A wide forest path leads leisurely uphill and soon into the forest. On the left side of the path is a meadow. At the end of the meadow, near a bench, a path turns left into the forest. We follow the marking "black, empty triangle with double bar". A wooden sign points us to the mountain path to the Kissinger Hut. It is quite steep and goes uphill in a few twists and turns. Somewhat flatter, the path leads through low beech trees (1) bent by the weather. Under natural conditions, beech would be by far the predominant tree species in the Rhön. Medieval records of Fulda monks refer to the Rhön as "Buchonia", land of virgin beech forests. Large-scale clearing in the Middle Ages created the "Land of Open Distances". It was not until 1730 that spruce was introduced by foresters. Increasingly, spruce is again being replaced by the more robust beech, as snow and storms cause great losses in the spruce forest. We walk across a mountain meadow directly to the Kissinger Hut (2), already built in 1914 and thus the oldest hikers' accommodation far and wide in the Rhön, welcomes us with a magnificent view, wooden sun loungers and a large children's playground. Here we also find the mountain station of the chairlift. The house of the Rhön Club is located in the midst of the magnificent low mountain range landscape "Naturpark Rhön" with a view of the Kreuzberg (928 m above sea level). The Kreuzberg, the holy mountain of the Franconians, is the highest excursion destination in the Bavarian Rhön. Every year, 70 to 80 pilgrimages take place to the "holy mountain". It can also be recognised by the broadcasting station of the Bavarian Broadcasting Corporation from 1951. Incidentally, the name "Rhön" is often derived from the Celtic "raino" (hilly). Numerous treeless hilltops characterise the image of this landscape in the border triangle of Bavaria, Hesse and Thuringia - witnesses to a volcanic past. Valuable landscape areas, deciduous and mixed forests, hedgerow landscapes and unique flora and fauna are the basis for the Rhön being recognised as a UNESCO biosphere reserve in 1991. The round basalt shapes are covered by green bristly grass meadows where the black-headed Rhön sheep graze. The Rhön sheep is one of the oldest livestock breeds in Germany. Since 1983, the population has been increasing again with the initiative of the "Zuchtgemeinschaft Rhönschafe" (Rhön Sheep Breeding Association). After enjoying the panoramic view, we walk to the left of the hut straight south towards the forest. Then we walk downhill on a forest path without many bends. We reach a crossroads and turn left. The gravel path leads between the active basalt plant (3) and the basalt pits to the road. The Rhön is still a main mining area for basalt in Germany. The hard, almost black basalt gravel is particularly suitable for the substructure of roads and railway tracks. We follow the wide gravel path about 200 m downhill to the left. At the second junction we leave the road and follow the gravel path marked "yellow drop". We hike about 1.5 km on the comfortable path. After a bend to the left, we turn right at a hunter's stand onto a forest path. This leads downhill and soon meets a cross path, which we follow to the right. The path goes downhill to a clearing. We walk along the edge of the meadow to the left until a blue hiking trail sign with the number three points us to the right. We walk straight downhill on a path through a high meadow and come back to the starting point of the hike. In Langenleiten, a street village with well-kept estates, we can finish the hike in the "Linde" inn.

title: Mountain tour to Oberstaufen
short_description: The very long, often lonely, but äußerst charming mountain tour offers numerous views of the Nagelfluhkette, the Alpine foothills, the Konstanz valley, the town of Immenstadt and the market town of Oberstaufen. On the way, we wander through species-rich flower meadows, reach old alps and bubbling brooks.
long_description:
The imposing Nagelfluh range, with such notable peaks as the Hochgrat or the Rindalphorn, is preceded to the north by a lower, often unnoticed mountain range. Both are separated from each other by the Ehrenschwang Valley. If the Weißach had not made its way towards Oberstaufen, we could easily continue on this ridge to Austria via the Imberg. But this way we have to descend to the banks of the river after the Spitzlerberg.
We cross the Wei&szlig on the so-called Tarzan bridge. The name suggests something imposing. However, it is only a footbridge fixed with wire ropes.
Our tour begins in the heart of Immenstadt at Marienplatz, where we can take in the beauty of the former imperial town.

Flowers in the mist at the pulpit.

title: From Filzbach to the enchanting Talalpsee and back
short_description: The Talalpsee on the Kerenzerberg in Glarus is a pearl worth discovering!
long_description:
Filzbach on the Kerenzerberg is the starting point for this hike. We climb up to the Habergschwänd mountain inn, always with a fantastic view of the fjord-like Walensee, the village of Amden lying on a sunny terrace and the striking Churfirsten peaks. A terrace with a magnificent panorama awaits us at the Habergschwänd mountain inn, where it is well worth taking a break.
Then we continue towards the Talalpsee. This enchanting place is hidden in a small side valley, which is already part of the UNESCO World Heritage Tectonic Arena Sardona.
After the lake, we can take a break.
After circling the lake, the hike takes us back down to Filzbach.
By the way: If you want to make it easier for yourself, save yourself the ascent or descent and take the chairlift from Filzbach to Habergschwänd.

short_description: Several rustic inns and the fairytale castle of King Ludwig II are on the route of this beautiful circular tour.

images.caption: At the Tegelberg summit we have a great view of the Säuling.

title: From Zwota to Kottenheide
short_description: This hike takes us from Zwota through the beautiful Glasbach valley to Kottenheide and back.
long_description: Our hike begins in Zwota at Hammerplatz. From there, we head onto Schönecker Straße, away from the centre of the village and soon change straight onto Glasbachweg. This leads us into the beautiful Glasbach valley, through which we walk for quite a while surrounded by forest. We pass the idyllically situated Glasbach pond and follow the Glasbach path, ignoring various descents. At a small clearing, three paths meet ours, which makes a left turn at this point. Some time later, the path leads us out of the forest and finally meets the road "Hämmerling", which we follow briefly to the left before we turn left over the Mühlsteig onto the "Mühlweg A". Through dense forest, we always stay on this path until it joins the Kottenheider Straße, which takes us to the village of Oberzwota. Then we take a sharp left onto Bahnhofstraße, which first turns into Bergstraße and then into Alter Weg, which takes us back to Zwota.

title: GM Ringway Stage 17 - Leigh to Irlam
short_description: Stage 17 of the GM Ringway - Greater Manchester's long-distance trail - links Leigh and Irlam via the Wigan and Salford mosslands.

title: Through the English Garden in Munich
short_description: We walk through the northern part of the English Garden in Munich.
long_description: The English Garden is a green oasis in the middle of Munich's city centre. Numerous intersecting footpaths lead through the park in magnificent natural surroundings with beautiful views of the Isar river. The northern part of the English Garden is less well known than the southern part, but offers wonderful landscape views.

images.caption: A monument commemorates Baron von Werneck, who was instrumental in the design of the English Garden around 1800.
The "Mittlere Isar" weir is used to generate electricity and at the same time offers a magnificent view over the river.
The English Garden can be traversed not only on foot, but also by carriage or bicycle taxi.
In the course of our tour, the landscape varies from typical parkland to heather-like birch forests.
Below the Mittlere Isar weir, the gravel banks are popular sunbathing spots for Munich residents.

title: Wallburg Round
short_description: This hike takes you from Wallburg on comfortable forest paths to Sulz. Again and again, the path offers magnificent views over the Rhine plain.
long_description: Our circular hike begins at the signpost in front of the Wallburg peace site. We follow the blue rhombus in the direction of Bergeneck and Sulz on the lower path to the left (not through the barrier!). At the edge of the forest, we continue to a wide road at Bergeneck and turn right to the Orschweierer Hütte. There we walk to the left past the Hubertus fountain and a barrier and above an elevated water tank to the Vogesenblick hikers' car park at the edge of the forest. Here we continue to follow the blue rhombus in the direction of Bildstöckle on the "Mittleren Weg". At the next crossroads, turn slightly left along the blue rhombus until you reach a forest road. Follow this to the left along a windthrow area to the Bildstöckle. Here you will find a memorial stone commemorating the hurricane "Lothar" of 26 December 1999. Only a few metres further on, we come to the actual wayside shrine and leave the wide path here. On an initially narrow path, we hike into the forest in the direction of Sulz. We cross a forest road and continue on the path to the next forest road, which we follow to the right. At the next fork in the path, we hike downhill past the bench on the left. After about 1 km, the path leads out of the forest above the village of Sulz. Numerous benches invite you to enjoy the view of the Rhine plain and the Vosges. Our path joins a small road, which we follow to the left, then immediately sharp right and left again into the street "Zum Schützenhaus" down into the village (blue rhombus). At the next crossroads, continue straight ahead on a footpath until it joins a road. Here we leave the path with the blue rhombus and follow the yellow rhombus to the right towards Helgenstöckle. We pass the natural swimming pool and continue to the signpost to the Sägmühle. Here we follow the road of the same name up to the right in the direction of Helgenstöckle (yellow rhombus). Before a meadow at the edge of the forest, turn left onto a farm track. About 500 m after a game reserve, we come to a fork in the road. Follow the yellow rhombus to the left (not to the right, even though the Helgenstöckle is also signposted there) along the edge of the forest on the Mattenweg. The path leads past a rest area and over a stream. After a short section of forest, we hike slightly uphill along meadows in the Sulzbach valley. In the forest, after passing a small shelter, we reach the signpost "Untere Rennweghütte" via a forest path. We go right on the forest path and after about 100 m further to the left. We also follow this path over the next intersection and continue on the unpaved Sulzbachtalwald road to the rest area at the Schützenhütte. As we are about halfway through our hike here, it is a good idea to take a break. The path continues to climb and we follow the signs towards Helgenstöckle along another windthrow area to the Altdorfer Hütte. To the right of the hut we see the wind farm at Heidenkopf. Our path continues on the Saatschulweg to the left, past the Helgenstöckle to the Schmalzgrüble. There we follow the sign towards "Lautenbach, Parkplatz" (Lautenbach, car park) to the right and continue hiking along Lautenbachstraße. Now the trail goes down the slope in large bends for about 2.5 km. 100 m after the Lautenbacher hut, we hike to the right onto the Löhleweg, which we continue to follow in the direction of Wallburg. At the edge of the forest, walk to the signpost "Glöcklinsberg". At the Löwenzahn forest kindergarten, the blue rhombus leads us right into the forest in the direction of Wallburg. We walk straight on past the Hundsrück and a large memorial stone until the path leads directly to the Wallburg peace site.

images.caption: Interesting: a sandstone tree at the side of the path.
A view of Schmieheim and the Rhine plain.
Impressive: sunset over the Black Forest heights.
This memorial stone commemorates hurricane "Lothar", which caused great devastation at Christmas 1999.

title: Large forest circuit Sanitz
short_description: We hike beautifully through the forest area north of Sanitz. If the weather is right, mushroom pickers can expect rich finds.
long_description: We circle the church clockwise and see beautiful half-timbered houses (1). We follow Fritz-Reuter-Straße to the right and turn right into the street "Hof Sanitz". Now we follow the street until it joins John-Brinckmann-Straße. Here we turn right. We walk straight ahead over a level crossing and a traffic light intersection. The path leads us out of the village. At the edge of the forest there is a farmstead with a beautiful old barn on the right. We walk straight ahead on a sandy path. This leads through the beautiful forest towards Groß Freienholz. Finally we turn left. On the left we see the Greencamp (2), a leisure facility for children and young people. Soon a rest area (3) on the right invites us to take a break. The path leads to an asphalt road, which we follow to the right. It eventually bends to the left and we continue straight ahead. We walk towards the beautifully situated Billenhagen forestry office (4) and follow the path along the fence to the right. We walk halfway around the forestry office and turn right at the fork into Schröder Schneise. Shortly after a crossroads, we see a beautiful hut on the left, a little off the path (5). We continue along the Schröder Schneise until it joins another path. Here we turn right. We walk straight on until we meet a paved path. We follow this to the left until we reach the country road. Here we turn right briefly and then turn left onto a path. This will take you to Klein Freienholz. Here a tram (6) surprises us in a garden. We go straight on at the crossroads and turn left at the next fork. Soon we come to Ribnitzer Straße, which we follow to the left. At the main road in the village, we turn right and then left into John-Brinckmann-Straße. We return to the starting point the way we came.

images.caption: This beautiful forest hut invites us to take a rest.
This bench near Klein Freienholz invites us to take a break.
The Greencamp is a very nice facility for children and young people.
The Billenhagen forestry office is charmingly situated in the forest.
The church in Sanitz was built in the 13th century.

title: Sapopema Trail - European Valley
short_description: Trail run within the indigenous lands of the Xoklengs, who develop community-based tourism in the region. The trail is in a preserved area of Atlantic Forest at an altitude of between 900 and 950 metres, passing waterfalls and incredible streams.
long_description:
Stretch 1800m long, done within a preserved stretch of secondary Atlantic Forest with some species of noble plants and many Xaxim trees in the headwaters of the Benedict River. The altitude of the trail varies from 900 à 950. The trail takes place in a remnant part of the Atlantic Forest, whose ecosystem is one of the richest in the world, but also one of the most threatened worldwide.
The journey  é carried out within the lands of the Xoklengs índios, who had their first friendly contacts with the officials of the Servício de Proteçao aos Índios (SPI), from 1914. Before this, these peoples were the survivors of a brutal process of colonisation of southern Brazil, which began in the middle of the last century and almost totally exterminated them.
The trail begins along a narrow track inside the forest. With one of the community's indigenous people as our guide, we get to know some species of native trees. From a wooden belvedere, we can see some of these species from above. We pass by one of the springs of the Benedito River, which soon becomes a beautiful creek with a stone bottom and incredibly clear waters. The trail continues along the bank and sometimes crossing the stream. Some ropes placed by the índios help us to walk on the stones, sometimes covered with slime and very slippery.
Next we come to a Sapopema tree, which gives the trail its name. This tree is native to the Atlantic Forest, and has a trunk that served as a hiding place for the Indians, who also used to communicate with other Indians by tapping on its trunk, making a loud sound that can be heard from a long distance. As we continue on the trail, we come across some tree ferns, a species of fern famous in the region. From its stem can be extracted one of the products for the manufacture of an alcoholic drink produced long ago by the Indians. Finally we arrive at an Indian hut in the middle of the forest, where we taste meat, a kind of bread and a natural tea, made from pieces of bamboo placed on the fire, as if they were natural pots. We listened to some stories of the Indians in their own Xokleng language, a language unique in the world and preserved by these people.
This was one of the most incredible experiences in the European Valley, in Santa Catarina. Without a doubt it is listed as one of the best trails in the region.

title: GM Ringway Stage 20 - Stretford to Manchester
short_description: Stage 20 of the GM Ringway - Greater Manchester's long-distance trail - connects Stretford with the city centre via a series of largely traffic-free waterside paths.

title: On the Jägersteig trail near Obernzell
short_description: This route leads almost exclusively through pleasant forest. On the Jägersteig, a fantastic view over the Danube valley rewards us for our efforts.
long_description: Right at the beginning of our tour we come across the community's protection and peace cross. It was erected in 2002 after a flash flood. We keep to the markings ("Donaunixe", white "8" in a red circle), enter the forest and follow the Eckerbach stream to the Hammermühle mill. From here we turn left. The path leads steeply upwards to the Niedernhof. We read on a sign that the area in front of the farm is called "Tabakstampf". We continue through the forest, cross a municipal road and arrive at the Jägersteig. This old hunting trail runs along the mountain parallel to the Danube. The trail is strenuous, but the views of the Danube valley from a rest area reconcile us before we get back to our starting point.

images.caption: In some places the Jägersteig is flooded with light.
One of the many views from the Jägersteig into the Danube valley.

title: Lomaș Cottage - Lake Iezer
short_description: This is the fastest route to Lake Iezer in Călimani, respectively to the crest of the Călimani Mountains, starting from Toplița (provided you arrive early at the starting point with a car). The route is not very frequented, however it is often recommended for families with children.
long_description:
The road from Toplița is more of a forest road, also good for a mountain bike, and it is also a good stretch of land near the lake.
From the hut you walk about half way through the pine forest, then you come out in a clearing where you enter several paths. Follow the signpost to Lake Iezer, your final destination.

title: Along the wild and romantic Mangfall
short_description: We enjoy an easy but scenic hike along the banks of the Mangfall in the area between Hohendilching and the Maxlmühle. The trail often runs along small paths in the riparian area.
long_description: The 58 km long Mangfall is fed by Lake Tegernsee. The adjacent mountain range of the Bavarian Alps to the south is called the Mangfall Mountains, as this is the main catchment area of the Mangfall. At Grub, at the so-called Mangfallknie, the river leaves its northern direction and turns southeast, later east. In Rosenheim, the Mangfall flows into the Inn. The course of the river has been strongly influenced by economic use, e.g. power generation, but today attempts are being made to compensate for this by means of renaturation measures. At Maxlmühle, the M-waterway meets the Mangfall. This cycle path leads from the Deutsches Museum to Gmund am Tegernsee. On the way, important stations of Munich's water supply are visited. At Fentbach we can visit a late Celtic oppidum.

title: Through the Lubmin Heath by the Baltic Sea
short_description: We hike through the Lubminer Heide to the former nuclear power plant, back along the Baltic Sea beach and have the choice between the dune path or the shore.
long_description: We start our walk at the tourist information (1). It is no coincidence that the carefully reconstructed building is reminiscent of a railway station. But the station lost its track in 1945 - it was dismantled as a reparation. We walk north past the supermarket and keep straight ahead at the roundabout on Freester Straße. It takes us past St. Peter's Church (2) and the cemetery. Finally, the asphalt road ends and we walk east on sandy heath ground to the former Lubmin nuclear power plant (3). The power station was shut down in 1995. Since the 1970s, it produced about ten percent of the GDR's electricity consumption. On the paved road, we pass the sewage treatment plant on the left. After 500 m, the main path bends slightly to the right. Our path branches off to the left towards the Baltic Sea. When we reach the coastal forest with the pine trees, we have the choice between walking directly along the shore of the Greifswald Bodden or along the edge of the coastal forest with beautiful views, but also through loose sand in places. On the way through the coastal forest, there are always beautiful views and numerous opportunities to rest. On the way through the coastal forest, after a few kilometres we come to the beach promenade of the seaside resort of Lubmin. Here we continue to the pier (4). The forest path on the left connects the pier with the tourist information office. Directly at the foot of the pier, Café Strandläufer invites you to take a break. On Waldstraße we pass the spa gardens (5) with the concert shell and return to our starting point.

title: Totenköppel Tour Ulrichstein-Helpershain
short_description:
The hike takes us to the Totenköppel near Meiches, one of only two Sippenfriedhöfen in Germany.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description: The hike continues in an easterly direction up the hill, past the sports field, then turns south across Meicheser Stra&szlig to Helges, where there are numerous wind turbines. It continues in an easterly direction, first along the edge of the forest, then a short distance through the Lohwald. At the edge of the forest, it turns north and affords a view of Meiches and the Schwalm valley. The trail continues in a northerly direction to the Totenköppel with the Sippenfriedhof (clan cemetery) and the Totenkirche (church for the dead). Each house in the village has its own grave, so that the deceased are usually buried in the graves of their ancestors. For strangers such as craftsmen, teachers, gypsies and priests there was a place at the edge of the cemetery. The church of the dead was built in 1729 on the remains of the original St. George's Church, which dates back to around 1300. Even today, an open-air service is held here every year on the second Pentecost holiday, attracting many visitors. First to the south, then to the west, the route continues to the edge of the forest. Back at the forest crossroads, the path continues south-west through the forest. At the top of the Goldener Steinrüch, from where you can enjoy a very beautiful view. Now head in a north-westerly direction, via Engelröder Stra&szlig into the valley of the Katharinenbach stream and further north back to Helpershain.

title: Up to Langenhard near Lahr
short_description: The hike leads from Lahr on comfortable forest paths up about 200 metres in altitude to Langenhard. From here, the trail leads back through the forest via the triangular Bannstein.
long_description: We go along the cycle path to the left and follow the blue rhombus in the direction of Langenhard to the edge of the town. The path marking with the yellow rhombus leads us in the direction of Marienquelle, to the left to Burghardseck and further in the direction of Langenhard. At the forester's lodge, turn right to the blue rhombus, which we follow uphill to the left of the Heidengraben. Majestic trees line the path. At a small clearing, a wooden sign points to the left to the Burghardrückenweg. After 1 km, the alley-like forest path leads to a former Celtic ring wall, which has been overgrown by brambles in the meantime. The actual hiking trail continues along the blue rhombus to the chapel on the panoramic plateau of Langenhard. Over the "Dreieckiger Bannstein" the yellow rhombus leads us towards "Lahr, Schlüssel" at the entrance to the town and straight on through the residential area to the town hall on Tiergartenstraße. We walk back along Tiergartenstraße to the right to the collegiate church.

title: Walking at the pilgrimage site Neukirchen b. Hl. Blut
short_description: This beautiful tour near the place of pilgrimage Neukirchen b. Hl. Blut offers us wonderful views and interesting surprises.
long_description: We follow the main road to the right and walk to the right into Morethgasse, which turns into a dirt road. A cross commemorates the plague dead who were once buried here. At the next fork in the road, we turn left. Here we are surprised by a colourful crucifix with a resting bench. Directly behind the football field, we turn right. In Altzern we follow the road to the right at the T-junction. We can stop at the Birnbaum inn. At the end of the village, at the group of dead men's boards with a rest area, we follow the path to the left. This leads into the Lamberger Straße - we walk to the right. At the T-junction we turn right into the main road. At the Iglhaut bakery, we turn right and walk up the steps to the starting point, where we can visit the pilgrimage museum.

title: Kellberg-Runde
short_description: On this Nordic walking tour we experience the lookout point of a Bavarian king and a natural outdoor pool.
long_description: We follow the markings ("Donaunixe", white "2" in a red circle) through sparse forest, soon pass the outskirts of Kapfham and continue hiking to the König-Max-Höhe. Here a memorial stone was set to commemorate the king's visit in 1852. Behind Wingersdorf we enter the forest again. At Hochstein we enjoy the magnificent view over the Danube. We continue walking to the outskirts of Buchsee and then across the open field towards Sonnenhang. After crossing the road, we walk along the Hörreuter Bach stream until we reach the natural outdoor swimming pool at the golf courses. We walk on a field path to Eggersdorf. From there we have a last wide view before we return to our starting point past the spa clinic.

title: Great Wall of China loop walk at Badaling
short_description: A nice but also crowded loop walk with some steeps climbs and descents on one of the most popular and best restored sections of the Great Wall of China at Badaling with spectacular views of the surrounding mountains.
long_description: The Great Wall at Badaling is the most well-restored section of the Great Wall of China and due to its vicinity to Beijing, also one of the most popular and crowded sections to visit. Due to its convenient accessibility, do not expect to be by yourself when you visit. The infrastructure is set up for large numbers of people, although public toilets can only be found at the start, at the middle and at the end of the walk. Because of the perfect restauration and the crowds that you will meet, especially on the first part of the suggested loop walk, do not expect an original or exclusive historic experience. Nevertheless, the spectacular backdrop of the Great Wall with the surrounding mountains will give provide a spectacular scenery and experience. Especially after passing the apline coaster, the cableways and the highest watch tower, the descent on the second part of the walk will be much less crowded. Here, you will also find sections of the wall, where you will have time to take a photo without crowds of people in the background.

short_description: This walk is 19.6 kilometres and takes 5 hours.
long_description:
The Pijnven forest area is a beautiful nature reserve where you can take a perfect forest walk. There are playing fields for children and long hiking trails for adults. The nature reserve consists of beautiful forests, heathland and shifting sands.

title: From Wissembourg in France to Guttenberg Castle Ruins and the German Wine Gate
short_description: On this moderately difficult tour we start in France.
long_description: We start our hike in the picturesque French town of Wissembourg. It will lead us to the worth seeing ruins of Guttenberg, a rock castle that was destroyed during the Peasants' War in 1525, and to the German Wine Gate in Schweigen, the southern end of the German Wine Route. It was built in 1936 to make the wine-growing region of the Palatinate better known. the Palatinate wine-growing region. In Wissembourg in France, just 1 km away, the German Wine Gate, which was with a swastika flag was regarded as a provocation. The Nazi symbol, which was also carved into one of the gate's pillars, was was subsequently removed.

title: Around the Bildstein in the High Rhön
short_description: This very beautiful tour takes us through forest and moorland areas around the Bildstein. We enjoy magnificent views from the heights into the beautiful Ulstertal valley.
long_description: We follow the marked hiking trail into the forest. At a fork with a sign warning of blasting work, we turn right. Soon a path branches off to the right to a viewpoint (1). From here we have a wonderful view into the Ulstertal valley. We continue to follow the main path and enjoy beautiful valley views where the forest opens up (2). After two hairpin bends, we come to an asphalt road, which we follow to the left. This part offers us another great view (3). We meet a road and go to the right. At a bend to the right, turn left. At a crossroads we turn left and follow the feeder mark of the Hochrhöner, the "green ó on a white background" , back to the starting point, where we can take a deep breath at a rest area.

title: Emerald Trail Grisons-Lombardy: Stage 5
short_description: On stage 5 of the Emerald Trail
long_description:
From Castasegna walk towards Italy, by the scenic variant of the Via Bregaglia in Somasascia, to Savogno and Piuro, where the Natural Landmark of the imposing Acquafraggia waterfalls can be admired. It is advised to use this trail only in summer, as the terrain is rugged and can become dangerous in winter or with rainy weather. The waterfalls became a natural landmark in 1983. The stream originate on the alpine watershed separating the Mediterranean water catchment from the Rhine's. The water flow out of a wonderful little Alpine lake, then flow precipitously in their steep and craggy river bed towards Savogno, to fall to the underlying Piuro flats. In summer it is pleasant to relax in the rest area at the foot of the waterfall. A trail leads up to the waterfall's first fall, in an enchanting environment, with rare plant species and a stunning view over Piuro. Once in Piuro you can visit the Vertemate Franchi Palace, the only building to survive the 1618 landslide. It is a typical 16th century palazzo with an Italian garden, historical vineyard and a century-old chestnut grove. In the area many characteristic taverns, named "crottos", can be found. They were originally found in the vicinity of natural caves that could ensure constant temperatures all year round and where wine, cheese and cured meats continue to be stored and sold. There are hundreds of crottos in Val Chiavenna, from the informal to the more sophisticated kind. Often you will be allowed, on request, to visit the cave. In the more modest types of crotto the typical table d'hote can be found: Val Chiavenna gnocchis, meat and vegetables on the stone, black polenta, cheese, Prosto biscuits, wine. In Piuro visit Crotto Belvedere, on the Mera River or take a break in the shade of old chestnut trees in the Crotto Quartino. After that head towards Chiavenna, a town at the foot of the Rhaetic Alps, where the Spluga and Bregaglia valleys meet. Along the towns alleyways you will find many vestiges of the past. The Museo del Tesoro, housed in the San Lorenzo parsonage, is of outstanding interest. The Bottonera Mill, in Chiavenna's old industrial neighbourhood, is an extremely rare example of industrial architecture where the life of XIX century millers can still be experienced. In the Comunità Montana della Valchiavenna the Valchiavenna Museum can be found. Last, though not least, visit the Natural Reserve of the Giants' potholes and their botanical garden.

Trail description: Maria Gredig, valchiavenna.com, viabregaglia.it



Environment, NATURA2000, Protected areas

Fauna, Natura2000 species

Insects: Libythea celtis
Birds: Pernis apivorus, Dryocopus martiu, Lyrurus tetrix

Other species of interest: Ficedula albilollis, Accipiter gentili, Tichodroma murari

Protected areas, proposed Emerald sites, Natura 2000 sites

WWF-proposed Emerald site Val Bregaglia:
Southern, almost Mediterranean wildlife characterizes the Val Bregaglia, with altitudes varying from 700 to 3300 m. The landscape is rich with chestnut woodland and dry meadows and generally high biological diversity. The site is shared by the municipalities of Bondo, Castasegna, Soglio, and Stampa. The most frequent habitats are dry meadows and wetlands.

The Val Bregaglia is an IBA (Important Bird Area), an internationally recognized stopover area for migratory birds. The identification and description of IBA's (a BirdLife project) was instrumental in the designation of the Special Protection Areas of the EU Natura 2000 network.

The Acquafraggia Falls are an imposing feature of the landscape. The falls are not only beautiful, they are also very fascinating geologically and constitute a unique habitat. On the rock walls, and at the foot of the falls, specialized plant species grow. (valchiavenna.com)

The "Parco delle Marmitte dei Giganti" ("Giants' Potholes Park"), that includes a Regional Nature Reserve, is just outside Chiavenna. It is easily accessible by the old paths and muletracks that once led to the ancient soapstone quarries. What you see now is the result of the erosive action of glaciers over the millennia. The nearby "Paradiso Botanical Garden" contains a rich collection of rare and interesting plant species. (valchiavenna.com)

WWF's tips for hikers

Plan each stage carefully, purchase a 1:25000 map, use light but sturdy equipment (hiking boots, rain cape, binoculars ). Be sure to carry a small supply of water and food. We suggest you taste local food (possibly organic) at resting places and restaurants.
Do not litter, do not pick up flowers or rocks and in no way disturb the local fauna. It is unsafe for inexperienced hikers to leave the marked trails and it may cause disturbance to wildlife.

title: Imsbach Officer's Trail in Theley
short_description: On the "Officers' Trail" we hike on shady forest paths around the Imsbach estate, which gave this tour its name. Wonderful views of the Schaumberger Land and the Hochwald open up along the way.
long_description:
The name "Offizierspfad" (Officers' Path) picks up on the history of the Imsbach farm estate, which had its heyday at the beginning of the 19th century. Louis Lapointe received the Hofgut from Napoleon as a reward for his military successes. He subsequently shaped the area around the Hofgut into a landscape park.
The trail leads us through extensive forest landscapes along the former border of the Saar region to the German Reich as well as the former border of the Imsbach farm estate to the district of Mettnich (part of today's Primstal, municipality of Nonnweiler). Along the way, we pass numerous historic boundary stones and the Rötel district between Theley and Selbach. The magnificent views reach as far as the Schaumberger Land, the Hochwald and the Freisener Höhe.
On the way back, we pass the Johann-Adams-Mühle. In the shady courtyard, you can take a rest in one of the last preserved mill buildings in the Saarland. We then come to the Imsbach estate with its restored chapel. At the idyllic pond, we can once again enjoy the nature of the Saarland before returning to the starting point.

title: Emerald Trail Grisons-Lombardy: Stage 4
short_description: Stage 4 on the Emerald Trail
long_description:
The border village of Castasegna lies on the mountain slope between the Mera River and the Brèntan plateau and is known for the surrounding vast chestnut forest. The village is made interesting by the vernacular architecture of its old centre, the many old fountains and washing troughs, and the more sophisticated Villa Garbald (1862). The nearby Casnàc ruins, on flatland beyond the Mera, are worth mentioning, as well as the Caslàc tower (rebuilt in 1891) on the northern slope. The Brentan chestnut forest is one of the largest in Europe. Of the village's two reformed churches, the SS. Trinità church dates back to 1660, while the one dedicated to st. John the Baptist was first mentioned in 1408.

The fourth stage of the trails starts between the confectioner's shop, and the post office. The trail will lead you to the river through the lower part of the village. You will cross the river on the stone bridge and start up the incline on ample hairpin turns, glimpsing chestnut groves and old cattle sheds. After 45 minutes you will get to a road that will take you down to Bondo. Bondo lies at the foot of a mountain that blocks out the sun and leaves the village in the shade during three months every winter. The most important building is the Salis Palace, built in the second half of the eighteenth century by the Grisons ambassador to the English court Geronimo Salis-Soglio. On the small square stands the S. Martino church. On its façade old frescoes were recently brought back to light. The trail will leave the village centre behind and take you to the Valle Bondasca on an uphill winding road. Just before the bridge, the trail will bend and lead you on a steep track to Cugian. On the way you will enjoy breath-taking views of the Bondasca valley and the Sciora range. In Cugian you will walk the dirt road leading down to Ceresc. Half an hour before getting to Ceresc, the trails will bend to the right and will steeply cut through the woods to the road below leading back to Bondo. On the same road you took at the start of the excursion you will head back down Castasegna.

Trail description: Chatrigna Signorell with information taken from viabregaglia.it

Chestnut forests can be found in Castasegna, with the Brentan forest and Brègan chestnut wood, which also include dry meadows and peat bogs.

title: To the Hessigheim rock gardens
short_description:
This varied hike takes us past fields and orchards to the Hessigheim rock formations, which are famous far beyond the region.
Through vineyards, the picturesque wine village of Hessigheim and a natural hillside forest back to Besigheim.
long_description:
After just a few metres, the shell limestone rocks of the Hessigheimer Felsengärten towering high above the Neckar valley catch the eye. The approximately 300 m long, almost closed rock face with natural rock walls and towers in front dates from the Upper Muschelkalk geological period (~235 million years ago). The nature reserve »Felsengärten« is home to a large number of rare plant and animal species. Another species that is no longer unknown in these latitudes is the climber, who finds a natural recreational and training environment here in the greater Stuttgart area. Especially on nice days, numerous hikers and climbers cavort on and between the walls. From the foot of the cliffs to the banks of the Neckar, steep slope vineyards have been cultivated for centuries, which is appreciated not only by local wine lovers.
  When walking through Hessigheim, it is worth taking a look to the left and right: a multitude of beautifully renovated half-timbered houses can be discovered in the town centre. Besides the 16th century town hall and the "Altes Rathaus" (Old Town Hall), the Martinskirche (St. Martin's Church) is particularly worth seeing.

title: Forest history border hike near Finsterau
short_description: A lonely, idyllic hike to the Bavarian border awaits us. We hike through a former timber drift region with many Bächenes and Klausen in the Bavarian Forest National Park and enjoy the rustic landscape, which is almost untouched by human hand, true to the National Park motto "Let nature be nature";
long_description: At the car park, follow the forest road downhill. Finally, a path branches off to the right, which leads us through young forest to the Alte Klause. A sunny path leads along the Reschbach to the Schwellgraben. Our next destination is the Reschbachklause, today a quiet mountain lake. The trail continues uphill to the German-Czech border. Here the path turns right and leads us up to the Siebenstein rock. A beautiful view awaits us. We hike downhill along the rocky path. Crossing the road to the Czech Republic, we walk to the Teufelsklause. We hike along several Bäche to Finsterauer Filz. The last part of our route runs parallel to the road back to the car park.

images.caption: View from the flat part of the Felsensteig, which has provided access to the forest area since 1910.
The view from Siebensteinfelsen to Finsterau.
The border also marks the watershed between the Elbe and the Danube.
The Reschbachklause is the largest Triftklause within the National Park and was still in use in 1950.
One of the many descriptive information boards that accompany the historical nature trail.

title: Via Gottardo: Erstfeld - Göschenen
long_description:
The historic Gotthard mule track had an important function as a national trade route. Until the opening of the Gotthard railway line in 1882, the connection between north and south was considered one of the most important in Europe.

The Amsteg section begins with the actual climb into the Riedweg to the Gotthard Pass. In Meitschlingen you leave the Riedweg and walk a short section along the national road to Felliboden. You cross the cantonal road, national road and Reuss river over the new suspension bridge.
With a view of the roaring river, the trail leads via Gurtnellen Wiler to Wassen. After a short stretch on the asphalt road, the trail turns into the left-bank mule track and climbs up the valley to Göschenen. Cross the station square at the SBB Göschenen railway station.

title: डेविड स्कॉट टरैक
short_description: ब्रिटिश प्रशासक डेविड स्कॉट के नाम वाली यह ट्रेल पूर्वोत्तर के मेघालय राज्य में है। इ स पुरानी और खूबसूरत ट्रेल को डेविड स्कॉट ने साल 1800 में घोड़ागाड़ी मार्ग के तौर पर बनवाया था।
long_description:
डेविड स्कॉट ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी राज के दौरान उत्तरपूर्व भारत आने पहले अंग्रेजी अधिकारियों में से एक थे। भारत में उनका कार्यकाल 30 साल तक चला जिस दौरान उनकी ज्यादातर गतिविधियाँ खासी पहाड़ियों के आसपास केंद्रित रहीं। डेविड स्कॉट ने पहाड़ियों और घने जंगलों के बीच से 100 किमी लम्बी एक बग्घी सड़क (Wagon Road) बनवायी जो असम को सिलहट (वर्तमान बांग्लादेश) से जोड़ती है। इस घोड़ागाड़ी सड़क का मावफलांग गाँव से लदमावफलांग गाँव का 16 किलोमीटर हिस्सा अब डेविड स्कॉट ट्रेल कहलाता है और हाइकर्स के बीच बहुत लोकप्रिय है। 
डेविड स्कॉट ट्रेल मावफलांग गांव से शुरू होकर पहाड़ियों, घाटियों, प्राचीन जंगलों, घास के मैदानों, पुलों, और तालाबों से होकर गुजरती है। साफ़ नीली उमियम नदी मार्ग के शुरुआती हिस्से में साथ साथ बहती है।
डेविड स्कॉट ट्रैक की शुरुआत में ही करीब 300 मीटर पर 'का कोर का शोरमाई' स्थान आता है, जिसका नाम एक ट्राइबल नेता की बेटी के नाम पर रखा गया है। आगे बढ़ने पर करीब एक किलोमीटर के बाद कैमिला मकबरा आता है जिसे 1843 में 7 साल की एक ब्रिटिश बच्ची की याद में बनाया गया था। करीब तीन किलोमीटर आगे चलकर उमियम नदी पर बना मशहूर हैंगिंग ब्रिज आता है। हाइकर्स यहाँ फोटोग्राफी करना पसंद करते हैं। हैंगिंग पुल से दो किलोमीटर आगे लैथसोमा नाम का खासी गांव आता है जहां एक अच्छा तालाब है। हाइकर्स आमतौर पर यहां अधिक समय तक रुकते हैं और लंच ब्रेक लेते हैं। यह मोटे तौर पर ट्रैक का मध्य बिंदु भी है। इसके बाद ट्रैक मार्ग फिर कुछ खासी बस्तियों से होकर गुजरता है और लगभग ढाई किलोमीटर के बाद एलीफैंट हिल और आर्च ब्रिज तक पहुंचता है। इसके बाद मार्ग करीब तीन किलोमीटर और जाने पर लदमावफलांग गाँव आता है जिसमें बहुत सारे विशाल शिला खंड (मोनोलिथ) हैं। यहाँ ट्रैक ख़त्म हो जाता है। पास में एक निकास बिंदु है जो हाइकर्स को सोहरा मुख्य सड़क से जोड़ता है जहां से बस पकड़कर शहर वापस जाया जा सकता है।

images.caption: मावफलांग गांव की लोकप्रिय डेविड स्कॉट ट्रेल के शुरूआती भाग के करीब बहती हुई उमियम नदी, मेघालय, भारत।
मावफलांग गाँव की डेविड स्कॉट ट्रेल से कुछ दूरी पर स्थित खासी हेरिटेज विलेज, मेघालय, भारत।

भारत के पूर्वोत्तर राज्य मेघालय में डेविड स्कॉट ट्रेल मार्ग पर एक झूला पुल।

title: Lakes Hike in Alpe d'Huez
short_description: Wonderful hike that takes us to no less than four mountain lakes near Alpe d'Huez.
long_description:
On this tour we hike through the magnificent mountain scenery near Huez. Since the starting point of our hike is at an altitude of 2,078m, we only have to climb about 150 metres, with the impressive view accompanying us throughout.
We start at the two mountain lakes Lac Noir and Lac Besson, which reflect the mountains in their wonderfully clear water and are already a highlight for all photographers among the hikers. The route continues to Lac Faucille and then to Lac Carrelet. Here we can take a break and enjoy some delicious French specialities.
On the way back we go right past the lakes. Finally, we go around Lac Noir and then return to our starting point.

images.caption: Lac Noir and Lac Besson in Alpe d' Huez

title: Back Basin Loop & Porcelain Basin in Norris Geysir Basin
short_description: A comprehensive circular tour route that includes the three circular routes in the Norris Geyser Springs Park that pass by most of the hot thermal springs and geysers in this springs park - one of the most impressive routes in Yellowstone National Park
long_description: One of the springs, the most beautiful and special routes that exist in Yellowstone National Park. This is a route that is mainly level and passes over a boardwalk built mostly from a network of wooden bridges that passes over more than 20 pools and hot thermal springs as well as geysers in a variety of shapes, colors and sizes. A simply beautiful and special itinerary! Those who have difficulty walking can of course only do their part and give up some of the circular routes, but it is recommended to do the three central circuits.

title: Over the Rottachberg to Martinszell
short_description: On this tour we get to know the Illertal from above. We experience small lakes, walk through pretty farming villages and take a look at the brewery village of Rettenberg. After a varied walk across meadows and through wooded areas, we reach the Vorderburg ruins shortly before the descent.
long_description:
The Humbacher Berg and the Rottachberg form the continuation of the Nagelfluhkette. Therefore, it is not surprising that one comes across Nagelfluh rock from time to time. However, separated by the Iller River, these hills are not assigned to the Nagelfluhkette.
Above the Egg farm, the remains of the Rauhlaubenberg ruin can be found hidden in the forest. It is very difficult to access through a narrow, barely visible forest path. The site has not been secured in any way, so you visit it at your own risk. The mighty west wall of the residential tower and a remnant of the circular wall have been preserved.
The Sacred Heart Cross stands between the district of Weiher and the main town of Rettenberg. From there you have a magnificent view over the upper Illertal. Similar views are then offered from the viewing pavilion on the Gebhardshöhe.
Before we descend into the Illertal at the end of the Rottachberg, we reach the ruins of Vorderburg Castle. This was once the site of Rettenberg Castle, a castle without a keep. It was built around 1100 and destroyed by fire in 1562.

title: Walking tour in the open air in Saint-Germain-sur-Ay
short_description: A beautiful circuit in the Manche department from the town of Saint-Germain-sur-Ay to discover the Regional Natural Park of the Cotentin and Bessin Marshes between the sea and the marshes.
long_description:
From the pretty village of Saint-Germain-sur-Ay, you quickly join the GR223 which runs along the coast of the Manche. The first steps on the path lead you to the village guardhouse. You walk along the Ouve and then the Ay to reach the Pointe du Banc (naturist beach). The view of the bay is exceptional, especially during high low tides.
We walk quietly along the path.
We advance quietly to the rhythm of the birds before joining the beaches on the other side of the point. It is here that we find the oyster beds a little further on. Oyster farming is one of the most important activities along with market gardening (leeks and carrots). At km 7.2, you can continue along the GR and take part of the outward journey or continue towards the seaside village by road.
.

title: The Paternkofel Crossing with the Three Peaks Circumnavigation
short_description: The Innerkofler De Luca Climb to the Paternkofel is the technical highlight of this tour, which offers breathtaking views of the Sesto Dolomites with the Three Peaks throughout the entire tour. The clearly visible traces from the First World War provide exciting insights into the dark chapter of the history of the Sesto Dolomites.
long_description:
The traverse of the Paternkofel from the south via the Paternsattel, the Paßportenscharte and on the descent from the Paternkofel via the Innerkofler De Luca-Steig offers fantastic views of the Sexten Dolomites with the Three Peaks as well as impressive remnants of the First World War. With the Auronzo Hut, the Lavaredo Hut and the Tre Cime di Lavaredo Hut, there are three places to stop directly on the trail. The route runs along artificial belts, in tunnels and caverns. Traces of the First World War can be found everywhere. The front between Italy and Austria ran right through the middle of this scenically stunning panorama of the Dolomites. On the descent from the Paternkofel via the Innerkofler De Luca trail, there is a tunnel about 600 m long. We strongly recommend that you bring a headlamp.
After the traverse, the tour can be extended by walking completely around the Three Peaks. If you leave early enough, you should not miss this magnificent panoramic tour. During the traverse of the Paternkofel, passages of difficulty level I (UIAA) have to be overcome. In places, the difficult walking terrain is extremely exposed. A head for heights is absolutely essential. In the early summer months, the tunnel can still be icy in places. The route is mainly exposed on the east side. The protection in the path itself is good.

images.caption: View from the summit of the Paternkofel to the north faces of the Drei Zinnen.
The Dreizinnenhütte seen from the south.
Panorama with Paternkofel and Drei Zinnen.
Approximate route of the Paternkofel traverse.

title: Foghorn
short_description: This tour takes us from the idyllic Hintersteiner Valley up to the heights of the Allgäu mountains with the famous Nebelhorn. We descend with the Nebelhorn cable car to Oberstdorf.
long_description: From the Giebelhaus in the Hintersteiner Tal (1060 m) we hike up to the Engeratsgundalpe (1156 m) and to the Laufbichlalpe (1200 m) and from there further over the Wengen Alps to the Edmund-Probst-Haus (1932 m, overnight accommodation of the DAV). Up to the Unteren Wengen Alpe (1288 m) we hike along a tarred alpine path, which then changes into a trail as we continue. There are numerous places to stop for refreshments along the way, as many of the alps are farmed. The Nebelhorn cable car takes us down to Oberstdorf. From here we reach our starting point by public transport.

title: A walk around the surroundings of the Gorki Leninskiye Museum-Reserve
short_description: Where and how the greatest man and visionary of the 20th century spent his short life can be found out and seen at his manor, now the Gorki Leninskie Museum.
long_description:
Lenin's estate survived and spent the entire tumultuous 20th century without a scratch. It is now a museum and nature reserve in one. The museum introduces visitors to history, holds exhibitions, celebrations and various festivals. Around the main museum complex there is a large park, in which you can walk and reminisce about a bygone era and dream up a new one at any time. And it is only 20 minutes from Moscow.
Come, visit, take interest in historical place where just recently the heart of the Union was beating, and as the director of the museum says: «Walk in Gorki!

title: मावफलांग डैम (उमियम झील) व्यू पॉइंट ट्रैक
short_description: मावफलांग डैम (उमियम झील) व्यू पॉइंट ट्रैक मे घालय के मावफलांग गांव से शुरू होकर पास की एक पहाड़ी तक जाता है जहाँ से उमियम नदी, मावफलांग डैम, और खासी पहाड़ियों के शानदार दृ श्य दिखते हैं।
long_description:
शिलांग से चेरापूंजी की तरफ जाने वाले रास्ते में 25 किलोमीटर की दूरी पर मावफलांग गांव पड़ता है जिसे एशिया के सबसे स्वच्छ गांव का खिताब दिया गया है। लेकिन स्वच्छता के अलावा जो चीज़ मावफलांग को लोकप्रिय बनाती है वो है इस क्षेत्र की प्राकृतिक सुंदरता। इस गांव में आपको सब कुछ देखने को मिलेगा जैसे की मावफलांग के  पवित्र वन, विश्व प्रसिद्ध डेविड स्कॉट ट्रेल, हरी-भरी खासी पहाड़ियाँ, ठंडे मीठे पानी वाली साफ नीली उमियम नदी, और  इस नदी को बांधकर बनाई गई एक विशाल उमियम झील।
मावफलांग गाँव में डेविड स्कॉट ट्रेल के अलावा मावफलांग डैम (उमियम झील) व्यू पॉइंट के लिए 3 किलोमीटर की एक छोटी ट्रेल भी है। मावफलांग डैम उमियम नदी पर बना है और इसके जलाशय को ही उमियम झील भी कहते हैं।
व्यू पॉइंट की पार्किंग से कुछ कदम नीचे उतरने के बाद उमियम झील को एक पहाड़ी के ऊपर से देखा जा सकता है। झील बहुत बड़ी है और दो कोनों में हरियाली से भरे खासी पहाड़ों से घिरी हुई है। नीचे नदी तक उतरना भी संभव है।
यह ट्रैक सभी हाइकर्स (शुरुआती और एक्सपर्ट) के लिए आसान और उपयुक्त है। यदि मावफलांग या शिलांग में ज्यादा समय तक रुकना का प्लान हो तो फिर खासी हेरिटेज विलेज का ट्रैक और विश्व प्रसिद्ध डेविड स्कॉट ट्रैक तो बेशक करने ही चाहिए।

images.caption: मावफलांग डैम व्यू पॉइंट के रास्ते से दिखता हुआ मावफलांग गांव और घाटी, मेघालय, भारत।
मावफलांग डैम व्यू पॉइंट से दिखता हुआ मावफलांग जलाशय और खासी पहाड़ियाँ, मेघालय, भारत।
मावफलांग गांव मेघालय राज्य राजमार्ग 5 के शिलांग-चेरापूंजी सड़क खंड पर स्थित है, मेघालय, भारत।

title: Pic de Paloumère via the Teches ridge
short_description: A superb hike that allows you to admire the Pyrenees chain from the front!
long_description:
I propose this route in a clockwise direction, in order to start with the most difficult part which goes up Cornud.
This first part in the woods is very pleasant but quite steep.
At the exit of the wood, a big part of the level is realised. We discover a magical panorama of the Pyrenees, from the Ariège to the Pic du Midi!
The next part goes from tuc to tuc on the grassy ridges, with always these magnificent panoramas (the Pyrenees on your left, the plain on your right).
At the Tuc de Haurades, you have the possibility to go back down directly to the car park by an easy forest path. Otherwise I recommend you to go to the Pic de Paloumère, in outward journey and return (or almost), to take advantage of beautiful views. It will take you an extra hour and 20 minutes and some 250m of climbing more.
It's a good way to get to the top.

long_description: At the beginning of our hike we mainly walk on paved paths and forest trails through easy terrain. Nevertheless, with a length of 20 km, this stage is one of the longest of the tour. We start at the small lake Bl vättnerna, which lies directly on the border between Västergötland and Halland. Our destination is the significantly larger lake Stensjön.

title: नैीताल में टिफ़िन टॉप ट्रैक
short_description: टिफ़िन टॉप एक सुंदर पर्वत चोटी और पिकनिक स्थल है जहां पर घुड़सवारी गतिविधियां होती हैं और जहाँ से नैनीताल शहर का पैनोरमिक दृश्य दिखाई देता है।
long_description:
टिफ़िन टॉप जिसे कभीकभी डॉरोथी सीट भी कहते हैं, एक हिलटॉप है जहाँ से नैनीताल शहर का विहंगम नज़ारा देखने को मिलता है। यह समुद्र तल से 2290 मीटर की ऊंचाई पर अयारपाटा नाम के इलाके में स्थित है।  नेचर फोटोग्राफर्स, हाइकर्स, और ट्रैकर्स के लिए यह एक उपयुक्त स्थान है। स्कूली छात्र, कॉलेज के प्रेमी जोड़े, और बच्चों वाले परिवार भी यहाँ अक्सर पिकनिक मानते दिखाई देते हैं। असल में इस जगह का नाम टिफिन टॉप पड़ा ही इसलिये क्योंकि लोग अपने टिफ़िन बॉक्स लेकर यहाँ पिकनिक मनाने आने लगे थे।   
इस पहाड़ी ट्रैक को 1 से 2 घंटे के भीतर पूरा किया जा सकता है। नैना देवी मंदिर से आने पर यह ट्रैक लगभग 5 किलोमीटर लम्बा है। यह आने के लिए नैनीताल शहर से होकर गुजरना पड़ता है। वैकल्पिक रूप से ट्रैक को कुमाऊं विश्वविद्यालय के पास से भी शुरू किया जा सकता है जहाँ से ट्रैक की कुल दूरी सिर्फ 4 किलोमीटर ही रहती है।

title: Bisse du Milieu - Bisse Vieux
short_description: The Bisse du Milieu and the Bisse Vieux lead through fir and larch woods, villages, meadows and irrigate raspberry and strawberry plantations.
long_description:
The «Bisse du Milieu» and the «Bisse Vieux» pass through spruce and larch forests, pass by chalets and pastures and irrigate the strawberry and raspberry fields.
At «Planchouet» and «Bleusy», take some time to admire their chapels dating back to the 1930's. There is the possibility to have a restaurant meal or snack along the way.
This walk is a comfortable hike linking both sides of the valley towards «Planchouet» and «Lavantier». A highly recommended walk for families.

Note(s)
DISCOVER NENDAZ, THE LAND OF THE «BISSES»

Scorched by the sun and often difficult to access, the valleys of the Valais are irrigated by «Bisses»- water channels - follow their course along fascinating paths. In Nendaz you'll find 8 «Bisses» and 6 still with water.
Dug into the ground, carved out of rock, or even attached to it, the scars of the Bisses are reminders of the constant battle against drought waged by the region's farmers. Today, gentle yet spectacular paths lead along these old water channels. The eight channels of Nendaz are particularly famous - for example, the high level walk along the Bisse de Chervé with views of the whole of the Rhone Valley, or the path to the enchanted idyll and waterfalls of the Bisse Vieux.

title: Bisse de Chervé - Barrage de Cleuson (Cleuson Dam)
short_description: Beautiful hike along the Bisse de Chervé - spectacular and without many metres of hike.
long_description:
A magnificent high altitude walk along a 'bisse' where you will feel like you are up in the clouds, spectacular and literally flat all the way. It is the highest of all the 8 canals in the commune of Nendaz. There is maybe no longer water flowing within its banks but it largely makes up for that with its sumptuous views of the dam and its turquoise water and the valley below. The Cleuson dam is a work of art in it own rights with its 87m in height and its 420m in width. The dam wall can be visited during the summer months.

short_description: Explore the «Vallée de la Printze» from Siviez üvia Planchouet to Saclentse. You will cross the village of Nendaz, hamlets and enter the forest the higher you go.

short_description: This scenic hike takes us from the Edmund-Probst-Haus via the Laufbacher Eck into the Bärgündeletal valley. Magnificent views in the middle of the nature reserve "Allgäuer Hochalpen" make this tour a unique experience.
long_description: This scenic tour starts at the Edmund-Probst-Haus (1927 m), which we reach with the Nebelhorn cable car. From there we head in the direction of Schochen, where magnificent views of the surrounding mountain landscape open up again and again. To the east of us is the Laufenbacher Eck. A narrow, very steep path leads us from the summit down to the Schönberghütte and on into the Bärgündeletal. There we finally reach our destination, the Giebelhaus. From there we take the bus back to the starting point.

title: Untersee - Swiss lower lake shore
long_description:
Experience the landscape along the Swiss shore of Untersee through the eyes of the painters Adolf Dietrich and Otto Meier!
Discover art and landscape along the Swiss shore of Untersee at the stations of the art route in Mammern and Berlingen. Let's look at the landscape through the frames set up here and compare our view with that of the artists.

Otto Meier was first a farmer and innkeeper at the Gasthof Adler in Mammern. After an accident in 1962 in which he lost a leg, he devoted himself to painting. From then on, he captured the Untersee landscape at all seasons in his oil paintings, which also express his intimate relationship with nature.

In Mammern, Switzerland, there are three stelae with paintings by the late artist in Ampelstrasse, Seehaldenstrasse (forest entrance) and at the Guldifuss Ost campsite, which we can look at during a leisurely tour of the village. If we want to see the original paintings, we should stop by the Gasthaus Adler on the main street and perhaps enjoy a Tröpfel right away - a non-alcoholic, sparkling one made from grapes and apples!
From Mammern we continue by boat or train to Berlingen, where the painter Adolf Dietrich, born in 1877 as the son of a small farmer, lived. Until the mid-twenties, he painted only at weekends and in the evenings. He earned his living as a machine knitter, forest and railway worker and with his smallholding. It was only with the first great sales successes - Dietrich was almost fifty years old at the time - that he was able to devote himself entirely to painting, which was shown not only in his home village but also in Berlin, Paris and New York. However, his home remained Berlingen until his death in 1957. Berlingen has dedicated three steles to this famous son. We find one directly at the ship's landing stage with the title: "Schiffsuntergang vor Berlingen"; the original can be seen in the Restaurant Schiff just behind us. In the Seestrasse, at the car park west of Berlingen, is the picture "View of Berlingen" and at the car park east of Berlingen another Dietrich stele with the title "Early Spring near Berlingen". The originals of the last two pictures hang in the Kartause Ittingen, the Thurgau Art Museum. On summer weekends we should definitely also plan a visit to the Adolf Dietrich House in Berlingen, where we can see, among other things, the authentic painting room and a documentary on the life and work of the painter. From Berlingen we can then return to Mammern by boat or train.

Note(s)
This route is one of four sections of the Untersee Art Route. Three others can be found on the island of Reichenau and in Allensbach, on the Höri peninsula and in Stein am Rhein.

A detailed brochure has been published on the Untersee Art Route, describing all 31 stations with the painters and pictures presented there. It is available at the local tourist information offices or from Tourismus Untersee e.V.

title: Through the high moor from Oberjoch to Unterjoch
short_description: This wonderful hike takes us through the interesting high moorland landscape between Oberjoch and Unterjoch.
long_description: This wonderful hike takes us through the interesting high moorland landscape between Oberjoch and Unterjoch. We also make a detour across the Austrian border to the riverbed of the Vils. Several places to stop for refreshments make this hike, which does not involve any major climbs, an enjoyable hike.

title: Sigiriya - Rock Fortress in Sri Lanka
short_description: The tour takes 1200 steps up to the ruins of the rock fortress on the monolith "Sigiriya" on Sri Lanka.
long_description:
After the first steps, we come to a small corridor via a steel staircase, where we can still see drawings from the times of the king.
After that, our path leads us past the mirrored wall. The wall was polished so much that it reflected the sunlight and illuminated the corridor.
After the mirror wall and more steps, we reach two lion paws. There used to be a complete lion's head here, through whose mouth one reached the last part of the ascent and the rock fortress. 
After a total of 1200 steps we have made it and reach the plateau on which the fortress was built. From here we have a very nice panoramic view from the lowlands to the foothills of the highlands of Sri Lanka.

title: Höhenflug von Hinterstoi über kleinen und großen Daumen zum Höfatsblick
short_description:
Eine ausgedehnte Trail Running Tour durch fast alle Vegatationszonen der Allgäuer Hochalpen. Von schmalen Wanderwegen bis technisch anspruchsvoller Kraxelei und Höhenflügen ist alles dabei.
Translate to English
long_description:
Die Trail Running Tour startet am Parkplatz Säge in Hinterstein und führt dich zum atemberaubenden Höfatsblick am Nebelhorn. Auf dem Weg passierst du zunächst den Gipfel der Rotspitz, von dem aus du einen fantastischen Ausblick auf die umliegenden Berge und Täler hast. Weiter geht es zur Heubatspitze, wo du die Weite des Allgäus unter dir liegen siehst.Der technische Anspruch der Strecke variiert von moderat bis anspruchsvoll, da einige Passagen steil und felsig sein können. Festes Schuhwerk und eine gute Kondition sind daher empfehlenswert. Vorbei am Kleinen Daumen erreichst du schließlich den Großen Daumen, von dem aus du einen unvergleichlichen Panoramablick auf die Allgäuer Alpen genießen kannst.Es wird empfohlen, ausreichend Wasser mitzunehmen, da es unterwegs keine Möglichkeit gibt, frisches Wasser aufzufüllen. Achte darauf, genügend Flüssigkeit dabei zu haben, um den Anforderungen des anspruchsvollen Trails gerecht zu werden. Genieße die Schönheit der Natur und die Herausforderung der Strecke auf dem Weg zum Höfatsblick am Nebelhorn.
Hinunter ins Tal gehts mit der Nebelhorn Bahn.

title: Höglandsleden - Stage 2 - From Ärnanäs to Eksjö
short_description: The second stage of our tour on the Höglandsleden leads from the campsite Ärnanäs around the lake Norra Vixen and further through the village Eksjö to the campsite.
long_description: Today's route takes us through the beautiful southern Swedish lakeland landscape to Eksjörn. The town has been the seat of the garrison since the 15th century, and the medieval old town is known for its unique wooden house architecture and is now almost entirely listed.

title: From Vorderweidenthal to Berwartstein Castle and Lindelbrunn Ruin
short_description: On this challenging tour we experience two castles, one preserved, the other destroyed.
long_description:
We start at the car park "Am Friedhof" in Vorderweidenthal and walk from here along the edge of the forest. We turn left into the road and walk up the steps at its end before turning right onto the driveway. After a right-hand bend, we walk along a path on the left and continue straight ahead at a crossroads. After the fork, keep to the right and walk above the road towards "Erlenbach". At the forest road we turn left and continue towards Erlenbach
and come to Berwartstein Castle.
We continue walking in the direction of "Lauterschwan" until we reach the Seehofweiher pond and at its end turn left and continue walking along the pond. We continue along the path until we reach Frauenwoog. We pass the pond on the right and after a while we reach the path to Lauterschwan.
We turn right into Brunnenweg and walk past the cemetery onto the forest path. At the next fork, we turn left in the direction of "Lindelbrunn".
Where there are forks, we follow the main path until we turn left towards "Bethof" at a fork. We turn left in the forest onto the road and then right again. At the next fork we reach a road. We now walk left along the "Schneckenpfad".
Cross the road and then turn left onto a footpath towards "Vorderweidenthal", which soon leads into a forest path. At the next fork, we walk left through the forest. We follow the path towards "Lindelbrunnn" until we reach the ruin.
We walk back down to Vorderweidenthal until we turn left into Rödelsteinstraße and talk back to our starting point.

images.caption: Berwartstein Castle - photographed from Little France.

title: Hiking route De Haan
short_description: This route is 21.5 kilometres long and takes about 5.5 hours. You'll enjoy walking through the dunes and along the beach.
long_description: De Haan is one of the better-known coastal towns in Belgiumë. You can enjoy hiking in the area. De Haan is a beautiful village, which is why it is also on the list of the most beautiful villages in Flanders. De Haan has only become famous since 1886. A railway line was built in 1886, making De Haan accessible.

title: Belgrade Forest Running Route, Istanbul
short_description: A different side of Istanbul, far from city life. An ideal 6km route for nature lovers, runners
long_description:
Belgrad Forest is undoubtedly an ideal area to get away from the city's gürültüsüsüsüsü and get out into nature for a while. Especially at the weekend, Belgrade Forest becomes an attractive spot for many outdoor enthusiasts. This nature and nature-friendly area, which is very suitable for travelling with family and friends, is almost a breathing point with its view and greenery. 
This 6km running route, which circles around the city and is very popular with Istanbulites, is definitely worth a try! Whether for your daily jogs, to get away from the crowds of the city after work, or to see a different side of the city when you come to Istanbul... This route is waiting for you to get in touch with fresh air, mingle with nature and find peace. 
Don't wait any longer to try this beautiful route in winter and summer! Like other outdoor enthusiasts, try this route now and enjoy the nature!

title: Heubacher Haubentour near Motten
short_description: A longer and scenic hike through the wonderful forests around Heubach and to the lookout tower of the Große Haube awaits us.
long_description: From the Frauenstein hikers' car park, we hike uphill, following the "red H on a white background" marking and the path to Frauenstein. The "red H" accompanies us throughout the Haubentour. The cube-shaped Frauenstein (1) on a hilltop crowns a prehistoric burial site. The top of the dolomite block is shaped like a basin and, according to tradition, served as a baptismal font for St. Kilian during his missionary work in Franconia. Behind the stone, we keep to the right and turn right again onto the forest path. We pass the mountain station of a ski lift - with a beautiful view of the northern Rhön. Soon a wonderful meadow path leads between fields, the "Breiten First" (2), until we reach the road at Sparhöfe. We do not hike into the village, but, with a wonderful distant view, uphill to the left. After 150 m, we turn right onto the forest path. The path leads up and down through high spruce and beech forest. We pass a large clearing. Afterwards, the path leads in a large curve out into the fields. In front of us we can see the houses of Heubach. But we turn right and pass an old oak tree, under which a bench invites us to take a rest. The path continues uphill towards a transmission mast. The gravel path bends to the right, then to the left and crosses the road to the Steiger car park. There we find a shelter. Choosing the forks to the right, we pass the crest with the transmission mast and continue walking uphill. In a left-hand bend there is another bench (3) with a view over the hilly landscape to Heubach. Then walk briefly along the edge of the forest and turn right into the forest. Turn right above the motorway and walk downhill to a bridge. Here we cross the motorway and continue straight ahead until the forest path makes a tight left turn. Here we turn right onto the grassy path that runs through a clearing and between larks, pines and firs. In summer, the poisonous but beautiful foxglove blooms here. Now a soft, narrow path runs through young forest. The romantic path runs along the old border between the Kingdom of Bavaria and Prussia, today's state border between Bavaria and Hesse. We find the Nassau lion on the old boundary stones (4) from 1729. If we follow this border straight on over the Kleine Haube, we reach the observation tower of the Große Haube (5) after a steeper climb. The new tower from 2005 is built of steel and wood. From its 23.8 m height and the eleven intermediate platforms, you can look out over the Rhön as far as the Taunus and Spessart. A shelter is built into the tower, but there is also a seating area for a rest. Finally, we follow the border for a short distance until a forest path leads us steeply downhill to the left. We come across a forest path, which we follow until we reach a crossroads with an old oak tree, the Jägereiche (6), with a seating area. Turn left and walk through the forest until you reach a road after about 2 km. Here we go downhill to the right, past a refuge and to a motorway subway. On the other side, we walk to the right, parallel to the motorway, until the "red H" shows us the way to the left across the fields. It goes downhill, we cross the stream "Schmidtwasser" and get past fruit trees to the Fuldaer Straße. The shortest way back to the car park would be to turn left on the road through Heubach. However, we prefer the path that branches off to the right again after 100 m and leads us to the edge of the forest. We pass a cosy, covered resting place for hikers. The hike continues across the fields, past the sports field, and towards the elevation of the Frauenstein. The last stretch of road leads up to the barbecue area and the Frauenstein car park.

images.caption: This path leads up to the Great Hood.
An enchanted forest path runs along the Hessian-Bavarian border.
The panoramic view from the lookout tower of the Great Hood.

title: Hotzenwald Transverse Route
short_description: This hiking trail leads us into the first south of the Black Forest. We experience the transition from the open hilly landscape of the Dinkelberg to the Hotzenwald and come close to the 1,000 m altitude limit at Hornberg.
long_description:
Stage 1: Schopfheim - Herrischried (23 km)
After a tour of Schopfheim, where we explore the Weinbrenner-style town hall, the Old Town Church of St. Michael and the Wiesenbrücke, we follow the trail markings out of town. Through the formerly independent village of Eichen we reach the Eichener See lake. To see this lake, which is up to three metres deep, is not a matter of course, because due to the lumpy limestone soil it only appears after rainfall and disappears during dry periods. The trail then leads through a small forest and then through fields and meadows to Hasel. Here we can visit the Erdmannshöhle, a stalactite cave, the Jostmühle and a shrink hole at the Schammerbach. Now the trail winds along winding paths towards the Hotzenwald mountains - from now on it is important to pay particular attention to the trail markings, as we leave the main trail several times! Passing the Wehratal dam, we start the challenging ascent to the Häuelkopf. Afterwards we descend steeply into a valley and then immediately climb up again to the Hornberg. We are rewarded with a great view and a place to stop for a bite to eat. We leave the reservoir of the Hotzenwald power station, the Ödlandkapelle and two ski lifts behind us and have already reached the first districts of the village of Herrischried.
Stage 2: Herrischried - Waldeshut (23 km)
We start freshly refreshed in Herrischried and hike up the Gugel behind the village of Giersbach. From Engelschwand we head south through a small forest and past Strittmatt. In Görwihl, a small museum invites you to take a tour of the history of the Hotzenwald. After crossing the striking Alb valley, we hike past Unteralpfen. The landscape thins out, fields and orchards line the path from now on, which leads us through Eschbach to Waldshut, the destination of our tour.

title: बुधेर गुफा-मोइला टॉप बुग्याल ट्रैक, उत्तराखंड, भारत
short_description: उत्तराखंड के सुन्दर पहाड़ी शहर चकराता में स्थित मोइला बुग्याल एक हरिया ली के स्वर्ग के सामान है। इतना ही नहीं इसके करीब पायी जाने वाली महाभारत काल की बु धेर गुफा भी देखने योग्य है।
long_description: चकराता के सुरम्य हिल स्टेशन पर आने वाले पर्यटकों के लिए बुधेर गुफा और मोइला टॉप बुग्याल दो लोकप्रिय गंतव्य हैं। महाभारत काल की यह रहस्यमय पौराणिक बुधेर गुफा और हरियाला वाला स्वर्ग मोइला बुग्याल एक दुसरे के आसपास स्थित हैं। चकराता शहर से इन दोनों स्थानों तक एक सुन्दर ट्रेल मार्ग से 3 घंटे में पहुँचा जो सकता है। इलाके में रुकने होटल के लिए कुछ होटल हैं और आपको प्रकृति का आनंद लेना है तो आप शिविर स्थान में टेंट/तंबू भी लगा सकते हैं। कुछ स्थानीय टूर ऑपरेटर यहाँ समूह में यात्रा भी आयोजित करवाते हैं। इलाके की बात करें तो यह स्वास्थवर्धक, सुंदर और बहुत फ्रेंडली है। हिमालय की पर्वत श्रृंखला दिखती है और साथ में बहुत अन्य गंतव्य जैसे की टाइगर फॉल, लाखामंडल मंदिर, महासू देवता मंदिर, कनासर देवदार जंगल भी हैं जिन्हे यहाँ बाद ज़रूर देखना चाहिए।

मोइला टॉप ट्रैक पर स्थित बुधेर वन विश्रामगृह उत्तराखंड, भारत।
