title: Snowshoe: Herzogstand above Lake Walchen
short_description: The Herzogstand is a popular touring destination due to its fantastic view of Lake Walchen.
long_description: This easy snowshoe tour takes us to an excellent panoramic mountain above Lake Walchen. As soon as we have reached the summit of the Herzogstand with its pavilion on only gently sloping to moderately steep slopes facing south to south-east, we are offered a magnificent view of the Karwendel and the Alpine foothills. With the Herzogstandhaus, we also have an almost year-round catered refreshment stop (closing time from around mid-November to Christmas), which allows us to pack our backpacks a little lighter, because we can have our snack there. Orientation is mostly easy, as a large part of the ascent is on the edge of the ski slopes.

title: A panoramic view of the Alps and the Alpine lakes from the town of Immanstadt
short_description: A hiking trail starting from the town of Immenstadt in the Allgäu region of southern Germany offers two amazing view points, one on the Alps and the other on the town's large lakes, Grosser & Kleiner Alpsee. You can extend the route and go down to the large Alfaza lake and from there through the small Alfaza lake to return to the starting point.
long_description: A hiking route with panoramic viewpoints starting from the alpine town of Immanstadt in the Allgäu region. The total length of the circular route is about 6 kilometers, but it can actually be done in a linear way and you can only visit some of the points, when the first view point overlooking the Alps is only 500 meters away from the parking lot, which means an average walking time of about 15 minutes on a moderate incline. The second view point is about a ten minute walk from the first point and overlooks the town's two large lakes: Groser Alfaza (translated into Hebrew: the large lake of the Alps) and Kleiner Alfaza (translated into Hebrew: the small lake of the Alps). From the second lookout, you can return the same way back to the car or extend the route and go down towards Grocer Alfaza lake and then go back the same way or make the road circular and pass the Kleiner Alfaza lake and from there through the town to return to the starting point.

images.caption: The view of the Alps from the first observation point in winter
Fischerman's houses at lake Großer Alpsee
The Kleiner Alpsee and the outdoor pool

title: To the lller breakthrough
short_description: This circular tour is a family-friendly half-day hike that leads along both sides of the Illerschleifen, includes a suspension bridge and castle ruins.
long_description: This hike is suitable for families and can be walked all year round. It leads through beautiful riverside deciduous forests always along the Iller, which winds through the landscape in an impressive way. A suspension bridge, Nagelfluh rock formations and a ruined castle complete the experience. The hike is particularly beautiful in spring, when the beech trees bear their first leaves.

title: Hike up the Touchal
short_description: This hike on the Touchal is particularly suitable for those who don't feel like sleeping at the weekend.
long_description:
We hike below the cable car from Touchal, always uphill.
Up to the first station we pass many shops and restaurants, then we climb up the sunny hillside to the 5th station of the cable car. As we ascend and descend, we have an excellent view of the north of Tehran.

images.caption: View of the Touchal from Tehran

title: Around the Forest Cemetery Heidenheim
short_description: The route goes slightly up and down around the forest cemetery.
long_description: From Friedrich-Degeler-Platz we walk westwards into Hauptstraße, then up to SCHLOSS ARKADEN. We follow Olgastraße to the left for a short distance until we reach the crossroads, turn right there into Schnaitheimer Straße and after 30 m turn left into the path "Am Ottilienberg". At a slight bend, we climb a few steps on the right to the viewing platform of the Ottilienberg. After the detour, we follow the path further upwards, cross the Felsen-/Zeppelinstraße junction and turn right into the Panoramaweg. After about 500 m, we go up the steps on the left and reach the small road to the Waldorf School via a footpath. Follow this road down the hill and turn left onto the footpath at the bottom (hiking sign). Walk up the slope to the Naturfreundehaus on the right, where you can stop for a break. There we briefly turn left, then walk right into the forest and walk around the forest cemetery on the gravel path. We return to the town centre via Bergstraße.

title: Schalksbachtour - Herbstein
short_description:
The tour leads into the nearby nature reserve.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description: The 7.5 km long tour takes us from the Hensler farm guesthouse via the nearby sports field through field, forest and nature reserve. We will cross the Eichholz Gewüsser and walk a while later through a small sea of rocks before we reach the Schalksbachteiche in the nature reserve. On this partly volcanic ring path there are two shelters that invite you to take a rest. Of course we can also stop at the Vulkantherme on the way and enjoy a break with coffee and cake or a snack. Afterwards we walk through the spa gardens back home or to the starting point, the Pension Hensler.

images.caption: Park at the Vulkantherme in Herbstein

title: Hiking route Flemish nature reserve Houterenberg
short_description: This walking route is just under 10 kilometres long. The route takes about 2.5 hours. Because this route is not super long, this tour is perfect when you want to do another small round of walking.
long_description: Houterberg is a beautiful nature reserve belonging to the Kempen region. The area consists of beautiful forests and many pieces of heathland. You will also find fens. Many woodpeckers live in the area so prick up your ears. Many deer also live in the area. Due to the heathland it can be a bit muddy if it has rained a lot.

title: From Ehingen through the Danube floodplains - Natour 3
short_description: This medium tour in the south of Ehingen takes us through the Danube floodplains and into the historic centre of the city.
long_description: From the car park at the stadium, we walk past the floodlight mast to the Danube cycle path. On the left to the Schillerlinde lime tree, a wide view of the Danube valley and the Swabian Oberland opens up. Turn right in front of the kindergarten and follow the "Kapellenstraße" downhill. After number 39, take a sharp right past the old water of the Danube through the Danube meadows. At a sharp bend to the right, turn left and follow a meadow path to the right over a wooden footbridge to the mouth of the Schmiech. We follow the Danube upwards, first crossing under the Danube bridge to Berg and arriving at the bridge to Dettingen. There we turn right, cross the railway line and the "Rottenackerstraße" and go straight up to the "Hundsfeld". From the wayside cross from 1869 we have a good view of Ehingen (Wolfertturm - Liebfrauenkirche). At the bottom on the right is the SAPPI paper factory (the oldest large industrial plant in the town). In the right-hand bend, where the path descends to the railway subway, we turn left and follow the newly built agricultural road up to a tarred road. We walk uphill to the left of the forged field cross, past industrial enterprises. At the end of the road we turn right and right again down the "Schwarze Gasse" to the traffic lights. Continue straight ahead through the forecourt of the St. Franziskus residential park, through the subway under the "Spitalstraße" to the tower of the Liebfrauenkirche. Walk left along the church downhill to the zebra crossing. Over the bridge, along the little Schmiech river, we come to the museum of the town of Ehingen (Heilig-Geist-Spital, 1340). We walk past the building complex on the left and along the "Hauptstraße" to the market square. On the right we see the "Schlössle" from 1688 and the market fountain, on the left the district court in the "Ständehaus" from 1750. From there we walk left along the town hall and the red information pillar, straight ahead over the pedestrian crossing, right past the "Lindenhalle", up and right past the metal pavilion to the end of the car park. There we take the footpath to "Schillerstraße" and uphill via "Winckelhoferstraße" to "Wolfertweg". Walk left up to the Wolfert Tower (Kaiser-Wilhelm- und Aussichtsturm, 1891), along a children's playground via "Müllerstraße" straight ahead. At the end of the sports field, turn left diagonally across the "Volksplatz" and return directly to the starting point.

images.caption: The Wolfert Tower from 1891 towers over Ehingen.

title: To the Heiligenberg - Heidelberg
short_description: On this moderately difficult tour, we walk along the Philosophenweg to the Heiligenberg and the Thingstätte.
long_description:
We start our walk at Bismarckplatz and walk in the direction of Neunheim over the Thodor-Heuss-Brücke bridge to the right into Brückenkopfstraße and then left into Bergstraße. We continue into Philosophenweg. We follow this path until we reach the Hölderlinanlage. At the Odenwälder Hütte we follow the path in the direction of Mausbach and at the next fork we choose the left path uphill through the forest. Past the Webersbrunnen we soon come to Moltkehütte. At follow the path in the direction of Mausbach/Weißer Stein past the Mausbach meadow and the Mausbach fountain.
We continue to the Mausbach spring and follow the forest path until we turn right into the upper Mausbach path. At the next junction we turn right. At the road spider at Stickelsplatz, we turn left into the path towards "Zollstock/Heiligenberg". When we reach the Heiligenberg, we visit the St. Michael's Basilica.
We continue walking past the monastery to the Thingstätte. There is an opportunity to stop at the Waldschenke inn. Opposite this inn, the foundation walls of the Stepahn Monastery still stand. From the Heiligenbert tower, which can be climbed, we have a fantastic panorama over Heidelberg.
We continue along the road until we reach a forest road, into which we turn left. We follow the path in the direction of the Bismarck Column. From the column, we walk along the path to the right and immediately left down a narrow path. Through the Eichendorffanlage we get back to the Philosophenweg. At the end of the Philosophenweg, we take the same path as at the beginning and return to Bismarckplatz.

images.caption: Ausblick auf den Heiligenberg bei Heidelberg

title: From Levanto to Bonassola north of Cinque Terre
short_description: This hike from Levanto to Bonassola connects the two Ligurian coastal towns. The views of the nearby sea are magnificent, and in Bonassola you have a wonderful swim in the crystal-clear water.
long_description: This short hike takes us from Levanto north of the Cinque Terre along small roads to Bonassola. In Bonassola there is a wonderful beach where the crystal-clear water invites you to swim. There are numerous places to stop for refreshments in both towns. In Levanto, the market hall is an excellent place to stock up on local produce for a beach picnic.

images.caption: Levanto north of the Cinque Terre.
Arishokes at the market in Levanto.
View of Levanto and the first part of the trail to Bonassola.

title: European watershed
short_description: The European watershed hiking trail is a Qualitätsweg Wanderbares Deutschland certified by the German Hiking Association.

title: Höglandsleden - Stage 3 - From Eksjö to Klinten
short_description: The third stage of our tour on the Höglandsleden leads from the campsite Eksjö through an extensive forest landscape to the campsite Klinten by the lake Forsjön.
long_description:
The trail runs far away from civilisation on this section. Mainly on forest paths, we walk along the markings first to the south, then to the east. On the way we repeatedly pass through moor landscapes, here the path then leads ührt over wooden planks. Our stage destination is Forsjön, a natural bathing and fishing lake.
At the two huts that you reach first, you can use the fireplaces that are available. About 50 m further on, there is another hut that is lockable and also has good access to the water. It is therefore more suitable for overnight stays.

title: The Vía de Plata by bike - Spain
short_description: The Vía de la Plata (Silver Route) is an alternative or secondary route of the Santiago de Compostela pilgrimage linking Seville in Andalusia to Gijon on the Asturias coast;
long_description:
The Vía de la Plata crosses western Spain, from south to north, from Seville, and passes through 4 regions (Andalusia, Extremadura, Castilla y Leon, Asturias) and 7 provinces, for about 800km. The route follows an ancient Roman road, built to facilitate the gold trade.
The State and the European Union
The Spanish State and local authorities have enhanced this route by making it accessible for cycle tourism and mountain biking, to our great delight.

title: From Niederstetten to the fortified church and Celtic redoubt
short_description: This extensive hike takes us through a gentle hilly landscape to the fortified church in Wildentierbach and to a Celtic square enclosure. The natural bathing lake in Rinderfeld invites you to swim.
long_description: We start at the festival hall in Oberstetter Straße and follow it in a southerly direction out of the village. Behind the last houses, we turn left into Heftensteige, turn right and immediately right again and walk along the slope parallel to Oberstetter Straße into the village of the same name. We leave Oberstetten on the Reutalweg and follow the idyllic Reutalbach stream past the Reutalmühle mill to Wildentierbach. Here we can visit a village detention cell from the 19th century in the gate tower of the fortified church. We hike north along the "Wildentierbach" road and shortly after Dunzendorf reach the natural bathing lake in Rinderfeld - a good opportunity for a refreshing swim in fine weather. At the nearby country road to Rinderfeld, we turn briefly left and then hike immediately right into a wooded area. After a short stretch across fields, we enter a second piece of woodland where there is a Celtic square enclosure. The Celtic redoubt, which is over 2000 years old, is one of 70 such ramparts in Baden-Württemberg and probably served as a sacrificial site. We pass a third wood on the right and return to Niederstetten and our starting point at the festival hall via the Rehhof and the Rehhofsteige.

title: Viewing tour up to the Wart Tower - Weikersheim
Erbisberg/Sternwarte circular hiking trail Heidenheim
short_description: Several vantage points with great views await us on this longer hike.
long_description:
From Friedrich-Degeler-Platz, our path leads along Helmut-Bornefeld-Straße past the Pauluskirche, a
neo-Gothic building with a 75-metre-high tower.
neo-Gothic building with a 75-metre-high tower, left into the street "Am Wedelgraben" to St. Pöltener Straße. Here we turn left, go straight on and after the subway turn right into Alte Ulmer Straße. Continue left into Mörikestraße and then right into Theodor-Schäfer-Straße. From there we turn right into Steinstraße and then turn left along Giengener Straße. In front of the Netto supermarket, Erzknappenweg turns off to the right. Follow this until you reach steps after 300 m, which take you to Sonnenrainweg. There we turn left and follow the path marked with a rhombus for 2 km. Here we turn sharply left onto a footpath to the Ötterlesbrunnen. The Ötterlesbrunnen is a spring outlet above the karst water table, whose name refers to an "Etter", a marker boundary.
After this detour, we go back again, following the Albvereinsweg path straight ahead for 200 m through the forest. Via a gravel path on the right, we come along the quarry fence to the viewing platform above the quarry. From there we can see a bizarre group of rocks. Here, marl rock consisting of clay and lime was extracted from pits or mine shafts. After 300 m, the observatory is on the right. It was inaugurated in September 2006 and is the first and so far the only one in the district. Information is available at: www.astronomie-heidenheim.de. Continue downhill and turn left before the houses to the Kinderfestplatz. At the TV transfer station, a footpath leads about 300 m to a viewing rock at the Hohlenstein. We walk back to the observatory and continue along the path until we reach the road "Oberer Erbisberg", where we turn left, walk to the Naturfreundehaus and cross the playground. Approx. 400 m up the hill, a footpath leads to the viewing rock on the Rappeshalde. Presumably wine was once grown here, "Rappes" indicates artificial wine made from marc. Back at the Naturfreundehaus, we hike along the Erzknappenweg to the Netto shopping centre and turn left there into the path "Am Baderhölzle". From there we continue to Hölderlinstraße, past the Waldkirche, down steps to the right into Eisenbergstraße until we reach Giengener Straße. We use the pedestrian subway on the left and return to the starting point via St. Pöltener Straße.

title: From Waldmünchen via the Cerchovsteig trail
short_description: We hike from Waldmünchen to the Cerchov. It is important not to forget your passport for this cross-border tour!
long_description: From the information board at the car park, we follow the signs for hiking trail "W 9" and its white-red-white markings uphill along Kramberger Weg. It soon leads us to the right into the Waffenschleifweg towards the sanatorium. At the first crossroads in the forest, we keep straight on and now hike very nicely through the dense forest. We cross a forest path and continue to walk half-right. When the path joins another one, we turn right. Now follows a wild-looking passage with large boulders at the edge of the path. For a short distance, we share the path with the educational trail on the history of settlement. On the clay pit path we reach the German-Czech border. At the border crossing, a covered rest area invites us to take a break. In winter, there is also an extensive cross-border network of cross-country ski trails here. From the border we first follow the white sign with the yellow direction symbol straight ahead in the direction of Odb. na Cerchov. The marking for the now following trail section consists of white-yellow-white bars. We soon pass a forest road. Shortly afterwards, we follow the markings to the left onto a short section of path. At the ruins of an old forest hut we come across a path, which we follow to the left. Cool, tasty water gushes from a spring at the ruin. From here we follow a new marking of white-green-white bars in the direction of Cerchov. The very beautiful forest path leads to a forest path, which we follow to the right. Shortly afterwards, we reach a T-junction and turn left. Soon after, the white-green-white marking leads us to the left onto a narrower forest path. From here, follow the markings to the right onto a path. There follows a short passage where we have to climb a few metres over a rock. If you want to save yourself this effort, you can skip the last turn. The path leads to a concrete slab path, which we follow to the right. Soon we reach the summit plateau of Cerchov. Dilapidated barracks bear witness to the former military use of this terrain. The high peaks near the border were used as listening posts on both sides of the Iron Curtain before the fall of the Wall. The lookout tower on Cerchov has existed since 1905, but for most of that time it did not serve its intended purpose, but was soon used by the German army of occupation and later by the Czechoslovak military. The small entrance fee is used to maintain the tower. From the top we enjoy a magnificent view in all directions. We can see especially far into the Bohemian plain. At the foot of the tower, a beautifully designed rest area invites us to take a break. We can stop at the Caffe Mila bistro. Monday is a day of rest. The actual summit of Cerchov, the highest mountain in the Upper Palatinate Forest, is easy to miss. It lies to the west of the lookout tower and is marked by a red and white pole. After our stay on the summit plateau, we hike back to Waldmünchen the way we came. Not far from the starting point, we can visit the Grenzland and Trenck Museum in the historic Schergenhaus. The exhibits, spread over three floors, vividly portray the town's history. One of the main themes is "Trenck the Pandur" who besieged Waldmünchen in the service of Empress Maria Theresa during the War of the Austrian Succession. This siege is also commemorated every year by the historic Trenck Festival in Waldmünchen. The other main topic, the location of the town of Waldmünchen on the national border, is more closely related to our hike.

title: Family Trail - Catch a view over Peja
short_description: The path leads directly from the city centre into the nature around Peja. Here you can find an easy path with beatiful nature and a nice view on the top on Peja.
long_description: You can easily start your way out of the city centre and into nature. Many residents of Peja use this path to stretch their legs after a day's work. The path is well signposted and gives you a first impression of the incredibly beautiful nature of Kosovo. On the way you pass a few restaurants with traditional food from the region.

.
Important: Walk on the signposted snowshoe trails at your own risk. Please pay attention to the current avalanche situation and game rest zones
.
long_description: This snowshoe route from Realp to the Hotel Tiefenbach offers a lot of variety in terms of distant views. Although the way home is the same route as the way up, it doesn't bother you because you have two different worlds in front of you. The ascent is advantageously made on the marked Furka pass road. On the descent, the one or other shortcut in the powder snow can bring a lot of fun and variety.

title: To the summit cross on the Eisenberg - Schlitz
short_description:
A tour of medium difficulty that takes us up the Eisenberg.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description:
After our starting point, the holiday farm Trier, we cross the main road to Bad Salzschlirf and walk through the new district to the Mittleren Weg (upper tarred field path). Here we walk to the left in the direction of Karlshof. Shortly before the high ropes course, we have a beautiful view of the Schlitz valley and the town of Schlitz to the rear. After a short hike past the high ropes course, we reach the Karlshof, a former estate of the Counts of Schlitz. At Karlshof we turn right at the traffic sign "End of the three-km zone" until we reach the next turn-off to the left. Continue straight on this road, past the composting plant, until you reach the junction with the road to Lauterbach. After crossing the road, turn left and walk past the bus stop to the junction with the next road. From here the trail E1 begins. On this path we pass the forester's lodge Eisenberg and shortly afterwards the former house Bambey. We then walk along the Ruhrwiesenbach valley to a fork, where we turn right onto the path marked E1. This path leads us directly to the Eisenberger Haus.
The house popularly known as the Eisenberger Häuschen“ was a hunting lodge of the counts of Schlitz. Kaiser Willhelm II spent a few days in this hunting lodge on his visits to the grand family for capercaillie hunting. Unfortunately, the house can only be visited from the outside. Even from the terrace you have a wonderful view of Schlitz and the Rhön in good weather.
After a short rest, we continue on an unmarked path that branches off from the E1/E2 hiking trail behind the house and goes uphill. On this path we walk approx. 200-250m to a fork of a forest path to the left,
which leads to the summit of the Eisenberg. If we are lucky, hikers have already walked along this path, if not, it means tramping along the path through the plants. After a not too long climb, we have reached our destination. From up here you have a fantastic view of the Vogelsberg, the Rhön, the Thüringer Wald and some places in the surrounding area.
After we have fortified ourselves from our rucksacks, enjoyed the view and signed the summit book, we will set off on the Rück trail. We now hike along the E1 at the
Eisenberger Häuschen valley. At the next junction we turn right on the E2 straight towards Schlitz.
From the Quebst we have a wonderful view of the old town. Pass the water reservoirs, turn right at the barbecue area and pass two farms to reach the country road to Lauterbach. Turn left towards Schlitz. Pass the town sign, cross the road and walk between two houses along Karlshofer Weg to Karshof and from there back to Ferienhof Trier.

images.caption: The route climbs gently up to the Eisenberg.

title: For body, mind and soul near Passau
short_description: Whether farmhouse food, fantastic views or a detour to the Bible garden - this hike is a treat for body, mind and soul.
long_description: We start our hike at the church in Jägerwirth and from here follow the white-green signpost "10" to the through road. We turn right into this road. Shortly after the turnoff to Fürstenzell, we then continue to the right on a gravel path. Soon we reach Haunreut. There we keep sharp right in the direction of "Haunreut 10". From here we walk past numerous apple trees on a meadow path and finally come across a wider field path again. We turn right onto this and reach an asphalt road again shortly before the Sieberhof. We keep to the left, again following the white-green marking "10", and hike up to Rehschaln. Immediately after entering the village, we turn right onto a gravel path. Follow this to the fork in the road and then continue uphill to the left. A little later you will reach the main road, cross it and continue on the other side to the left on the footpath to the granite church of Rehschaln (1). Behind this church, we then turn right towards Irsham, again following the white-green markings. We hike down to Oberirsham and turn sharp left onto a field path. Cross the Gurlarner Bach stream and shortly afterwards you will come to an asphalted road again at Untereichet. Turn left there and climb up to Langdobl. Here we have the opportunity to replenish our provisions with farm produce at the Haindlhof cheese dairy (2). Our path then continues uphill to the through road. We turn left onto this and hike straight ahead to Gföhret. From here we can now enjoy the view down to Fürstenzell, but also into the Danube valley and up to the mountains of the Bavarian Forest. Shortly after leaving the village, we turn right onto a grassy forest path. This leads us up to the "Platte" (3) in Altenmarkt - the highest point of our tour. Here we can not only enjoy the impressive view again, but also fortify ourselves at the "Zur Platte" inn. Finally, we follow the asphalt road first downhill to the left, but then turn right onto a meadow path, again following the white-green markings "10" and now also "14". Our path leads us through the forest for a bit until we come across a wider forest path again, which we turn left onto. After a few metres we reach a small rest area on the through road. Here we continue a few steps to the left and then cross the road. We walk straight ahead into the forest again, following the green and white signposting "14" in the direction of Heiligenbrunn. After about 300 m, we turn left onto a forest path overgrown with gnarled tree roots. Finally, we reach another crossroads at the so-called Jägersteig and turn left here. At the asphalt road, we keep to the right, cross the Laufenbach stream and then continue to the right on the forest path. At the first fork, we leave the route with the green and white marking "14" and choose the path to the right until we reach a clearing. There we walk to the left along the edge of the forest until we reach the pilgrimage chapel Heiligenbrunn (4). At the crossroads near the car park, keep to the left. Our path now leads us straight ahead through the forest. Finally, at a wide fork in the road, we again follow the white-green marking "10" and thus turn right. Via Obereichet we reach the through road in Jägerwirth. We cross this and walk the few metres back to our starting point at the church. Finally, we have the opportunity to take a short detour into the Bible Garden.

images.caption: The mountains of the Bavarian Forest and the Danube Valley.
View of the granite church Rehschaln.

title: PostBus ride to the Witzweg
long_description:
Heiden, the starting point of the hike, is easily reached by post bus. - From St.Gallen you can choose between two different routes.
On the double-decker postbus via Eggersriet-Grub AR, you are offered an impressive view of the Alpstein mountains and, in good visibility conditions, a wonderful view of Lake Constance. This first-class panorama can be particularly enjoyed from the top floor of the double-decker postbus. The journey takes 34 minutes.
The St.Gallen-Rehetobel-Heiden route is served by conventional 41-seater postbuses. The approximately 40-minute journey takes you on a winding route through the hilly landscape of the Appenzeller Vorderland. Sit back, look out of the Postbus and take in the impressive images of Appenzell-ausserrhodian villages and the Alpstein mountain range - unique and original !

The Biedermeier village of Heiden captivates with its fabulous location as a terrace above Lake Constance. The joke trail starts at the village square in Heiden with the "listig-träfen" Appenzeller jokes that accompany you on the way via Wolfhalden to Walzenhausen. Children's jokes placed at eye level motivate the little ones to hike along. The path is unsuitable for prams.

The post bus regularly connects the villages along the way and offers the ideal return or lift if you don't want to walk the whole way.

From Walzenhausen you also have the option of travelling by train to Rheineck and back to St.Gallen via Rorschach, or you can change in Rheineck to the boat to Rorschach and complete your journey with another comfortable ride on the Postbus to St.Gallen. The Rorschach St.Gallen route is also partly served by double-decker Postbuses.

Note(s)
- The starting point for the opposite direction of the Witzweg is Walzenhausen station.
- With the OSTWIND day ticket you can enjoy a cheap day trip.
- A tour of the village of Heiden with ascent to the church tower (open from May to September from
13.00-15.30) is worthwhile.

images.caption: In the double decker near Grub

title: From Hinterstein over the Rauhhorn to the Schrecksee lake
short_description: A tour of contrasting names: The Rauhhorn lives up to its name, because its summit area is exposed and rugged and, compared to other mountains in the Allgäu, is therefore not often climbed. In contrast, we pass by the picturesquely situated and therefore much-visited Schrecksee, which bears this name at the very least because of its temperature.
long_description:
A first highlight of this tour should be the Willersalpe at 1456 m, which is only served by transport horses due to the lack of a road. Afterwards, the Vordere Schafwanne offers a first view of the mountains in the immediate vicinity: Bschießer (2000 m), Ponten (2045 m), Gaishorn (2249 m), the Rauhhorn (2240 m), which has to be climbed, and the peaks of the Hindelanger Klettersteig. On the Austrian side, you will discover the Vilsalpsee in the valley.
On the summit of the Rauhhorn you can enjoy an even better view of the peaks already mentioned. In addition, towards the south you can see the Kugelhorn (2126 m), the pyramid-shaped Hochvogel (2592 m) and our next destination, the Schrecksee. To the west we see the peaks of the Hindelanger Klettersteig with the Gro&szlig Daumen (2280 m), the prominent rock needle of the Schneck (2268 m) and in the distance to the southwest further peaks of the Allgäuer Hauptkamm.

images.caption: Gems on the way to the Front Sheep Pan.
Looking back over the descent ridge.

title: Through valleys and meadows in the Rhön
short_description: The Rhön is not called the "land of a thousand streams" for nothing. We can experience the diversity of water and species on this wonderful circular trail.
long_description: We follow the main road briefly to the left and turn right into the street "Am Bahnhof". Behind the former Aumühle, now a carpenter's workshop, we walk to the right across the Scheppenbach and the country road and turn right at the height of a rest area. We turn left and follow the white "9" on a black background into a magnificent valley. At the level of the ponds on the left, we turn right and follow the blue wedge, red angle and green circle markings. We reach the Ziegelhof Chapel, where a rest area invites us to take a break. We first follow the markings, behind a right-hand bend the path joins another one. Here we walk to the right until we reach an asphalt road, which we follow to the right back to the starting point.

images.caption: The Scheppenbach valley is a prime example of the revitalisation of habitats in the Rhön biosphere reserve.
This rest area invites us to linger.
After leaving the Scheppenbach valley, we walk through another magnificent valley.
We soon reach the beautifully situated Ziegelhof Chapel.
We start at the car park near the Scheppenbachhaus.
The former Aumühle is now a carpentry workshop.

title: At the Pic du Midi d'Osseau
short_description: This easy circular route passes under the Pic du Midi d'Osseau.

title: On the Eco Trail around Dörnberg near Weimar
short_description: A fine circular walk on archaeological tracks around the Dörnberg. We encounter old ramparts, the Wichtelkirche and the Helfenstein and hike in a varied way sometimes across meadows, sometimes through forests.
long_description: The starting point of our tour is the sports field in Dörnberg. First we follow the signpost, which looks like an arrowhead without an arrow (or a triangle without a third edge with the tip pointing upwards), on slightly winding paths up to the Dörnberg plateau: above the sports field we reach a forest road, where we keep to the right. At the next bend we turn left. Over two terrain steps we reach the next forest road and now climb on a path of the south side of the Dörnberg up to the plateau. The Dörnberg rises about 200 to 300 m above the surrounding heights and offers us a magnificent view on all sides. In the meantime we have come across the sign of the eco-path, an interrupted circle. We follow it around the plateau. On the north side we descend to an information board and continue to the settlement of Friedrichstein. We cannot miss the Wichtelkirche, a basalt stone and our next destination, it is clearly visible in front of us. We cross the open space straight on towards the glider camp. To the right is the Helfenstein, a rock formation exposed by erosion. We follow the signpost in the direction of the hut at Immelburg and further into the spruce forest until we meet a forest road. We keep to the right until we come to a rest area. The eco-path would now lead us further in the direction of Hohlestein (a detour of about 2.5 km in total), but we follow the cycle path sign until we reach the village of Dörnberg again and our starting point, the sports field.

images.caption: The legendary Church of the Secret Santa.

title: Towards the viewpoint of Falcon's Rock
short_description: A very easy, relaxing trail, also suitable for children, leading to a viewpoint above the Mures Valley.
long_description: Stânca Șoimului (or Șoimului), a rocky formation with a fairytale name, can be reached by anyone who wants to take a short walk, în slight climb, starting from DN15. From the road you can see all of Neagra and beyond, as well as a good part of the Mures Valley, places that are part of the Deda-Toplița Landscape Reserve.

images.caption: Panoramic view of the Mures Valley

title: Moor circuit around Grassau
short_description: The moor circuit around Grassau offers us very beautiful views, but also interesting insights into the nature and former cultivation of the high moor near Grassau.
long_description: Our tour starts on the church square in Grassau at the King Ludwig II fountain directly in front of the tourist information office. At the pedestrian lights we cross Rottauer Straße and turn right. Continue to the left into Niederfeldstraße. Shortly afterwards, a brown sign shows us the way into Moosbacher Straße and in the direction of Moorrundweg. Soon Moosbacher Straße turns off to the right as a dead end. From now on, our path follows the continuous signage, a yellow sign with a white directional arrow and the inscription "Grassau und Rottau im Chiemgau - www.laeuferseminar.de". On a small bridge with wooden railings, we pass the Grassauer Bach stream turning left. Finally, you cross a farmstead and then continue to follow the asphalt path to the right until you reach another bridge. We now cross the Hindlinger Bach stream and behind the Moosbauer homestead we reach the nature reserve. The path leads us through a forest and moor landscape to an interesting information board on the "Kendlmühlfilzen" nature reserve (1). This raised bog is one of the most valuable in Central Europe. Together with the Rottauer Filzen, the Kendlmühlfilzen ("Filz" = Bavarian for "moor") form the complex of the "Southern Chiemsee Moors" with a total area of 1800 hectares. Although it was intensively farmed until the 1980s, it still has the original surface form and plant cover in its core area. Shortly after the information board, we leave the moor circuit for a worthwhile detour to a viewing platform (2). In front of the platform you can see the remains of the railway network built from 1920 onwards. The transport of the cut peat by narrow-gauge railway was a basic prerequisite for the cultivation of the moor. Thus, a special peat station was established in Rottau on the Munich-Salzburg railway line. In addition, here you have a good overview of the moor and enjoy a magnificent panorama. We return to the moor circular path and now hike through the middle of the moor. Again and again, benches invite you to take a break. Soon the path joins another one, which we follow to the left. Now the route leads us along the edge of the moor through some woodland. This is followed by a short field passage until, at the level of the hamlet of Klaus, we turn right again towards the moor. Now the Moorrundweg and the Moorlehrpfad Rottau-Grassau run together for a while. Interesting information boards provide information about the flora and fauna in the moor, but also about the aspects of cultivation. A wooden footbridge leads a short distance into the area, which is otherwise off-limits. We then leave the moor and cross the German Alpine Road, briefly turn left on the path running parallel to the roadway and then turn right. On a slight uphill stretch, we walk through the forest until the moor circular path turns off to the left. However, we continue to the right and make a detour to a waterfall (3) of the Grießenbach stream. To do this, we have to cross the stream to the right over a wooden bridge and then follow the path further uphill to the left. You can take a breather on a bench and watch the natural spectacle. Back at the moor round path, we now continue to follow the yellow signs with white direction arrow. We hike on paths and trails slightly uphill through the forest until we meet a forest road. This leads us downhill to the left and meets a road at the former mountain bath. Here the "Bergbadstüberl am Krötenteich" (4) invites you to take a break. The road takes us further down the valley until we meet the Rottacher Straße. The road leads us to the right and back to the starting point at the tourist information office in Grassau.

images.caption: The path ends at a waterfall.
The observation tower offers a beautiful view of the moor.
We look across the moor to the mountains.
A viewing walkway leads into the moor.

title: The Hell Mountain at Mellensee near Saalow
short_description: A leisurely hiking tour through the beautiful forests around the Höllenberg at Mellensee near Saalow.
long_description:
To avoid getting lost, this hiking trail is marked throughout with a yellow dot on a white background.
We start our hiking tour at the windmill barn in Saalow. We walk west along the Dorfstraße and turn left at the crossroads into the Friedhofweg. We pass the resting place, keep to the right and continue walking through the idyllic forest. After a short stretch along the edge of the forest, we turn left onto the forest path, cross a fork and turn right at the next T-junction towards Horstweg. Now we follow this to the left, enjoying the view of further fields, until we reach the forest again, where we turn off to our right after a few metres. At the next T-junction, we continue straight ahead until we reach a clearing. We now cross the hiking trail and continue straight ahead to the edge of the forest. Between forest and meadows, the route leads us to the right around the Höllenberg after a left turn again to a fork, where we continue our hike on the right through the forest. Straight ahead we again reach a T-junction. We keep to the right. At the next crossroads we turn left. This path leads us out of the thicket to the edge of the forest, where we turn onto a field path on our right. This takes us back to the starting point, the windmill in Saalow.

title: अंधरबन ट्रैक
short_description: अंधरबन एक घना जंगल ट्रेल मार्ग है जो कुंडलिका घाटी, तम्हिनी घाट, और सह्याद्री पर्वतमाला के हरेभरे जंगलों के शानदार दृश्य प्रस्तुत करता है। यह टॉप मानसून ट्रैक है जब बारिश, धुंध,और, हरियाली इसे किसी सपने जैसा बना देते हैं।
long_description:
अंधरबन दो मराठी शब्दों 'अंधेर' यानि की 'अंधेरा' और 'बन' यानि की 'जंगल' से मिल कर बना है और इसलिए इसका मतलब है 'अंधेरा जंगल'। यह नाम इस इलाके पर एकदम सटीक बैठता है क्योंकि यहाँ के जंगल इतने घने हैं की सूरज की रौशनी को ऊपर ही रोक लेते हैं और नीचे अँधेरा रहता है।
तम्हिनी घाट में अंधरबन जंगल 2160 फीट की ऊंचाई पर स्थित है और इस बारह किलोमीटर ट्रैक को करने में लगभग पाँच घंटे का समय लगता है। यह एक अपेक्षाकृत आसान ट्रेल है है इसलिए नौसिखिए हाइकर्स के लिए भी अच्छा है। एक और दिलचस्प बात यह  है कि यह ट्रेल ज्यादातर ढलान वाली है जिसके कुछ हिस्से सपाट और चढ़ाई तो बिल्कुल नहीं है।
अंधरबन ट्रैक की शुरुआत पिंपरी गांव में बने पिंपरी बांध से होती है। यहां से ट्रेल मार्ग अच्छी तरह से दिखाई देता है। लेकिन अगर चाहें तो एक स्थानीय गाइड को किराए पर लिया जा सकता है ताकि वह आपका मार्गदर्शन कर सके। 
ट्रेल मार्ग पिंपरी बांध की ऊपरी दीवार (आउटलेट/अबुदेमेंट ) से होकर गुजरता है जो एक खुले मैदान और उसके बाद कृषि क्षेत्रों में प्रवेश करता हे। जैसे आप आगे बढ़ते हैं तो ट्रेल अंततः वन क्षेत्र में प्रवेश करती है। यहाँ पर सूरज की रौशनी ना पंहुचने की वजह से ठंडक और अँधेरा होना आम बात है। ट्रेल मार्ग में पानी की कई साफ ठंडी धाराएं भी आएँगी लेकिन उनका पानी पीने योग्य नहीं है। रास्ते में में कई जगहों से कुंडलिका घाटी और तम्हिनी घाट के शानदार नज़ारें दिखते है। लगभग 5 घंटे तक इस सुन्दर ट्रेल से चलकर भीरा बांध आएगा जो इस फारेस्ट ट्रेल का समापन बिंदु है।

title: Rocks and views near Jestädt 3 - Eschwege Meinhard
short_description: An easy hike suitable for all seasons and times of day, alternating river and mountain scenery.
long_description:
You can see the precipices and impressive rocks on the "Weinberg", climb through a hollow path to a small plateau and have wonderful views of the Werratal and Fürstenstein Castle with its impressive location (large deer enclosure).
You can always let your gaze wander all around. In the valley you can see the mountain ranges that border the Werratal, on the other side lies Albungen in the valley, the limestone quarries at the "Hohe Bahn" are close enough to touch.

images.caption: On our hike we see Hörne and Hörnelücke.

title: Höglandsleden - Stage 1 - From Nässjö to Ärnanäs
short_description: The first stage of our tour on Höglandsleden leads from Nässjö station through the Lövhult nature reserve to Ärnanäs campsite by Norra Vixen lake.
long_description: The first section of our trail leads through the beautiful nature reserve Lövhult, which is only a short distance from the small town of Nässjö. The area is popular with sports enthusiasts of all kinds, with well-maintained jogging trails, bridle paths and even a cross-country ski trail in winter. Passing old manor houses, we come to Lake Vixen and walk leisurely along its shore to the campsite.

title: The Wadi Kabir hilltop trail run/hike
short_description: Take a run or walk on this set of tracks and paths that overlook Wadi Kabir on one side and gently rolling jebel on the other.
long_description:
With the exception of a few wadis - and even those usually come with a bit too much vehicle traffic -  the Muscat area sadly lacks trails that really lend themselves to running - especially anything that's elevated.
This is a loop I used to enjoy running after work, but it can just as easily be walked and is a nice way to spend a few hours.  There's no real destination - it's more just an oportunity to stretch your legs and take in the view. 
The route itself is a mix of a random paved footpath that extends along the ridgeline followed by a meandering dirt road that hugs the southern flank of the mountain, with some gentle inclines thrown in to help get the blood pumping.  The approach is also interesting which means your run/walk can be followed by a scenic drive.     
Worth a look.... in my opinion :)

Some of the random paved sections
Looking towards the Al Bustan Palace hotel
The road leading to Barr Al Jissa
The mast on the other side of the wadi after a storm

title: Postcard trail in Serra dos Órgãos National Park
short_description: Considered the most beautiful trail in Teresópolis, the Postcard Trail has a beautiful view of the Serra dos Órgãos mountain range.
long_description: This beautiful trail, accessed by Estrada da Barragem just after the Casa do Montanhista  crosses an area of Atlantic Forest with beautiful views of the mountains and gives access to the Dedo de Deus Viewpoint, facing the mountain range of Serra dos Órgatilde;os. If you are driving, you can leave it at the old inn located a little in front of the trail entrance. On the way, it is possible to observe various trees, such as the jequitib. <PARNA classifies this trail as moderate, it has several stretches of steep climbing with steps and unevenness almost 300 meters. If you are used to hiking trails, will find quite easy. The whole path is well signposted at the viewpoint there a sign indicating names main peaks, such Escalavrado, Dedo de Deus, Santo Antocirc;nio, among others.

title: Vierzehnheiligen and the Staffelberg - from Lichtenfels to Bad Staffelstein
short_description: This tour takes us to the two landmarks of the "Garden of God on the Obermain", the pilgrimage basilica Vierzehnheiligen and the Staffelberg.
long_description:
Our tour starts at the railway station in Lichtenfels. The district town is known as the "German Basket Town" - the "Basket Market" every year in September and many a shop in the town centre bear witness to the town's tradition as the centre of the German wicker industry and craft. At the station, we keep heading south and follow Bamberger Straße along the pavement for quite some time. This takes us through the district of Seubelsdorf before we turn left shortly before the slip road to the B173 trunk road. Passing the sports home of the SV Borussia Siedlung Lichtenfels, we come to the pilgrims' path, which leads us to the car park below the basilica. Along the access road we walk uphill to the "Franconian Basilica" Vierzehnheiligen. It was built where a shepherd once had an apparition and impresses with its rich, imposing baroque interior. Perhaps we will be lucky and arrive at the same time as one of the numerous pilgrimages - in this case, the ringing of bells and brass band music would accompany us. Around the basilica we come across numerous stalls and several places to stop for refreshments. After the rest, we walk uphill towards the east along the road before we follow the sign "Staffelberg" onto a path into the forest. We walk steadily uphill on paths and trails, partly over rocky steps, until we reach the high trail along the Alte Staffelberg up to the Staffelberg. The plateau of the Staffelberg is reached after another ascent, here we have the opportunity to stop for a break in the Staffelberg-Klause, we can also take a look at the Adelgundis Chapel, which as a pilgrimage chapel was more or less the predecessor of Vierzehnheiligen. It is a matter of honour that we walk around the plateau on the meadow path and enjoy the wonderful views in all directions.
On the descent, we follow the signs to Bad Staffelstein at the Klause, which we reach after a good three quarters of an hour, always downhill. In the spa town, we first pass the cemetery before turning left down Lichtenfelser Straße to the market square. There you can either stop for a bite to eat or turn right and walk back to the station, which you reach after about 1 km on Bahnhofsstraße. The trains take us back to our starting point in Lichtenfels every half hour.

images.caption: The Adelgundis Chapel on the Staffelberg.
Historical jewel: the town hall in Bad Staffelstein.

title: चौकोरी हिमालयन व्यू पॉइंट का साइकिल दौरा
short_description: उत्तराखंड का चौकोरी एक सुन्दर हिमालयी हिल स्टेशन है जो बर्फीले हिमालय , हरी-भरी घाटियों, सुन्दर मंदिरों, खुशबूदार चाय बागानों के साथ साथ दे वदार और बुरांश के जंगलों से भरा हुआ है।
long_description:
यह साइकिल दौरा छोटा लेकिन बेहद सुन्दर है। सहूलियत के लिए इस साइकिल दौरे को पिथौरागढ़ ज़िले के चौकोरी हिलस्टेशन में बने हुए कुमाऊँ मंडल विकास निगम के गेस्ट हाउस से शुरू किया जा सकता है। गेस्ट हाउस से बाहर निकलते ही कुछ ही दूरी पर एक डामर वाली पक्की सड़क है जिस पर करीब 1200 मीटर साइकिल चलाने के बाद एक नेचर ट्रेल आती है। यह नेचर ट्रेल देवदार से जंगलों से होते हुए सीधे हिमालयन व्यू पॉइंट पर जा कर ख़तम होती है। हिमालयन व्यू पॉइंट से शानदार हिमालयी चोटियाँ दिखती हैं जो मंत्रमुग्ध कर देना वाला दृश्य है। 
यह साइकिल मार्ग आसान है और सभी स्तर के साइकिलिस्ट के लिए उपयुक्त है। इस आउट एंड बैक (आना-जाना) ट्रेल ) को एक घंटे में आराम कवर किया जा सकता है और बाकी समय चौकोरी हिमालयन व्यू पॉइंट से हिमालय की सुंदरता देखने में बिताया जा सकता है। यहाँ पर कई पर्यटक, साइकिलिस्ट, मोटरसाइकिलिस्ट, हाइकर, और ट्रैकर आते हैं।

भारत के उत्तराखंड राज्य के पिथौरागढ़ जिले के चौकोरी शहर से हिमालय का शानदार दृश्य।

title: Through the Hörnerdörfer
short_description: On this entertaining hike we can enjoy the charms of the Allgäu landscape to the full.
long_description: Via Westerhofen we reach the Hörner villages. Below the main villages of Ofterschwang and Bolsterlang, we hike through the picturesque landscape to Fischen in the Allgäu.

The Allgäu Alps tower behind Schweineberg

title: Nice view of Stuttgart from Grabkapelle auf dem Württemberg
short_description: A short, but valuable hike in Stuttgart with vineyards, chapels, and good views.
long_description: A nice tour starting in Untertürkheim, strolling through the vineyards and ending with a magnificent view of the city of Stuttgart from the Grabkapelle, there you will be able to enjoy a cultural heritage very close to the starting point and appreciate the elegant Roman design of the chapel and the sarcophagus where Queen Katharina and her husband, King Wilhelm I, rest together.

title: Páramo Circuit on the slopes of Volcán Pichincha
short_description: Hard to believe you're right above the city: This easy walk lets you explore the fascinating high-andean landscape of the Páramo vegetation with stunning views of Ruccu Pichincha.
long_description: This circular route from the TeleferiQo cable car traverses the slopes of the mighty volcano Rucu Pichincha, offering panoramic views of Quito's surrounding volcanoes including Cayambe, Antisana, and Cotopaxi. Explore the unique páramo ecosystem, a high-altitude tapestry of cushion plants and frailejones adapted to the harsh conditions. This is a relatively easy hike that lets you delve into the high andean landscape without any need to complete the more challenging scramble up to the summit of Ruccu Pichincha. Breathe in the crisp mountain air scented with local flora and keep an eye out for birds flitting amongst the colorful blooms. This gentle loop provides a fantastic opportunity to explore the unique biodiversity of the Andes while soaking in the majesty of Ecuador's volcanic landscape - a mere 15-minute cable car ride from the capital.

images.caption: Páramo on the slopes of Rucu Pichincha

title: Across the forest
short_description: Romanshorn, with its wonderful location on Lake Constance, its intact hinterland and its ideal location in terms of transport, is a unique starting point for great hiking tours.
long_description:
The accessibility with intercity connections, the regional train THURBO, Lake Constance shipping and the ferry connection to Germany makes Romanshorn an Eldorado for all non-motorised traffic. The numerous leisure activities in and on the water as well as the wide range of catering and accommodation options round off an unforgettable stay in Romanshorn.

The route leads from Bahnhofplatz up Bahnhofstrasse to the Alleestrasse junction. There you turn right and then immediately left again onto the small Schützengasse. After crossing Hafenstrasse, you will find yourself on Bachweg. This leads past the schoolhouse and sports field, via Kreuzlingerstrasse to Romis. From there it goes straight up into the Romanshorn forest. In the forest past the start of the Vitaparcours, straight on to the edge of the forest, turn left there. At the next crossroads, turn right to the Uttwil pond. Turn left before the pond. Take the second turning on the right to the castle-like water reservoir. There is a nice barbecue area here. Now continue in the direction of the forester's lodge until you reach the Waldschenke. This idyllically situated «Open Air Restaurant» invites you to a leisurely lunch. After the Waldschenke, turn left to Spitz. From here, the bus takes you back to Romanshorn.

images.caption: Hiking in and around the orchards

title: Walking near Wald a.d. Alz
short_description: This short walking tour takes us to the beautiful castle church of St. Erasmus, romantically situated in the forest.
long_description: In the centre of Wald a. d. Alz, at the pavilion, walk south along Schlossbergstraße, towards the forest and then turn right uphill into Max-von-Mayer-Straße. After just a few metres, the road becomes a narrow path leading up into the forest. We leave the last houses behind us and continue right at the first junction in the forest (1). When the mixed forest changes to a monotonous spruce forest, we pay attention to the path branching off to the left, which leads us up to the high trail. At the top of the turning point (2), we take the left path and reach the houses of Oberberg (3) at the edge of the forest. In the village, we go left to the church of St. Erasmus (4) and also look at the castle church from the inside. At the archway, a staircase leads down to our way back.

images.caption: A short climb leads us to the turning point of our hike.
A short but steep descent leads us back to the starting point of our tour.
Hidden in the forest is the small castle church of St. Erasmus.
Our hike starts at the pavilion in the centre of Wald a. d. Alz.

title: Extratour Büdingen
short_description: The narrow streets of Büdingen, the half-timbered houses and the castle make this moderately difficult tour an experience.
long_description: Büdingen is an ideal hiking start and end point. Other unusual sights follow along the route. The sections of trail in between often run on wide, easily passable gravel roads. The exception is the last section between the Thiergartenweiher pond and the basalt formation, where the trail crosses paths in places and views into the Seemenbach valley are possible again and again. A particularly attractive section of the trail is the sunken path on the ascent in Büdingen Forest. This consists partly of pure beech and spruce stands, but in other places larches, birches, pines and oaks are also mixed in.

title: On the shore of Lake Constance
Nordic Walking Kneipp in Bad Peterstal-Griesbach
short_description: This tour takes you on a Nordic walking circuit of a special kind, the Nordic walking Kneipp course of the municipality of Bad Peterstal-Griesbach, which is probably unique in Germany.
long_description: We start our tour at the car park of the Kurhaus in Bad Peterstal-Griesbach. On Schwimmbadstraße we turn right and cross the Freiersbach at the Kurhaus. Here we keep to the right on Kurhausweg and turn right at the next junction into Schwarzwaldstraße. At the tourist information office we turn left and shortly afterwards we are in front of the "Kneippanlage an der Rench". We keep to the left, walk briefly along the tracks and walk under them on the right. At the next junction, turn left, then immediately right and follow the path until you reach the "Wassertretstelle Wendelsberg" at the Freiersbach. From there we walk in a right turn to the railway tracks and along them until a path joins from the left. Now walk straight ahead and finally turn right under the tracks and cross the Rench. Immediately behind the river, we turn right into Kirchbergweg. After a short stretch of walking, we reach the Kirchberg water treading facility, keeping to the left. There we can cool down one last time. We return to the starting point via the sports field.

title: Hong Kong: from Victoria Peak to Central Station
short_description: Victoria Peak: a must-see in Hong Kong
long_description: Take the cable car to PIc Victoria near Central Station (exit the station and walk about 800 metres along the road).<Climb up and enjoy the view, then after enjoying breathtaking view of Hong Kong its bay, take a beautiful descent to foot skyscrapers Central Station.

title: From the Bachweg to the Uttwil Pond
short_description: Romanshorn, with its wonderful location on Lake Constance, its intact hinterland and its ideal location in terms of transport, is a unique starting point for great hiking tours.
long_description:
For this hike, it is advisable to take drinks and food from your rucksack.
From Bahnhofplatz, walk up Bahnhofstrasse to the Alleestrasse junction. Turn right there and then immediately left again onto the small Schützengasse. After crossing Hafenstrasse, you will find yourself on Bachweg. This leads past the schoolhouse and sports field, via Kreuzlingerstrasse to Romis. Now turn left up to Eichhof and then into the Romanshorn forest. In the forest, the path passes the target stand on the left. Turn right after the target stand. At the next fork, keep left and continue to the Spitz car park. Turn sharp right there and then immediately right again. Now go straight on until you reach the Uttwiler Weiher. Turn left before the pond and go straight on past a farm to Uttwil. As you cross the village, you pass the modern town hall and arrive at the railway station. From there, the Thurbo lake line runs halfway to Romanshorn.

.

images.caption: From Uttwil back with the Thurbo

title: On the beach in Binz
short_description: Our Nordic walking tour takes us along the beach and promenade through the sophisticated Baltic resort of Binz to Prora.
long_description: The starting point of our Nordic walking tour is at the square in front of the pier in the Baltic resort of Binz. Binz is the best known and largest seaside resort on the island of Rügen. In addition to the approximately 4 km long sandy beach, many visitors are attracted by the prestigious beach promenade. We first walk past the pier on the left to the beach. The Binz pier was built in its present form in 1994, but with a length of 370 m it is much shorter than the 560 m long pier built in 1902. The ice winters of 1903/04 and 1942/43 destroyed this pier. We walk along the wide sandy beach (1) to Prora. The view stretches across the Schmale Heide to Sassnitz and the heights of the Jasmund peninsula. About 800 metres away we see the brick quay of the former KdF baths (2) Prora. This enormous building, about 4.5 km long, was built from 1936 onwards as a holiday resort for the National Socialist "Strength through Joy" organisation. Probably the longest building in Europe, it was intended to accommodate up to 20,000 guests. With the beginning of the Second World War, construction activities were stopped. Now the listed building is a reminder of a dark period in German history. Behind the first block of former KdF buildings, we leave the beach on the left and walk along a forest path to a road. We walk past the buildings of the former KdF facility (3) on the left, before the Bundeswehr campsite we turn left through the forest and then right on a path above the beach back to Binz. At the end of the campsite, we walk straight ahead on the beach promenade past Villa Undine (4) and the Kurhaus in Binz (5) until we arrive back at the starting point of our tour, the square in front of the pier.

images.caption: The beach promenade of the Baltic resort of Binz is lined with villas in the seaside style.
The kilometre-long sandy beach stretches from Binz to Prora.
Excursion boats depart regularly from the pier in Binz.
Villa Undine, built in 1885, is one of the three preserved, listed Wolgasthäuser on the island of Rügen.
The site of the planned National Socialist "Kraft-durch-Freude" seaside resort is now a listed building.

title: On the shore of Lake Constance
Walking tour: from hamlets to washhouses
short_description: This is a family-friendly walking trail that takes you from hamlets to washhouses, taking in remarkable views of the Luzarch landscape and the surrounding villages.
long_description:
Luzarches still has in its heart a rare wooden hall, mentioned from the 14th century and rebuilt in 1740. Under its spidery wooden legs, protected from humidity by large stone shoes and its tiled roof, a weekly market and the various festivities of Luzarch still take place today. <Luzarches has always been an ideal stopover on the Paris-Amiens route and welcomed travellers: there were already 16 inns hostels in 17th century. It was therefore quite natural that wealthy Parisians built their holiday homes here 19th century, enjoying mildness of place benefiting from practical arrival railway 1880. Their suite restaurants, hunting rendezvous, guinguettes, whose laughter music have since become part air times (Lassy Mill Villa des Champs, …), brought in.

The village map, pointing to the sky with its rigid but square bell tower,the church of Saint-Côme and Saint-Damien has been watching over the villagers since the early Middle Ages, and was first mentioned in a charter issued by Charlemagne in 775. In a beautiful Romanesque style, the choir and the base of the belfry are evidence of the reconstruction of the original church. But it is above all its facade that is remarkable, completed in 1548 by Nicolas de Saint-Michel, in the midst of the late Renaissance, it recaptures the charm of the Antiques through the use of vaults, pediments and rich sculpted horns.
The church is also a good example of a church in the Renaissance.
The covered washhouses were built, under Napoleon III, out of a desire to introduce hygiene into domestic practices. Municipalities were not very concerned with hygiene before the law of 3 February 1851, by which the State opened an extraordinary fund of six hundred thousand francs to encourage the communes to build public baths and washhouses. Formerly places of life filled with village gossip, they are now peaceful places where wild animals often come to drink.
Please note that this is not the case with the public baths. <In this area, the water was washed 2 or 3 times a year. In huge tub we put layer of ash, linen and so on then covered with boiling water. It an extraordinary atmosphere, according to Luzarches resident in 1900.&In Luzarches, you can find 4th washhouse F, at bottom avenue de la libeacute;ration direction sports ground.
The washhouse is located in the centre of the village of Luzarches.
Wetlands.These soils flooded or saturated with water are the kidneys of our Earth, they are true natural filters. They constitute a highly sought-after habitat for a multitude of animal and plant species. One finds, as here, specific plants such as the meadow, the Comfrey, the water mint, the yellow iris, the meadow queen (at the exit of Plessis-Luzarches).
.

title: दीपोर बील (झील) ट्रैक
short_description: यह ट्रैक गुवाहाटी शहर के पास मौजूद मीठे पानी की दी पोर बील झील का बेहद सुन्दर दौरा ह ै।
long_description:
असमी भाषा में बील का मतलब झील होता है। दीपोर बील (झील) निचले असम क्षेत्र में मीठे पानी की सबसे बड़ी झीलों में से एक है। यह असम के कामरूप मेट्रोपॉलिटन जिले में स्थित है हालाँकि इस तक गुवाहाटी शहर से पहुंचना ज्यादा पास पड़ता है।
दीपोर झील को रामसर (RAMSAR) कन्वेंशन के तहत एक आर्द्रभूमि (वेटलैंड) का दर्जा मिला हुआ है और यह एक बहुत महत्पूर्ण पक्षी अभयारण्य की तरह भी जानी जाती है।
दीपोर बील/झील का हाइकिंग ट्रैक राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग 27 के किनारे से एक साइड रोड पर शुरू होता है। यह आरंभ बिंदु कामरूप मेट्रोपॉलिटन जिले से लगभग 36 किलोमीटर दूर और गुवाहाटी शहर से लगभग 8 किलोमीटर की दूरी पर पड़ता है। इस साइड रोड पर लगभग 200 मीटर चलने के बाद, झील के लिए एक नेचर ट्रेल शुरू होती है जो फिर कच्ची सड़क और छोटे-छोटे तालाबों/जल निकायों से गुजरते हुए अंत में विशाल और सुन्दर दीपोर झील तक पहुँचती है। इस ट्रेल की एक-तरफ़ा लंबाई लगभग 2.5 किलोमीटर है। ट्रेल मार्ग ज्यादातर समतल है और सरल है। इस ट्रैक का कठिनाई स्तर आसान है और किसी भी हाइकर को इसमें कोई समस्या नहीं होनी चाहिए।
ट्रेल के अंत में झील के किनारे पहुंचकर हाइकर्स शानदार दृश्य के साथ-साथ खूबसूरत पक्षियों को देखने का आनंद ले सकते हैं।

कामरूप जिले की दीपोर बील झील को जाने वाली ट्रेल, असम, भारत।
कामरूप जिले की दीपोर बील झील की ट्रेल पर साइनपोस्ट, असम, भारत।
गुवाहाटी शहर के पास दीपोर बील में नावें, असम, भारत।

title: Across the bottom of the lake to the sunken church of Mavrovo
short_description: In autumn and winter, when the water level of the Mavrovo reservoir is low enough, you can walk where there is usually water to the usually half-sunken church.
long_description:
A short walk from the parking lot of the sports hall in Mavrovo along unpaved footpaths to the ruins of the old church of Mavrovo. This path and the ruins of the church are accessible only from late summer when the water level of the lake is low. The trail route changes a bit every year, but as long as you stick to the rough direction, you can safely walk on the drained floodplain. The way back via the road offers additional views of the church and the lake from new perspectives; of course, you can also make your way back via the trails.
With children, it is a real adventure, of course, and with appropriate clothing it is a good option even for rainy days due to the shortness of the tour. Although the collapsed church roof does not protect against moisture, you can always find a dry spot for a rest in the gateways.

title: The Rhine Route - Switzerland - Great Bicycle Route
short_description: The "Rhine Route", known in the European cycle route network as EuroVelo 15, follows the river of the same name from its source in the Swiss mountains to its mouth in the Netherlands, from the Alps to the North Sea. It crosses 4 countries (Switzerland, France, Germany and the Netherlands), 9 Unesco World Heritage sites, and covers 1230 km of track.

title: Night time Winter Walk in Fjerdingby: Smestad - Tristylen - Hektnerhøgåsen - Ramstadsjøen - Trisitilen - Smestad
short_description:
A nice winter walk with steep climbs and descents. In the winter, the paths are snow covered but usually walkable with spikes. Hektnerhøgåsen is one of the highest peaks in Nordmarka. The trail will take you to Hulderheim at Ramstadsjøen which is a listed area dating back to the stone age with a vivid history in the 1900s. Bring with you spikes and headlamp.
For this hike we followed the blue summer markings on the threes in addition to the signage (Blue markings are the summer trails, red winter).

images.caption: Skating in the Heart of Mostindia

title: Redwoods in the Naturpark Hochtaunus
short_description: A short but surprising hiking route in nature on the outskirts of the city of Frankfurt leading to two impressive redwood trees
long_description:
When you think of Frankfurt, you naturally think of a big city and less of nature, but through a secret tip we received from a local acquaintance, we found out that in a park called Naturpark Hochtaunus, which is located northwest of the city, you can see a spectacle of redwood trees that usually characterizes forests in the western United States. Within a short and easy walking distance, you too can admire two huge sequoia trees that were planted on the spot in 1848.
The road is mostly paved and therefore accessible for walking with prams and wheelchairs (take into account a slight slope and that the last meter of the road is on dirt, but it is flat and comfortable).

images.caption: The crossroads leading to the trees, turn right here
A joint picture of the two sequoia trees
A blessing not only for feet!

title: Farms around Pirka
short_description: This Nordic walking tour takes us to typical farms of the Bavarian Forest. The route in the deep forest opens up to wide clearings in some places.
long_description: We start at the Waldesruh inn and walk up the narrow road. After a short distance, the gravelled forest road begins, which leads us via Hohenleiten to the Kaltenbrunn farm with a beautiful view. Now we go down the slope and reach a path deeper into the forest. We hike through the village of Lammerbach. There we realise that the timber industry is one of the main economic sources of the region. We follow the forest path to the Gröllerhaus with its horse breeding. Finally, we hike through the forest and across some clearings to Pirka. A loop around the village shows us more farms and offers us a view over the campsite. Then we return to the starting point.

images.caption: A farm on the southern outskirts of Lammerbach.
A horse breeding farm also belongs to the Gröllerhaus farm.

title: From Wangerooge to the airfield
short_description: We walk from the main town of the island to the east end and the airfield.
long_description: Wangerooge is the easternmost of the seven inhabited East Frisian islands and lies in the Lower Saxony Wadden Sea. On this leisurely hike we walk from the main village to the east of the island. Back we go around the airfield and through the dunes to the northern beach.

images.caption: Wangerooge is perfect for long walks on the beach.

title: Walking around Fischerbach
short_description: The easy mountain tour starts above Fischerbach in Vordertal and leads through forest and pasture with excellent views into the Kinzigtal valley beyond Fischerbach.
long_description: This easy Nordic walking tour starts above Fischerbach in Vordertal and leads through forest and pasture with excellent views of the Kinzigtal and Fischerbach. From the hikers' car park at Gasthof Krone, we walk in the direction of the inn. Shortly before, a path branches off to the left, leading us along the carpenter's workshop and up the meadow to the left next to a small wood. After about 200 m, we walk on the meadow path near the telephone line to the Bergeck. Now follow the Nordic Walking signs "22" to the left and turn right below the houses. Along the edge of the forest, we pass the Wilhelmshütte. At a playground, we turn right along the Kreuzweg stones to a wayside cross. Here is half-time and our route leads uphill to the right - always following the signposts with the number 22 - into the forest. Above the Bergeck, the path leads out of the forest and we turn left again across the meadow to the starting point.

images.caption: Beautiful Black Forest houses line our path.
This panoramic view is offered from the Bergeck.

title: Mary Schäffer Loop Trail
short_description: A panoramic, circular, relatively short and easy hiking trail that runs right next to the breathtaking Lake Maligne
long_description: The hiking trail is known as the "Mary Schäffer Loop" and named after Mrs. Marie Schäffer, who is said to have discovered Lake Maligne for the first time in 1908. The length of the trail is about 3 kilometers. The route offers a panoramic view of the northern part of Lake Maligne and starts at the lower parking space, descends towards the lake, runs alongside it and leads through the forest back to the car parks.

images.caption: View of Lake Maligne from the trail
Beautiful Lake Maligne and mountain backdrop
Snowy mountain panorama at Lake Maligne

title: Ceraunian Mountains Grand Traverse (Maja e Çikës)
short_description: Touching the sky on the coastal mountains: the Grand Traverse of the Ceraunian Mountains is both one of the most rewarding and most challenging hikes along the Albanian Riviera.
long_description: Traversing the Ceraunian Mountains from Llogara Pass in the West all the way to Pilur is surely one of the most strenous and challenging hikes you can possibly do in a day along the Albanian Riviera. Following a steep climb to the summit ridge of Maja e Çikës you make your way to the high pastures right below the peaks of the coastal mountain range. A sheer endless descend over the hilltops of the lower mountains takes you to the traditional mountain village Pilur, nestled into the hillside high above the coast. Wayfinding can be tricky in parts and the walk is long and challenging, but the incredible views both over the coastal hinterlands and the Mediterranean sea (on clear days all the way to Italy!) are out of this world. Only for hikers with plenty of experience and excellent physical condition.
