title: Kust till Kustleden - from Bjärabygget to Koarp
short_description: The twelfth stage of the Kust till Kustledens leads from the Bjärabygget campsite over the Hallandsåsen rise on the Swedish-Danish border to the Koarp campsite.
long_description: This section of the trail leads through sparsely inhabited territory. We hike over several steep hills and pastures on the Hallandsåsen mountain range, which was formed many millions of years ago when the European plate collided with the African plate. The landscape is characterised by gorges, erratic blocks and field caves. It is therefore not surprising that, according to legend, it was home to trolls and giants.

title: Alzey Nature and Culture Route
short_description: On this medium-difficulty route we experience the wine village of Dautenheim.
long_description:
We start at the Dautenheim sports field at the Flutgraben. From here we walk past the Obere Weidaser Mühle, the tax fruit meadows and the bird nature trail and up into the vineyards at the "Himmelacker". We continue to the panoramic view over the floodplains of the Weidastal and on to the Wartberg tower. When we get back to the village, we should take time to visit the over 200-year-old Protestant church. The barbecue area in the grove invites you to take a break. But we can also rest and relax at a typical "Rheinhessen wine tasting" in the picturesque Dautenheimer Winzerhöfe.
An attraction also worth seeing in Dautenheim is the historic farm garden, which was established according to Charlemagne's specifications.

title: From Krupka to Mosquito Hill and the ruins of Kyšperk Castle
short_description: Varied hike with a visit to a historic castle, beautiful views of the Ore Mountains and a descent into the depths of the mountains, where inexhaustible ore reserves are still to be found.
long_description:
Before hiking to the Ore Mountains, you should not miss some of the many significant sights in the town of Krupka. The market square (Mariánské náměstí) in Krupka-Bohosudov is dominated by the pilgrimage church of Mariaschein. Inseparably connected with the pilgrimage church is the complex of the former Jesuit monastery with the episcopal grammar school.
The Krupka district is relatively large and has considerable differences in altitude. The town centre (Bohosudov) lies at an altitude of 262 m, the highest place is the peak of the Mückenberg (Komáří hůrka, also called Mückentürmchen/Komáří vížka) at an altitude of 807 m, to which a chairlift leads up.
From a distance we can see the first destination of our hike: the ruins of Krupka Castle, which was built as a fortress on a rocky promontory in the middle of the town at the beginning of the 14th  century. From its walls you have a magnificent view of the historic centre of Krupka. The poet J. W. von Goethe also visited the castle several times, which is still commemorated by a monument.
The path leads us further up the ridge of the Ore Mountains, past the visitor mine "Alter Martin" (Starý Martin). There you can learn a lot about the history and the ways of tin extraction. The special thing about this mine is the length of the gallery of about 2 km - the longest tin vein in the Czech Republic and Central Europe.
After visiting the mine, we climb even further up the Ore Mountains ridge to the landmark and oldest lookout tower in this area - the Mückentürmchen. Excursionists can enjoy a view of the Ore Mountains foothills from the hotel terrace and, on a clear day, also of the peaks of the Bohemian Central Uplands. The magnificent view of the landscape was also admired by Alexander von Humboldt and Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, for example, and Woerl's travel guide from 1890 describes it as one of the most beautiful views in Europe!
Taking the high plateau near Fojtovice (Fojtovická pláň) with fascinating views of the Bohemian low mountain range, we smell the ruins of Kyšperk Castle. The former Geiersburg, now Kyšperk Castle, is located on a rocky promontory on one of the typical steep slopes of the Ore Mountains. Kyšperk Castle was first mentioned in 1319 and was inhabited, until it burned down in 1526 and was not rebuilt. Remains of the castle walls and a high tower can still be seen today. In one of the better preserved parts, you can visit the cellars and admire the view from the cliff.
Through the beautiful valley of the stream "Unčínský potok" we hike back to the foothills of the Ore Mountains to the village Unčín. In between  wide views of the Ore Mountains foothills and the picturesque Bohemian Uplands open up before we finally reach our starting point again at the market square in Krupka.

title: The Golden Ring of Russia
short_description: The Golden Ring of Russia is a famous touristic, pilgrimage route consisting of the ancient cities of North-East Russia.
long_description: In 1967, art historian Yuri Bychkov received an assignment from the newspaper Sovetskaya Kultura to write articles about towns in the Vladimir region, and set off on a journey from Moscow to Vladimir in his good, tried-and-true Moskvitch. Having visited the Vladimir region, he decided not to return by the same route to Moscow, but to drive through Yaroslavl. Thus, a circular route began to form, which included the central cities to the north-east of Moscow with a profound architectural heritage. The noble essays on Yuri Bychkov's journey entitled 'Golden Ring' were soon published, which included 8 cities: Sergiev Posad - Pereslavl-Zalessky - Rostov Veliky - Yaroslavl - Kostroma - Ivanovo - Suzdal - Vladimir. These major cities have preserved a unique memory of Russian history and culture.

title: From Sage to the fish ponds near Ahlhorn
short_description: This circular walk takes us to the picturesque Sager Heide and the Ahlhorn fish ponds.
long_description:
Our tour starts at the corner of Sager Straße and Im Sande, from where we walk along Sager Straße in the direction of Ahlhorn. Then we turn right into Brunnenweg. For quite a while we can now orientate ourselves by the signs of the long-distance hiking trail "Geestweg" and cross a beautiful forest section of the Sager Heide. We continue along the road called "Blanker Schlatt". This name goes back to an old field designation. In former times, the road was characterised by hollows. These were created by wind blowing the sandy soil down to the water table. These depressions were called "Schlatts". Due to the lowering of the groundwater level, the originally water-filled Schlatts have dried up and only the name "Blanker Schlatt" remains. We cross the motorway bridge and turn left a few hundred metres further on, walk straight ahead and then turn right onto a farm track. After a short while we reach a rest area on the left in the middle of the picturesque heath landscape. Here we can linger for a moment. Back on the path, we keep to the left and walk straight on until we come to a T-junction. There we turn left and come to the natural monument "12 Apostles". This is a group of erratic boulders, where it is assumed that the stones did not reach there by glaciers during the ice age, but were specially placed by human hand.
Our path continues past the "12 Apostles" and ends on the Baumweg, where the Ahlhorn pond farm is on the left. Here we follow the Baumweg to the right and leave it to the right at the "Karpfen" hikers' car park. After a short while, we reach the shore of the Ahlhorn fish ponds and turn left onto the long-distance hiking trail "Geest". This now leads us through the middle of the pond area before we continue to the left on a hilly forest path and take the turnoff to the right at the crossroads. Now we go straight on for quite a while until we reach the road "Ahlhorner Fischteiche", behind which we can orientate ourselves again on the long-distance hiking trail "Geestweg". We cross the motorway once more and a little later turn left into the "Blanken Schlatt". At the fork where the road "Vierte" turns diagonally right, we leave the "Blanken Schlatt" behind us and walk straight ahead until the fork to the right into the road "Sandpfänder", which takes us back to Sage. There it turns into the street Im Sande, at the end of which is our starting point.

title: Planet path
short_description: The Planet Trail on the Uetliberg is easily accessible from Zurich and offers an educational and fun route that appeals to hikers of all ages.
long_description:
On a path leading from the Uetliberg station to Felsenegg, visitors can walk through a model of the solar system.

Planets visited are Mercury, Venus, Jupiter and other planets. In Felsenegg you take a gondola through the Sihltal valley to Adliswil.

images.caption: Viewpoint on the Uetliberg in Zurich

title: Alzey Round
short_description: This difficult Nordic walking tour opens up several magnificent panoramas of the town of Alzey.
long_description:
We start at the Alzey reservoir, which we walk almost completely around. Then we walk on a quite varied route up into the vineyards, in the direction of Heimersheim.
On reaching the top, we enjoy the magnificent view of the Alzey district of Heimerheim. We walk further along the Engbach and now already begin the way back. It leads over the Heimerheimer Berg, which again reveals a fantastic panorama to us. From up here we can see Alzey Castle, St. Nicholas Church and the Wartberg Tower.

images.caption: We also walk through some vineyards.

title: Three Castles Hike around Riedenburg in the Altmühl Valley
short_description: This short hike takes us to the three castles in Riedberg in the Altmühltal. From the Tachenstein ruin we go to the Rosenburg with its museum and falconry and on to the Rabenstein ruin. Boards along the way inform us about the history of the region.
long_description:
This tour starts in the climatic health resort of Riedenburg, the three-castle town in the Altmühltal Nature Park.
On a deciduous forest path close to the town, partly with steps, short steep sections, but with fantastic panoramic views, the tour leads to the three castles of Tachenstein, Rosenburg and Rabenstein. Rosenburg Castle has a museum and a falconry that is well worth a visit.

title: Brecherspitz Freudenreich Alm loop
short_description: Oma Helga - Brecherspitz - Brecherspitz Vorgipfel (Brecherspitz Wintergipfel) - Birkenstein - St. Leonhard - SCA

title: The Brocken in view - snowshoe hike around the Ebersberg mountain
short_description: This circular hike in the Upper Harz takes you around the wintry Ebersberg. The tour provides some views worth seeing of the surrounding peaks such as the striking Brocken.
long_description: &Over a distance of 10 km, the snowshoe hike takes us around the Ebersberg. We will be walking on predominantly flat terrain, which is why the tour is ideally suited as a family excursion in the wintry Harz mountains. In particular, the fact that we have the highest mountains in the region, such as the Wurmberg and the Brocken, in view along the route makes the tour a special highlight. On the Ebersberg road, the route is shared with groomed cross-country ski trails.

images.caption: Wanderung im Harz mit Blick auf den Brocken

title: Walking to the lion fountain near Bad Rippoldsau
short_description: This medium-difficulty trail begins not far from Bad Rippoldsau. It runs entirely in the forest, so it is also suitable for training in summer.
long_description: Our Nordic walking tour begins at the Teuchelwald car park (red marking). First it leads us straight ahead into the forest and we reach a crossroads. The trail leads sharply down to the right and crosses another intersection downwards. At the bottom of the road, we follow a driveway on the left that leads to the open-air swimming pool. We see the Langenwaldersee lake to our right and continue straight ahead above it on the Teuchelweg path. This leads you past a pulse measuring station, the Löwenbrunnen (lion fountain) and a sunken path and up to a larger road, where you turn left. From this road we turn left again in the direction of Agnesruhe. We go downhill to a crossroads, which we cross straight on. At the next fork, we choose the left path. We already know the next fork from the beginning of our tour. Back to the car park, we take the path that leads slightly uphill to the right and arrive back at our starting point.

images.caption: A pulse measuring station in idyllic surroundings can also be found on our tour.
Pure nature: We pass through deep forest during our tour.

title: Illerdamm route
short_description:
A beautiful short Nordic walking route with a wonderful view of the Oberstdorf mountains and the Illerauen
.
long_description:
From the car park, we walk along the bridge in the direction of Sigishofen. After the bridge, we turn left onto the field path.
Here we go along the Illerdam in a semi-curve for a very long time. To the left of us the Iller river splashes, to the right of us meadows stretch out.
We have the opportunity to take a break at one of the many benches. We can also head off in the direction of the Iller and reach large gravel pits.
We have the opportunity to take a break at one of the many benches.

title: Walking around Spielberg
short_description: This easy tour, well suited for beginners, takes you into the valley of the Zinsbach. You walk on a well-signposted circular route along forest paths and trails as well as asphalted roads.
long_description: We start our easy Nordic walking tour, an ideal beginner's tour, at the Spielberg town hall. After a short warm-up phase, we keep to the left and follow the signs with the "5" on the main road out of town in the direction of the B28, which we cross underneath. Turn right and walk downhill through the forest into the Zinsbach valley. We walk along wide, relatively flat forest paths above the stream. Soon, we take a path that becomes narrower and narrower, with a natural surface, which leads us slightly uphill away from the stream. Shortly before the Reesenmühle, we reach the steep access road, which we follow. After checking our circulation and doing some strengthening exercises, we pass the sports field on our right and come to the B28. On a level path we walk back to Spielberg on the left. At our end point, the town hall, we check our values again and relax with some loosening exercises.

images.caption: Wonderful impressions of nature are guaranteed in the Zinsbach Valley.
The Zinsbach Valley is a dream for hikers and walkers.

title: Le Chasseron
long_description:
The wild gorge "Poëta-Raisse" is reached from Môtiers after about an hour's walk along the two streams "Le Breuil" and "Le Bied". It is not without difficulties in winter, because the bridges, stairs and wire ropes are either iced over or disappear in the snow. If conditions are too difficult, it is advisable to choose one of the two ascent options. The tour continues through the Bois de la Vaux and leads in a south-westerly direction, climbing steadily to the ridge path of the Chasseron. The view from this rocky pulpit of the Alpine chain, Lake Neuchâtel and the Chasseral massif is magnificent.
The descent is over the pass and the ski area to Sainte-Croix. The village was long active in precision mechanics (typewriters, projectors, gramophones ). The village is world-famous for its music boxes and music automatons. Thanks to its sun terrace, Sainte-Croix is a popular high-altitude and holiday resort.

title: Paris-London, the Green Avenue - Major cycle route
short_description: The Green Avenue Paris-London itinerary is the result of a beautiful project, that of linking the two emblematic capitals by bicycle paths and small roads. It was officially inaugurated in 2012 on the occasion of the London Olympic Games.
long_description:
In France, 2 itineraries are proposed, via the French Vexin and Gisors on the one hand, and via the Oise valley on the other. It is this 2nd itinerary, made up of bucolic landscapes and historical discoveries, that we describe here.
Beware however, if joining the 2 capitals à vélo is a superb experience, the route is not yet all done à at the level of the « Loire à Vélo » in terms of organisation. But the adventure is well worth the effort.

title: Trail in the Muritiba (Serrano) Municipal Park in Lençóis
short_description: The Muritiba Park is just a few minutes from the centre of Lençóis, in the Chapada Diamantina. Explore in this trail millenary geological formations, waterfalls and natural pools, and contemplate a beautiful view of the city.
long_description: On this trail you will have the opportunity to stroll through the historic centre of Lençóis and get to know the main attractions of the Muritiba Municipal Park: the rapids of the Serrano, which offer several natural whirlpools and a beautiful view of the city, especially at sunset; the impressive rocks of the Salatilde;There are also the impressive rocks in the Salatilde; the Coloured Sands, where the local people used to extract coloured sand to use in different types of dyeing and handicrafts and the great places to bathe in the Halley Pool, the Primavera Waterfall and the Cachoeirinha.

title: Chapel circuit hike: South of Appenzell
Easy trekking on Kermen Hill
short_description: An easy trek on the Kermen Hill is an almost weekly habit for the locals in Brașov, especially those residing in Valea Cetății. Climbing the Kermen segment is part of the many easy hikes to try in Brasov, or in the Postavaru Massif, respectively.
long_description:
Mirroring the less touristy side of Mount Tâmpa, the Kermen Hill makes the transition from Valea Cetății (Răcădău) to Postăvaru. Thus, this hill leads either up or down to/from the Postavaru cabin & peak.
If you choose to walk circularly, the path starts at one end of the neighborhood and ends at another. It comes rather as a wide and relaxing walk through the forest, with no panoramas or other spectacular views.
The walk does not pose technical or access problems and is marked for the most part. The segment from Valea Cetății to/from the main path - the variant followed here - is unmarked, and is quite difficult to distinguish as a path that goes up / down steeply.

images.caption: Marked path leading to Postăvaru Peak

title: Moos circular trail near Sonthofen
short_description: From Muderbolz we hike to Tiefenberger Moos and back.
long_description: The circular trail 20 leads from Muderbolz, past the Sonnenalp Hotel to Tiefenberg in the Tiefenberger Moos. Peat was cut here 50 years ago and used as fuel. Individual peat diggings can still be seen. The path leads through the unique natural beauty of a moor. Passing the golf course, you return to Muderbolz.

images.caption: On our way we enjoy the landscape.

title: From Schmannewitz to Reudlitz
short_description: This tour takes us through a lot of forest to Reudlitz.
long_description: We start our hike in Schmannewitz at the Mühlgraben, from where we walk along the Alter Teichweg to Torgauer Straße. We follow this road for a while until we reach the forester's lodge and turn off in the direction of Dalequelle to the Jägereiche. From here we continue on the G path to Reudnitz. The path here takes us past the tobacco pine. The Waldschänke Reudnitz offers us the opportunity to stop for refreshments. From Reudnitz we choose the M-path and walk in the direction of Lattenberg to the Käthe-Kollwitz-Hütte. This path takes us to the Pumpenteich pond and the Schmannwitz forest pool. We continue on the Buchaer Straße to the forester's lodge and back to our starting point.

title: On the Brotjacklriegel
short_description: A short but steep hike brings us to the lookout tower on the Brotjacklriegel.
long_description: Short but steep tour to Brotjacklriegel past the information boards on nature around the mountain.

images.caption: At 127 m, the transmission mast is the highest of the Bavarian Broadcasting Corporation.
The observation tower offers a unique panoramic view.

title: A trip to the Lotenbach-Klamm
short_description: A relatively short and easy trip, rich in water and views in the Lotenbach-Klamm gorge in the southwest of the Black Forest.
long_description:
A linear and easy hiking trail about one and a half kilometers long in the Lotenbach-Klam gorge next to waterfalls, water reservoirs and running water. The trip includes walking on hanging wooden bridges as well as climbing stairs. A short trip but full of nature and landscapes.
Entrance to the gorge is free and can be visited all year round depending on the prevailing weather conditions. You can walk there with children, but due to the stairs, the route is not fully accessible for strollers.
The distance and walking time shown are for one direction, at the end of the route you must retrace your steps back to the starting point.

title: Three Lakes Tour
short_description: Varied and interesting hike with wonderful views of the Alps.
long_description:
This hike starts in Nussbaumen, which you can reach by post bus from Frauenfeld. The village with its beautiful timber-framed houses is picturesquely situated on a sunny terrace. From there you descend to the lakes. Lakes Nussbaumer, Hüttwiler and Hasensee together form a natural landscape with something to discover in every season. In summer they also invite you to swim. Then continue in the direction of Uerschhausen and soon reach Trüttlikon. Between the last buildings, turn right off the main road and after a slight incline you reach a ridge. The path now leads down to the vineyard, from there keep left and walk along the upper edge of the vineyard. On a clear day you have a wonderful view of the Alps. Shortly before Iselisberg you descend into the vineyard and cross the Uesslingen-Iselisberg road, which you follow to the Uesslingen-Buch road. Here you follow the main road to Uesslingen for about 200 m and turn left into the forest at the next footpath. After crossing the forest, you stand in front of the west portal of Ittingen Charterhouse. From Warth it is about 1 hour's walk across the Thur and along the Murg river to Frauenfeld.

.

title: From Thalkirchdorf to the Salmaser Höhe
short_description: This scenic hike takes us from Thalkirchdorf to the Salmaser Höhe. There, at an altitude of 1254 m, we are rewarded with magnificent views.
long_description: This beautiful hike takes us from Thalkirchdorf to the Salmaser Höhe. On narrow hiking trails we first pass the Wannerles Alpe and the Micheles Alpe before we reach the highest point. At an altitude of 1254 m, we have a magnificent panoramic view of the Constance Valley, the Nagelfluhkette Nature Park and the Alpsee from the Salmaser Hütte. Surrounded by lush alpine meadows, we finally descend to Salmas. There we follow the tracks to Wiesemannsdorf. From there we return to the starting point on familiar paths.

title: Koblenz-Remstecken: Jogging circuit
short_description: Great entertaining and varied jogging tour on the Remstecken near Koblenz

title: Himmelreichweg Bad Kösen
short_description: Our circular walk leads from Bad Kösen to Rudelsburg Castle, well-known to students, and to Saaleck Castle.
long_description:
We start our tour at the Ringhotel "Courageous Knight" and walk under the double-span artificial rods past the weir to the Loreleypromenade. Now we walk along the Saale for a bit until we reach the Johannisquelle. Here we turn right towards the Saaleauen and continue to the campsite. Before the campsite, we turn left into the forest. The path leads us on steps in the direction of Rudelsburg. But first we reach a memorial to the fallen, the "Löwendenkmal". We now walk along a narrow path parallel to the road to the Rudelsburg. After visiting it, we fortify ourselves with a cold beer.  As the old student song says: "The Rudelsburg, that's a place to rave and to drink."
The castle road leads us on to Saaleck Castle, which is also worth a visit. Alternatively, we can choose a small path instead of the asphalt road. To do this, we cross the bridge, then turn left and follow the lower hiking trail immediately to the right (signage: Saaleck). This way we also reach the tarred road just before the castle.
For the way back, we follow the castle road further through the village of Saaleck and left across the Saale. After crossing the river, we turn right to Stendorf. We cross the small village and follow Bergstraße and Waldstraße back towards Bad Kösen, stay on Waldstraße until we meet the Saale and walk left on Thüringer Straße towards Lengefeld. At the level crossing, we follow the course of the Saale on the right and arrive at the bridge over the Saale on Rudelsburgpromenade and along the tracks on Bahnhofstraße. Now we cross the river again and get back to our starting point.

title: Buffalora - Val Mora - Sta. Maria
short_description: This hike leads through one of the most beautiful areas of the Val Müstairs.
long_description:
The Val Mora and the Val Vau are among the most pristine areas of the region, the mixture of wide valley and rugged mountains is äusely impressive.
The trail begins at the border to the Swiss National Park at the Buffalora inn. Past the Buffalora Alp, we climb up to the Jufplaun plain. The gravel path leads us level to slightly ascending to the crossing to Val Mora. Here a wonderful panorama opens up towards Italy. A steep, stony path leads us down into Val Mora, an unspoilt mountain valley with old pine trees, visited only by hikers and bikers. First through rocks, then on comfortable forest roads with views of the surrounding peaks and waterfalls, we hike through this beautiful valley. At Döss Radond (2234 m ü. M.) is the watershed, on one side the water flows through Val Mora into the Livigno reservoir, on the other side through Val Vau into Val Müstair. Now we start the descent. Passing Alp Praveder with its impressive rockfall area, we reach Alp Clastras. Both alps belong to the Müstair monastery. At Tschuccai the path branches off. We keep to the right and after some time reach Sta. Maria via the hiking trail.

title: Vineyard
short_description: The hike takes you from Frauenfeld railway station in an easterly direction;
long_description:
A few steps after the station, you pass the underpass of the SBB line. From there you walk along the left bank of the Murg over the Thurebene to the Rohrerbrücke, then follow the signs to Ittingen Charterhouse. The hiking trail leads in a westerly direction to the Bärlingerhof and to Iselisberg. On the hike between Iselisberg and Niederneunforn you can enjoy a unique view of the Thur valley and the distant Alps. There are several beautiful vineyards to admire in this vineyard area.
From Niederneunforn the path leads to the Thur dam, which you follow upstream on the southern side towards Roherbrücke.

title: From Bad Hindelang to Oberjoch
short_description: On this hike to Germany­s highest mountain village, we pass the romantic Wildbach­tobel and enjoy imposing views of Bad Hindelang and the mountains of the Hörnerkette from the Kanzel vantage point.
long_description: We hike through the impressive Wildbachtobel to Oberjoch. In Germany's highest mountain village, the Hochmoor swimming pool and various huts and restaurants invite you to relax in summer. On the Rückweg (hiking trail) we experience magnificent views of Bad Hindelang, Sonthofen and the mountains of the Hörnerkette from the Kanzel vantage point.

title: Drongengoed forest walking route
short_description: This walk is about 14 kilometres and takes 3.5 hours.
long_description:
During this walking route, you walk through the Drongengoedbos. At 750 hectares, this forest is the largest forest in East Flanders. The largest part of this forest used to consist of heathland and fens. Nowadays, it is mainly woods with occasional patches of heathland. The nature reserve is protected and people are working hard to restore it.
During your walk, you will also pass Prinsenveld castle. The beginning of this castle was built in 1846. After that, it was expanded twice more into the building that stands today.

title: GR 249. Stage 01: Málaga - Rincón de la Victoria (ID 23534349)
short_description: The first stage of the Gran Senda de Málaga heads east along the coastline towards the Axarquía region. It is an easy route due to its length but, above all, because of the few slopes that are crossed.
long_description:
To connect the western part of the capital of Málaga and Cala del Moral, in the Rincón de la Victoria, you have to describe a gentle arc to the north and east following the outlines of the Ensenada de Málaga and, of course, cross the entire urban area mainly by promenades. Gradually you pass the different coastal districts of Malaga from the most central to El Palo, traditional places of beach bars and restaurants with the well-known espeteros.
The Alleyway of the Victoria is the main road through the city centre.
The Carretera de Almería marks the end of this model of coastal landscape with the Puerto del Candado, some sea cliffs (which the road crosses by means of a tunnel) and the impressive Cementera de la Araña. The final part of the route takes in the beautiful sandy coves of Peñón del Cuervo, while the highest point is a little further on at Torre Vigía de las Palomas, at an altitude of 23 metres.
The route continues alongside the Nacional 340, on the right-hand verge, and ends next to the limestone cliffs of Cala del Moral at the little bridge that allows you to cross the Arroyo Totalán, which is the border between the municipalities of Málaga and Rincón de la Victoria, without any problems.
The route continues along the right-hand verge of the Nacional 340.
The best
The GR-249 offers as a start the possibility of covering practically the entire coastal strip of the capital. After a long history of neglect, the 21st-century Málaga has begun the millennium by opening up to the Mediterranean Sea, which has always given it its meaning as a city.
Numerous new developments bear witness to this new approach in the Port area, which has of course generated lengthy debates and which the trail covers one by one. Meanwhile, the Guadalmedina River continues to wait its turn, reclaiming its rightful role as the city's other great backbone.
The territorial model of this part of the western coast of Málagacuenta has many years of adjustments, so that it preserves part of the fishing idiosyncrasy that is its raison d'être while adapting to the new times. The traveller will contemplate emblematic places such as the Port and its Farola, the beaches of La Malagueta, La Caleta, Pedregalejo and El Palo and the numerous beach bars that at the beginning of this century are also finding their own place and aesthetics.
The last part of the journey will take you to the last part of the coast.
The last part of the route holds a series of surprises of different kinds, from enclaves of privileged nature with exclusive botanical species to perfectly preserved medieval watchtowers, passing through factory installations on the beach or secluded coves with evocative landscapes. A whole compendium in little more than 15 kilometres, in short, of the evolution of the Costa del Sol, all the way to the Rincón de la Victoria.

title: The Bay of Canche
short_description: The route takes in a fascinating variety of scenery, offering a bewitching alternation between vast stretches of fine sandy beach, wooded dunes, mollières (salt meadows) sheltering the picturesque huts of water game hunters, and the elegant seaside architecture that characterises the resort of Le Mans.mollières (salt meadows), home to the picturesque huts of waterfowl hunters, and the elegant seaside architecture that characterises the resort of Le Touquet.
long_description: This visual diversity creates an immersive experience where each stage reveals a unique aspect of the surrounding nature, from the tranquil shores to the unspoilt ecosystems of the wetlands, finally blending harmoniously with the coastal aesthetic of the famous seaside resort of Le Touquet.This visual diversity creates an immersive experience where each stage reveals a unique aspect of the surrounding nature, from tranquil shores to unspoilt wetland ecosystems, finally blending seamlessly with the coastal aesthetic of the famous seaside resort of Le Touquet.

title: Lü - Süsom Givè
short_description: From Lü the trail leads through sparse larch forest to Alp Champatsch.
long_description:
The restaurant «La Posa» on Alp Champatsch serves specialities from the region. Strengthened, we can continue the two-hour panoramic hike from Alp Champatsch to Süsom Givè. We now walk along the Senda Val Müstair, a hiking trail that takes us through enchanting areas and high, quiet plains. Various alpine flowers grow here, such as gentian, heather, alpine roses or anemones. Before we reach Alp da Munt, a wonderful view opens up at Lai da Juata into the Münstertal.
After a break at Alp da Munt, we continue our hike and follow the signposts towards Ofenpass. We hike through the Plaun da l'Aua. The last 20 minutes are on a narrow path that winds up and down through a forest of trees. We finish our hike at the Ofenpasshöhe «Süsom Givè». From here, the post bus will take us back to the valley or, if you wish, you can spend the night in a hotel or in the tourist camp on the Ofen Pass.

title: Dolomites high trail 5
short_description: Lonely traverse of the eastern Dolomites from Sesto to Pieve di Cadore
long_description: The Dolomites High-Altitude Trail No. 5, also known as the Titian High-Altitude Trail, is a challenge for persevering, experienced and climbing-skilled mountaineers. The entire undertaking is higher in difficulty than the high-altitude trails 1-4 and requires at least ten days of hiking. Starting in Sesto, you first hike through the Sesto Dolomites in a southerly direction. After the intermediate descent to Auronzo di Cadore, the technically more demanding crossing of the Marmarole massif from east to west follows. The last section, like the high trail no. 4 from Riugio San Marco, runs south-eastwards through the Antelao Group into the Piave Valley. The traverse offers both panoramic, comfortable high-altitude hikes and exposed climbs such as the Sentiero degli Alpini, the Strada Sanmarchi, the Sentiero attrezzato Adriano Cipriano and the Via ferrata del Cadorin. When crossing the Marmarole group, expect at least one night in a bivouac on the section between the Rifugio Chiggiato and the next managed refuge, the Rifugio San Marco. The high-level trail is marked with a red-white-red marking and a five in a red triangle.

title: Von Alpe Eschbach zur Rappenseehütte
short_description:
Von der Alpe Eschbach über die Enzian- und Rappenseehütte (mögliche Übernachtung) zurück über den Eselsweg zur Schwarzhütte und retour zur Alpe Eschbach.
Translate to English
long_description:
Die Wanderung beginnt an der Alpe Eschbach, einem idyllischen Ausgangspunkt im Allgäu. Von dort aus führt der Weg durch grüne Wiesen und Wälder zur Enzianhütte auf 1.804 Metern. Diese urige Hütte lädt mit regionalen Köstlichkeiten und einem herrlichen Bergblick zu einer Pause ein.
Weiter geht es über steile Pfade in alpines Gelände zur Rappenseehütte auf 2.091 Metern. Umgeben von den Allgäuer Alpen und am malerischen Rappensee gelegen, ist sie eine der größten Hütten der Region. Hier genießt man das Panorama und die Ruhe des Bergsees.
Für den Rückweg führt die Route über den historischen Eselsweg, der landschaftlich reizvoll und weniger frequentiert ist. Der Abstieg geht weiter zur Schwarzhütte, die inmitten von Wäldern zur letzten Rast einlädt. Von dort aus geht es über den Fahrweg zurück Richtung Sennalpe Eschbach und schließt die Tour in einer beeindruckenden Naturkulisse ab. Dieser Fahrweg ist ein beliebter Fahrradweg der entpsrechend hoch frequentiert ist.

title: Great Chulchinsky Waterfall or Uchar.
short_description: The great Chulchinsky Waterfall, or Uchar in the Altai language, means "flying" or "impregnable". The waterfall is located in the Altai Republic on the territory of the Altai Reserve.
long_description:
Route thread: Gorno-Altaysk - Artybash - the mouth of the river. Chulyshman - Balykcha - Koo - the mouth of the river. Chulcha.
  The distance from Gorno-Altaysk to the beginning of the trail is about 490 km. The hiking part of the route begins at the mouth of the Chulcha River. It is necessary to cross the Chulyshman River by boat. This service is provided by local residents. Along the Chulcha River, a hiking trail leads to the Uchar waterfall. The hiking route is about 8 km long and takes about 4 hours.
  The trail is offered by residents.
  In 2011, the Association of Travel Agents included the Uchar Waterfall in the rating of "5 hard-to-reach sights of the Russian Federation". Moreover, it is the youngest masterpiece of the Altai Mountains and the largest waterfall on the continent. Because the waterfall cascades and the water flows down the boulders, it is also called a water slide. The height of the waterfall reaches more than 160 metres.

title: Wimpole Estate Walk
short_description: Leisurely walk around the front and west side of .
long_description: Leisurely walk around the front and west side of Wimpole Estate. Mostly paved trail, with unmarked grass paths towards the end of the route. A few inclines, but lots of areas to stop and take in the views and have some water.

title: Architectural circular route to the Brother Klaus Chapel near Bad Münstereifel
short_description: During this short tour, we visit the Bruder Klaus Chapel near Wachendorf in the Eifel, designed by star architect Peter Zumthor.
long_description: Anyone interested in modern architecture will be thrilled by this round: even from a distance, the building, reminiscent of a concrete silo, catches the eye. A local farmer donated the chapel, which was designed by star architect Peter Zumthor - without a fee. Only inside does the sacred purpose of the building become clear. From the outside, only a small cross above the entrance door reminds us of the purpose of the 12-metre-high building. The chapel is dedicated to Brother Klaus, Saint Nicholas of the Flüe. 112 tree trunks from the Bad Münstereifel forest were felled for the chapel's interior framework. These formed a tent-like space, which was then to serve as a kind of formwork for many layers of concrete. The concrete consists of a mixture of reddish sand and river gravel, as found in the surrounding area. A fire that burned inside the chapel for three weeks left behind the now imposing interior. The traces of the logs form the interior walls and the pungent smell of burnt wood will probably be noticeable for a while. A roof is missing and so all four elements fire, water, earth and air can be united there, because on the floor, which is made of a lead-tin mixture, water now collects when it rains and forms puddles. The use of lead is meant to remind us of the lead mining town of Mechernich. The connecting holes in the formwork for the concrete, which were created after the chapel was burnt out, are now filled with 300 hemispheres of glass. In this way, a unique atmosphere is created inside the chapel.

images.caption: The Brother Klaus Chapel from the north.

title: Kust till Kustleden - from Koarp to Brammarp
short_description: The thirteenth stage of the Kust till Kustleden leads from the Koarp campsite through extensive forest and marshland to the Brammarp campsite. The trail here is identical to Hallandsleden.
long_description: This stage leads almost exclusively through dense forests and across marshy meadows. The wide plains were largely left to themselves after the decline of medieval settlements, and so many interesting biotopes with remarkable flora and fauna were able to form.

title: From the Riedberg Pass to the mystical limestone cliffs of the Besler
short_description: A quick and spectacular arm tour through the Allgäu Alps
long_description: In the southern tip of Germany, we managed to take a hike in the Alps in what could hardly be described as summer weather. From the car you can see that you're entering a picturesque part of the Oberallgäu, because you can't miss these imposing vertical rock faces, and I dare say it would be a shame to miss them. Even though the mountain is covered in clouds again and again, it is still beautiful and even a little mystical in this weather. So we jumped out of the car and headed for the limestone cliff of Besler, 1679 metres high. From here we hoped to head east all the way to the Breitach valley, which eventually failed due to clouds. The view below us is only glimpsed for a few moments. If the views had been better and we hadn't been soaked to the skin, we would certainly have climbed the Beslerkopf, which is lower than Besler, and the Beslergrat, which can also be climbed with a detour. Our route took us over concrete, dirt tracks and oddly shaped limestone, surrounded by gravity-defying cows and donkeys at will. The climb was manageable, but in wet weather it would have been more stable with poles, as you can slide here and there on the limestone. Refreshments were available at the seasonally open alp at the beginning and end of the hike. Overall, we would recommend it to everyone, as it is beautiful in rain and sunshine.

title: Cape Blanc Nez
short_description: A not-to-be-missed hike in the Pas-de-Calais, the natural site of Cap Blanc Nez is truly magnificent: a series of steep, vertiginous cliffs made of chalk that gives it its characteristic white colour.
long_description:
The walk, which has no major difficulties, starts at Escales, skirting the cliffs above, offering a view of the English coastline on a clear day, then overlooks Sangatte before returning to the starting point through the countryside.
Several Second World War relics dot the route, including the Lindemann MKB Battery.

title: देवलसारी - नाग टिब्बा ट्रैक
short_description: टिहरी ज़िले के देवलसारी गाँव से नाग टिब्बा तक जाने वाला यह ट्रैक मार्ग देवदार के पेड़ों औ र हरे भरे घास के मैदानों से भरी हुई एक बहुत सुन्दर नेचर ट्रेल ह ै।
long_description:
ब्रिटिश शासन के दौरान देवलसारी, अंग्रेज़ो का एक प्रसिद्ध विश्राम स्थल था जैसा की साल 1935 में अंग्रेजों द्वारा बनाये गए सुसज्जित फॉरेस्ट रेस्टहाउस से पता चलता है। मसूरी और धनौल्टी में अच्छी सड़के और बेहतर बुनियादी सुविधाएँ आने के कारण देवलसारी गाँव क्षेत्र धीरे-धीरे आम पर्यटक की नजरों से ओझल सा हो गया। लेकिन मसूरी, देहरादून, और आसपास के वर्ल्ड क्लास स्कूलों के सैकड़ों छात्रों के लिए, देवलसारी सालों-साल से एक महत्वपूर्ण अवकाश स्थान रहा है। आज भी कान्वेंट स्कूलों के छात्रों में देवलसारी के स्वास्थ्यप्रद और शांत वातावरण में शिविर लगाने और आउटिंग करने की परंपरा है।
देवलसारी-नागटिब्बा हाइक अपने लोकप्रिय जुड़वाँ मार्ग पंतवाड़ी-नागटिब्बा हाइक से भी ज्यादा खूबसूरत है। हाइकर्स सात किलोमीटर लम्बी यात्रा के दौरान रंगीन तितलियों, सुन्दर चिड़ियों, भौंकने वाले हिरणों, और गिलहरियों के अलावा कई फूलों की प्रजातियों, देवदार के जंगलों और विशाल घास के मैदानों की सुंदरता से मंत्रमुग्ध हो जाते हैं। रास्ते में भगवान शिव को समर्पित एक प्राचीन और सुंदर मंदिर भी आता है जिसे कोनेश्वर महादेव कहते हैं।
टूरिस्ट और नेचर प्रेमियों को आकर्षित करने वाली सभी खूबियां होने के बावजूद अभी तक देवलसारी अपनी पहचान नहीं बना पाया है हालाँकि यह अनुभवी हाइकर्स के बीच बहुत प्रसिद्ध है। हाल फिलहाल वन विभाग ने इस इलाके की क्षमता को महसूस किया है और जापान इंटरनेशनल कोऑपरेशन एजेंसी की मदद से इसे एक प्रमुख इको-टूरिज्म गंतव्य के रूप में विकसित करने की प्रक्रिया में है। इस परियोजना के तहत देवलसारी के ब्रिटिश वन विश्राम गृह को अपग्रेड किया जाएगा। नाग टिब्बा तक ट्रैकिंग के लिए देवलसारी की बेस कैंप के रूप में भी मार्केटिंग की जाएगी और स्थानीय निवासियों को होम-स्टे बनाने के लिए वित्तीय मदद, और गाइड ट्रेनिंग भी दी जाएगी।

title: Best of Zugerberg
short_description: This hike takes you through the beautiful high moors of the Zugerberg and promises a unique panorama as far as the Bernese Alps.
long_description:
Get away from it all! You can get away from the hectic town centre by bus and funicular, and be in pure countryside in under 30 minutes! The Zugerberg is the perfect recreation area in Zugerland. This hike takes you through the wonderful high moorland of the Zugerberg and offers unique panoramic views as far as the Bernese Alps.

Zugerberg top station - direction Walchwil - Altenboden - chellenweid - over Ober-Horbach to the Schnuristein - continue at the same height to Lienisberg and Tossetschwändi - turn right down over Schwändeli to Gibel - sharp ascent to Freudenberg - walk along the road to Walchwil railway station (altitude difference 544 metres downhill)

- Adventure Playground Schattwäldli

title: कुलेम स्टेशन से दूधसागर झरने तक हाईक
short_description: भारत के गोवा राज्य में स्थित दूधसागर जलप्रपात एक शानदार चार स्तरीय झरना ह ै। इस तक आने के लिए हाइकिंग करना टूरिस्टों की सबसे पसंदीदा गतिविधियों म ें है।
long_description:
इस झरने का देखने से छलकते हुए दूध सा आभास होता है, इसलिए इसका नाम दूधसागर पड़ा जिसका अर्थ है दूध का समुद्र। गोवा में भगवान महावीर अभयारण्य और मोल्लेम राष्ट्रीय उद्यान के अंदर स्थित यह झरना मांडवी नदी समुद्र में मिलने से पहले बनता है। 1017 फीट की ऊंचाई और 100 फीट की औसत चौड़ाई के साथ यह भारत का तीसरा सबसे ऊंचा झरना है।
गर्मियों में यह झरना उतना प्रभावशाली नहीं लगता है क्योंकि तब मांडवी नदी में गर्मियों के दौरान पानी काफी कम हो जाता है, लेकिन मानसून के मौसम में लगातार होती बारिश से नदी का जलस्तर बहुत बढ़ जाता है और झरना अपने पूरे जोश में आ जा जाता है। मानसून और उसके तुरंत बाद झरने की सुंदरता देखते ही बनती है।
यहाँ तक आने के लिए कई अच्छे नेचर ट्रेल, पगडंडियां, और हाइकिंग मार्ग मौजूद हैं। कुलेम रेलवे स्टेशन से एक बहुत ही सुन्दर ट्रैकिंग मार्ग सीधे झरने तक आता है। यह मार्ग अच्छी तरह से साइन-पोस्टेड है और इसका रखरखाव भी अच्छा है इसलिए टूरिस्ट इस में ट्रैक करना पसंद करते हैं।
संरक्षित इलाके में होने की वजह से झरने के आसपास का क्षेत्र जैव विविधता वाले हरभरे जंगलों से घिरा हुआ है। यह जंगल कई किस्म के वनस्पति और पशुओं का घर है। झरने के तल पर नीले-हरे पानी का एक सुंदर स्वच्छ तालाब है। पर्यटक इस तालाब में जल क्रीड़ाएं और तैरने के लिए आते हैं। झरने के पास में ही कुछ छोटे घरेलू रेस्त्रां भी हैं जो घर का बना हुआ स्वादिष्ट स्थानीय भोजन गरमागरम उपलब्ध करते हैं।

title: Bohusleden - Section 10 - Glimmingen to Metsjö
short_description: The tenth stage of the Bohusleden leads from Glimmingen through a popular hiking area to Metsjö See.
long_description: This stage reveals the full beauty of the southern Swedish landscape. Dark forests, glistening lakes and idyllic moors are just as much a part of the route as the scattered mussel beds that bear witness to the fact that the area was once flooded by the Baltic Sea. In addition, the landscape is strongly marked by the inland ice and the terrain is correspondingly hilly. Through a quiet forest area we finally reach a busy network of hiking trails in the Herrestadsfjället nature reserve, where we meet many joggers, hikers and anglers, especially in the summer months.

title: SAN LAZARO DE ESCOMARCA: CERRO TRES VENTANAS
short_description: SAN LAZARO DE ESCOMARCA: CERRO TRES VENTANAS
long_description:
Ruta dominical realizada con los amigos del Team Wayra. Se inicia desde el Pueblo de San Lázaro de Escomarca. Para llegar al pueblo, no es recurrente el traslado de colectivos o buses. La opción más viable es ir en movilidad propia. La caminata en sí no representa dificultad técnica. Basta con un buen mapa o GPS, siendo lo ideal. La posible dificultad que se pueda presentar son las lluvias y/o granizos, que son recurrentes e impredecibles en las zonas sierra del país. Siempre recomendable llevar buen impermeable y botas de trekking, puesto que los senderos se llenan de mucho barro rápidamente al llover.
En el presente trayecto, se tomo un buen tiempo dentro de las cuevas hasta que termine de llover y granizar, y así comenzar un retorno más rápido y seguro.Las movilidades pueden llegar al pueblo tanto por la ruta Cieneguilla - Antioquía - Escomarca o por la ruta panamericana sur que sale desde Chilca. Ambos trayectos tienen muy bellas panorámicas de la zona.Si se regresa por la tarde/noche hacia Lima tener mucha precaución puesto que buena parte de la trocha vehicular está llena de neblina y esto sumado a que la trocha se encuentra llena de barro por las lluvias, hacen que el recorrido en movilidad sea dificultoso.

title: Altenberg Cathedral and Quarry
short_description: On this short hike we experience a sacred and a prophane testimony of the Middle Ages.
long_description: Altenberg is the old seat of the Counts of Berg. In the course of their reign, they expanded the area around their residence that we know today as "Bergisches Land". We can still see the High Gothic cathedral, begun in 1259, but it was never the seat of a bishop. The hike gives us an impression of the place, but also takes us through the quiet forest and to a quarry from the Middle Ages.

title: Church hike around Stadtsteinach
short_description: This hike takes us to Christian signs in the town and the surrounding area of Stadtsteinach.
long_description:
A brochure about the Marterl-Rundwanderweg with a detailed description of the individual description of the individual Christian waymarkers is available from the The trail takes us through Stadtsteinach and the surrounding area. Along the way, we will pass various ecclesiastical testimonies, including marteles, chapels and wayside crosses.
We can stop for refreshments at the Frankenwald inn.

title: Dolomites High Altitude Trail 2
short_description: Scenic, impressive high-altitude hike through the western Dolomites from Bressanone in the Valle Isarco to Feltre in the province of Belluno.
long_description: The Dolomites High Altitude Trail 2 represents a crossing of the Dolomites from north to south. From the Plose Group we start our way into the Dolomite area, where we hike through the Geisler and Puez Groups before turning our attention to the magnificent Sella Plateau. Grandiose landscapes also await us on the Bindelweg trail, after which we set off on the impressive, high-alpine traverse of the Marmolada glacier. We continue into the realm of the Pala Group with fascinating rock sceneries. Finally, the lesser known, but no less rich in breathtaking views, Feltriner Dolomiten await us. Technically, the hike is one of the easier Dolomite high-altitude trails, but the sometimes long stages are demanding in terms of fitness. Sufficient climbing experience is necessary for the frequent climbing sections, and ice skills are also required for the traverse of the Marmolada-Scharte. You should plan about two weeks for the ascent. The route is marked red-white-red and with the number 2 in a triangle.

title: Lorze Industry Trail
long_description:
Commercial life and the factories that were built to meet the industrial needs of the area, characterise the lives and landscape of a region over a long period. They become part of the regional culture and in order to preserve this cultural heritage and to increase people's awareness, the Lorze Industry Trail was created in 1995 and maintained by the association of the same name. The trail is over 30 km long and stretches from Unterägeri via Baar, Zug and Cham as far as the old Reuss Bridge between Hünenberg and Sins, right across the scenic countryside of the River Lorze area in Canton Zug. Along the trail there are 65 information boards with lots of pictures and historical facts about the industrial development of the Canton, which is closely connected with the Lorze itself. This is pure living history, documenting the changes of the past centuries and its influence on the lives of the people living here.

title: Winter climbing on Clăbucetul Taurului peak (Predeal - Azuga)
short_description: An easy hike, which can be done in any season; it's also recommended as a weekend activity with children. Once you reach the peak, on a clear day, you're rewarded with beautiful views.
long_description:
If you spend a few days in the resorts on Prahova Valley skiing, sledding, or just relaxing, add this hike to your travel plans. The circuit is popular, so you will most likely not be the one to clear the path.
Excepting the middle of the circuit - near the Gârbova cabin - you'll walk through the forest, on a clear path or forest road. The Gârbova cabin is an ideal place to stop for rest, a snack, lunch or even to stay overnight.
Coming from Predeal, the forest thins in about two places, revealing the ridge of the Bucegi Mountains almost entirely, in all its splendor. The view just above the cabin, as you climb towards Clabucetul Taurului, gets even more splendid. Even before reaching the top, you can admire the Postavaru Massif in the back, and Bucegi and Piatra Mare mountains to your right. The Baiului Mountains can be seen on the left.
The peak stands on the route of the Romanian front during the First World War. Trench tracks are covered in snow in winter but are much more visible in summer.
The descent variant chosen here - blue dot - follows the forest road called "The Cannon Road", on which the Romanian soldiers carried their artillery to the top, in the 1916 campaign.

title: Sculpture Trail
short_description: Are you looking for the ideal Sunday afternoon walk for the whole family? We have found it for you.
long_description:
Looking for the ideal Sunday afternoon walk for the whole family? We've found it for you. On the 4.5 km long hiking path of the Sculture Trail on the Zugerberg you will meet 19 well-known inhabitants of forest and mountain. The young forester, Pascal Sturm, sculpted with a chain-saw these animal figures out of wood damaged by the Lothar hurricane in 1999. There are a number of benches - also out of damaged wood - and cosy barbecue spots where you can relax and picnic on this unique hiking trail. The sculpture trail is no problem for pushchairs either!

title: Wildspitz -  the highest point in Canton Zug
short_description: This tour takes you right to the top , to the highest point in the canton of Zug. The hike starts leisurely at the Zugerberg mountain station.
long_description:
This tour takes you way up to the highest point in Canton Zug. The hike starts leisurely at the top station of the Zugerberg funicular railway. From there you follow the elegant, extended ridge of the Zugerberg as far as Zuger Alpli. Fortify yourself here now for the steep ascent to the Wildspitz. Your effort will be rewarded with an incredible view of the valley of Schwyz, the Aegeri valley, Lake Zug and the surrounding alpine scenery. Enjoy a well-earned lunch in the Wildspitz restaurant and drink in the beauty of your surroundings.

title: Höglandsleden - Stage 6 - From Ingatorp to Mariannelund
short_description: The sixth and last stage of our tour on the Höglandsleden leads from the campsite north of Ingatorp üvia Katthult-Hof to Mariannelund.
long_description: We take a journey back to our childhood on the tour from Ingatorp to Mariannelund. We visit the famous Katthult farm, where Astrid Lindgren's children's book hero Michel from Lönneberga lived. Katthult was not built as a film set, the farm is part of the nearby Gibberyd estate and is still farmed today. The grounds with the main house, the farmhouse and the carpenter's shed, where Michel carved his little wood, are partly open to the public.

On the Raten Trail there are information boards with interesting text and pictures about the forest, animals, hunting, tradition and even pilgrims. The hike takes us through wonderful countryside with a magnificent panoramic view of the idyllic Lake Aegeri. A wonderful outing for the whole family, suitable for all ages.

title: From Stralsbach to Oberweißenbrunn - Rhön
short_description: This section of the Hochrhöner leads us to the Kreuzberg. Here a special refreshment awaits us: Franziskaner Klosterbräu.
long_description:
The starting point of our tour is in the centre of Stralsbach.
Past village gardens, the Hochrhöner follows the stream to the Borstmühle mill on this stage. Soon you reach the romantic Frauenroth monastery church with the touching grave of the minnesinger Otto von Botenlauben. From the resting place under the branches of the mighty hat beech at the end of the village, the Hochrhöner meanders on along the stream and the edge of the forest. A steep descent leads to Premich and offers wide views from the Black Mountains over the Kreuzberg with the transmission mast to the Lange Rhön. The Hochrhöner first follows the valley of the Kellersbach upwards and turns off to Langenleiten, a long street village. For centuries, the Franciscans have compensated pilgrims for the steep climb up the Kreuzberg with their monastery beer. We hikers also appreciate a good sip before the descent to Oberweißenbrunn, our destination.

images.caption: The minnesinger Otto von der Botenlauben is buried in the Cistercian convent Frauenroth.
At 864 m, the Kreuzberg is the highest mountain in the Bavarian Rhön.
The Kreuzberg monastery also has a brewery with a beer garden.
A meeting of mountain bikers takes place every Wednesday at the Kreuzberg monastery.

short_description: With nearly 200 kilometres, the GR 30 goes around many lakes in Auvergne of glacial origin (Lac de Guacute;ry), volcanic origin (Lac Pavin, Lac de la Cassière...) or dam lakes (Lac d'Aydat).
long_description: Nature, history, heritage and gastronomy are the ingredients of this fantastic route, which can be completed in less than 10 days.

title: Down to the Höll caves
long_description:
Their name sounds like «hell» in German, but that's not where you're going. First an easy walk along the banks of the River Lorze as a warm-up. You cross two imposing bridges that connect valley and hill and glimpse the Wildenburg ruins, an insider tip, over the three bridges: giving some idea how important it once was. Soon we reach the entrance to the Höll caves where you will discover many impressive stalagmites and stalactites in the mystic Höll Grotto, and be enchanted by this fairytale world underground. Back to earth, there are numerous barbecue areas right by the river where you can relax and enjoy the surroundings.

title: Running around Lake Herăstrău
short_description: A green island in the center of a city that never sleeps.
long_description:
Herăstrău is an artificial lake located north of Bucharest from the Colentina River, in the area where it crosses the city limits, between Lake Băneasa upstream and the Floreasca River. The lake is located in the Herăstrău Park, which covers an area of almost 110 hectares.
The route is completely paved (renovation 2016/2017). The Herăstrău See tour is the most popular training site for the Bucharest inhabitants who come here as soon as their activities allow them to. You can run there any time of year, even if the wind blows a little on your face in winter.
In the summer, water fountains are available on the flower island. They allow you to cool down because the heat can be suffocating (due to the continental climate). Small traders that are open all year round can also sell bottled water to you.For those who listen to music online while on their cell phones, the entire course is covered with 4G.

title: Mont Tendre (2): Cabane du Cunay - Bière
long_description: While the massif of Mont Tendre is characteristically characterised by cart fields for a Jura peak, its south-eastern slope is interspersed with alps and partly dense forests. To get from Cabane du Cunay to Alp Druchaux, you have to descend briefly and then ascend again. Further Jura pastures of Petit Pré, Pré de St-Livres and Foirausaz are crossed. On hiking trails through the densely forested "Côte de Bière", the tour finally leads to Bière.

HUARAZ: CIRCUITO ALPAMAYO COMPLETO
short_description: Ruta completa de 8 días y 7 noches, bordeando principalmente a la montaña Alpamayo. Durante el recorrido y sobre todo en los respectivos campos bases o miradores sur y norte se pueden apreciar las demás montañas como Santa Cruz, Pumapampa, Quitaraju, Jancacurish y Tayapampa.
long_description:
Ruta completa de 8 días y 7 noches, bordeando principalmente a la montaña Alpamayo. Durante el recorrido y sobre todo en los respectivos campos bases o miradores sur y norte se pueden apreciar las demás montañas como Santa Cruz, Pumapampa, Quitaraju, Jancacurish y Tayapampa. También se observarán diversidad de lagunas. Este recorrdio contiene en gran parte a las rutas conocidad como Cedros Trek y Santa Cruz Trek.

8: CAMP LLAMACORRAL - CASHAPAMPA
  El Alpamayo (en quechua I: Allpa mayu), también conocido localmente como Shuytu rahu (del quechua ancashino: 'nevado oblongo'), es una montaña de la cordillera de los Andes, situada en la parte norte del ramal occidental de la cordillera Blanca, dentro del parque nacional Huascarán en el Perú.2 Alcanza una altitud de 5947 m s. n. m., y fue considerada «la montaña más bella del mundo» en un Concurso de Fotografía Escénica organizado por la revista Alpinismus en Múnich en mayo de 1966.23Ubicada cerca del caserío de Alpamayo, entre las quebradas Los Cedros y Arhuaycocha, en el distrito de Santa Cruz, provincia de Huaylas, departamento de Áncash, tiene un área glaciar de 4.69 km², con una altitud mínima de 4745 y una máxima de 6005 m s. n. m.24Su acceso tiene lugar desde la ciudad de Caraz, a 2250 m s. n. m. (467 km de Lima), en el extremo norte del Callejón de Huaylas, por una trocha carrozable de 28 km, hasta el poblado de Cashapampa a 2900 m s. n. m. Desde aquí, son 22 km de caminata a lo largo de la quebrada Santa Cruz, hasta el sector de Quisuarpampa, a 4000 m s. n. m., donde se toma el desvío al norte, ascendiendo por la quebrada Arhuaycocha, hasta el Campo Base, a 4300 m s. n. m.«La montaña más bella del mundo»En 1965 el andinista peruano César Morales Arnao recibió una carta del alpinista director de la revista alemana Alpinismus, invitándolo a enviar a nombre del Perú las fotos de las montañas peruanas que podían entrar a competir en el Concurso de Fotografía Escénica,3 que elegiría las diez montañas más bellas del mundo.

title: अंतरगंगे पर्वत ट्रैक
short_description: करीब 5600 फ़ीट की ऊंचाई पर स्थित अंतरगंगे पर्वत शिखर कर्न ाटक के कोलार जिले के शतश्रृंगा पर्वत श्रृंखला में हाइकिंग, रॉक क्लाइम ्बिंग, और गुफाओं की खोज करने के लिए एक बेहतरीन गंतव्य है।
long_description:
अंतरगंगे पर्वत शिखर कोलार शहर से लगभग 4 किलोमीटर और बंगलौर से लगभग 70 किलोमीटर दूर स्थित है। जमीन की गहराईयों से निकलकर और शतश्रुंगा पहाड़ो से होकर बहने वाले एक सदाबहार मीठे पानी के श्रोत के कारण इस इलाके का नाम अंतरगंगे पड़ा। अंतरगंगे का मतलब है 'गहराई से निकलने वाली गंगा' इस जलधारा की उत्पत्ति अभी भी एक रहस्य है।
पहाड़ों के अलावा इस स्थान में भूमिगत गुफाएं और कई बोल्डर भी हैं। इस क्षेत्र को दक्षिण की काशी भी कहा जाता है क्योंकि इसमें प्रसिद्ध काशी विशेश्वर मंदिर है जो हर साल हजारों भक्तों को आकर्षित करता है।

title: Emerald Trail Wallis-Piedmont: Stage 6
short_description: The route runs entirely along the Stockalperweg up to the Simplon Pass. The historic mule track was developed in the 17th century by the Briger merchant Kaspar Jodok von Stockalper for transalpine mule traffic. Stockalper's muleteers were on the move day and night for decades. We follow his tracks through varied cultural and natural landscapes. Our destination is the wide pass landscape in breathtaking mountain scenery on the Simplon.
long_description:
The trail follows the entire Stockalper trak to the Simplon Pass. The historical mule track was enlarged in the 17th century by Kaspar Jodok von Stockalper, a merchant from Brig, to facilitate transalpine traffic on pack animals. Stockalper's mule packs travelled day and night for decades. You will follow their tracks in breath-taking and extremely diverse cultural and natural landscapes. Your destination is the wide-open, overwhelmingly beautiful Simplon pass natural scenery.

Trail description
Start your excursion by the Stockalper Mansion in Brig. Follow the old Simplon road's brown direction signs behind the Riedbachstrasse and the Römerweg for 50 minutes uphill until you get to Lingwurm and Brei. After a short stretch on a secondary road turn left and walk uphill on the zigzag road in the dry pine wood. To overcome the vertical wall in Chalchofe, Stockalper had a road excavated in solid rock through the 300 metre-deep Saltina Gorge. The old Napoleonic road will take you to Schallberg (1316) with a scenic view on the branching valleys on Simplon's northern slopes. The descent from Schallberg to the Gantergrund on Simplon's south-facing slope cuts across a biologically diverse rocky Wallis steppe to take you to Grund (1072 m). The Gantergrund is a riverine landscape of national importance. In the Middle Ages, Ganter and Grund were autonomous communes. Grund's barn proves that corn farming is a very old practice in the region. From the autumn 2008 the Gantergrund can be reached directly from Brig through the Grindji (Little Grund) and the dramatic Saltina Gorge. Following in Stockalper's tracks, the municipality of Brig-Glis used explosives to cut open a road through kilometres of solid rock. From the Gantergrund follow a forest road, then a mule track through spruce and alder, that will take you repeatedly across the Taferna creek. The churning stream's name comes from a small hamlet situated at an altitude of 1597 m. Here, in Stockalper's times, there was a tavern whose innkeeper, Johannely Fy, notoriously put water in her wine - at least that's what the legend says - and is now atoning as a damned soul buried deep in the glacier. Overcome the steep drop towards the Simplon Pass, on a winding road that cuts through larch. You will then reach the gap at Lärchmatte (2004). The view opens up on a wide landscape rich in peat bogs and mountain ponds reflecting the imposing shape of the Fletschhorn (3996 m). Simplon's high peat bogs are a landscape of national importance.

Trail description: Andreas Weissen

Landscape, NATURA2000, protected areas

Landscape and nature
The trail from Brig to Simplon Pass will take you through diverse landscape, dry pine wood with rocky steppe plants, wet spruce forests and dense larch woods. You will also walk through two landscapes of national importance: the Grund riverine landscape and Simplon's high peat bogs. In the Laggintal nature reserve the Erebia Christi can be found: Erebia is a rare diurnal butterfly that was discovered in 1882 and described in 1890, living on the Simplon's southern slope. For decades collectors and enthomologists captured these butterflies causing a decrease in the population. In 1982 and 1983 excavation material dumped on the slopes from a road construction site in Laggintal led to the destruction of the two most representative habitats. In 1985 the government of Wallis banned the collection of butterflies, larvae and chrysalises, and established a butterfly reserve. In 1998 the Laggintal valley and the surrounding territories of the Zwischbergental and Simplon were recognised as landscapes of national importance and listed in the "Swiss national inventory of landscapes, sites, and natural landmarks" (IFP number 1717) (surface: 11.498 hectares)

WWF's tips for hikers

Plan each stage carefully, purchase a 1:25000 map, use light but sturdy equipment (hiking boots, rain cape, binoculars ). Be sure to carry a small supply of water and food. We suggest you taste local food (possibly organic) at resting places and restaurants.
Do not litter, do not pick up flowers or rocks and in no way disturb the local fauna. It is unsafe for inexperienced hikers to leave the marked trails and it may cause disturbance to wildlife.

Note(s)
To see

History and culture

Stockalper's trail connectin Brig and Gondo, on the Italian border, is the "umbilical cord" of the Simplon Ecomuseum. Differently from conventional walled-in museums, the Ecomuseum illustrates nature and culture in an open landscape, namely the Simplon Pass. The Ecomuseum does not only present the natural space, but illustrates the region's history that shaped the natural landscape. In Simplon's case that history is the history f trade and agriculture. During the excursion on Stockalper's trail you will experience the region's historical background: Stockalper's castle in Brig, the ruins of the old tavern in Taferna, Simplon's hospice (19th century), the old hospital dating back to Stockalper's times, and the Second World War stone eagle. Stockalper's mule track (17th century) is very well preserved; on the contrary the 1805 napoleonic road is hardly visible, since in 1965 route A9 was built upon it. Today many lorries use the pass road, sometimes carrying dangerous freight, although the Swiss Federal Constitution states that freight traffic be transferred to the rail from 2004. On the steep descent to Brig overheated brakes can easily fail and cause catastrophic accidents.

title: Juneau Mendenhall Glacier Trail to Forest Ecology Trail
short_description: Mendenhall Glacier Visitor Center Wildflower Viewing Area offers a unique opportunity to observe plant succession in action.
long_description: Glacial movements have, and still are influencing where, when, and what plants may occur. Several trails radiate from the visitor center offering access to a variety of habitat types and stages of plant community development.  For panoramic views of the lake, glacier, peaks and sandy shoreline with its collection of early succession plants, try the Photo Point Trail (0.3 miles) and Nugget Falls Trail (0.7 miles), both begin in front of the Visitor Center. A close-up look at early succession vegetation will reveal pioneers such as tiny fungi, mosses and lichens that form a “crust” over the loose sand and facilitate the establishment of larger plants. You may notice scattered lupines (Lupinus nootkatensis), young willows (Salix spp.), Sitka spruce trees (Picea sitchensis), and Sitka alder shrubs beginning to work their way into the landscape which has been ice free for only fifty years or less.

title: Monkey Trail
short_description: The best known of the routes within the Utinga Environmental State Park, the Monkey Trail is a route that is considered easy but has many attractions for everyone.
long_description: Being the best known trail in the Utinga State Environmental Park, the Monkey Trail is also the most used by visitors. The trail has its name due to the species of monkey that lives there. The trail lasts about 40 minutes a day and begins in the Clareira do Macaco, near Lake Bologna, and ends near the Centro de Visitaço, with access to the lake Água Preta. The trail is designed for people from 15 years old. Among the forest species found, we can highlight the Embauba, Jabuti Ladder, Mumbaca, Quarubatinga and other specimens of the Amazon.

title: Emerald Trail Wallis-Piedmont: Stage 5
long_description:
This diverse trail will give you the opportunity to look at the landscape from a cultural point of view. You will follow an old water pipe, walk on pastureland between Hockmatta and Bister, make a detour towards a mid-altitude pasture, and visit the corn fields of Ried Briga. Above Grengiols you will visit the Tulip Hill where, in late May a tulip blooms that is found nowhere else in the world and carries the village name: Tulipa grengiolensis. Spectacular plants occur also in the Ried-Briga corn fields. Our destination is "2008 City of the Alps" Brig-Glis.

Trail description
You will Ernen's historical centre on a seldom-used trail. Behind the tourist centre a path bends to the right of the Rappetal. Follow it until you find the sign to the Frid pasture and the "Waldkapelle", then take the track leading up into the spruce forest. After climbing approximately 120 metres a water pipe crosses the path: it is the so-called "Trusera", Ernen's longest conduit, taking water four km away from the Rappetal to the Binnachra Valley. The old pipeline was restored a few years ago. Follow it down and west to the valley through the Aerner Wald forest. These water pipelines, called "Suonen" by German-speaking Wallisers and "bisses" by their French-speaking fellow citizens, are of key importance for the "dry river bed agriculture" of the internal portion of the Alps. A more modern form of water management can be found at Am Wasen (1240 m): a reservoir where water is accumulated before being channelled through a penstock to move turbines for the production of electricity. At Am Wasen leave the "Trusera" and cross the main road by the bus stop, follow the sign to Hockmatta. Through pastures and a small patch of wood, the trail will take you down to the Binna creek and across it on a footbridge. Stop in the middle of the bridge to watch the mountain creek and the gorge wood. After a few turns you will get to Hockmatta (1198), with its square and church. Some 100 people lived here at the beginning of the 20th century, today the tiny village is inhabited only in the summertime. Above the village you will meet the military road that corresponds to the western portion of the Arbola road. Today this is part of the very popular cycling trail "Rhone 1". The road, recently partially paved anew, and bordered by dry walls, winds through the traditional cultural landscape of pastures and barns, interspersed with patches of wood and landslide scars. The road is unfortunately paved in bitumen above Grengiols from Viertel to Bister. Beyond Bächerhyschere, the Milibach creek bed and the 1904 avalanche memorial you will be happy to enter a good albeit unmarked track by a wooden cross. The trail will lead you directly to the Tulpenhügel, the Tulip Hill. Here, in a cattle pasture, botanist Thommen discovered in 1946 a previously unknown tulip variety that he named after the village: Tulipa grengiolensis. The wild tulip thrives in corn fields and usually blooms in the second half of May. To date between 2000 and 4000 specimens have been counted. The flower attracts hundred of nature lovers each year. From Tulip Hill, by the football pitch, get back on the paved road. Grengiols, set on fire in 1799 by Austrian troops fighting the French and subsequently rebuilt from scratch, is definitely worth a visit. Three bars or restaurants invite you to rest a little before continuing your walk. Back on the paved road by the school in front of the church take the short cut on the right. Continue west beyond Bädel and Ze Hyschere to Bister (1040 m). Along the way you will exit, without being aware of it, the Binntal Landscape Park. The village of Bister is made of different small hamlets. On the left side of the road a sign shows the way to Tunetsch. The steepest track of the day awaits you at this moment and will take you through spruce and the Gifetschgraben to the Tunetsch high pasture (1492 m). The high meadow is now basically a summer pasture for the sheep and donkeys of an organic farmer. Walk down the gentle slopes of the pasture by the place called Erli to the small village of Zen Achru (1120 m). Turn left at the fork in the track towards Termen. Follow the steep and arid slope between isolated birch trees and juniper shrubs to the Tunetschgraben. Through a shady mixed forest you will reach the traditional farming landscape of Termen, where an educational trail provides interesting information on farming activities. From Termen (927 m) follow the bitumen road to Biela, where it branches off towards Brig. In early summer it is worth it to detour shortly to the Achera Biela corn fields. Among winter cereals you will find here the most diverse accompanying flora of all Switzerland. Walk by some mown meadows and a small suburb of terraced houses and the walk down leisurely to Brig (680 m). You will reach the 2008 City of the Alps by Stockalper Castle, the symbol of the city and of the Simplon Pass.

Trail description: Andreas Weissen

Landscape, NATURA2000, protected areas

Landscape and nature
This varied excursion will take you to the Rappetal, the most secluded valley in the Binntal Landscape Park. In a short distance you will cross very diverse habitats: pine, spruce, and larch forests; pasture and grassland, high mown meadows and Alpine pastures. On the shady slope of the Rappetal only alder grows; the ground is very steep and numerous avalanches and landslides do not allow trees to root. On the sunny side, by the creek, wide pastures exists, the fruit of centuries long tillage. With the abandonment of pastures dwarf bush (rhododendron, blueberry) and larch are making a return.

WWF's tips for hikers

Plan each stage carefully, purchase a 1:25000 map, use light but sturdy equipment (hiking boots, rain cape, binoculars ). Be sure to carry a small supply of water and food. We suggest you taste local food (possibly organic) at resting places and restaurants.
Do not litter, do not pick up flowers or rocks and in no way disturb the local fauna. It is unsafe for inexperienced hikers to leave the marked trails and it may cause disturbance to wildlife.

Note(s)
To see

History and culture

The village of Hockmatta is splendidly preserved, although from the 1960's it is uninhabited for most of the year. In Bächerhyschere visit the local chapel with an altar-piece by painter Raphael Ritz and dedicated to "Our Lady of the Alps". Grengiols is the fifth village of national relevance we meet in the Binntal Landscape Park. Besides steep Dorfgasse alley and the village square, the church is also worth a visit: it is a basilica-like building with surprising pieces of art. Termen's educational trail will provide a living portrait of mountain agriculture.
Brig is a jewel city with numerous attractions, mostly from the 17th century (Stockalper Castle with its impressive courtyard, the collegiate church, the Saint Ursula convent church) when merchant Kaspar Jodok von Stockalper established a thriving trade route between Italy and France through the Simplon Pass, becoming wealth and a nobleman in the process. Today the local square is abuzz with activity day and night. Brig is also the starting point of the 19.8 km-long Simplon connecting Switzerland and Italy. With the 1970's merger with a nearby town the official name became Brig-Glis.

- Visit Hockmatta and the Holy Virgin chapel in Bächerhyschere
- Detour to the village of Grengiols, village of national relevance and outstanding religious building
- Detour to the Tulpenhügel (Tulip Hill) with traditional barns and accompanying species-rich flora
- Termen's educational trail on mountain agriculture
- Educational trail in Achera Biela with biodiversity rich accompanying flora

title: Swabian Alb South Rim Trail (HW2)
short_description: The Schwäbische Alb Südrand-Weg is the main hiking trail No. 2 of the Schwäbische Albverein. It leads from Donauwörth to Tuttlingen.
long_description:
The trail starts in Donauwörth and leads us üht via Dischingen to Giengen an der Brenz. We pass the Charlottenhüll and hike through the Lone Valley before arriving in Ulm via Langenau. The Ulmer Münster, at 161 m the highest church tower in the world, offers a magnificent panoramic view. After a stroll through the picturesque old town, we continue our hike over the Hochstrass to Blaubeuren to the legendary Blautopf (a 22 m deep karst spring).
&Uml;ber Schelklingen it goes on the Schwäbische Alb and we reach the Gro&szlig Lautertal at Erbstetten. The trail follows the river for a short time, then leads up to Hayingen and past the Wimsener Hütte into the valley of the Zwiefalter Ach.
From the Zwiefalter monastery church we then walk over the little-known Gro&szlig Heuneburg (near Upflamör) to Bingen and Sigmaringen with its Hohenzollern castle. We hike up the Danube, past ruins and castles such as Ruine Falkenstein, Ruine Hausen, Burg Werenwag, Burg Wildenstein. From towering cliffs, we enjoy repeated views of the Danube valley, which is one of the most beautiful river landscapes in Europe.
From Beuron Monastery, we can either walk along the banks of the young Danube or up to the former hunting lodge of Bronnen and back down to the Danube to the seepage points near Fridingen. These offer a special natural spectacle in dry summers. We end our tour in the district town of Tuttlingen.
