title: Vogelsberg volcanic ring
short_description: In six one-day stages, the route takes us around the Vogelsberg, Europe's largest extinct volcano. The entire route takes us through the varied Hoher Vogelsberg Nature Park and can be started at any point.
long_description:
Stage 1: Laubach - Rainrod (17 km)
Winding alleyways, half-timbered houses and an imposing castle await us in Laubach. After a short tour of the town, we set off on a leisurely hike through forests and along small streams. Several valleys and natural orchards lead us past Stornfels to Rainrod, which lies in the Nidda valley.
Stage 2: Rainrod - Schotten-Burkhards (19.5 km)
Today we first walk along the edge of the forest with wonderful views and touch the village of Eichelsdorf. In the Eichköppel bird sanctuary, we cross several small streams and enjoy nature. Descending into the Eichelbach valley, we reach the end point of our day's stage, Schotten-Burkhards, via Gederner See.
Stage 3: Schotten-Burkhards - Herchenhain (16 km)
From Schotten-Burkhards, we circle a large wooded area and reach Völzberg via the Alte Burg rock formation. The route now climbs up to the Völzberger Köpfchen and via the village of Hartmannshain to the Herchenhainer Höhe - both of which offer wonderful views.
Stage 4: Herchenhain - Herbstein (15.5 km)
From the Herchenhainer Höhe, we head towards a chain of basalt formations one behind the other, including the Bonifatiuskanzel geotope and the "Gesicht". On the way to Ilbeschausen-Hochwaldhausen, we see the "Burg" and the "Uhuklippen" as well as many other impressive volcanic geotopes. Our destination is the Kolping vacation village near Herbstein. In Herbstein, we stroll through the beautiful old town and can pay a visit to the carnival museum and the Catholic church of St. James.
Stage 5: Herbstein - Ulrichstein (23 km)
We reach Helpershain through the nature reserve at the Schalksbach ponds and the Eisenbach valley. A little later, we reach the "Dicken Steine", which, according to legend, were used by Frau Holle to access the underworld. In Ulrichstein, the Vogelsberg garden, the castle ruins and the hunting museum are well worth a visit.
Stage 6: Ulrichstein - Laubach (23 km)
Today we embark on the last stage of the circular tour, which once again offers breathtaking views, e.g. from the Schleuningsteine. We walk past Kölzenhain through the idyllic Seenbachtal valley and admire numerous old mills along the way. After Freienseen, we leave the valley and walk through a hilly wooded area back to Laubach, the starting point of our long circular walk.

title: Loop to the Denecourt Tower from Fontainebleau-Avon station
short_description: This beautiful itinerary, accessible to all, leads from Fontainebleau-Avon to the famous and unmissable Tour Denecourt. You will return to the starting point by taking paths via numerous points of interest: Fontaine D&eacutee, Fontaine Dorly, Fontaine Isabelle or Roche Eponge.
long_description:
The outward journey is simply along the road to the Tour Denecourt, following the yellow markings.
Once you have reached the Tour Denecourt, don't hesitate to climb to the top (you will be 136m above sea level) and enjoy a 360° view over the forest. Magnificent ! The édifice was built by Claude-François Denecourt (who landscaped the forêt of Fontainebleau) in 1851, and then restored à several times.
The return journey follows a blue trail.
While no river crosses the Fontainebleau forest, you will pass respectively:
- The Fountain of Fontainebleau
- La Fontaine du Touring Club de France, created in 1901;
- La Fontaine Désirée, covered in 1837 then improved by Denecourt in 1852;
- La Fontaine Dorly, also created in 1852 by Denecourt;
- La Fontaine Isabelle, created by Denecourt in 1866 and restored by Colinet in 1893.
The details of these 4 fountains are however very variable.
Finally, take a break at the Roche Eponge, a curiosity in the Fontainebleau forest, which owes its name to an aspect resulting from the erosion.

title: Emerald Trail Wallis-Piedmont: Stage 4
short_description: Hike from Ausserbin to Ernen through the Binn Valley
long_description:
The Rappetal is a secluded, wild valley in the Binntal Lanscape Park. Today it is a sheep shelter with the old pasture huts in ruins. Mühlebach, at the mouth of the valley, is Switzerland's most ancient wooden village. Ernen, the stage's arrival point, is Wallis' most beautiful village. An imposing square, surrounded by stately mansions, still stands testimony to the importance of the former chief town of Goms district.

Trail description
In Ausserbinn take the road to Ernen. After a short stretch on bitumen, the road winds along the old mule track. Cross the sunny slope where grass and aspen conquered what were once farmed corn fields. You now have a full view of the Rhone River valley, the Binna stream banks, the traditional farmlands of Hockmatta and Binnachra. Mown meadows and pastures on both sides of the Binna are part of an ecological networks project aiming to convince farmers to convert to biodiversity-friendly farming by, among other things, cutting hay only after the blooming period, or refraining from using dung-water, fertilizers or insecticides.
Just before the ruins of the abandoned "Zur frohen Aussicht" inn, turn right along the mountain ridge towards Eggen among biodiversity-rich mown meadows. Dry pinewood is replaced by thick spruce. After a few more zigzags you will reach the village of Eggen, with its wonderful mown meadows and a breath-taking view over the Bernese Alps. The trail, framed by typical hedges, passes by several settlements, the idyllic view somewhat disturbed by a concrete compensation reservoir.
In summer the big white wooden cross of the Frid pasture (1936 m) is visible from afar. The milk of the pasture's many cows is not worked into cheese on site but is funnelled down to the valley through a conduit. A dirt track will take you to a small plateau surrounded by larch, where black grouse perform their mating dances after snow thaw. Turn left at the fork in the track and enter the wood. Wild Rappetal opens in front of you. Follow the flat track for a few kilometres through alder, scree, landslide tracks, and alpine pastures until you get to a stream. By Z'Mühbach a shepherd shelter can be found. A footbridge will take you to the opposite bank. Follow the Mühlebach stream to its namesake village, through alpine pastureland and small peat bogs, by abandoned farming buildings, and through larch and spruce.
The historical centre of Mühlebach is a real gemstone. In no other Swiss town or village will you find so many ancient wooden buildings. All the sunburnt larch houses and barns bear plates with the dates of construction. Most buildings date back to the 14th, 15th and 16th centuries. One house bears a larger sign reading "Birth home of Cardinal Matthäus Schinner, 1465-1522". On a hill above the village stands a blindingly white church. You can rest on one of the numerous benches before heading to Ernen, the stage's destination.
Walk through the village towards the west, cross the Mühlebach stream on the main road. Turn right behind a recently built barn on a country road. The hamlet with a conspicuous wooden structure is called Ze Kännle. Large wooden conduits were built on stilts to transport water to the pastures and fields of the Mooshubel. Walk over the Mooshubel through spruce and then over its summit covered in steppe-like vegetation. On the hill's western slope three imposing stone pillars can be seen, what is left of Ernen's old executioner's ground. Leave that macabre place behind you and walk through a narrow alleyway to the "Bergland" organic farm, where panels in the fields will provide interesting information on the farm's herbal production. You are now in Ernen, Wallis' most beautiful village, with a wide and inviting square, stately wooden mansions and a small stone town hall. The 16th century parish church, set on a high scenic terrace, is a jewel in itself. Several museums will invite you to dive into the long history of Goms' old chief town.

Trail description: Andreas Weissen

Landscape, NATURA2000, protected areas

Landscape and nature
This varied excursion will take you to the Rappetal, the most secluded valley in the Binntal Landscape Park. In a short distance you will cross very diverse habitats: pine, spruce, and larch forests; pasture and grassland, high mown meadows and Alpine pastures. On the shady slope of the Rappetal only alder grows; the ground is very steep and numerous avalanches and landslides do not allow trees to root. On the sunny side, by the creek, wide pastures exists, the fruit of centuries long tillage. With the abandonment of pastures dwarf bush (rhododendron, blueberry) and larch are making a return.

Protected areas, proposed Emerald sites, Natura 2000sites

- Binntal Landscape Park
- Federal Inventory of Landscapes, Binntal, IFP n. 1701

Wildlife, Natura2000 species

Wildlife, Emerald / Natura 2000 species found along the trail

Birds: Aquila chrysaetos (ca), Dryocopus martius (ca), Cinclus cinclus (ca), Monticola saxatilis (RL CH), Tetrao tetrix (ca / S).

More species of interest
Adonis aestivalis (RL CH / §), Agrostemma githago (RL CH), Paradisea liliastrum (RL CH / §), Parnassius mnemosyne (RL CH), Chenopodium bonus-henricus (ca), Dactylorhiza sambucina (RL CH / §), Orchis ustulata (RL CH / §), Danthus carthusianorum (ca), Epilobium angustifolium (ca), Larix decidua (ca), Gentiana purpurea (ca), Luzula nivea (ca), Pulsatilla apiflora (ca), Alnus viridis (ca), Aster alpinus (ca), Leontopodium alpinum (ca), Nigritella nigra (RL CH / §), Gentiana kochiana (ca), Juncus jacquinii (ca), Pulsatilla vernalis (ca), Ranunculus kuepferi (ca).

Categories:

§: Species enjoying national protection
E: Endemic species

More information on plants and animals
Regional habitats: traditional farmed fields, mown meadows and extensive pastureland, rich meadows and hay fields, dry meadows, spruce and larch forests, matgrass and other grassland, bush hedges, and wind-exposed areas.

- Plants and habitats in the Binntal Landscape Park

"Alpe Veglia e Alpe Devero: conservation of high mountain meadows and bogs", Dr. Nat. Paolo Pirocchi, Dr. Nat. Giovanna Ianner, Parco Naturale Alpe Veglia e Alpe Devero, 2003.

WWF's tips for hikers

Plan each stage carefully, purchase a 1:25000 map, use light but sturdy equipment (hiking boots, rain cape, binoculars ). Be sure to carry a small supply of water and food. We suggest you taste local food (possibly organic) at resting places and restaurants.
Do not litter, do not pick up flowers or rocks and in no way disturb the local fauna. It is unsafe for inexperienced hikers to leave the marked trails and it may cause disturbance to wildlife.

Note(s)
To see

History and culture

The Ausserbinn trail on the Binnegga, with the abandoned "Zur frohen Aussicht" inn, belongs to the Arbola trail. Until the late Middle Ages the Arbola mule track was the main trade thoroughfare from the Po River Valley to transalpine Switzerland and Bern, through the villages of Binn, Ausserbinn and Ernen, and the Furka and Grimsel Passes.
Ernen owes its historical importance to the trade traffic going through the region's passes From the 16th to the 18th century Ernen's main families played a major role in the entire Wallis economy and society. From those families stemmed bishops, regional governors and standard bearers who influenced the region's destiny. Ernen's many stately mansions are a testimony to its past wealth and influence.
Mühlebach also stands on an important road of the past. Contrary to what happened in many other Wallis villages, Mühlebach was never destroyed by fire. Its precious and unique architectural heritage was therefore preserved to our days. Both Ernen and Mühlebach are mentioned on the National Inventory of Protected Sites (ISOS). The municipality of Ernen, to which Mühlebach belongs since 2005, is responsible for the conservation of its precious legacy.
Recently Ernen gained international renown as a "music village". Composer and pianist György Sebök created "The Future Festival", inviting young musicians from all over the world to the small mountain village. Every summer world-class concerts are held in Ernen's parish church.

- Mühlebach: Switzerland's oldest wooden village; site of national relevance;
- Ernen: Wallis' most beautiful village: square, mansions, church; view over the Rhone River Valley
- Most ancient William Tell frescoes (16th century) in the "Tellenhaus"
- Jost Sigristen Museum in the residence of the last governor of the state of Old Wallis (1798)
- Zenden Museum by the Town Hall with precious parchments and documents dating back to the 13th century
- Museum and treasure of the church with precious chasubles, chalices, crosses, etc.
- "Music village" Ernen: concerts, composition workshops, classes, etc

title: Panoramic hike up the Staffelberg
short_description: This short hike from the Freudensee lake to the Staffelberg offers beautiful views from the viewing tower and a little summit bliss.
long_description: From the Freudensee parking lot, the hike first goes over the Staffelbach stream and past Staffelöd up the mountain towards the forest. At the edge of the forest there is a small rest area with a bench and table, where it is worth taking a look back at Hauzenberg. We continue uphill, initially on a small hiking trail through a beautiful mixed forest. After a while, the path turns into a forest road, which we follow on a steep ascent to the summit of the Staffelberg. On the summit plateau there is a summit cross and a viewing tower. Here you have a great panoramic view, especially in good weather, and can see as far as the Alps when the foehn is blowing.

title: Moselle Heights Trail
short_description: The almost 100 km long Moselhöhenweg has existed since 1910 and celebrated its 100th anniversary in 2010. From Wasserbilligerbrück, however, this long-distance hike does not always run directly along the Moselle - as the name suggests - but cuts off some Moselle bends to reach beautiful vantage points and finally ends in the village of Heißer Stein.
long_description: The Moselhöhenweg starts in the Moselstraße in the village of Wasserbilligerbrück near Oberbillig, on the northern bank of the Moselle. The first kilometres of this scenic long-distance hiking trail lead us immediately over the Olkener Berg through the village of Herresthal and past the Mohrenkopf to Pallien, a district of the lively and worth seeing city of Trier. We hike a short distance along the left bank of the Moselle and arrive behind Biewer on forest paths in the Pfalzel forest. Immediately after the forest we reach the outskirts of Ehrang and then march via Quint to the town centre of Schweich. There we recharge our batteries in one of the numerous cafés for the rest of the hike, on which we can now expect some elevations. We first tackle the ascent to Mehringer Berg and then hike up to Hundbuckel via a Landwehrkreuz at Hummelsberg. Once we have completed the two ascents, we are greeted by the Ensch forest with its vineyards, which we eagerly hike through. The Moselhöhenweg leads us out of the forest past the Kahlbachmühle, which we visit. We hike up the elevation of the Stallsack, follow the route via the regions of Schlingenborn and Krumfurche to the Weißlei viewpoint and continue through the village of Monzel to Lieser on the Moselle. Now the Wehlen forest lies ahead of us, which we hike through in a north-westerly direction. We then cross the B50 and orientate ourselves in the Zeltingen Rachtiger Forest towards the Lorenzenberg. However, we do not climb the summit, but hike around the Lorenzenberg and via Berghof to our long-distance hiking destination, the village of Heißer Stein on the Moselle.

title: England Coast Path - Walney Island
short_description: This route is part of the England Coast Path National Trail.
long_description:
The 26.1 km (16.2 miles) stretch of the England Coast Path (ECP) around Walney Island is now open to the public. 
  The England Coast Path is happening because of a completely new right of access that gives everyone the legal right to explore our coast for the very first time. It is much more than just a path, it gives access to beaches, cliff-tops, and most of the wonderful habitats around our coast. You can see the open sections and how they relate to the other National Trails here.
  Coastal sections of existing National Trails will become part of the England Coast Path in time. This will give the Trails better protection when the coast erodes. The Trails won't lose their own identities though, they will still be National Trails in their own right and the signage will be the same, but you may see new signs saying 'part of the England Coast Path'.
  You can find out about the other National trails on the official National Trail website.

title: HUARAZ: RUTA PASO DEL ZORRO Y CUATRO LAGUNAS
short_description: El presente trayecto inicia desde el poblado de Wilkawain y se va en sentido antihorario para recorrer las 4 lagunas y el Paso del Zorro hasta llegar al cruce de carretera que va hacia el pueblo San Miguel de Recresh.
long_description:
Recorrido realizado en un día. Opcional se puede realizar en dos días ya que hay habilitadas zonas de campamento durante el trayecto. Cabe destacar que en caso de portear equipaje de campamento, el recorrido es más favorable en el sentido contrario a este trayecto.El presente trayecto inicia desde el poblado de Wilkawain, muy cerca del Museo del mismo nombre y se va en sentido antihorario para recorrer las 4 lagunas y el Paso del Zorro (4,980 m.s.n.m.) hasta llegar al cruce de carretera que va hacia el pueblo San Miguel de Recresh. Desde este punto se continúa hasta llegar al mismo Wilkawain, donde se empezó el trekking.
Las lagunas que se observan son las siguientes en este orden:Laguna Ahuac-Laguna Mullaca-Laguna Carhuac-Laguna Radián
Recomendable realizar en día sin pronóstico de lluvias, puesto que algunas partes del tramo para llegar al Paso del Zorro es de enormes rocas por donde hay que caminar. Si estas están mojadas le agrega dificultad. De todas formas, el clima en la zona es impredecible.

title: Sirona Way
short_description: The goddess of this eventful hiking trail is the Gallo-Roman goddess Sirona, who in mythology is responsible for wells, streams and rivers. Following in the footsteps of the Celts and Romans, we walk along numerous watercourses and over scenic mountains through the Hunsrück-Nahe region and the Birkenfeld countryside. Step by step, numerous information boards, reconstructed Celtic villages, cultural monuments, hilltop castles, burial mounds, sanctuaries, museums and information pavilions take us into the world of early historical life.
long_description:
Stage 1: Bundenbach - Stipshausen (16 km)
We start our hike at the eastern edge of the small community of Bundenbach. After only a few metres, we reach the Altburg, a reconstructed Celtic hilltop settlement that is one of the most impressive archaeological sites in Germany. We continue along the Hahnenbach and Idarbach streams through Rhaunen. Now we hike into the Idarwald forest to the stage destination in Stipshausen.
Stage 2: Stipshausen - Berschweiler near Kirn (21 km)
Past the Viergötterstein in Hottenbach, we reach the Hardter Wald via Sulzbach. After crossing this, shady forest paths alternate with fields and meadows, and after a few kilometres we reach Berschweiler near Kirn.
Stage 3: Berschweiler near Kirn - Kempfeld (25 km)
Today we hike in a wide arc first over the Staufenbergskopf and the Feuerkopf to Fischbach. In the idyllic valley of the Hosenbach we continue leisurely and then steadily uphill via Herrstein, Mörschied and the mountain peak Mörschieder Burr to Wildenburg near Kempfeld. The village itself lies on the edge of the forest, a little to the north of the designated route.
Stage 4: Kempfeld - Oberhambach (22 km)
Past Kirschweiler, we hike steadily through the forest or along the edge of the forest today. Behind Leisel, the Heiligbösch church, Schwollen and Hattgenstein await us. Past the holiday park in Oberhambach, we descend to the Sauerbrunnen.
Stage 5: Oberhambach - Hoppstädten-Weiersbach (22 km)
The last stage takes us via Gollenberg into the state forest of Birkenfeld and into the town of the same name. We leave this along the Steinaubach stream, below the Burgbirkenfeld ruins, and continue to follow the stream in a southerly direction. In Hoppstädten-Weiersbach we cross the Nahe and shortly afterwards reach the destination of the Sirona Trail, the Altburg near Weiersbach.
In addition, there are two interesting connecting routes:
1) from Weitersbach to the Belginum Archaeological Park near Wederath
.
2) from Birkenfeld to the Celtic ring wall in Otzenhausen
.

title: HUARAZ: SANTA CRUZ TREK
short_description: Ruta de senderismo clásica y muy popular habilitada para 4 días y 3 noches por la quebrada de Santa Cruz.
long_description:
Ruta de senderismo clásica y muy popular habilitada para 4 días y 3 noches por la quebrada de Santa Cruz. Adicional se encuentra dentro de la presente ruta el recorrido hacia el C.B. Alpamayo Sur con la posterior Laguna Arhuaycocha.Hay la opción de realizarla de manera inversa también. aunque esta demanda más esfuerzo por la continua y larga pendiente que inicia desde Cashapampa hasta más o menos la zona de campamento de Llamacorral.
  La quebrada Santa Cruz es una de las quebradas con mayor extensión en el Parque Nacional Huascarán, con una longitud de 17 km. aproximadamente. La quebrada nace en el Abra Punta Unión, concluyendo en el río Santa. En toda la quebrada se mantiene el clima frío, propio de las regiones naturales en las que se encuentra (suni y puna). Las precipitaciones promedio están en 700 mm/año y la temperatura promedio alrededor de 12ºC, con heladas durante el invierno. Durante el recorrido, se puede apreciar la rica flora y fauna alto-andina, diversos glaciares y lagunas.Durante el recorrido, se puede apreciar la rica flora y fauna altoandina, diversos glaciares y lagunas. La ruta de caminata hacia esta quebrada se inicia en la comunidad de Cashapampa (2,850 m.s.n.m.), caserío del distrito de Santa Cruz, pueblo agricultor y ganadero; desde ahí se pueden contratar los servicios de porteadores, arrieros y acémilas que llevarán el equipaje. Otro punto de partida es Colcas, un camino de trocha carrozable nos conduce a Hualcayán, tomando el desvío al sur, cruzando por las aguas termales de Huancarhuaz para llegar a Cashapampa

title: Deoria Tal - Chandrashila Track, Uttarakhand, India
short_description: Chandrashila is actually the peak of the Chandranath mountain on which the Tungnath temple is situated. The grand Himalayan panorama can be seen from the Chandrashila peak. This trekking route is very beautiful.
long_description:
Located in the Kedarnath Wildlife Sanctuary in Uttarakhand, the Deoria Tal - Chandrashila trek is a treasure trove for wildlife lovers. But the rare animals aren't the only thing that makes it special. Where most other Himalayan treks only cover a specific part of the Himalayan ranges, on this trek all the major mountains of western and eastern Uttarakhand can be seen till Chandrashila peak.
The trail route not only has many geographical features such as alpine lakes, alpine meadows (bugyal), rhododendron forests, mountain peaks and Himalayan views but also houses at least 2 dozen species of rare birds.
This is one of the most beautiful routes in Uttarakhand trekking circuit. Hikers who have trekked this route before can attest to its natural beauty and serenity. A part of this route is also a small pilgrimage section which runs from Chopta to Tungnath Temple. It is not unusual to see lines of devotees walking happily towards the temple on this 4 kilometer long route.
In short, it suffices to say that no Himalayan trekking tour is truly complete without the Sari-Deoriatal-Chandrashila track.

title: Tijuca Park: from the Forest Gate to the Visitors Center
short_description: Easy and light trail to get to know some famous and historical places of the Forest Sector of Tijuca National Park, in Rio de Janeiro.
long_description:
The sector Floresta has beautiful landscapes, and privileged spaces for recreation to enjoy the day with friends, family and children.
Going up the Forest Gate, visit the Cascatinha Viewpoint, the Açude Museum, the Visitors Center, the Mayrink Chapel and the Cascatinha Square. Here you can see the historical monument to the Barão de Taunay and the most famous waterfall of the park: the Cascatinha Taunay.
The Tijuca National Park é the most visited conservation unit in Brazil. Although it was created in 1961, the project of reforestation and protection of the region began in 1861, by order of D. Pedro II.
Today the Park has a green area of almost 40 km ², and among its beautiful forests é possible still recognize a little of the history of the place, through the ruins of the coffee farms é that were expropriated to allow the reforestation of the region

title: Trip to Gollinger Wasserfall
short_description: A short hiking trail leading to the foothills and observation of the impressive Gollinger waterfall in the Salzburg region, Austria
long_description:
A hiking route rich in landscapes that leads to Gollinger waterfall and to observe it. Walking the route includes water, rich vegetation and views while walking on a zigzag bridge, steps and natural paths.
Due to the fact that the route is linear, the walking time as well as the distance shown are in one direction only, but at any point on the route you can retrace the steps to the beginning of the route.

title: Hohenwarte Reservoir Trail
short_description: The Hohenwarter Stausee long-distance hiking trail directly on the so-called "Thuringian Sea" is 75 km long and divided into four stages. Along the way you will find the characteristic flora and fauna of the region.
long_description: A beautiful loop along the largest contiguous reservoir area in Europe. The challenging but family-friendly stage tour offers many sports and cultural activities.

images.caption: Best to leave early. Beautiful atmosphere and not a soul

title: Rigi-Kulm
long_description:
The Rigi is probably the most popular excursion mountain in Switzerland. With its hiking and walking trails, Nordic walking trails, children's playgrounds, ski and toboggan runs, sun terraces ... etc., it offers unique experiences for young and old, in winter as well as in summer.

This tour is intended more for beginners, as the groomed winter hiking trails always leave the option of continuing without snowshoes. For those who are more experienced, the variant via Seebodenalp is recommended (but only in safe conditions!).

title: Rigi-Dossen
long_description: This tour is truly a feast for the eyes. A panorama of a particularly splendid kind (constant view of Lake Lucerne and the surrounding mountains) accompanies us practically the entire tour, as the route runs up and down along the ridge.

title: Orfű lake seat
short_description: Easy to combine with family and holidays on the shores of Lake Pécs.
long_description: If you want to do a little bit of groundwork, the Lake Pécs circumnavigation is the ideal distance in a fabulous setting. Fortunately, more than half of the circuit is on a footpath for pedestrians. It can be combined with a holiday or a beach holiday, as there is an open-air beach at one end of the lake and the Aquapark and campsite at the other. Even if you only come for an afternoon, you'll have plenty of time to soak up the fresh air of the Mecsek mountains.

title: Salzburg High Throne over the Mittagsscharte
short_description: Beautiful hike along the south side of the Untersberg with a magnificent view of the Steinerne Meer and the Watzmann. Small path through a rock tunnel!

title: Morgartenberg
long_description:
This tour is made for beginners and connoisseurs. It is easy, but offers a lot for the eye. The view from Morgartenberg is unique and breathtaking!
If you still want to take on more, we highly recommend option B!

title: Kas - Limanagzi Beach - Kas
short_description: Starting from Kaş Municipality Public Beach, this route travels around Limanağzı with beautiful views and then back to Kaş.
long_description:
A paradise in every corner, Antalya is a unique place for nature lovers. The fact that there are many routes where the sea and green meet in this city with its natural beauties makes this city a blessing for nature lovers and travellers. You feel incomplete if you do not try all the routes.
Antalya's breathtaking sea view is again accompanied by the route. Starting from the public beach, the route also includes the famous Antiphellos Ancient City. Before continuing the route, you can visit this ancient city, which is an important value of Antalya, and set off again for the route.
After the ancient city, the route passes through Kaş and heads towards Limanağzı on a line with plenty of campsites. After reaching Limanağzı, the route connects us back to the Kas road again, not from the coastal side but from the side line parallel to it. 
You will enjoy experiencing this route, which is one of the güzel routes you can try in this bölge.

title: Rigi-Scheidegg
long_description:
This tour is almost considered an insider tip. This is not because of the highest point on the much-visited Rigi-Scheidegg, but because of two lesser-known cable cars that have to be used for this route.

Note(s)
The tour leads north of Rigi Hochflue through an avalanche slope! Sufficient touring experience and study of the avalanche bulletin are mandatory!

title: Snowshoe Hike through the Kellwasser Valley
short_description: 11 km long, moderately difficult snowshoe tour in the Harz Mountains. The starting and finishing point is not far from the village centre of the mountain town of Altenau.
long_description: This snowshoe hike takes us around the health resort of Altenau in the Upper Harz at the foot of the Bruchberg. With sufficient snowfall, the area is transformed into an impressive winter wonderland and offers optimal conditions for snowshoe hikes. On this circular tour, we climb 340 metres in altitude and pass the Fünf-Groschen-Brunnen (Five-Groschen Fountain) and the Altenau Herb Park. The largest of its kind in Germany gives the town its nickname as the town of herbs and spices. A detour to the Ockertal dam is also worthwhile.

title: From the Edmund Probst House to the Seealp Lake
short_description: A short tour with magnificent views.
long_description: It's downhill from the Höfatsalpe to the Seealpsee. A fantastic mountain panorama that definitely deserves a place in the photo album. The way back to the Höfatsblick station requires some stamina, so gather enough strength and refresh yourself at the lake. The tour is not too crowded and you can enjoy the mountain world all to yourself.

title: Quiet walk in the hills around Slieveboy
short_description: A quiet walk, starting from Askamore, through lots of woodland to access the hill area around Slieveboy.
long_description: Away from all the tourist hustle and bustle in the small village of Askamore, the path begins to climb up into the forest surrounding Slieveboy. Here we first walk on a narrow path between the almost always green trees and bushes, to later take the wider path on the other side of the hill with beautiful views of the surrounding landscape to the Slieveboy. Below this peak we do another loop and then return to Askamore. One of the best things about this remote walk is the silence, uninterrupted by distant engine noise or other people.

title: Mount Nittany Loop
short_description: With nearly 9 miles of volunteer-maintained trails and scenic views, Mt. Nittany offers a unique setting for hiking and recreation.
long_description: Mt. Nittany is the most recognizable and legendary symbol of Centre County and Penn State. It is the most popular hike for Penn State students and visitors alike and features birds-eye views of campus, Nittany Valley, and Penns Valley from seven scenic overlooks. Mt. Nittany is more than a local landscape or symbol, it is a place of bustling activity. It has been called the “classic hike for local residents, tourists and returning alumni,” providing exceptional views of the campus and the community from several natural overlooks. The popular Mike Lynch Overlook features a birds-eye view of the campus, including Beaver Stadium and the Bryce Jordan Center. Up and down, the trails are rocky and steep. Those on top are relatively flat. Following the primary trails is simply a big loop. Take a right at the top and follow the perimeter trail around the whole mountain and enjoy several overlooks – town and campus to the west; south to Boalsburg, the ski slopes of Tussey Mountain, and across Penns Valley.

title: Kust till Kustleden - from Brammarp to Körröd
short_description: The fourteenth stage of the Kust till Kustledens leads from the Brammarp üd campsite via the Höhenzug along the former Swedish-Dänish border to the Körröd campsite near Båstad.
long_description: We also hike along the old King's Path on this stage. In the borderland between Sweden and Denmark, it was an important messenger and trade route. Even at that time it was quite well developed, but also dangerous because of the many crossings. The landscape changes from forest and moorland to pastureland, and here the bridle paths sometimes have to be climbed over.

title: नाशिक ज़िले में अंजनेरी किले तक ट्रैकिंग। महाराष्ट्र, भारत
short_description: अंजनेरी किला नाशिक और त्रयम्बक से क्रमशः 26 और 6 किलोमीटर दूर है। यह ट्रैक न केवल अपनी प्राकृतिक सुंदरता बल्कि धार्मिक कारणों से भी प्रसिद्ध है। ट्रैक की एक गुफा को भगवान हनुमान जी का जन्मस्थान माना जाता है। हनुमान जी की माता देवी "अंजना" के नाम से यह इलाका "अंजनेरी" कहलाता है।
long_description:
अंजनेरी पर्वत का मुख्य आकर्षण अंजनेरी किला है जो समुद्र तल से 1300 मीटर की ऊँचाई पर स्थित है और इस तक अंजनेरी गाँव द्वारा पहुँचा जा सकता है। स्थानीय लोगों का मानना है कि यह किला भगवान हनुमान की जन्मभूमि है। इसलिए, यह हिंदू भक्तों के बीच धार्मिक आस्था का विशेष प्रतीक है।
इस ट्रेक के मार्ग में कई छोटे जैन मंदिर, गुफाएँ और एक पैर के आकार की झील पड़ती हैं। भगवान हनुमान की माता अंजनी देवी के दो मंदिर भी हैं। बड़ा वाला मंदिर ट्रैक का आरंभ बिंदु है और दूसरा छोटा मंदिर किले को जाने वाली सीढ़ियों के पास बना हुआ है और एक वेपॉइंट का काम भी करता है।
पश्चिमी घाट के ट्रैक आमतौर पर बोल्डर सेक्शन, उच्च घास के मैदान, जंगल, और रिज़ से भरे होते हैं । लेकिन इस ट्रैक में आपको सुंदर फूलों से ढंका एक विशाल मैदान दिखाई देता है। यह रास्ता झीलों, गुफाओं और झरनों जैसे तीन विविध भूवैज्ञानिक संरचनाओं से बना हुआ है। अंजनेरी किले की अपनी एक विशाल परिधि है और वहां से त्र्यंबकेश्वर शिखर, वैतरणा बैकवाटर, और ब्रह्मगिरि के शानदार दृश्य देखे जा सकते हैं।

title: From the city to the forest: Barcelona-Tibidabo-Vallvidrera
short_description: Hiking route through the forests of Collserola with views of the city of Barcelona and stops at various points of interest.
long_description: Although it may seem impossible, the city of Barcelona has lush natural spaces just waiting to be discovered. The forests of the Sierra de Collserola are located at an altitude of around 500 m and not only offer fantastic views of the metropolis with the sea in the background, but are also accessible by public transport. This hike, perfect for a morning or afternoon of outdoor activity, takes advantage of the city's infrastructure and makes the most of the nature just around the corner. The route runs mostly along wooded trails that will make you forget the hustle and bustle of the city at your feet.

title: About the harrows
short_description: Tour through forest and pastures
long_description: From the Vögelinsegg stop, the path leads up to the battle monument, which commemorates the fight for freedom that the people of Appenzell won against the people of St. Gallen and their allies in 1405. The ascent to the Höhenweg runs along a tarred road for the first quarter of an hour. With good visibility, you can see far across Lake Constance from there. Then turn left up to the edge of the forest where a gravel path leads through the Steineggerwald. You are now on the high trail, which leads up and down along the ridge. At the hamlet of Oberhorst, the path climbs to the meadow ridge - with a view of the entire Alpstein chain. A first highlight is the Waldegg. It is worth visiting the interior of the inn. Through forest and pastures you hike to Schäflisegg. Continue to Fröhlichsegg, where there is a large picnic area with tables Bänken and a fireplace. The trail descends over meadow paths to the Gstalden junction and then along a path down to the Lustmühle.

title: Round tour through the Wissbach Valley
short_description: Beautiful and varied hike across meadows and forest paths through the Wissbach Valley
long_description: Start at Weissbad railway station in a south-westerly direction. After the bridge over the Schwendibach, the trail leads past the Hotel Hof Weissbad on the right. Cross the Wissbach stream on the right and after a few metres turn left uphill. A zigzag path leads along the edge of the forest, climbing steeply to Rechböhl. You cross the road and 100 metres further up, the path leads left to Sonnenhalb. Shortly before the chapel, turn right. Walk across meadows and along shady forest paths to the Ahorn Chapel. The beautiful pilgrimage chapel, the cosy inn and the view of the mighty north walls of the Alpstein massif will not let you move on so quickly. The way back leads down to the Wissbach. Shortly afterwards, you cross the Berndlibach stream, which foams and plunges into the depths above the Leuenfall on the right. After an easy ascent, you reach the inviting Lehmen forest inn. Walk about 500 metres on the forest road out of the valley until the signpost at the Eugst farm indicates the left turn-off. Once again you cross the Wissbach stream, first slightly uphill and then comfortably to the Sonnenhalb chapel. On the same path as at the beginning of the hike, you move towards the destination of Weissbad.

title: Hill walk up the High Hirschberg
short_description: Über meadows and the edge of the forest from Hügelbummel to Hoher Hirschberg
long_description: From the Appenzell parish church, walk in a northerly direction to the crossroads at the Appenzell hospital. Take the field path up to the main road. After 200 metres, turn south across the railway track to the barn, where you turn left. Walk across meadows and along the edge of the forest until you reach the hillside. On this you hike leisurely ütlich over hütten up to the highest point, the Hoher Hirschberg. A magnificent panoramic view and the beautiful inn invite you to linger. To the south you look into the Alpstein mountains and to the east you see the peaks of the Vorarlberg. On the descent, follow the same route to Hütten. At the trail junction, climb a few metres to the northwest. This path takes you to the assembly point. Head towards Appenzell along the road for 200 metres, then branch off to the right. Walk along the road past the Lehnkapelle chapel until you reach the left fork. This field path leads you back to Appenzell.

title: On the heights around Gais
short_description: Beautiful hike with a view of the Alpstein.
long_description: From Gais railway station you hike in a southerly direction über Zwislen up to the Hoher Hirschberg. Here you can already enjoy a beautiful view of the Alpstein. Continue over pastures and through the forest down to Rietli. Take a short detour to the chapel and the battle monument at Stoss, which commemorates the freedom fights of the Appenzellers. Enjoy the view down into the Rhine valley and into Vorarlberg in Austria. This is followed by an approx. half-hour climb up the Sommersberg. Then it goes up to the Schwäbrig. At the Gäbrisseeli below the Gäbris there is a fireplace and it is worthwhile to hike around the beautifully planted Moorseelein. On the Gäbrissträsschen you will reach the Gäbris lookout point a short time later. On the other side of the Rhine valley you will see the Vorarlberg mountains and the mighty Alpstein massif opposite. Further to the right, the view extends from the Kronberg to the Glarus and Central Swiss Alps. A fireplace is also available here. From the Gäbris you can start the descent, depending on your preference, in a southerly or westerly direction.

images.caption: On the way up the Hoher Hirschberg

title: माथेरान सनसेट-पॉइंट ट्रैक
short_description: माथेरान का अर्थ है"पर्वत के माथे का जंगल। यह एशिया का एकमात्र मोटर-गाड ़ी मुक्त हिलस्टेशन है। यह कई सुंदर हाईकिंग ट्रेल वाला एक लोकप्रिय वीकेंड गंतव्य ह ै।
long_description:
माथेरान भारत के सबसे छोटे हिल स्टेशनों में से एक है। पश्चिमी घाट पर 2625 फीट की ऊंचाई पर स्थित माथेरान एक प्रसिद्ध वीकेंड गंतव्य है। यह भारत सरकार द्वारा एक पर्यावरण-संवेदनशील क्षेत्र घोषित किया गया है।
माथेरान में पुरानी ब्रिटिश शैली की वास्तुकला संरक्षित है। कई इमारतें अभी भी ब्रिटिश राज की याद दिलाती हैं। यहां पूरे इलाके की कोई भी सड़क डामर से नहीं बनी हैं बल्कि दक्षिणी पत्थर की चारित्रिक लाल लेटराइट मिटटी की हैं ।ये विशेषताएं माथेरान को एक ओल्ड-रस्टिक चार्म देती हैं।
माथेरान में कई सारे हाईकिंग और ट्रैकिंग मार्ग हैं। सभी मार्ग चढ़ाई की दृष्टि से आसान हैं। सनसेट पॉइंट हाइकिंग मार्ग भी एक लोकप्रिय मार्ग है। हालाँकि पहले हाईकर 'दोधानी गाँव-सनसेट पॉइंट हाईकिंग मार्ग" लेते थे, लेकिन हाल के समय में अपनी अच्छी और आसान पहुँच के कारण "अमन लॉज-सनसेट पॉइंट हाइकिंग मार्ग" मुम्बई और पुणे के हाइकर्स के बीच अधिक लोकप्रियता प्राप्त कर रहा है। इस मार्ग की एक और फायदा माथेरान हिल रेलवे द्वारा संचालित प्रसिद्ध टॉय ट्रेन में यात्रा करने का मौका भी है। सनसेट पॉइंट माथेरान का सबसे दूरस्थ ट्रैकिंग पॉइंट हे और इसका हाईकिंग मार्ग पूरी तरह से प्राकृतिक ट्रेल है। सनसेट पॉइंट पश्चिमी घाट की सह्याद्री पर्वत श्रृंखला में सूर्यास्त का शानदार नज़ारा दिखता है।

title: From Heiden to the Fünfländerblick
short_description: Across meadows and woods to a view of the forest
long_description: From Heiden you first walk along the road towards Grub AR. At the Frauenrüti junction, turn right and hike down to the Mattenbach stream, which you cross and then ascend to the cosy village of Grub SG. Continue across meadows and a short stretch through the forest to Rossbüchel. At the chapel, which was built in 1892, we stand on the Fünfländerblick. The name comes from the time when the countries of Bavaria, Baden and Wurttemberg were still distinguished. Together with Switzerland and Austria, this makes five countries. The panoramic view of Lake Constance and the Vorarlberg mountains is overwhelming. From Fünderblick, the route leads down ürt via Unterbilchen and along a beautiful forest path to Landegg - Wienacht. Wienacht, a health resort and holiday village, is situated on a mountain promontory, 300 m above Lake Constance. In about 10 minutes you reach the Wienacht Tobel railway station on the Rorschach-Heiden line. A detour to the hamlet of «Tobel» is worthwhile. Here you can visit the old Appenzeller settlement with wooden houses from the 17th century, all of which are under heritage protection. A short tour of the only vineyard in Appenzell Ausserrhoden concludes this memorable hike.

title: From Herisau to the seat
short_description: Scenic hike to the seat
long_description: From Herisau railway station, first take the road to Müli and a little further on Schwellbrunnerstrasse. Then branch off to reach Stierweid via Brugg. After a gentle climb and further along meadow paths, you reach Hinterwiesen. Up to Rötschwil, where the village of Schwellbrunn is in sight, you have to overcome a considerable difference in altitude. From Schwellbrunn there is another short climb up to the seat. In return, you can enjoy a wonderful panoramic view from the mountain inn. The Rückweg üvia Risi and the Säntisblick to Geisshalden above the village of Waldstatt is very varied and pleasant. You return to Herisau via the Nieschberg.

title: Elfstedentocht stage 9
short_description: Another stage after this, but today first stage 9.
long_description: Today you will cycle the longest stage of the Elfstdentocht. You will stretch from Franeker to Dokkum. You will cycle through several small villages in Friesland. This stage is not easy, but it is very beautiful. Dokkum is the northernmost city in the Netherlands. This town offers great shopping and a bite to eat.

title: Romanticism at the dreamy Forstseeli
short_description: A panoramic hike with a view of the Alpstein.
long_description: From the car park at the church in the hamlet of Eggerstanden, start in an easterly direction. After 600 metres, turn right. Follow the signpost that leads up to the Bildstein Alps. The path leads through forest and over pastures, past alps to the deserted Forstseeli. This beautiful place invites you to rest and the fireplace to barbecue. Continue up through the forest to the alpine pastures on the northern slope of the Fähnern. Slightly descending you reach the Eggli inn via Alp Heieren. Enjoy the unique view of the three mountain ranges of the Alpstein in the garden restaurant. From Eggli, take the same path for about 200 metres back to the turnoff down to Eggerstanden. On the north slope, the descent path leads back to the starting point.

images.caption: Ausblick vom Eggli in den Alpstein

title: From Geltendorf to Landsberg am Lech
short_description: We experience a varied tour that begins in the hilly landscape near Geltendorf. We hike through forests, meadows and fields and small villages to Landsberg am Lech.
long_description:
St. Ottilien is nestled in a beautiful landscape about 2 km from Geltendorf railway station. If you wish, you can also take the Ammersee railway directly to St. Ottilien station. However, the facilities do not only include the monastery. The following facilities can be found there: Monastery Gate, Monastery Church, Ottilien Chapel, Seminary Church, Mission Museum, Nähmaschinenmuseum, Galerie St. Ottilien, Retreat house, Herb garden, Railway station, Cemetery,  Grammar school, Day home, boarding school, Mission procuration, Monastery shop, Farm shop, Büchermarket, Emminger Hof, EOS-Verlag+Druck, Agriculture, Energy centre, Biogas plant
The Penzing air base is located between Penzing and Landsberg. With a bit of luck, we can watch one of the planes taking off or landing.
On the way, we pass through beautiful villages such as Eresing, Ramsach, Schwifting and Reisch.
Landsberg am Lech lies in the so-called Lechrain, the border landscape between Old Bavaria and Swabia. A first settlement existed at this location as early as 1135. The old town with its pretty houses and winding lanes is well worth seeing and we should bring plenty of time to explore. From the Lechbrücken there are wonderful views of the old town and the Mutterturm. The town also has a very special flair at night. Landsberg's railway station was awarded the title of "Germany's most beautiful small town railway station" in 2007.

title: Torchlight hike in the Braitachklamm gorge
short_description: The tour takes us through the Breitachklamm, the deepest gorge in the Bavarian Alps. Along the way we experience frozen waterfalls, curtains of ice and countless icicles on snow-covered rock faces. By firelight we discover the gorge in a completely new light, an unforgettable experience!
long_description: Today's tour takes us through the Breitachklamm, the deepest gorge in the Bavarian Alps. After a short walk along a natural path, we reach the gorge and hike along the Breitach on increasingly narrow paths. Along the way we experience frozen waterfalls, curtains of ice and countless icicles on snow-covered rock faces. By firelight we discover the gorge in a completely new light, an unforgettable experience!

title: HUAROCHIRI: GLACIAR CHUECON - LAGUNA SUIRICOCHA
short_description: Perteneciente al distrito de San Lorenzo de Quinti, se trata de una caminata de moderada a exigente debido a que se parte desde una altura considerable para luego hacer una contínua subida que llega hasta los 5000 MSNM en promedio.
long_description:
Trekking de un día, partiendo desde las 6:00 AM en el punto ubicado en la trocha vehicular PE-22A al lado de la Laguna Paccha. Ubicado en Huarochirí, el glaciar y laguna Chuecón es un lugar muy visitado de la cordillera central. Perteneciente al distrito de San Lorenzo de Quinti, se trata de una caminata de moderada a exigente debido a que se parte desde una altura considerable (4569 MSNM) para luego hacer una contínua subida que llega hasta los 5000 MSNM en promedio.
Los puntos principales del track son:
Laguna Paccha
Mirador Glaciar Chuecon
Glaciar y Laguna Chuecon
Mirador Laguna Suiricocha
  Los tours de full day normalmente llegan sólo hasta el Mirador Glaciar Chuecon, justo al lado de la antena instalada en el lugar. En mi caso, decidí hacer el regreso pasando por el sendero (no señalizado) que va hacia la Laguna Suiricocha, para luego retomar el sendero principal que va hacia el mirador. El sendero hacia este mirador si está bien identificable, por lo que esta parte no representa dificultades excepto por la resistencia a la altura. En cambio, el camino de regreso si es necesario guiarse bien con los distintos tracks GPS que se pueden encontrar en esta app.Para llegar al inicio del trekking, se toma la ruta hacia San Mateo para luego hacer un desvío en la trocha Rio Blanco hasta llegar a las cercanías de la Laguna Paccha.Se recomienda altamente estar bien adaptado a la altura y así evitar el soroche.

title: Three Lakes Tour
short_description: Through beautiful mixed forests, past impressive rocky outcrops from lake to lake from Wasserauen to Brülisau.
long_description:
From Wasserauen walk along the «Schwendebach» stream into the valley and climb your way up to the Seealpsee lake. At the end of the lake the trail will go up to the left through the picturesque mixed forest to the ridges along the «Unterstrich». You'll soon arrive at the idyllic alpine dairy-farming village of Meglisalp. The rest of the trail is rather steep as you head southeast to the «Bötzelsattel», crossing from there to the «Widderalpsattel» at nearly the same altitude. Then enjoy a gentle descent from the «Widderalp». Take a right before reaching the forest and you'll arrive at the «Stiefelfelsen» («boot rock»). As you pass this rock, there is a short ascent to where a spectacular view awaits you: the Fälensee lake shimmering before your eyes, embedded between steep rocky cliffs. By now you'll have reached the «Berggasthaus Bollenwees» mountain inn. As you approach the valley along a little lane, you'll cross «Alp Furgglen» and go through the mountain forest to reach the Sämtisersee lake. Like the Fälensee lake, there is no visible outlet since the water from both lakes flows underground and surfaces in the Rheintal valley. After a short ascent on the other side to the «Berggasthaus Plattenbödeli» mountain inn, follow the steep descent through the Brüeltobel ravine, passing the «Hexenwäldli» («witch's forest») down to Brülisau.

Note(s)
The trail can be followed in both directions.
Mountain inns: Seealpsee, Forelle, Meglisalp, Bollenwees, Plattenbödeli.

title: Bohusleden - Stage 2 - Stensjön to Maderna
short_description: The second stage of the Bohusleden trail leads from Lake Stensjön through two nature reserves and past the Skåtas sports and recreation facility to Lake Maderna.
long_description: On the second day we hike in the Delsjöområdet nature reserve. Stora Delsjön is one of the largest lakes in the Göteborg region and a popular destination for families. It is home to a well-known lakeside resort and a large sports facility called Skataring. The 19th-century stone castle of Stora Torp is worth a visit a little further along the trail. We then continue through the Knipeflågsbergen nature reserve, a vast bedrock plateau on the border with Delsjöområdet. We hike through the forest over the Getryggen elevation past the small lake Blacktjärn. In this area there is a good chance that we will encounter moose, deer and other animals. Legend has it that there are even trolls here.

title: From the village of Appenzell to the Kronberg
short_description: Hike with a beautiful view of the Säntis chain
long_description: The hike begins at the south exit of Appenzell railway station. Past the Freudenberg restaurant, the trail leads along the ski slope up to Sollegg, the top station of the ski lift. On the alpine path you hike almost level through magnificent fir forest in a westerly direction to the alps of Vorder and Hinter Wasserschaffen. Let your gaze wander northwards to the Säntis chain with Ebenalp, Schäfler, Altenalptürme, Öhrli and Säntis. Via Alp Blatten you reach the Scheidegg mountain inn. Stop for a walk before tackling the ascent. The last stretch leads past the St. Jakob Chapel up to the Kronberg, the highest point of the hike. Glide comfortably with the cable car to Jakobsbad or take one of the many valley descents under your feet.

title: Le Tour du Haut Giffre
short_description:
Cet itinéraire en boucle à faire sur plusieurs jours explore le massif du Haut Giffre, offrant des panoramas spectaculaires sur les montagnes environnantes, des forêts denses, des alpages verdoyants et des lacs de haute altitude. 
Translate to English
long_description:
Ce trek de plusieurs jours emmène les randonneurs dans une exploration complète du massif du Haut Giffre, une chaîne de montagnes spectaculaire située non loin du Mont Blanc. Le parcours est généralement divisé en étapes quotidiennes et permet de découvrir une grande diversité de paysages, des vastes prairies alpines aux impressionnantes falaises calcaires en passant par des forêts de conifères et des rivières cristallines.
Le circuit propose des vues imprenables sur des sommets comme le Tête à l'Âne, la Tête de Bostan ou encore le Buet, surnommé "le Mont Blanc des Dames". Les randonneurs traversent également des cols élevés, certains dépassant les 2 000 mètres d'altitude, et passent par des villages pittoresques comme Samoëns et Sixt-Fer-à-Cheval.

title: From the Schwägalp to the Säntis
short_description: Beautiful tour to the highest point of the Alpstein.
long_description:
The Säntisweg begins 400 metres to the southwest of the Schwägalp valley station, at the Gmeinenwisen. The path winds steeply up to the rock bastion «Musfalle», which is easy to climb thanks to wire rope protection. The path continues «over a wide band of grass and scaffolding, then along the foot of a rock face. You come to the «elbow», from where the trail climbs steeply again. Via steps and stairs you soon reach the traditional mountain inn Tierwis. Then continue climbing to the large cart field. Markings guide you between funnels and crevasses to the foot of the slope below the Girensattel and to the ridge itself. Continue past the Blauschneelücke and up üover the rock staircase, the so-called «Himmelsleiter», to the Säntis summit.


.

title: Potersalp
short_description: Circular hike from Weissbad to Potersalp.
long_description: You can reach the starting point of this hike by car or PubliCar from Weissbad. The signpost opposite the Waldgasthaus Lehmen shows the direction. You climb briefly in the open countryside. Hike leisurely through the Cholh forest. Now the path leads through the three alpine pastures Vorderleu - Leustückli - Grossleu. In front of you rise the rocky walls of the northern Säntis chain, from east to west the Schäfler summit, the climbing mountains of the Altenalptürme and the protruding, striking Öhrli. Via the Berndlibach - Grossberndli and Schwizerälpli the ascent leads to the highest point of the round tour, the upper Borstböhl. The route continues comfortably to the Potersalp communal alps. Every year at alpine time, the Potersalp Stobete, organised by the alpine dairymen, takes place at Dreihütten. On the gravel road you hike down to the Böhlwald. After an extensive hike through the forest, you come to the Leuenfall. Here the waters of the Berndlibach torrent thunder into the depths and shortly afterwards merge with the Wissbach. Just a few more steps and you are back at the starting point in Lehmen.

title: Sincholagua
short_description:
Aussichtsreiche Wanderung auf den höchsten Gipfel am Rande der Caldera des historischen Vulkans Pululahua im Norden der Hauptstadt Quito mit Abstiegsvariante über Cerro La Marca.
Translate to English
long_description:
Der Pululahua ist die mehrere Kilometer große Caldera eines antiken Vulkan, die heutzutage eine einzigartige Kulturlandschaft im Inneren einer vor langer Zeit kollabierten Magmakammer beherbergt. Am östlichen Kraterrand und direkt nördlich von Quitos Vorstadt-Sehenswürdigkeit "Mitad del Mundo" ("Mittelpunkt der Welt") liegen der 3.356 Meter hohe Sincholagua sowie seine kleine Schwester, der Cerro La Marca. Die hier beschriebene Tour folgt einem gut ausgetretenen Wanderweg ohne größere technische Schwierigkeiten zum aussichtsreichen Gipfelplateau des Sincholagua sowie eine Abstiegsvariante auf staubigen Wegspuren über den kleineren Nachbargipfel. Eine wunderbare Halb- bis Ganztagestour in unmittelbarer Nähe der Stadt mit eindrucksvollen Ausblicken auf die umliegenden Bergketten, Vulkanriesen und über das Häusermeer der ecuadorianischen Hauptstadt.

title: Lake Sämtis with Alps
short_description: Hike along the Sämtiser lake
long_description: From Brülisau you hike along the Gütersträsschen to the Pfannenstil. Accompanied by the murmur of the Brüelbach stream, the partly steep mountain trail leads up to the Plattenbödeli mountain inn. Just south of it, the Maria Heimsuchung chapel rises out of a forest clearing, where services are celebrated on Sundays in the summertime. The trail continues slightly downhill to the blue-green Sämtiser lake. The mountain lake with its pleasant water temperature invites you to swim and linger. The hike continues along the shore of the lake. At the end of the lake you climb northwards to Lawannen and Alp Soll. Via the Mädi-Hasenplatte alp rights, the trail leads to the Ruhsitz mountain inn. A splendid view into the heart of the Alpstein massif and, in fine weather, far out to sea, make the short climb worthwhile. The path to the Hoher Kasten crosses here. The descent goes over pastures of the Rossberg to the year-round inhabited farmhouses with steep mountain slopes down to Brülisau.

title: Walk around the Seealpsee («rond-omm»)
short_description: Hike around the tranquil Seealpsee lake
long_description:
There is a car park between the two inns in Wasserauen where a signpost marks the mountain trail branching off to the left. After a short stroll through the alpine meadow, an ascent will take you through the Huttentobel ravine. In the green beech forest the trickling sounds of the mountain stream will accompany you up to «Alp Hütten», where the view opens up to reveal a magnificent mountain landscape. Then enjoy a pleasant walk to «Alp Waldhütte», where you'll enjoy a view of Säntis, the highest mountain in the Alpstein massif. In the meantime, you'll have hardly noticed that the picturesque Seealpsee lake lies right before you. Take a relaxing stroll around the lake, walking along the left side of the shore, and see the countless little alpine huts scattered at the base of the large «Seealp». On the other side of the lake, walk until you reach the lake's outlet. Two cosy mountain inns invite you to come in and stay a while. More sentimental walkers will also enjoy a pleasant cable car ride surrounded by the magnificent mountain backdrop. In a sparse forest along the lake, almost hidden from view, you'll see the Bruder Klaus mountain chapel. Make your descent along the overhanging rock face to Chobel. The ravine of the «Schwendibach» stream lies below you to the right. The trail goes past Appenzell's water and power plant, and into the valley to Wasserauen.

Note(s)
Mountain inns: Seealpsee, Forelle. Alpenrose and Bahnhof Wasserauen in Wasserauen

title: A relaxing hike in Piatra Craiului via Cheile Pisicii & Toanches Hill
short_description: A one-day trip just at the base of Piatra Craiului; it takes you through Cheile Pisicii and on the slightly shady paths that cut through the Toancheș Hill to reach Casa Folea.
long_description:
The route starts with the forest road in the Zărnești Gorge. On weekends, this road is very crowded, attracting both occasional hikers and cyclists.
Just upon entering Cheile Pisicii (Cat's Gorges), all the noise and crowds will suddenly go away. It's about a 15-20 minute walk from the barrier to the entry point into these short gorges.
The area is less known and less explored, although many people have heard of the gorges and wonder how to find them. At a steady pace, jumping from rock to rock in the gorges takes 20-30 minutes. You exit into the same forest road that comes from Zarnesti down below.
Follow this road a little further and enjoy the high rocky walls. The yellow triangle sign appears shortly on the left, leading you through the forest on Toancheș Hill. The path is quite clear, although not very beaten. If you go in the summer, you will find strawberry bushes in the forest.
On the other side of the hill you have a superb view over the village of Măgura, but also towards the Bucegi ridge. The descent is steep and fast, leading you to a wide forest road above Magura village. We cut the walk short by following an almost invisible signpost on the left that showed a route back to the Zarnesti gorges that we didn't know. It was the fastest descent from Magura to Zarnesti I've ever seen.

title: Around the Gufelstock
short_description: Beautiful tour with a fantastic panorama;
long_description:
Experience the mountain waters and their energy around the Gufelstock in the centre of Glarnerland. In the evening, you will rave about the clear, clean, fresh and available cooling water.

From Engi, the path leads steadily and evenly uphill past the holiday home to the Gufeli Oberstafel. It belongs only to the game and nature. The panoramic view at the finish is impressive.
During the descent via 'Bi den Seelenen' and Fessis to Schwanden, the Glarnerland lies at our feet.

Note(s)
In uncertain weather or snow, the summit area is difficult to find. Carts or pathless sections make luck more difficult.

Nebel macht nicht immer so glücklich!

title: Family hike: Over castle ruins to the Alpsee lake
short_description:
Easy hike from the Laubenbergerstein ruins across meadows, woods and pastures, past other castle ruins to one of the most beautiful lakes in the Allgäu
.
long_description:
The easy tour from the Laubenbergerstein ruins to the Alpsee lake takes you over beautiful pastures and shady forest tracks and offers fantastic views of the Allgäu Alps.
The starting point is already a highlight: on the grounds of Laubenbergerstein Castle, children can run around, learn about the history on information boards and enjoy the beautiful view. After a short stretch along the road, the trail leads over pastureland past cows, along steep forest paths and through beautiful mountain meadows. In addition, the ruins of Rothenfels and Hugofels castles lie along the way; in fact, there are only remains of walls here. Nevertheless, there is a lot to discover – and a beautiful view of the Alpsee.
The asphalted path leads to the castle ruins.
An asphalt path leads from the ruins along picturesque meadows to the Alpsee. Here you will find plenty of leisure activities: Bathing places, beer garden, mini-golf, skytrail, playground or (pedal) boats.

images.caption: Blick auf Ruine Laubenbergerstein mit Grünten
Blick von Hugofels auf den Großen Alpsee

title: Walk to Äscher-Ebenalp and the Wildkirchli caves
short_description: Hike with panoramic views of Kamor, Hoher Kasten and the long rock face of Alp Sigel
long_description:
From the railway station in Schwende the trail goes past St. Martin's church, before ascending west to Triebern. Follow the lane before soon taking a left through shady shrubbery, and then continue for a short distance until you reach Eugst. The wide ski trail goes to «Alp Bommen» and up to the «Gartenwald» (garden forest). When you come to a fork in the trail, take a left and enjoy a beautiful panoramic view of Kamor, Hoher Kasten and the long rock face of Alp Sigel. The «Berggasthaus Äscher» mountain inn will also suddenly come into view, nestled up directly into the vertical rock face on the east side of the Ebenalp. Walk over the wooden bridge firmly secured to the steep rock face until you come to the Wildkirchli caves, first reaching the altar cave in front of which there stands a wooden bell tower from the 19th century. Then follow the caves until you reach the Ebenalp. The Wildkirchli caves have become world-famous, thanks to prehistoric findings dating back to the Stone Age. Skeletons of cave bears and stone tools are evidence that hunters lived here in prehistoric times. These findings are exhibited at the Appenzell Local History Museum (Heimatmuseum Appenzell) and at the Historical and Ethnological Museum of St. Gallen (Historisches und Völkerkundemuseum). After visiting the caves ascend to the plateau of the Ebenalp. Take some time for yourself and enjoy the impressive panoramic view before taking the cable car back down to the valley.

Note(s)
Mountain inns: Äscher, Ebenalp

title: Klausensaumpfad
short_description: Beautiful hike through an area steeped in history! The legend about the determination of the cantonal border is amazing!
long_description:
Experience the breathtaking mountain landscape around Urnerboden and its watercourses.

From Linthal, the trail leads to the Fätschbach stream. From there the climb begins, with every metre of altitude covered improving the view of the imposing mountain world. Past the Bergli restaurant, the Berglist waterfall, along the rushing stream, we reach the Argenseeli, the Urnerboden. Up to the Klausen Pass at 1948 m.

On the post bus you can reminisce about the last few hours. It goes back down to Linthal or alternatively to Altdorf.

Note(s)
With the PostBus you ride the best connections.

.

Cattle drive on the Klausen Pass road near the Vorfrutt Alp

title: Via Ferrata Zermatt - Route C
long_description:
Route C of the via ferrata above Zermatt is often done after routes A and B. It is only suitable for experienced climbers. It is only suitable for experienced via ferrata climbers, because in addition to mountain experience, it requires a lot of strength, stamina and endurance.

To access the Schweifinen via ferrata, turn into the Trifttal valley. Before the hiking trail crosses the Triftbach stream, turn right and in about 30 minutes you reach a via ferrata with some tricky sections: a vertical wall, a swinging wire rope ladder and an exposed traverse on iron bars.

The route ends on the hiking trail that leads directly to Zermatt from the Wisshorn (approx. 1h).

title: Glacier trekking to the Monte Rosa hut
Rothorn Hut
long_description:
The Rothornhütte at the foot of the Zinalrothorn is a cosy mountain restaurant with an attractive terrace and a unique mountain panorama. Hikers and alpinists whose destination is the Zinalrothorn, Obergabelhorn, Wellenkuppe, Trifthorn, or Aeschhorn gather here.

In untouched nature, the path climbs to the legendary mountain inn "Hotel du Trift". After Vieliboden, you find yourself in the fascinating world of a former glacier landscape and climb steadily towards the hut.

Note(s)
If you are not staying at the hut, please allow enough time for the return.

title: Hönggerberg Hiking
short_description: If you want to escape the hustle and bustle of the city and enjoy a few hours surrounded by greenery, this is just the itinerary for you. What better way to end the walk than to enjoy a slice of cake with one of the best views of the city of Zurich?
long_description: The entire route is asphalted and presents no particular difficulty, making it suitable for the whole family. The route starts along football pitches and expanses of meadows. All along the walk there are beautiful panoramic viewpoints from which you can enjoy an overview of the Uetliberg and Altstetten district. About halfway along, the route proceeds into the campus of the ETH, one of the most prestigious university institutes in Switzerland and considered one of the most important research centres in the world, so don't be surprise to see a lot of students around. Once through this busiest part, the route continues to the Waidberg forest and from that moment forward take your time to enjoy the city view from one of the highest spots. To be sure to fully appreciate it, take a seat at terrace of the Waid restaurant for a cup of coffee before heading back.

title: Platthorn and Mettelhorn
long_description:
The Trifttal is not yet accessible by cable cars and ski slopes. At the top, in the valley basin, the "Hotel du Trift" is enthroned in its unique, almost untouched nature. Chamois, marmots, eagles and ibexes can be observed here.

From the inn, the trail leads over the Triftchumme to the Platthorn, becoming increasingly steep and demanding. Over the strongly receding glacier you reach the Mettelhorn in a short time. Both peaks offer a breathtaking view of the mountain world of Zermatt.

Note(s)
Be careful of wet trails and bad weather!
Information about snow conditions on the glacier firn can be obtained at the mountain inn.

title: Cherkizovo pond and park - come and see!
short_description: Cherkizovsky Pond and Park is located in the Cherkizovo district of Moscow. The pond – one of the oldest ponds and named after the village located here in the 15th century.
long_description:
The pond originated on the site of the village of Cherkizovo, which was ruled by an Horde prince with the Mongolian name Cherkiz.
The pond has been landscaped, with trails and paths for pleasant walks. A park with sports grounds was arranged near the pond. Between the pond and the park there is a well-known trail «green ring of Moscow, the distance of which is only 160 km.
  The Church of Elijah the Prophet is located near Cherkizovsky Pond. The date of foundation of the church is 1690. The temple was founded by Elijah Ozakov in honour of his patron, who actually gave the name of the church.

images.caption: View of Elijah the Prophet Church from Cherkizovsky Pond
Church of Elijah the Prophet in Cherkizovo

title: Riedholzer ball
short_description: Beautiful snowshoe tour through the forest and across small open spaces with views of the Bregenzerwald and Allgäu from the summit;
long_description: The tour leads from the road junction to the Iberg ski lift up to the forest. Over snow-covered roots, the trail climbs upwards through coniferous forest with medium steepness. At the highest point of the Riedholzer Kugel, the Nagelfluhkette and the peaks of the Bregenzerwald can be admired in good visibility. Walk across an open space in a westerly direction to the mountain station of the Iberg ski lift, carefully cross the drag lift at the mountain station and descend along the left edge of the piste to a path that leads through the small forest and then back north along the edge of the forest to the path in the direction of the Iberg ski lift/ valley station.

title: The lava mold caves in Călimani Mountains
short_description: A 2-in-1 hiking idea, also ideal to hike with children, to get to the only two lava mold caves in Romania, at the foot of the Călimani Mountains.
long_description:
The route starts from the main road and splits a few hundred meters into the forest. At that point, you have to choose which way to go. The path takes you only through the forest, slightly upwards.
The route to the Andreneasa Cave is a bit longer than the one to the „Căsoaia lui Ladaș” cave. Both caves have their own particular elements, and their uniqueness in the local carstic relief is quite a promising calling card.
At the end of both trails, on the edge of the caves, overwhelming panoramas open up over the Mureș Gorge and the Gurghiu Mountains to your front. Such views you can only see if you climb much more serious trails.

images.caption: Path to Căsoaia lui Ladaș cave
Entrance to the cave of Căsoaia lui Ladaș

title: Motta Naluns - Alp Clünas - Alp Laret - Ftan
Around Iceland in 10 days
short_description: Iceland is hardly comparable to continental Europe: The peaceful and largely untouched landscape radiates a heavenly calm. Numerous craters protrude from the ground, hot springs emit impressive clouds of steam. Not only nature lovers will lose themselves in this diverse and pristine nature.
long_description: The following stage tour takes us in ten days along the roads of Iceland to the most interesting places on the island. From Keflavík International Airport, we travel along Iceland's panoramic roads to impressive waterfalls such as Gullfoss, gigantic gorges, numerous coastal areas and picturesque fishing villages. To make sure that relaxing moments are also included, the route also takes us to pleasantly warm thermal baths, where we can once again enjoy the impressive panorama of Iceland. A special highlight is the whale watching in the metropolis of Húsavík. The 2650 km route also includes many an undisturbed geyser such as the famous Strokkur or the spectacular crater lake Kerið. In direct contrast to this is the extravagant capital Reykjavík, which immediately captivates us with its lust for life and cosmopolitan nature. The motorised tour is rounded off with a foray through the vast Vatnajökull National Park and the Krýsuvík volcano system. This provides a comprehensive insight into the impressive volcanic landscape that created the island 16 million years ago.

images.caption: Auf Islands Landstraßen stellt sich automatisch ein Gefühl von grenzenloser Freiheit ein.
Einer von vielen Panoramablicken auf Islands usprüngliche Vulkanlandschaften.

Reykjavík's streets are modern, extravagant and varied

title: Along the entire Mourne Wall
short_description: You are looking for a hiking challenge, for beautiful views and a stunning landscape, and you don't want to care about orientation while walking? Follow the complete circle of the Mourne Wall and climb many of the Mourne Mountains, including the top of this outstanding small mountain range, the Slieve Donnard.
long_description:
This route covers many of the Mourne Mountains and follows nearly all the time the Mourne Wall. This is a up to two meter high wall, which was build in the early 20th century. The parents of many locals built this monument by hand. Walking for many hours along this wall makes one humble before the hardships of the builders! Even more you will enjoy the great views and the stunning and special landscape which is quite unique for the whole green island.
I recommend to walk clockwise. You start with the steepest climb (Slieve Binnian) and the worse way conditions on the descent to the Silent Valley and some more boggy parts until you have reached Slieve Muck and the climb to latter summit. From here there are many paths along the wall. Depending from the wind direction you should choose the wind protected side. This saves a lot of energy through the day!
When walking clockwise, you arrive the highest peak in the afternoon and the chance to find this most popular spot in the Mournes completely empty is much higher. And finally the descent towards the Irish Sea in the fading evening light let you forget all the strains of the day!
Don't forget to carry enough water with you. There is no reliable and clean spring on the whole way!

images.caption: hike in Mourne: Along the entire Mourne Wall

title: Anza-Borrego Desert State Park The Slot
short_description: The Slot is a fun loop hike near Borrego Springs, California that is rated as moderate. It features beautiful flora and fauna. The slot canyon in Anza Borrego is one of those hikes that you never realized you had right in California.
long_description: Anza-Borrego is discovered in the Slot. There, the geological landscape opens up, revealing the land defeated by time and water. Walking easily through the narrow siltstone canyon of the Slot is an exciting adventure in the desert, like an attraction Mother Nature would have created. In addition, it is located southwest of Borrego Springs and the dusty road leading to it is passable by cars. The entrance to the canyon is not very well indicated, but it is obvious. Follow the countless footprints that descend more than 6 metres into the crevasse, turn left and follow the slight descent. The canyon tightens almost immediately and you will have to sneak between walls whose width is sometimes less than a shoulder width. The pink and beige siltstone of the Slot, enhanced by the blue of the sky, offers splendid photos.

title: HUAROCHIRI: LAGUNA CASHPE
short_description:
Trekking de un día hacia la Laguna Cashpe principalmente. El el trayecto se pueden observar demasiadas lagunas muy bellas, que trataré de colocar los respectivos waypoints que pude grabar durante la caminata.
Translate to English
long_description:
Este trekking, a diferencia de los rutas que ofrecen la mayoría de agencias o grupos, inicia desde un punto de carretera LIM - 116 (Carretera Milloc - Marcapomacocha) y finaliza en el parking donde comienzan los demás grupos. Se trata de una ruta de más horas y un poco más exigente que las convencionales.
Entre los lugares más resaltantes que se pueden observar son:
LAGUNA CANCHIS-LAGUNA PUCRO-LAGUNA CHICHIS-LAGUNA LACHIS-LAGUNA WARMI-LAGUNA RUMICRUZ-LAGUNA CHULLO-LAGUNA PUCARCOCHA-LAGUNA CARPA-LAGUNA CASHPE-LAGUNA QUIUSHA-LAGUNA HUASCA

title: Tomülpass
long_description:
The Tomülpass connects the Safiental with the Valsertal. Far from the hustle and bustle of the world, in the midst of a wonderful mountain backdrop, at the Turrahus (refreshments and overnight accommodation), the tour climbs quite steeply right from the start. You reach the top of the pass on the Polenweg, via Alp Falätscha. During the Second World War, this path was upgraded and made passable. However, the pass never had any major economic significance. Today it serves mainly as a technical and physical challenge for mountain bikers.
From the pass, the tracks lead down to Alp Tomül, and continue almost straight ahead over the Spindlebüdemli onto the forest hiking trail to Vals. We are happy to be able to fully take in the panorama of the Vals valley in the quiet rhythm of our steps.

title: Regnitz Cycle Path - Valley Route
short_description: This easy river route is well signposted and leads along idyllic paths along the rivers Pegnitz and Regnitz through Franconia.
long_description: The cycle path, divided into four stages, leads along the Pegnitz and Regnitz rivers for 85 km. We cycle without major climbs on side roads and farm tracks and experience both the nature and the culture of the region. As the route runs on mainly asphalted roads and without much traffic, it is particularly well suited for family tours.
